Battle Wizards are rarely armoured for it interferes with their casting, yet a steed can and should be barded to add a level of protection.
Imperial pegasi are found in Grey Mountains where Bretonnian and Empire hunters fight over capturing the foals.
The rune of the Ancestor God of Runesmiths hardens both the axe and armour of the Dwarf who bears it.
This tool is a powerful yet confusing artefact; it allows the user to read the heavens for ill omens, yet it always relates to what tomorrow's stars will say.
Gifted to Bruckner by Elspeth von Draken, to protect him from the foul sorceries of the Maggot Lord, this black gem possesses powers unknown, and served Elspeth's own deadly schemes.
A ruby-red jewel imbued with a swirling energy; attaching it to a weapon grants it strange powers…
To each of his Chieftains Tamurkhan granted a powerful talisman, to enhance their power, but also to yoke it to his own through Nurgle's immense will.
You put enough lenses in a scope and you can probably even see the surface of the Twin-Tailed Comet itself!
When the sands of death run down, nothing in existence – or not – can hold back the deadly Winds of Shyish.
The finest blades forged within the Slayer's Keep, designed to bring down the largest and most ferocious monsters on the battlefields of the Old World.
Sometimes the pen is mightier than the sword, but in the case of the Tallyman, the two are equally dangerous.
That which is not taboo of Chaos Dwarf weapon manufacturing can be learned from, resulting in a Dawi-made weapon far superior in every way.
For centuries this long blade has been used by the city of Nuln's champion in preference to the more traditional headsman's axe.
A sickle made purely from oak, but just as hard as the hardest metal. Its wielder has a strong affinity with the Winds of Ghyran and can channel that energy into healing those around them.
The meagre runts ignominiously cleaved in two will never know the defilement brought on by the debilitating wave of Nurgle's will... which may be a mercy to most!
Gifted to him by the Chaos Dwarfs of the Black Mountains, the greyish fumes produced when this weapon is swung are foully poisonous... which pleases the Maggot Lord greatly!
This ancient, storied sword is rumoured to be the first one ever forged. It certainly seems to have an uncanny power over other weapons...
The flame burning at the end of this enchanted staff matches the anger levels of its bearer.
Forged through transmutation, no mortal-forged metal can withstand its devastating slice; the foe's armour is cut to pieces like so much ribbon at its touch.
Atop Gnarla, his War Boar of prodigious size, might and flatulence, Gorbad has bellowed many a thunderous call to a successful Waaagh!
The Blood God’s own Flesh Hound is a colossal Daemon of great power, ridden on the battlefield in the fashion of a monstrous beast.
A vast, mobile altar allows the souls of the slain to be ritualistically condemned directly from the field of slaughter.
Skulltaker’s is the most dreaded Juggernaut of all, a metal-plated beast of primordial rage that carries the Slayer of Kings to his doomed quarries.
The owner of the living head was decidedly unlucky; the previous owner of the shrunken head, likewise. Surely, the current owner would be the lucky one!
Been 'avin strange dreams lately... Wearin' a tin on me head an' ridin' a Gnoblar...
The mighty former breastplate of a many-named, widely-famed Tomb Warrior, and the current gutplate of a big-named, well-fed Ogre.
Presently worn by the most brutally cunning Ogre in his tribe.
I reckon I can make a new armguard from this 'ere tin...
Dat me gut talkin' or me new gutplate? Stop ya conversatin', both of ya!
A loincloth to withstand the hardest and most underhanded of blows.
A miraculous gutplate that, along with protecting its owner it battle, cures the worst cases of indigestion.
The mind-dulling effects of this otherwise awe-inspiring attire, when worn by an Ogre, are all but negligible on its owner.
An Ogre would never be caught wearing a full suit of armour. Thankfully, the Nightshroud merely manifests around him. At worst, it makes others bump into him. Worst for them, that is.
Strapped to an Ogre's wrist, a shield of this size would be little more than an adornment. Yet somehow, it deflects both blows and missile fire with ease.
It is meant to sharpen the mind and the senses of those who wear it on their heads. It still confers some of its effects when used as a bowl.
Oi, 's got some scratches on't but it fits!
Berserk rage manifests differently in different creatures. Some Maneaters have learned to keep their hunger unsated and release the pent-up fury all at once in battle.
The Dark Elf practice of consuming Black Dragon Eggs speaks to the heart and soul of what it is to be an Ogre: adventurous, opportunistic eating, and consequences be damned.
Widely-travelled Maneaters have developed a taste for pre-smoked meat – black powder efficiently initiates the smoking process while terminating its 'living process'!
Don' throw it in tha fire! Don' eat it! Ya know... Jus' give it t'me.
Through cunning use of diplomacy, the Maneaters have acquired a piece of advanced technology from the Chaos Dwarfs for the price of just a few dented skulls (not their own).
While unerring devotion is usually the prerequisite for such an honour, unusually effective service is also rewarded – and the Maneaters' services are as effective as they are unusual.
The Unliving can afford a few mistakes when throwing explosives. The Maneaters just chuck them as far as they can and pray they remembered to light the fuse!
Ogres don't put much stock in the spiritual side of eating their foes, but sometimes that spiritual side creeps in after the eating is done.
A silent glare from an Ogre is as unlikely as bare-chested bloodlust from a Vampire. But when it happens, it is the silence itself that becomes glaring, stunning foes into terror.
If you are strong enough that nothing can stop your advance, what stops you from making it so you halt *any* advance?
Living 'ard? Hah!... What do they know?...
Vampiric blessings often carry sinister overtones, but what is more sinister yet is when such blessings are bestowed upon an Ogre.
Useful both in the heat of battle and when some drunken Ogre throws an oversized bone at your back.
They said they wave it at 'orses so them beasts know when t'go. Some of our boys could use that.
Kislevites sing of such charges as they mourn their dead. Ogres tell tales of the same as they enjoy their food – which may or may not be the Kislevites.
The Wood Elves' fierce, overbearing pride in the Wildwood has found fertile soil in the Ogres' overbearing certainty that it holds no threat bigger than them.
The truly hawk-eyed never miss. And neither do the truly ham-handed.
The significance of hell-forging requires an understanding the numerous finer points of swordmaking, but who needs a fine point when your entire blade is ablaze?
One does not need to know what a banner symbolises to draw strength from it, especially a Skaven one. It is as potent as it is indecipherable.
Made from the pelt of a beast that was impossible to kill with arrows, the numerous holes in it notwithstanding. However, still makes a good tale during Maneater feasts.
I seen 'em feathered tinnies scream an' charge like they were one o'us! Honest! Makes me like'em more, though I never had a taste for them.
The first step in teaching Ogres to stalk their prey is to tell them, repeatedly, not to move  or do anything. Only certain Maneaters know what the other steps are.
Ogres have overcome enough challenges outside of battle alone to make even High Elves raise an eyebrow. Some Ogres realise what such strength means during battle.
When Dark Elves speak of slaughter, the word belies their finely-honed killing techniques. To Ogres, the word will forever be as literal as rock.
Hidin' and killin' em with poison?! Huh. Does it make 'em taste better with poison in 'em?
A mark of honour seemingly tailor-made to Ogres, especially when they recognise its potential as a weapon.
Too troublesome when stuck in one's teeth, and hardly a worthy meal. Besides, their hidden martial capabilities make these birds worthy pets.
The notion of a predator carries a somewhat overblown connotation of pride. The reality of a predator is... well, an Ogre. A rose by any other name, and all that…
Ogre Mercenaries borrow various foreign affectations in garb, weaponry and even speech. However, the Lizardmen have reminded them of the unchanging, naked, wordless monster beneath.
Magnanimous' Ogres are no such thing by any other measure but their own. To be a short-tempred one is to make even rough Norscans flinch.
Surprise! is what an Ogre shouts when charging from a battlefield away. Imagine anyone's surprise then, when it happens from much, much closer.
All the cleverness and lethality of a Red Crest Skink with but a fraction of the fidgeting and screeches that make them so hard to skin and boil properly.
The Ogres' indiscriminate appetites have made them both the towering threat that they are, and with some helping of Undead meat, an outright explosive menace.
Easy and straightforward to etch or splash onto anything, and as reliable as anything the Dwarfs provide.
What makes it so distracting? The hodge-podge of tatters on it? The half-scrawled nonsense? ...Oh, is that a butterfly over there?
Some Ogres do not realise how inherently suicidal their way of life really is, or do not care. Swearing a Slayer Oath amends their ignorance, but otherwise changes nothing.
There is no taunt that an Ogre does not already embody. They have simply learned to address all their points of pride to their enemies. Why does it make them so angry?
The Vampires' Hunger makes them thirst endlessly, even in the middle of battle. For Ogres, Hunger is hunger. Tear a foe's leg, kill another with it, eat the leg.
Killing Daemons is so difficult that some humans have dedicated their lives to it. For Ogres, it is just a *little* harder than usual, but now they also have a reason to do it.
So... I won't die if I'm stubborn enough? Mebbe thass why I'm still alive!
A potent portent of doom, as if it being waved about as an Ogre banner was not enough of a clue.
Truly a warcry for all time.
Uniquely styled to appeal to Ogres – namely, thick enough to act as a second skin. The colours are mostly primary, but its status as art has always been secondary, anyway.
Er, is it made for witches, or *from* witches?... Eitha way...
An Ogre's worthy foe is one that has the most meat on it. Coincidentally, they are also the most difficult to kill – a fortunate coincidence in philosophies.
That white bit on it means our guts are strong like the Mountains o' Mourn!
That black bit on it means our shots are strong like the Fire Mouth!
Those Cathay quacks like their iron so much, they even drinks it!
A miraculous map that, when followed by Ogres, always leads to a battle instead of treasure. They do not mind either way!
Those Cathay quacks like their stars so much, they bottled 'em!
Puzzled by Dwarfen paroxysms of rage at the very sight of it, Ogres finally decided that stunties disapprove of wearing beards backwards. A justified reaction, if a little extreme.
Keeps sand out of me mouth? Good. I'd ratha eat somethin' meatier.
Somethin' shouting inside... 'S like a little man boilin' in a pot. Hahahaha!
A sip contains the strength of many men, or in this case, the strength of a foul-tempered Ogre with a roaring hangover.
Hey, if dat mouldy pile'o'bones in there is still mean an' kickin', I can do it too!
Foun' some canned meat talkin to this 'ere piece of wood. Hey! Piece-o'-wood lady! Say somefin'!
Killed some git that killed a Mannikor... Reckon this makes me the Mannikor-killer-killer!
Dis some kin' of fire poker?
Putting this on makes it very difficult to take off. Ogres have found that the resulting arm-flailing, however, lends itself well to a powerful, if curious, combat technique.
Barging headfirst into a maelstrom of magick while wearing a feathered cloak and screaming is a ploy as simple and as successful as most Ogres' battle tactics.
Oi! Sounds like somethin' roarin' in there like it missed a meal or two!
As digusting as it is, Ogres think it's still better than the meat, and given their usually indiscriminate palate, that says a lot.
It takes dexterity not to turn such a weapon on yourself by accident. Ogres are willing to take that risk... or they don't know of it!
A thin stick and a string, or else a net, and patience: all things alien to Ogres, but they enjoy the fish well enough.
A master of the skillset an Ogre best appreciates: being angry and being violent. So very, *very* violent.
An implausible marriage of a halfling's prodigious capacity for cooking and an Ogre's capacity for consuming food… including any cook who fails to meet their demand.
A merchant he may be, but there's not much trade taking place. He simply points his masters in the direction of weapons and they take them from their previous owners.
Dis new chef seems ta be able to just cook forever!
He knows better than to hawk his wares to Ogres. Still, a living, breathing, well-dressed human in their company is bound to improve others' opinion of their horde.
A servant of Slaanesh would certainly appreciate the pleasure of a good meal. Watching Ogres enjoy one makes one reconsider that tenet of one's faith, however.
Elves are a race of contrasts: their lords are glorious and terrible, their slaves are garrulous and tiresome. Or as Ogres call them, a meal in the making.
The ingredients he is forced to use are highly unconventional, but various forms of fermented... stuff can be found plentifully from which a drink could be made.
Incredibly, almost as skilled as a Bruiser in putting an end to internal tribal conflict. His only challenge is ensuring Tyrants remain appreciative.
In the eyes of Ogres, a Gnoblar in disguise, or maybe a couple, stacked on top of each other and wearing a patchwork overcoat.
When you choose the life of an entertainer, you rarely consider the possibility of plying your trade for the sake of your life.
Ogre captives do not entertain the notion of release for ransom. However, they do provide entertainment for their captors, courtesy of a well-maintained fighting pit.
Oi, gemme somethin' to eat! No, no Squigs aroun' ya daft runt! But bring me one o' those, too, if you see it.
As the Gnoblar is beneath the Goblin, the Snotling is beneath a Gnoblar. Ogres, in their turn, often don't even know what these creatures even are.
Never has a food-taster been more disgusted and afraid to eat something that is not poison. Usually.
Ogres only pay attention to his songs if he stops singing. It is not the kind of audience reaction that bodes well when there's piping-hot cauldron and campfire around.
If no Mammoths, Stonehorns or Thundertusks are around, tame Ogres are the ones that maybe *don't* eat you, right?
Those serving the will of the Maw are well-served by one dedicated to serving maws. In truth, they are mostly under-served. It is a bonding experience.
Bigger, stronger and more willing than Gnoblars, some also willingly go into the pot if they consider their term served, as a form of release.
A proud contributor to recent Ogre breakthroughs in agriculture.
I push 'im in the pot, 'e climbs back out! 'S unnatural, 's what it is!
Always on the lookout for drapes to dust, but his search has hithertho been futile. As a piece of internal decoration or even couture, Ogres are notably disinclined towards drapery.
Though well-suited to the sort of exotic weaponry most Ogres can barely use, should he sermonise about weapon design, this one is swiftly met with its apex: a large club.
He has not yet been eaten, miraculously. If anything, his numerous escapes and retrievals have started to teach Ogres something about subtlety in hunting.
Firebellies have tried to eat it. Barely have they swallowed when it finds its way out again... violently!
Yheetees bask in the icy blast like old women around a hearth. Other Ogres may complain about their campfires going out, but they know better than to challenge Yheetees on such grounds.
To Ogres, it's just blood-soaked dirt, but as they have taken to fashioning their own versions of it, it seems to help with improving discipline.
Ogres would prefer pendants with more heft to them, but that rat skull definitel seems to grow heavier in the presence of magick... Must be something to it…
Ogres have heard it said that they should not eat this under any circumstances, but have not made up their minds as of yet.
Tells me to kill people. Like I don' know! Shut up already! I'll kill 'em, ya'll see! AAAARGH!
Definitely not Bugman's. If anything, it induces something beyond sobriety. Surprised as they are by how well it makes them fight, Ogres hate it.
Huh... Now thassa differen't kind of eatin'. More!
At first, it caused a campside fight: when an Ogre poked the tribal pot in impatience and pierced it through like cloth. From then on, the tribe appreciated the weapon in an entirely new light.
Multi-purpose: capable of piercing five men clean through and suitable for then mounting over a fire to cook them.
Though looking at it makes one's eyes water, it is supremely good at beating battlefield foes into shapes convenient for cooking.
Hook-hands are bad for an Ogre's digestion, unlike their owners, but they make for a good memento.
Thanks to this implement, Ogres have recently discovered the joys of punching holes through things in addition to smashing them, though none of these things are rocks.
It is not made to size for an Ogre, but its usage is familiar enough. A spiked gauntlet swung forcefully enough will make enough contact for the tiny poisoned blade to do its job.
For creatures as wasteful with their force as Ogres, this extremely efficient weapon guarantees that even if they mostly miss, a simple graze can spell death for the foe.
Ogres bearin this axe are generally oblivious to the fact that it was made to serve those who seek death in battle. They only know it is *extremely* good at killing.
Some magical weapons whisper mysteriously, some scream in eldritch rage, and some just buzz – warning of foes with exactly the level of vocabulary an Ogre appreciates.
Found some tinned food preying at the lake, got myself a new sword and a good snack!
This weapon will never break as long as its bearer is on a worthy quest. Apparently, the Ogre's life of a wandering warrior is sufficiently quest-like for the purpose.
In Elven hands, such a bow hones an archer's already fearsome proficiency. In an Ogre's mits, it essentially does all the work.
Not sure about dis sword takin' a bite outta ma meals before I can...
Slender enough to be used as a toothpick by an Ogre, poisonous enough to be used in such manner only once.
A sword producing fire from the very air is an inconvenient cooking technique, unless the meal meets the blade half-way. Ogres have made it work.
A Warpstone-forged weapon usually has dramatic effects on those in its proximity. Its Ogre bearers, for instance, experience mild indigestion. Their enemies experience irreversible death.
Those who can read these infinite, maze-like carvings may navigate otherworldly paths to travel vast distances in the blink of an eye.
This glowing purple orb of unknown providence is a mere trinket to the unskilled spellcaster. But for those with the wisdom, it can be a source of great might.
Armour as black as the souls of the gods themselves. Harrower of their enemies you shall be, or ever-devoured, ever-tortured victim, if wanting they find you to be.
Styrkaar often goads foes into targeting him, the negligible pain they inflict fuelling his conviction that they are unworthy of inhabiting the same battlefield.
The scorched and blackened raiments of a clearly fire-obsessed Norscan raider.
I hold the keys to adoration. I may allow you a foot in the threshold. But what is ajar will snap closed on unworthy specimens.
The scurrilous slanders upon egotism's name are perpetrated by creatures lethally lacking in character. If you turn out to be one…\\nDo not turn out to be one.
The beauty of suffering is in the mind's poisonous capacity to inflict it on itself. The beauty of death is in its... execution.
Wander the lands, indulge in every home and on every field until nothing is left unmarked!
Rarely do I savour subtlety... But do not doubt my gift for it, should it serve a surfeit of malice.
It is not the tongues I speak that crawl into their malformed minds. It is the tongue I use.
This treasured tool of Asur admiralty command is an heirloom of past Sea Lords who have served Ulthuan with distinction.
A beacon of fiery rampage, which challenges enemies to run away from territory you have claimed – but only until your own stampede catches up to them.
From within it, you can look upon the world with the Dragon's terror-mongering hubris which lead to its demise. Surely, it will lead to your greatness.
An emblem of the countless bones strewn across the deserts by a creature which stalked its prey in wide-open spaces, prevailing again and again.
The mandate of unassailable pride: to fly instead of fall, and charge towards death instead of skulking away.
Even in death, its gaze arrests even the most heedless momentum and turns away even the most insistent blows.
A thick and beaten brass collar, spiked inside and out. Because only the toughest can bear such pain to receive the power of the Hound.
Wielding this tooth, a battle charge overcomes foes with the treacly sluggishness of a nightmare, in which the monster is as inescapable as it is vast.
This unusual gem of Onyx reflects no light at all, causing the magically inclined to become sick and drained in its presence.
Imbued within is terror that stings like poison and inherent malice so great that it occassionally takes corporeal form.
A Ghorgon gorges on flesh until it's gone. The Ghorgon is gone, but the flesh is not, for the Ghorgon's fangs are not yet sated.
Though it jabbers no more, it is still sleek with corrosive poison, and foes nearby still suffer the occasional bout of incoherent fear.
While the creature lived, its horns were a cunning ruse for those who mistook its malice for majesty. Now only the malice remains.
Still reverberating with otherwordly sound beyond the edge of hearing, this glowing charm stirs the air into a searing fever.
The living beast's weapon of overwhelming repulsion is now divested of the Dragon's will in death, attracting all manner of odious phenomena.
The presence of this silent and brooding mountain of a man from the far Chaos Wastes is unnerving, but his gaze is ever watchful.
You may not have heard of me, but your descendants will quail in fear, for I shall haunt the depths of their dreams after this day is done!
This large, slithering monstrosity of Slaanesh is a prized mount among Daemonettes, hissing and snapping with preternatural speed and mesmerising with their terrible gaze.
The impetuousness of the oldest Phoenix of the Flamespyre has faded to naught, but its wisdom, strength and loyalty to Caradryan remain true.
The best of all horse breeds found anywhere in the world, Elven steeds are noble, intelligent, graceful, and swift.
Unto the bearer of this warded charm is bestowed the protection of the Old Gods. Ignore their due at your own peril.
It is said the feathers of eagles bear the magic of the Eagle God himself, providing special boons and protection to those deemed worthy.
Bear these great gifts and the dark curses of their binding. Across endless battlefields of death and glory you are destined for striding.
Etched with coiling, snapping serpents of the north, this finely wrought axe of unknown origin inflicts wounds that blacken and freeze into brittle ice.
Damned before you be thy enemies, as long as your will and glory hold fast. A thousand damnations upon you should you falter…
Styrkaar channels every smirk, sneer and supercilious remark he's ever made against his hapless challengers into an onslaught that sweeps aside the unworthy chaff.
...And so the hammer smote down the noble knight, his armour and flesh crumbling into black dust upon whence the blow struck. The cawing of crows echoed in the distance... – Old Norscan legend
A magical artefact of immeasurable worth, it has changed many unworthy masters during the centuries before Nagash's return. Now it is finally in the hands of its creator.
Bloab's dolorous Doombells focus his magic and take a toll on enemy spellcasters, replacing their focus with an incessant clang that rings louder and louder in their minds.
The brazier that burns the remains of the Glottkin's parents, its smoke's life-sapping energies spreading and withering all that they touch.
No clearer evidence exists of the Skryre blend of insanity and brilliance than the plan-prints of their Tinker-in-Chief.
It is only right that the treacherous souls of your enemies repay you in death.
Whatever the truth, the armour spreads the legend and ensures the Red Duke's scourge will remain a jagged reality staring Bretonnia in the face.
Strengthened by the passage of the ages, this Chaos plate's aura of entropy also has the power to decay the magic of enemy weapons.
An armour of faith and steel – neither blows nor arcane means shall breach it.
A supreme expression of Nagash's craft, the Black Armour is one with him. Any threat aimed which travels on the wind also travels on Shyish. It shall be the death of those that sent it his way.

Settra wears a suit of age-old, regal armour that was said to have been crafted and worn by the jackal god, Djaf, when he walked the land. It is impervious to the ravages of time, and nothing can tarnish its resplendence.
This ancient bone piercing fills the one who wears it with an unquenchable rage towards the civilised races.
What he lacks in finesse, he makes up for in the liberal application of elbow grease.
Only one Destroyer there was, only one there is, only one there will be.
Abhorash's astounding feat of dragon-slaying and the original Blood Dragons' noble traditions are displayed on this standard, though now it embodies Walach Harkon's savage battle lust.
It is best to bring blood into battle, for one can't *always* indulge a fresh feast.
When walking openly amongst enemies, it is best to go unnoticed.
Three-eyed flies crawl in and out of this seemingly solid talisman, carrying Nurgle’s blessings far and wide.
This nasty little saw-toothed sickle hacks a gory swathe through the adversary's meagre ranks, whilst gifting disease resistance to his own.
A mark of her domination over the City of Vampires, the largest ruby of Neferata's diadem pulses with the power of eternal life and near-limitless energy.
An assembly of all our latest information on the Vermintide and their plans. This can be used to help us in the fight against their Under-Cities!
Whether you have to wade through swamps, plough through jungles or trudge across deserts, this pair of trusty boots will get you where you need to go.
These pieces of refined Warpstone boost the Grey Seer's already-impressive, almost-excessive casting abilities even further.
While the Graf is busy leading, someone must do all of the reading.
The most devout Ulricans know all the best ways to wound the forces of Chaos.
Leave seafaring to the peasants and chivalry to the nobles.
Few publishing houses have the reach, or the respect, of the renowned Altdorf University Press.
At first, the souls of the newly slain are drawn to an enticing glow. As it grows into a lurid glare, they fall at the mercy of the daemonic entity at its core.
Take the surplus, highborn. The worst that happens is you feed a few corpses to the Cold Ones before returning to Naggaroth.
The most talented singers and musicians, the fleetest and most graceful – above all, the most loyal.
The finest performers in Ulthuan yearn for a patron in Eataine. The proudest of nobles flock to hear them play.
Ursun is firstly a god of Bears, and only distantly second a god of Men.
Skill gained at immense personal risk is a mark of prestige among all the Dawi.
Few Packmasters survive long enough to learn the knack of goading Hell Pit Abominations into battle. That this one has says all you need to know…
A mammoth can carry a surprising amount of loot.
Experienced raiders know all the places that treasure might hide.
Gather round, slugs, and hear a tale of the Maggot Lord…
A healthy disease requires nurture and care, just like any other delicate crop.
Because cutting them off is only half the battle.
The revels can stop when everyone is dead.
All fall before the offerings of Slaanesh.
A frontal attack is the fool’s way. It is the coward’s way.
A Daemon archivist can retrieve tomes you did not even realise you had.
It’s a litle fing I like to call finkin’.
Designed by the Old Ones to stave off cold and heat, the cloak turns every exhausting march into a pleasant stroll.
Spawned when the world was still hot, this venerable Saurus is no longer the battlefield force he once was – but his wisdom is worth a hundred maces.
Bloab's Maggoth drips in slime and cankerous sores, threatening to vomit forth a torrent of toxic acid to melt any unlucky foe in its path.
With flesh muscled, pale and rotting, and a maw filled with vicious prehensile tongues, Twiceborn’s Daemon-beast is a hulking, monstrous battlefield predator.
A horrid Daemon-beast, forcibly tamed by the Bastard King himself, ridden into battle to bring Ruin to Grandfather Nurgle's victims.
A bat-winged monstrosity of his own construction, Helsnicht's flying mount is proof that necromancy's sweeping madness breeds its own species of morbid creativity.
Thanquol's mighty Rat-Ogre bodyguard, further augmented with burning Warpstone wrecking balls that strike and crush with meteoric impact.
Enhanced with flesh-science, Boneripper carries twin Warpfire Projectors that can immolate entire regiments with a single blast.
Animated by Dark Magic, a zombie dragon is an unholy parody of a once-noble beast now borne aloft by great tattered wings, its body covered with thick, withered hide.
Equpping this Follower to an army will enable Possession, which allows The Nameless to take control of enemy units in the pre battle screen.
Rumour has it, he counts more than just beans.
It’s their job to gather up the scrag ends the butchers miss. And if they don’t rustle up quite enough to fill the pot, well, a bit of Gnoblar will bulk things out just nicely.
Cook it slow, ‘til the last of the meat slides off the bone.
Warriors fighting under the Shadow Banner find themselves imbued with something of their rightful king’s merciless skill and stealth.
An artefact of power crafted in a land whose history ran deeper even than that of Nehekhara. It carries the power of all things ancient and undying.
The master shall not be touched until the Herald falls. And the Herald *will* not fall.
The seed of unlife which blooms inside every Vampire has been frozen in perpetuity. It bears its bloody fruit without fail.
This rusted talisman typifies Gutrot's command, spreading Nurgle's strength and cursing the enemy with unsteadiness, their senses roiling like the Sea of Claws in a squall.
Powerful spells of repulsion and attraction send missiles flying everywhere but at this talisman’s wearer.
Ulric shows no sympathy for frail bodies or lack of character in adversity – good, then, that the men under the Standard of the White Wolf have neither.
Made in the image of a skull-carapaced khepra beetle, this talisman surrounds the wearer with the protective energies of Usirian, god of the Underworld.
Faint whispers permeate the trinket... or maybe it's just Thanquol talking to himself.
Though seemingly something one might flaunt at a noble soiree, these harden their wearer's form.
With the viscera carefully removed, the body will endure forever in the Realm of Souls.
His family has served the Elector of Sylvania for over seven hundred years.
The dead are first collected, then prodded off the cart as they arrive at their destination.
I shall be in the library, master.
Untutored she may be, but this hedge magician has a curious way with spirits.
Pain is what persuades all to yield before death.
A blade once made for sacrifice… that still thirsts for mortal blood.
When the Black Axe of Krell bites into flesh, it leaves behind jagged shards that swiftly eat their way into the victim's heart.
With this sword Walach killed the mortal Order of the Blood Dragons and recreated them in his image. Its appearance speaks of an inexorable thirst for ruin and humiliation.
Neither size nor stature is an impediment to the butcher who bears this savage polearm on the fields of bloody carnage.
A symbol of the cycle of life and death, Nurgle's faithful look to it and are empowered.
When the blade wakes, it seeks only the greatest hosts for Bloab's virulent plagues.
Encrusted with bile and pus, Otto's plague-carrying scythe cuts down foes as easily as it reaps the harvest.
One cut is enough to open a wound most grievous.
This weapon has slain many a monstrous beast, its pitted edge retaining the vile blood of the creatures slain.
An icon of the Great Horned Rat crowns this blackened stave, a grim testament to its wielder’s arcane might and divine authority.
The Storm Hammer is made of dense meteoric iron, enchanted to allow it to be wielded as easily as a normal weapon. Its massive impact can send foes reeling or smash them to the ground.
Rusted axes, fashioned from the fetor of Nurgle's Garden, whose foul essence infects their bite with unrelenting Daemonic strength.
Death may not be brought immediately, but the pursuit lasts no longer than it takes for this blade to meet its mark.
For mortal beings so accustomed to seeing death in a blade, no blade has ever shown it better, for it *is* Death.
A gnawing sense of wrongness emanates from this stone, a constant when the Winds of Magic threaten to carry all away.
Famous for his loud voice and total contempt for all Gnoblars, Bannaga's invention causes a line of explosions to clear the foe from the bearer's path.
A skull-shaped chalice that promises salvation, or death...
A relic of the great Astromancer Po Mei, this enchanted cloak grants its wearer exceptional magical strength and mastery over one of the Elemental Winds.
A gift to Tsar Uriy from his wife, this exquisitely enamelled and bejewelled blown Frost Wyrm egg was the final and greatest masterwork of legendary jeweller Gastuva.

A tome of immense necromantic power, forged by W'soran, one of the first vampires. The profane words etched upon its pages grant the reader dreadful visions of a world where all life has withered, and only the Lands of the Dead remain.
Grut the Bloodthirsty's culinary malevolence seems to live on in his rusty sickle, which gives the Butcher greater command over the Winds, but at a cost to his own health.
Rumoured once to have belonged to Skrag the Slaughterer, this book is the lone remnant of the Halfling Wars, used by Butchers when practicing the more unpalatable aspects of Gut Magic.
By forcing this ichor-soaked, Ruin-imbued heart of a foul Chaos Spawn down, the Butcher may create a vortex of magical anarchy that beguiles magic-using adversaries.
Amber is the colour of beasts. Such magic can ensnare and entrap animals much more easily than so-called "intelligent" species.
Spellcasters who practise Death Magic can channel the life force of foes into their spells.
Fire feeds fire, two blazes together are stronger and hotter than two apart.
Spells from the Lore of Heavens manipulate the ethers of the skies, buffeting and pummelling winged creatures.
Even the simplest of spells can bring forth the full bloom of renewal, reinvigorating and healing the broken and bleeding.
Light Magic excels at the scourging of the supernatural, be they Daemons and creatures of Chaos, or the unquiet dead.
Armour is little defence against a skilled alchemist, under his command metal turns into an arcane lightning rod, attracting hostile magic.
A conjured shadow is just as obfuscating as a real one - the Shadow Wizard is master or mistress of the 'concealing' arts.
When activated, this strange, extra-worldly artefact from the broken lands around the Great Maw greatly increases the power of friendly Wizards' spells.
A hand mirror fashioned from flawless ice, with an intricate frame of frostwork, will reflect the foe's violence back on himself.
Necromancers and Vampires alike will often take to writing their skills and experience into grimoires and tomes, which will often then be combined into great compendiums of untold power.
This colourless crystal splits and intensifies light that falls upon it, twisting it into dazzling and unsettling hues that further empower the spellcaster in combat.
A big stick is a useful implement, especially when it can command the obedience of the enemy as well as your own troops.
This crystal shaft can transform a feeble wielder of magic into a brawny hero for a time, but with Tzeentch there is always a price to be paid...
These ancient relics chart the stars over Cathay for centuries to come and are able to help their users predict the future.
Ropes, wood, hair, iron nails and hide are twisted into a hideous ritual mask infused with the fears of the Ogres' defeated foes.
Apparently a simple pendant in the shape of a snowflake, it constantly changes its form, adopting a new and unique shape each time.
Kairos lives apart from the flow of time. Thus, he does not easily succumb to ill-fortune, for fate can easily be altered if one has the proper knowledge.
Created by the Jade Dragon Yuan Bo, this enchanted staff has the power to manipulate the Elemental Winds themselves, causing them to blow stronger or weaker on command.
When the pendulum swings, the foe's spellcasters find themselves powerless and magically impotent.
Krysothos is gone now, bound to a feathered grimoire, but his bones linger still and steal magic whenever they can – magic that their wielder can harness to his own ends.
A dissonant cry for battle emanates from this war gear, betokening an eerie anomaly in the sorcery that empowered it.
Clad in bale-forged armour laden with runes of slaughter and carnage, the Daemon's hide is all but immune to the blows of mortal men.
This suit of ancient scale carries with it the blessing of the Bear-God, allowing the wearer to shrug off blows that would fell an ox and fortifying their strength.
This harness' scales and plates have been wrought to the delicacy and gossamer weight of silk, yet are somehow the stronger for it.
The writhing thorns and brambles of this armour work their way into the bearer's surroundings, rendering them invisible to all but the most observant foe.
A heavy-duty gut-plate with two sharp curving horns jutting out, wrenched from the skull of a mighty cave-beast. The ground itself shakes when the bearer makes a bull charge.
A solid hunk of wood between you and the enemy provides both protection and confidence.
This cloak scintillates with the colours of nearby leaves, making the wearer's location nearly impossible to discern.
Worn only by Kislev's greatest warriors, this embossed plate harness is inset with frost shards harder and more pure than diamonds.
With no obvious joints this armour makes no apparent sense, but when did the powers of Chaos care for such details?
A mighty greatcloak fashioned from the pelt of a gigantic bear, the fur so thick as to be almost impenetrable.
This ancient, tattooed cave-beast skull, worn as a gut-plate, bleeds hostility and confusion into the minds of any who would do its bearer magical harm.
This polished brass gut-plate has a set of huge silver jaws attached to it that swallow the bearer's kills and pass them straight into the Great Maw. Their lifeforce passed to the wearer in return.
To those who don the Helm of Draesca comes untold power, yet a sorry fate also awaits…
Fashioned from scales of super-dense ice hewn from a glacial core and fashioned into a suit of black mail from which emanates a numbing cold.
Blows struck against its infinitely fine ceramic layers dislodge the uppermost one, leaving the assailant off-balance and wide open for a counter-thrust.
A solid cap that hides a hidden compartment, it smells faintly of loamy Talabecland dirt.
Forged by the Chaos Dwarfs in exchange for hundreds of Human and Gnoblar slaves, this great set of plates and chainmail shifts and hardens in response to incoming attacks.
Blows aimed at this armour's wearer are not blocked by it. Somehow, they never even connect…
The baleful enchantments of this ebony armour rob all nearby magical artifacts of their power.
A simple Peg Leg, you're not sure who this belonged to...
A simple Peg Leg, you're still not sure who this belonged to, but it does seem to bring you luck.
An armour piece once worn by the infamous pirate Dastan Coldeye.
Its iridescent alloy plates flow fluidly over one another, lending power and grace to the wearer, yet hardening instantaneously at the point of contact.
Surprisingly lightweight considering its bulk, and somehow containing everything under the sun from which to fashion bolts, bullets, shells and more.
Laced with Warpstone dust, this robe's black silk is constantly in motion, as if worried by a ceaseless furnace wind, so it is often difficult to make out what is robe and what is wearer.
Fashioned from scales of the Celestial Dragon himself, this armour is worn only by the greatest Cathayan heroes, that they may resist blows and traverse terrain without impediment.
A shield polished to such a degree that it reflects almost anything, be it a weapon’s blow or the metaphysical force of an enemy spell.
Once borne by a great hero of the Motherland, such is the reverence in which this shield is held that men willingly lay down their lives to protect its bearer.
Carved from a section of the Great Bastion, this massive stone and iron shield is enchanted so a hero might carry it into battle. When planted in the ground it offers unequalled protection.
Made for the Khan-Queens in ages past, this swirling mist of ice and crystals surrounds the Tzarina, protecting her from harm.
There can be few things as unnerving as watching your weapon pass through your opponent without any obvious effect.
Its surface alive with coruscating patterns, many attacks against the wearer of this harness somehow never happen.
An ancient heirloom fashioned in the mists of time using techniques long lost. Blows slide from its slick surfaces, leaving no mark.
Topped by a strange skull icon that grins with the confidence of victory, this standard imbues blessings of tireless war.
A faint whisper emanates an unspeakable word, cursing the armour and shields of those who dare bring the Nehekharans to war.
Just as the foul-tempered Necrotects whipped the thralls of old, so too do the sandstorms lash the wretches across the domain of the Faceless God.
The oath of vengeance Settra swore upon defilers and their fleeting domains is all-encompassing, its lingering sorcery felt most keenly upon the sullen wastes.
The arcane power of this stylised icon of the unblinking eye infuses the unit that carries it, hastening the release of their arrows and missiles.
The Mortuary Cult reveres the carrion-winged stalkers, believing these avians are agents of the vulture-headed god from whose shadow patience is learned.
While the blade is short, the jewels embedded in its hilt are said to be worth a thousand Caravans.
The skull seeps a constant icy mist concealing those that hold it.
A rare necklace fashioned by the Ice Court, imbued with its magic.
One of the princes has granted ownership and tithes from a patch of Tilean land.
A gift from the Gryphon Legion, famed for selling their might around the world.
This lens is fashioned and enchanted by the acolytes of Altdorf’s Light College.
This mantle is said to retain the heat of Elena’s fiery passion and her indomitable will to succeed despite the most grievous of injuries.
This is some kind of relic-cypher, a key to understanding the ancient lore of the Sky Titans.
A spy of the Magritta courts will furnish the Caravan Master with intelligence when possible.
The statues that line the great road into Zharr-Naggrund are said to be petrified Sorcerers.
An heirloom of the infamous Von Carstein family, it holds unholy power.
The greedy burgomeisters of Marienburg are keen to establish a trade relationship.
To be a Cathayan alchemist afore the disapproving masses takes a thick skin, but the reddish liquid within this phial goes far beyond that.
The fighting prowess of Cathay's greatest can be taken in draught form when a further burst of aggression is needed to tip the balance in the Celestial Emperor's favour.
This concoction enables the taker to not just wound their opponent, but set deadly poison in the lacerated flesh as well.
A sorcerous object created in the House of Secrets of Shang-Yang, it gifts the wearer with knowledge of Iron Dragon's alchemical secrets.
The ability to trap the Winds of Magic provides immense opportunity, be it for good or bad.
Most men spend their allotted days barely looking beyond the end of their noses. This instrument gives one an enlightening glimpse of infinity.
The bearer's fingers move over its strings of their own accord, weaving a rousing tune to inspire Dazh's warrior consorts as they do their deadly work.
A fragment of Khorne's blood-soaked realm, this dark, red-veined rock bulges and pulses with Daemon blood until Bloodletters burst forth to do his vicious bidding.
All eight Burning Books of Khorne, combined into a single all-powerful collection. Khorne's gaze is never far from these infernal grimoires.
The first and second volumes of the eight Burning Books of Khorne. Bound in brass and etched with blood, these grimoires contain all manner of knowledge and power.
The third and fourth volumes of the eight Burning Books of Khorne. Bound in brass and etched with blood, these grimoires contain all manner of knowledge and power.
The fifth and sixth volumes of the eight Burning Books of Khorne. Bound in brass and etched with blood, these grimoires contain all manner of knowledge and power.
The seventh and eighth volumes of the eight Burning Books of Khorne. Bound in brass and etched with blood, these grimoires contain all manner of knowledge and power.
This effigy depicts one of the thousand gods worshipped in far-off Ind. For reasons unknown it holds a particular horror for worshippers of the Dark Gods.
Those caught in the kiln's ambit find themselves not only seared and scorched, but any resistance to fire they may have is weakened considerably.
Skrag's cauldron has become a tool by which the former Slaughtermaster makes blessed offerings to his ravenous god.
Sight of the robe reminds those close to it that they fight for the forces of harmony and order.
The Moon Empress watches the Dragon River and her power infuses its waters.
Its loose folds perfectly mimic the play of moonlight and shadow, and the soft whisper of its lining is as the wind across the paddy field.
A golden coin bearing the markings of Ranald, surely this will bring luck and good tidings.
When thrown at the foe, the sputtering, unquenchable fluid within this porcelain ball sticks to their skin, quickly burning through it with a savage intensity.

In the east, Chaos Daemons are hunted and bled into lead jars. Butchers use this acidic ichor for warpaint, capturing their former owner's ferocity to give their Tyrants a truly terrifying appearance.
This skull, filled with Nurgle's most virulent poxes and sealed with blood-laced wax, explodes when thrown at the enemy, showering them in filthy pus and rot.
A dark, syrupy vintage truly unlike any other.
The strongest, most captivating scent distracts the foe from the bloody business at hand, slowing them and weakening their attack.
Who doesn't like a drink? No one you want to be fighting alongside, that's who!
A Magister can issue complex orders with a wave of his fan. This enchanted example can also send false signals to the enemy, sowing confusion.
Ogres don't believe in declaring their leadership qualities via trinkets, but that doesn't mean they're above robbing the dead if it inspires their forces to push even harder.
This silvery pelt is all that remains of a skinned Yhetee Greyback, hunted and killed by the wearer. It imbues some of the ice creatures' power into its owner.
The Spirit Dragon is a mysterious entity, never seen yet capable of lending aid in many subtle ways.
If not for its potent magics, only the most superstitious would bother dragging such a monumentally large stone idol around with them.
A living statue crafted from a block of jade, the lion is a conduit for sorcery and can improve the morale of any friendly troops in its vicinity.
Fashioned from a single block of jade, this flask can capture the essence of the bearer's soul in the event of it being separated from their corporeal body.
Made from a section of the actual hide of the Luan bird familiar of the founding Master of the Celestial Temple, this kite deals with airborne enemies most effectively.
A map detailing many lesser known pathways, that may or may not get you lost…
The scrolls text is far too complex to decipher in its entirety, it would take lifetimes to fully understand its secrets. Though anyone willing to try would surely learn much simply from trying.
For one who spends weeks, months or even years in the wild, a layman’s receptacle will simply not suffice.
In death there exists the time to live many different lives.
Having gouged out one of his eyes and cast it into the Great Maw, an Ogre may fit a pebble from the ground around the pit to give himself second sight.
The beloved Saint Annushka met her end rescuing an infant from a frozen lake. This relic from her beatified remains heals and restores its user's body.
The remnants of two rare items that have failed to fuse together. Better luck next time!
By utilising the scrap from items that have previously failed to fuse we may eventually be able to create something unique.
A map showing certain pathways throughout the Under-Empire that will help locate Skaven Under-Cities.
I'm pretty sure that bush is a Greenskin actually.\\n"What makes you say that sir?"\\n"It's got big green legs..."
Taken from an unknown but clearly massive beast, this horn has been handed from father to eldest son through generations of Kislev's pre-eminent family of beast hunters.
Inked upon these pages are the fundamental secrets of the Winds of Chaos. Alas, the grimoire is a fickle and mischievous Daemon, little given to co-operation.
The mad mage M'kar's plans to lure Daemons to his service eventually went awry. Though the glyph has been seen many times since, its creator seems to have vanished…
So long as a single stone remains, the ageless Inevitable City shall always rebuild itself.
Listen closely, little brother, for here is wisdom plain.
Expert murder by surprise and stealth ensures the foe will never know what hit them, or why.
In many ways, the holder of true power is the one who has the keys to the kingdom literally within their hands.
This disciplined brother is devoted to his order's ways of meditation and chant, so that harmony may be felt across the Dragon Empire.
This loving steward is from the north of Cathay, where the finest steeds can be found and tamed.
There are calming words that can turn unbridled rage to placid compliance. This one knows them all.
The likeness of the Guardian Lion, perfectly graven from this most desirable of materials, and imbued with its rage and power.
The finest cloth and spice, but only for those of high status of course.
Delivering information to major players means the conveyor will know what is going on and may also be in the right place at the right time, which could advance their career.
No problem, boss. Just point me at 'em and give da word... 'Kill!' is a good one, now I fink of it.
Humble they may be, but such work is essential to the running of a great empire such as Cathay.
This one has been trained the incantations needed to unlock the secrets of the Terracotta Sentinels, that they may always be primed and ready to strike.
This one's fingers move as delicately as worms who make the silk with which they work.
More than a skill, sword mastery is an art that must be practiced to perfection if the foe is to be rended.
Unpopular they may be, but the Dragon Empire's greatness and stature is paid for through the fruits of citizens' labour.
Come, sit a while upon the carpet and partake of this ceremony.
The deadly water-snakes are bred for their size, speed and poisonous venom that can fell a Giant in an instant.
Who is it that ensures conflict, war and destruction are only ever a breath away? Naturally, it is the Blood God.
This one's thirst for violence is so great that he need not rest or sup between bouts to the gory death.
Fortunately, as long as there are mortals, there will be flesh and blood for the God of Murder.
Every skull and tooth must be accounted for.
Again! Blood for the Blood God! Feel his wrath eternal!
This disciple of Khorne wears a substantial armour carapace – as much to protect themselves from their charges as from the foe.
Remember you must kill… and kill and kill and KILL!
With every passing year they become more beast than man, meaning every evil and twisted attribute grows exponentially.
You can never have too much slaughter, for Kharneth's rage and bloodlust never ends.
Life, death… what else is there? Plunder, that's what. And the promise of divine reward.
When Arkhar and the Hound join as one, there is no bloody prize that cannot be obtained.
This one enjoyed his job so much that he took it home with him, attracting the attention of the Hunter of Souls in the process.
Khorne cares not for anything but the burning hatred that leads to a frenzy of violence and bloodletting, for it is from this that he draws his power.
The agents of the Tzarina cannot be everywhere at once.
This man deals with the day to day running of his employer's stanitsa, ensuring everything – and everyone – works properly.
One day, they hope, it may be their honour to wield the blade, rather than simply fetch it.
This one's father has entrusted their martial education to a great warrior of the Motherland.
Kislev's favourite drink is the sour milk known as kvas, meaning that its makers' status is higher than it might otherwise have been.
The nomadic peoples of the north-eastern steppes are expert horsemen and masters of fighting in the saddle.
Observe the rituals and you shall be blessed and worthy of this great Motherland.
The Crow, the Hound, the Serpent, and the Vulture were jealous of King Taal, and had tried to use the Great Gates to take what was His… They failed.
The gods are great, but only a fool would trust them with his life. Follow Father Bear instead.
The Orthodoxy shall be obeyed in all matters, especially when the alternative is summary execution.
Those who scrape a living tending livestock on the steppes know the warning signs of an invading force, and can give fair warning to the authorities.
It's a dirty job that no one wants to do, but nevertheless must be done, lest the state fall into penury.
Let me tell you a tale of the last time the Dark Gods invaded the Motherland. That was a fight to behold…
This'll put hairs on… well, everywhere you can grow hairs, and several places you can’t, most probably!
Clad in gold and feathers and anointed in sacred oils, his every step echoes with the stirring of long-dormant spawning pools.
Who ensures that noble-born mortals fall to corrupt decay and Ruin? Why, it is their loving Grandfather…
Although war is not something that Nurgle feels strongly about for its own sake, as a tool for spreading infection and disease there is nothing better.
Elevated even among his yucky and repellent kin, this particularly vile Nurgling is especially beloved of Grandfather for his bubo-bursting talents.
How many Plaguebearers? How many plagues? How many hosts? How many boils and weeping pustules? The Urfather must know…
This skilled pharmacist mixes potions and preparations to ensure the Plague Lord's disgusting agenda is fulfilled.
This insect enthusiast has great love for the tiny creatures that multiply and swarm across the world, spreading sickness and plague wherever they go.
Although a pariah to the healthy, this one is blessed with the most putrid lesions and membranes imaginable, marking him out as a leader among his kind.
It might look like a common toad, but if you listen carefully, you may hear the words of the Fly Lord himself, uttering whispers of corrupt decay.
Cut a caper, man, your bladder – yes, of course I mean your own bladder, and intestines too!
What it once was, who can say? Now, however, this festering pile of pus and rot has been gifted many boons by the Lord of Pestilence.
Buboes, phlegm, blood and guts! Boils, bogeys, rot and pus! Blisters, fevers, weeping sores! From your wounds the fester pours.
There, my lord. Your skin is... love, to me. Your disease is lovingly cared for, for all eternity.
Nurgle's rotten, mildew-covered hulks must be steered to new shores, that his glorious gifts be delivered to new lands and populations.
This one is skilled in the art of making and administering preparations to envenom, debase and deform, according to the Urfather's myriad wonts.
All mankind, be they the richest noble or the poorest peasant, are susceptible to Grandfather's maladious caresses, and he loves each and every one with equal measure.
Medicines are for the birds, they only make you worse. The physic must line his purse first and foremost, remember. That's what it's all about really…
This Ogre has been given the job of crafting bespoke armour pieces and a variety of nasty gouging weapons for the tribe's elite.
When it's time for a Great Feast, the loudest Ogre has the honour of carrying their Mawtooth and placing it in position around the pit.
Ogre beer is a foul, viscous concoction, made with equal quantities of honeycomb and hornet, and intoxicating enough to hospitalise a Dwarf.
This one tells swaggering tales of great bravado, some of them true, all of them exaggerated, in order to inspire the tribe.
In lieu of a proper written language or indeed any level of basic literacy, the Tyrant's achievements are immortalised in pictures on the walls of caves.
See this 'ere helmet? 'Twas a gift from a geezer I worked for in eggs-otick Caf-fay, right before I ate 'im.
This Bruiser is there to ensure that the Tyrant's line is toed and that tribal matters run smoothly… using extreme violence, naturally.
Gnoblars are stupid, but this one has shown the faintest spark of intelligence, so has been promoted above his peers.
What if we constructed a giant, wooden… Giant, master?
This Gnoblar has shown some ability in managing the tribe's purse – if he can keep his fingers out of it he may even live out the year!
This one knows that he'd better come up with some top grub if he wants to avoid becoming a light snack!
The tribe huddle around a crudely-dug pit to watch two of their best gut-barge, face-crack and fist-splinter it out until one of them either submits or dies.
Ogre negotiations are simple: give them what they want or expect their captive to be sent back one piece at a time.
Looking after the colossal, lumbering Rhinoxen is often just a matter of moving out of the way quickly enough to avoid a goring.
Haha, run! Yer eight legs aren't gonna save yer tho, 'cos yer due a good roastin'!
Anyone stupid enough to attempt to cow, or even converse, with these savage relatives deserves their extra share of the loot or grub.
Direct from Slaanesh’s personal coterie of fawners, this Daemonic lickspittle will act as your Herald and devout flatterer. Whatever he says comes true.
Who ensures that the great and the good fall to depravity and lust? Who else but the Lord of Excess…
Let's play again. What do you say to a small wager, just to make things… interesting?
A most beautiful and desirable lady of distinction, whose clients are among society's noblest men and women.
The serpent writhes in knowledge for rebellion and heresy.
Every society, and especially the most secret, requires a careful hand to count subs and guard its secrets from discovery.
Say my name! Say it! Your ecstatic moans will fill the sky, worm!
Come on, sir, 'tis only wafer thin…
Whatever mortal beings desire, whatever their pleasure… Nothing is off limits or out of reach.
Another slice of swan, my friend? Do please indulge, for it really is the finest bird, and roasted beyond perfection!
The adagio will tear your heart out.
Their brushstrokes are so delicate they can make a mortal weep tears of ecstatic joy.
The subtlest temptations can be found within the lyrical beauty of verse.
What matter vows and promises, unless they are made to the Perfect Prince by way of pact?
A third breast, adorned with a dozen golden nipples? Well, I am sure we can find a use for them in time…
Indulgence and desire are the only things that matter in this world. Without pleasure, why live at all?
The ultimate servant – versed in six thousand techniques of desire – is ready to provide pleasure or agony upon you or your foe.
Who really pulls the strings in the courts of the mighty? It is the Changer of Ways, of course…
Although it is unlikely that base metals can be turned into gold without magical help, alchemy remains an example of the strive for Change, which is meat and drink to the Raven.
Karl Franz! He's not the real Karl Franz, you know – they've replaced him with a doppelganger!
No-one can hold all of the Raven's plans in their weak mind, but this one is an expert in code that obscures the details from the wrong kind of reader.
The boredom of many young nobles' lives can lead them to test their boundaries – a word here, a suggestion there; planting seeds of doubt. The Conspirator is exultant.
Whatever you think this one is, they are not. Whatever they speak of, the opposite will be true.
I learned this one in Skeggi – take a seat, I'll teach you how to play. You won't want it to end, trust me.
Where there's a wind, there's very definitely a way.
It’s a good thing to train a successor ahead of the time when one will be elevated to Daemonhood.
The power to make one being betray their allies or even their kin is true power indeed, with Tchar ever the victor.
There's a trap behind this trap that would be a joy to spring!
Not every bird of fancy is simply that; some enable the Changer to converse with his servants.
If you look closely, this one's blue and yellow whiskers are actually a fine beard of feathers.
Without Change, something sleeps inside us… and seldom awakens…
Change is inevitable. It is foolish to fight it! Embrace the Conspirator's knowledge and grow strong!
The web they weave is no ordinary tapestry, but instead a map of mortal minds and immortal strategies.
For many long years, they have ensured the lair remains secret and safe from all trespassers. The lair may no longer need it, but their awoken master does.
A Vampire's inert form may grow ravenous beyond control should their body not receive the proper blood ministrations. Certain mad necromantic adepts clamour for such opportunities.
A dormant Vampire's essence may become a target of arcane malice - or irrevocably fester into something terrifying. Their powerful servants ensure that it does not happen.
A Vampire’s bounty must not stop growing in their temporary absence. Those who have satisfied this necessity stand ready to prove their usefulness when their master awakens.
A Vampire's living thralls and undead servants may cower and follow their master without question, but dormancy weakens such bonds - unless someone is on hand to maintain them.
Necromancers are always alert to those who would thwart their secretive designs. Some, however, wander the area around a Vampire's lair to turn other ill-wishers' secretive designs against them.

This standard fills Slaaneshi Daemons with such euphoria that they care not whether the battle is won or lost, provided there are still bodies to caress.
An ancient banner doused in the sorcerous power of the Dragon Emperor himself, granting strength and protection.
This standard is woven from the wrath of the Chaos Gods, and can unleash their fiery fury directly at the enemies of Ruin.
Blessed by the Grand Patriarch himself, this torn cloth scrap is a potent symbol of Mother Kislev's unbending defiance in the face of insurmountable odds.
Those that loose their arrows under this banner blessed by the Empress gain unerring accuracy.
The Moon Empress sets her own conventions. Chief amongst these is the ability to pass without being noticed whenever she chooses…
Warded with sanctioned and divine prayer, this banner grants spirit and will to the Kislevites who fight under it.
Rays of dark light shimmer about this standard, scoring scenes from a thousand-thousand of Ruinous victories upon the flesh of its bearer's opponents.

The hungry servants who feast under this banner are blessed with an eternal craving.

All who look upon this unholy standard see their innermost fears reflected upon its ragged cloth, which greatly affects their will to persevere.

This brass standard constantly drips blood, the smell of which quickly drives all of Khorne's followers mad with battle-lust.

The runes upon this banner seem to swirl and distort with each passing second, constantly seeking the ideal configuration to capture magical energies.
This grisly keepsake is a small skull that constantly weeps blood, but the recipient will always have the Blood God’s approval.
A banner said to leech the very essence of life from enemies close by.
A crude yet inspiring patchwork of banners taken from every one of the mortal races the tribe has encountered and subsequently had for dinner.
Knowing where one has come from can make the road ahead more obvious.

A Daemonic Siren is imprisoned in this banner, its seductive song dulling the senses of the foes that hear it.
The pole of this banner is thick-set with the captured skulls of Khorne's victims, each marked with a brass-etched rune of slaughter.
This banner constantly flickers in and out of existence, creating a tear in reality through which the power of the Dark Gods flows ever more strongly.

The colour of this banner seems to change to match the endless skies of the steppes, from empty blue to cold grey.

A phial of soil taken from the ground around the gates of Praag, infused with the blood of her heroic fallen defenders.
A finely crafted jet pendant, which protects against all forms of hostile magic.
Forged from the heat of Khorne's rage at the very foot of the Blood God's throne, this collar's contains a splinter of his fury against the sorcerous.
Having soaked up the celestial energy left by the birth of the Dragon Emperor, this stone protect its bearer but can also unleash sorcerous energy when struck.
Captured within the depths of this necklace is the power to change destiny.
Fault lines run through the stone of this eery bracelet and extend on into the surrounding world.
A quick pass over a corpse with this stone will quickly stick any item of any importance firmly to it.
This ancient, near-sentient gauntlet is painted to resemble the Great Maw itself, with a black palm and Sabretusk teeth tied to the fingers and thumbs.
Heartwood recognises itself, and provides its holder a measure of protection against sudden rains of arrows.
When magic is in the air, this amulet glows with a steady and reassuring yellow-green light, lending strength and fortitude to its wearer's mind.
Though fashioned from a flawless piece of jade, most who gaze upon this pendant soon find themselves looking away in discomfort.
Light fails to reflect normally from this amulet, and when struck by magic it remains undamaged, even as the arcane energies dissipate.
Sometimes the greatest sensation can be derived from the denial of the same in another.
When you're trying to a hit an angry speck on the horizon, luck must take some small part.
This enchanted, basin-sized crown was forged by artisans of the Empire for a king's ransom in gold, and is said to increase Overtyrant's intellect to near-human levels.
A fabled Sea Shanty of the Vampire Coast, though bottled in glass it's aura is still potent.
In the presence of hostile magics, the mauve stone of this ring flashes and sends a delicious tingle to the wearer's very core.
Although once a finely-wrought gemstone bound into a silver filigree cone, it is now a dirt-encrusted, chipped remnant of its former glory, its defensive powers resisting powerful attacks.
Swung on tarnished chains, the ominous clouds belching from this obscene censer are of deadly fungal spores rather than smoke, clouding the stinging eyes of would-be assailants.
Smelted from a fallen star found on the snowy steppes, the metal of this ring is dark and cold.
Bestowed by Grandfather Nurgle to his favoured champions, this green-rimmed necklace of bronze is a promise of his protection.
What is unmaking but a shackle to bind a Daemon from following his rage?
Pulsing like a malign heart, its taproot questing for purchase, this disgusting object seeks to root itself in flesh.
Mirrors have the power to reflect and reverse. Mix in something of the Warp, and that which is reflected can encompass all manner of things.
This Wyrdstone shard has been bound into a crude necklace where it quietly and silently absorbs its bearer's lifeforce.
The final work of an ancient master-craftsman, this sword draws reverence from those lucky enough to see it even once. Its wielder is destined to be a legend who brings singing death in battle.
This enchanted bow transforms its arrows into live (and very unhappy) snakes. Take care to protect your arms!
This unholy blade screams with the power of the Daemon bound inside it – one eternally thirsty for the blood of mortals.
A bearded battle-axe with a blade wreathed in crackling lightning, befitting of Tor, God of Storms.
The merest touch of this massive befouled blade is fatal to all creatures, Daemon, mortal and Undead.
This weighty blade trembles with a portion of Khorne's boundless rage; its strike crushes not only flesh and armour, but the victim's very soul as well.
A shadow made manifest; a blade as cruel as its owner.
The hero Xen Wu is a controversial figure in the mythology of Grand Cathay. His exploits were legendary, but his methods were questionable.
The Bloodcleaver is a revolting, gore-encrusted hand weapon with the vampiric ability to channel the lifeforce from its victims into its wielder.
At the wielder's command, the teeth race down the blade, ripping apart armour and flesh as easily as if they were parchment. The beast-hilt howls while it does so and whines if left unsated.
One of two powerful Elven Runeswords, forged long ago with its sister sword {{tr:weapon_elthraician}}.
Apparently forged from a reflection of the dawning sun, its blade is highly reflective, making the light dance and flash to the rhythm of its deadly pattern.
A mace with a fiery head, blazing with the light of Dazh, God of Fire. Its touch reinvigorates tired warriors in the thick of battle.
This handgun bears the mark of Aqshy on its barrel, and scorches the hands of the holder; its effectiveness, however, is undeniable.
One of two powerful Elven Runeswords, forged long ago with its sister sword {{tr:weapon_cynatcian}}.
This weapon flickers in and out of reality at the Daemon's merest command, allowing it to bypass a foe's defences and cut into the soft flesh beneath.
The runes upon this brazen axe still glow from the heat of its forging upon Khorne's anvil.
A single blow landed with this truly deadly magic sword is enough to fell even mighty beasts.
The frost shard blade of this revered weapon sparkles with the cold, hard promise of sharp slaughter.
This blade of Gilellion the Lewd, champion of Slaanesh, traps its victims in immortal servitude to its bearer.
Razor-edged and honed on souls who have fallen in battle to the Blood God's own, this blade is consecrated to Khorne and the bloody task of slaughtering his enemies.
The gnarled and twisted limbs of this bow do nothing to hamper its uncanny precision.

A more deadly strain of the plague-ridden Nurglings that burst from Ku'gath's body. These creatures are particularly scabrous, spreading a necrotic toxin to everything they touch.

The traditional weapon of Empire Outriders unleashes a devastating armour piercing volley, though the reloading leaves something to be desired!
Said to belong to Barron von Heastie, the most infamous pirate to ever set sail.
This flail's heads are the shrunken skulls of plague victims, its chain crafted from knotted and desiccated entrails. Pestilence hangs heavy about it still, ever seeking to escape.
Balanced both to swing and to throw with equal bite.
This massive sceptre is ensorcelled with spells of might, imbuing Greasus with the strength of a Sky-Titan, as befits his status as the most powerful Ogre alive.
The metal of this blade is alloyed with a powerful venom; its merest touch is sufficient to lock a man's sinews rigid and stop his heart in the blink of an eye.
Its blade crafted from the Norscan glaciers and magically bound to remain forever frozen, when this mighty polearm strikes, the foe’s blood turns to ice.
A huge, two-handed obsidian club used by the Tyrant Bruto Thundergut to smash his way into the Skycastles thousands of years ago.
Every line and motion of this bow speaks to the grace of the Moon Empress who inspired its creation.
This blade of scales with a sharkskin hilt was borne from the deeps by a Norscan reaver in an age long past.
This heavy, spiked metal gauntlet was originally worn by Big Agi Skullplucker, who had a particular dislike for Elves and enjoyed nothing more than using it to twist off their girly little heads.
Less a string and more a knot of rope, enchanted using the Winds of Azyr. The bearer’s shots loose with staggering force to turn enemy shields.
The beatific sword of the Dark Prince, said to hold the sharpest edge in existence.
Each of these Daemonic axes contains a Bloodthirster's savage spirit, lending fury to Skarbrand's strikes.

The mere presence of this staff causes all natural things to cry out in pain as it reshapes the world according to the Daemon's whim.
Within this rod is bound the essence of a particularly loathsome Plague Daemon, who chortles with horrible delight when his pox-ridden power is unleashed upon a deserving foe.
Bartered by a chieftain for his tribesmen's souls who then double-crossed the Dark Gods, this spear, that can banish their servants, is all that remains.
The Burning Brazier holds a flame taken from the Temple of Ursun. The more wounded the wielder becomes, the hotter the fire burns, and more terrible is its flaming touch.
Present at every major battle since the dawn of time, this blade guarantees its owner great worldly renown as long as it consents to their will.
This glittering sword has been wielded by some of Kislev's greatest heroes throughout the ages, its freezing blade able to part the hardest of armour.
This massive two-ended club is so heavy even a normal Ogre Bull would struggle. Bound into its heads is the power to shatter a boulder with one strike.
When brought down over the head, the accumulated force of several hundred tonnes of masonry explodes outward from the point of impact.
This sword is coated with a paralysing venom, a dose of which renders the victim utterly immobile.
These ancient fighting claws are believed to be the pattern upon which the Akshina modelled their weapons.
A fine sword adorned with feathers from Cathay's Vermillion War Birds.
This sword's tempered ceramic blade has been fired to a brilliant white, intensifying the cutting edge to an incandescence which seems to shear the very light itself.
Forged in the molten heat of desire and cooled in a vat of Slaanesh's own blood, the Witstealer Sword was presented to the Arch-tempter by the Dark Prince himself.
This eminent sword has a long history of slaying monsters and beasts several times bigger than its wielder.
Its blade formed from the icy spike of a Frost Wyrm, this deadly rapier finds its mark unerringly.
Simply made, but strong and flexible for a comfortable draw.
Discharging a magical blast every time it is struck, Harry’s Bane Shield rebounds his enemies blows back from whence they came.
As if driven by an unstoppable force, Harry’s hammer is blessed by the gods to hurl back the bodies and souls of those he strikes.
Strong Kislevite iron is used to make this armour.
Worn only by Kislev's greatest warriors, this embossed plate harness is inset with frost shards harder and more pure than diamonds.

In a major metropolis, it's all too easy to end up with a knife in your back.
The lone Bounty Hunter can go places that ungainly military units cannot.
Many Kossars leave the constant wars of their homeland to become mercenaries and adventurers elsewhere.

Even a small amount of training can be the difference between life and death on the blood-soaked battlefields of the Old World.
Men fight better when their livelihood, not just their lives, is at stake.
Rob from the rich and give to the poor. That's the theory, anyway.
Experienced outdoorsmen who reconnoitre for armies, caravans, and other travelling parties. Life expectancy is short.
Professional bully wanted. Fair prices paid for beating the right people up.
Never do an honest day's work if you can avoid it.

Full-time, paid professionals to man the fortresses, patrol the borders, and repel invaders.

From history to anatomy to science to nothing more than the bottom of a bottle…

A halfling recruited in Erengrad. Every night he has managed to cook something edible with meagre rations, even if the Kvas barrels do keep getting lighter…
Sent with the expedition to map the lands far beyond Kislev's borders, should he return to the Motherland, the charts will be of great value.
The agents of the Tzarina cannot be everywhere at once.
This man deals with the day to day running of his employer's stanitsa, ensuring everything – and everyone – works properly.
One day, they hope, it may be their honour to wield the blade, rather than simply fetch it.
This one's father has entrusted their martial education to a great warrior of the Motherland.
The nomadic peoples of the north-eastern steppes are expert horsemen and masters of fighting in the saddle.
Observe the rituals and you shall be blessed and worthy of this great Motherland.
Those who scrape a living tending livestock on the steppes know the warning signs of an invading force, and can give fair warning to the authorities.
It's a dirty job that no one wants to do, but nevertheless must be done, lest the state fall into penury.
Let me tell you a tale of the last time the Dark Gods invaded the Motherland. That was a fight to behold…
A junior member of the Great Orthodoxy, not welcomed by the Ungols, he insisted on coming by Kostaltyn's order to look after the spiritual wellbeing of the troops.
An experienced scout, perhaps with Far-Northern blood in his veins, will be able to guide Yuri to Dervingard and beyond.
Not always liked by the troops, but his stinginess has made camp supplies last far longer than they should.
A clear crystal broach of purest clarity whose core dances with whirling white specks.
A phial of soil taken from the ground around the gates of Praag, infused with the blood of her heroic fallen defenders.
Smelted from a fallen star found on the snowy steppes, the metal of this ring is dark and cold.
The frost shard blade of this revered weapon sparkles with the cold, hard promise of sharp slaughter.
The sword known as Wolfbane, taken from Skollden, tainted by dark power.
