Tournament grounds can be found in most of the southern provinces as well as Bretonnia. Hedge Knights, freelancers, Knights of the Realm and even, occasionally, the Knightly Orders enter the competition. It is a carnival atmosphere, a time when commoner and noble alike mix to enjoy the spectacle of the jousts. It a rare moment of joy in a world beset with terrors.

In the godly pantheon, Taal is the older brother of Ulric, so the worshippers of both traditionally get on well. The gods themselves do also, according to the Al-Ulric and Taal High Priest. It is for this reason that where there is a shrine to Ulric, it's a sure bet there will be an unassuming, round abode decorated with antlers and animal skulls close by.

Temples to Taal are much rarer than his ubiquitous but humble shrines. There are a few, the largest of which can be found in the city that bears his name, Talabheim. There are monasteries also, but no true worshipper of the nature god would build such a lavish pile. Having said that, they have been known to take over such places if they have fallen into disuse - the most infamous example being La Maisontaal in Bretonnia.

While Dwarfs carve quays out of solid rock, the Orcs and Norse have little more than wooden planks that jut into the sea. Empire wharfs - including those in Sylvania - are generally much sturdier. Since much of their trade comes down the large rivers they need reliable platforms of timber and stone to enable their ships to dock.

There are many harbours in the Old World, as the nations oft use the large flowing rivers to transport goods from one place to another. Even the Empire's great inland cities have some kind of harbour for massive river barges to dock. The most famous of all harbours, perhaps, is in Barak Varr, the sea-gate of the Karaz Ankor.

Erengrad, Marienburg, Altdorf, Barak Varr, even the Orc pirate forts that riddle the coast by the Dragonback mountains are all built around or contain a series of ports. These are normally places that attract wealth, as they are great trading stations in those rare moments when there is a lull in the eternal war and also home to the fleet when it returns.

Shrines to the Goddess of War and Strategy are well-tended places, usually set near a fountain. In Tilea and Estalia the fountain and the likeness of Myrmidia – a beautiful young woman in warrior's garb – are one and the same; the fountain spouts from the top of the head, with water following the contours of her cape as an metaphor for shaping the fortunes of war with good strategy.

Under the stern eye of Myrmidia's ruling council, known as the Archecclesiastium, the temples of the war goddess, patron of soldiers, are kept in stern, disciplined, order. Tithes are collected and passed to the council, who then furnish the better performing temples with the finances required to make their domes and porticos grander still.

In the time before Sigmar, it was often customary for tribal Chieftains to be buried with their vast wealth, intending to impress their primitive gods in the afterlife. Such naivety has proven a boon for Dark Magic-users many centuries later, who have been able to summon these entombed warriors back to life and raid the ancient armouries within.

The old tribes would keep their most treasured items in reliquaries. It is a custom that has continued all the way through the history of the Empire, even the Grand Theogonist making use of sacred vaults underneath the Grand Temple. Even in Sylvania, old reliquaries installed by the Priests of Morr or Templars of Sigmar are used as weapon stashes against the Vampiric threat.

Balefire braziers are large corroded iron cages, burning with a bright, sickly hellfire. As the smoke billows outwards it spreads across the lands withering trees, scorching grass and drawing the buried dead closer to the surface. It is little wonder that Undead hosts leave such braziers in their wake, for the land will wither and more Undead will come.

The great hearths located in the main halls of the largest Sylvanian castles have belched out the black, green and acrid smoke of corruption for as long as the von Carsteins have ruled. Once built, the balefire within the heath blazes hot and sonorous, bathing the battlefield in acrid smoke. Soon, others were created, spreading Undeathly contagions across the suffering world.

Grave harridans - evil souls now stuck in the ether as Tomb Banshees - can often be found haunting their mortal abodes, where many sacrifices took place. These witch houses were built on places of dark power - maybe a ruined temple or a dark altar of an ancient cult. In its grate burns balefire that pumps out of the chimney to wither the lands.

Deep under the larger cemeteries and Morr's Gardens are cairns and crypts, labyrinthine catacombs where the bodies of noble families, dignitaries and important priests rest in eternal sleep. In Sylvania especially, such places are lost to darker creatures; things that may have once been human, generations ago, but have since devolved into bestial cannibals that feed on the dead.

Even modest practitioners of Dark Magic must be wary when summoning dark forces from within a circle of binding, for while Dark Magic is subtly different from the arcane lores dedicated to the Ruinous Powers, a wrong word or missed syllable can bring forth something even more dangerous than a Tomb Banshee.

When a Lodestone is placed inside a binding circle, and a Necromancer recites words that haven't been spoken since the Fall of Nehekhara, then the Wight Kings emerge from their burial mounds. Clad in the raiments of war, the wraiths leave their cairns and the Hexwraiths will gallop into existence, all drawn to the master that controls the lodestone.

Not every soul can be safety interned into a Garden of Morr. These cemeteries are bound by blessed walls, patrolled by Priests and warded against evil. Even then, such places can be defiled, their tombs robbed and corpses made into soulless puppets for dark masters. The poor are buried more mundanely or flung into charnel pits. Either way, their bodies may rise again as Zombies or Skeletons if left long enough for their flesh to slough away...

A powerful Necromancer or Vampire can call the long-dead back to serve him. Those buried in the Old World make excellent warriors - they fought in life and can do so again. No Zombies are found here for flesh has long since rotted away, there is just dust, bones, and a willingness to fight again. Summoning the Wight Kings requires more powerful rituals, for they retain their independence and are not easily controlled.

As well as being statements of wealth, power and status, the mausoleums of the rich and powerful were warded to keep the remains away from prowling ghouls or Dark Magic-users. Of course, in many cases such efforts are futile, for a Vampire is a determined creature with eternity to spare. Some of those within would have fought with, or even against, Sigmar - an irony not lost on the Undead.

Like much of the Empire, Sylvania is heavily wooded. Unlike other places though, the trees seem to crave blood. There are many tales of how a hut built too close to a copse was discovered to have a tree roots boring into the bodies of the unfortunates sleeping within. It's not just trees the smallfolk must be wary of, for in those sinister copses the fauna is as blood-hunger as the flora...

Sylvanians know not to venture into the woods. Even lumberjacks go only in large parties when wood is at its scarcest, and even then chopping down a tree could easily bring about a bloody retaliation. Of course, there are abyssal things there, even more terrifying than the trees themselves. Such things are sought by the Midnight Aristocracy, who wish to add them to their hordes.

The forests of Sylvania are perilous, their rotting canopies housing the deadliest creatures that roam the lands. Nowhere is more despised than Hunger Wood, a collection of briars and bogs to trap the unwary. Legends speak of a whole flock of Terrorgheists residing within its twisted boughs. Should a Vampire Lord find such a menagerie, he could become powerful enough to challenge the von Carsteins' throne.

Piles of cadavers are deposited by Corpse Carts in places that a Vampire or Necromancer wants watched. Occasionally, one or two corpses will pull themselves free from the mire of writhing limbs and shamble forth on a short patrol route before merging back into the pile - assuming there was nothing living to feed off.

Standing sentinel throughout Sylvania are watchtowers. At the top stand the vigilant Grave Guard, with yearning mouths always open and piercing red eyes that never close. The tower's inhabitants do not take such action just against the smallfolk, but any intruders and invaders that dare approach.

There are many prohibited volumes published and distributed throughout civilisation - some authored by heretics, others by Necromancers who wish to share their diabolical secrets. Even Nagash himself wrote nine tomes of power. Such books tend to be collected by dark archivists, ignorant of the lore they have gathered, or even Witch Hunters who retrieve these blasphemous tomes and store them for 'safekeeping'.

Necromancers usually start their careers in secret. As they delve into the dark arts, inevitably suspicion is raised as cadavers go missing, milk sours and ominous clouds gather. Some leave in search of a master before being ostracised, others are chased from their former lives. Once outed, a Necromancer will seek out another to continue his dread education, and a lair to continue his vile experiments.

In a world of unremitting war, a decent burial is something granted only to the few. For the remainder, a mass grave must suffice, with enough stones on top to deter wild beasts, and enough icons to draw down the blessing of the various gods of the dead. Alas, such charnel pits attract Necromancers and other dark sorcerers like, vultures to carrion.

Lichyards are may once have been gravesites but that use has long since been forgotten - now they are pits of the damned. Where fallen mausoleums are mashed together with desiccated limbs, broken, zombified parts that refuse to return inanimate, chittering skulls and piles upon piles of bone.

When a Priests of Morr perishes, his remains are treated with extreme reverence by his brethren and placed in a an ossuary, often located at the centre of a Garden of Morr. A Vampire Count that excavates such a find will be able to increase his Undead host quickly, as the remains are summoned to join them.

Gibbet cages can be found throughout Sylvania - indeed, much of the Old World uses this gruesome punishment for thieves, bandits and other criminals, and as a warning to others who might contemplate such malfeasance. In Sylvania, living is a crime and those that, having displeased the Vampire Counts, aren’t instantly torn to shreds or consumed may end up in a cage, on display as a stark warning, but also as a way of leeching lifeforce from the condemned. Their energy slowly drips away even as Zombies and carrion birds gather to nibble at the remains through the rusted iron bars.

Should brigands, Witch Hunters or the living tenants of Sylvania dare to rise against the Midnight Aristocracy, then those not fed to the Crypt Ghouls or given over to the Necromancers may well be sent to the gallows. Such grisly structures are often seen in Sylvania’s villages and decrepit townships, a sure sign of the Undead nobility’s hold over the area and of just how far the peasantry cursed to live in the area are from Sigmar’s light. Those sent to the gallows - a punishment for even the most minor of infractions - are escorted by hooded and gruesome executioners - who knows if they are living or dead servants of the von Carsteins? As sentences are carried out, and the living do their macabre jigs upon the rope, the Wind of Shyish blows ever stronger.

Mercury is in demand throughout the Empire. In its raw form, it can be refined as pigment for clothing and inks. The Gold College will go to extensive lengths to obtain it - including striking secret deals with dark forces. Of course, Sylvanian residents have other uses for mercury, as it works well with Dark Magic - the two things bond extremely well.

The Blood Mines are so called for the cinnabar found in the area. That is not to say that the mines are never awash with blood. Should a Varghulf take residence then there will be half-eaten corpses and streams of bloody gore. Yet the unrefined mercury within is a powerful resource, both domestically and commercially, providing the right sort of factors and intermediaries are used.

Red as a colour is always in demand, for it is the colour of blood, of war and even used by the von Carsteins on their banners. For pigment grinders, red is more ubiquitous than noble purple but more difficult to formulate than brown or green. Sylvanian red is known as "blood red" for obvious reasons.

The hunting grounds within the moors and forests of Sylvania see action from poachers, trying to find the odd emaciated hare to put on the table. There are also hunts organised for the nobility. The Midnight Aristocracy make a great show of a hunt, but it isn't small game the Vampires chase, their prey is far more monstrous, and trophies far more advantageous.

Poaching Camps are forbidden by dread landlords who have long since forgotten the need to eat in the conventional sense. However, peasants can become so desperate that to hunt on von Carstein land is their only option. Of course, survival, even in a larger party, is far from guaranteed, even without the threat that their Vampire overlord will find out!

The flayer is a creature of Sylvanian folklore, a nursery rhyme monster to keep children in their beds. Yet deep in the woods it lurks, ready to do the bidding of the Vampire Counts, ready to bring the hides and skins of various beasts and to punish the smallfolk by skinning them alive - should they displease their Undead overlords.

Gold can be found in Sylvania's mountains but it is always tarnished, as if ruined by its proximity to Warpstone. Even so, tarnished gold can find markets further into Stirland and even Ostermark. Still, Sylvania is bordered by the World's Edge Mountains, those very same seams where Dwarfs find their gold and gems...

Larger seams of tarnished gold benefit from a grander infrastructure - dank mines are established and run throughout the day and night, as Zombie workers tirelessly hack into the mountain to bring the black-hearted noble his mound of tarnished gold.

There are a few smelteries within Sylvania, although the vast majority of its blackened gold is shipped out to provinces where skilled goldsmiths are able to make the best of it. Even so, smelteries under the Vampires' dominion produce a gold with a greenish sheen. Dwarfs reject such material outright, but Vampires enjoy the aesthetic, and even take pride in it.

Deep in the caverns that riddle Sylvania's mountains are the black iron pits - noxious, scabrous places where black iron ore can be found next to hunks of raw Warpstone. Peasants are sent in as punishment and rarely emerge alive or... unchanged. It is perhaps a blessing to be slain first and then sent into the pit as a fleshy puppet than alive.

When a Vampire or Necromancer discovers a seam of black iron or something more valuable such as Warpstone, then they will send in Zombies to rend the ore from the mountains. Zombies have many advantages over the living in this regard, as they don't require pay, or rest, or indeed any kind of safety considerations!

A scoured iron mine is one where such a seam of cursed iron is discovered. Only the Undead can mine this, for mortals will be mutated by the iron within. The ore is priceless, sought by Necromancers from across the world to fuel the darkest experiments. There are also other creatures that crave such material - red eyed and be-tailed, but we do not talk about them...

The forges in the bowels of Sylvania's castles may have once been used like any other, to produce good castle-forged steel to arm Stirland's soldiery, but that has changed since the coming of the Vampires. Now the forges are unholy relics, burning with the heat of a thousand cursed souls - now Sylvania's unholy forges serve the Vampire Counts.

The workshops of Sylvanian stone cutters - often known locally as Brimstone Cutters, for they build the lairs of fiends - are full of large cutting blades and grinding machines. Such contraptions are taken or bought from itinerant imperial engineers who have more interest in seeing their contrivance working over who actually ends up owning them and for what ends.

Tombstone makers are never short of work. Peasants can rarely afford such ostentatious graves, and are lucky to receive any kind of burial marking except maybe a small hammer or comet marker if they are lucky. It is the von Carsteins and their ilk who contract the tombstone makers and demand grand edifices and mausoleums for their private vaults.

In the poor, dingy townships there are garrets where sculptors make their living, fashioning stone into grim and gregarious creatures. There are far more gargoyles perching on the gothic walls, gatehouses and ramparts than could conceivably be fashioned by all the craftsmen in the Empire. Where do they come from? Only the Vampire Counts truly know.

The parts of Sylvania not covered by blackened moors or twisted forests have fields of withering crops. Nothing good can grow in Sylvania, yet the smallfolk must make a living as well as eat. They tend the cursed fields, growing stunted crops of pathetic yields and bare grazing for the skinny cattle to feed on.

The peasants have known for years that their landlords are Undead monsters, but to acknowledge it is to bring down ruination. As such, they continue to live under a pall of servitude and darkness, never being rich enough to move away. They collect what harvests they can, always knowing a von Carstein or his minions may summon them to the castle at any time.

The black bread of Sylvania is an acquired taste. Its loaves are black and lumpen; the flour coming from the haunted mills, whose weed-swaddled water wheels turn at night to produce a course meal of grain and ground bone. The bread tastes abominably sour. Nevertheless, the loaves are sold and consumed by the hungry populace.

Found close to the salt marshes, and in the stinking bogs that clog up the streams feeding into the River Aver and the River Stir, are clay pits. This dense clay, when mixed with ground bone, can create a surprisingly good base material for potters, urn makers and such like.

Urns of Sylvania are powerful artefacts in their own right, made and decorated by adding baroque and gothic trappings. Once fired in the screeching kilns, they are enchanted to hold the remains of powerful beings, Vampire Lords, Ghoul Kings and even the spiritual essence of ancient warriors. Such urns can find themselves at the centre of Mortis Engines, such is their arcane might.

Screeching kilns can only be found in the potteries of Sylvania. Why they screech is a bit of mystery - perhaps the ground bones' owners are freed by the heat? Maybe there are Tomb Banshees trapped inside or some other restless spirit burning as punishment? Such a thing is not beyond the dark imaginings of Mannfred von Carstein!

Brackish water, no doubt contaminated by Warpstone, forms in rivers and streams and in stagnant bodies throughout Sylvania. On top float skulls, dead rats and other foul things that would make it an interesting aside for any of Nurgle's followers. Underneath the surface, live the things of nightmares.

Salt is a commodity that has value outside the realm of Sylvania, where people use it to season their food. Vampires sell it to mortals through various factors and underhand merchants. The smallfolk are sent onto the marshes to harvest the salt, but hazards abound - clutching hands in the ground and Tomb Banshees that patrol the desolate marshes in a mournful stupor.

The dead marches are home to many of the salt marshes in Sylvania's bounds. In their centre lies the salt pans, covered in a field of bleached bones. For living things to get to the salt pans is all but impossible; Zombies make the taxing journey on their masters' behalf - the irony being that it is likely they were once the original salt collectors!

Timber is required for building materials, fencing and many other reasons, even in Sylvania. Stout Talabecland oak is hard to come by, so denizens must put up with the twisted, rotting wood from Sylvania's dense and hazardous forests. A forester of Sylvanian origin in the employ of the Midnight Aristocracy is given certain privileges, allowing him to enter the copses largely undisturbed.

At the turn of second millennium, the Elector Count of Stirland invested heavily in sawmills, as he saw wood as the future - an ever-renewable resource. A few years later a Sylvanian noble, Vlad, was unveiled as a creature of the night and the Vampire Wars began. The Elector's timber enterprise was in tatters, his network of sawmills left to ruin.

Should the provenance of a Sylvanian object or resource be uncovered it is shunned by most, destroyed on sight by many others. Dwarfs especially hate anything made by Sylvanian hands, living or no. The dark timber is secreted onto the market by merchant spies and greedy factors, who store it in abandoned sheds, far from trade routes and out of sight of the Emperor's Road Wardens.

Deeper in Hunger Wood is an old barn, decrepit in age, its original use long forgotten. Inside are rows upon rows of furs, the hides of myriad creatures, and the stench of death. Fallen timber piles up around it - no man has been there in years - and yet something lives there, for no one has dared take the potentially valuable - if hideous - contents.

Fallen timber piles up around it - no thing has been there in years - and yet something has, for no one has dared take the potentially valuable - if hideous - contents.

Blood Grapes are unique to Sylvania, found in the tangled and thorn-ridden vine patches in the south. If fermented properly the grapes make a full-bodied vintage, deeply red and rich in iron. Never mind that the occasional grape will contain a dead sparrow or shrivelled finger instead of a seed.

While crops always struggle to grow in Sylvania, its trees are rigorous and thrive in often harsh conditions. The low hung and thorny apple trees can provide surprisingly good yields, but farmers must be quick, for the fruits ripen and rot on the branch extremely quickly, attracting large flies who lay maggots that have far too many teeth.

Whether made from Sylvanian blood grapes, or simply the rancid gore of peasant cadavers, the animated winepress does most of the labour - crushing body or grape and fermenting and refining. Zombies are there to lift and carry but the spirit entrapped within the device is the true expert.

Hamlets are usually a lone group of hovels on a muddy, rutted road in the middle of the dour countryside. Despite the desperate state of the buildings, all have barred or boarded windows and surprisingly stout doors. On the roofs, wicked iron spikes emerge from the thatch. All to keep out the night's predators.

Sylvanian villages are in a constant state of disrepair, for good stone and wood is hard to come by. Crude fetishes and the charms hang on every lintel and frame. Villagers daub symbols of protection on their doors with pig's blood and roofs are laid with mantraps, spikes and far worse to ward off anything that might coming prowling in the night.

Hanging outside the decrepit townships' gates and walls are criminals and travellers trapped in iron maidens, feeding the crows and vampire bats. To be a stranger in such a town is to invite hostile stares from the locals, and mention "Sigmar" or the "Emperor" and you will find yourself dangling before nightfall, as such demagoguery could bring the von Carstein wrath upon you all!

Sylvania does not have any settlement that can truly be called a city, Vampire Counts have captured cities and declared them part of their realm. Any surviving occupants quickly feel the creeping dread, as friends and family go missing, Dire Wolves hunt the silent streets and Zombies shamble in the open. A perpetual night dominates the skyline; those still living think themselves accursed and the truth is... they are.

In the time of Sigmar, Sylvania was a refuge for those who refused to follow the Unberogen banner, so there have always been castles in the area to oversee this sorry part of Stirland. When Vlad got his claws into the realm, its destitute nobles were turned to the Vampire's cause; castles took on a sinister aspect, growing in size as extra citadels and towers were added for fell rituals and dark designs.

A Vampire's tomb lies deep within the crypts of his castle, or his master's domain, should the Vampire be in thrall to a more powerful being of the bloodline. Soon after receiving the Blood Kiss, a nascent Vampire will need to feed and then seek seclusion as its body is wracked with changes and Dark Magic.

Among the dread towers and gargoyles of Sylvania's castles are its keeps - the sanctuaries from where the Vampire Lord will entertain his allies or unwary mortals, and make his fell plans for domination of the living. The Midnight Aristocracy are of noble stock and so enjoy doing what nobles tend to do - entertain and plot.

A ghost fence is a barrier with little physical substance - merely a series of poles or posts upon which are hung accursed fetishes and totems to which Daemonic and Undead spirits have been bound with forbidden spells. Only a brave or foolish warrior crosses a ghost fence without good cause - or without powerful protective wards.

Not all creatures are raised back to join a Vampire's Undead horde, for bone is a useful material. Larger walls that mark boundaries around Vampire strongholds are often made from the bones and skulls of former enemies. Such a terrifying structure will make an invader think twice about climbing it, especially when the embedded skulls begin to scream!

The great curtain walls of Sylvania's Castles are massive bulwarks of stone, compacted bone and cursed relics, topped by leering gargoyles. They make any potential siege a formidable prospect, especially when such walls are guarded by observers that never tire, and will always stand ready to repulse any foolish mortal invaders.

Otto von Drak was the father of Isabella, noted for his degenerate madness – the final act of which was the joining of his hitherto selfish, immoral daughter to Vlad von Carstein. Although he did not personally know the suitor, Otto agreed the union to prevent his twisted brother, Leopold, from ascending to the throne, in an instant ensuring that the chaos of uncertainty did not befall the Drakenwald in the absence of a male heir. Little did he know that this marriage of convenience would blossom into the greatest of loves, defying time and dust to endure in obsessive devotion and eternal bliss. Isabella has not forgotten her beloved father, despite the centuries, and looks back upon his final act as the true beginning of her own life. So that the Mad Count – as he was frequently known – should always be remembered, she had his corpse interred inside a splendid chamber, dedicated to his life and achievements, so that the smallfolk may show suitable reverence.

Despite its run-down state, the mighty Saurus legions will once again spawn here.

Ancient forges and sand-clogged furnaces can be reignited and turned again to the cause of war.

The once great industrial centre of Nehekhara - now ruined and its old workers risen from their tombs.

Trees watered with the ancient powers of these pools will grow mighty indeed.
The bitter fury of the Savage Huntress is nothing compared to the ancient rage of the forest.
With the Pale Queen's temple corrupted, Elven souls can be put to... better use.
Athel Loren existed before any Elven 'Goddess of Nature'.
Elves are not the only hunters in the forest...
Little will the men of the Empire suspect what dark influence clouds the minds of their trading partners.
The umbrous depths of the Forest of Gloom are well-suited to the worship of the Shadow Dancer.

An impotent monolith lies toppled and fragmented in the dirt, a warning of past dangers that may one day return.
Once-great landmarks, torn from their foundations and trodden into the ground, are a prime location for a Herdstone of marked significance.

The people of Kislev flee to the forests – little good that will do.

Covered in ash, a mighty Herdstone breaks through a layer of smoke.

A noxious preparation of leaves, lichens and weeds imbued with ancient magic sends out coiling mists aglow with evil.
To the raving, chanting Shamans, burning living souls is the preferred method for siphoning great magical power.
So many heads, so few spikes…
When corpses are left mostly intact, uneaten and on display, it's only for the purposes of spreading all-consuming horror.

Gatherings at this place are… dour affairs, you might say.

Those brave - or foolish - enough to venture into Druchii territory may find respite here, however brief.
Cast off, if you dare, for these waters carry some stranger tides…

Although one of the less-powerful guilds, every sale of every beast nevertheless goes through them.

Dwarfs have little interest in wine, but fortunately it can be distilled into stronger beverages.
The Empire's greatest engineering minds aim to enter the centre of excellence at the academy.

Don't stick yer finga inna Squig Nest!

Horse bray and wicker, whilst soldiers look anxiously to the horizon. They have all rallied, for battle is near.
Great minds come together to discuss the storm that gathers around the Elven race.

Magically-warded battlements will hold as long as the Mages can sustain the spell.

What courteous words are spoken herein always belie a deeper meaning.

A High Elf may find a moment of tranquillity during a measured perambulation.

From Ulthuan shores to foreign climes, and back again; trade drives life.

Busy, noisy markets of the rich and powerful, where buyers vie for ownership of their exotic beasts.

Elven vases and other ceramics are some of the most beautiful artefacts in the world.

A healthy horse is a mighty horse, and a mighty horse is vital indeed.
Mastery of their mount is vital to any would-be champion of the Asur.
A simple shrine, to pray homage to the god of gods.
Make a little effort - you stand before an altar to the greatest god!
Splendour and magnificence, to pay glory to Asuryan.

Much larger cauldrons to hold even larger amounts of the corrosive brew.

Skink Priests with defensive lore will manifest mystic barriers used to repel trespassers and other invaders.
Walls of volcanic stone, laced with gold circuitry to better conduct the magic that imbues the walls with repulsive force.

Saurus cohorts on garrison duty are tasked with protecting the temple-cities and the Old Ones' legacy.

These needle-like spires are constructed to maintain the flow of Geomantic power.
The locus is a prism – a large geometric crystal floating in a constantly revolving state – and a junction where lines of power merge.
Skink hunters will oft make secret camps on well-trodden routes they know prey will roam.
Agriculture is not an alien concept to Lizardmen, they farm many breeds of insects, often in great domes that buzz with sound of swarms.
Cooling halls that shelter meat away from the Chotec's rage, the sun, helps keep the food relatively fresh.
The Skink districts are busy areas, where markets thrive, goods are exchanged and reptiles from foreign cities meet to trade.
The barrios are another part of the heavily-populated Skink districts, where many crafts are practised and artefacts created.
The labour districts are where the Skink handlers farm out Kroxigor labour for favour or a price.
Personifications of the Old Ones are frowned upon in some temple-cities, while others embrace the great statues as a place to focus their reverence.
Plazas are critical routes through the temple-cities, the Grand Plaza typically being the main causeway from the gate to the central ziggurat.
Drifting glades revolve in an eternal dance, where the Slann contemplate when the glades align in auspicious patterns.
Built more of instinctual reverence than true understanding of the Old Ones' geomantic alignment, Skink engineers still erect monolithic structures of inscrutable design.
Their religious ardour pointed squarely at the apexes of the pyramid-temples, few Lizardmen can fathom the power stowed away in vaulted devices and mummified Slann.
Pliodons are large, river-going creatures that seldom move on to land. They are used by the Lizardmen to ferry cohorts across bodies of water.
Natural harbours fashioned long ago by the Old Ones themselves, and now used by their servants.
Temple-cities close to the coast or major rivers will have designated port districts, where sea-going vessels of the Lizardmen make anchor.
The collecting of Itzl's creations, especially the colour changing chameleons, is deigned of use by the Slann.
Rarer Terradons distinguished by different beaks or patina are caged until tamed.
The great paddocks are where creatures are displayed and Skink Priests come with the blessings of Itzl and Conalxa.
Blood rock is a key ingredient in creating dyes for daubing on scales.
Blood rock mines are larger excavation sites, made when substantial cinnabar deposits are discovered.
Much blood rock is collected, ground with grit and thrown into sandstone vats, to create the dye.
Wearing the warmblood's skin is a good way to intimidate warmblood foes.
Skinks gemcutters are always in demand, as powerful crystals are used throughout the Lizardmen realms.
Gold holds a strange value to warmbloods, but for the Lizardmen it is a highly conductive and useful material.
Gold is melted down on thermal streams and then fashioned into any image the Mage-Priests desire.
Ore is taken from deep pits or mines; Kroxigor perform the labour but Skinks may have to work in smaller shafts.
Using methods described on plaque, the ore is heated and weapons can then be fashioned.
Marble is used in some form in certain temple-cities, but is not always the preferred material.
Skink adepts with a proficiency for stone carve images of the Old Ones into the walls of temple-cities.
Some Skinks have an innate knowledge of which jungle berries to use to salve bites and other nasty injuries.
Jungle lotus is one of the most potent of plants, and only a few know where it grows most regularly.
Jungle clearings and waterholes are where prey will gather; these are often protected by Lizardmen as a form of husbandry.
Lizardmen, especially Saurus, are meat-eaters, and so many animals are bred to slaughter and consume.
Insects are a large part of the Lizardmen diet; these jungles have both in abundance.
Skink potters are surprisingly adept, creating not just practical receptacles but often works of art.
Kilns are large Geomantic energy-powered ovens capable of mass-production.
Salt is mined. It’s an unpleasant and hazardous job - send in the Kroxigor.
When the Lizardmen need wood, the jungle provides.
Wood in its natural form is hard to work with, so the timber mills turn it into lumber ready for sale.
Found deep in the barrios, lumber from the jungle is bartered across the reptilian realms.
When squashed, certain berries and grapes make a pleasant drink somewhat above swamp water.
Once the draft is made, it is stored in great vats, where it will ferment, often sending Saurus into a groggy state!
When ready, Skink factors sell the draft in clay pots to others with a taste for it.
In times of war, the large lagoons in the Saurus caverns can be adjusted to gestate many warrior cohorts simultaneously.
Skink aggregators believe that cooler spawning climates found under the ground can produce better quality warriors.
The Temple Guard are placed in a dedicated barracks where they train and bask awaiting their sacred duty.
In blessed pools will the Slann bathe or stare - often for decades - until enlightenment is found.
A small gathering of cohorts, usually a settlement along the Geomantic Web in thrall to a more prominent temple-city.
A minor node on a smaller tributary of the Geomantic Web, comprising a lone ziggurat, often ruled by a later generation Mage-Priest.
Located on a lesser tributary of the Geomantic Web, comprising a ziggurat and surrounding barrios, and often ruled by a later generation Mage-Priest.
The temple-cities are where the Lizardmen spawn and live. They scatter the Southlands and Lustria, comprising of great pyramids, barrios and plazas.
All temple-cities are nodes in the Geomantic Web, but some are true nexus points - massive cities and major tributaries in power.
Spawning ponds are used for lower ranking Skink castes - the ponds themselves are small bodies of water, although many in number.
The hunter-caste spawning pools hold thousands of eggs that quickly gestate new Skinks, with a subtle temperature rise, at a Slann's command.
Elevated pools, closer to the central pyramid, are more likely to gestate specialist Skink castes and their bodyguards.
Located at the peak of the ziggurats are the Star Chambers, where the prominent Mage-priests ponder in their trance-like slumber.
Certain barrios in the temple-city are where Skink artisans reside, arguably the most important of which are the weapon-crafters.
The hatcheries are tall pylons that nearly match the peak of the central pyramid. Within their tips are nests containing many Terradon eggs.
Shrines to certain lesser or forgotten Old Ones are scattered throughout the temple-cities; no matter how insignificant, they are still highly revered.
Temples of the Old Ones populated by many Skink acolytes and dedicated Mage-Priests are found throughout the temple-cities.
The great pyramids and temples are normally clustered at the end of the grand plazas at the centre of the temple-cities.
Where Skinks come to show devotion to the serpentine Old One god, and warm-blooded prisoners are put to the sword.
The site of many, many blood sacrifices of Lizardmen foes to the satisfy the Serpent God's eternal thirst.
A great fall crests the top of Sotek's pyramid, but it is not water that cascades down.
Razordon-like, the angular protrusions of the ziggurat stretch out in mute augury towards the forked tongue of the serpent crawling across the night sky.
Warpstone is concentrated Dark Magic, which has the tendency to attract more of itself.
Precious Warpstone seams, once found, will need defending against thieves.
This small settlement is claimed by a rogue force.
This settlement is claimed by a rogue force.
A sprawling settlement claimed by a rogue force.
The mountain peaks of Parravon are known for their large bird roosts, but even more famous for pegasi.
Lower-ranking Clan Eshin rats remain apart from the other clans' rabble in hidden burrows that remain Eshin territory no matter what the dominant Warlord believes.
Unbeknownst to most - often even the ranking Warlord - Clan Eshin has their own outpost or den within the lair, where Eshin members gather to plot.
The business of secret murder makes the establishment of escape routes, secret tunnels and concealed hidey-holes a necessity.
The pit is where many of the Clanrat packs congregate in a writhing mass to eat and enact their own petty plans and downfalls.
Favoured Clanrats, or those that have clawed their way through the vicious hierarchy, have a place in the barracks and access to better arms.
Deep in the warrens are the clan armouries; heavily-guarded by Stormvermin, it is the first place the Skavenslaves ransack.
Should the things invade, devious tunnel design forces them to chokepoints, where Warp-fire emplacements scorch the intruders to death.
Ingenious back-tunnels allow the clans to move their rodents quickly through the maze-like warrens.
Clan Moulder-rejected Rat Ogres and others are conscripted and chained to key defensive junctions and outposts - their handlers unleashing them at trespassers.
Shrill alarms sound off should detection sensors be triggered by incorrect tail swishes; only those in the clan know the right combination.
Jagged, irregular, wooden and metal fortifications surround the largest and most important entrances to the lair.
The most basic way of generating power for even the poorest clans is through rows of slave wheels, where Skavenslaves are run to exhaustion.
In the piston house, Warp-steam driven pistons power the foundries, laboratories and feeding dens that ratmen society relies.
Skaven have quickly adopted the generator systems of the Greater Clans which use Skavenslaves on treadmills to generate power.
While energy generation is rarely a problem for Skaven society, power storage can be a challenge unless the warren has capacitors.
A Warpstone reactor is the pinnacle of Clan Skryre engineering, hence they charge a premium, as well as a hefty vassal contract.
Large caverns, close to the surface, are often used as workshops, where Skaven war machines are built, laboured on by thousands of expendable slaves.
Warpstone is sent here for refinement and used in myriad other applications. Warlock Engineers and Warp-smiths learn their craft here.
Warp-turbines cost thousands of Skavenslave lives while in operation; a small price to pay for the development of the infamous Doomwheel.
The warrens are full-to-teeming with ratlings and immature vermin yet to prove themselves. Survival in this environment is brutal, harsh and often fatal.
Nest-nurseries are where powerful or special pups are taken to ensure they are not eaten by their ravenous siblings, or indeed their parents.
While some broodmothers are vaunted, such as the bearers of Stormvermin and other higher-caste specimens, the majority are kept in filthy pits.
Established breeding techniques applied to specially selected feral pups is the first step towards rearing bloodthirsty horrors.
The Packmasters’ expert monster-breaking methods allow even the most tameless brutes to be whipped into veritable monsters of war.
Growth Vats are used in most Clan Moulder facilities, but more rudimentary methods can also be utilised to enlarge certain specimens.
Although Clan Moulder's Hell Pit is the largest facility of its kind, many Skaven clans have laboratories dotted throughout the Under-Empire.
From his raised platform, the taskmaster guides and directs the noisome hordes, setting tasks or mustering the Clanrats for war.
The overseer chitters at the taskmaster, who in turn takes his anger out on the Clanrats below - Skaven society as microcosm.
The screaming foundries are where the Grey Seers set their Warpsmiths and slaves to cast the vile bells of the Horned Rat.
The Clanrats of Pestilens are baptised in a font known as the Pox Cauldron; their pustules swell and their transformation into Plague Monks begins.
From the unholy pulpits the Plague Priests chant and preach to their diseased congregation - sowing animus, disease and hatred of the no-furs.
Within the fell abbey, the Plague Priests preach to the frenzied plague monks amidst the putrid fog of the swaying censers.
Where the Skaven lairs meet the sea are ragged wharfs on which many thousands of Skavenslaves are offloaded from one clan to another.
The under-docks are harbours where slave-barges, captured thing-navies and all kinds of commercial products from all over the Under-Empire are delivered.
Home to the bell-fleets - the Lords of Decay's great navies - these are hidden places, giving the sea-clans advantage over the others.
Skaven collect exotic creatures, but not out of curiosity. Clan Moulder will always pay a good price for new specimens.
Once hunted, the creatures are stored in pens and cages for spectators or potential buyers.
In such underground markets, factors from Moulder and other interested clans come to barter-trade for specimens.
While red rock is not as prized as green rock, it still has its uses as dyes for banners and armour.
Skaven dye-plants are arcane-chemical nightmares that spew out toxic waste in an attempt to create… something.
Hidden caves and tunnel alcoves allow access to the overground, where Skaven hunters can stalk their prey.
If no-furs insist on wearing furs, then Skaven should wear furs too-too!
Skaven gemcutters practice on what Man-things consider precious stones, for it is Warpstone they really want to slice.
Skaven sniff out gold, and will excavate out of spite, knowing Man-things and Dwarf-things crave it.
Although they have no use for it themselves, Skaven purposely mine gold purely to inconvenience the other races.
Skavenslaves are sent to excavate iron seams - they will labour until exhaustion.
Metal-working is known to only a few clans, while others scavenge or barter for forged weapons.
Weird-stone not Warpstone! Smooth and lined, but some warlords like it…
Clan Skryre has cutting machines that can slice through stone… and limbs.
Some Skaven adepts are skilled at carving; warlords will patronise them in order to sell their services on for their own profit or status.
There are few herbs growing underground, so some Skaven scavenge for plants above it.
Alchemy has always been an area in which Skaven have excelled, having an innate willingness to experiment combined with little worry for personal risk…
Pastures? Underground mud-yards where mewling meat-things are kept ready for slaughter.
Skaven factory farms are hellish places where half-formed things are bred to feed the masses.
Larger factory farms are more than mere underground pastures – they provide food on an industrial scale.
Ratmen pots are far from the aesthetically-pleasing pieces of other races: they are scraggy, untidy mass-produced.
Kilns are large Warpfire-powered ovens capable of mass-production.
Salt is mined. It’s an unpleasant and hazardous job - send in the slaves!
Clan Eshin has a tunnel network that reaches into the far east, of which they bring powders coveted by the other clans.
Warpstone-enhanced lumber is always needed in the Under-Empire.
Wood in its natural form is hard to work with, so the timber mills turn it into lumber ready for sale.
Underground lumber yards, held under by clans and their factors, where goods are exchanged for many Warptokens.
Squashing sour fruits creates an intoxicating drink better than Skavenbrew, yes-yes!
Factors will store the fruit brew and let it ferment, like the Beard-things do with grains.
Clan factors will then sell the brew far and wide, often lacing it with Warpstone essence for those who can afford the price.
The worst pieces of broken swag scavenged from battlefields above and below, is thrown into the trash hole and fought over by the Skavenslaves.
Scavenge-piles are where the useful accoutrements claimed and stolen by the clans after battle are placed for its champions to scour.
The scrap heap is made from the most valuable items scavenged from the over-worlds of the Man-things, Elf-things and Beard-things.
Packs of Skaven gather in smaller burrows often used as staging areas where clans make ready to burst forth.
Usually owned by a dominant clan, these places are much larger nests linked by an impenetrable maze of tunnels.
The teeming tunnel networks of warrens do not just sprawl underground, but can riddle entire mountains and chasm walls as well.
Giant corridors and endless passageways run through these decadent Skaven hubs, where the ratmen mobilise in unimaginably vast numbers.
Skaven cities sprawl beneath the ground like swollen ulcers, with other races' ruins shamelessly usurped into their erratic architecture.
The foetid, shambolic temple is a maze of tunnels that all lead to the Altar of the Great Horned One.
Weapon burrows, where combustible Skryre techno-weapons are stored, are not jealously guarded because if incompetently handled the user will quickly perish.
For logistical reasons, Skaven clans have arsenals of their most successful and 'reliable' weaponry, kept secure with arcane locks.
The pure, unfiltered darkness oozing from this altar is enough to give even the hardest warrior pause.
The capital Reiksfort - home of the imperious order of the Reiksguard.
The Emperor's palace is the grandest edifice in Altdorf - home to the Altdorf Princes of old.
This Bretonnian outpost in conquered Altdorf has been given over to the ruling duke.
Palace of the Eternal Emperor, seat of the von Carsteins now and forever.
Etched in barely decipherable runic Khazalid, timeworn Runestones chronicle Karak Zorn’s ancient and tumultuous past.
Anaerion himself once sat upon the throne at Tor Anlec, making the city a focal point of Asur defences.
In Conalxa's shrine do the Chameleon Skinks give thanks to the Old One who preserves and enhances them.
Ancestral home of the Blood Dragon Order, an honourable martial order until Walach Harkon visited.
Arch-Necromancer Constant Drachenfels once imprisoned his victims within these crypts, so they could be tortured at his leisure.
Constant Drachenfels lived for over ten thousand years, constructing a vast library of ancient tomes and dread grimoires.
Those who visit the Chamber of Visions shall see what the Old Ones see: the many threads of the future.
Deep below the Tower of Doom, all manner of beasts are kept and … investigated, in the name of greater power.
Beneath the frozen glaciers of Karak Izor's peaks lie gargantuan lodestones of copper ore that lend this proud Dwarfhold its name.
Beneath Karak Izor’s frozen peaks, the Skaven exploit its massive copper ore deposits for the nastier weapons in their arsenal.
Spawning pools defiled by Clan Pestilens; the half-formed creatures that emerge make for easy pickings.
The sea-faring High Elves of Cothique built grand edifices into the cliffsides, creating palatial underground cities.
The Druchii give praise to the God of Smiths, in the hope he will bestow the legendary artefacts upon them.
All the best places are ones you've nicked from other races and then made your own by leaving piles of poo and shiny stuff everywhere.
The dilapidated Court Hall of the Von Carsteins, it does need to be given a new life...
The Court Hall are where the Undead nobles, and living thralls come to play games of courtly intrigue.
Dark artefacts and codified writings line these chamber walls, waiting for someone to unlock their arcane secrets.
While the surface city of Karak Eight Peaks is grand, it is, underneath, in the colonnaded halls, deep underground where the true wealth resides. It is ripe for Clan Mors to take!

The tombs of the revered Dwarf kings of the Eight Peaks are situated even deeper than the vaults. If Clan Mors break the seals of the crypts, it will ensure their entry in the Book of Grudges for all eternity!

The greatest riches in all of Vala-Azril-Ungol are kept in the treasury, a massive chamber that once held the wealth of the Dwarfhold and its greatest relics. Its seals were the hardest to prise apart… until now.
The finest steeds for the finest Elves. So it has always been. So it will always be.
Not even the noblest of Elven steeds are immune from corruption.
The court of Avelorn is a great carnival, pitching silken pavilions in which Elves make sport and recite epic poetry.
Within the great plateau of this ancient construct is the stellar engine; the secrets of its construction jealously guarded.
From the safety of a fortified position, warriors fire destructive ordnance upon approaching attackers.
Mourkain is the ancient Vampire kingdom of Kadon, who once controlled the Badlands. It was superseded by the Strygos Empire, of which ghoul-infested ruins still remain.
Blimey, dats one massive pile of bonez!
While Khorne may not approve of using the skulls of those killed by others, this near-infinite supply will still come in useful.
A mass open grave is a macabre sight to most, but to the Necromantically-inclined it is a place to conjure martial might.
A mass open grave is a macabre sight to most, but to the Necromantically-inclined it is a place to conjure martial might.
Oathgold or 'Galbaraz' is the purest gold, mined from the deepest of deeps. Only small deposits exist, usually in remote locations.
The Dark Cultists studying within say they can see the future. To this end, they study tirelessly and without cease.
The dark tomes that are studied herein, and the vicious incantations practised can shake the very foundations of the world.
The Tower of Ghrond’s luxuries are of little interest to the Skaven, yet beneath its decadence are dwellings considered far more suitable.
The screams of Elves tortured for the Hag Sorceress’ pleasure have now been replaced by the howls, snarls and shrieks of mutant abominations.
Let its thousand lamps guide you to safe harbour.
An ancient tower clad in pure gold, constructed by the Lizardmen at the order of the Old Ones in an age long past.
While this tower was constructed at the behest of the Old Ones, it now serves only to amplify the power of their greatest rivals.
Far, far below Hag Graef, slaves toil in darkness for their masters' wealth.
The precious minerals, so desired by the Druchii, are prized from the rock by bloodied, blackened hands.
The mines stretch on, seemingly endless, with every shaft and seam another hazardous tunnel of possibility.
Nowhere in Naggaroth is less safe. One could lose much and more along the treacherous crags.
Gaze upon the majestic beasts of old and realise your place within the world.
From within, the Blood Queen unearths new and excruciating methods of murder.
The Druchii worship the brutality of Khaine above all, founding centres of agony in his name.
Down, deep in Hell Pit are where Clan Moulder keep their most promising and... foul specimens.
Even at these shallow depths, noxious steam accompanies the dreadful cacophony of howls, screams and shrieks of unspeakable things.
The deepest depths of Hell Pit are where Clan Moulder keep their most promising and foul specimens.
Within the Blessed Incubator, the beasts of Hexoatl are kept, ready for the Old One Itzl to leave his mark.
Upon the southern horizon of Hexoatl, on the eve of the equinox, stellar pyramids will rise above the jungle canopy.
The shimmering, healing Emerald Pools of Itza are truly a sight to behold; even cold-blooded eyes appreciate their beauty.
Under Itza, the Vaults of the Old Ones contain many secrets of the Ancient Enemy, and, some say, how to finally defeat them.
This palace is the result of years of back-breaking labour. Somebody else's, of course. Not mine. No, no!
A treacherous path, to be sure, but safety lies beyond to those who can navigate it.
Safety, friend. Come ashore; you're in the greatest city in the world, now.
These towering gates bar passage to anyone harbouring ill designs about Ulthuan.
Deep below Iron Rock lie its vast magma chambers, formed by great earthquakes in ages past.
The gathering place and centre of power for Clan Mors, where Warlords address their kin-lords.
The once beatific fortress of Mousillon is now a decrepit pile, but still a formidable stronghold for the living to attack.
Leering over the landscape, an ominous sentinel keeping would-be brigands in check.
The citadel stands as a deathly warning to any who would oppose Malekith's hegemony over the Druchii.
The creatures that take flight flock to the Shrine of Birds, the Old One whose essence resides within awarding all creatures that take flight.
All manner of questionable items eventually end up here. Buyers beware, however, as pickpockets relieve customers of their valuables almost immediately.
At the court of the Phoenix King, many come to petition Finubar and play their intrigues.
We will continue to empty the Elven palace until every slight in the Dammaz Kron has been repaid in full.
According to the Norscans, those unable to defend their valuables have no business owning such things.
The first of Nagash's great and powerful edifices. Even millennia later it is still surrounded by fell magic.
It is only fitting that the great Black Pyramid is under Undead ownership.
It is in Quetza where Sotek's followers are the most fervent. The ratmen should fear the coldbloods that emerge from these lairs.
The catacombs of this impossibly ancient city conceal treasures that are not of this realm.
Quintex has stood since before the dawn of recorded history. Within its vaults lie treasures beyond comprehension.
The deepest chancels within Quintex may very well hold treasures and learnings that unlock the past, and foretell the future.
The great hangars of Karaz-a-Karak are the home of its infamous Airkorps.
The forest of Laurelorn is home to a thriving enclave of Elves that refused to leave the Old World at the conclusion of the War of the Beard.
Skavenblight is the noisome capital of the ratmen - a sprawling metropolis and chief lair of the Thirteen Lords of Decay.
Skavenblight, the noisome capital of the ratmen, is the most infamous of all under-cities - a sprawling metropolis and chief lair of the Thirteen Lords of Decay.
Here the High Elves may give praise to the ruler of the Elven pantheon, Asuryan.
What was once a place of worship, reduced now to so much cinder.
Give praise to the Lord of War, and hope he answers with righteous fury.
What was once a place of worship, reduced now to so much cinder.
Kraka Drak, famous for its gemstone and silver mines, is so rich that an entire hall has been lined with thick silver sheets.
Skavenblight is the centre of all Skaven power, where the Lords of Decay meet to decide the fates of all.
The impossibly high tower reaches from the darkest depths to scrape the sky; at its tip, the Bell of the Horned Rat.
Skeggi’s original founder named it for his daughter, constructing this magnificent hall at the start of his second Lustrian expedition.
Thanks to the established outpost of Skeggi, many warbands have sailed from Norsca to Lustria, eager to enrich themselves on ancient treasures.
An Imperial sailor discharged for his drunkenness and thievery, Smithy won the noisiest tavern on Sartosa in a game of dice.
Positioned close to one of the mountain passes that lead into the Empire, Pfeildorf Market gives travellers their first taste of Imperial wares.
At the sunken palace of Tor Anroc the Hall of Charioteers is an eternal legacy for Tiranoc's greatest.
Tiranoc is a hard-forged diamond: a resplendent city of defiance in the face of would-be catastrophe.
In the City of the Moon sits the Temple of the Eclipse, its power reverberating whenever the two moons align.
White Lions are proud predators that roam the northern forests, who in turn are hunted by Chrace's warriors.
The Loremasters of the High Elves take great pride in their vast scroll collections.
Visible from many miles, the White Tower is the greatest sanctuary of knowledge in the known world.

One of the reasons Eight Peaks rivalled Everpeak in greatness was the colonnaded hub of the Underway, in the lower deeps. This was a key crossroads, allowing trade and military access throughout the Karaz Ankor.

Beneath the Eight Peaks is a key nexus for all tunnels in the region – a junction that unlocks the World’s Edge Mountains for any ambitious Skaven Warlord. Whichever clan controls this hub can influence the entire Under-Empire.
The Underworld Sea is a cavernous ocean under Naggaroth that allows Druchii navies to swiftly travel from coast to coast.
The once-great court of Avelorn now lies sacked and broken in the wake of savage Druchii terror.
The Temple of Mists is surrounded by enchanted fog that protects all of Xlanhuapec.
They say of Tor Yvresse that it is easily as grand as any Elven city of old.
By dawn's early light… does it call to the bosom of the Old Ones for their protection and illumination.
Some battles are fought over areas drenched in magic. The corpses that litter these sites are ripe for Necromancers…
Lairs of the dreaded Undead Terrorgheists are massive caves filled with the bones of their prey.
Restless souls are lured by Necromancers into arcane wells and tethered to others for ever more.
An unholy font of dark dreams and trapped spirits, used by Undead Lords to bolster their legions.
The tree-lined courts are where kindreds send their princes to increase their status through fine deeds.
The healing magics of the Asrai are among the best in all the mortal realms.
An odd assortment of standing stones have long held watch over Albion, enacting an ancient purpose that has long been forgotten.
These rune-bound Waystones of unknown origin have received a patchwork of venerations from Albion’s long history of inhabitants.
Cleansed and restored at last, the once-derelict Ogham Stones channel their considerable powers to serve your cause.
Its fumes offend keener senses, yet draught, powder, and drum alike lend strength to the hunt.
Alchemical art grows bolder here, raising sky-borne scouts and battle-signals that sharpen eye and instinct.
Wondrous and disquieting, these arts send engines through the heavens, where sorcery and craft become one.
Here, claw and jade stand as one, each warcraft sharpening the other for battles yet to come.
Arms are tempered by Bastion lore, where seasoned wardens teach the arts of steadfast war.
A greater host is armed here, where shield, lance, and crossbow answer the Tiger Warriors’ charge.
Where white banners are first planted, and wandering blades seek stillness beneath timber, hide, and Kamau’s watch.
Palisades, humble shrines and sturdy quarters mark a company’s first true roots, nourished by discipline and hard-earned coin.
Unwavering in their honour, the Tiger Warriors turn wealth into order, and order into a settlement of purpose.
In time, mercenary toil matures into a lasting edifice, where proud custom and iron resolve endure in stone itself.
A great citadel of claw, prayer, and unbroken discipline, where the proud customs of a hardened war-host deepen into legacy.
Here, fang and blade are honed as one, and young warriors learn the savage discipline of the Tiger path.
Shrine and war-lair alike, this lodge heeds the Clawspeakers, whose rites and sorceries call Kamau’s fury to battle.
The Iron Claw ever perfect their killing arts, proven against mighty beasts and sworn to unyielding service.
The stench is harsh and the thunder harsher, but such weapons reap a bloody toll before claw meets flesh.
Let iron and flame break the foe from afar, that the Tiger Warriors may fall upon what remains.
No martial grace can rival this pitiless hail, whose far-shot ruin fells beast, warlord, and rank.
Beneath watchful heavens, sacred beasts are bound to war, and Astromancers read the omens of victory.
Here soar moon-birds and longma, called by celestial craft to bear war beyond the reach of claw.
From earth and star alike come towering guardians, wrought to endure where even the fiercest hunter might fall.
Humble homes, serve to shelter common folk. Providing labour in peace and a stout militia in times of need.
Though tigers have little love for the saddle, swift horsemen still earn their keep where speed must answer steel.
To reach the port of the City of Dawn, trade vessels are hoisted hundreds of feet up the steep cliffside of Mount Li by this marvel of Cathayan engineering.
A shadow of the Celestial Court, the House of Secrets provides a safe haven for outcast practitioners of elemental magic, dabbling in obscure arcane and alchemical experiments.
Travellers between the cities of Nan Gau and Wei-Jin feel safe in the shadows of the giant terracotta protectors lining the road, their gazes fixed on the Great Bastion.

Be'lakor corrupted the Oak to hold the gate of the city centuries ago. While it has lain dormant since, with the right approach it could still be a valuable ally.

A wretched, twisted tree with white fronds spreading far and wide. Bones adorn its branches, and the folklore tells that it is inhabited by a spirit older than some gods.
Deep within the Black Pit, in a valley where sunlight never shines, is the breeding ground of the fearsome, deadly Arachnarok Spiders.
With sufficient supplication, Mathlann could be coaxed into surrendering his victim, and one of the lost Black Arks would return to us.
With a sacrifice that will echo down the ages, the Druchii proclaim their mastery over the sea itself, and reclaim what their ancestors had lost to its cruel embrace.
Beneath the earth lies a pit of corruption, festering in the bowels of the city beyond the reach of prying eyes.
Daemonic echoes reverberate within the Temple's crumbling walls, as the faithful gather in secrecy to pledge their souls to darkness.
There is no greater trick than to twist the heart and mind of an enemy until the concept of friend and foe become entwined.
Whispers echo everywhere, reshaping every thought according to the Changer's will.
There is no room for subtlety where recruitment is concerned – eventually all must bow.
Knowledge and new followers must be gathered at any cost… by the point of a blade if necessary.
The cult of Ruin's influence only grows, permeating neighbouring lands and aggressively proselytising to the masses.
From here the Raven's flock quietly separates, spreading far and wide to pluck mystic knowledge from the heads and hands of the unworthy.
The disciples of Tzeentch sweep out from every shadow, to sow the Ruinous seeds of Change across the land.
With every grimoire gathered and every fragment of arcane knowledge found, the Changer's dark influence burrows ever deeper.
Masked cultists stalk the shadows, terrorising the local populace before disappearing back into the dark.
The region despairs, drowning in theft, conspiracy and intrigue! Alas, the source of such Chaos remains a mystery…
Here walk the harbingers of terror, snatching all in sight and leaving discord in its place.
The agents of Change wear many faces, 're-possessing' resources and weaving their webs of deceit.
Where power lies, the puppets dance, while the agents of Tzeentch pull their strings.
Woe to the one who gives his trust with ease, for a smiling face often distracts from the dagger hidden in hand.
What is gold to the Changer of Ways but an aid in His conspiracies, paving the path to horror and Ruin?
Raven-feathered raiders spill the blood of the unsuspecting, painting every coin a deathly red.
Economic structures balance on the brink of collapse, for every ounce of gold is met with magic and corruption.
A steady stream of income is easy to come by... one need only wear the right face.
Amid the ruthless realm of commerce, the agents of Tzeentch spread their wings, siphoning gold from the unwary.
The Changer's magic creates a simple façade, smoothing the way towards riches and Ruin.
Thus rise the tendrils of corruption, fanning out in all directions in search of easy prey.
The riotous energy of Chaos overflows, exploding into slaughter; the ravens will circle until the bones of this place are picked clean.
A convergence of ruinous energy, oozing corruption until reality itself has torn asunder.
Out pour the raging armies of Chaos from the jaws of fate, opened wide.
A dark cloud sweeps in from above, swirling with the mystical energies of corruption.
The ritual is concluded; the Changeling's forces are called forth, to wreak death and Ruin upon all.
Elspeth frequently divides her time between her Towers, studying the darkest magics in silent seclusion.
Not even death could stop the dedicated warriors of Morr from defending the lands they call home.
The Amethyst Wizard must always study their craft to avoid falling foul of their own sorcery!
A font of collective knowledge, shared between generations of Amethyst Wizards so that their craft may be advanced..
The Amethyst College is dedicated to the study of Shyish, the most feared and powerful Lore of Death.
A shrine provides a place of worship for those who cannot easily reach a temple; the dead require their last rites, regardless of location.
The temple doors are always open, representing the portal which allows the safe passing of life to the other side.
The temple is surrounded by a grand, black rose garden littered with graves and monuments.
This metallic skeleton creaks a little, but it's more than sturdy enough to uphold the entire structure of the Airship.
Whatever damage the Spirit of Grungni takes is absorbed by its durable hull, bolstered by layers of the most resilient materials.
Runesmiths have etched their work into the metal frame, warding the Airship against the evils of Chaos and enemy magic.
As the rigours of war take their toll, a more robust frame is necessary for any Airship destined for the battlefield.
Inscribed with powerful warding runes, the hull is interweaved with protective magic, deflecting every barrage of Ruin.
No Airship is complete without a working forge, though this one is what some might describe as "fun-size".
Within such limited space, the smelting process has been optimised to work on a smaller – yet no less efficient – scale.
Automating parts of the production process enables complex machinery to continue working night and day.
Settling down into rows of rickety beds, the Dwarfen warriors aboard the Spirit of Grungni always sleep with their axes in arm's reach.
A cozy room and a warm bed; it's everything any soldier could want… as long as one can ignore the sound of the engines.
The grizzled veterans of war keep to themselves, sleeping surrounded by glorious tapestries of victories long past.
A tinny voice rings out across the battlefield, offering a rousing speech that rallies the hearts of every Dwarf on the ground.
The deployment of fiery explosives ensures that even the most stubborn enemies are sent running away in terror.
For when one harpoon just isn't enough… which is surprisingly more often than you'd think!
When the Gyrocopters deploy from their station, friend and foe alike down below can do little but watch in wonder.
It's got to be five o'clock somewhere!
The beer hall is always the happiest place to be on any Airship, evidenced by the constant singing.
Why leave your post when you can have beer delivered to you? Surely nothing could go wrong…
With a constant source of beer at the ready, drinking on the job is so commonplace it's practically mandatory.
With racks installed along every wall, nobody can complain about lack of storage.
This cavernous hold is always put to good use, filled to the brim with provisions.
When battle rages and lives are on the line, ease of access is vital for the quick transfer of goods and munitions.
Huge, automated mechanisms load cargo in and out, speeding up the process tenfold.
This dummy looks a little worse for wear, but it's more than good enough for target practice.
A small gallery allows for more guns firing at once; it's efficient, despite the awful racket!
This large compartment has been reinforced a dozen times to compensate for the occasional stray bullet.
Where better for engineers to tinker away on their latest designs than their own dedicated workbench?
Flying machines take up every available inch of space, in various states of repair.
Construction has reached new heights of efficiency, allowing the most complex designs to be brought to life along the assembly line.
Basic propellers provide limited thrust, but enough to get the Spirit of Grungni sailing through the clouds.
Ingenious calculations and a little practiced tinkering have left the Spirit of Grungni with a vastly improved thrust-to-weight ratio.
Standing taller than an irate Ogre, these huge metallic blades carve through the skies with ease, utilising the full speed of the Airship's engines.
Nothing beats the roaring sound of an Airship's engines when the captain pushes them to their limits.
The Slayers rarely leave their workshop, preparing night and day to be transported to their glorious doom.
This vast array of weaponry has become somewhat of a shrine, where the Slayers worship them as symbols of their coming death.
There is no better use of an armed Airship than to sail it headlong into the raging tumult of battle.
More ammunition means more dead enemies and a whole host of grudges settled.
When the battlefield calls, a hasty rearmament is more than essential – Dwarfen lives depend upon it!
When smoke rises in the distance, the Spirit sails at full speed, answering the summons with all guns blazing.
When the chain of beacons is lit, the crew of the Spirit know that something is afoot... something requiring their urgent attention!
The Council convenes on all manner of matters, from lowly planning regulations to designing new feats of engineering genius.
Usually close to the trade depot, the Guild marketplace is a bazaar of grumpy, haggling, Guild factors selling their wares and services.
Despite relatively limited confines and heavy foot traffic, this overly-populated district buzzes with market trade.
Here, trading is overseen and regulations are set to send even the most studious Dwarf into a slumber.
The telling scent of Black powder lingers in the air, where a continuous stream of weapons are forged to outfit the Dwarfen infantry.
The Irondrakes spew vicious flames from their Drakeguns, forged by an expert in the foundry.
Every target is punched through with holes clustered around its red-painted centre.
The cacophony of the shooting range is ample training for the raging uproar of the battlefield.
Military colleges such as this help prospective Imperial soldiers take their first steps towards becoming gunnery experts on the battlefield.
Empire Gunnery School's are second to none, training the most elite sharpshooters of every generation.
Nurgle's power grows with the splendour of his gardens, which depend on special micro-organisms to ensure they stay fertile and vibrant.
The dead are left to decompose in a swamp of blood and entrails, offering their foul nutrients to the soil.
A whole host of deadly microbes sink into the land, feeding a rush of Nurgle's toxins directly into the earth.

Nurgle's influence stretches out into the world, creating new avenues of infection among the populace.
Nurgle's vegetation creeps ever further from its root, secreting a malodorous toxin that burrows deep in the brain.
The ground itself pulsates with Nurgle's influence, as sprawling roots of disease sink deep between rock and soil.
Vines twist around every surface, ensnaring everything in their path until it oozes with infection and decay.

Lethal spores take flight, flooding the air with a deathly stench and suffocating all doubt from the lungs of Nurgle's faithful.
Fungal infections fester and spread, twisting the minds of the local populace until they bow in subservience, offering their gold as a form of tribute.
A deathly mould infects the minds of the living, encouraging even greater offerings to prove the depths of their devotion.
The warriors of Nurgle dwell at close-quarters, allowing disease to run rampant among their putrescent ranks.
A huge host requires a huge hall, decorated with the blood and rotting viscera of their victims.
Large stakes settle deep into the earth, forming a protective ring of spikes sharp enough to skewer any foolish would-be attackers.
Stinking corpses pile high, forming an ever-decaying barricade that grows larger by the day.
Bodies hang from towering walls as a warning to all, picked apart by the carrion birds until more corpses arrive to replace them.

The Knights of the Order of the Black Rose are shrouded in secrecy, recruiting only from among the local nobility and said to worship Morr and wear his symbols.
This ancient Cathayan pagoda harbours priceless knowledge on how to better control each of the Winds of Magic.
Once complete, this embassy will help to establish good relations with the Cathayan people. Until then, we must defend ourselves from the rebel forces that roam the land!
An embassy enables people to work together freely in order to push back the Chaos plaguing the world.
Seal off the tombs and ward them against the foul magics to which they have been exposed!
The Hold has been reclaimed! Now the long process of purging it of Neferata's malign influence can begin...
The Gallows Tree is said to be home to an unclean hag-Daemon shunned by her own kind. To those that please her, she divulges the foulest hidden secrets.
Reaching the Throne of Chaos is the greatest feat possible for a mortal champion of the Dark Powers, and a sure path to immortality.
Goblin dwellings are tidier than Orcish ones, if only because Goblins are less lazy than their bigger cousins.
The sun-hating Night Goblins keep to their lightless pits and cackle madly on occasion – or whenever they feel like it!
Foul-smelling fumes billow out from dark burrows, where the craziest Night Goblins brew the Mad Cap, bestowing both supreme bliss and swift death.
After a certain threshold, a loot pile becomes a hoard. Greenskins don't build vaults, but the next best thing – stash hideouts guarded by loyal boyz.
Only the bravest Goblins dare enter in those dark arboreal voids enshrouded with perilous bone-white veils.
The snarling and munching sounds are much more terrifying than those heard from the regular cages… and far more disgusting!
A towering citadel of infernal industry, relentlessly churning an endless stream of monsters.
