No one dares enter these eerily quiet grounds save the greatest of Khorne's Chosen, lest they face their doom therein.
Cultists round up local creatures – and people – to be infused with Daemonic energies, turning them into bloodthirsty monsters.
Monster-breeding pits and caves which will fill any witnessing mortal with revulsion and dread.
No Cultists serve in these monstrous spawning complexes, their work taken by brutish taskmasters chosen from the very stock they raise.
The underhanded nature of the Great Game dictates that, on occasion, Khorne's agents appear as the servants of another.
For now, subterfuge, but in the end, the world *will* be stained red with the blood of mortals, at the Murder Lord's vicious hand!
Think of Tzeentch's anger when He learns of double agents in His midst, doing the Blood God's hellish bidding and beating Him at His own game...
For Khorne and His servants, trade is a necessary evil to facilitate their true aims: to tip the world into eternal Ruin.
Such things are useful when brokering accord with other races, but the Blood God has no use for baubles – only violence, blood and skulls matter to Him!
Mortals, however savagely fearless, lack the intrinsic might of Daemonkind; they need external implements to even begin to balance the scales.
Larger iron-smelting operations mean better-equipped mortal fighters. Unusually, it's as simple as that.
Here lieth a military industrial complex of the heaviest metals and most raging of infernos.
Tusks?! Bones? Skulls. For the Skull Throne. For the Blood God's eternal glory.
Big skulls. Small skulls. Weird skulls. Skulls aplenty. Skulls.
Skulls for the Skull Throne! For Khorne!!
Marble quarries make ideal ritual sites, and are a great source of sturdy building materials.
In dark, blood-soaked pits, slaves toil to harvest Warp-infused marble who seethe with silent scorn.
Even Khorne's most loyal servants, savage and wild as they are, require healing after a battle.
Certain plants produce powerful restorative tinctures that even the most zealous of Khorne's Chosen find useful.
The Blood God has nothing against herbal enhancements – as long as the blood flows and the land burns.
Like others of their despicable ilk, Cultists of Khorne seek obsidian for use in summoning rituals... and for tearing rifts in the fabric of reality itself!
Khorne’s Norscan servants, such as Chaos Marauders and Chaos Champions, honour the Hound, protect themselves and frighten their adversaries with armour of void-black obsidian.

For sheer weight, and therefore force of blow, as well as its natural sharpness, Norscan swordsmiths have found nothing quite so effective as obsidian, formed in volcanic fires beneath the world’s surface.
Ceramic pots can be used to store flammable tar, acids, boiling blood and other defensive siege payloads.
Walls and buildings clad in ceramic layers can absorb impact from all kinds of bombardment during a siege.
Ceramics infused with Daemonic energies are just as durable as the strongest mortal-made steel.
Ordinary salt can nullify all kinds of spells and enchantments – a useful property to magic-hating Khorne.
Khorne's Cultists have become experts at torturing victims with salt, either for sport or for interrogation.
Salting the earth is the final wound to the heart of a dying world.
These particular 'spices' have little to do with the flavouring of cuisine…
Workers in 'spice' production facilities need to wear special protective garments, lest the fumes make them as volatile as the intended recipients!
Long term effects' and 'substance abuse' are foreign concepts to the Blood God.
Blood wine is a staple beverage among Cults of Khorne. The details of its production are stomach churning, yet it is nonetheless highly addictive.
Blood wine distilleries are a grotesque sight that would make any mortal recoil in disgust – unless of course they are already regular consumers!
Timber is a versatile and sturdy building material, appreciated even by Daemons, if only for its tendency to burn.
When other building materials are lacking, Khorne's hordes are ordered to stop burning forests and harvest them instead.
Massive strip-mining operations can deforest entire regions in mere weeks, fuelling the ever-hungry war machine of the Blood God.
Gnoblars don't play many games, yet the ones they do play are typically about inflicting injury on others – or each other.
Rotting animal carcasses and rusty traps are strewn around the Gnoblar Trappers' abodes, their smell overpowering even to their smaller brethren.
For all their haphazard behaviour, Gnoblars are an inventive bunch, especially when given copious amounts of scrap to work with.
The Halflings’ diminutive stature allows them to fit into their own cauldrons - a hearty snack for any Orc about to Waaagh!
Built from the ruins of the cold-blooded ones' city pyramid, these idols watch over the Bone Nose tribe and guard its fortunes with silent malice.
The Spotted Skulls tribe carved many sigils into the totems that protect their tribe from corruption of death tainting their lands.
Within the great plateau of this ancient construct is a monument to the Old Ones greatest failure.
If you want da biggest and meanest Boars, you go to da Iron Pig Tribe!
The shimmering, healing Emerald Pools of Itza now shine red with the colour of blood as Khorne's grip on this area is tightened.
Creatures that take flight flock to the Shrine of Birds. It is here Khorne's own flying Daemons meet these creatures and let their blood spill down to the jungle canopy below.
The Temple of Mists' enchanted fog protects no one as the Daemons of Khorne walk freely through it.
Ancient tradition deems every citizen of Ulthuan be a warrior. The local militia drills with the same discipline as the Phoenix King’s standing armies.
From the dogged defense of Tor Yvresse to the endless battles for the Griffon Gate, these rune-etched walls recall past defiance.
Modelled on the legendary gateway fortresses of Ulthuan's final lines of defense, this bastion’s elite garrison are sworn to die before they yield.

Constructed in the image of Lothern's famed Glittering Tower, this lighthouse-fortress is a beacon of Ulthuan's impregnable might.

Master shipwrights work alongside Mages of Saphery to weave enchantments of resilience into every hull, an exhibit of proficiency in naval artifice.
Unrestrained by the inner kingdoms’ rigid pride, the shrewd mariners of Cothique have long understood that power can be found in commerce as well as war.

Cothiquan sea masters have long acted as intermediaries with the outside world, knowing Ulthuan's nobility can more easily ignore those they never meet.
This harbor, built in the name of Finubar the Seafarer's philosophy, has become a Lothern in miniature – complete with its fracturing from Ulthuan's traditionalist court.
A network of sea masters moves like mist upon the waves, securing supplies through quiet pacts and the "liberation" of cargo from the Asur’s enemies.
Master silversmiths and gem-cutters practice ancient crafts, creating the exquisite jewellery and Ithilmar-filigree trinkets for which the Asur are famed.

Vintners and artisans from local estates gather in a display of serene and orderly custom. Even commerce is an art to the Asur.
From this guildhall the great mercantile families dispatch envoys to broker distant treaties, monopolising the flow of goods to far-flung colonies.
From the ports of Lustria to the shores of Cathay, grand ships embark to secure Ulthuan's global merchant routes in the Phoenix King’s name.
This trading house gathers the province’s bounty – rich wines from sun-drenched vineyards, rare spices, and potent medicinal herbs from ancient glades.
Inspired by the lucrative spice routes to the Far East, this bustling exchange attracts trade from across the globe.
The produce of these Isha-blessed lands is beyond compare. A cornerstone of economic power that grants Ulthuan leverage over the less enlightened nations of the world.
The promise of safety and civilisation under the Phoenix banner encourages colonists to settle nearby, fostering new communities far from their island home.
Tiranoc craftsmen are bound by the shared mastery of shaping light, resilient timbers into elegant instruments of war.
Elegant craft rest upon cushions of woven magic, ready to be drawn through the skies by noble Swiftfeather Rocs tamed and trained within these very walls.
Here, the most savage of beasts are broken to the harness and yoked to heavy war chariots, while engineers mount bolt throwers upon enchanted chassis.
The levy system decreed by the Phoenix King Morvael has resulted in a tradition of elite infantry that can be drilled in any humble surroundings.
The Sea Guard’s fluid fighting style is born from centuries of battling across rolling decks of warships and securing shores against overwhelming odds.
When the need is dire, all children of Ulthuan – from the noblest guardian to the most haunted outcast – answer the call to war.
While the warrior-scholars of the White Tower practice, Asuryan's anointed stand in solemn vigil. Watching over all are the sworn handmaidens of the Everqueen.
Like in Ellyrion’s sweeping plains, where young nobles learn to ride before they can walk, here the horsemasters drill ancient skirmishing tactics of the Reaver Knights.
In these hallowed stables, the noble sons of the Asur trade the skirmisher's bow for the heavy lance and don the iconic silvered helms that give their order its name.
It is said that to call upon the arrogant and aloof Dragon-riding bloodlines of Caledor one must promise them a battle worthy of song!
Defiant Phoenix banners rise in this fledgling colony, signifying the arrival of the light, order, and protection of the Asur.
It is important that Ulthuan’s beauty shines through the hardships of foreign soil, such is the length of time the Phoenix King demands an Elven presence here.
The ceaselessly marching Sea Guard patrol the colonists’ halls and groves. Every day, newly claimed plots extend the burgeoning city’s perimeter.
From an unfamiliar landscape, a cluster of ivory towers rises in domination of the local skyline; a beacon of perseverance against the world’s challenges.
This long-established Elven foothold has become a prestigious center of Asur hegemony, projecting unto the world Ulthuan’s eternal watchfulness from afar.
Few have ever stepped inside Aislinn's private quarters. Those who have do not gossip idly about it. Their silence only fuels the rumours.
Forged in answer to Norscan raids, the fleet’s nimblest vessels weave through shoals and reefs in steadfast service to the Dragonship.
The shipwrights of Ulthuan hew each Eagleship from a single trunk of majestic Starwood, forming an indomitable backbone of the Asur navy.
Bridges are sculpted and masts are grown, the living timbers of the vessel's hull carved by master shipwrights and blessed by the Phoenix King.
Honed by years of tumbling warfare upon the restless seas, these swift-handed crews lade the ship's hold with the spoils of war.
A Dragonship's Starwood-wrought hull is able to withstand great storms, devastating magic, and leviathan claws.
Cold and uncaring, the Lord of the Deeps is more respected than revered. Yet he can grant powerful boons for apt veneration.
The cold, dark depths hide things which strike fear and madness even in the bravest seafarers.
Armed and ready to deliver swift judgement hundreds of yards away.
Like clouds, their wings block the sun. Like rain, the arrows fall and drench the land in death.
Outriders always stand ready to fly ahead, either as scouts or to deliver a sudden strike in an upcoming battle.
Rows upon tight rows of pointed spears and lustrous shields stand at attention, ready for use at a moment's notice.
Every last item in place, every section in immaculate order: an unspoken saga of Elven military discipline.
The rhythmic clangs of well-trained combat manoeuvres sound almost like a song among these walls.
Incarnations of Hoeth's stratagems and the sovereign gaze of the Phoenix King are ever near, whether practising their deadly arts or keeping solemn vigil.
Soldiers gather the large feathers which fall below, convinced they bring courage in battle.
Restless and vexed by the sea, these fabled beasts yield only to the most skilled of handlers.
Beauty and grace permeate this place, both alluring and dangerous to those who dare peek inside.
Atop the highest spires of the Dragonship, this place seems almost ethereal, like a lucid dream.
A Dragonship gliding through the waves is awe-inspiring. With a majestic Dragon perched atop a great mast, the sight is utterly unforgettable.
Dragonships always have ample space dedicated to their ancient namesakes.
A visit aboard a Dragonship offers the rare boon of witnessing the finest sailors of the Old World at their craft.
While bothersome, bringing representatives of court aboard a Dragonship is often a necessity, as such vessels are beyond precious.
When Dragonships crest the horizon, friend and foe alike recall that these fabled vessels and their silver-helmed crew are never sent forth for parley.
These towering twin-hulled catamarans host a wealth of maritime purveyors, eager to show that Asur trade sails unbowed by war.
In the hands of an experienced admiral, this cumbersome behemoth turns into a devastating battleship.
Spacious and lavishly decorated, the halls of the Dragonship resemble a noble's mansion in all but function.
Pointed azure rooftops reach toward the clouds, presenting convenient perches for seabirds.
First, our enemies will see a bastion on the horizon, riding the waves. Then, the mists will flow out and they will see no more.
It is nigh-on impossible to comprehend the mastery of Elven shipwrights, capable of building such marvels of naval warfare.
The highest point on a Dragonship offers sights akin to standing the towering slopes of the Annulii.
Human seamsters never cease to wonder how the Elves manage to weave such exquisite – and expansive! – sails.
Maps and sea charts from across the world cover the walls, astonishing all first-time visitors.
The Druchii sail shrouded in cruel secrecy. Dawi ram the waves in smoke-belching steamcraft. Not so the Asur, their white sails gleaming swift upon the sea.
The plain, thick canvas mirrors the harsh life upon Ulthuan’s northern shores – a lifetime of grim vigil against the Druchii’s black sails and Norscan wolf-prows.
Ensorcelment weaves the hair of shriven priestesses into the sail’s fabric; a tapestry of solemn sorrow ennobling the very waves it rides upon.
Enchanted to be impervious to fire, so Phoenixes have a place to roost.
The father of the High Elves watches over his children no matter where they are.
Atop the highest spires of the Dragonship, this place looks ethereal, like a lucid dream.
The Sea Patrol are famous for their hardiness and discipline, yet their mess halls are full of animated discussion more often than not.
In this makeshift apothecary, several dedicated shelves contain herbs specifically intended to alleviate sea sickness.
As the Everqueen preserves the spirit and welfare of her people, her attendants minister healing and wardship to the crew entrusted to them.
When the fleet makes landfall, adherents of the All-Seeing Eye set forth, a blessing to any beleaguered host.
While bothersome, bringing representatives of court aboard a Dragonship is often a necessity, as such vessels are beyond precious.
This is a place to discuss politics, court intrigue, and diplomatic correspondence. Wise admirals avoid it.
The small cabin brims with heavy tomes, yellowed scrolls, and magical devices, the air heavy with arcane energy.
Students of the White Tower are not fond of sea travel. Those who choose a seafaring life are therefore indispensable to the High Elf navy.
These lofty places aften obscured by thick fog, as Asur Mages prefer their privacy regardless of where they are.
A Dragonship is large enough to accommodate an entire army, sailing the seas for weeks without seeing, or requiring, land.
Fine goods and treasures, ’confiscated’ by the Asur navy during military campaigns, are stored here for future use.
Ulthuan nobles drag their feet when it comes to military funding, so the Sea Patrol is constantly encouraged to ’live off the land’.
Deep holds are laden with enchanted racks and barrels of spell-fletched arrows, so that bowstrings never slacken nor bolt throwers fall silent.
The Dragonships draw upon the finest mariners of Ulthuan, the unseasoned among them betrayed only by the modesty of their cabins.
Wrought in austere grace, these quarters afford the seafarer solitude and meditation before battle’s onset.
So precise is the Dragonblade that when it cleaves the foe’s vessel, the appointed chambers of Asur officers scarcely tremble.
By necessity, the Dragonship’s crew are cautious where Eagleships are bold, methodical where Hawkships are rash, yet the result is always the foe’s ruin.
Asur archers pride themselves on their marksmanship skills, each equal to an entire regiment of sharpshooters from other races.
The Sea Patrol builds fortifications wherever they can, in case reinforcements are too far away when trouble strikes.
The most important Elven outposts train their own special forces for pre-emptive strikes and surgically-precise warfare.
Unlikely though it may sound, these holding areas have more amenities and creature comforts than some human settlements.
In the Elven sense, an Aviary is compact complex of perching pillars, mooring towers and landing pads for aerial vehicles.
Elven steeds are smart and hardy beasts, able to carry their riders through foreign lands far and wide.
An area of cleared land just outside the outpost, offering both visibility and opportunity to train for deadly mounted sorties.
Be it a small forest clearing or a vast open field, Elven charioteers perform with grace and blinding speed under any circumstances.
Quietude and contemplation suffuse this shrine, exuding serene wisdom; the perfect space in which to consume knowledge.
As one might hope and expect, there is always at least one blade resting against this Dragon-crested shrine.
Important outposts are guarded by dedicated local rapid-response force under an assigned Sea Helm, who can assemble a more-than-rudimentary defence in short order.
Whenever possible, the Sea Patrol deploys additional troops in troublesome regions, so local forces may be bolstered.
Silver sigils long-known to the Sea Guard act as binding points for the Elementals called upon to defend Ulthuan's will.
The most important Elven outposts train their own special forces for pre-emptive strikes and surgically-precise warfare.
Whenever possible, the Sea Helm houses additional troops from his retinue in more troublesome regions, so local forces may be bolstered.
Large and important outposts are guarded by dedicated local rapid-response forces, who can assemble a more-than-rudimentary defence in short order.
Caledorian rites chanted from atop this soaring tower echo into clifftop sanctums. Ancient, slumbering guardians rise.
The Asur back home might scorn the notion of venerating Mathlann in such open manner. The Sea Patrol is different, though their god may be indifferent.
A series of watchtowers act as stark monuments to intrusion, their masonry promising security for Elven trade – a semblance paid for with the lives of its garrison.
From white battlements, the eagle-eyed Sea Guard survey the land. Asur discipline secures the fragile seed of commerce below.
The safety of an Asur outpost is oft ensured at the ingenious intersection of military engineering with keen-eyed bestial vigour.
Aloof in every respect, High Elves are always polite to other races,  when on speaking terms, if not always respectful.
Real negotiations are conducted behind closed doors in well-soundproofed chambers; the journey to accord is not always a smooth ride.
As Ulthuan’s vast web of power extends another grasping thread, a berth earmarked for the Sea Lord's operations puts these waters under his watch.
A storehouse and headquarters hidden from enemy eyes enables the Sea Patrol to keep their Dragonships at maximum operational potential, regardless of where they are in the world.
These sea-lanes are no longer currents of chance – they are rivers, their courses tamed and directed by our will. Such is the finality in the argument of Asur Domination.
Beneath Ulthuan’s fluttering banners, a Trade Warden’s watchful eye and diligent record-keeping focus the outpost’s efforts on matters of import and export.
The wares sold here may not be as refined as goods produced in Ulthuan, but are quality merchandise nonetheless.
Everyone wonders why a master artisan would want to leave their homeland, but their expertise is always welcomed regardless.
The amount of quality goods on display is enough to make any non-Elven merchant green with envy.
The sensitivities of foreign relations require trade to be negotiated behind closed doors, but more importantly by someone who knows the way to profitable accord.
A humble venture serves as a depot for goods moving to and from an outpost, including a storage lockup used by newly migrated labourers and artisans.
Though there may be no better way to transport goods than by sea, the logistics of doing so from anywhere requires no small amount of forethought.
Establishing local connections with Asur charm and efficiency, envoys work diligently to help turn the hubbub of a new outpost into predictable sources of income.
Well-worn cart tracks long known to local merchants are hastily appropriated, giving immediate priority passage for Asur trade and diplomatic affairs.
The wares sold here may not be as refined as goods produced in Ulthuan, but are quality merchandise nonetheless.
Accumulating so many goods and resources in one place is a sign local business is thriving, while indulging the Asur tendency for flawless record-keeping.
Where a region possesses a resource deemed worthy of Ulthuan's attention, the trade branch shifts focus from general commerce to specialised acquisition and shipping.
This outpost's business has grown so vast it has earned a royal charter, granting it legal monopoly over the region's diplomatic and economic affairs.
The cart-rattling cobbles of all sea-bound routes must make way for near-seamless granite paving, keeping the open seas swiftly accessible.
This hub of elegance proffers a steady supply of locally sourced Asur goods. Fine silks, glasswares and wine are displayed for the appraisal of local nobles.
A place to stop and rest for the traders on their way to the nearby Elven colonies.
A dedicated location built to serve the nearby Elven colonies need for trader transport.
When Elven colonies reach a large enough size, they need a purpose built trading hub nearby.
Simple market stalls, for those wishing to do some trading.
Fancy shops, set up by traders who prefer to stay in one place than to bother traveling.
A purpose built market center where all manner of traders, big or small, can gather to do business.
Little more than well trodden dirt paths, but they do at least stop merchants getting lost.
Roads purpose built to improve the local economy.
Dedicated highways that can handle all manner of carts going about their business.
Elven ship crews practice combat both on land and at sea, in order to be able to respond to any given situation.
Even when far from home, Elven soldiers maintain their quarters in perfect order, as if the Phoenix King himself will inspect them.
Veteran Asur warriors maintain their chops here, as well as their slices, gouges and charges. No chinks in their armour.
Research is secondary to magical defence in these arcane quarters, where Elven Mages hone their craft.
Most Elves would scorn the notion of venerating Mathlann in such open manner. The Sea Patrol is different, though their god may be indifferent.
The mere existence of this incongruously ostentatious temple is borderline blasphemy among genteel Elven society.
Rough frontier logistics are usually overseen by an equally dour quartermaster.
The prices they set may well be outrageous, but their services are sorely needed nevertheless.
Commerce always finds ways to thrive, whether during times peace or war.
The Dwarfs grunt over their anvils; the humans toil and curse. Not so the Asur, who sing metal into its true shape.
Wrought of gold and gems from the Ten Kingdoms, here the reclaimed Phoenix Crown bears solace, yet also the bitterness of prideful errors past.
Time and again razed and rebuilt, the citadel endures upon the merciless Arnheim promontory, a campaign bastion and watchpoint against Druchii incursions.
“In rings of flawless order are the Asur moored, even within the gloom of the sea-cavern – ever watchful against Druchii corsairs.”
Marble needles encircle a colossal waystone, its ceaseless throb of latent power older than the Asur who now guard it.
Even the Asur – a race of memory and tradition beyond the ken of mortals – make pilgrimage here by rote, their reasons blurred by the vast passage of time.
A cruel history of poisoned tarns and felled forests marks these bleak fortresses – a reminder of a riven Oath of Friendship.
Sartosan ruffians scoff at the alabaster steeple that thrusts above the sargasso of rot, unwitting of the wealth drawn from the mangroves.
From the ramparts of charnel ruin, Asur eyes behold not wrath at its doom – but a mysterious certainty that stewardship of this bulwark is sacred.
Beneath the Tower of Stars, far from Ulthuan and kindred lands, the gleaming hosts are consecrated by the Loremasters of Hoeth.
In reverence, a flight of Moon Dragons shadows the elite hosts of Avelorn, forming the Everqueen’s retinue on her ten-year pilgrimage.
The attainment of war's spoils is no mere sport – it is an experience that helps brings one closer to the Gods.
Brass chains gird the menhir, their ends fixed to runic axes, driven deep into rough stone to anchor the jutting skull offerings.
Hexes traced in blackened blood profane the spoils of numberless civilisations, heedlessly heaped at the heart of the cairn’s gloom.
A brazen strike upon the plinth shatters the weapon of the unworthy, yet the blade of the Axe-Father’s progeny is blessed for reaving.
The earthen walls of this ritual mound soak with hymns of depravity, rousing the berserkers to feats of unimaginable savagery.
Brass for the brass chains! Bones for the bone path! Gore for the gore pits! – Gulkil Ruptongue
Wrought into a nightmarish comb pocked with pustulent clusters, this many-layered shale-hive is a marvel of decay.
A reeking, moss-covered monolith teems with plague-flies, their swarms attending Marauders who bleed offerings at the hatchery.
Corpulent rot-priests attend this urn of pus and mire to keep it ever bubbling, daubing eager raiders with sigils wrought in filth.
Warped by malice, Reavers loom transfixed before a fetish of skulls streaked with blood-matted hair and bashed into a formless scaffold beneath.
Before the crude effigy, the berserkers grapple in madness into the fen, whence the tar-black corruption births brutes of deeper malice.
A corpse idol amidst an unearthly moor attracts the fanged misshapen and rouses vagabonds to feral zeal in equal measure.
A shard draped in the flayed skins of softer races, silkier than cushion, masking the agonies whispered to all who linger.
Exotic flesh and clotted resins smoulder with fumes, mingling into a heady opiate that hurls devotees into a mad charge.
Passing beneath the coiling, entrancing arch, pillagers slough off all humility and restraint into a blood-drunk bacchanal.
Deep within the rune-carved basin, a shifting kaleidoscope of unearthly hued waters casts omens by prismatic fracture.
Along the spiral stair of this obsidian lump slithers an unbidden susurrus, its shadow never falling twice alike upon the earth.
Sorcerers' skulls lie arrayed in inscrutable geometry along niches of an umbral hollow, their howling litany dooming foes to Ruin.
As the edifice dreams of far-off gods, offerings seethe to hissing slag and coalesce into its blasphemy of quivering flesh and lifeless matter.
The dolmen's scabrous mass is veined with warpstone that drinks deep of the land’s lifeblood and howls a cacophony of arcane glut.
In the witching hour, feeble lords writhe in restless torment, slipping from one nightmare to the next beneath the totem's baleful grimace.
Day after day, the earth beneath the sheep gives way, sinking into a ghostly morass wherein they fancy the faces of their fallen.
Deep within the bog, fiendish thugs wallow in waiting until the calling of battle.
Crude yet ostentatious totems daubed in the blood of war-ruined victims challenge predators to approach and partake.
Vast burial mounds for the swelling Spoils of war mean less left behind and less effort required to leverage excess plunder for the tribe’s benefit.
Surrounded by stolen treasures glimmering beneath torchlight, warriors brawl and feast as warlords divide the spoils and barter wailing captives.
You couldn’t call what happens here "trade", but something between shouting, bartering, and violence that lets Marauders offload their surplus weapons to other aspiring madmen.
The tribe’s most hardened warriors gravitate towards great leaders willing to fight to death for the honour of leading the next raid.
The greatest favours of the Dark Ones do not come easily – blood must be spilt by the gallons; war must be waged!
In the lumbering Curs’d Ettin that dwell here, one witnesses firsthand the gods’ anger and cruelty visited upon the people of Norsca.
Unshackled living, even underground, hints that freedom is perhaps not so far away. It is the carrot that keeps the captives toiling and submissive.
As it was for the Bearmen who raided far and wide, the Hall of Urslo hosts the blood-oaths and boasts of plunder to foreshadow other bloodthirsty forays.
Many a Norse explorer’s spoils made their way into Losteriksson’s personal collection. Some believe his gem and barnacle-covered corpse will be uncovered any day now…
Relinquishing Chaos’ gifts to die as a mortal, Lord Mortkin retains remnants of the embittered gods’ power in the dimmed aura of his relics.
Upon these frigid moors is built a shrine to the Great Kurgan, one of the greatest Champions of Chaos to ever march from the north.
An ancient landmark of pilgrimage for raiders who make it this far, reminding them that these lands have never been safe from the predations of Norsca – and never will be.
From the mountain’s dark depths, ghostly echoes of Valmir Aesling’s gloating taunts still shame the Norse Dwarfs whose ancestors were left for slaughter.
A small sinkhole seized by the troop is kept littered with carrion and the uneaten battle-slain, attracting myriad priceless exotic beasts to exploit.
Even the most witless Trolls stay away from this predatory abyss, save those tasked with harvesting the exotic eggs and spawnlings within.
A cave sought out by Heroes and monster slayers alike, yet it makes a Troll’s dinner out of most of them.
Enticed by the unmistakable stench of other Troll activity, more disparately gather...
A Troll’s forest den rarely escapes the interests of aspiring Heroes and monster slayers, most of whom eventually end up as their quarry’s woodland fertiliser.
Trolls know no borders, heedlessly seeking out new dens and scavenging grounds where conditions are ideal for budding local bands to expand into.
Whether in a fortress of ice, gigantic mountainside cavern, or bottomless pit, the Troll King’s power amasses unseen from the ill-fated world.
A towering, overgrown structure known to local Trolls and visible to musterless bands, repurposed to attract Trolls great and small to the Troll King’s endeavours.
In time, those of Sayl's choosing follow the paths hidden to all but his mutated vision – leading allies to victory and foes to their doom.
Whether mundane war gear or the Chaos energies of the enemy arsenal, Sayl has just enough of a hold on the material and immaterial to withhold their strength.
During battle, a degree of milling confusion is inevitable. But prior to that, all needs to be in order. Sayl does not agree.
A whisper of uncertainty hovers in the air. Words on the shifting Winds – Sayl's wiles move in ways as insidious as he is.
Even as forces gather with uncanny ease, somehow nothing feels wrong… Until it does.
A little theft goes mostly unseen, as do the perpetrators… until those holding the treasury keys suddenly no longer do. Sayl will put them to good use.
An army brimming with strength and raring to go does not ask whence that strength came. Yet in the end, they will get their answer.
Cloying incense, subtle music and gorgeous silks fill worshippers with vivid visions of the Dark Prince’s triumphs.
Adorned to each grandee's personal taste – food, sport and adornments all provided by, and from, willing thralls.
The grandees are bathed in light most favourable, words pealing in sonorous echoes as the obseqeous form the floor on which their masters tread.
The pools are akin to a blessing from the Dark Prince himself, yet what fills them is no water.
A haphazard scattering of gifts to the glory and terror of Dechala – some of which occasionally twitch and moan, beset by swooping Furies and cavorting Daemonettes.
A sinuous tear in reality slashed across the lines of accumulated despair, whetting the appetites of whatever comes through.
A place of all-encompasing silence and velvety shadows, broken only by Dechala's soft hisses of preening self-regard.
Vast, opulent and uninhabited, save for mute, tormented souls, frozen in glassy terror and adulation – most fitting witnesses to Dechala's piques of vainglory.
Garments stitched from living skin, finely peeled, expertly cauterised and impeccably sutured, made with the tailor's own raw material.
Architectural works of art experienced only as one moves across the arrangement of red-hot floors, blinding window-panes and howling fluted columns.
A space of repose and contemplation wherein all previous sensations are woven into the fiber of one's soul.
Here Chaos Sorcerers receive an allotment of thralls, which they welcome in chambers draped in blood-stained satin.
Sorcerers are left to their torturous, obsessive musings as thralls offer themselves, body and soul, to strengthen their masters' magic.
Here pleasure is honed through the sweet torments of never having enough. Thus are laid the strongest foundations of Dechala's desires.
As appetite for sensation grows, it is at first as indiscriminate as the unformed longings that drive it.
Where indulgences are freely provided, no matter the cost to those that are tasked with providing them.
Here a thousand unslaked passions are given silken tongues. They haunt visitors with promises of excess, though their satisfaction is but an empty void.
As one climbs ever upwards, the longing for Dechala's perfection grows unbearable. Thus she inhabits the top of the palace alone – save for one other, to whom all of it truly belongs.
Cast away out of boredom by its mistress, or a plaything broken beyond repair by her enemies?
Many are admitted to this receptacle-filled antechamber. Far fewer leave after the receptacles are filled.
What is more graceful than Dechala's mesmeric progress across the spiral floors? What is more amusing than those forced to follow?
Performances never before seen. Songs of singular despair. Tales unheard of.  Afterwards, the audience are left eyeless, deaf and dumb – and next in line to perform.
At such heights, the vigilant Tormentors are properly sensitised to any presence, physical or otherwise, that would disturb their revels atop the lethal summit.
Embedded with glittering, gemlike shards, the tower suspends the watchers in a state of supreme, brittle awareness, ready to break into readiness for battle.
The Winds sough along a web of flickering nervous tissue spread across the ramparts, which forever thrums and chimes with predatory alertness.
Internal hierarchies collapse as these warriors vie for Dechala's favour and commiserate over her disdain.
Sword and scourge sing and snap with fevered grace as warriors suffer and celebrate each others' ordeals, ever closer to the day their mistress will lead them in battle.
Dechala delights in taking away the power which the Hellstriders bargained for, depriving them of their steeds so they thirst for it even more once they regain them.
Dechala's Chosen are made to learn that they shall be forever denied the Dark Prince's promise of perfection – but her own perfection is more than enough.
Walls strong enough to contain the misery that does not love company from without.
The watchers are held in place, eternally vigilant and longing for the liberating distances ahead, while their traitorous bodies make any such longing bitter and hollow.
Nothing steadies trembling hands and addled minds like forced labour to craft the tools of one's own misery.
Minds all but gone, what these creatures retain of the people they once were lies in their hands and handiwork.
A semblance of strength and selfhood remains in those that follow orders with a singular, desperate focus, making up for their deficiencies of the soul.
No dying. Not yet. There is worse to come, and we want to see it.
This offers neither – merely assurances that they are in sight. Somehow, it is enough, for a time.
Thralls do what they will with the implements of the surgeon. Sometimes the pain is wonderfully revitalising.
A smattering of wretches, aching to clutch at something, anything – yet hurting at the touch. Their mouths burn with nought but the memory of the Elixir.
Some grasp at a return to normalcy, yet are plunged deeper into a void of Dechala's making which they were tricked into believing is their own.
In these crammed quarters, senses' peaks and sensations' valleys mark nothing but the progress from one nightmare to another.
Its ruined denizens marked it as a place of terror. Its empty ruins are a different mark, in some ways a more benign one.
The inhabitants' denial of their home and hearth in favour of excess leave the rest susceptible to the same feverish despair.
Those who abandon this place willingly forsake all hope, offering it to their alluring mistress, while the few left behind are denied any hope of ever reaching her.
As the bladebearer's obsession with battle sharpens, so too does their blade.
Experiencing the minutiae of pain improves one's focus at inflicting it.
Mere defence is but a choice away from admitting you are no better than a thrall.
Does it matter how good the settlement's protection is when the settlement can *attack*? This is a Tormentors' Hold, not a Tower of Civility.
Watch for opportunity until your mouth waters in anticipation. Strike forth. Lash out. Lap up the last guttering remnants of the enemy's will to fight.
Preening displays of dominance, whether you feast or fight, is the atavistic stuff Chaos Marauders are made for. It is also how devotion to Slaanesh begins.
Those who seek to wield the scourge must be prepared to taste the flensing lash themselves.
Mercifully, apart from Dechala's irresistible presence, these supreme warriors have taken battle as their mistress, unlike their palace peers.
Aspirants of a certain sort gather here, who value touch above all other sensations, and the touch of steel on skin more than any other.
Mere killing is something even thralls can do. Murder is but an expedient triviality. Slaughter is for slavering curs. What is practiced here is a form of art.
Within the Ritual Arena, a tapestry of beautiful death is weaved that tears at the veil between the realms.
The destruction may have been a mere whim, or maybe an expedience. What is certain is that if defeat brought this on, it will never be acknowledged.
Here are stocked the steeds that carry both the fools and the depraved to war.
Within cages, scourges breed in writhing bundles, squirming for the taste of flesh. Steeds stomp the earth, tongues lolling in anticipation.
No snake is permitted to vie with the prowling seekers' sibilant calls – save for when Dechala enters. A serpent of serpents she may be, but she is *no* snake.
Furies squint from the ceiling with unlike calm. Daemonettes stand unmoving. Slaanesh has stilled their bodies, but their essence rattles with dreams of iniquity.
The orderly congregation is a sham. Service begins and the vestments of worship are torn away. Underneath, all is twisted, beastly, shameless and proud.
As the doors close behind you, each moment is a fleeting thing, mind wiped in a wash of sensation. On and on it goes.
The fields bristle with blades and the wild passions of sentinels honing their bladework as they watch for approaching threats.
Barbed spikes are thoughtfully provided for sentries to keep themselves alert and raring for yet more blood to spill – just not theirs.
After having their sport, the sentries' blood glistens in rivulets on their skin, their minds shimmering with awareness.
The Dark Prince’s icon is a locus to the excesses of his enthralled followers
To gather around the Dark Prince’s banner is to taste the joy and the dominion of excess.
No mere gathering place for Slaanesh’s servants, for this ground is sanctified to the glory of hedonism fulfilled.
Like an angler fish in the ocean depths, the glimmer of irresistible promise leads many to His darkness. The mightiest make it their home.
Even mighty champions cannot resist the mysterious allure of this gorgeous structure. Unspoken whispers promise the fulfilment of every desire.
None of the warriors harbour any doubt in their own perfection, yet all of them are certain it could never be enough. Such are the minds of Slaanesh's Chosen.
A monolith of intoxicating resonance enthrals abominables to pull the chariots of the zealous and bear the shrines of temptation.
Clanging steel, anguished shrieks, and rapturous laughter echo throughout the arena, as Chaos Knights hone their skill, egos, and devotion.
Cirienvel’s tragedy feeds the ground of this accursed clearing, as echoes of Daemonic shrieking bind the Dark Prince’s hosts in fervent unity.
Where marble plazas once gleamed and spires once shone with resplendence, the Dark Prince's supplicants cavort and revel among silken banners of excess.
Scattered runes lie on shattered crystal still radiating with Ulthuan’s magic, but twisted to infuse Daemonic ichor rather than suppress it.
The pain of the unanointed transmutes into empowering rapture. The pleasure of mortal desires transmutes into dark ecstasies.
Around slime-pools of bubbling filth loom malignant shadows of protruding stomachs. How they rumble with the stewing of meat maggots!
Strange dripstones writhing in slime and glowing fungi are usually a sign that Chaos has taken hold of a cave, and anything that dwells within.
Eerily still waters, an absence of local fauna, the stench of rotten fish… River Trolls are surely nearby!
In a deep grotto amidst soaring peaks, the mountain's immovable strength instills stone-like resilience in the things that lair beneath.
Also known as the City of the White Wolf, for Ulric is believed to have shaped its foundations himself.
Though Ulric's warriors are deadly devout, a reminder of their god's creed never goes amiss.
An inconspicuous structure, for Ulric cares only for courage and might.
Warriors gather to be inspired by Ulric's priests, whose words echo the will of the White Wolf himself!
None who wish to foil Nagash’s design will ever go unnoticed. None who wish to impose their domain upon his will even disturb a single fleck of dust.
What was forbidden before, now simply ceases. What outside force withered before now simply is unmade.
What these Ushabti guarded is no more. They are stripped of meaning. From now on, they are deadly possessions.
Whatever stood upon them is to be discarded, the way it should have been long ago. The horizon has a new master.
The sentinels in the sands need neither sight, nor other senses. There is a vast mind inside their hollow skulls, and that is more than enough.
The quicksands the horses died in have cowered away from Nagash’s gaze. Now they have been brought back to their riders.
In the past, they meant a way out into another world. That afterlife is now here, not elsewhere.
The space is never enough for the dead yet to rise. The former rulers of this place had the imaginations of beggars.
Where the living go to die, but not to rest. Those who watch bear the mark of the rope around their necks as well.
With the power of inevitability, an opportunistic Vampire's cunning flourishes, while mindless bones protect their safe harbour.
As it empties, it is replenished in short order. There are no gunpowder “accidents” – they do not exist.
Those dim-witted, mad or foolhardy enough to set sail with no second thought die on such shores. Under Nagash, *everyone* dies on these shores.
Here rise again those adept at plumbing death’s depths, before which pales every oceanic abyss.
The failures of these impermanent tools will be compensated for by the endless procession of cold, dead hands that wield them.
Swathed in silence, it gapes at the ocean, as if to swallow it. Greenish flames glimmer outside. Power gathers within.
The perfect form of spreading unlife has been achieved already, long ago. The debased contrivances of Vampires are only a facade.
Warriors and wretches, the worthy and unworthy – all are here. Ghouls burrow in to feast and the bones, picked clean, emerge to serve. Nagash permits no waste.
Buried with nothing, these remains claw their way out filled with the purpose they never had in life. Their crude weapons will not stop them from carrying it out.
The voracious creatures stalking the crypts have been commanded out. They roam this grove like their wolf-like counterparts, a pack of monstrous hunger.
Nagash wipes clean the maze of a Necromancer’s maddened thought. But the twists and turns of death remain, for Necromancers must wander along, to better feed Nagash’s hunger.
There is power in a living creature’s release from mortality’s noose. Yet the power amplifies, should the soul be utterly consumed.
None who serve Nagash hope for dissolution. They cannot hope. For some, dissolution may yet come, later rather than sooner.
Twice-risen is but a turn of phrase. There are those amongst them who cannot remember how many times it has been. They only know there will be more.
A place for those who have tasted death and do not wish to do so again. Their tastes have reddened, though the true death of all else save them remains inevitable.
Here worldly plenty dies to feed Nagash’s dark world-ending appetites.
These inanimate pillars overpower souls and render them inert. Henceforth, they are no longer souls but a part of Nagash.
As they grow, they glow and fold into themselves entire histories of death – that of people and peoples, of single settlements and sprawling kingdoms.
In the Lands of the Dead, life ends before it dares begin, so much has Nagash’s thirst for more power increased.
When all is fallow and barren, its emptiness itself become a new and even more potent source of power.
Those dead who still clutched their weapons as they perished now rise first to secure Nagash’s mightiest abodes.
When the gates open, they do only so death may come out in a clatter of hooves and the creak of bare bones.
The hafts of the weapons here can barely hold the weight of their pitted blades, yet both rise and fall with the finality of their wielders' intent, which is that of their master.
The defenders' dessicated voices are bolstered by the screams of mortar barrages and their targets - the sounds of death’s arrival.
Bodies long gone – souls unravelled by madness, grief or iniquity – are crushed back into shape and pulled through by sheer power.
The lumbering giants on its edges are chiseled in the likeness of death. Indeed, nothing less than death could wield weapons that can blot out the sky and pierce the sun.
The looming shapes are humanoid yet nothing like a human; a ship that sails itself on land. It wields a gun that shoots no bullets, but vortices of pure oblivion.
Even the most formidable Vampires cannot shed the the gilded finery and false glory of life. Nagash lets them wander these halls only to awaken them to the much greater truth.
Whatever the bones used to belong to, they are reknit and fused together at a word from Nagash, to assume the shapes of horse and rider.
Side by side the long-dead beasts and their riders emerge and silently assume their place, souls merged into their master’s single-minded intent.
Mounted warriors awaken and spur their skeletal steeds along expanses of black marble: shadows strike green sparks from black stone, beset by bloodlust in the name of the greatest shadow of all.
Walls and statues depict Vampiric glory as mighty exemplars wander the passage – some clinging to beatific visions of ancient superiority, others feverish with blood and triumph yet to come.
Amidst the sounds of bone and metal, stone and lacquered wood unite with a final solitary snap – a Tomb Scorpion has awakened. It is ushered out by Ushabti sentinels.
The boundary of Nagash’s domain will be measured by the reach of his Ushabti’s bows and the advance of his serpentine Stalkers. And the sky is a meagre boundary to stop at.
No feral instinct drives these warsphinxes as Necroserpents weave around their feet. But the warriors tethered to the serpents clack their teeth in bloodlust waiting to be sated.
The titanic effigies within the vast chamber once strode to war as images of Nehekhara’s divine overlords. Now they are a reminder of who these deities serve now.
Handmaidens test their wiles on greater Undead as intransigent as stone and sand. Only the most adept manage to spark a brief flash of their targets' former vainglory.
The inhabitants are both blacksmith and warrior. Both those who staked and lost their lives on either piety or profanity are equal before Nagash.
Loyal sentries whose existence only ever rested on their loyalty. Deeper within, starved ghouls cower at the passing of Wight Kings prowling their assigned domain.
Massive, ancient weapons scrape across the floor as the guards wielding them make their tireless rounds – less a patrol and more a part of some inscrutable ritual.
A dead, malevolent reflection of nature, much like its inhabitants – beasts that snarl and wrestle with the pillars of stone. Wings of bone and bloodlust carry in the air above.
Brutish hulks emerge from caverns on its sides to roar down into the depths. The call is answered from the waters at the bottom. Along the shores stand creatures made of malice and bone.
The darkness of a Vampire's ruthless soul and the insatiable bloody passions of their bodies have been cloven asunder and let fly – yet are bound still to him who made them so.
As deep as its inhabitants' ancient abode was high, Morghasts cling to the stone where their bones once rested. Nagash heralded their fall and now they herald his ultimate rise.
In these caverns, nightmares of the air and waters are unassailable proof that the gesture with which Nagash brought them to heel will soon encompass all nature and everything therein.
Here those who aim are also targets in turn. The only living thing here is the missile-agitated air.
The space is filled with the wails of sturdy guns and of fellbats carrying the ones who shoot them.
The noise is deafening - though the silence of deafness after a roar of deadly power has always been Nagash's way of war.
A half-drowned, cunningly wrought maze steeped in darkness. Crews stagger atop gargantuan Prometheans, death-numbed hands struggling with their firearms, overseen by Gunnery Wights.
They will remain dry, for Nagash has sapped some vital quality of their essence that would spoil them in the open. Fire and death is all they are meant for now.
It is strewn with once hallowed objects and mortal remains. Through them Nagash has drawn and locked away the souls once held in reverence. The skulls he shall hurl at his enemies.
The water crackles with frost carried from the cairns around. Wraiths prowl them, there and gone. Underwater, incorporeal forms flitter. All furiously cling to their existence, and Nagash's will.
Those who travel along these pathways need a wide berth, for they ride out to collect a heavy surfeit of souls.
The monolith is somehow capable of lulling a current of Shyish. This solid form imbues it into the Undead over vast distances.
Memories of one's former life pass the polished ebon surface, but in those who look upon them no trace of mortal yearning remains. They leave eyes sharp with clarity of purpose.
The march beyond it is a rite that fates Nagash's servants to a ceaseless advance and toughen them to that which may halt it.
Carved into the wall is a wilderness where life and death, the animate and the inanimate have been warped to Nagash's desire. Some of the monstrous shapes it teems with flicker.
Carved by Shyish and sharpened to a vanishing point, they likewise sharpen the purpose of those who chisel away and pierce through the Old World’s hoary illusion of permanence.
A gigantic horn mounted upon nothing, made of bones filed away to seamless smoothness, like the crude edges of the minds Nagash crushes into shape and calls to charge.
A pall of blinding size, utterly textureless – a weave no bleeding finger can achieve. A testament to overwhelming power none can oppose without being trampled into nothing.
The coin of sea-trade, for all its lustre, is a mere heap of rust. The coin Nagash’s ships carry is the same – a heap of rotting death.
The sea-trade’s promise of prosperity dissolves in the dark depths. The waters from which Nagash’s ships sail away carry those depths' guarantee.
The silence in which those ships are wrought is also what will follow in their wake. What Nagash considers even trade is to take. There is no “give”.
The ruin befits them - yet it is but a new beginning. As they grow again, so will the ruin they are a symbol of.
The yet-living prey is accorded this rare honour just to be driven into the clearing – and then driven to terror and death.
The red is blood. Those who provide it have no further use for it, though all who are picked carry warrior potential. They will never fulfil it in life.
After the animals leave, patches of their fur remain – the only part of them that stays truly dead.
It may have been cursed once because of the monsters within. Now it is cursed because of the ones chiseled out of its bare, cold stone.
What it yields will do for the spare adornments carried by the Ushabti’s ilk.
Only the blackest iron in the hands of Nagash’s footsoldiers can bring about the shade of the sky above the world he is about to master.
The murky glint of ivory – a promise of desolate purity.
What was shaped by tireless hands before is now also shaped by a will far surpassing those hands’ skill.
It is not the herbs wherein Nagash’s source of power over the Winds comes – it is in their death.
The fields tremble under hooves and wheels and sough with the voiceless cries of Undead warriors riding at hurtling speeds.
It is not the bones that must be excavated out of the clay, but the opposite.
A tiny piece of salt desert to hearken back to the vast sand deserts of Nagash’s exalted past.
Anything, living or otherwise, with a speck of magic is dissipated here so Nagash can feed on the accumulated power.
The trees themselves are unnecessary. Their stumps and the withering branches strewn along the earth are a good start.
*Something* has been wrung out of their husks by sorcerous means. It looks like a liquid and can be drunk. Docility follows, of the kind Nagash exacts.
Opening an earthly grave and turning the sky into one are all the same. The land-bound dead crawl up. Dead birds fall awhile, but fly again before they touch the ground.
Buried memories of something that, perhaps, existed. But even a grave may open again, in time.
Much of it is submerged, yet the work persists. The traffic of wordly goods has been supplanted by something of a different nature.
For once, the ruins are only that. The planks and stones will not take up arms – for now.
A seed of Vampiric vitality. Blood will make it flourish, but its fruit will be ashes.
A gathering of ragged souls, at most. But even this little is enough, sometimes.
The tombs will be made wider, and deeper. This multitude of last abodes will become one.
Chambers wide enough for crowds to pass through to the place where they will endlessly keep their vigil over their own graves.
It already beggars belief but, both above and below, it will only grow larger.
Death as far as the eye can see. But Nagash’s gaze reaches beyond it still.
A monument to the Supreme Ruler of the Undead. But where there is one, another will follow. And then, it will be one again, and that one will be all there is.
A place where death does not walk, at last… though for those with eyes to see it, death is never still.
Some pawns are not worth the costly inducements to make them stay in place and do the Lahmians' bidding. Those are simply removed or broken in ways instructive to the rest.
In diverting more coin to those whose whispers carry the farthest, our true nature will remain unspoken.
It takes little digging to uncover dirt on the local garrison commander, and even less effort to use a touch of entrapment to keep him and his cronies quiet.
Few questions are asked about bodies disappearing that would otherwise rot in the streets, particularly if you suppress the questions about how they got there.
A land increasingly afflicted by longer nights and walking corpses will provide more than enough distraction to keep the Coven working towards Neferata’s ends.
Every diplomat or person of influence placed under our thumb helps the Coven conceal its true nature.
Once a Lahmian has someone's undivided attention, she can distract them from anything she chooses, no matter their station.
It is often the most innocuous of places that sit unprotected, thus providing the safest refuge when the Handmaidens must lay low.
Few dare disturb unmarried maidens in their chambers after dark, and by this guise the Coven endures.
With the right Blood Kisses placed on the right necks, our tendrils extend deep into the echelons of power.
A lady need not resort to thievery when she is so often lavished with oppulent gifts.
The sisters never stop training in enemy lands, for tact is just another means to win the battle.
Every faked weakness lends credence to her ruse, whilst every lingering touch draws men into her trap.
A noble lady must never overstay her welcome.
Under the cover of deep night, when it is most improper to see maidens out and about, they study within their chambers to master the Coven’s ways.
The maidens of this Coven have become highly adept at achieving its ends, and training others to do so.
The sisterhood manipulates from the shadows, furthering the Coven’s creeping strength as it hides in plain sight.
Lahmia’s faithful revel in spinning destructive lies to further Neferata's ambitions, especially when they know eavesdroppers are nearby.
Vibrant settlements are ripest for the spread of the most inflammatory rumours, where running additional risks for grander plans is acceptable.
The earth is broken and sown, methods learned from the Glottkin's father.
Life begins to bloom, from gnarled vines to writhing maggots.
The Garden thrives, rot and new life, in the mould of Nurgle's own garden.
Well-tilled and full of life, the dream of the Glottkin's parents, twisted by Nurgle's fecund grace.
The Glottkin's new father looks on proudly to see the flourishing of life in all its forms.
The barren fields and lifeless groves nourish nothing – not even despair.
Skavenslaves beyond recount perish in gruesome labour accidents, yet more are hurled into the works without a second thought, their black blood greasing the contraption’s foundations.

Indistinguishable beneath their hooded robes and interchangeable in the eyes of their cruel masters, Grey Seer initiates toil deep within the apparatus’ entrails, amassing the one substance the Skaven would trust for so momentous an undertaking.

Wreathed in smoke and the arcing sparks of overloaded machinery, fiendish amalgamations of rat-flesh and warp-engineering strain and slobber beneath carts heaped with pig iron – struggling to satisfy the Engine’s ravenous demands.

Skryre engineers scuttle along the contraption's body. Its crude scaffolding of structural rods belies an intricate balance of interlocking warp-ductors and beam-amplifiers, crowned with the gaping menace of a three-pronged cannon snout.

The Grey Seers provide the finishing touches. Using thirteenfold-blessed pigments of ground Warpstone mixed with blood, they scratch-mark the Horned One's unholiest runes along the weapon-engine's length, all while droning wicked prayers.
Rat Ogres do not lack in brawn or ferocity – it is an improvement to their mental capacity to use a specially-bred Skaven that allows them to make use of Skryre weaponry!
Collaboration between Skaven clans is rare and unreliable – the incredible power of the Stormfiends is undeniable proof that if the Vermintide bands together, they are unstoppable!
A grim symbol of a realm slowly but inexorably strangled in the all-consuming grip of Chaos.
Once a pinnacle of Lizardmen dominance over the jungles, the pyramids lay wasted by the Vermintide.
The shimmering, healing Emerald Pools of Itza now resemble more of an infested swamp after the Skaven have ransacked it.
From the city's most reputable kennels come the fiercest and trustiest attack dogs, bred and trained to serve as the Empire’s elite hounds of war.
Once the heart of Athel Loren, its magic and roots are now intertwined with the vibrantly pestilential rot of Nurgle, as the sickly tree approaches the splendour of His very own garden.
His contemplations do not expand towards the world without. They suck it inwards and crumble it to nothing.
The roof glimmers with souls without number. Great or small, he can embody one of any size into his servants.
In this cavern-sized hollow , the Sigils carved are no longer meant to be read, but spoken. Nagash may have required the knowledge, but now all he requires is a word.
Grotesque mockeries of the Great Plan crawl forth from the primordial liquids of Chaqua's spawning pools, now befouled by the influence of Chaos.
In the Empire's northernmost reaches, far from "soft" Sigmarite influence, the Knightly traditions of the White Wolf take deepest root.
The memories of the Rat Spawn which littered it and that of past failures have died. Now its power can take root again.
The roots of death itself never wither. Nagashizzar’s grip has strengthened to now carry a measure of the mountain it was carved from.
Nagashizzar’s towering presence where Cripple Peak used to be has not diminished. It is the presence *within* which grows more powerful by the moment.
As the fortress nears the peak of its glory, so does the world’s glory fade. What is lost shall never be regained.
Nagashizzar’s dominion over its land is absolute. Nagash’s dominion over all lands is at hand.
Its midnight marble may drink all light, yet its echoing depths have yet to fill themselves with the power Nagash desires.
Awakened to its master's purpose - the purpose which led to the countless deaths of the slaves who built it by his absolute decree. It may now begin to fulfil it.
Forgotten presences within the pyramid stir and glow - of long-dead servants etched into its walls, body and soul. Yet more souls fill the halls in silence, made mute by Nagash’s word.
Only those permitted by Nagash dare stalk the depths of the Black Pyramid. None other would even endure the fulness of what it has accumulated.
Its shadow falls where Nagash wills it, for it is now his will made manifest. And where it falls, so does all else. First it falls in death. Then it falls in supplication.
Wrapped in obscurity, little dispels the impression that it is no more than a remnant of someone's idle dreams of what they lost long ago.
Dark shapes flitter to and fro. The sounds of bone on stone grate on the ear. Something stirs here, among the ancient treasure hoards.
Leathery wings and dark bodies widen and thicken the ever-present shadows. At the top of the luxurious towers lurk darker presences still.
The grasp of darkness is almost crushing. The memories of lost greatness are no longer just memories. The treasures have assumed a blood-red glimmer.
The darkness overflows. From now on, the hoarded finery shall adorn those who march forth to proclaim Silver Pinnacle's glory, disguising not the dread power underneath.
What was once a hallowed location of Elven worship is now reduced to a Daemonic monument to corruption.
“In the blackest gloom and breathless quiet of your deepest gnaw-hole, He watches.”
“From the death throes of the Skavenslave to the triumphant gloating of the Warlord, He listens.”
“Scratch this into memory, you fool-wretch. Wherever the Horned One points His claw, the Grey Seers follow!” – Grey Seer Kreaquill
The Wolf God's overbearing faith has failed its warriors and priests. Let them gnash their teeth in shame, and then let the Flame burn, a symbol of a God of Battle bested in his own domain.
Beneath age-worn azure enamel, a carapace of lacquered onyx softly gleams – a sepulchre for warriors sworn to eternal vigil.
This mighty Blood Dragon yearns to drink the blood of his enemies while it still pours hot from their bodies, and so they have set out upon their grisly conquest.
The Lahmian shall remain as secretive as she was in her lair, but her true work is now begun.
The Necrarch in this lair has imbibed the dust of their own secrets long enough. They thirst for fresh ones - and fresh blood.
The monster none wished to see desires to be seen. All shall take note and feel its vengeful claws and fangs.
A von Carstein has emerged from its lair, for a "lair" will not do. Their bloodline's dark legacy deserves far more.
Beneath this hidden Vampire Lair lies a sealed sarcophagus, where a Lord of the Night slumbers amid the spoils of their past conquests and tyrannies.
To celebrate their feats of strength, these cursed Knights drank blood from silver chalices, reciting ancient oaths of martial loyalty.
Long have these beautiful maidens trained in the shadows of oppulent halls to infiltrate the mortal world.
Rotting sorcerers may favour secluded towers, but it is there they hone their twisted power to harness the Winds of Death!
Beneath the damp, dark earth, where few else dare to tread, monsters embrace the beast within.
For the noblest Vampiric bloodline, only the finest castles sufficed to suffer an eternity beside the peasantry cattle.
Those who were once enslaved to their master's will, feel the chains tighten around their neck once more.
One who has prowled these lands for centuries knows precisely where the locals dig their graves.
Despite gruesome rumours, foolish mortals have forgotten to burn their dead.
A loyal mount recognises the smell of their master's flesh, even as it rots.
A Vampire's loyal Necromancer serves long beyond their own untimely death.
Another chance at immortal life will indebt even the most ambitious of one's servants
Why go to the trouble of sourcing a competent Necromancer when one waits just beyond the grave.
Necromancers flock to those who have proven willing to trade their dark secrets.
Only the most confident Necromancers would risk their immortal lives before a freshly woken Vampire.
An opportunist always prepares for the chance to be woken once more.
Only the most loyal servants would lavish their master's vulnerable corpse in treasure.
Ancient and macabre treasures yearn to taste blood once more…
One must not let rival Vampires get their unworthy claws on the sources of one's power.
Seasoned Vampires know that isolated lairs are far too vulnerable against snooping Witch Hunters.
Necromancers that seek out their risen master know their eagerness and knowledge of rival lairs is sure to please.
Ancient knowledge is highly guarded, except within one's own bloodline.
Vampires are the most feared of the Undead because they retain their devious intelligence and ambition.
The gift of undeath only enhances the natural strength of a warrior.
Only direct decendants of the ancient bloodlines wake ready to dominate the night.
Here Nurgle's faithful congregate joyously in the Garden. Those that fall during the festivities are trodden underfoot, becoming nourishment for the soil.
The power of rot and numbing despair heightens the connection to the warp. Nurgle's magic is accessed more freely, with the dead so close underfoot.
The nourishing rot spreads far through the soil, the ground itself a conduit for corruption.
Tendrils of decay burrow deep beneath the earth, spreading the comforting touch of Nurgle to all, far and wide.
Great, teeming pits of filth and life, birthing the most virulent and fecund acolytes of Nurgle.
The great beasts erupt from the fruitful earth, enduring and propagating the vile pathogens they were born alongside.
The prodigious gardens of Nurgle, disgorging the blighted creatures that swell his armies.
The foetid, swarming masses of Nurgle are birthed here, their existence is devotion manifest.
Giant, looming fungal stalks release spores high into the air, spreading Nurgle's touch and settling on the unseen.
The spores become more virulent and more deadly, reaching into hidden tunnels and passages, forgotten by the mortal, but not by the floral.
The stalks, grown to new heights, spread the spores to the air currents above, letting them drift to the nearby areas, falling like malign rain.
The defences of the garden are, as life itself, forever in flux. Forever regrowing.
The wall of life and death meshes together, leaving fewer and fewer gaps.
Each section is covered with pox-coated thorns or strangling vines. A cornucopia of dense, varied growth and decay.
Nurgle grants boons to those that prove their devotion, shown here with flourishing, unbridled life. Rot, in all its forms, piling high amongst the foetid earth.
Mires of decaying grasses ensure the strains of rot, as well as the creatures that live among it, are always plentiful.
Rewards of abundant growth for the servants of Nurgle are given, if the ground is fully saturated with his power.
Further strata and canopies of growth and abundance can be harnessed to Nurgle's designs, nourishing the whole, and nourishing the cycle.
Memory is woven into disease. New creatures born here recall morsels of former experiences.
The barrier between the material world and the warp is stretched sinew-thin, allowing Nurgle's gifts to pass through.
The birthed ranks of Nurgle's armies are imbued with resilience and echoes of those that once lived. A beautiful and horrible cycle.
Growth springs from the virulent soil, spreading to the far corners of Nurgle's Garden.
Life is encouraged across the Garden, but here, it is concentrated and nourished without bounds, spilling and reaching far and wide.
The sheer potency of life, arrayed in all its forms, blurs the barrier between the material world and the warp. Little pleases the Urfather greater than this.
Nurgle values life above all, but he always has need of favour. Unique plants, flowers and even insects can fetch a price with those who will trade.
Valuable herbs, with a variety of applications, can be cultivated and exchanged with apothecaries, sorcerers and herbalists.
Bespoke strains of plant or insect life, cultivated to bring potent favour for those who desire to trade.
Nurgle's Garden teems with unbound life, and death to balance. There is little that could be wanted that does not exist within the Urfather's groves.
A patch of ground, dedicated to cultivating the deadliest strains found within the Garden. No trifling task...
Various strains are adapted to reach the desired virality in a shorter time, as well as spreading further before symptoms become apparent.
Strains mutate and buboes flourish, the death of mortals becomes a foregone conclusion at your hand.
The cultivation of the deadliest strands of plague is an act of gleeful worship for those favoured with the task.
For those afflicted by the pleasantly abhorrent strains of maladies flourishing here, a fertile death arrives in moments, and the Garden is nourished once more.
A Knight and his retinue are sent to lay claim to a portion of this settlement for the Lady.
This district is claimed by the peasants of Bretonnia and their Knightly masters.
Bretonnians are not averse to establishing colonies beyond their traditional borders. Araby has long been a favoured destination.
In order to tear down civilisation, perhaps it is better to start from inside it?
The overgrown lair that is the Beastmen district will be the place where a settlement's collapse shall surely begin.
A Beast-camp within the very walls of civilisation will ensure it is destroyed from within.
It is not unknown for Norscans and other hardy folk of the Far North to wander down and establish outposts in allied settlements.
A larger outpost of the northern tribes, who have been granted an area of the city to skulk and fester in.
A colony of vicious tribesmen that even harbours the more devout and fearsome followers of the Dark Gods.
A hoard worthy of a true conqueror of worlds.
Battle-worn banners planted in the corpses of the fallen; the Dark Gods celebrated.
Be wary when you stare upon the symbols of Chaos, for such sights can pierce the very soul.
Accept Ruin and corruption into your black heart. There is no other way but down.
Among the carnage and the rubble and the lost souls, it is here that the Ruinous Powers erect their twisted monuments.
Be they men, Dwarfs, Elves or Goblins, flesh in all its forms can be found here, ready to be put to best use.
Those foolish enough to challenge the Dark Gods’ foothold in this world stain these ramparts with their blood.
The despairing faces of the damned stare out in warning to all who would dare enter this terrible place.
Nothing saps courage from the foe like a mighty wall of iron and corpses.
More than a mere graveyard, here the dead remain awake serving a master who is abroad for now.
This district is haunted – only the dead roam its silent streets.
This necropolis rises high into the skyline, casting the rest of this settlement under its ghastly pall.
The Dragon Emperor's presence is everywhere. This outpost is a haven for both trade and his spies.
Eastern districts, surprisingly common in the Old World and beyond, are where exotic goods are stored and exotic street food is consumed.
A larger district of Cathayan subjects, this area will be full of merchants, soldiers and many spies.
Legend has it the Dragons passed the secret of black powder to their subjects, which was then spread across the world. Within, the powdermakers concoct that very recipe.
While powder houses are located remotely in case of 'accidents', towers use height to minimise the risk to neighbours in more densely populated areas.
Designed by Nan-Gau's master War-Artificer, the Sky-junks are wonders of Cathay's military; logistical boarding challenges are overcome by tall mooring towers.
Convicts of the Dragon Empire are oft-sent to the Great Bastion. They are the brunt – the first of its defenders to face northern invaders.
Injured defenders will be sent to the Great Bastion's network of hospices, where monks practised in the healing ways of Yin work their magicks.
Shrines dedicated to various ancestors and the Dragons themselves bring a sense of being, and restore the Wu of any lingering Cathayan.
The temples built into the Great Bastion not only bring health and strengthen the spirit, but are blessed by the Dragons themselves.
The mighty pagodas that line the Great Bastion are powerful shrines, said to be in the vicinity of gigantic Sentinels that rest in the wall itself.
Watch Masts are small, incredibly tall platforms with only room for two sentries. They are positioned regularly and reduce the need for constant patrols.
The more Barracks there are along the Great Bastion, the better the defences and the lower the pressure on regular patrols.
Fitting accommodation for officers and their garrisons, allowing the soldiers to focus on the defence of the Great Bastion.
Larger emplacements that jut out from the Bastion's north side give greater views of the Red Waste beyond for a more efficient defence.
Command Towers dot the Great Bastion; they are the strategic centres where the defence of the wall is co-ordinated, allowing for greater focus of resources.
Great stocks of bamboo and hardy redwoods are harvested and taken to the Great Bastion's lumber piles to ensure a ready supply of blessed wood.
The mills of the Bastion are filled with the buzzing of saws, shaving and shaping the lumber for use up the wall.
A network of workshops and forges that span the foundations of the Great Bastion, fashioning weapons and siege defences for the defenders above.
The largest foundries are spaced several leagues apart but are fed ores and labour from Nan-Gau and other smaller cities along the Bastion's length.
At the top of the wall, at regular intervals, are the arsenals of the Great Bastion, each filled with the freshly-forged weapons of Nan-Gau.
Water points placed at regular intervals along the wall ensure patrols remain refreshed and alert.
The garrisons of the Great Bastion are well fed and provisioned to ensure strong defenders and more-able bodies man the wall.
Feast Halls are used when patrols from a far section of the Great Bastion reach another garrison. It's tradition that the guests are made welcome by the home defenders.
Tea is served high in the parlours, for that is where the officers gather to exchange intelligence, discuss patrol routes and other business of defence.
Atop the Bastion Pagodas are the Grand Parlours, where the highest-ranking officers meet – accompanied by their retinues – with their peers to discuss defensive strategies.
The Great Bastion has many gatehouses along its sprawling ramparts at regular intervals. Below each is a gate allowing ingress into the Dragon Empire when opened.
Standing Sentinel over the Great Bastion are tall towers festooned with flying lanterns and ribbons of warning, each one containing a lethal array of defensive batteries.
Citadels of the Great Bastion are placed every few leagues. They are heavily garrisoned and from there patrols of hundreds across the wall's causeway.
Strongholds are massive emplacements within the Great Bastion, containing thousands of stern soldiers and arrays of lethal mechanical and arcane weaponry.
There are fewer than ten Fortresses across the breadth of the Bastion, but they are strongpoints – cities within the wall that hold countless troops.
This Bastion lies in ruins. Only the architechts of Cathay could restore this bulwark.
Peasant horses are kept in loose pens or corrals. Horses are not common in such households, so the loss is devastating when the beasts are conscripted.
The stables of the Jade Lancers, are palatial liveries where heavy warhorse are kept in prime condition, ready to ferry their riders into battle.
Longma are said to share the blood of the Dragons. They are winged and scaled mounts, whose elite riders make them the most lethal cavalry in the world.
Only the Dragon Guard and their serfs reside here. Trespassers enter under pain of death.
Some of the most prized weapons within the Celestial Empire are kept within, especially the powerful Celestial crossbows of Kunlan.
A break in the wall, allowing for a rampart where gunner and rocket positions can be taken.
Reinforced areas of the wall that jut out allowing for permanent artillery emplacement, be they cannon or rocket.
