Usually situated in the same noxious district as the tanners, a dye-maker’s plant also spills out fumes.
Huntsmen are known for their skill with a bow. Camps are where they launch their forays into the forest.
Lodges are located deep within the forested hunting grounds, where hunters gather and store their prey.
It is not just meat that has its uses, skins and furs do too - at the tannery.
Gold has ever been lusted after by both men and Dwarfs. Small mines dot the Old World, their owners hoping to strike big.
On discovering a substantial seam of gold, a small mine gets larger and needs fortifying against other treasure-seekers.
Once recovered from the mountains, gold is smelted into bars or minted into coins of the realm.
Iron ore is a necessity in a world that craves weapons and armour. Smaller mines usually comprise a single shaft.
Iron mines are the most common underground works of both men and Dwarfs.
Iron smelters process the raw iron ore, so it can be turned into steel or fashioned by smiths.
The Old World has very few master swordsmiths, for they are the finest craftsmen in the realm and always in demand.
Marble is used in opulent residences and grand halls. Where large deposits are discovered, a quarry is constructed to get at it!
A stone cutter fashions large hunks of stone, for ease of transport and in preparation for construction.
A mason is more than a mere stone cutter, he adds craft to the role and is able to form grand shapes from his chosen material.
There are farms that are little more than tiny, muddy fields, on which graze scrawny goats or cattle with shrivelled udders.
Larger cattle farms have more land and better, more permanent, housing for the animals they keep.
Milk and beef from cows, mutton, pork, and goat are all valuable commodities in a hungry nation.
Warhorse breeders excel at sourcing the bravest and finest destriers for stud.
Unsurprisingly, clay pits hold vast amounts of clay, a malleable material that hardens when baked.
A potter is a craftsman who fashions clay into pottery and other ceramics, from fine crockery to the most basic of bowls.
Kilns are large ovens mostly used by local potters, who bring their merchandise to be baked prior to sale.
Brine wells are where solidified salt is mined. It’s an unpleasant and hazardous job, but perfect for the underclasses.
Larger brine deposits need more intensive mining, so more pits delving ever deeper into the ground.
These facilities are used for breaking down and grinding brine, as well as extracting salt from bodies of saltwater.
Wood is an ever-needed resource, and yet the forests of the Old World are not safe places to harvest it.
Wood in its natural form is hard to work with, so the timber mills turn it into lumber ready for sale.
Lumber yards are wholesale markets where wood is stored in great quantities before being shipped to its final customer.
Woodworkers, while not as skilled as carpenters, are as fundamental to the realms of men as builders and blacksmiths.
Smaller vineyards can be nothing more than a farm with a few rows of grapes, with a yield hardly worth taxing.
The Empire’s southern provinces have a modest wine industry, but nothing compared to Bretonnia's vineyards.
The great winemakers hail from Bretonnia, although the states of Tilea and the southern Empire have a few as well.
Proper roads facilitate trade and encourage travel. Bandits tend to be put off, lest they meet the Emperor's agents along the way.
Public works must be paid for; invariably, it is the ordinary man who foots the bill.
The Empire is riddled with homesteads, farms and tiny groups of sullen houses filled with sullen folk.
Villages dot the Empire, usually comprising a marktplaz, a tavern, and a stockade – if their denizens are lucky.
The towns of the Empire are walled islands of civilisation amidst the unrelenting and hostile wilderness.
Cities are massive places, crammed with ramshackle buildings – all teeming with the stench of mankind.
The greatest cities of the Empire are self-governing capitals, more powerful than the provinces they sit within.
Many places have a local smith – skilled at shaping metal but usually good at cracking troublesome skulls with his hammer as well!
Armouries are massive storehouses brimming with weapons of war to outfit the regiments of state troops.
Stabling yards are where the young nobles train with their steeds, leaning to shoot from the saddle.
Liveries are more than mere stables – they are where the proud warhorses of the Empire’s Knights are kept.
A place to hold the many dangerous and exotic beasts that would otherwise dwell in the wilderness.
Smaller taverns are often little more than rooms with kegs of ale stacked along one side of a hay-strewn floor.
Man’s villages and towns across the Old World are dominated by taverns as much as any smithy or general store.
Coaching Inns are large establishments with rooms and stables, found on busy trade routes or in large town centres.
Up-righting wooden shafts to create a stockade or a low stone wall may hinder the enemy, but will not keep them out.
Cities are usually ringed by high walls of stone to defend against threats within and without the nation’s borders.
The largest of settlements will have great walls, many feet thick, and reinforced with pillars of stone.
Wizards are wanderers and often loners by nature but, should one or two of them meet, a conclave is formed.
The Colleges of Magic are located in Altdorf, although the Orders have campuses in cities across the Empire.
Wizards come in all shapes and sizes, and if this gargantuan tower is anything to go by, so too do their dwellings.
Sigmarite Shrines vary from roadside memorials to more substantial chapels that hold a small congregation.
Temples of the Sigmarite Cult are bedecked in holy comets; they are altars to the Warrior-God – founder of the Empire!
The grandest structures of the Sigmarite Cult are the cathedrals dedicated to Sigmar’s worship.
The stinking, stubborn War Boars are kept in sties, where visitors smell them long before they see them.
When does a sty become a farm? When there are lots of Boars there.
Goblin Big Bosses have a big tent, bigga than the lads’ tents with more skulls on it.
A status symbol, a show of the Boss’ rising power and a place he can "ang me boots".
A Boss with his own camp to keep his boyz close is to be feared.
Another ruined Karak now lies dormant, a vestige of some upstart's attempt to dominate Dwarf lands.
Another ruined Karak now lies dormant, a vestige of some upstart's attempt to dominate Dwarf lands.
Greenskins love their gods, so will quickly carve effigies of Gork and Mork out of stone or other materials when they settle.
A totem pole rises above the shacks and tents of the Greenskin settlement as a sign of its success.
A boss pole is a material reminder of how powerful a Warboss has become. It's a mark of great power.
Wolves are rarely penned in, for to keep such creatures against their will is a mistake.
It is in the gloomiest, dankest parts of the forest where the Spiders make their nests and lay their eggs.
Deep in the forests, the children of the many-eyed and many-legged 'Feasters from Beyond' lurk.
Goblins have keener sight than Orcs, so the "scrawny gits" generally man the watch towers.
Orcs that get guard duty are not the Boss’ chosen boyz, they probably skulked at the back during a charge.
When something is guarded by a garrison of Big ‘Uns it must be important.
A pile of shiny stuff is what the Greenskins have collected from raidin'.
A heap of shiny stuff is like a pile but bigga!
A hoard is not just a heap but multiple piles of shiny fings!
The boyz need big open spaces to swing their choppas about.
A large area set aside for the belligerent gits to slap each other about.
This is where Big ‘Uns are forged and many teef lost to gambling.
The meanest and strongest of their kind, the Black Orcs rarely mix with others, preferring their own barracks.
Trolls can be found in their foetid lairs – dank caves or burrows, ankle-deep in rotting bones.
Less of an actual hut, more of a rickety, dung-smeared shelter built over an overpoweringly foul-smelling mudhole.
Giants, descendants of the Sky-Titans, are more likely to be found in the stompin' groundz than anywhere else.
Shamans often order other Orcs to pile detritus and debris in mounds, to create Rock Idols via obscene rituals.
Wharfs are platforms jutting out of the water, allowing ships to be boarded easily.
Whether man-made or natural, a harbour is a place for vessels to wait out Stromfels' rage.
Large port-cities are strategically key during wartime, for they are home to its great fleets, both military or mercantile.
In dis cave, da boyz often discover shiny rocks that may well be worth a few teef for da Boss!
Some pits are for throwing useless gobbos down, others have gold and other shiny stuff in them. Send in the sniffer squigs and claim it!
Taking mines from da stunties gets their beards in a real twist, especially when da boyz nick all da shiny rocks in ‘em as well.
Da Black Orcs don't mix with da other gits and prefer ta 'ave dere own fire ta throw stuff into.
All Orcs like to "'ave a go" at something big, hoping to claim not only its teef, but the hide too.
Goblins, being consummate tinkerers, have figured out that a great big saw is a way to cut up wood… "and yer mates!"
Smaller Greenskin tribes and gatherings rarely stay put, although they will seek out caves when they wish to keep "outta da way".
Orc and Goblin tribes are, in the main, nomadic, but will set up a large camp when the Boss wants to stop for a bit.
When the crap-pile gets too big and the horde of shiny stuff too large to shovel on a cart, it’s "time ta stop moving".
Greenskins like a good fort, it makes them feel important when they can shout and fling excrement from the walls.
The biggest and bestest Warbosses rule from formidable strongholds - the shattered Karaks of the Dwarfs.
Shamans live apart from their green-skinned kin.
Night Goblin Shamans tend to reside in hovels - mouldy lairs deep underground and surrounded by fungal patches.
A place of deep trances, where ghostly green images are projected above furrowed brows, and monstrous conjurations are invoked.
If a camp is "stayin’ put", gobbos will be sent out to dig a ditch around it as a basic defence.
Large stakes of pointy wood and other ramshackle defences of timber and bone are surpassingly effective.
A big wall is a good way of stopping an enemy from "gettin’ in".
The smartest gobbos can be right tools, in more ways than one!
A few Goblins have a base understanding of concepts such as physics - much to the disgust of their fellow Greenskins!
By making deadly war machines Goblins can grudgingly get the resources they need to make even "betta stuff".
No one truly knows when and how Dragon Ogres gather, but they always assemble on ground sacred to their ancient pact.
Where the Shaggoths go to invigorate themselves, standing upon mountain tops to bathe in the tempest.
A forge, deep within the Chaos Wastes, is no mortal smithy. Likewise the Hellsmiths hammering in the fire.
Within the hell fires are the Daemonsmiths, creators of fell and ignoble machines; grim chariots pulled by grim creatures.
Giants stride the world, mostly in an intemperate stupor. Those that wander too far north are enslaved and corrupted by Chaos.
Much like Warshrines, grisly trophies carried in the wake of Chaos Knights may attract the eyes of the Gods.
When a Chaos Knight's trophy haul becomes too large, a more permanent structure of bone and skulls is needed.
The preferred route of the magic-using servants of Chaos, an arcane vortex is for the damned alone to step into.
A tear in the fabric of the mortal realm from which Daemons and other horrors can - and will - emerge.
The Marauder tribes have no sense of place, wandering the northern wastes until drawn together by relics of power.
To prove their might they fight in the trial pit, from which only the chosen emerge.
The Marauders spar upon the bloody field, desperately hoping that the Ruinous Ones will notice and perhaps show their favour…
The tribes of the far north set up camps, not for sustenance but for worship and bonding under Ruinous scrutiny.
When warbands gather along tribal lines, they have likely been summoned by their Ruinous patrons.
Chaos' multifarious warbands range in size from small groups to veritable hordes.
When the omens are strong, the Unholy Legion converges.
Only Everchosen have sufficiently risen in power to command a true Warhost of Chaos.
The lairs of Trolls are foetid and disgusting; the further north they are, the more disturbing they become.
Stashed within this filthy lair are the trinkets and plunder from myriad battles fought in Ruin’s dreaded name.
By planting an icon in the ground, a siren call is sent forth that Chaos Warriors must heed.
Glorifying acts before Ruinous altars are summoning rituals that draw the most powerful of the Gods' mortal followers.
Warshrines attract the attention of the Chaos Gods, along with the mightiest of their mortal servants, for power attracts power.
A collection of infernal weaponry, some plundered from southlanders, some fashioned by the Hellsmiths.
Within the damned reliquary is stored the true weapons of power, culled from temples and secret places beneath the world.
Orcs like to eat, and they’re not choosey - game, enemy corpses and even their mates are all potential menu items!
While Greenskins will eat meat raw - they certainly have the gnashers for it - they do, in general, prefer to have it cooked.
Squigs are choice morsels – there aren't many Orcs that can turn down a roasted one!
Greenskins love to fight, as we all know, but there are more mundane tasks that still must be performed.
Even the Orcs realise that for wood to be a building material you need to do more than pick it up off the floor.
Sawn into boards, wood is ready for use in war engines, fencing, huts, and even just planks for spanking unruly gits!
The Father of Bears cares little for grand edifices, but in Kislev bear caves or standing stones are considered sacred.
Shrines to Ursun are rare, but temples are even rarer, with only the sacred groves in the capital and Erengrad known.
Wharfs are platforms jutting out of the water, allowing ships to be boarded easily.
Whether man-made or natural, a harbour is a place for vessels to wait out Stromfels' rage.
Large port-cities are strategically key during wartime, for they are home to its great fleets, both military or mercantile.
A shrine to Ulric, the God of Wolves, Winter and Battles and the patron of Middenland.
Normally found in northern towns and cities, the temples of Ulric answer to the great castle-shrine in Middenheim.
Some beasts are near-untameable, but at least you can pen them up until you have use for them.
Mutating energies of Chaos constantly infect the many wolf species of Norsca, producing all manner of lupine abominations.
Within these caverns, local tribesmen leave offerings to keep the ferally-mutated champions at bay.
The various Norscan depictions of the Ruinous Ones are put on display for all to see.
Mysterious shamanic ritual helps bring even the most powerful and destructive leviathans under the warband’s control.
Roaring pits and cursed ravines are conduits for Chaos' mutating influence between ground and sky, twisting nature into the Northmen’s living weapons of war.
Here the Winds blow strong, but less so than in the changing lands of the north… Still, beware the things nesting in these crags.
Frozen tunnels under the ancient ice harbour unimaginable nightmares, offering no shelter from Chaos’ mutating influence.
Deep within an icy labyrinth strewn with the gnawed corpses of once-mighty heroes, sits the Troll King’s rocky throne.
Norsemen guard their possessions and keep themselves safe from the harsh land's many predators.
Watch Towers are erected if a settlement grows to the extent that it is considered worth guarding against external terrors.
The militia forced to protect the camp tend to be angrier, more bloodthirsty, and hell-bent on having their day.
Savage northerners subdue the very beasts softer folk burrow and fortify against – set now as frothing sentinels and prowling ward over their crude halls.
In the harsh north, to wage war is to subsist.
Vast rewards of war flow in freely to those adept at the art of perpetual killing.
A place to stockpile the trinkets, jewels, and treasures pillaged from those now either enslaved or dead.
To preserve a tribe’s strength, young warriors are sometimes pitted against beasts before one another. The weak perish quickly.
When not called upon for full-scale invasion, the Northmen frequently amass to mercilessly pillage the farmsteads and villages of the civilised races.
Although universally bloodthirsty, barbaric and fierce, Norsca's squabbling tribesmen are swiftly united under the gaze of their gods and the revelries of glory.
A monument dedicated to the Crow God has been erected here – all will be befouled before it feasts on their decaying flesh!
A monument dedicated to the Eagle God has been erected here – all fear its looming shadow cast from above!
A monument dedicated to the Hound God has been erected here – all fear the feeding frenzy that is to come!
A monument dedicated to the Serpent God has been erected here – all fear that which slithers from the depths of Norsca!
All Trolls love a good cave, but the Norscan variety prefer them as frosty and frigid as possible.
Given enough meat and mead, Norscan Giants are kept docile enough to keep around between battles – just as long as you can afford them the space!
Permanent war paint is one way that Norscans attract the gaze of their Gods and show their devotion to slaughter.
The white-hot irons of the Dark Furnace sear symbols of the tribe and their Gods directly onto living flesh.
Whether through mutation or mutilation, Norscans consider disfigurements and scars to be blessed markings of war.
In a Norscan occupation, those not enslaved will often end up burned alive as an offering to the Masters.
Norscan raiders sometimes place the rotting corpses of their dead in a ceremonial circular arrangment for display to the Gods.
To draw their Gods' attentions outside of battle, Marauders duel in Blood-Groves to spill each other’s blood in deathly combat.
Whenever possible, the skeletons of kings and champions slain by the Northmen are kept still adorning their priceless crowns and valuable armour.
Where the warriors lay their head is home – until the next raid.
As more warriors flock to the cause of murder and plunder, the outpost grows.
By reclaiming and reshaping the coast, an outpost can be more strategically defended against attacks from both land and sea.
Wharfs are platforms jutting out of the water, allowing ships to be boarded easily.
Norsca’s ship-building workshops enable their raiding Marauders to be the infamous scourge of the Old World’s seas.
From their raiding ports the Northmen pour out into all directions, intent on sending the world to wrack and ruin.
In a brutal land where war is the natural state, strongholds are necessary to assert effective authority.
The greater the Norscan stronghold, the more bloodthirsty killers that can be drawn to a warlord's banner.
The Norse tribes are mainly nomadic, making their camps where they may and moving on when the dark energies wane.
During a gathering of tribes or 'moot', many sacrifices are thrown into a large fire pit as the Chieftains parley.
The most permanent Norse settlement is a shanty village, close to a wharf, with a crude meeting hall at its centre.
Mutant pelts, with their unique textures and qualities, do not come cheap due to being highly difficult to obtain.
Treating and colouring beast-skins requires the use of lethal concoctions, a hazardous task best left to the thralls.
A living, breathing slave is much more valuable than the soulless vehicle of rotting flesh left after he dies.
Smiths are usually thralls, stolen from the south and kept alive for their skills, with access to a very basic smithy.
Higher forge temperatures offer more than just bigger and harder axes, but also useful things like beast-barding and chariot modifications.
“Don’t get too close – it burns with the hellish heat of the instability between worlds!”
Taken from the steppes of the Northern Wastes, Norse steeds are kept at crude shielings, feeding on diluted blood.
In tribal villages, steeds are kept in corrals, which stops them from wandering too far and becoming Manticore quarry.
As the war-gathering grows, stables become more necessary to keep the myriad mounts and beasts confined and separated – especially from each other.
When attackers are foolish enough to challenge a Norscan enclave, these ramparts drip crimson, drenched in their blood.
The fleshless faces of the dead stare out in warning to all enemies of the tribe.
Nothing saps the courage out of an enemy like a massive wall of dead bodies.
Tipped with fearsome figureheads, the weathered keels of longships form the spine of a grim palisade – a bulwark and grim omen of what awaits the foolish.
The Chaos Gods exist, as undeniable as the night. They are worshipped at Ruinous Altars, intended for sacrifice and more.
The larger a village becomes, the more significant and vile its shrine to the Dark Gods.
Wherever dark energies can be channelled, the seers commune with godlings and daemons to guide the tribe towards war.
To worship war is to endlessly indulge in it until death, or into immortality – whichever comes first.

Bone is a plentiful material for the Savage Orcs, and they use it all manner of ways.
The bone crafter dwelling is easily recognisable due to all the clattering bone fetishes that hang from its roof.
Naturally, the Savage Orc Warboss’ favoured bone carver gets to work in the Hut of Bones.
The boyz need big open spaces to swing their choppas about.
A large area set aside for the belligerent gits to slap each other about.
This is where Big ‘Uns are forged and many teef lost to gambling.
Savage Orcs are nomadic, but there are certain areas, deep in the Badlands, where they gather.
A Savage Orc camp is an even more disorganised rabble of tents than a traditional Orc settlement.
Savage Orcs can Waaagh! just like any Greenskin, giving thanks to Gork or Mork before charging off.
The Halflings’ diminutive stature masks a ravenous appetite, and as you might expect, highly-developed culinary skills; as such, their cauldrons bubble day and night!
The Order of Merciful Sisters of Sigmar dedicate their lives to recovering Warpstone from across the world and bringing it to Sigmar's Rock for safekeeping.
These structures lie in ruins. Nothing remains but destruction, ashes and the sorrowful taste of defeat.
While the Archecclesiastium is technically the governing council of Myrmidia's cult, it has become the main temple's name by association.
The Knights of the Blazing Sun are dedicated to Myrmidia. Their large chapter house is emblazoned with her likeness.
The Bokha Palace is the seat of the ruling Tzars, a whole wing of which is fashioned from Ice Magic.
The Lady herself blessed the Morceaux Valley, washing the land with crystal water from the Grail.
The finest Bretonnian wines can be found in the Bordeleaux dukedom and the finest grapes in the Morceaux Valley.
Vintners gather the grapes blessed by the Lady, turning them into wine for future generations.
The wine market is a bustling and often dangerous place, as casks and bottles of the best vintages are sold for many gold coins.
Brightstone is highly valuable. It's therefore a pity that the mines at Mount Gunbad are infested with Night Goblins.
The Altdorf Colleges of Magic teach gifted students from across the Old World in the ways of Battle Magic.
The Altdorf Colleges of Magic teach gifted students from across the Old World in the ways of Battle Magic.
Surrounding the colleges are many conclaves, unions and societies where Wizards share knowledge and secrets.

There are many docks in Erengrad - the 'Doorway to Kislev' - goods arrive here from Bretonnia, Marienburg and even Norsca.
Known simply as "the harbour", Erengrad is one of the largest ports, despite being under the control of its infamous Guilds.
The port encompasses the harbour and docks, from the bay to the mouth of the Lynsk.
The Slayer Hold of Karak Kadrin houses the greatest shrine to the Ancestor God, Grimnir, the first Slayer.
Sat atop the Ulricsberg, the fortress-temple at the heart of Middenheim dominates the city.
Da Dropz are where the Orcs like to relieve themselves; they particularly enjoy doing it in enemy settlements.
Greenskins like to "let da world know" a place has been conquered in the strongest (and stinkiest) way possible!
When a heap of crap isn't humiliating enough, the Greenskins can really "go for it" with a towering pillar of the stuff!
A stinky idol is not only a message to the enemy but a tribute to Mork (or Gork), using readily available materials.
A Troll's face made out of poo can be an intimidating thing to come across, depending on the quality of the "sculpture" of course.
Where the Throne of Power lies when in residence; where the High King sits reading the Dammaz Kron.
Under the great banners of this chapterhouse depicting Araby’s fabled spotted panther, the Knights Panther consolidate their power and command of their Order.
Many Knights Panther enclaves are found deep within Middenland, although detachments are present in armies across the Empire.
Marienburg is not a safe place in which to loiter, although the riches that pass through make it worth the risk.
The greater harbour of Marienburg lies past the Manannspoort Sea, just beyond Rijker's Isle.
Marienburg's infamous port, the Rijkspoort, is where the majority of the 'legitimate' goods arrive.
Its hallowed spaces emanate the strong, fierce and honourable nature of Ulric and his followers.
Expansive halls and courtyards where new worshippers and hoary warriors alike listen the priests' words of veneration to the Wolf.
Wolf pelts bedeck temple walls, as hallways lead to chambers and training yards where war is studied and practiced by all according to the tenets of Ulric.
The vast, fortified temple dominates the environs of Middenheim – an enduring symbol of Ulrican strength, faith, and constant readiness for battle. Within, the Eternal Flame rages with righteousness.
The foundry districts of Nuln are full of choking soot, as the forges burn night and day churning out Imperial artillery.
The Gunnery School is a centre of excellence, where the nation's greatest artillerymen are trained and cannons forged.
The Reiksguard is barracked in Altdorf. However, they maintain battle-ready fortresses scattered throughout the Empire.

A Savage Orc camp is an even more disorganised rabble of tents than a traditional Orc settlement.
Savage Orcs can Waaagh! just like any Greenskin, giving thanks to Gork or Mork before charging off.
The current capital of the Empire and seat of the Reikland Emperors. Altdorf is a large, cosmopolitan city-port full of wonders and danger.
Screams are sweet music to the ears of the Undead as they prowl the blood-soaked streets of their new empire.
Once the proud Hold of Karak Drazh, it is now the most formidable of Orc Strongholds, in the hands of the Red Fang tribe, until very recently.
Drakenhof is the sprawling ancestral fortress of the von Carstein bloodline. Ever since the coming of Vlad it has been the de facto political centre of Sylvania.
Formed in an ancient Elven stronghold many centuries ago, the city of Couronne houses the palace and ruling court of King Leoncoeur.
Bones of the once honourable now litter their feasting halls, their blood overflowing from prized chalices.
Karaz-a-Karak, known as Everpeak, capital of the Karaz Ankor. It is the richest, deepest, and most powerful of all Dwarfholds.
The tower stands in the heart of Great Cathay, a beacon of the Dragon Emperor's glory.
With thick walls and looming towers, the fortress is the bulwark of Wei-Jin's defences.
The grand palace is a symbol of opulence, paying homage to the Celestial Dragon's power.
The Celestial City rises above Wei-Jin, a shining symbol of Cathay's glory and the awe of all who stand in its shadow.
Magnificent is too small a word for a city known by all as the home of endless wonders and the seat of the Dragon Throne.
Once thought to be the greatest city in the world, Wei-Jin now lies in ruins, its wonders buried beneath a blanket of rubble and ash.
The nations of man enjoy a good tourney, especially the Bretonnians whose Knights relish showing off their skills to the smallfolk.
Such secrets that the innkeeper Franz Lohner does not know probably aren't worth knowing to begin with.
Taal's shrines are rustic abodes, small circular buildings with conical roofs, topped with the skull of a stag.
The greatest temple to Taal is found in Talabheim, the cratered city at the centre of the Empire.
Wharfs are platforms jutting out of the water, allowing ships to be boarded easily.
Whether man-made or natural, a harbour is a place for vessels to wait out Stromfels' rage.

Shrines of Myrmidia can be found in most southern provinces. They are well ordered, martial places, as befits their deity.
Myrmidia's temples are some of the grandest structures in the southern nations, reflecting how liked the goddess is.
Located in the barrows or tombs of long-dead Chieftains are dusty racks of aged weaponry, still sharp despite the centuries.
The most treasured and arcane possessions are kept in reliquaries, many made safe from looters… until now.
Often seen on Corpse Carts, balefire braziers contain an infernal flame that spreads a foul contagion.
A balefire hearth is a larger structure than a mere brazier - a raging hellfire inferno contained in a large, unholy fire pit.
Deep in the woods stands a hovel, surrounded by cruel fetishes. From its chimney pumps balefire smoke to wither the lands.
The crypts of Sylvania can be dangerous places, for ghouls lurk and feed on the rotting remains within.
To summon vile minions, a circle must be etched in the ground, with symbols of a dead language scrawled around it.
An infernal lodestone is planted inside a binding circle, summoning the most powerful of all spirits as it glows.
Ancient Vampires are not limited by the size of their circle, for their power defies all constraints!
Graveyards and cemeteries are ubiquitous - a particular favourite source of "fresh recruits" for Necromancers.
Ancient warriors are found in barrows, usually at the sites of forgotten battles or the former seats of long-dead Chieftains.
The richer and more powerful the warrior, the grander his tomb. Such mausoleums contain great prizes for Dark Magic wielders.
Where do Dragons go to die? Only the most resourceful dead-raiser knows.
The trees in Sylvania are as evil as its denizens, for they shelter many predators such as Fell Bats and Dire Wolves.
Sylvania's woods are dingy copses of twisted, half-rotted trees that claw what nourishment they can from the bone-strewn soil.
Dark and yellow-leafed forests surround the wind-swept moors of Sylvania, where criminals and far darker, hungrier, things lurk.
Men fear what lurks in the blackened depths, for it is that which abandons reason to hunt without mercy.
There is no respite in the dark, for the horrors here take to the skies to hunt their prey.
A pile of writhing corpses from which a shambling patrol of Zombies will emerge.
Throughout the cursed realm stand watchtowers of bone. Within are the Grave Guard - always on duty and ready to strike.
From private collections to tomes gathered in temple vaults, Necromancers will do anything to seek out forbidden lore.
Any Necromancer worth his infamy needs a dread tower from which to conduct blasphemous experiments and research.
This mass grave acts like a locus for Necromancers and their ilk, for it contains many fresh bodies ripe for recruitment.
A vile place of discarded gravestones, statuary, rotting limbs, headless bodies that still crawl, and lots and lots of bones.
Ossuaries are the resting places of skeletal remains, originally reserved for Morr's greatest subjects, but long since defiled.
A common sight across Sylvania and beyond, the gibbet - or hanging cage - is where the living who displease their Undead lords often end up.
Another common sight in the Unliving realms are gallows - although hanged corpses rarely stay dead and can often be seen struggling to untie their nooses.
For instilling even greater dread in the beating hearts of mortals, massive scaffolds are erected where many of those same hearts beat their last.
Deep in the red pits can be found mercury in the raw form of cinnabar. A material often used in Dark Magic rituals.
The Blood Mines are red as cinnabar - and occasionally Warpstone - are found here in significant seams.
Best not choose the dark green powder, though, it certainly isn't snuff!
To hunt here is to become the hunted, for the prey is vicious and probably dead already…
Should the smallfolk organise themselves, a whole expedition will venture into the haunted woods in search of game.
What is the Flayer? A myth, but one that is all too real.
Gold found here is always tarnished and far from the pure element so beloved by Dwarfs. Nevertheless, it has value.
When a Vampire Count discovers a large seam of gold, he will send his minions forth to scour it clean.
A great furnace with an ornate, brazen face, and yellow-green balefire within its sneering mouth.
The blackest iron ore can be found in the deepest pits, underneath the mountains upon which gothic castles perch.
Since before the building of Nagashizzar, Necromancers have used Zombies to burrow and mine mountains for their minerals.
Cursed iron ore is laced with Warpstone. Such mines are prized.
Burning with balefire, an unholy forge is a relic of Stirland's more prosperous days, now defiled and used by a Vampire's thralls.
The dread castles of Sylvania are made from stone shaped by stone cutters, under von Carstein's thrall.
There is an art to creating a memorable tombstone or grand mausoleum.
Some gargoyles are fashioned by sculptors - others just appear, as if they flew there themselves.
The low-born of Sylvania that have heartbeats must still make a living. Most do in the cursed fields, tending to withering crops.
Sylvanian peasants tend to wretched farms, continuing the pretence that the realm's nobles are kind and generous lords.
At night, the mill by the blood-clotted streams begins to turn, mixing grains with grinded bone.
Beneath the blood-clotted streams and rank sewage are pits of dense, dark clay.
Using the raw clay compound, urn makers create opulent vessels to carry the ashes of powerful beings.
Perhaps there is some spirit trapped within, burning in abject agony every time the kilns are lit?
Stagnant ponds can be found by their disgusting reek, the brackish water full of brine and other things…
The only thing that rises from the crumbling salt marshes of Sylvania are bony hands reaching toward the sky.
Deep in the dead marches are salt pans, containing piles and piles of bones, bleached and scoured white.
Foresting in Hunger Wood or the Spider Haunts is surely a fool's job?
Once part of Stirland's burgeoning timber industry, the sawmills have remained in a ruined, yet operational state since the Vampire Wars…
From the ruined sawmills, Zombie bearers transport their cursed loads to large sheds long-thought abandoned by mortals.
There is a cabin in the woods… a place where someone, or thing, keeps certain other things…
There is a cabin in the woods, you know, where darkness dwells eternally…
When a Vampire drinks an "aged red" from a wine glass, chances are it hasn't been made from grapes…
Sylvanian orchards contain low-hanging, spooky trees, whose thorny branches are as likely to grab a passer-by as provide fruit.
The Vampire Counts crave the illusion that they are nobles, and so they bottle their own "special" vintages.
The scattered hamlets of Undead-stricken lands are even more isolated, parochial and pathetic than those of the living.
The peasantry live in small communities of inter-related families, and never venture far from their hovels.
Townships are little more than larger villages, usually within sight of a grand castle - its shadow looming over the terrified denizens.
When a Vampire marches forth, the cities of other realms fear - for should the Night Lord invade they become accursed places.
Dread, gothic citadels are scattered throughout Sylvania. They grow more ominous as their chief resident grows in power.
Within the tomb of the Vampire lies its coffin, filled with loam from Lahmia. It is where the beast rests, waiting to be awoken…
A Vampire's keep is quite literally its castle - a dark, gothic stronghold from which it plots and assembles its forces.
The Lords of the Night must keep threats at bay, whilst luring prey to their doors for an untimely end.
Here reside the Vampires who ride proudly amongst the fabled Blood Knights.
Gory fetishes are used to chain spirits to the insubstantial barriers known as ghost fences. To cross it without wards is a foolish act.
Walls of wood, stone, bone and skulls are used by the master of the Undead to form defences and instil terror.
Larger walls form mighty bulwarks that can be infused with Dark Magic to keep out and curse the enemy.
Honour mine father in death as in life…
The centuries-old wreckage of two beached Black Arks provide the Druchii with their most solid naval foothold in Albion.
Returned to its former glory, this great port is now as defensible as the mighty Black Arks that once stood in its place.
This once-bustling port lies in ruins. Nothing remains but destruction, ashes and the sorrowful taste of defeat.
Known simply as the Ancient Dragon Cave, it was once home to an infamous Drake, said to have come from the Far East. The creature has not been seen in aeons.
Dedicated to the Blood God, the Brazen Altar is the lair of dread Flesh Hound Simaergul, one of Khorne’s favoured pets.

This supposed unholy offspring of the Great Maw and the Sun, which lights the skies above the Ogre Kingdoms a fiery red, is itself worshipped as a god by those who have witnessed its titanic eruptions.
Found within the Chaos Realm’s pall, time has no meaning here. Daemons and mortals battle for a victory that will never come.
This gigantic monolith is constantly battered by the Winds of Chamon. Treasure seekers have sought its legend but they are fools if they think to claim it.

The ravine it sits above is not only a key strategic route into Middenland but is thought to be a prominent beast-path, hence so many warherds find themselves at Grimmenhagen's walls.
When the Warpshowers came, the cursed swamp of Hel Fenn boiled and churned – spewing forth the rotted corpses buried beside it in centuries past.
The ancient Frost Dragon who lives here has breath so powerful it once froze an entire Ogre tribe into a single, glacier-like block of ice.

Strange rituals are performed by the local Savage Orcs beneath large but crude dung-smeared totems. A leader of the Shrunken Headz tribe once attempted to pile up enough skulls here to challenge Gork himself to a headbutting contest!

The double-edged sword of Black Fire Pass has long been both a chink in the Empire’s armour and a vital lifeline of its trade routes. Glassy black cliffs echo with a history of triumphs against the odds, as well as bitter defeats.

When the Goblin Shaman Raknik and his Forest Goblins plagued Reikland from their lair in Bloodpine Woods, Karl Franz marched out with his army and defeated him in a tumultuous battle, strengthening his rule but nearly losing his life in the process.

The Waaagh! of the legendary Orc Warboss Grudsnik was known to have rampaged as far as ancient Nehekhara, the resulting spoils now entombed along with his remains in his hallowed mound.

The remains of Estalian kings and their royal retinues once lay in peace in the earth. Now their souls know no rest, for an opportunistic Necromancer is always in need of the greatest Undead warriors.

The site of a famous battle in 2427 that culminated in a duel fought in the middle of a ford between the Elector Counts of Stirland and Talabecland.

The Endal king was afforded the funeral rites of the greatest heroes, for such was his bravery in saving Sigmar from the Greenskin horde at Black Fire Pass.

It is said that Druids of the ancient, long-dead tribes of Albion bade a race of Giants to construct a series of stone circles across their island, whose mystical properties would allow them to channel Chaos-warding magic.

A powerful Storm of Magic once whipped up a great arcane fulcrum from the ground, a supernatural pillar seemingly made of solid bone. A mage who sits atop it can still harness a glimmer of power, scrying the future or plucking lost knowledge of the past.
Overgrown, exhumed graves sit around a fell shrine that glows with sinister power, known to be responsible for rousing the nearby dead.
An ancient, enduring symbol of the courage of the Kislevite people. Since Ursun’s absence, the Bear cult’s influence has lessened as the Great Orthodoxy affirms more control over the holy site.

The strategically important River Stir forms the border between the oft-bickering states of Stirland and Talabecland. It is even said that past Elector Counts of the two duelled in the middle of the river itself.

In the time of Chaos, the eldritch machineries of the Old Ones’ cosmic gates into this realm collapsed, crashing down upon the world in a burning hail of star-metal as the poles imploded and opened rifts into the beyond.

While Boris’ body was lost at an unknown crossing on the River Lynsk, legend has it that the Motherland spirited his body away via the current; he was found years later, encased in ice, at the Frozen Falls.
The Ogres’ ever-hungry chief deity is in fact an enormous crater caused by a meteorite so huge it almost wiped their entire race from the face of the world.

To the Isle of the Dead are all the magical energies of the world inexorably drawn, like the waters of a whirlpool, to Ulthuan’s heart. Here, the magic is drained from this reality by the Great Vortex; the last – and most brilliant – world-preserving enchantment of Caledor the Great.

Built to funnel the tumultuous winds that sweep across the Chaos Wastes, only a few knew this was to power a portal within the Citadel that led directly to the Chaos Realms. The gate was destroyed when Ursun roared.

Situated close to the Black Gulf, the caverns are a nexus of the Under-Empire, visible above ground via luminous chasms. Those not aligned to the Council of Thirteen that loiter around this part of the Badlands will quickly disappear.
The forges in the Daemonium are powdered by the fiery breath of Hashut.
The Skull of the First glowers high above Khorne's realm.
Dangling from the Tree of Souls are all manner of weapons and ordnance.
There are challengers waiting afore the Wrathgate, eager to prove their worth.

Beware, for setting foot on this island will see you cast with the most virulent of poxes.

Where does the Eternity Stair lead? Some say only the Great Architect truly knows.
The roosts of the Watchers offer great vantage from which to observe myriad worlds and realities.
Within the Heavenward Halls are games of skill, mystery, mental and the physical.
Why does the Dead King no longer live? He possesses knowledge that Tzeentch does not want told...
Falsehoods and secrets are the weapons of a true liar, but for every deceit there must be a chance of truth.

Riches kept, and invested, will surely pay dividends. This is sense when the future is uncertain.
It is time to fight, to draw the foe's blood and spill it upon the snow.
…because a better, safer province is just common sense, right?
Embrace innovation, for Kislev's very survival may depend upon it.
Just one is granted resilience, though ultimately the cost is born by all.
This way, every resident benefits, and feels that the town is run with their interests at heart.
If the defences hold, people will survive, and the foe may be dissuaded from returning.
Embrace innovation, for Kislev's very survival may depend upon it.
It is clear to all that a wise hand holds the tiller.
…because you simply never know when calamity will strike.
Expect nothing but the very best. Anything less is folly, and invites doom.
Buildings are the priority, for a larger town will attract business and bring greater prosperity.
Showing loyalty to the Tzarina is surely prudent and politic?
The Patriarchs have great sway among the people, you know…
Allowing the Frost Maidens to come and go as they please buys favour with the Tzarina.
Unquestionable loyalty to the Great Orthodoxy ensures they will keep the people on side.
Worshippers of the Dark Gods shall not be harboured, for they are not welcome here.
Bring your skills, your laughter and your fighting arms! Huzzah!
The Black Glove was sent, so infantrymen will be mustered.
Never mind what Erengrad demands, local considerations must come first.
This will see infantry more readily accepted into the village.
Steeds and their riders are welcome here.
The Ataman's ceremonial role must be upheld, for in tradition there is security.
The hearth can wait. Foes must be sought and put down, lest they become a greater threat.
Ungol blood must flow in his veins, for truly he is an ally of the horsemen.
The Ataman's thugs shall find the heretics. Ruin shall not take root here.

War and the gold required to fight it; it is this which dominates oblast communities and provides the stark choice an Ataman must face. Should income be invested, to make all in the community richer, or should warriors be paid to fight and defend the Motherland?
A crucial decision is asked of the Ataman. Should valuable resources be used to shore up the province or spent focusing on innovations and research?

Oft times, an Ataman must act as a justice – determining guilt and metering out punishment as required, as well as settling other disputes, legal or otherwise. Such a judgement is now required. Should one be compensated at the expense of the town?
Where should effort and resources be channelled? The Ataman must make a tough decision to reinforce the defences or quickly recruit and grow his local forces.

Appropriating funds and channelling them for the benefit of their charges is a sworn duty of the Atamans. Should the funds go toward investments or to better bolster the defences against insurrection and overt enemies?

There are only so many of Kislev's sons and daughters available, and the needs of the town put strain on the labour. The Ataman must therefore decide whether it is construction or recruitment that is his priority.

Tensions between the Tzarina's agents and the Great Orthodoxy increase, spilling further out from the capital and into the oblasts. The Ataman is called upon by the factions to prove his loyalty once more.

In Kislev city there is said to be a power struggle between the suffocating Great Orthodoxy and the emergent influence of the Ice Court, led by the Tzarina. Now a Patriarch of the Orthodoxy approaches, as does a Frost Maiden, agent of the Ice Queen. To whom should the Ataman show favour?

The folk of Kislev can be generous and welcoming hosts, especially if the guest is willing to drink with them. And yet… there are those who are greeted with suspicion, to whom strong drinks are not offered and about whom whispers of Dark Worship spread. How should the Ataman act as refugees approach?

By tradition, once the Black Glove has been delivered from Erengrad, an Ataman must immediately muster the tribes, for war is inevitable. However, his advisors suggest going against the custom on this occasion and exerting more influence across the province.

It is considered a mark of great fortune for the Ataman to lead the settlement's hunters in a procession through the streets at the start of the season. Yet, the hunters are factionalised between the trappers, who shun horse, and the archers who chase down prey on their beloved steeds. Which side should the Ataman endorse?

It is the Time of Dazh, where the Ataman must think of home in reverence to the God of Fire and Sun. However, the desire to wander far from the hearth must also be considered. Should the Ataman shrug off his ceremonial role and risk resentment in his own community?

Resources are always finite. The Ataman must make a choice whether to address rumours and root out the taint of the Dark Gods, or to ensure the oblasts are patrolled to protect them from more overt threats.

A dangerous, murderous Chaos Frost Dragon is a great offering to the Gods indeed, and none are more dangerous and murderous than Frigustrex, Scion of the Cold-Void. All War Hydras live to be incredibly ancient, but legend has it that the Beast of Raema will never die of old age. The older it gets, the larger it grows; its scales denser, its teeth get sharper and claws longer. The legends recount that the mere sight of the creature has a mesmerising effect, driving soon-to-be victims mad by the movements of its swaying, intertwined necks. Until now, the beast has remained in its hunting grounds in the far north of Naggarond, but could be a lucrative catch should it venture beyond its usual territory…
Hunt down and slay the savage War Hydra known as [[col:yellow]]The Beast of Raema[[/col]]

A hideous being of unparalleled size and ferocity, the Hellbeast of Seep-Gore staggers frantically around the Chaos Wastes bellowing in pain, guts bulging as if filled with swarms of living creatures. It is rumoured to have been created by the Master Moulders of Hell Pit – at whose behest and for what purpose, no one knows. Yet one purpose it does serve is to be hunted by heroes and madmen up to the task.
Hunt down and slay the foul Hell Pit Abomination known as [[col:yellow]]The Hellbeast of Seep-Gore[[/col]]

Perhaps the scariest of all giant humanoid monster species, Cygors are some of the angriest creatures to roam the Old World. Some оf their bloodlines single themselves out by being bigger and stronger than others of their kind, making them both an alluring and a daunting target for a hunt . Their cycloptic eyes not only see the Winds of Magic, but also dampen their use for most spellcasters in their presence.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Cygors[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining their kind to your will

As creatures of Chaos, Dragon Ogre Shaggoths are a highly-favourable sacrifice to the Dark Gods, but also extremely difficult to bring down. Their strength and power are proportional to their age, which makes any living member of their kind immeasurably old compared to most inhabitants of the world. Many of them welcome powerful adversaries and gladly sanction any hunters' attempts to withstand their lightning and bring them down.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Dragon Ogre Shaggoth[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

Arachnarok Queens are the type of despicable poisonous monster that should not be trifled with. One Venom Queen is hard enough to bring down, but to take on this bounty you will have to face multiple Queens – the Brood Queens of Karak Azul. All in a day’s hunt!
Hunt down and slay the venomous [[col:yellow]]Brood Queens of Karak Azul[[/col]]

Blorgar the Mad Titan is a brutish and highly flatulent Giant wreaking havoc with no other purpose than to mindlessly trample settlements and squish their inhabitants under his colossal wart-ridden feet. He has personally contributed to the desolation across the wastelands he stomps around. That, however makes the creature easier to track than most – should anyone decide to do it.
Hunt down and slay the belligerent Giant known as [[col:yellow]]Blorgar the Mad Titan[[/col]]

Forest Dragons are truly remarkable creatures, dominating the habitat that defines them. For most others, however, stepping into the infamous Radixashen's domain is either an act of extreme bravery or hopeless stupidity, such is his cunning and elusive nature even compared to his Forest Dragon kin. Many who thought they were hunting him found themselves hunted in turn. But this would never stop those who think themselves truly worthy.
Hunt down and slay the elusive Forest Dragon known as [[col:yellow]]Radixashen, Serpent of the World Roots[[/col]]

A great prize awaits the hunter who dares brave the most desolate reaches of the northern tundra. One particular herd of mammoths known as the Great Mawherd of Bloodfjord has earned notoriety throughout the tribes for having the most powerful and unpredictably aggressive beasts in its parade. Slaying them will surely bring great favour!
Capture the mighty Mammoths of [[col:yellow]]The Great Mawherd of Bloodfjord[[/col]]

The Abyssal Shrieker is a terrible flying beast of legend, shrouded in macabre myth. This nightmare of the sky, whose shrieks of the damned emanate from the Ruinous Realm itself, is of the giant Undead bat species known as Terrorgheists. Little is known about the Abyssal Shrieker, except that many a hunter has fallen trying to fell it!
Hunt down and slay the ghastly Terrorgheist known as [[col:yellow]]the Abyssal Shrieker[[/col]]

As a Flamespyre Phoenix ages, its body cools, and even begins to sap heat from its surroundings. Not so the Mother of the Flame, who burns as brightly now as when she was first born within the heart of a volcano. The Mother is said to spend much of her life within the Realm of Chaos itself, gliding upon the Winds of Magic and hunting Daemonic essence. Upon entering the mortal world, mighty eruptions precede her, bringing purifying fire into the world – as well as a clutch of her flaming children.
Hunt down and slay the deadly Flamespyre Phoenix known as [[col:yellow]]Mother of the Flame[[/col]]

While the most infamous Carnosaur is Grymloq – mount of the mighty Kroq-Gar – there is another known to the Lizardmen across the world. A Carnosaur like no other; a creature that can never be tamed and blessed with an eternal hunger that has seen it grow to a massive size. The Lizardmen call it 'Gargantulzan' and worship it as a minor god, devoting many sacrifices to the monster. Yet even a behemoth such as Gargantulzan may serve as a sacrifice in turn, should he be brought down... somehow.
Hunt down and slay the behemoth Carnosaur known as [[col:yellow]]Gargantulzan[[/col]]

Even more so than most Bloodshriek Chimerae, The Voice of the Wasteland has gained particular notoriety for its capacity to attract the coruscating energies of Chaos. Its varicoloured hide is a maleficent beacon visible far and wide across the Chaos Wastes – a baleful warning to other inhabitants and even its own kin. Snuffing out its power, or maybe even ensnaring the beast. would be a feat to make others of its kind take note.
Capture the eldritch Bloodshriek Chimera known as [[col:yellow]]The Voice of the Wastes[[/col]]

Though the mutating influences of the Chaos Wastes has wiped clean any vestige of a mind Toad Dragons may have possessed, it has proven powerless to mask the pustulence they leave across the otherwise trackless wastes. To many, it has served as a warning. To others, it has served as a grave. To some, it is a hunting trail to follow.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Toad Dragon[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

Nondescript environments which rarely fully experience the taint of Chaos readily conceal one of the deadlier and more elusive creatures favoured by the Dark Gods – the Lord of Change's very own cherished pet, the Cockatrice. For what inscrutable purpose does the monster infest such lands? \\n\\nOne simple, satisfactory answer presents itself: to be hunted, of course. Though its potential allyship may yet be a part of the Eagle's schemes...
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Cockatrice[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

As befits their unruly nature, Feral Manticores prefer riding the wild winds and landscapes littered with reminders of ruin. They are uniquely unlike each other in appearance and uniformly the same in murderous drive. Manticores care for no masters who have not already proven themselves capable of hunting down and killing one of their feral kind.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Feral Manticore[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

To look upon a Jabberslythe is to know madness – though what is the single-minded pursuit of such a beast if not a species of madness in itself? Would such hunters be immune to its gibbering wiles for long enough to slay it? Would they then be as far gone as to *employ* another of its kind? If such questions prompt you to attempt it, you may already be on the path to madness.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Jabberslythe[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

How much flesh can a Ghorgon gorge on? As the saying goes, "a Ghorgon gorges on flesh 'til it's gone". Mellow climes and abundant food suit them well, for they do not seek a challenge but a meal. Their ravening single-mindedness makes them appropriate targets for a hunt, and with the proper inducement – the flesh of another Ghorgon maybe – they could be turned to one's cause.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Ghorgon[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

Lammasu rarely assert themselves in the pecking order of their environment, mostly due to disinterest. Their cunning and magic afford them a comfortable existence to the point where some decide to wield their power over other magical beasts across the deserts of the world, where they are least likely to be disturbed by the presence of civilisation. To hunters willing to brave such desolation - or to whom civilisation means little to begin with - this is certainly no obstacle.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Lammasu[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining their kind to your will

A Bale Taurus following the scent of Aqshy's wayward currents is often the reason they seek out the lifeless, desolate places of this world. It marks its territory by reducing the already-sparse natural beauties of the landscape to shimmering slag and boiling the oases into steam-laden mirages on the horizon. Even novice hunters can follow such trails, though even veteran ones may not be prepared for what awaits them at the end of the path.
Hunt down and slay the destructive Bale Taurus known as [[col:yellow]]The Bull of Aqshy[[/col]]

Preytons are a particularly virulent sort of Chaos beast, as they bear a superficial resemblance to the noble Great Stags – enough to fool the unwary and turn awe into terror in a single breath. To hunters, however, neither awe nor terror matters – only finding the creature and turning its predatory instincts against itself.
Hunt down the [[col:yellow]]Preyton[[/col]] of these climes to learn the secrets of chaining its kind to your will

Though no longer omnipotent paragons of creation, mighty Dragons still strive pridefully to be the stuff of legend. And pride burns hot in the Ascendant, and the desire to be named much like his mythical kin: Sulekh, Seraphon, Maelstrom, Shackolot, Bracchus...\\n\\nA worthy hunter's purpose is to make it so that never happens. A Dragon turned prey does not deserve a name.
Hunt down and slay the prideful Black Dragon known as [[col:yellow]]The Ascendant[[/col]]

Of all the reptilian nightmares that inhabit the jungle-shrouded continent of Lustria, Dread Saurians are one of the most feared; an echo of ancient days when huge beasts such as this did battle with the forefathers of the dragоns for supremacy. Those times may be long past but the Dread Saurians, larger even than the towering Carnosaurs, remain the biggest physical threat on their lands and many more besides.\\nThe Runt has become one such threat - ironically unbeknownst to him, as his behaviour bespeaks a creature of a much smaller size. It is difficult to fathom why that would be, and the even larger beasts he may have encountered on his way. But the hunt for The Runt remains the biggest game hunt anyone knows of, making it an irresistible offering.
Hunt down and slay the colossal Dread Saurian known as [[col:yellow]]The Runt[[/col]]

Carrions circling above lifeless deserts rely on their preternatural instinct for blood to carry them across the distances to their fleshly prey. Yet the Carrion Eater has been making sport of its own kind for hundreds of years, darkening the sun above them just as its lessers have done for the unwary, the unwise or the downright unhinged trespassers on their territory.\\n\\nThis beast has never felt the eyes of hunters upon itself, but there is a first time for everything.
Hunt down and slay the supreme desert predator known as [[col:yellow]]The Carrion Eater[[/col]

Reclaimed from Chaos by the magic of the Dragon Emperor, Celestial Lions are considered a direct affront to the Dark Gods that any follower of theirs must redress in blood.\\n\\nThe Wise One has evaded countless such pursuits, for it is said he pities the degenerate servants of Chaos for their mindless hatred. Yet he has also broken just as many of them in the field, his roar as terrible as his pity. But even the Wise One knows that one of these days, he must face his final hunters.
Hunt down and slay the noble Celestial Lion known as [[col:yellow]]The Wise One[[/col]]

Powerful spellcasters in battle, Liche Priests replenish fallen warriors within their armies, cleanse the corruption left by other races in the campaign, and improve the rate at which you can research new dynasties.
The sand nourishes the dead until their time of arising. Our troops will be strengthened by the earth.
Like the desert wind, our riders will move fiercely and swiftly with the Faceless God at their shoulders.
To lose one of our most prestigious, most sacred temples is a risk too great to bear. We cannot risk its collapse - use everything to reinforce it and prevent that from occurring.
Pah! The cities of the Tomb Kings have stood for millennia and will continue to – so great is the power of their creators. Do nothing and no catastrophe shall befall us.
In time, this whole world will turn to sand; first this river, then the oceans! At the end, our empire will continue to stand, unswerving and eternal.
Tasking our slaves with changing the river's course could be the key to averting disaster, along with all the prayers and rites to the higher powers that we can muster!
Our many bound servants have been busied labouring for our greatness, but we can spare a small number to labour at our venerable Liche Priests' behest.

Without the tireless work of the Liche Priests, the Tomb Kings would not be properly preserved and adequately prepared for their glorious reawakenings. We must give the Mortuary Cult that which they ask, lest their great work be halted!
Our focus should be on restoring those buildings which provide troops for our armies. Doing so will hasten the reconquest of our former territories.
The greatest empires were launched from stable foundations. Improving the buildings that form our essential infrastructure will surely bring us closer to paradise?
One thousand years confined to his tomb, with maybe just a few scarabs and scorpions for company, should teach this treacherous cleric the error of his ways!
Let him talk, allow him his intrigue and scheming, for in the end everyone serves their Unliving liege, one way or another.
There is secret knowledge to be found inside that chamber. We should continue our excavation to uncover it at once.
There are many other tombs to be explored here, whose rewards are just as fruitful and could be unearthed much more quickly.
These 'men' are not warriors - they are not even real men - and are therefore not worthy of our time and attention. Move on!
All must serve the Tomb Kings one way or another… Spare no expense: use the Lizardmen's flesh and blood to ensure those Tomb Kings yet to awaken do so stronger than ever before!
Possibly, our labourers have not worked hard enough. A swelling of their numbers, and some encouragement with the lash, should better align their priorities with our own!
Reinforcing the contingent guarding the sinking tomb would show prudence - our troops will ensure that the pyramid remains above ground.
It matters not what power controls the Necrosphinx, only that it obeys our orders and brings destruction to our enemies on command!
Usekph, you say? We cannot allow those gods shunned by our ancestors a new foothold on our sands - order the Necrosphinx back underground to be with its dusty patron!
We have slaves aplenty, and no need of living mouths which must be fed lest they cease to breathe. Let them wander but offer no help; they will most likely perish in the unforgiving sands.
Any found wandering our lands are the property of the Tomb Kings! Really, it is a simple matter: they are in our lands so they belong to us. Put them to work digging, and don't spare the lash!
Long ago, Alcadizaar fought to defeat a great evil from our lands. We should honour the loyalty of his troops by observing the correct funeral rites.
We can be certain that the Conqueror no longer requires his servants, at least not on this mortal plane. Let us use their desiccated bones in continuance of our quest for a worldly-paradise!

The swords of gods are not for this world. Let some other fool try to dominate that which cannot be tamed.
Bah! Every pirate worth their salt has brought down a dozen curses upon themselves, so what’s one more?
This prize isn’t worth the trouble it 'arbours. The bottom of the ocean shall 'ave a new trinket! Let's throw it overboard an' forget this affair ever 'appened.
Masters of the ballistic arts, even in death Gunnery Wights maintain the lines and a steady flow of black powder.
Fearsome creatures of the night; the very stuff of nightmares. Mourngul Haunters strike fear into the hearts of their helpless prey.
Our oldest foe 'as long been a thorn in our side, so we should take delight in this opportunity to gain both riches an' deliver a slight to our enemies.

The consequences of destroying this temple far outweigh the value of this idol. Takin' it would therefore make us 'enemy number one' of every coldblood in Lustria! Best we leave it alone, I reckon… for now at least.
We should make 'aste for this site - these veterans sailors must be made part of our crew. We can't risk losin' 'em to the ocean, or worse yet - to other pirates with a talent for raisin' the dead!
The ocean's filled with the rottin' corpses of the dead, but why rush to a watery grave? Instead, 'ow about we take advantage of the lull in naval action against us?
We must be cautious when moving ahead - reef the sails an' keep alert. I daresay Manann would not intervene so flippantly…
We mustn't be so suspicious of each an' every change in the tides. If Manann truly is warning us, we'll just 'ave to deal wiv the danger as it arises.

Those sanctimonious sops in armour, the Bretonnians, 'ave sent an 'eavily-defended convoy of merchant ships our way. Crow reckons they be heading to Araby, and by their sluggishness I'd say they're carrying a goodly haul by those escorts. Let's strike now an' take their riches for ourselves!

Pah! Northmen! Those stinkin' Norscan raiders 'ave been spotted heading back north of Naggaroth frozen following a successful raid on the coasts of the Empire. This particular tribe are known always to take captives for ransom at a later date, so this is an ample opportunity to fill our ratings.

So… it would appear that some enterprising fellows from the New World 'ave decided to risk it all against the elements an' of course ourselves, who surely 'ave nothin' left to lose anyway. It's looking pretty likely that Sartosa is their destination. Though they're well protected, taking their cargo as our prize presents an opportunity we daren't pass up.

A convoy of Dark Elf slave ships are heading back to Slaver's Bay, laden with captives raided from Ulthuan's coasts. We should free them... not for altruistic reasons, you understand, but because of their potential as fresh recruits to go on account with us an' join the crew - drowned, raised 'n' bound, they'll be worth more than a cutter full o'gold sovereigns!
We 'ave nothin' to lose in this situation, so should accept their offer an' take a cut of the plundered loot as payment.
The more pirates in one place, the more likely the authorities are to discover our presence. We can't take this risk, but can't rightly pass up the chance for plunder either. I say we attack - yarrr!
The time 'as come for us to assert our control over the seas. With this magical boon we'll be able to persevere through the greatest perils the Great Ocean can throw at us!
The time's come to make port an' build ourselves an empire, conquering new cities an' pillaging towns as we go. No hazards shall slow our advance!
Our fleet is already strong, so we must focus on buildin' up our settlements instead. We'll need to focus all resources an' labour on the towns to do this.
Our fleet is the backbone of our empire, so we must reinforce it if we're to, er, 'survive'. We'll need to divert all resources an' labour to our ships if this is to work!
We can't fight on without our weapons, so they must be protected from water damage where at all possible. Let's get 'em all up from the cargo hold at once, shall we?
We must protect ourselves first an' foremost, as a rusty sword will still end a man if wielded with purpose. I saw we move the armour to the upper deck before it's too late!
A large merchant vessel stocked with a variety of luxury goods 'as been spotted makin' for a juicy target. Let's head 'em off - after all, we can never 'ave too much treasure!
An unguarded civilian ship is transporting refugees nearby. This is excellent news - we always need fresh hands to join the crew!
We're eternal - time means little to an Undead crew. Therefore, let's wait until the winds blow favourably once more, shall we?

The dead lie in every corner of the world an' almost all of 'em would make acceptable crewmembers, with a little bit of bindin'. Should our current rabble crumble away we'll raise new forces in no time I'm sure. Let's march on!

The core of any army is its frontline troops, as any general worth their salt should surely know. If they break, everyone behind 'em becomes instantly vulnerable. These supplies will help our dead boys up the front, I reckon.

I've sailed many a year, and seen a lot of things go down, so I can say wiv confidence that the fastest way to kill your enemy is with a well-placed shot to their forehead! We should re-supply our gunners with haste - we don't wanna be caught out at sea!

The power the Brazier holds is great enough to help fuel the Great Drill of Hashut! We would be fools to pass up this opportunity!
Let your peers celebrate your victory in Zharr-Naggrund as you parade the relic in a mighty show of strength!
Hand the Golden Bands over to your Daemonsmiths; the Great Drill needs power if we are ever to reach Hashut's realm!
The Golden Bands of Grimnir will be displayed throughout Zharr-Naggrund, where your achievement will be the envy of all!
The Ever-Burning Helmet will be one of the keys to unlocking Hashut's realm. Use its power for the Great Drill!
Such a thing doesn't come around often. You must keep it and watch as foe and friend alike cower in awe!
Reaching the Blood of Hashut is all that matters. Summon the Daemonsmiths – this Lens must be corrupted!
The relic of Morgrim will cause a stir in Zharr-Naggrund! Who could deny your might once you march through the streets with it on display?
There will be no small delight in watching the Runic Braces of Skavor be corrupted. Let the binding commence!
We must put the Braces on display before your peers in Zharr-Naggrund. Only then will they see that you clearly bear Hashut's favour!

Claiming the Smithing Hammer of Smednir is a victory for all Dawi-Zharr! Let us show off the relic where all can celebrate your victory!
What is a Runic Tablet next to the awesome power of the Blood of Hashut? We must bind the relic, so that the Drill may burrow its way between realms!
Thungni's relic is yours and yours alone. Its display will be a statement of conquest and glory that none can deny!
A Healing Salve is worth nothing! Better to bind the relic and use its power to drive us towards Hashut's realm of fire!
The Great Drill of Hashut can wait – your reputation in Zharr-Naggrund is far more pressing!
Guns for political favours? What a great idea…
Gold for our guns? Who could say no?
Resources for money? This fool is practically giving them away…
Labourers for resources? We would be fools not to accept.
Greed is good. In fact, it's better than good. Greed is GREAT.
Domination over meagre souls. There can be no greater pleasure.
With armaments comes the opportunity for even greater cruelty. Who could refuse?
In matters of the Conclave, influence is the only real power.
Desecrate the idol and use it as a banner for one of our regiments.
Take it to Zharr-Naggrund and offer it to Hashut. The Ancestor Gods mean nothing to us now.
Curses upon the false gods of times part – we follow Hashut alone!
Khorne offers us the souls of Slaaneshi Daemons…
Slaanesh offers us the souls of Khornate Daemons…
Nurgle offers us the souls of Tzeentchian Daemons…
Tzeentch offers us the souls of Nurglish Daemons…
Our soldiers there could do with some help, and additional Labourers would surely ease their burden.
This one seems perfectly suited to a quiet post overseeing industrial production...
This will make our enemies tremble even more 'neath the might of the Dawi-Zharr!
He is clearly trying to trick us. Ignore him, for now at least, and simply increase the bore of our slugs and bolts.
Traitors of this sort must be made an example of, no matter who they are.
Is this not something we have all done at one time or another?
By keeping the leaders among our Labour force on side, we reduce the chances of unrest or a full-blown rebellion erupting.
Tell all of Zharr-Naggrund of the rich bounty our mines have produced.
Our warriors will make up for any deficiencies in materiel with sheer Dawi willpower!
Nothing but the best for those who expand our empire!
Damn the consequences, but the resources the machine carries in its hoppers are more valuable than anything else.
The drill must be stopped before it does even more damage. Send Labourers into the tunnel to destroy the machine!
Attack and enslave the Daemons! Let them see the mettle of those they now serve.
Our Dwarfen cousins shall suffer, as is their miserable, curmudgeonly lot...
Replenish our Labourers by enslaving more Greenkins. There's no such thing as too many!
Perhaps those filthy, foul skaven will serve well in our mines?
A further injection of Labourers should see the factory running without any loss in output.
By limiting the movements of our Labourers, we should be able to stop this sort of thing from happening in future.
Perhaps he will have found something of use? What harm is there in listening? We can always kill him afterwards…
We will not suffer liars in our midst – take him to the Sprouting Chamber!
The empire of the Dawi-Zharr lives and dies by its machines of war. Build bigger, build better, build more!
We must build ever larger forges and from these, drills, to bore ever deeper in search of Hashut's unholy blood.
The Dawi-Zharr never back down from a fight! Time to slaughter these Cathayans and see what their Caravan has to offer…
One lousy Caravan isn't worth the bother. The Cathayans can keep their lives for today, and their paltry cargo.
These foolish wazzocks must be taught a lesson... Uzkul-Dhrath-Zharr, tear them apart!
Fight on sight! There's no other answer when it comes to those wretched interlopers. Time to call our warriors to battle and spill some Dawi blood!
Fight them! Break their ancient bones and seize their wealth.
We must not be distracted from our goal. Leave them to their Unlife.
At the very least, these Hobgoblins will make for great cannon fodder. Better they die first than your fellow Dawi-Zharr!
Probably best to let them get on with their silly blessing so we can be on our way.
Hungry are they? Well in that case they can fill their bellies with our blades!
What's a few sacrifices for the many? It was probably time to cull the weak anyway – these Daemons are doing you a favour!
We will crush this host and make our consignment even more lucrative than it already is!
Hostilities and losses can be easily avoided if we just keep moving.
To end a fight as quickly and easily as possible, one needs the capacity to deal the lethal blow.
One who can endure the most dangerous and prolonged attacks has the best chance of landing a lethal counterattack.
Who are we to leave these poor Ogre mercenaries without work? Times are hard, after all!
You are a strong, independent Chaos Dwarf who needs no Ogre!
A detour through a strange portal in a dark, underground passageway… When you put it like that, what could go wrong?
We have no time to go wandering through portals. We must continue on our journey!
We found it and it's ours! If these Daemons love their Cargo so much, they shouldn't have just left it lying around!
We don't need their goods, anyway. Grateful Daemons, on the other hand…
Powerful Daemons for our army? Yes please!
Obviously these are the superior Daemons... Think of the bloodshed!
The urge to throw one of the retinue into this strange formation is hard to ignore; it feels like there is great power to be had here.
Go around it – it is best not to meddle in things we do not understand.
We can handle a few off-road chicanes – any potential losses will probably cost us less in the long run than gaining a reputation for tardiness.
We should stick to the main route and avoid exposing the cargo to any unnecessary risks.
Kill some rats and reduce the length of our journey? Sounds like a win-win!
We don't know how many rats are in this tunnel. The last thing we need is to be overwhelmed by the vermin!
The smell of gunpowder is preferable to the smell of rotting flesh. Eliminate them!
Their sacrifice allows us to continue without further losses.
Their attempts at an ambush are frankly so embarrassing it would be an insult to Hashut to let them live.
They might get lucky one day. Probably not any time soon, though.
We don't need any guidance! We Dawi-Zharr have an excellent sense of direction, thank you very much!
We need to reach our destination quickly; this guide had better be worth the price!
With this beast in our Convoy’s ranks, assailants will not consider us an easy target.
It would be foolish to part with some of our cargo – we have no need for this beast and can adequately protect ourselves.
We can brook no frailty in this Convoy. This is time well invested.
Training is always important, but we must not lose track of time.
Lives are cheap, but cargo is expensive. We cannot risk this untested path.
Our troops can handle a few burns and blisters. After all, are we not the Dwarfs of fire?
Dire times as they are, if the homeland is to be protected then allies cannot be turned away.
This abomination will always be a threat! She will be brought before the Court, then executed.
Nobody else can be trusted to protect Shang-Wu as you would; keep the city – you will defend it to the last if you must!
The Lustrian expedition must remain your priority. Someone else would be better placed to rule over Shang-Wu in your absence.
You will remain in Bleak Hold Fortress and focus your efforts toward Naggaroth.
