For all lofty ideals, there is an underlying fundamental truth. Words may move the heart, but wealth moves mountains.
One cannot stand truly alone; summon the diplomatic corps and prepare more shipments for the Ivory Road.
We must turn our gaze inward and weed out the weakness in our hearts.
The Great Bastion supposedly keeps Cathay safe from outside influences. Let's see how it copes with a flying tomb full of skeletons…
The poor Tomb Kings have suffered too long in the intense heat of the desert. Send them to cool off in Norsca.
Some folks just don't get along, especially when necromancy is involved. Isn't it time for a skeletal delegation to greet the Vampire Counts of Sylvania?

The witches of the west will surely give your forces a warm reception!
The Dragons think a simple wall will keep Daemons out. Let's test that theory!
Why make a choice when you can do everything?

Hitching a ride with a Caravan will get your cultists to Pigbarter, a prominent trading hub that will serve as a great nexus for expansion.

Desperate Elven survivors are fleeing towards the Shrine of Khaine in Ulthuan. Your new toys could easily overpower the crew and take control of the vessel!
A perilous journey that few ships are willing to make. That only makes it more likely that nobody will see you coming.
Some of the destroyed Arks are drifting towards Grand Cathay. It wouldn't be too much work to slip a cultist or two into their holds…
The Pirates of Sartosa have a staging base in Bretonnia. Chances are that they probably wouldn't notice an extra ship or two appearing in their harbour…
A prime opportunity exists to destabilise the High Elves. Direct the Norscans towards Ulthuan!
The sleeping Dragons of the east won't know what hit them. Send the Norscan raiders to invade the coast of Grand Cathay!
The lands of men offer ample opportunity for mischief. Let the rebels bring Chaos to their fellow brethren!
The Dark Lands have a variety of bickering Lords, all of whom would make excellent targets.
Whilst not quite as efficient, spreading your cultists out could give you influence in both theatres.
Aekold joins you and brings with him the monument’s arcane knowledge of martial skill.
Aekold joins you and brings with him the monument’s arcane knowledge of mental fortitude.
Allow the Blue Scribes to take residence in your libraries, offering them enough space achieve their task.
Lead the Blue Scribes through chaotic battles to further their studies in the mortal realm.
Let's see if their scheming was worth it once their armies lie defeated!
Record this slight in the Book of Grudges to deal with in due course, lest we forget this vile misdeed!
The brutal punishment in battle is the only way to answer this disrespect!
Their words will be recorded in the Dammaz Kron, so none shall forget their blasphemy!
They won't be laughing anymore once the legions of the Dawi descend!
Enter their name into the Dammaz Kron – this disrespect must be remembered through the ages!
The Slayers are eager to crush our foes; why not let them try?
Rushing to action solves nothing! Patience is required, for all grudges will be settled in time.
Feed the flames of this rivalry; our enemy's arrogance cannot go unanswered!
The Clans can rest assured that this grudge will be settled soon enough!
Reaching out to the Guilds could earn you gold galore, not to mention the support of their artisans.
Surely the veterans among the Clans would be proud to raise their axes in your name.
Call upon your warriors – it is time to cross some names from the Book of Grudges!
Let it be known that the whole realm shall quake with the ferocity of our vengeance!
We have other priorities; we cannot allow ourselves to be distracted by petty nonsense!
Recompense the Cathayans – they are well-connected, our reputation amongst the other races must not be tarnished by a rat problem!
Members of their cavalcade have seen the Skaven menace and have a measure of the blockade forces – knowledge that could be vital for the task at hand!
Receive a single gift of high value.
Receive a selection of useful gifts.
The Caravan Master’s driver knows the trade route that bypasses the hub, but is asking for a steep bribe in return for his information.
The scout saw the enemy with his own eyes, but was deeply traumatised by what he saw; his information is only a tad more useful than useless.
Putting roofs over heads and hot food into bellies can heal any Dwarf’s spirit, at least for a time.
The anger of loss should be channelled into defeating the one responsible – have them join the warriors and be given military rations.
The best way to assimilate the refugees is to put them to work for the good of the Hold, brick by brick.
There are other Holds under your jurisdiction that could benefit from a boost in their populations.
Some of these Dwarfs are already weathered warriors, but just short of the right weapon for the job at hand.
Tragedy has driven some of these Dwarfs to madness, but your host can still benefit from such a quality…
Help these foolish, small-minded manlings to help you, even if it puts you out of pocket.

Leave peacefully now, but ensure retribution is claimed soon, in line with tradition. This will not be forgotten!
In large enough quantities, gold is always a good means of apology.
There is no time for delay while you're in charge... only constant, unrelenting vengeance!
Just for now, you have other things to attend to while our kin continue to settle our scores...

These regions were neglected by the Iron Dragon, so will stay under our stewardship whether Cathay likes it or not.
This excursion has been a successful endeavour in improving our relations with the east, but matters back home are of greater importance.
The Iron Dragon could be a powerful local ally should we decide to establish a longer-term foothold here.

We are not here to make friends; the wealth of this land is ours for the taking. The rebels will be dealt with if they happen to get in our way.

Cowardice on the field must be punished. It is time to make a bloody example of {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_nur_cha_bray_shaman_wild_chieftain}}.

Clearly, Kayzk is mistaken. {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_nur_cha_bray_shaman_wild_chieftain}} followed orders and worked his magic as intended.

Put a stop to this nonsense and silence any further religious debate with brute force.

Assure Grukmur that both he and Mournhowl are equal in the eyes of their loving Grandfather.

The zealot's charges must be withheld until the barrage has ceased.
The value of these captives should be traded to increase the might of the warhost.
Slaughter and carnage are encouraged – a few hostages won't be missed.
Someone needs to talk the fool down, but Khargan need make no apologies.
Defend the honour of your Chaos Dwarf ally. After this, none will dare challenge him again!
This madness must stop. Exert your dominance and brook no dissent from either Chieftain!
Curtail the use of dangerous magic. You cannot risk such forces raging out of control.
Power is always a good thing – let the Winds of Magic blow!
Commit to both to channelling and directing Ketzak's magic in a more productively controlled fashion.
Knowledge is a weapon, and it's always better to be armed!
Disregard Ketzak's request; the Chaos Dwarfs are trusted allies, and not to be trifled with!
Ketzak may be a worm, but his words ring true. Kayzk constantly oversteps – it's clear he cannot be trusted.
The Fimir is a trifling monstrosity, not to be trusted over one of Nurgle's own.
Put Khargan in his place at once – this madness must end!
Let the madman run amok – his insane penchant for violence is much too useful to be curtailed.
Assert your authority over the meddling Fimir.
Secrets cannot be tolerated in camp; insist the Fimir gets what he needs.
The Crown's influence is legendary; under your command, its power will shape the fate of the world!
Such dark power is much too dangerous to reside in anyone's hands. Seal it away for eternity!
Though you have lost His favour, there is more blood to be spilled.
Arbaal's story ends here, bow out of the campaign.
Dis iz it, boyz! We smashed dem propa, and now da treasure iz ours!
Feral monsters follow wherever Orcs wreak havoc and ruin. With enough applied violence, some of them can even be tamed to serve the tribe.
The mounds of dead have attracted throngs of ravenous Squigs. Those nasty little buggers can be useful in the right circumstances.
Giant arachnids crawl out from numerous holes in the wake of wholesale destruction. Goblins in particular seem to have a way with them...
Surely, you cannot do worse than this one has.
The bigger the gut, the more he can afford lenience.
Still meat left on them bones, an' we're still 'ungry!
Job's done! No point in fightin' unless someone's payin'.
Our enemy is merely posturing, they have no intention of acting on these threats.
The nature of war is that it expands, the Asur stand ready to fend off any who seek to invade our lands.
You retain your settlement in Norsca.

In the East, we shall muster – to strike Fellheart’s fleet, decimate the carrion corsairs, and shatter the marauding Orcs.

Let the Defender of Ulthuan ready his blade!
The Everqueen must be warned – her realm lies in peril.
The black-fletched arrows of the Shadow King strike where no fleet may sail.
The Loremaster's mighty sorceries will shield us against the coming storm.
The Warden of Tor Yvresse will not see Ulthuan fall.
The slumbering might of Caledor stirs with its Dragon Prince.
All keels aligned at last; the invasion is surely near.
The storm has broken – let the Dragonships haste to Ulthuan’s aid.
Ulthuan stands inviolate, her foes broken, her fleets ascendant. From Starwood’s gift arises our dominion – the seas shall ever be ours.

Though the world teeters on the brink, Ulthuan must not fall. Teclis must return to safeguard the White Tower.
Saphery shall have aid and counsel, yet the High Loremaster’s path lies elsewhere.
Our strength must serve the wider world. The White Tower shall stand firm under its own light.
This chieftan has earned the right to live... perhaps this will benefit us in time?
It is your custom. It is your choice. It is your pleasure.
Let the carrion fuse with my mortal rot, that we may become one virulent power!
Be gone, winged vermin – ride the pestilent winds that bore you to my sight.
Remake my form, recast my soul – for in Change alone lies truth.
Your unblinking gaze has already divined my immutable path.
No life is too frail to be slain, no blood too sacred to be spilled!
I cast you out, Hound – kinless, to run the trail of the slaughter yet to come.
In our shared excess we shall weave indulgence eternal – an ecstasy of fleshly torment and obsessive agony.
Feast upon the dolour of our parting, and shed its scales as you would your serpent’s skin.
It could not have gone far, surely. We could take it before we are too tired to go on, surely…
Falling prey to rashness is the surest way to give up one's role as predator.
Wounds will heal, eventually – not so for beast and anything it leaves behind.
The price of avoiding battle is not as steep as that of hurtling headlong into it – though a price there will be.
More pairs of eyes, whose sharpness could be of use. Not to mention the sharpness of the newcomers' blades.
The rival hunters hoped their pursuit would end here and they would be victorious. Only the former will come to pass.
Norscans do not feast in order to forget – on the contrary, this is how they are reminded of their purpose. So let them revel and remember.
Some may be given to intermittent infighting. Some may try to peel away from the main force and seek their fortunes elsewhere.
They found it. They will keep it.
They found it. You will keep it.
The wretches' ploy was successful enough that some got to keep their lives, and your supplies. These ones, however…
These one will lead you to the others, or whatever cache they keep hidden – or they will die. Well… *and then* they will die.
For once, as you pay honour this place, the only sacrifice your faith requires turns out to be a material one. It has an obvious bracing effect on your warriors.
The price of devotion is sometimes to steep. Pass by this place  in silence, and hope your own silence passes before battle is joined.
You and your hunters all died here. This is what your failure looks like. May it speed you on to a different outcome. Or not. I said the same thing to those corpses here…
On your hunt, you may sometimes see my bird, and hear my voice. Follow them and you will reach your target. Unlike these poor wretches…
The Dark Gods may not exactly show you the way, but they can imbue your warriors' hearts with a predatory fire.
If they must face a foe, they shall do it here – once. Whomever survives will come out the stronger for it.
Let the hunters glare and plod. The steady routine of pursuit will quench their dissatisfaction, eventually.
Prayer and sacrifice will not suffice. Once found – and found they will be, no matter how painstaking the search – the lost ones will steel the rest's resolve.
The quicker the pace, the further behind the memory of those lost will be left.
The slower the pace, the quicker the replacements will arrive. Surely this was also the Dark Gods' intent?
The march is but a prelude to the true challenge: the battle itself. It is there where strength must be the equal of resolve.
Much like frequent revelries, spoils are wonderfully rejuvenative to both flesh and spirit.
The march will separate true ice from mere heaps of shuddering snow.
You will exchange the divine ill-will evident in this place for the ill-will of your hunters, who will provide spoils for the propitiation.
You will hunt down the mundane beasts of these climes in place of your ultimate quarry and slaughter them to appease the Dark Gods.
As much as you tell yourselves it is a sign of strength, it is in fact a form of punishment – maybe the one the Dark Gods intended.
A challenge blessed by the Dark Gods, surely. Their strength will favour the victor.
Killing a wretch in a duel is pointless when other can do it on the your behalf. Yet such a murder carries a sour aftertaste.
A madman's tales of failure may prove instructive… at least until he finds a blade of grass or a bit of moss to wage war on.
The offering certainly has its uses. Yet any boon from the Dark Gods is  double-edged.
The Dark Gods' benevolence – or what counts for one – could usually be counted on, as long as you give enough.
It is not that the Dark Gods are prone to answering those. But the ritual itself will bolster your the hunters' resolve.
To better rend the monster's hide.
To better keep one's hide one's own.
The recollection of claws and blades tearing through the foe, and of the foe's own weapons breaking harmlessly against you.
Their weapons would have failed them were they to stand alone. Now, they could carry the day.
Folded into the hunters' ranks, their presence will forge a stronger force.
There are more ways than one to participate in a hunt. Fighting the beast, yes, but just as importantly – finding one's way in its lands.
Nothing steadies a mercenary heart's traitorous flutters more than spoils in hand. Your warriors will remain yours.
For Norscans, the best place for a mercenary heart is in one's own chest. The second best place, should the heart belong to an enemy, is in one's fist.
If they have thought to do it, they are just as susceptible as their marks. The distance between  cunning and gullibility is measured in gold.
Spurred on by their rage and the enemy’s unexpected temerity, the hunters press on.
Progress can be sacrificed, for a time. Your Lord’s survival cannot.
The Dark Gods will be repaid in blood once you reach your target. For now, an offering will suffice to restore your Lord to full strength – and more.
If a Norscan can breathe and walk at the same time, then a Norscan can raid and hunt a monster at the same time, as well.
Distractions would ill-serve the real purpose. However, the raiders' knowledge can focus the hunters' efforts most effectively.
No spoils can be spared at this moment. Let the raiders eke out what they can from the land – your concern is but a single inhabitant.
Accomplishment thus preordained, the hunters lengthen their stride.
There is no better nourishment than a clear vision of victory.
Surely the apparitions have already revelled somewhere along the way through their imaginary expanses. Your hunters feel compelled to re-create their own version of that feast.
There is always time. Maybe some of the zeal will return.
You cannot succeed what you do not finish – though neither can you fail. Every dark pit has its frost-rimmed lining.
The battle will commence! May the Dark Gods revel in the slaughter to unfold – you certainly shall!
You can wait. And so the beast will, too.
Let our shared virulence wax upon the mortal coil, that it may learn decay is the only truth.
Let us weave upon the endless complexity of fate – an architecture of layer upon cunning layer.
Take the fallen, struck down by my cunning, upon our shared path of Ruin.
Let us be drawn into the abyss of rapturous excess and exquisite torment.
Give them food and shelter and they shall serve your Troll Kingdom in return, one way or another.
Leave the mindless fools be – you aren’t looking for more subjects right now.
You assign the lesser Trolls to your settlements.
You assign the lesser Trolls to your armies.
“We strike at Marienburg's tender underbelly – its magnates fat with coin and complacency!”
“Tonight, we batter down the Slaver's Gate and bask in the riches of the Druchii taskmasters!”
“We make crimson the mouth of the Lynsk, and hang the Boyars from the ramparts for all to behold!”
“Let the wine-soaked squabblers of Bordeleaux find sobriety upon our pikes!”
Let them come. The rageful brutes have given you enough advance warning. Khornates enjoy poor odds, don't they? That suits you just fine.
A challenge too random and too easy to circumvent – though the Khornates may engage in some fear-mongering and depredation before they inevitably forget all about you and move on.
Why not send a messenger of your own to return the challenge – and guide them to the monstrous presence you felt? They can come for you later, if they live.
Fire will safeguard you from the disease, but may draw the malice of those who consider such acts as sacrilege against the Fly Lord.
Banishing them will preserve your forces at next to no cost. But the outcasts may become the breeding ground for something more insistently tumorous...
A gamble it is. Should it turn into a culling by plague-ridden death, they can only blame themselves. And never repeat it.
This is how it begins – how *he* begins. You must end it, even at the cost of incurring his lesser followers' enmity.
You have practiced the part of sagely Shaman to perfection. True, they will spread the message on their way – until they lose it for good.
Feeding the egos of those so enraptured by the Serpent is risky, but oh so tempting…
...but not intrigued enough. A beacon they shall have. They will be it. Whoever comes after, let them.
You must know. They will draw their symbols of power in your presence. Maybe it will be for the worse, but you cannot resist the pull of knowledge.
They are not competent enough to achieve anything unexpected – including anything that hurts you. This you know well. The unexpected benefits, however...
Vengeful, prideful children and Khorne's favour are trouble waiting to happen. Best you don't take chances and crush the whelp at once.
Those keen on joining your tribe must first face this boy's warriors. Doubtless you will lose potential recruits, but so will the boy lose his life, eventually.
By right of conquest, *he* should serve *you*. You can direct his Hound-blessed ire more usefully. Or maybe the mere offer will fan his vengeance even further?...
If they have started talking, some fraction of the Crow's attention is on you already. But culling them swiftly may only anger some of his lesser servants.
At worst, they may suffer a little. At best, some will suffer so excruciatingly that they will turn into something very... useful.
Whoever he is working for (apart from *that one*) will not hear from him again. They will seek a reprisal. So predictable.
Who knows who else he may have influenced here, or on his way here. Well... he does. About the latter, you cannot do much. About the former...
Create a threat he'll easily escape, then follow. Meeting enemies would be expected. Finding something of use, less so, but a pleasant surprise. The only kind you allow.
Give them an opening to strike in force before their "subtler" methods invite a worse outcome.
Killing for riches and not asking questions is what your people were born and bred to do. A simple solution, though expensive.
What you did once, one of yours will do again. If he can lure someone to your side, even better.
Apparently, you did enough to get their attention. None of it was by accident. Yours is not the scent of prey, but the challenge of a predator.
You never make yourself available without making yourself ready. They will reach you, certainly. Well, some of them will.
You have prepared incantations for just such cases. They will have some of what is yours – something you can afford to part with – but not you.
Under the guise of being one of your own, this harbinger of decay reveals themselves as a harbinger of a powerful cohort of Nurgle followers. And they are coming.
It is one of your hand-picked agents. Disappointing. Not the betrayal – you always expect that. But the rank nonchalance with which they accept their return to oblivion.
Your followers know some of your strength. They should remain ignorant of that of a Ruinous Power. A plague will come, a plague will go. Nothing more, nothing less.
An open clash is much preferrable to poisonous words – especially those not your own.
Such desperate zealotry is bound to end up badly for this one, knowing the Serpent. Though it will hurt you somewhat in the process.
You warriors may not fully understand what the Serpent is, but they are veritable savants on the subject of riches. This zealot's words cannot compare.
You would overcome him in a duel, but the ensuing magical conflagration might draw his patron's extremely unwanted attention. Open battle it is.
It is difficult to impress upon your warriors the import of avoiding this particular encounter. They will be disgruntled – but it is a small price to pay.
Apprehension and pride in your craft battle for a short while. Pride wins out.
A Champion will challenge theirs in single combat. Not you, of course. But you will... help yours along. Yet, knowing Khornates, things may just turn out for the worse...
It is no ritual you've ever heard of, but offering that your warriors – and theirs – bloody themselves before battle will seem "sacred" to them, surely. May they will be worse off.
First, you fully turn the poison upon the carrier. Then you track him as he staggers, dying, to those who corrupted him. Just as you thought.
You give him his fill of agony, commensurate with his betrayal. The unseen malefactor is deterred for now, but this one's joyous acceptance of his torments makes your warriors uneasy.
You make sure the brew will have an agonising aftermath for the assassin and those around him, and send him out to whoever corrupted him. You hope they will get a nasty surprise.
His strength cannot be allowed to grow. His superficial idiocy even more so.
He will encounter some other form of ugliness soon enough to wage war on – though his jibes would sting your warriors' pride for a while.
Twisting his body beyond recognition would ruin his path to perfection and leave him stranded by his followers. Would it be costly? Yes. Would it be petty? Yes. But oh so satisfying...
You will make it easy for him. He knows what you are capable of. And now you will show him.
Your stillness will oppose his Change. It may not be possible to nullify it completely, but it would be close enough for comfort.
One of your Shamans may be neutralised but you have more where he came from. They will do job – if properly incentivised.
It will do no good to run. It will barely do any good to fight, but you may well preserve your life – before the real battle begins.
You can escape unscathed. The Daemon's vendetta is not personal. Unfortunately, that means it will do at scale what it fails to do to you.
A combined display of mindless fury from your warriors may *just* slow it down long enough for you to find a way to banish it.
You can gain distance and sufficiently shield yourself from the creature's miasma. Others in your army, and across your domain, will not be as lucky.
The inhabitants of your lands will make the Daemon's acquaintance in your stead. It seems only happy to do so. You can do nothing but oblige.
Knowing you know nothing was your bane as a fledgling sorcerer, and even now. Saying it – nay, shouting it on your knees – is... Well, the Keeper will enjoy it and so will go away.
As of just now, the coming of the Daemon was *always* the intention. You shall house its secrets in your domain and not in any way try to learn them. For once, you may be sincere.
They enjoy their playthings, don't they? Flesh and essence swapped, minds fractured and conjoined. Poor lonesome Sayl cannot offer much. But looking at your forces, you have an idea...
There will be no answer, and neither does it expect it. But it seems amused by your attempts at piling interrogatives until your mouth and mind drip with nonsense.
A ten-foot tall mirror in an elaborate golden frame. You look… exquisite.
A painting of Quai Yin, delicately traced and framed in pearl.  The lofty image of the Moon Empress, mounted on the wall over the revel pits of your Pleasure Palace... Hmm. Delightfully wicked.
A jade torque, expertly fashioned to resemble the coiled form of a Dragon. It is the perfect fit for your arm.
From the Cathayan general’s own collection – possibly an invaluable gift from some immortal tyrant or other. Learning how to play might amuse you for a day or two.
Surely Skavenkind will struggle to survive without the Rat Daemons' future assistance?
If disease is your only dream, the Corruptor is its mortal embodiment, spreading a withering death wherever it goes.
See beyond the heroic posing and posturing to the additional burning rage gradually fired among the lowly Skaven warriors in attendance, and smile.
You may think you have chosen badly, right up until death itself races from the shadows, disappearing again just as quickly as it showed its jagged, blood-soaked face.
It may never be clear exactly which schemes have come to fruition and which have not, or how, or why, but the Horned Rat's work will get done.
You don't care who or what might take ahold of the book, as the opportunity for additional wealth is much more intriguing.
For the better of everyone, yourself including, this book will be contained in a safe location at your capital.
Dismissing a Legendary Lord will allow them to return to their faction. You may get another chance to defeat them and Subjugate them in the future.
Test their mettle and decide their fate – they may yet be worthy of a place in your warhost.
You have little time for weaklings already once shamed – send them away.
A friend to Daemons, Orghotts Daemonspew considers himself a conduit for the fate he will soon achieve, searching for servants to enable his true and final ascendancy.
An individual fascinated with the smaller creatures, Bloab Rotspawned was a perfect follower of Nurgle. Now a vessel for the spread of Nurgle's Rot, he gleefully spreads it wherever possible.
Once seeking fervent vengeance against Tzeentch, Morbidex instead found the comforting embrace of the Urfather's Nurglings.
These donations are needed for the war effort and cannot be spared for frivolous festivities.
A funeral procession with Ulric and Morr's representatives will be arranged. These souls deserve to rest easy.
This tragedy cannot be allowed to repeat itself! New recruits will be diverted to protecting these people.
Though it may be fruitless, an attempt to seek out these beasts must be made to avenge the fallen.
Though there may be no love lost between their races, the Beastmen are a threat to all.
The Wood Elves have been known to murder men for approaching the forests of the Old World and Todbringer cannot take a risk supporting potential future enemies.
The Hunter's eyes are that of a vicious wolf – canny and forthright. Ulric's support is plain to see and the Graf would never doubt one touched by the Wolf God.
If the nobility chased after every shadow the peasantry claim to have seen, then nothing would ever be achieved.
My oath is sworn to the thirteenth Everchosen, and my forces to the ruinous tide that shall scour the realms!
Favour today is nought but distant and cruel laughter tomorrow. I shall wreak a ruin mightier still!
Alone amongst such destruction, is there even a world left to save?
There is nowhere to run, there is nowhere left to hide.
Stories will be told, generations from now, of those who did not give up.
Abandon the weak. Abandon the wounded.\\nGods forgive us, but we must collect our strength.
Perhaps it is not us or the Dark Gods that decide these final moments, but fate itself.
Everyone must fight, else we all share the same fate.
Our forces are strong, our people prepared.
Hit them where it hurts most – attack Marienburg!
Seek out the dark apothecary and his secrets.
Steady and unyielding, like an avalanche of rot.
From a meagre sapling, a garden. From meagre devotion, a conquest.
An arcane cornucopia shall be borne upon the discordant peal of bronze.
Thrive in the menace freshly stamped into the southern mulch.
Our armies will take from the ships and feast!
This port shall be a conduit to the Winds of Magic!

Reclaim the remnants that are strong, and dispose of those that are not. Kindling for the cold fires of more consequential servants.
The scraps must be used where they can to patch up the remnants of broken forces.
A token to be carried on Nagash's behalf, for he was the source of its power.
A trifling artefact. Its magic will flow into Nagash. The rest will be dust.
This one carries a whisper of them who served Nagash during the war against the wretched fool Alcadizaar.
This one carries a whisper of Nehekhara's pride and martial glory undiluted by kingly squabbles. He serves only absolute strength.
This one carries a whisper of when first Nagash, in secret, rose foremost among his peers obsessed with necromancy.
This one carries a whisper of hard-earned martial skill unmarred by death's oblivion, the wasteland of memory.
They will never walk free of Nagash's will, but they will not require as much of it to walk, either.
All soil is fruitful for Nagash's purpose when it is barren of all life.
Nothing is new, and once all of it was his. This as well.
None will have the knowledge, but all will know what it feels like to have more of it.
Memory of what was, so they know what can be no more.
Memory of what never was, so they know what will be, forever.
The "trade" has changed. The stock will be these peddlers' souls, the Land of the Dead its new and final port of call.
Whatever they carry, they will carry into Nagash's hands. There will be no negotiations. Nagash does not trade in coin.
Some of them Nagash will not even deign to raise again.
Before Nagash, only words of obeisance will do, until no further words are necessary.
Their souls' worshipful outcries will be the mortar of Nagash's edifices. Their bodies are redundant.
Their limbs will not forget their mortal skill as they fulfil their duty. Their souls are redundant.
Let them continue. A lesson will be learned by all, but more harshly by one.
They have one duty only. In that, they have faltered. On the march, they will not.
At long last, the toil of your horrid hunt bears fruit – for you gain valuable insight of the verminous deeds…
The Master Assassin is adept in the gruesome arts of theft, murder, and silencing the complications that tend to follow.
The Warlord is a hardy war leader who towers over his subordinates. His size, however, belies a keen tactical acumen.
The Warlock Master is an exemplar of the engineer breed, capable of producing results either explosively impressive or impressively explosive.
The Grey Seer falls back in a smaller vessel and casts a great shroud of addling darkness over the pursuing enforcers.
The Master Assassin plants a nest of exquisite smoke-bombs in the enforcers' path, their near-sentient fumes curling into the victims' lungs.
The Warlord’s death squad draws the enemy vanguard into a bloodbath and leaves the gruesome remains for the rest to see. Sheer terror halts the chase – at least for a time.
The Warlock Master sabotages the water turbines that propel vessels through the murksome flow, greatly slowing down the trailing enforcer-barges.
Thanquol had faced the Empire many times, and against the pathetic stratagems of the man-things, his victory was most assured.
Like refining Warpstone, the anger of the beard-things only strengthened with time, and their bitterness at the loss of Zhufbar could not be overstated.
All Skaven resented the pointy-ears, for their island-nest was both naturally fortified and magically warded against the Under-Empire's reach.
A new and powerful Vampire Lord joins your faction!
We would benefit greatly from having the Lords of Aquitaine serve under our banner, and they are hardly in a position to refuse such a "request".
Gold should help smooth their Lords transition to serving under our banner.
Perhaps now is not the time to force matters, and there is always the chance to convince them later diplomatically.
The power of the books is great... and that power is ours!
This power is beyond us! For the good of this world, the books must be destroyed!
Boris is required at the capital to sure-up support for the Bokha bloodline.
Boris will forsake his followers and join with your forces for the good of the Motherland.
Send him to the port-city, where he can confront Chaos on the Sea of Claws.
The Red Tzar travels north to Praag, so ensuring Kislev remains the bulwark of the Old World.
Be'lakor can never be truly destroyed, but near-eternity as a pale shadow-form is torment enough.
Tzeentch's curse will ensure he shall obey you. Use his power against your enemies!

This is Chi'an Chi's doing, without a doubt. Too often have naive citizens of Cathay fallen under the Changer's wicked thrall. We must scour every home until we find the traitors who have ensorcelled these simple-minded simians.

We cannot hope to locate the agents of Chi'an Chi responsible for this simian menace, for the God of Lies excels subterfuge. All we can do is slaughter every monkey on sight and pray nothing worse follows.
Their minds are out of balance. Only by the release of the excess Yin energies swirling within their skulls may harmony be regained. This will require the finest surgeons in all Cathay.

Let the afflicted rest and recuperate. The Winds forever shift, and so too will this magical malaise. Fine teas and medicinal herbs will leave them refreshed and more determined than ever to serve our Emperor.

Upon bathing in those sacred waters, not only will their fire be dimmed, but the Spirit Dragon will have their ancestors bear witness to their ugly fury. In their shame, they will know harmony once more.
If the fury cannot be quenched, perhaps it can be mastered. Breathing exercises will calm them until the next battle, and there they can unleash this rage upon deserving targets.

The woman seems credible and honest. Her noble status must be restored. To save face, her true family will ply us with tribute for this belated act of justice, though in truth they will despise us for the shame this heaps upon them.
If she were truly descended from the Celestial Dragon, she would not need to beg others for aid. Clap her in irons and send her away. It is for the noblewoman she sought to usurp to decide her fate.
Though his manner is abhorrent, we have much to learn from this well-travelled thug. His permanent services will be costly to secure, but every one of our warriors will greatly benefit.
Let the Maneater feast upon the finest meats and richest wines Grand Cathay has to offer. Soon enough, secrets will spill from his drunken, drooling maw.

Absurd though it seems, you sense in this creature a maternal care toward you. Upon its back, barely visible, blue furs create the shape of a crescent moon. You should show her that you adore her too.
You haven’t got time for felines!

As you fight the strange urge to bow, the cat's tail twitches impatiently. Along its length is red patterning which uncannily resembles a great serpent. The haughty feline refuses table scraps, but perhaps an offering of sublimely roasted boar leg would suffice?
Perhaps they are evil spirits – Chi’an Chi takes many forms. There’s a well nearby – grab the cats by the scruff and cast them in!
Breathe deep of the strange vapours within, and you shall be infused with the Winds themselves. As the harmonious power of Yin pulses through your veins, none will even dream of questioning you.
Entertain the alchemist. Bring forth some tea, but then send the madman and his box on their way.
All the Emperor's subjects should prosper from this singular discovery. Should we sink the opened chest into the river, the swirling magic within will touch every soul in the land.
Beware of strangers and their exotic gifts. Kill this imposter and have this box buried with them!

Ply the trader with whatever luxuries we have an excess of. It is imperative this enchanted stone is restored to its rightful place, lest its absence one day enable the Great Enemy to topple the Bastion.
It is heresy for a mere merchant to claim ownership of an artifact infused with the Emperor's Celestial magic. You will, however, look the other way if sufficiently remunerated.

The apparition of their disapproving forebears, beseeching them to pursue peace, will surely soften their hearts towards us. They will never know that this was merely an illusion wrought by our most inventive Alchemists.
You have bigger issues to address. Let the fools play at sabotage. It matters not.
Let us spread the rumour that our foe has fallen under the sway of the Great Enemy. Incensed by this supreme act of blasphemy and corruption, our legions will fight more tirelessly than ever before.
Execute one fifth of the army. They are short-lived mortals, and some will be traitors. The rest will be afraid to act further.
Lace the bananas and melons with serpent venom, and this infestation shall soon run its course. Disposing of the endless simian corpses will be a fiendish task, however.
These are citizens of the Celestial Empire! If they cannot deal with a few thieving monkeys themselves, they barely deserve the Moon Empress' love.
The Caravan's slender profits are not to be shared with these chancers. We shall take the usual route and get to our destination anyway.
Pay the price and arrive faster… maybe.
These guides are not to be trusted, they could be leading us into an ambush. Stay on the known route.
Entrepreneurs take chances. Agree to the profit-share and see us reach the markets before our rivals.
We keep to the Emperor’s road, tried and tested.
We take the trail, and damn the cost!
Your guides mutter that to take such cargo is cursed. Perhaps it is best to leave it.
If you don't take it, someone else will! This is an enterprise run for profit, so let's make more money!
There are crates stamped with the sigil of Shallya. Within are medicines and tinctures that can be put to good use.
Exotic spices are worth far more. Add this to your Caravan's inventory and see your wealth greatly increase.
Leave the dead to their silence. We march on.
A brief detour may yield what haste would forfeit.
No, taking on strangers mid-journey is not advised by the Caravan guilds for good reason.
The stranger may prove useful should the Caravan come under threat, but they have a strange look in their eyes…
The Caravan doesn't need the additional protection, and picking up strangers mid-journey is never a good idea.
Another hired sword will bolster the Caravan's protection, and if they are as good as they claim, should be worth the price.
His help was welcome, but we cannot pay a drifter from the cargo.
Let him march with us. A man who can master beasts may yet master worse.
Originally sent to hunt down your enemies, they are now ready to restock on ammunition and head into battle.
Eager to wet their blades with enemy blood once more, they will fight for you if they are but shown a way back home.
Keen fighters wish to return home and fight in your armies once more!
These missile specialists run low on ammunition. Send them back so they can restock and join your armies!
Your coin is theirs. Their service is yours. The honour will be shared.
Pay them. Veterans who choose their cause are worth more than common sellswords.
Honour they may have, but we will not buy it at such a price.
On arrival, the cargo held in the Caravan has doubled in size and value! This might be the most profitable venture yet!
The Caravan no longer holds mundane cargo, but exquisite weapons of exceptional quality instead. These should not be sold, but retained for our armies!
A wise man once said: "Better to pay than fight all day".
We will not be held to ransom by these yokels!
Perhaps on this occasion giving up some of the cargo is the best option.
We shall brook no delay! Slay these would-be ambushers.
Best to arrive, even if it's late.
We know they are there, they cannot surprise us – we can win this!
This will incur a delay, but we shall at least arrive intact.
They can go hungry rather than eat our comrades! Prepare for battle.
Perhaps let them eat one unit… and the rest can get away while the Ogres feed.
The Dark Powers shall not claim our souls!
Remember the names of the brave ones who stayed behind to let us escape!
We carve our passage through them. Let these corrupted creatures learn whose road this is.
We turn aside and march the longer road, avoiding the iron rain of the blockade’s sentinels.
One of your Sorcerers believes they can translate one of the inscriptions. Runic magic is generally beneath notice, but perhaps something of minor worth may result from this endeavour.
Dwarfen magic is paltry at best. Why squander your time attempting to translate these worthless runes? The tome is not without value, however – gold is, after all, gold.
Though her claim seem beyond absurd, you do have the wealth to pay the seer's tithe. Was that a flash of blue feathers beneath her sleeve?
The aged seer should be obliterated for her preposterous demands. Yet a peculiar half-smile on her face seems to suggest she expects this fate...
The renegade deity can sabotage even hate itself, or so your frothing cultist claims. Zuvassin's intentions are frankly bewildering, but to dim an enemy's fury is surely to your benefit.

Zuvassin's mouthpiece claims that emptying a sack of gold into the nearest river will cause an equal number of eyeballs to rain from the sky – consuming them will grant your legion sight beyond sight.
Order the construction of a great war-pit, where you will challenge your doubters to face you in unarmed combat. Few will dare attempt this.
You could look the other way, but the obscene, carnal rituals intended to weaken your influence will continue unabated. Whether they succeed remains to be seen.
Order all involved in the libidinous rite flayed to death, and a vast and bleeding statue of your own form constructed from their remains.
Rather than end the carnal ceremony, you could take your measure of pleasure. The experience will be unforgettable, though your followers will regard you with disdain.
If the eight-pronged star of Chaos is burned into the screaming fiend's hide, they will know rage as never before.
The near-forgotten symbol of the first Everchosen is reputed to grant unnatural power to those whose flesh bears it.
There is no need to exert yourself more than is necessary by making a show of things – a river of Gnoblar blood will yield sufficient dividend.
The long and bloody hunt will be most invigorating, and the Ruinous Powers will surely provide appropriate reward for such entertainment.
To feast upon the betrayer's lifeblood will surely flood your immortal veins with Ruinous sorcery. Not to mention that your legion will revere you all the more for your brutality.
Crush the traitor's skull to pulp, then beckon your loyal champion to drink the grey-red gore from your great hand. They deserve ascension.
The colossal goblet, carved from a great skull of unknown origin, houses a gallon of boiling blood. Drinking deep of it will demonstrate your incomparable courage.
The yellow growth palpitates horribly. The thought of forcing the pulsing, reeking malignancy down your throat is nauseating, but it would earn the Fly Lord's love.
The crystal vial houses a lilac fluid, its scent intoxicating. You sense that dousing yourself with it will cause indescribable agony – but render you irresistible.
The nine-eyed, twisted face upon the hovering book's leathery cover tries to tear itself free at your approach. It seeks to bond itself to your flesh.
Order the immediate execution of every mortal kept in your dungeons and torture chambers, then burn the bodies in a vast pyre. The touch of Chaos shall grow yet stronger.
With their inhabitants in hiding or oblivious in their madness, there would be little resistance as your cackling Daemons scour nearby mortal homesteads for wealth.
An Exalted Bloodthirster shall replace the Herald of Khorne to lead this Daemonic army to even greater massacres. Skulls for the Skull Throne!
The Herald demands more time with this army to collect more skulls for Khorne. The Exalted one will return to claim the mantle of command in time.
To disobey Khorne's will is to invite His scrutiny; ensure the blood flows and the skulls are collected, or face His wrath.
An Exalted Great Unclean One shall replace the Herald of Nurgle to lead this Daemonic host to even greater contagions. Spread Grandfather's blessings!
The Herald has yet to unleash a tide of virulence. The Exalted One will return to claim the mantle of command in time.
Nurgle will let this act of defiance stand if the Herald successfully increases the Plague God's tally. To fail would not be wise.
An Exalted Keeper of Secrets shall replace the Herald of Slaanesh to lead this Daemonic host to even greater depravities. Hail the Dark Prince!
The Herald demurs for a truly violent release has yet to occur. The Exalted One will return to claim the mantle of command in time.
A selfish Herald, declining to be subsumed, wanting to experience the climax of depravity herself. Slaanesh is intrigued, but must not to be disappointed, or else…
An Exalted Lord of Change shall replace the Herald of Tzeentch to lead this Daemonic host to even greater feats of destruction. Change is inevitable.
The Herald has plots in place that have yet to come to fruition. The Exalted One will return to claim the mantle of command in time.
Rebuffing Tzeentch's demand, the Herald puts his own schemes in play. Only fate will judge if this was a wise move.
We must make haste, or the campaign lost!
A cautious approach can be made.
Khorne prizes honour as much as He does wanton savagery. A contest of brutal champions would please the Blood God greatly.
These witless Bullgors regard Kharneth's Daemons as mere entertainment. They should be butchered for this affront.
At significant cost and effort, capture a pack of starving Yhetees from the mountains, and allow your followers to slake their battle-thirst upon the raging ice-beasts.
Surely the troublemakers will grow tired of their deafening protest eventually? There is always the risk that others may join them, however.
Desperate measures are called for. Only by tearing the ears from the skulls of every single fiend in your populace may they become immune to Slaanesh's hypnotic beat.
There is nothing for it but to join the dread drumming yourself. Perhaps it will inspire you to greater feats of slaughter? Or perhaps it will enable Slaanesh to seduce more to his cause?
Summon an ambassador from every empire – an unprecedented conclave of all this world's powers. Then disembowel them where they stand, and claim their high-ranking skulls for Kharneth.
Raze everything in your kingdom that is not brass, bone or steel. Leave nothing living, save for the mightiest of your Daemons.
If your blood legion is rendered irreversibly immune to Slaaneshi charms, they will surely prevail in battle against the Perfect Prince's perfumed fiends.
Storm every home, and behead any being caught in an act of congress. To be on the safe side, the same applies to all those guilty of reading poetry, playing games of chance, or drinking fine wines.
A simple proclamation of approval from the Skull Throne would be sufficient to send countless Daemons flocking to your cause.
None may leave Kharneth's service without His express decree. Should you desire it, the fulminated Bloodthirster will be reborn as a new and fiercely loyal servant of blood.
The container is emblazoned with Khornate iconography. Though the enfeebled fiends will escape, to refuse this relic of the Skull Throne would be blasphemy.
No trinket can make an act of mercy forgivable. Ignore the relic, and grant a brutal second death to each and every one of these Unliving wretches.
The ruined flesh atop their fiendish heart will grow nigh-unbreakable as it knits.
Have your follower render themselves so horrific to gaze upon that their every enemy will loose their bowels in terror.
Show your respect to a worthy foe, and teach your complacent allies that Khornate tolerance of others only lasts until the next great battle.
Deposit a slaughtered Stonehorn before an erstwhile rival's gates – a vast and bloody tribute to prove that you consider them worthy.
Select the strongest Bloodletter from every regiment, harvest their skulls, fill them to the brim with blood and then send this great tribute to your foe.
Arrange for the capture of one of their weaker underlings. They will yield soon their secrets if they value their skull.
The support of the Ice Court shall see Kislev prevail.
The Orthodoxy’s strength bolsters the people.
For now, neutrality is the best course of action.

Instil new fervour within the populace. Make every child understand exactly what happens when Ruin visits Kislev. As the nightmares grip them, they will beg their parents to protect them, no matter the cost.
The other kingdoms do not realise how close doom is to their doors. We must send our most gifted orators to make these pampered fools understand. Once they do, they will surely aid our cause.
Warm her frozen blood with our finest Kvas. And once her palate has known the incomparable taste of Jewel of Kislev, she will pay a king's ransom for more.
They will want to know that she is alive, and she will want them to know that she is so much stronger than they realise.
Have the farmer ask this crack of his to grant Kislev's armies the strength of the soil.
Have the farmer request that the Motherland bless us with the power of the elements.
Let us bury this magnificent beast on the Hill of Heroes, for it deserves respect and peace, not a gaudy show. Honour the bears, and they will honour us.
Bid a public farewell with flame and fervour, in the heart of Geroyev Square. Doubtless, this show of pomp and ceremony will inspire others to pledge themselves to Ursun.
Years of flash-flooding and countless thousands of footsteps have taken a heavy toll on the ancient market. Restore its former glory, and goods will flow like never before.
We have long consigned Bretonnian artisans to one of the most forlorn areas of the city, but they do know a thing or two about steel. Let us gain their favour, and in turn their wisdom.
Food is too precious in Praag to waste even this monstrously spoiled harvest. Perhaps it may even be a boon to sorcery, though who knows what horror will we invite across our threshold?
Though our populace will go hungry, we cannot permit this foul affliction to pass into proud Kislevite blood. Once the fasting is done, purity shall reign.
Search the fields and barns, scour the grain silos and troughs, comb the wells and riverbeds. If a sorcerous artifact is responsible for this corruption, it must be ours.
The Akshina can resolve this discreetly. While he espouses mayhem and heresy, perhaps a chimney could topple from a nearby rooftop. We will then buy the silence of all who ask questions.
If our response is too brazen, there will be those who feel we only prove his point. It would be better to quietly inform him that his current course of action is… unwise.

If trust is so hard won, then, alas, fear it must be. Have our most devout Patriarchs flay his traitorous flesh, remove his fingers then, finally, burn him alive. There will doubtless be turmoil, but we can control that.

So the Motherland's errant children dare to doubt us. They will soon discover what happens when they no longer have faith to armour them. Chaos will stalk their land, and they will only have themselves to blame.
Smear the buboe with carrion, mulch and excrement in the hope it will grow yet more fecund, and thus feed the land with Nurgle's putrescent power.
Whatever pestilent horrors swim within this vast and necrotic edifice shall be loosed upon the land, spreading the Urfather's foul touch wherever they go.
If buried within the soil and carefully tended to, the putrescent sac – no doubt sent from the Fly Lord's decomposing Garden – shall surely bear uncommonly rancid seed.
There is no better breeding ground for Nurgle's putrid spawn than dung-caked waste-tunnels. In those filthy depths, the egg-fruit will birth something marvellously mephitic.
Imagine the glorious putrescence that will result from carrion on this scale! Should its rot be expedited, Grandfather will doubtless shower you with rancid gifts.
The vast cadaver will make a fine breeding ground for pox-spreading insects. The foul grubs will grow fat upon its mouldering flesh, and upon reaching adulthood they will blight the land.
Your champion can rake away the pollution, but doing so will scrub off vast strips of their own mouldering meat. Such a beauteous emissary of Nurgle they shall be.
The foul gut-fluids will bubble and burn indefinitely, and your faithful follower shall leave a glistening trail of infection wheresoever they tread.
If your rotted legion barely have minds left to twist, they will become inherently resistant to madness. Tzeentch's changelings will thus be powerless against them.
All corvids must be slain on sight. In fact, anything with feathers is fair game, lest it be a sorcerous emissary of the Raven God.
The filthy flood-waters contain generations of waste, and thus will be a breeding ground for manifold new and wondrous diseases. Truly, this is a miracle of science!
Order your Tallybands to bathe in the disease-strewn brown waters. The countless bacteria within shall work wonders upon their festering flesh.
Miracles should not be expected, for Plaguebearers' vocal cords have nigh-on rotted away. Guiding them into a simple three-note refrain will yield potent results, however.
So slow-witted are Plaguebearers that the process will be torturous, but you believe you can teach them a basic summoning chant.
Sneaking the brain-grub past all those bodyguards and henchmen will be a breathtakingly expensive business, but infecting the ruler of an empire will have truly transformative results…
It will be easy enough to have the grub feast upon a low-ranking brain, and once done they will quietly sow warm sentiment about us throughout their lands.
Once your enemy's rank-and-file have imbibed parasite-polluted waters, they will be too besotted to do battle with your rancid legions.
While this has perhaps unwelcome overtones of Slaaneshi sorcery, causing a high-ranking foe to become captivated by your singularly horrendous form would yield invaluable insights.
Maybe they're bored of eatin' the same ol' raw flesh for sixteen meals a day. Tell the Butchers to make somethin' fancier, like stuffin' one kind of meat with another kind of meat. Delicious, yeah?
An Ogre who don't wanna eat ain't no Ogre at all. Shrug it off an' the skinny ones'll just get eaten by the fatter ones. Survival of the fittest, innit?

Get raidin' like never before, and round up the finest meats, cheeses, cakes and boozes in the 'old world. We're gonna have ourselves the buffet to end all buffets. If this don't fatten 'em up, nothin' will.
This ain't natural. Probably them Chaos lads are muckin' about again. Whatever it is, we ain't got no use for skinny Bulls. Might as well feed 'em to somethin' wot will eat, yeah?
Feed 'em them lava-chillies the Butchers have been too scared to touch. Once they've finished thrashing in agony they'll soon be belchin' fire. Maw only knows what they'll break first, mind.
All that grease on their flesh will make our boys burn a treat. They won't thank us for the pain and the flames'll probably spread, but the scars'll make 'em tough as old boots.
No point in muckin' about. The tribe's 'ungry, so let's chop this sucker down and work out who gets to eat what.
Tasty as this magic meat tree looks, if we gnosh the whole thing now it ain't never gonna grow more chops. Just pick the ripe ones, yeah?
It'll fill up the loot-pile alright, but the tribe ain't gonna be 'appy that you ain't sharin' it around. They'll probably 'ave a massive sulk.
A few shiny things for every Bull sounds a like a plan. They'll surely blow it all on meat 'n' booze, and maybe stop botherin' you for it for a while.
Look, this duel ain't gonna pretty to watch, so might as well set 'im against someone who'll get it over with as soon as possible, yeah?
This old Bull couldn't beat a Gnoblar in a stand-up fight, so no point in makin' a show of things. Just let whoever's gut is rumblin' loudest 'ave themselves an easy meal.
It don't matter 'ow that beast ended up so weird, we can't let good meat go to waste. Get those 'earts cooked sharpish, then get 'em in the tribe's guts.
The Butcher's itchin' to get slicin' and dicin' all those 'earts. Reckons 'e can perfect 'is art or something. Don't see the 'arm in it.
Gnoblars don't taste great – far too stringy, innit? Maybe these little-nosed types will 'ave a bit more fat on 'em, mind.
We can thump some sense into 'em. Or out of 'em, as the case may be. The other Gnoblars'll look at 'em funny, but that don't matter.
Toss a few prime cuts the Maw's way and the ol' god-mouth's bound to settle down. Might even belch us up a nice reward.
Fair's fair, the tribe's only had eight breakfastses today. Stuff a bit more fat 'n' grease down 'em and they'll be right as rain. Better, even.
Have our boy put the 'ole lot of 'em down. It'll be a nasty old fight, but we don't want anyone else thinkin' they can come an' give us aggro whenever they feel like it.
One-to-one our boy'll win, though them hooks'll tear chunks outta the poor bastard's gut. A smaller belly's nothin' to be proud of, but a win's a win, and at least he'll eat less after.
There's a fence on the Ivory Road who'll buy anything. Maw only knows it's the last deal the mad bastard will ever do, but it ain't like we care.
We'll lose a few boys in the process, but we can make these pups do what we says. Once they're all grown up, we got ourselves a weapon, yeah?
There'll be Bulls queuing up to fight for ya if it means they get to splatter some of this red stuff on their lunch. 'Course, they'll probably eat us outta house and home.
No self-respectin' Ogre stuffs anything that ain't meat down their maw. Get the tribes back on a pure-flesh diet, and their guts'll soon be bigger than ever.
The first taste is free. All others come at a heart-stopping cost. But rest assured, all who sample this incomparable wine will gladly, desperately pay any price for more of it.
Your pleasure-toys will rhapsodise about the drink's wondrous qualities to their countless other partners. Soon enough, all will beg to join your cause, hoping for a taste of their own.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder – and no doubt the loins too. If the people are forcibly denied that which they have grown bored of, they will soon desperately desire its return.
While it seems unthinkable that your people are bored of transgression, perhaps they simply need encouragement. With a little more imagination, could this torpor resolve itself?
Somehow, lust has been swapped for rage. To undo this will require a great harvest of souls, which will then be imbibed by your populace. Their loins shall soon be aflame once more.
There is Khornate blood in the water supply: so that is how this pleasure-slaying sabotage was wrought. There is nothing for it but wait for the boiling ichor to drain away.
Carve the mark of Slaanesh into their hide, six hundred times over. Let suffering be their mantra, let pain be their guiding light, and let torment drive them forth.
Hang their flesh with glittering piercings, infuse their blood with intoxicating spices and rub aromatic lotions into their supple skin. They will be made irresistible.
So nightmarish and so endless is the composition that eardrums will burst, eyeballs will melt and brains will bleed. This mass sacrifice will be delicious indeed, and the dark rewards immeasurable.

Their suffering will be exquisite to behold. They will beg you to stop before their senses are forever ruined and their very souls forfeit, and thus will gladly pay any price to end this free-verse torture.
No-one, not even the Dark Prince himself, may rob you of your legendary allure. Demolish the portrait to restore your perfect form, and you shall bathe in pleasure-slaves like never before.

Beauty is not binary. Convention is stagnation. Embrace your changed image. Own your changed form, and wield it like the flawless weapon it is. This is perhaps the greatest lesson of the Perfect Prince – a reward may follow in time.

In truth, the doubters would do anything, anything to know your embrace. Afterwards, they will tell of the unforgettable sensations they experienced, and countless more will beg to do the same. Glory be to Slaanesh!

This, too, is a test from Slaanesh. Resist despair and silence the scurrilous voices, together with all those who have heard them. As they die in torment, the Dark Prince will thank you for this banquet of souls.
Send the Druchii to your decadent brothers and sisters in sin. They will be so very easily made willing, and your freshly-satiated kin will owe you a debt of gratitude.

If it is cruelty they desire, then cruelty they shall receive. Release the Druchii, naked and unarmed, into battle, and no servant of Kharneth will be able to resist this invitation to slaughter. The distraction will serve us well.

Meaty walls clamp tight to you as you climb through the oozing fissure. They hold you there for six days and six nights, flexing and moaning all the while. When you are finally released, delirious from near-asphyxiation, something gleams in your exhausted hand.
Slaanesh desires an offering. Promise a captivated mortal the pleasures of your flesh if only they will venture inside the trembling aperture. There, they will know His touch and be forever changed.

It is outrageous that there exists anyone who does not dream of you night and day, let alone an entire empire. A spell of temptation on this scale will be draining indeed, but a great wrong must be righted.
Once we know what forbidden sins their leaders secretly crave, we may tease them with the forever-unfulfilled promise of indulging these deviant desires. In this way, they shall become ours.

There is more to Slaanesh than simple sin and suffering. Perform a great opera for our enemies, a flawless artistic accomplishment to melt even the coldest of souls. As they fall to their knees in desperate gratitude, the Dark Prince shall applaud.

One unforgettable night of fine wine, heavenly music and extreme debauchery will be all it takes to coax secrets and strategies from their hungry lips. How Slaanesh will revel in our foe's subsequent suffering.
This gift from Tzeentch will undoubtedly grant dark knowledge, though the struggle to adapt to their newly-divided mind will cause grievous harm to your follower.
Excise the uninvited presence, lest it seize control of your follower's body. The experience will be horrific, but your champion will only grow stronger for it.
The sacred number heralds sublime transmutation. Offer up an icon of Tzeentch and it shall be transformed!
Abduct a condemned man, chain him to a dead tree, and leave him to hear the constant dirge for nine days and nine nights. Then, he will be ours.
Have your Sorcerers invoke a great ward of stabilisation. Though draining, it should lock your followers' fluctuating forms to this plane of existence.
Such is the nature of Change. If this is the Great Schemer's will, any consequences are inevitable, no matter which course of action you might take.
Scour the libraries for spells of voiding. If one does not work, move on to the next. Do whatever it takes to find a magical vaccine for Nurgle's latest pox.

When sufficient numbers of the Changer's Followers have dissolved into horrific goo, those not yet infected will most probably be immune to the plague's deliquescent touch. The casualties shall be many, however.
Grant unto your champion an aura of whispering tendrils around their head, which as they writhe and twitch shall siphon magic away from your foes.
Grant unto your champion a cloud of phantom hands around their feet, forever clawing at the air and drumming their hideous fingers upon the earth.
Chant the scar-drawn runes aloud, and your changelings' limbs will catch alight with blue-gold fire – all the better to burn away diseased flesh.
The inscription will grant voice to your army's every missile, magical or otherwise – an ethereal shriek capable of reversing decay.
Your marionette believes she can steal a treasured relic from the Grand Observatory of Xing Po. No doubt it will prove useful, once the gore is scrubbed from it.
Instruct your puppet to adorn herself with whatever precious trinkets she can grab, before she embarks upon her final voyage.
Their flesh shall erupt in squirming tendrils and shapeless new limbs, chattering mouths will sprout upon their hides, and indescribable new creatures shall be birthed from their spines.
All reason shall leave them, and they shall forever speak in half-truths, impossible prophecies and unknown tongues. All who hear them will suffer the same fate.
Tzeentch will shower your ally's foe with gifts, each emblazoned with His writhing rune. This open declaration of forbidden admiration shall birth purest disorder.
Subtlety yields the greatest rewards. Tzeentch will whisper your sometime rival's darkest truths to you, in order that they will become beholden to us.
Have the fingers discreetly seek out your enemy's lords and generals, tunnel through their ears and into their minds, and there rewrite their very thoughts.
Once the disembodied digits dig painlessly into the eyeballs of your foe's soldiers, their sight shall become yours. The cost of concealing this grand act of sorcery will, however, be high.
Let us move our throne to Karak Eight peaks and establish our new capital there.
I like where we currently are. Let's do nothing.
You decide to focus on getting rid of any and all Orcs around you!
You will maintain control and balance!
These are our lands, your Caravans aren't welcome.
Pay the toll and move along.
Life with the Portal has become normality.
The Portal does whatever the Chaos Gods desire.
We must keep a keen eye on this Portal’s actions.
It is only our survival that matters.
A small price to avoid a grudge.
I do not pay for idle hands.
Give the hapless paying Dwarfs another chance and hope it doesn’t happen again.
The mining-obsessed Dwarfs can take their unsafe operations elsewhere!
You have more important matters to attend to.
A merchant cult may not sound like a trustworthy bunch, but a short-term financial boost could be useful.
You know better than to trust a bunch of merchants who have made a religion out of their affluence.

This continues to be a great deal for both parties.
Despite past reassurances, they have settled in your territory yet again... perhaps this time they will listen?
Whatever the Tileans are up to, this much coin easily outweighs the settlement’s value to you.
The quantity of coin is considerable, but it certainly feels unwise to cede territory to unknown figures.
Ah, the scent of past glories. Relive them again and Slaanesh will reward you now.
There is little time to bask in your own arrogance. Descend to the next circle.
Listen to the voices, let them remind you of your many victories. Well done.
Never mind this self-congratulatory preening. Descend to the next circle.
Your army will be ejected from the Chaos Realms.
A race does not have to be won in a sprint. Let fools go on while you marvel as your treasury grows fat.
The gems are eggs for Daemon birthlings, the statues are hollow and the gold is worthless to all but Dwarfs. Pass through the gate and descend to the next circle.
Gold builds empires and a small delay is a minor cost for such a generous gift.
To stay and revel in the baubles is to forget why we come here. Descend to the next circle.
All you need do is sit but for a moment upon this throne and great power shall be yours.
Power for the sake of power is no power at all. Descend to the next circle.
Such power is yours to command, Slaanesh shall gift you armies if you but agree.
True power lies at the heart of the Dark Prince's realm – descend to the next circle.
Food, sustenance, even Daemons eat (be it souls). The Dark Prince offers a large satisfying feast.
There is no time to sample this fare. Pass through the gate and descend to the next circle.
Delicious morsels that shall banish famine, there is more than enough for all.
The hungry starve, as it has always been. Descend to the next circle.
Lie here. Close your eyes. Rest.
Let us rest, you'll not regret it.
A tryst with the Dark Prince's lovers will bring great pleasure and ensure your armies are fully stocked – for the paramours are always fertile.
Let them frolic with each other, for the palace is closer. Descend to the next circle.
Cavort while you can. Slaanesh will bless us for bringing such pleasure into existence.
Ignore the fools that pander to such base urges – descend to the next circle.

Entomb this insolent fool, and let the dunes claim their ilk.

Disperse Karanak’s destructive and vicious energies throughout your Hound packs.

Go to the Beacon to save Kislevite lives above all else.
Hurry to punish the tribal chief that threatens the Beacon.
Harnessing the Gorebull’s destructive nature is the obvious choice. The great, weird moon - Morrslieb - hangs low; we are incensed!
What do the Chaos Gods whisper? What dark machinations do they plot? The Bray-Shaman will surely reveal these secrets to us...
Take what you can from them to sustain us and let us be gone!
Their temples and pitiful gods lay before us, ripe for desecration. Let us leave our mark and be on our way.
The proud and ignorant Empire are a bigger prize. Their flesh will taste all the better for the challenge!
Bretonnians are arrogant and foolish people, haughty and easily exploited. Let us take them apart.
The whelp has learned his place. Removing his horns ensures he can never again challenge you. A good decision, and punishment enough - he can re-join the herd.
Insubordination is unacceptable. The entire herd must know of your unswerving will - that you and you alone are Lord of them all! Put him to death!
What is madness but a gift from the Gods? Some will fall to the creature's maddening influence, but the rest of the herd will be greatly improved by the abomination's presence.
We do not need this bizarre curio to win the day. Our enemies are Uncloven fools and will be rended by our power alone!
What dark favour is brought forth by our dedication to destruction and ruin? We will receive it in payment!
Your refusal of our master's Ruinous generosity has signalled your strength to others, who now flock to your warherd, desperate to fight under such a powerful Beastlord.
They could not be stopped now even if you wanted it. Revelry is in their blood - let them feast! Let them be raucous! They will be grateful for it.
No matter what their blood calls for, the herdstone must be worshipped! The Ruinous rites must be obeyed!
The great herdstone at the Heart of the Dark calls out. Who are we to stop the pull of that foul and powerful monolith?
Although denied his opportunity, the Shaman resolves to remain and draw the Greater Winds of Magic across the blood-ground!
The Gods must be appeased and their Ruinous gifts bestowed upon us once more. Kill the warriors! Accept the price! Blood for the Blood God!
The herd is yours and nobody - not even the Gods - can wrest it from your control.
The call cannot be ignored! Though answering it may thin our numbers, those that survive will fight stronger for it. There only the roar of battle - the call of blood!
We need no brayherd to make our way in the world, we can create destruction and discord very well on our own!
They can worship the Chaos Gods if they like, but there is only ruin to be found in such a foolish course of action!
They are not the children of Chaos. The Uncloven Ones must pay the price for their ignorance! Human blood must ALWAYS be spilled.

Gors of all strengths and ages are welcome here. All have their places, even those whose fighting prowess is less… developed.
The herd can replace their fallen with ferocious alacrity, yet the latecomers are more reluctant to fight.
By currying favour with the Ruinous Powers, the herd grows ever stronger. However, dark favour comes at a price…
The herd moves, going where you tell them until their legs give out from the exertion!
In the deep forests dwell the mightiest, grizzled beasts. They only fight for a Beastlord who enjoys the darkest favour…

Vampires respond best to a show of brutal force. Vlad's rage was legendary back in the day, remind these fools why - let the bloodletting begin!
Vlad is a charismatic creature of low cunning when he can best his temper. This was how he first seduced the nobility of Sylvania. A promise to share wealth and power should lure them to his side.
Our kin have travelled far with gladness in their heart, a gladness we share fully - grant them their audience, let them treat with us as family.
The arrogance! After so long, and so much silence, they deem us worthy to talk with them? No! Send them back across the waves; we care not!
Cast them out. These Dryads have done us a great wrong but to destroy them would be to anger the forest. Send them away; far away!
This slight against the Asrai cannot go unpunished. Introduce them to their mortal foe; turn them into kindling for the great pyre!
There is no hope that this impetuous knave can hope to best a Wardancer, but it would be an amusement to see him try. Take the wager!
This insolence adds another heinous crime to the list. You will suffer it no more. Kill him immediately!
In these troubled times, the wisdom of Asuryan flies as true as any Elven arrow.
We are in a dark and bitter age; the battle-hardened fury of Khaine would surely be a boon to our efforts.
This scheme, although shameless, can only help to undermine the haughty Bretonnians who encroach on the forest. Aid them we shall!
Such underhanded plans are not fit for the nobility of the Elven High Houses. Tell Cavaroc they must do this without our blessing!
Though the Dreaming Wood is steeped in treachery, this Glade Lord's intentions are noble. Who are we to stop them?
No. The Dreaming Wood is forbidden for a reason. Slaanesh cannot claim another Asrai soul. Not this day!
This was a warrior, who deserves a warrior's send-off. Light the pyres, prepare the bier, and let us do this one justice!
As we are all born from the forest, so we return to the forest. Dig the hole deep; let the forest reclaim its child…
The Hunt makes fair targets of us all; the Great Stag will make a dazzling addition to any hunter's trophy collection.
The soul of the forest is sacred; the beast should not be harmed, representing as it does the spirit of Athel Loren.
What dark and twisted deeds they may be weaving throughout the Night Glens is their business, and the repercussions theirs to deal with. You will have no part of it…
Though these spells are not strictly… permitted, what may be advantage to the Asrai should surely be harnessed?
The fatter they become, the greater the eventual sacrifice. Have patience and it shall be rewarded in the end.
The guests have enjoyed our hospitality for long enough. It is time they repaid our kindness with the ultimate generosity. Prepare them!
The merchants and craftsmen of the city are hard workers and deserve this small token of gratitude!
Will they stop their ceaseless complaining if we feed them this once? I suppose we can find out.
We would benefit greatly from having the Lords of Artois serve under our banner, and they are hardly in a position to refuse such a "request".
Gold should help smooth their Lords transition to serving under our banner.
Perhaps now is not the time to force matters, and there is always the chance to convince them later diplomatically.
