Gravity is for man-things to fear. "Reality" is for scaly-ones to keep. No self-respecting Skaven engineer feels bound by natural law.
If half the deeds scratched into his battered armour were true, this scarred tyrant would be legend. Best not test which boasts are lies.
Better blades are wasted on cowards. Arm the cruelest clawpacks, and they will repay the cost in trophies, captives, and stolen meat.
A grizzled Warlord carries a stink of old violence and cold malice. Clanrats scent it, straighten their backs, and find fresh courage for cruelty.
Commander Tchit Skinslink proved a failed tunnel need not be waste: bury the slaves inside, call it a diversion, and dig cheaper elsewhere.
Superstition says this rat blinked against Morrslieb at his birth. Whatever the truth, hostile magic clings poorly to his hide.
There is a hollow, pitiless drive behind those eyes. Whips begin the charge, but something darker keeps the clawpack killing.

The living power of Chaos can be channelled through instruments of mortal steel, charging them for their bearer's bloodthirsty ends.
Ruin's own lair-nest beneath the rotting earth is finally at hand…

The ability to herd and control the disorganised, cowardly rabble found in Skaven army ranks is not to be sniffed at!

Clan Moulder's innate understanding of flesh-craft is more than a simple boon when combined with the Verminking's power.
The walls separating the mortal world from the Realm of Ruin are gossamer-thin; when Verminlords cross over, Chaos come with them.

Changing the plan at the last second is a risky gamble, but one that Thanquol cannot resist, time and time again!

Those Skaven pressed into his service are wholly expendable, mere pawns in the Grey Seer's deadly game.

There are always further, far darker depths to be plumbed in the endless thirst for the eldritch and arcane.
Boneripper is a behemoth of a brute, whose body can absorb a horrendous amount of damage before ever succumbing.
Further augmentations endow Boneripper with the cutting edge of murderous technology, much to his enemies' vexation!
No matter what weapons are grafted to his flesh, at his very core, Boneripper remains a creature of barbarous urges.
Far more than just heavyset, Boneripper is a flesh mountain, and almost immovable with it.
That the Winds of Magic can be harnessed to convey foul pestilence upon the foe is sheer delight for the Corruptor, who is disease personified.
The foulest of maladies is meat and drink to a Verminlord Corruptor, and unlikely to trouble his forces in battle.

Sting-fleas, three-eyes mites, and other foul parasites teem across every fibre of the Corruptor's pelt, forming a living shield of filth to protect his most pestilent warriors.
Silently they march across the frail, vulnerable bodies of the fools who dare stand against the might of the Horned One.
Obsessed with the aura of creeping sickness surrounding them, the Corruptor also knows who best wields it to Skaven advantage.
Utilising the very best (or is it worst?) of Skaven nature combined with their magical abilities, the Deceiver always lives up to his name.
All you'll see is the flash of red, rodent eyes before agonising, flesh-ripping death comes to claim you!
The Deceiver's agility, so great that they can both throw and catch their own deadly killing stars, makes their host utterly devastating to their opponents.
The Verminlord Deceiver moves in the shadows, appearing apparently from nowhere at the place and time least expected.
Blink and you'll do more than miss them – you'll be very dead indeed!
You cannot kill what you cannot see. And what you cannot see can certainly kill you.
Those Skaven who bask beneath the Warbringer's towering majesty are gradually steeled by their murderous fury.
The Warbringer's desire for not only plunder but territory increases with every baggage caravan captured and city looted along the way.
There is no deed too grim for those who serve the awe-inspiring Rat Daemons that stride across the gore-soaked battlefields of the mortal world.
In the claws of a Warbringer, any weapon can be wielded to extremely gory effect against almost all comers.
Plans and schemes of a myriad dishonourable kinds are further bolstered by the Warpseer's superlative command of the Winds of Magic.
The hardest, most unadulterated Warpstone is far stronger than steel or even diamond, and makes a perfect edge for sword, spear or arrow.
Schemes and plots, interwoven and inter-dependent, allow the Warpseer to know where all the threads will lead.
One may think they have some congress with the Winds, but their knowledge is worthless next to the arcane power of the Warpseer.
This Rat Daemon's intelligence is elevated, even among his peers, to the level where only the Warlock Engineers understand his game, let alone play it with skill.
Weak-minded fools are driven to gibbering madness and beyond once the fumes from the Verminlord Warpseer's Scry-Orb take hold.
Death has shriveled this one completely – his frail silhouette blends with the shifting dunes of Nehekhara desert and only the eyes of the unliving can discern him.
In a headlong charge, sturdy bones break brittle ones.
Roaring brutes and cackling beastlings are met with ice-cold hatred.
Incantation flows into incantation as a milennia-old ceremonies repeat onwards into eternity.
It is said that death brings final peace, but some of the unliving retain a spark of what might have been impulsive nature.
Words of conviction spoken amidst the silence of forgotten cities draws to light the faithful dead.
As arcane power grows over centuries it is not uncommon for former flesh to fade into translucency.
Every word is an oath and an oath never breaks. Death only strengthens it.
Act promptly  when an enemy turns their back towards you – a second opportunity might never come!
Sacred words flow like flame, each invocation delivered with swiftness and precision.
The souls of Liche High Priests are a constant, cold glow drawing weaker souls back to the mortal realm.
The rote rigour with which a Liche performs his duties has allowed him to outlast entire civilisations. Such persistence does not crumble easily.
A Liche Priest's most important duty has always been to preserve and reawaken their king. But it will not do for a ruler's sworn protectors to emerge in a decrepit state.
A forceful general can muster mind and muscle, but when free will and mortal vigour are forbidden, a strong mastery of arcane craft is what the march calls for.
Many hands and minds lifted Nehekhara to its glory. It was kings who left their stamp on the land, but the priests left theirs on the Winds – some more than others.
Grains of knowledge lost, regained, refined and torn down only to rise again to the current heights of understanding: the Cult's masters have sifted through it all.
Nehekharan tombs are places of cold stone and souls simmering, waiting to be released, era after era, all illuminated by the glow of these past masters of their craft.
A king's soul returns after millennia of arcane craft, priestly minds swept clean by rote effort. No Wind of Magic must carry this soul away again – a duty which falls to the Herald.
The foundation of Nehekhara’s glory is the service its people rendered to its kings. In battle, most steadfast of all were always the Heralds.
Death did not disquiet them in life. Now they have shed their wariness in battle just as they did the weariness of mortal flesh.
In a duel protecting the honour of their king, Heralds know there is another goal: to strip the foe of theirs. It takes little to turn first-blood strike into a killing blow.
By his very presence, the name of his title and sometimes his own name, a Herald is a quiet but undeniable presence when matters between kingdoms are decided.
Long-dead destriers, awakened to serve their Unliving masters far beyond death.
To strike at a Banshee with a weapon is to strike a fire with ice. Such fools are a favoured prey.
As tireless as her wrath and hatred are indiscriminate. It is what made her such.
Wayward will o' the wisps are not the only ones swirling about the one which tormented them in life, for she has her own kindred in woe.
The bile of centuries of bitterness is not just in her voice. Those who dare come near will learn how it feels.
An arrow slit, a murder hole, a faint crack – anything will carry her wail. Armour is useless and flesh could never withstand her fury.
Every living soul’s whisper is a reminder of what this one can no longer have.
Before the maddened howl of the Banshee, there was the canny silence of the living witch she was. This one remembers.
Honour and worthy foes spur a Blood Dragon to action, or so he would proclaim… It is, in truth, the bloodshed and nothing else.
Spoils of war are brutally torn from the defeated.
The Undead display the best type of loyalty, which endures unendingly and without question.
Give them a taste of what awaits! And do treat yourself to a taste, too.
The power to command armies, beasts, and even darkness itself may be uncanny, but even with a mere blade in hand a von Carstein is an otherworldly sight.
His mere presence throws a Stygian pall over the land. His voice invokes the misty tendrils of Vampiric magic.
Von Carsteins think themselves the pinnacle of true poise, decisive power, command through mere presence... Yet within every Vampire's soul lurks a slavering monster, driven to feed.
I am blessed by the power of gods to break even immortal constraints!
The Lichemaster scours every battlefield for fresh corpses with which to restore his Undead horde.
From diminutive forest-lurkers to hulking monstrosities, all manner of creatures heed her beckoning call, ravenously seeking out those she marks for death.
All that noble dance and etiquette training is quite transferable indeed.
The sisterhood are trained relentlessly so that they never expose their weakness.
I was so gracious to unburden them of their heavy treasures.
A Lahmian's claws are as vicious on the field as her tongue is witty in court.
A grudge is a powerful force. Mighty Necromancers hold endless grudges against the death gods and those that fuel their perseverance.
Innumerable daily births sustain a thriving kingdom. But in the dead of night, there are also births.
No more whimpering flesh. No more throats labouring for a sip of air. A Necromancer’s servants are unchained from death and bound to him.
Necromancers brave the briars of obsession. The path of death is their destination. Some have walked a long way.
The grave art of Necromancy is the art of walking the whispering line separating life and unlife.
The dead know not their strength, but would have marvelled at it in life, while Necromancers turn such awe to a terror of slaughter.
Tendons knit together and wounds weld shut, as the body remembers its shape.
Preservation of unlife is a practice much more subtle and rewarding than the preservation of life.
Admirable willpower is perhaps the least unsavoury of a Necromancer’s traits of character, employed towards most unsavoury ends.
Long practice has made the restoration of dead flesh swift, precise and almost effortless.
Having paid the toll of years with pieces of his soul, the Necromancer’s power can now inflict the same toll on the souls of his enemies.
Necromancers feel no shame in stealing, be it corpses or the arcane secrets of those much greater.
Every corpse is gathered, every crypt emptied, and every death made profitable.
As the Corpse Cart rolls onward, the magic and the spoiled of war not just collect, but spread.
Necromancers are a profanity aimed at all gods of death and laws of the living. A clever Necromancer ensures that none of them can retaliate in kind.
Having paid the toll of years with pieces of his soul, the Necromancer’s power can now inflict the same toll on the souls of his enemies.
Years of harvesting mortal blood has refined the Queen's most discerning palate.
All courts belong to the Night Queen, for none are exempt from her influence.
No one knows how far the Queen's reach extends, nor how many serve her in secret.
Stay your hand! You couldn't possibly mean to hurt a defenseless maiden?
The Winds come naturally to one who once studied the texts of the Great Necromancer himself.
Using the unseen networks of her shadowed sisterhood, Neferata tightens her grip on the mortal realms.
A lady mustn't churn through the mud like a common peasant!
Neferata weaves countless schemes, each hidden behind another layer of deception.

The hex isn't too disturbing, if one can look past the ominous chanting and the lingering stench of death.

That's the thing about rats... they always survive, endlessly scurrying towards safety.
You'd best start believing in ghost stories…

Nehekhara once stood as a shining beacon of civilisation and human achievement. But this great realm was destroyed through acts of great treachery and powerful sorcery. The living of Nehekhara perished in a single, mournful night, and in their absence, the dead stirred from their graves and claimed the land anew.\\n\\nEven as their ancient civilisation now lies buried beneath the sand, the Tomb Kings have once more awoken from their deep sleep. Rising from their sarcophagi, the mummified rulers of Nehekhara have returned to reclaim that which is rightfully theirs, their legions innumerable, brandishing weapons of polished bronze and priceless gold. Ancient, emotionless and spiteful to all those who have slighted them, woe betide those foolish enough to stand before their silent onslaught.

The origins of the Undead pirates said to ravage the coasts of Lustria are steeped in mystery. Legend has it that a Norscan longship took on a precious cargo during a raid – an ancient coffin containing, unbeknownst to the crew, the Vampire Luthor Harkon. When the vessel floundered off the Volcanic Islands, the drowned crew were raised as zombies through the Vampire's Dark Magic.\\n\\nThe stretch of coastline known as the Vampire Coast has become infamous amongst seafarers, with countless ships wrecked and raised up from the depths to bolster the fleets of the Unliving. Luthor was but the first. In the years since, more Undead pirates ply the seas for bounty and fresh crews.

The Dark Elves – or the Druchii, in their own tongue – are one of the most ancient, powerful, and certainly the most sadistic of the three Elven civilisations. The Druchii are raiders, slavers and heartless reavers of the first degree, their every whim being nothing more than to sow misery and pain to all who oppose them, for cruelty is the very lifeblood of their existence. Thus do their Black Arks and Corsair Fleets ply the great waters of the world, raiding and enslaving all before them as a tribute to their own avaricious desires.\\n\\nYet they reserve their most precious hatred for the Elves of Ulthuan, their brethren in ancient times who refused to follow them under the Witch King's reign. Until the High Elves are sundered from Ulthuan, the Dark Elves will continue to bring woe and destruction to all the shores of the world.

The High Elves – or the Asur, as they call themselves – are one of the most ancient and powerful civilisations of the Old World. Hailing from a mighty, mist-shrouded island-continent located at the centre of the Great Ocean, the High Elves of Ulthuan are a proud and mighty kingdom of masterful warriors, peerless mages and lords of sky and sea. At the zenith of their power, the world was truly theirs for the taking, but in their arrogance they brought about a bloody war against the Dwarfs which crippled both of these two elder races.\\n\\nThe time of the High Elves has passed, yet such is their immense pride that they fight on regardless, for they consider themselves the true and rightful protectors of the known world. Let the servants of destruction beware the Asur's righteous wrath!

The Lizardmen are an ancient race of cold-blooded reptilians said to be the first and oldest civilisation. Alien, enigmatic, and entirely without mercy, the Lizardmen were there at the start of all things and will be there when the world draws its last dying breath, never tiring nor relenting until order is finally restored to this uncaring, chaotic world.\\n\\nFrom the primeval jungles of Lustria they come, disciplined cohorts of Saurian warriors with giant scaly beasts in their midst, led by the most powerful Sorcerers the world has ever seen. The ground trembles from their approach. They go to battle for reasons indecipherable to others – an ancient plan known only to themselves.

The Skaven are a cunning and diabolical race of scuttering humanoid rat-creatures that have spread their loathsome corruption to the farthest corners of the world. From deep below the ground, these scavengers have built a vast Under-Empire, whose military power and incomprehensible numbers has the potential to smother the kingdoms of the Old World in a seething tide of violence and anarchy.\\n\\nThey follow the malevolent deity known as the Horned Rat, whose wishes and demands are both supreme and absolute. It is said that the ultimate goal of the Skaven is to conquer the surface world and bring about the Great Ascendancy, whence the Horned Rat's children will swarm across its face and claim all of it as their own.

Malign, dark-souled and merciless, Chaos Dwarfs are known in legend as a warrior race of Daemonsmiths, craftsmen and brutal killers who have dominated the northern reaches of the Dark Lands for thousands of years.\\n\\nLong separated from their fading kin of the west, the Dawi-Zharr have given themselves over to their dark master Hashut and allowed Chaos to work its twisted terrors on their minds and souls, transforming them into a calculatingly cruel reflection of what they once were. They are deeply learned in the sorcerous arts and obsessed with the control of hellish forces and fires of the deep earth, combining dark lore with artisanship and skill for metalwork and industry. Thus, the Chaos Dwarfs have produced a bewildering variety of strange and infernal war engines, Daemon-bound weapons and deadly tools of war, and their power grows still.

The history of all Undead beings starts with Nagash, as does that of all who would attempt what Nagash did: achieve power through Necromancy. Throughout time, all kinds have grown into a disparate multitude with goals just as incompatible.\\nAristocratic Vampires seek to crown themselves kings and queens and emperors in the mortal tradition. Their buccaneering kin pushes onward into seas uncharted, laying both claim and waste upon the shores they disembark on. The Tomb Kings endlessly burnish the fading past of their ancient kingdom, which promised them immortality, but not of the sort they were granted. Necromancers delve into the millennial secrets left behind by the Great Necromancer himself, to impose their will upon the spirit world.\\nWith Nagash's final coming, that disparate multitude is shaped into a legion with a single purpose – to end all history and do away with all power except that of the Necromancy of Nagash himself.

Past the Mountains of Mourn and the steppes beyond lies the fabled empire of Cathay. Travellers returning from the eastern reaches tell tales of jade cities and golden pagodas. They recount strange creatures from serpentine Dragons to monolithic stone sentinels, and flying Sky-Junks that rain multi-hued firepower from up above. But most of all they tell of the imposing and disciplined armies that march forth in defence of their kingdom – the thousands of devoted foot soldiers, unswerving in their loyalty and unrivalled in the harmonics of war.\\n\\nThat their armies face northwards to garrison the Great Bastion and defend it against the Ruinous Powers is perhaps a blessing, for should the Celestial Dragon Emperor have to turn his legions toward the nations of the west, the threat to all that may be unleashed does not bear thinking about...

Manipulated into a horrifying act by another, the Ungol Prince has given himself up entirely in exchange for the Ruinous blessings of all the Chaos Gods and ascendancy to Daemonhood. The newly arisen Daemon Prince shrugs off his mortal form to take on an ever-changing aspect more pleasing to his new patrons, who continue to war for his ravaged soul.\\n\\nNow, it is the destiny of the Daemon Prince to command the legions of Chaos Undivided in waging eternal war against entire nations and immortal rivals, as he seeks a terrible vengeance on sovereigns and even gods. Will he claim the Mark of one master or forge a path that will bring him to utter domination, which even the Dark Powers will struggle to harness?

Khorne, the Blood God, rages upon his brass throne, resting atop a mountain of skulls, built from the countless heads of the great champions his followers have slain over an immeasurable number of aeons. He cares not from where blood flows so long as it is done in his name. It is not uncommon to see the warriors of Khorne fighting amongst themselves, battling to prove their skill in combat and rise higher in the eyes of their wrathful master.\\n\\nTo follow Khorne is to embrace violence and destruction, and to pledge utter subservience to his cause. Khorne's most favoured servants are gifted with immense powers. Some may even ascend to Daemonhood, and it is these chosen few who are tasked with bringing his wrath down upon the world. Blood for the Blood God!

The Tzardom of Kislev, known as the Realm of the Ice Queen, is the most northerly civilisation within the Old World, a powerful and war-driven country. The inhabitants of Kislev are wolf-tough and self-reliant warriors, valiant and determined in the defence of their Motherland, for they are the bulwark against the horrors of the north.\\n\\nSince its founding, Kislev has been under constant assault by the hordes of Chaos. Countless generations of Kislevites have fought and died in the snowy tundra of those harsh northern oblasts, and it is thanks to these brave Kislevite warriors that mankind has managed to flourish in the south, huddled together in their warm, safe homes, whilst the sons and daughters of Kislev fight on until they draw their dying breaths.

Nurgle, also known as the Plague Lord, is the Chaos God of disease, decay, death and degradation. He is perhaps the oldest of his brother Gods, for the process of decay began with life. Yet Nurgle is also the personification of rebirth. After all, atrophy is simply one part of life's cycle, without which nothing new can grow.\\n\\nAnd so those who embrace Nurgle, accept their own doom with good humour. Disfigured by disease and mutation, they are keen to spread Grandfather's blessings to the poor souls that wander through life unafflicted. As plagues spread, so to does Nurgle's power and status amongst his brothers – he waxes and wanes, weakest when bellies are full and mortals are healthy, but quickly rising to absolute ascendancy when his followers unleash the most lethal of diseases.

Ogres are a race of large humanoids, tough, vicious and always hungry. Semi-nomadic in nature, wandering Ogre tribes can be found wrecking their way across the known world, yet no matter how far away they may be, all Ogres consider the scattered tribal kingdoms that dominate the slopes and river valleys of the Mountains of Mourn to be their rightful, hard-earned homeland.\\n\\nThey fight as thugs, bandits and mercenaries, picking on the strong and the weak alike, battling mighty foes and powerful kingdoms thousands of leagues away. They do this for the alluring promise of gold, plunder and, most importantly, meat, for their endless destruction and looting serves only to appease their gluttonous appetites and their ever-hungry god, the Great Maw.

Slaanesh is dedicated to the pursuit of excess, gratification, hedonism, pain and amoral pleasure at the expense of any other soul. He is the youngest of the Chaos Gods, for the complex emotions of erotic desire and decadence only exist within the minds of intelligent races. From within the Realm of Chaos, the Dark Prince revels in each new sensation discovered. He guides the mortal inhabitants laden with desire to go ever further in their pursuit of stimulation.\\n\\nThose who serve Slaanesh are consumed by their own dark passions, driven by the need for their mistress-master’s approval to commit more sordid atrocities. And so Slaanesh's followers practice war upon the nations of the south, seducing their foes into the service of their Dark God and inflicting symphonies of misery upon those who resist his call.

Tzeentch – the Changer of the Ways – is the Chaos God of magic, evolution, manipulation and trickery. He is flux incarnate – the God who truly embodies the endless, broiling change that is Chaos. It is Tzeentch above all who holds the terrible knowledge of fate and destiny in his talons. His worshippers are desperate to share in such lore but are merely pawns in the Great Game; another piece to move on the board and outplay the other Chaos Gods.\\n\\nTo serve Tzeentch is to invite insanity. His servants weave their own complex webs of influence and manipulation, founding cults in high society as well as armed legions of puppet-followers. They pay no mind to the fact that their master views such plots as mere petty distractions, for the Architect of Fate's own design is aeons in the making.

Deep within the dark twisted forests of the Old World range the Beastmen, a race of savage mutants that bear various traits of bestial appearance. Beastmen are creatures of Chaos. They follow the Ruinous Powers, so civilisation is anathema to them; they tear down progress and society wherever it is found. And so they raid, destroying hamlets, villages and even towns that dare to exist close to their blood-grounds.\\n\\nYet should a brayherd be gathered, then even mankind's cities are under threat, for the Beastmen go to war with savage intent, slaughtering civilised races like cattle, burning down and shattering their homes, and stomping on the remains with their cloven hooves until there is nothing left but devastation and ruin.

The Wood Elves – or Asrai – are the guardians of Athel Loren, the most ancient forest in the Old World. They are a reclusive and mysterious race who rarely emerge from the forest and are generally only seen when coming to its defence. Although they can appear cruel or capricious, in reality the Asrai are a neutral power who act only to maintain the balance of their environment.\\n\\nIt is this cause for which they fight, for no land remains untarnished long if it cannot take up arms against those that wish it harm. The waking woodlands of Athel Loren have endured for many thousands of years, so long as the watchful eyes of her protectors continue their loyal vigilance.

Warlike and cruel, the Norscan tribes of the icy north are savage fur-clad warriors who have sworn allegiance to the Ruinous Powers with unquestioning fervour. For them, the Chaos Gods are harsh yet benevolent deities, who provide them with the tools to endure life in their brutal homelands. The Norsemen range far, sailing the seas in fearsome longships to unleash their devastating fury on the south, looting and razing the realms of civilised races.\\n\\nThey are reckoned to be amongst the most adept sailors and navigators in the Old World, and the brutality of Norscan raids has been felt as far as the Witch King's baleful domain of Naggaroth and even, far to the east, in the mysterious realm of Cathay.

Bretonnia is a feudal society, split between the rich nobles with their gallant Knights and the lowly peasant class toiling in the fields. The Knights of Bretonnia – the flower of its military – have a code of chivalry that forms an unbreakable duty to protect its subjects, and when called to war, are considered by many to be the most powerful heavy cavalry in the Old World. However, a Bretonnian army rarely consists of Knights alone, and so ranks of solid, if unremarkable, foot troops and peasant levies are provided to soak up damage from unchivalrous cannons and other ranged devices.\\n\\nSo it is that in times of need the Knights of Bretonnia ride forth with lances dipped, and a prayer to the Lady on their lips!

Chaos Warriors are mortals who have left their natural way of life and chosen to dedicate themselves to a Chaos God in order to gain their favour, with the ultimate goal of Daemonhood and eternal life. They are the chosen servants of Chaos who live for nothing more than spreading terror and death to those weaker than themselves, gathering about them northern tribes of vicious marauders, desperate to despoil the lands of milk and honey to the south.\\n\\nAnd so from the icy fjords of Norsca and the blasted Chaos Wastes beyond, the innumerable armies of Chaos surge southward, either raiding across the icy seas in longships or marching inland to wreak crimson destruction upon the cities and strongholds of the Old World.

Dwarfs are a proud, bearded folk who are quick to temper, often defined by a love of gems, gold and other precious metals. With their Dwarfholds established across the Old World, the Dawi – as they call themselves in Khazalid – prospered for many generations until their realm was riven by a chain of devastating conflicts and earthquakes.\\n\\nIn recent times, the Dwarfs are a race barely holding onto glories past, with only a few strongholds remaining in their hands and the rest lost to enemies or abandoned to the elements. To this day the Dawi still fight; their ultimate goal is to restore the 'Karaz Ankor' and they have the means to do it with fearsome throngs of warriors and the most advanced weaponry in the Old World.

Lying at the heart of the Old World, the Empire is the greatest and most powerful of all the kingdoms forged by men. But it is a realm in constant turmoil, both from enemies without and strife from within as rival Elector Counts vie for the throne. Whether fighting between themselves or the many exterior invaders, the greatest nation of man can muster a formidable army of disciplined warriors, magic, steam-powered wonders and menageries of fantastical beasts.\\n\\nNow, the Twin-Tailed Comet blazes across the sky once again and a new Emperor has been crowned – surely an omen that the time has come to unite the Empire, secure its borders and bring prosperity to its beleaguered citizens.

Orcs and Goblins are the scourge of the Old World. Orcs are built for violence; Goblins, by contrast, are smaller but more cunning. Collectively known as Greenskins, they are an aggressive and brutal race with an unquenchable love of fighting. While the Greenskins have made lairs in ransacked Dwarfholds, they can be found across the Old World – the majority residing in the arid Badlands, mainly fighting amongst themselves and only coming together when the call to Waaagh! goes out.\\n\\nOne such occasion is now, and with a strong Warboss to unite the tribes, the time has surely come to unleash da Green Tide and ravage the lands of both humies and stunties alike! For such are the demands of Gork and Mork – and who would go against the word of da Green Godz? Exactly. Waaagh!

Long ago, Queen Neferata stole the secrets of eternal life from Nagash. The elixir she created was flawed, bestowing immortality but at great cost. And so the Vampires were created and they have been a plague upon the living ever since.\\n\\nMillennia later, the darkling figure of Vlad von Carstein arrived in Sylvania – before long, the region's destitute nobility were in his thrall and the von Carstein bloodline was born. Every few centuries, a von Carstein would take the reins of power and strike out against mortals at the head of an Unliving army of zombies, wraiths, Necromancers and other abyssal monstrosities.\\n\\n The Empire has thwarted such legions before, but the dead have never rested easily in Sylvania and now they lurch from their graves, summoned to Unlife by the Midnight Aristocracy as each prepares to challenge mankind once more.

It is said that Azazel’s beauty is second only to that of Slaanesh himself, and those who gaze upon him cannot gainsay such claims. As the Prince of Damnation prowls the mortal plane, his arrival is met by the usual fanfare he has become accustomed to, the barbarians of the Steppes fling themselves at his feet as they wail and proclaim their allegiance and love. Yet this time the world must take heed, for the darkling monster’s appearance is a portent most dire. Deep within the psyche of the other three Powers has always lurked the suspicion that Slaanesh’s influence could one day eclipse them all. By the might of His Ecstatic Legions, that day is nigh.

From the day Doctor Festus’ brilliant mortal mind suffered its horrific awakening, the vagaries of fate had oft twisted in his favour. Never is the Leechlord happier than when planting Nurgle’s seeds of malady across the world, force-feeding his vile experimental concoctions to the many unfortunates who stray into his path. Yet soon shall be the dawn of a far greater opportunity for mass infection; the unleashing of a dark power so great, it shall be thirsted after by the Gods themselves. A means for the Doctor and his Patron to spread unbound life – and death – into the material realm on an unimaginable scale.

The annals of history recall many of Valkia the Bloody’s appearances in the world, her arrival always met with fear but also reverence from the faithful of the Blood God who worship her as a goddess. And now the Consort of Khorne comes to blight the mortal plane once again, this time her coming foretold many years in advance by tribal shamans, with the iconic and primitive etchings of the winged warrior-queen long adorning the walls of hermit grottos across the north. As the world teeters on the precipice of epochal events, Khorne’s bloodlust crescendos once more, His violent whims, as ever, to be served unquestioningly by the inimitable Gorequeen.

What is the true purpose of those who serve within Tzeentch’s schemes? The answer eludes Vilitch the Curseling no less than his Master’s other puppets. Legitimised long ago as a horribly remarkable agent of Change by the Great Conspirator himself, the disturbing creature known as the Twisted Twin acts with inscrutable intent, leading his hard-bitten host through warpaths of misrule, disorder and death. As the fate of a lesser god draws to its conclusion, the Sorcerer-runt is soon to turn his attention back north, where broils something ancient and potent deep within the Wastes. Most importantly, a rare chance to secure favour in the eyes of his master and perhaps never be forsaken again…

A champion rises, chief among the armies of Ruin! With all challengers vanquished, and the souls of Zanbaijin claimed, a true paragon of Chaos has emerged. There is surely now no force in any realm capable of barring the path to total domination! The whole of the mortal plane shall soon quake in abject terror, for where the Altar of Battle's eternal champion goes, a legacy of pure destruction is sure to follow close behind...

The name Astragoth Ironhand is legendary amongst the Dhrath-Zharr, powerful, loyal and zealous acolytes of Hashut. But that was many years ago, and the rigors of time and Dark Magic hardened the Sorcerer-Prophet’s limbs until they turned to stone. Not resigned to becoming a statue, he forged a suit of machinery in which to continue his work.\\n\\nCarried by his own designs and dark intellect, Astragoth Ironhand now travels freely, relying on his own twisted science and construction to convey him.\\n\\nUpstarts may now see him as a fossil, a remnant embedded in stone and well beyond his prime, but Astragoth’s time is not yet over! Age and petrification are mere obstacles to overcome, and with the fabled Blood of Hashut, this domination will be secured!

In his youth, the fearsome Daemonsmith Drazhoath lost favour amongst the Sorcerer-Prophets, a victim of the savage politics of Zharr-Naggrund. For this, he was exiled from the heart of the Chaos Dwarf empire to the Black Fortress, in the distant reaches south of the Mountains of Mourn.\\n\\nDrazhoath has since risen to become Lord of the Black Fortress and Commander of the Legion of Azgorh from his border citadel near the banks of the mighty River Ruin. Looking again to the Tower of Fire, he seeks revenge against those that exiled him.\\n\\nA method for Drazhoath the Ashen to return home now presents itself, not as a penitent pilgrim, but as the rightful and irrefutably brutal Lord of Zharr-Naggrund.

Ghorth the Cruel, Sorcerer-Prophet of Zharr-Naggrund, demands much from his generals. Fresh Labourers are required daily to meet the harsh demands of the Chaos Dwarf’s vast factory forges. No Dhrath-Zharr would accept this task more gladly, or with darker, even crueller glee, than Zhatan the Black, Commander of the Tower of Zharr.\\n\\nA call from Ghorth for even greater harvests reaches Zhatan; rumblings of a new venture are heard. The challenge is welcomed: new lands will be conquered for the glory of Hashut and Ghorth, and the weak will be inevitably subsumed.\\n\\nThe screams of the weak will echo throughout the forges, and the ecstatic laughs of Zhatan shall ring out all the louder!

The Jade Dragon, architect of the Dragon Emperor’s vision for Grand Cathay and Lord of the Jade Court, is a master of many disciplines; administration, record keeping, magic and espionage.\\n\\nFrom the trade city of Shang-Wu, he plans the prosperity of the entire realm. But now, the time for overt action is at hand. The Dragon Emperor himself has tasked Yuan Bo with fulfilling a centuries-long scheme to ensure Cathay’s prominence. This must be attended to personally. No other faithful servant of the Dragon Emperor can be trusted with this undertaking.\\n\\nAnd so, Yuan Bo must step out from the shadows and take to the field. With the accumulated knowledge of the Jade Court, Yuan Bo seeks to realign the Celestial Compass, and secure the safety of Grand Cathay from all dangers, either within or without.

In Kislev, children both rich and poor are scared into obedience with whispers of the dreaded hag in the woods. Yet the reality is far more horrifying than any child could conceive, for the old crone spoken about in such tales is no mere myth.\\n\\nMother Ostankya, an elusive figure empowered by the land itself, draws her terrifying magic from woodland, fen and oblast alike. Those with transgressions against the Motherland, be they of this world or another, find no refuge from her vengeance, even on their own soil.\\n\\nTo the distant north, where stands Kislev’s abandoned watchtowers against the Ruinous incursions, she brings her wrath. There can be no doubt: her appearance so far from home is a portent of terrible curses soon to come.\\n\\n[[i]]Mother Ostankya will get you![[/i]]

An eternity of meddling in the Chaos Realm inevitably led Tzeentch’s brother-Gods to vie for the Changeling’s destruction.\\n\\nFor it was the Changeling who cut away Slaanesh’s hair as the Dark Prince slept to weave a cloak presented to a champion of Tzeentch. It was the Changeling who sealed the doors of Khorne’s citadel while he was campaigning, forcing the Blood God to shatter his own proud gates when he returned.\\n\\nYet it is the Daemon’s boredom with such inanities of the Great Game, rather than the ire of the Chaos Realm, that leads him to the Old World to seek greater tapestries of disruption. By the time the deceiving horror becomes known to his victims, be they kings, emperors, or even gods, they will be impotent to act against him.

After multiple tragedies born of miscalculation and catastrophic failure, the blood on Malakai Makaisson's hands will not be easy to wipe clean. Ejected from the Engineers' Guild, the eager inventor plies his trade as a sworn Slayer, hoping his work can be of some use until he finds redemption in glorious sacrifice.\\n\\nYet, as the oncoming tides of Chaos threaten to swallow the world whole, his noble demise may lie just beyond the horizon. Aboard the Spirit of Grungni – an Airship of his own design – he traverses the skies, honour-bound to defend the Dwarfholds with his most deadly creations.\\n\\nFor now, Makaisson's calling draws him onwards. There await the hordes of Chaos, and the chance to reclaim the respect of his people and erase his shame once and for all!

An ancient prophecy foretells of a vile and deathly force of Chaos, led by a monstrous champion capable of uniting the armies of their wretched God to conquer the unholy proving ground of Zanbaijin. Now, legend sits on the verge of reality. Tamurkhan, the great Kurgan Lord of Chaos, has declared himself the fabled Bringer of Desolation, seeking to lead the virulent war hosts of Nurgle in a sweeping tide of rot.\\n\\nBurrowed deep in the body of an Ogre Tyrant, he puppets his hideous host with the blessing of the Urfather, riding before his great horde to spread death and destruction in abundance. The misguided pawns of lesser Gods will no doubt try to stand in his way – a mistake the Maggot Lord will make sure to punish severely!

Your father and mother – the Dragon Emperor and Moon Empress – have been missing for over a century. It is the Time of Darkness and Disharmony. Unrest is rife. Your siblings look to their own affairs, caring not that the hordes of Chaos mass just beyond the Great Bastion. But even on this side of the barrier the cults of Chi’an Chi foster dissention. The coming conflict will be difficult without aid, so perhaps the Ogres will side with you for a large fee? Or maybe your younger brother, the Iron Dragon, can be convinced to send the legions of Shang-yang? Harmony must be restored… and soon… or Grand Cathay will fall.

Grand Cathay is the land of the Celestial Dragon Emperor. Before the world was blighted by Chaos, the Celestial Dragon learned how to take human form. To aid his rule, he took a mate, the Moon Dragon, and they had nine children who became noble rulers of Cathay's many provinces.\\n\\nOf the nine, four have been lost to time and enmity. Miao Ying, the Storm Dragon, was the first-born, given the honour of ruling the Northern Provinces and charged with Cathay's defence as commander of the Great Bastion. But the predations of Chaos grow, the bastion is under strain.\\n\\nThe power of a god may aid in securing Cathay's borders. Perhaps there is an opportunity to lure the Storm Dragon into the Chaos Realms? I travel east to gain an audience.

The Dragon Emperor and Moon Empress have been missing for over a century, and your siblings seem distracted. You have been left to your own devices – a chance to expand your power base without interference perhaps? However, your spies in Nan-Gau bring dire tidings that the legions of Chaos muster beyond the Great Bastion in numbers not seen in generations. Your older sister will no doubt try and defend the walls alone, but why should her pride deprive Cathay of your alchemical insights? Perhaps your status will be enhanced upon your father’s inevitable return should you make a direct intervention in the realm’s defence? Then again, if the Storm Dragon fails, she will have further to fall...

Grand Cathay is the land of the Celestial Dragon Emperor. In the distant past the Dragon Emperor founded his domain amongst the human tribes who dwelt in the east. To aid his rule, he took a mate, the Moon Dragon, and they had nine children who became noble rulers of Cathay's many provinces.\\n\\nOf the nine, four have been lost to time and enmity. Zhao Ming, the Iron Dragon, is closer to his mother and perceived with suspicion by his siblings. He rules Western Cathay yet the Skaven that lurk in the Warpstone Desert have been emboldened of late.\\n\\nThe power of a god may aid in pacifying his regions, increasing his standing amongst his kin. Will such a prize lure him into the Chaos Realms? I travel east to gain an audience.

The god-slayer is returned back to the mortal plane, forever changed. And now the Dark Powers circle around him like carrion, each vying for the prize – of yoking this Daemon Prince to their servitude. Until then, they offer him gifts and servants of his own, and so he raises an army that serves no single God – a Legion of Chaos.\\n\\nYet even as he's courted by the Dark Powers, there is a greater bounty found in the Chaos Realms.\\n\\nI do not need to travel far to find the Daemon Prince and make my offer. Already, he lays the foundations to a new fortress from which he will cast a reign of terror.

Weakness cannot be abided, and Grand Cathay is weak. The Dragon Emperor and his consort have fled their thrones; their scions are meek and must be destroyed. The other gods wish a share of the spoils, but do not let that distract you. Dominate the mortal and Daemonic legions, break through the dam, and flood the eastern lands in blood. Most importantly of all, bring Khorne the skulls of the Dragon-children and he may yet forgive you.

No subtlety, has Khorne. He yearns only for battle – slaughter is his desire, blood to sate an unquenchable thirst, and skulls to pile about his throne. Skarbrand was the most worthy of Khorne's Bloodthirsters, the greatest of the Blood God's reapers. But that was before his exile, cast from Khorne's presence, and now he finds himself on the wrong side of the maelstrom in the aftermath of Ursun's roar.\\n\\nBut there is a way for the Greater Daemon to find favour with his master again. Guided by the tome, I travel across the Chaos Wastes, through jagged mountains and lava rivers to Skarbrand's lair... Infernius.

Heretics spew forth across the land. This is what the Great Orthodoxy always feared would happen, and why the godless and unbelievers were excised, but it seems even that was not enough!\\n\\nThe cults of the Kislev pantheon were united under the Great Orthodoxy, and so must its sovereigns be also. Find common cause with Katarin and her father, the Red Tzar, for that is what Ursun demands. Only then can Kislev be purged of Chaos filth! Arm the faithful and unleash them – for Kislev and the Great Bear!

Kislev. The bulwark against the darkness. It is Kislevite blood that has protected the Old World, and yet where is their gratitude?\\n\\nSuch sermons are preached by the Supreme Patriarch of the Ursunite Cult, and Leader of the Great Orthodoxy, Kostaltyn. But who do they put upon the throne? A child. The daughter of the Red Tzar has fallen to the heresies of the Ice Witches. If Kostaltyn is to save Ursun, to step into the Chaos Realms, then the Supreme Patriarch must take control of the Motherland and have a united nation at his back.\\n\\nI journey to him now; he prays at a sacred site hidden by the Orthodoxy... the resting place of Boris Ursus.

Chaos spills forth, befouling the oblasts of Kislev, corrupting and slaying your subjects. The nation and your reign are in peril. The Empire revels in its own strife so it is up to you to act. However, there are unlikely allies: rumours persist that your father, the Red Tzar, strides across Kislev once again, and even the Great Orthodoxy makes overtures to face the greater threat.\\n\\nNow is the time to fight. Take back the oblasts from the Daemons and you will be remembered as the greatest of Khan-Queens!

Kislev. A realm forged by the Khan Queens of old. The bulwark against the darkness. The living bastion that protects the Empire and the soft nations to the south.\\n\\nSince her father's death, Katarin has taken the throne, but there are many within the realm who resent her rule, even now, the power of the Great Orthodoxy rises against the Ice Queen. If she is to save Ursun, to step beyond her borders and into the Chaos Realms, Katarin must have a united nation at her back.\\n\\nI journey to her now, across the icy fringes, to the Ice Court. If she is to take my advice, I fear she will need convincing. Word has reached the Ice Court of my coming, and an audience in her throne room has been granted.

Once more you have been summoned by the Motherland to protect its folk against the predations of Chaos. There will be no help from the south, for the Empire revels in its own strife, so Kislev must look to its own kith and kin. This is fortunate, for your daughter is on the throne and the Great Orthodoxy has risen to become a powerful defence against the Dark Powers. They must unite under you and the auspices of the Great Bear, and together the Daemons can be excised from Mother Kislev!

Kislev. The bulwark against the darkness. Yet the Motherland suffers, severed from its god.\\n\\nIf it is to survive, the nation needs its saviour once more. The folk of Kislev think Boris Bokha dead, but his body was claimed by the Motherland, and he has slept in ice ever since. Yet Ursun's pained roar will surely have started to rouse the Red Tzar.\\n\\nI journey to him now. He lays at a sacred site hidden by the Great Orthodoxy, deep in the cold oblasts of Kislev. If anyone can save the Bear-God of Kislev, it is Ursun's High Priest... Raddi Bokha... Boris Ursus.\\n\\nBut even should I manage to wake him, I will need to make a strong case that he should listen to me.

Cathay has been left to fester for over a century. Left leaderless and devoid of the healing aura of the Moon Empress, it is ripe for experimentation. First, the bulwark that guards Grand Cathay must be shattered. Ally with other servants of the Chaos Gods, dominate them if you must, and then break through the Great Bastion to spread your glorious gifts.

Decay and rot. Nurgle is the God of Plagues and poxes, and while the countless mortals suffer in misery, He believes to have bestowed them all with great gifts. Nurgle's most eager apprentice is the Foetid Brewmaster, Ku'gath Plaguefather.\\n\\nThe Plaguefather has always preferred lurking in the dark places of the mortal world, so it is no surprise that he was far from the Realm of Chaos when Ursun's roar caused the maelstrom. But there is a way to lure him back there... the promise of the ultimate specimen upon which to experiment.\\n\\nFor a time he was well hidden, even from the Tome of Fate's pages, and I wandered needlessly until I picked up his noxious trail and it led me underground. I must make my offer quickly, before I succumb...

The Maw sends you visions of Cathay, the land of the Astromancers. The Dragon King and Queen have flown away. Their nation is weak. Yet there is opportunity to profit if we work for the Dragons. The Dark Gods too offer riches if we help them topple the mountain-wall. Plenty of meat no matter which side we choose. The Maw cares not which banner you fight under, if any. The visions starts to coalesce: a chance to expand the Mouth-God’s influence beyond the mountains and see Ogrekind thrive...

The Ogre Kingdoms, a group of greedy, brutish tribes that fight with each other over riches and meat, are found in the east across the Mountains of Mourn. Oft-times, their violence spills out beyond the mountains, and so the Ogres roam far, occasionally even welcomed as mercenaries.\\n\\nSkrag, the Prophet of the Great Maw, is such a wanderer, and that is why he makes such an ideal candidate for this quest.\\n\\nI trek across the Chaos Wastes, avoiding the slave patrols in the Dark Lands, and at last reach the Ogre Kingdoms. I fear I will not have long to make my case before the audience get hungry.

The Dragon Emperor is long gone and so you – the Overtyrant – never one to look a gift Rhinox in the jaw, sense an opportunity… While Daemon and human scrap with each other, you are shrewd enough to sell the services of your Maneaters and Bulls to the highest bidder. It’s time to make a killing – quite literally!

The Ogre Kingdoms sprawl across the Mountains of Mourn. They have taken the peaks from the now-extinct Sky-titans. This mountainous realm is a place of rocks, bones and great beasts to be eaten or tamed.\\n\\nPerhaps 'kingdoms' is a misnomer, for there is no king, but an Overtyrant who rules with an iron fist and demands tribute from the other tribes in the form of meat and gold. He is Greasus Goldtooth.\\n\\nI travel far, for the Mountains of Mourn are beyond the Dark Lands, in the east. This gives me time to ruminate on how to approach them, and convince the Overtyrant to invade the Chaos Realms. Avarice is the key, for there is no one greedier than Greasus!
The great Bear-God of Kislev is missing. Prayers go unanswered and the roar of spring has not been heard. Prince Yuri is sent north by the Tzarina Katarin to search for Kislev’s lost god.

The She-Dragon and her Celestial Emperor have fled, leaving their nest of souls – what mortals call "Cathay" – painfully exposed. Now is the time to sample an eastern menu, majestic tempter. First you must dominate the supplicant legions of rival Gods, and then thrust them toward the Great Bastion, breach it and consume the screaming souls of Grand Cathay.

The Chaos God of desire, Slaanesh, is the youngest of the Dark Powers, but has the potential to eclipse them all. He is the Dark Prince and Lord of Excess. His servants embody those traits to perfection, and none more so than N'Kari, the Arch-tempter.\\n\\nHis search for the exquisite saw him stranded on the wrong side of the maelstrom. Not that the Keeper of Secrets would be concerned, for a being such as N'Kari will always find... distractions.\\n\\nNevertheless, I can perhaps offer a greater prize to tempt the Arch-tempter.\\n\\nI make my way through perfumed fog – ignoring the tormented screams – to his palace. The negotiations will be challenging.
Pathetic! You were no challenge for Khorne's servants. Remember, without the Daemon Prince's soul, the Forge of Souls cannot be reached.

You breached the Brass Citadel, a feat so rare as to draw Khorne’s gaze! Whether that is in ire or respect is yet to be known, for a long shadow is cast over your mighty victory, as Be’lakor remains in the Forge of Souls with the prize. You have the first soul, but three more are required to light the Bridge of Shadows.

The Dragon Emperor of Grand Cathay and his consort have been absent from their lands for over a century. Much to your consternation, even you do not know of their whereabouts, and the stygian depths within the Well of Eternity offer no hints. Even so, what is left unguarded should be stolen. Lead the Chaos invasion from without and fan the flames of unrest from within. Souls are a worthy prize, but Tzeentch craves knowledge above all – smother the eastern lands in the Changer’s corruption and the Dragon Emperor’s location will be revealed.

Tzeentch is the Great Architect, the Changer of the Ways, the God of magic, mischief and manipulation. Kairos Fateweaver is His oracle, able to see past and future but blind to the present.\\n\\nUrsun's death-howl has stranded Kairos on the mortal plane while he is in the midst of a grand scheme – an incursion into the Celestial Dragon Empire of Cathay. But there is a greater boon awaiting in the Chaos Realms, if he can bypass the maelstrom.\\n\\nI travel to reach Fateweaver at the Silvered Tower, hoping to be retained before he teleports to a staging post in the east. He will know of my coming.

Among those who study the obscure depths of the occult there are mages who walk the tenuous bounds between life and death. Throughout the cavernous courts of Nuln are whispers of one who exists within this nebulous realm of reality, regarded as an inhuman spectre of Unlife.\\n\\nElspeth von Draken, Magisterix of the Amethyst Order, steeps herself in Shyish and the mastery of the Lore of Death. Though many shun the wielders of the deathly arts, the “Graveyard Rose” is unquestioned in her steadfast defence of the Empire.\\n\\nHeeding her warnings of evil on the horizon, the Elector Countess of Wissenland has granted the pallid Sorceress access to the renowned might of the Imperial Gunnery School. Whether by her command of magic or the lethal guns of Nuln, the Empire’s enemies shall be granted death everlasting!
Points are generated when your [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord inflicts damage (damage inflicted on higher tier units will confer more points).

Waaagh! points are generated for each entity engaged in melee. When enough points are generated, the bar will fill up and the Waaagh! ability will become available for use. The more friendly units in the battle the more points required to fill the bar. Each use of the ability also increases the number of points required.
Points are generated for each friendly unit charging.
As Tomb Kings warriors die on the battlefield, their spirits enter the Realm of Souls.
Points are generated for each enemy entity killed.
Points are generated based on the number of enemy units debilitated by sources such as spells, abilities, and contact phase effects, such as poison.
Points are generated for killing entities in units that have negative [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]Leadership states.
Points are generated by casting spells with the Winds of Magic.

Barricades are designed to waylay an opponent rather than inflict casulties. Often made from trees, stones or dug earth, a barricade can stop a cavalry charge, slow an infantry march, or create a killing zone for missile units.

Brimstone (sulphur) and bitumen, amongst other things, can be composited to create a highly-dangerous weapon. Bitumen helps a slow-burning brimstone composite stick to things, especially men and mounts, causing severe burns if not death. In addition to fire arrows, the mixture can also be poured from towers during sieges. A brimstone pit can be deployed before a battle begins and ignited when an enemy charge is underway, ideally too late for it to be aborted.

Sudes are an extremely versatile weapon. Due to the nature of their construction they can be placed in the ground to create low palisades or interlocked to create a caltrop shape. In caltrop form, sudes can kill charging/running units from either direction (something that stakes cannot).

Sharp stone beds are created from various types of stone, constructed as a form of non-lethal defence around settlements. Stones can either sunk into the ground or layed in irregular piles. Infantry find these difficult objects to traverse, whereas cavalry can only pass through by picking routes between the stones. This slowing effect produces an effective killing zone in and around the stones, ideal ground for missile units to trap their targets.
Spike traps are sunken stakes or groups of stakes concealed by foliage. Often producing more kills when charging, the foliage collapses when stepped on causing injury or death by impalement.

Wooden stakes are among the most common settlement defences. A simple yet effective device, sharpened stakes are set in 45 degree lines to impale charging men or horses. They can easily be navigated around when moving slowly, but even this can be used to the advantage of missile units. Stakes angled this way can also enable defenders to sally forth without the risk of impalement.
Barricades prevent units from progressing for a short period of time.\\n\\nThey can be destroyed by flaming shots.
Fire pits can be ignited to set alight unsuspecting units. They can be activated by flaming projectiles or unit interaction.
Sudes cause damage to mounted units approaching from any angle, and extra damage if they are moving quickly.
Sharp stones impede a unit's progress, presenting an easy target for missile troops.
Spike traps are a concealed danger, causing high casualties to any units who attempt to move across them.
Stakes cause damage to mounted units approaching from the front. They cause extra damage if the unit is moving quickly.

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:CharacterTargetName}}, leader of the {{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:FirstTargetFactionNameWithIcon}} tribe has been defeated; a once powerful warlord now reduced to obscurity beneath your might. For as you stand tall in victory he kneels at your side, hands in chains, his followers stood amongst yours, brought to a halt in anticipation of your next utterance. His men now see him as weak and unfit to lead any longer, this is a chance for you to take control of this faction's forces and land, as well as its followers' dubious loyalty.\\n\\nThough, while the allure of land may appear to make this choice a simple one, do not let the challenges that a larger empire creates escape you - perhaps simply killing this man and letting whatever is left of his faction fade into memory may be a more fitting end...

The leader of {{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:FirstTargetFactionNameWithIcon}}, {{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:CharacterTargetName}}, has been defeated. His followers look on in horror, their unwavering belief in their leader dashed in an instant, even this legend cannot deny your supremacy amongst all Norscans now. Surely now is the time to seize control, bring his domain into yours, take all that was once his. Or, you may free him... as an insult perhaps, an unending torment for this foe – the choice is yours.
A Tomb Prince, Necrotect and Liche Priest enter your throne room and offer themselves in your service...

Tretch’s luck holds once again. On the third day of pillaging the surrounding countryside his Gutter Runners apprehend the assassins whose attempt he foiled. One is slain while resisting capture, but the other is tackled, trussed like a turkey, and dumped before the Warlord.\\n\\nHow should the interrogation proceed?

There is little left of this city's past splendour. Its crumbling edifices and dilapidated porticos are host to naught now but the desert winds. The agent scours the ruins, and eventually locates the entrance to a grand tomb, with Alcadizaar's name barely legible over the grand architrave. In front of the tomb lie the bodies of Lizardmen, entangled with mouldering remains. The blood and ichor is still wet: this skirmish was recent. Perhaps the battle still rages within? Should the agent enter the tomb and risk becoming a combatant? Or remain circumspect and tarry without for a sign?

The raid was a success. A barbarian chief, draped in ancient gold and gem-studded trinkets, is dragged before Settra. He is larger by far than the average human and wears a growling mask of surliness, but Settra revels in the terror that lurks behind his eyes. The creature's soul is forfeit, of course; Phakth demands eternal justice, and Settra his due. What will be the manner of this insect's passing?

A new monument will show the gods that their veneration is still our foremost concern. They, in turn, will strengthen our hands in this time of endless war. But to whom among our pantheon should it be dedicated?

In cities as old as the deserts it is the natural order that even the finest buildings eventually crumble and fall. One of our largest temples has started to collapse and we fear that it will soon topple, bringing down calamity. Should we reinforce it?

The main tributary used for trade and transport of materials from one holy site to another is slowly drying out. The water level has now dropped to a dangerous level - what should be done, if anything, to prevent it from drying out completely?

The Liche Priests of the Mortuary Cult have left their necropoli in search of servants to aid them in their holy work; the incantations of preservation must be maintained and furthered. However, not everyone is a suitable candidate for such work. Who can we spare?

The cities of Nehekhara are without compare in their scale and grandeur. However, time ravages stone just the same as flesh and now our buildings are badly in need of restoration. Upon which of them should we focus our endeavours?

Liche Priests should live only to serve their king's undying will. Betrayal should be anathema to their order, yet one among their number has betrayed us by conspiring with a rival Tomb King. How should we proceed?

During the excavation of one of our Lord's tombs, a disaster occurred; the more we dug, the more sand poured into the breach, trapping our unfortunate workers inside and re-sealing the chamber. Is the loss of a few wretched labourers sufficient reason to dig elsewhere? Or should we persevere here and redouble our efforts?

Whilst traversing the jungles on the edge of the world, with a view to bringing them within our sphere of influence, our forces have encountered a village of tribal Lizardmen. Naturally, they cower and beg for their meagre lives. Should we sacrifice them to empower our future?

Despite the best efforts of our chief Necrotect, one of our tombs has started to sink back into the sand once more, before giving up its illustrious, arcane secrets; if we do not act quickly to shore up its entrance, we risk losing everything we have thus far gained.

One of our Liche Priests has dared approach with concerns that one of the Necrosphinxes is no longer under the control of our warriors' souls but instead is in thrall to Usekph, the destructive god buried beneath the sands. Dare we destroy it and risk his unending wrath?

Men, whose flesh still crowds their bones, with hearts that continue to beat, have been found wandering the land. Throwing themselves upon our mercy, they beg for their lives and the freedom to return to their faraway homes. What should we do?

We have made a great discovery! During the course of our excavations, remains of the army that once served Alcadizaar the Conqueror, the last and maybe the greatest of all the Priest Kings of Nehekhara, have been unearthed. It would take but a little magic to raise them to our service, should we do so or give them a ritual burial in the classical Nehekharan style?

The creature's soul is forfeit, of course; Phakth demands eternal justice, and Settra his due. What will be the manner of this insect's passing?

Dargoth is in the aftermath of some attack. The towers still burn even amongst the snow and ice, and the bodies of the recently-mauled litter the ground. The survivors look upon the Norse with suspicion and hostility. It is clear your force does not come to offer aid. You speak out, asking if this was the work of the immortal War Hydra. You get only silence in response...

This scheming Druchii trader has been surprisingly forthcoming thus far, but as you suspect, it is not long before he proposes a bargain. He is willing to hand over the extinguished Phoenix pinion, stating that it will prove useful on the hunt to come, and provide the location of the volcano in which the Mother of the Flame is reborn into this world.\\n\\nHowever, there is a cost; he has need of a favour regarding an unrelated matter. He wishes to divert you from your hunt - only temporarily - to kill one of his enemies. He claims he has bad credit with the assassins of his own race, so requires the murderous skills of your men. Once the death is certified he will hand over the pinion and the information you need to continue the hunt.

You wield the power of Khaine's might. The sword strikes terror in all your enemies. On the battlefield you reap a mighty toll as foes fall before the blade with ease. Yet, nightmares torment your soul, and a sickness leeches into your lands... \\n\\nPerhaps it is wiser to relinquish such power? You will be weaker... feebler... but is it not a price worth paying to becalm your dreams?

Is the sword now controlling your decisions? Your power is absolute - a force to match the gods themselves - but your moods are permanently dark, your allies lose confidence, and your followers surely plot regicide. You reign over hollow lands and a desperate folk who now despise their sovereign!\\n\\nWill you give up this power to rule the world?
Through battle, the sword grows ever stronger, while at home your lands fester and become more corrupted with the passing of time. You must choose whether to continue down this darkest of paths…

The Sword of Khaine will always be drawn to the powerful. You have defeated its most recent owner, and even as their body cools, the sword calls to you – the power of a god bound within the blade waiting to be unleashed!

A self-obsessed singer needs a doting audience, and Cylostra is well aware that it is the Bretonnians who appreciate her talents the most. After all, it was a Bretonnian king who once favoured her above all other court singers, frequently inviting the diva to give private performances and serenade eminent guests at important stately banquets.\\n\\nOn the other hand, Cylostra is technically still well overdue for a high-profile performance before the High Elves of Ulthuan. Many years ago, when the Lamprey succumbed to a storm in the Eastern Straits of the Great Ocean, before Cylostra’s transformation, she was on an important diplomatic voyage to sing before the Phoenix King. A treaty of great import was reliant on his pleasure in her performance, for the Elves believe good art – music in particular – to be as valuable as gems and gold. It was an important engagement, so surely the High Elves will still be waiting for her?!\\n\\nTo find an audience, Cylostra could head east from the islands of Northern Yvresse towards Bretonnia, retracing the fateful voyage which led to her transforming into the eternally-vengeful spirit she has become. Alternatively, she could head towards the southern end of the Shifting Isles, where the High Elves' Old World shipping lanes are located, following them directly into the great Elven port of Lothern and, hopefully, to the Phoenix King himself...

Although most entrepreneurial, our endeavours 'ave presented something of a dilemma. A large, jewel-adorned statue of sandstone has... found its way into our possession. It's far too large to take away 'ole, but its adornments would make quite the prize! It's also covered in glyphs indicating woe might befall any who mistreat it, but that's probably just flannel so less tenacious pirates leave it alone. Should we ignore the markings an' loot its jewels or be wary?

Ahoy there! We've come across an enemy encampment devoid of life an' littered with corpses. Half-devoured bodies are scattered about the clearing. The fallen dead were elite riflemen - surely one among 'em will be of use to us? Or perhaps we should seek out the creature that caused this massacre?

Apparently, a great Lizardmen temple 'as been unearthed. Though most of it is dilapidated, a single statue stands at the centre of what was likely a ceremonial garden - it must be worth a fortune, but removing it will certainly cause the temple to collapse, which will surely draw somebody's ire. Should we take the idol an' ignore the consequences or be cautious not to attract too much attention - an' their cold, unforgiving bloodlust, our way?

A major naval battle has ended, leavin' hundreds dead on each side. Death is no barrier to continued service, as well you know - those who fell in battle would make fine new recruits. If we make haste and 'ead off at full sail, the perished could be reanimated before they're lost to the ocean. We must decide if this boon is worth the toll it would take on our crew - should we make haste or ignore the battle?
The tides seem uneasy an' force us off course. Could this be a warning from Manann? This would not be the first time he has guided us out of danger - should we continue our course or take heed?

'Conversations' with several captured admirals 'ave brought information to light regarding several potential targets. We'll only 'ave time to strike one, however, so must choose wisely. Which convoy should we attack?

A rival band o'pirates 'ave requested access to some of our coves an' are willing for pay for it. Should we allow 'em to shelter in our territory or kill 'em and 'liberate' the loot they're currently carrying?

The night sky bleeds purple! The Wind of Shyish is strong, instilling the crew with new found vigour an' strength. Now is the time for action - for conquest - an' for using this magical boon to our advantage. Should we control the seas or turn our attention to new lands?

The harsh weather has caused severe damage to our timber reserves, makin' it difficult to repair any combat-damaged ships at sea. We must now choose where to focus our remaining resources - should our ships suffer or our settlements?

Our cargo hold has sprung a leak! Some of the booty has already been damaged an' our weapons an' armour are now at risk too! There is only so much space above deck, 'owever, so which supplies should we try to save whilst the ship is bein' repaired.

We've acquired a ledger covering much of the recently-raided area, filled with useful information 'bout shippin' routes an' cargo inventories. Two targets appear particularly valuable, yet strangely they're undefended. There is only time to pursue one of 'em though - which should we target?

Those purple Winds of Magic are strangely absent 'round these parts, makin' the bindings that tie our troops to this world an' our will tenuous at best! Should we wait for the winds to blow more favourably for us or press on regardless?

The sight of wrecked ships is nothing new for a seasoned pirate, but this particular one 'eralds a welcome surprise! Packed to the keel with brand new weapons, armour an' gunpowder, this ship's cargo hold is several times the size of our own. However, some supplies will 'ave to be left behind. What should we loot from the ship?

The remains of a large sea beast are spotted floating in some nearby backwaters. The unidentified creature has been inexplicably ripped to pieces by an explosive force, its belly torn open and exposed. This mysterious find could prove bountiful, for who knows what devoured treasures might reside within its guts? An unidentified ship has also been spotted nearby – rival scavengers. Whoever they are, you are not one to share salvage with anyone!

Your ocean scouts bring news that the bloated corpse of a massive sea monster has floated to the surface in some nearby straits. Although its carcass swells dangerously with noxious gases, you know that the belly of such a gargantuan monster can potentially yield numerous valuable treasures. A salvage mission may be a risky endeavour, however, as it is likely that other salvagers have also caught wind of the opportunity.

With a gush of putrid water, the bloated corpse of an ancient sea leviathan surfaces close by. You consider sending your crew to investigate what secrets the cadaver of the sea beast will bestow, but such an expedition is not without risk. When alive, these creatures are known to host parasites the size of wolves and even colonies of needle-toothed aquatic man-things. Even so, there may be valuables to be found within its stinking gut.

A convoy of trading ships carrying myriad precious goods across a nearby sea trade route have been brought low by the angry Sea-God, Stromfels, much to the chagrin of wealthy merchants and investors back at their homeports. Knowing that such a wreckage could be a highly profitable salvage opportunity, you sail towards the area but unsurprisingly, others have also caught wind of it. You could continue your approach, but this might end in a confrontation at sea…

The seabed is littered with the barnacle-clad hulls of ships that once set out to tame the oceans. Recently, rumours started circulating that one particularly notable wreckage had been spotted – a partially sunken ship that was rumoured to have been sailing back to Marienburg with a hold full of mysterious trinkets looted from across the Old World before suffering Stromfels’ ire. You know its location, but there’s always the chance that others have caught wind of these rumours too…

From the crow's nest come shouts that broken masts can be seen piercing the ocean's surface. The lookout has spotted a sunken ship lying in the waters amongst some distant shoals. Located far from an inhabited shoreline or any known sailing routes, it has the markings of a pirate galleon. A mysterious sunken pirate ship in this location cannot be here without good reason, and perhaps that reason involves treasure!

You receive word of a wooden carcass of a ship that has been discovered strewn across a small, mysterious island. You are told that beyond the beach, gold and other trinkets can be found in abundance, surrounded by the long-dead crewmen who starved whilst waiting to be rescued. Some of your own crew whisper of curses which may be worth heeding, but such things rarely deter you when looted wealth and riches are involved…

While on an ocean crossing, an island inexplicably rises out of the sea before you. As your fleet approaches, the crew hear an eerie but ensnaring song that carries over the turbulent surf; a tune that promises much, with lyrics singing of everything from the untold riches of Greasus Goldtooth to some of Nagash's secrets of Undeath. The verses foretell the attainment of great power and wealth - all you must do is order your vessel closer to shore… It is what the Syreens want…

As you make your way across the sea, the ocean mists suddenly part to reveal an island which, by all accounts, is unchartered even by the Great Mapwright himself. High spars of rock jut from sea, like spikes in a trap that has ensnared some prey. Indeed, a wrecked ship lies impaled on the small island's coastline; its crew seem to have moved into the interior along with any valuables that may have been onboard.

Pirate coves are some of the world’s most elusive places, where the wealth of local sea brigands is secretly kept and fiercely defended. It seems that today may be your lucky day, as your lookout in the crow’s nest claims to have spotted one – a small island cave, next to which a black ship is moored. The ship belongs to an infamous fleet of Vampire pirates, and it appears that there are Zombie Deckhands transferring treasure chests onto the ship right now. It’s an opportunity for a big payday, but these Unliving sea-dogs certainly won’t give up their wealth too easily.

A self-obsessed singer needs a doting audience, and Cylostra is well aware that it is the Bretonnians who appreciate her talents the most. After all, it was a Bretonnian king who once favoured her above all other court singers, frequently inviting the diva to give private performances and serenade eminent guests at important stately banquets.\\n\\nOn the other hand, Cylostra is technically still well overdue for a high-profile performance before the High Elves of Ulthuan. Many years ago, when the Lamprey succumbed to a storm in the Eastern Straits of the Great Ocean, before Cylostra’s transformation, she was on an important diplomatic voyage to sing before the Phoenix King. A treaty of great import was reliant on his pleasure in her performance, for the Elves believe good art – music in particular – to be as valuable as gems and gold. It was an important engagement, so surely the High Elves will still be waiting for her?!\\n\\nTo find an audience, Cylostra could head east from the islands of Northern Yvresse towards Bretonnia, retracing the fateful voyage which led to her transforming into the eternally-vengeful spirit she has become. Alternatively, she could head towards the southern end of the Shifting Isles, where the High Elves' Old World shipping lanes are located, following them directly into the great Elven port of Lothern and, hopefully, to the Phoenix King himself...

This places the Averlanders in close contact with the Dwarfs, with whom they have a long and amicable trading history.\\n\\nWill you accept Averland’s offer of confederation?

Balthasar Gelt has suggested that the Golden Order join you in a confederation.\\n\\nThe Golden Order are an arm of the Colleges of Magic dedicated to the study of alchemy and the Lore of Metal. Their Supreme Patriarch, Balthasar Gelt, is a fiercely intelligent and powerful battle Wizard who has served the Empire well in the past. Should you accept his offer, he will join your ranks.\\n\\nWill you accept the Golden Order’s offer of confederation?
