Welcome, kin. You must want something, it better not be my head!
It is always a pleasure - a dubious pleasure - to welcome a fellow Lord of the Night to my domain.
Greetings, brothers, what does mine Blood Line require?
Very well, let us hold a conclave, my kin.
I will take thy word, but only a fool would renege on me. Are you a fool, mortal?
Bind your soul to this commitment. It is forfeit if thou fail me!
I accept those terms, but the reek of betrayal surrounds thou. I warn thee, do not succumb to it!
I accept these terms, we'll sign the contracts in blood… thy blood.
We have agreement, mortal, keep thou side of the bargain and I may do mine.
Very well, we have a pact. Do not disappoint me.
A fine choice, one I will savour!
This is the correct pact to make!
Thou strivest to preserve that which is already lost, Bretonnian fool. Nevertheless, I will hear thine offer!
I shall harken to thy king's words - but I can already tell thee, the answer shall not be to thine liking, mortal…
Bretonnian, make thine offer. Only then shall I decide if thou join mine hordes or return to thy feckless lands.
I struggle to address the riddle in mine head - art thou brave or foolish for approaching me with this 'offer'?
Hahaha - mortals of Bretonnia, welcome. Drink of this wine, I have some robust reds in my cellar…
How fares thy kingdom? I hear of unrest in thy city of Mousillon, nothing too troubling I hope…
A truce then - if such a thing is needed with such an insignificant nation of flesh bags.
Scrawl thy name on this contract mortal, do it in blood so I can scent you out, when thy betray me!
I accept, mine Knights and thous shall charge as one.
Very well - thy smallfolk shall not be feasted on until our alliance comes to an end.
Yesss, why not… and should thy troops prove feckless in life I may have a use for them in death.
We have a pact, thrall of the Breton. Do not fail me.
I have no time for such pathetic creatures - thy blood is thin, thou lands are riddled with disease.
Haha, you are some thrall, recently emerged from the Blood Kiss? My legions shall march on Bretonnia not ally with it!
Back to your dreary land, mortal - tell the wench you worship that I shall suck her people dry!
No… Now thy must face my legions... and they hunger…
I think not. Take your offers back to thy wretched realm; tell thy nobles to expect me soon enough.
Such an alliance was always unlikely, mortals. Thy stock tend to make weak allies.
Surely you see wisdom in holding thy tongue.
I will not lend mine ear to some arrogant foreigner who darest presume to know my wants!
Thou art at the limits of thy power, immortal. Only death can protect thy kingdom, now.
Thy presence is noted, Dragon-Lord. Its worth remains unproven.
So be it. I'll deign to work with the Chaos Gods, but take care not to let thy servants anger me, for there will be consequence.
Yes, we shall work together to free the world of the living, but when thou think to betray, know that my vengeance will run deep.
This suits our purposes, tell thy master we have a pact.
Very well, but do not mistake this for acquiescence on all souls. The von Carsteins will have their share!
Yesss, a doom befalls the world. If I can't have it no one will!
The so-called Everchosen has no idea with whom he trifles! Bid him to step into thine court so that I may rip his throat out!
Thine Chaos Gods are spectators to what happens here. I am the God of Inexhaustible Blood and I shall have my way!
Chaos, thy Gods mutate thee as reward, but I can give thee the ultimate gift… death.
Speak then, Northman, but know I shall drink thy bestial blood if thou displeases me.
Welcome, brothers of the darkness. What could mine blood line do for thee?
Ahh, the minions of Chaos, come to mine grave, looking for common cause no doubt?
No, the mortals belong to me! Send thy champions in challenge and I will end them all.
I think not! Tell thy Lord Archaon, he is a greedy peon to weakling Gods and that will cost him dear!
No, tainted ones, I would feast on your flesh if I knew thou blood was not infected so.
I see no benefit here - Archaon is a fool, a charlatan who needs to be taught a lesson in manners.
Thou hast erred, Chaos thrall - we both wish death upon the world, but while thou take souls - I cull them!
Impossible - the cattle are mine to reap, not yours to taint!
An alliance with piteous stone-gatherers and grudge-mongers? Very well, mortals.
An alliance with such close-minded creatures… acceptable on this occasion.
Why, yes, prepare thyselves, Dwarfs, for my stipend will be demanding.
I see. Ally with us, and I'll overlook the perceived notions of unfairness recorded in thine little book.
I take your pledge, Dwarf, ensure it is kept as thy reputation states.
Yesss, let's seal it in blood, even the dusty blood of thy Dwarfs will do!
I'll have no such thing! Thou are creatures of deformed height, and I will spare thou no mercy!
Prepare, Dwarfs, for when I come for you I shall shave the beards of thy Unliving corpses!
Thy beards must be interfering with thy heads, we will not ally with stunted hole-dwellers!
I am von Carstein! You think I need the help of an atrophying empire to further my destiny!
Ha! I think not, stone-gatherer. I've had my fill of Dwarf bile this night.
No, I grow weary of Dwarfs. Their blood tastes as dour as their mood.
Speak thy insults, stuntling – let me hear thy pleas, for it is music to mine ears.
Dwarfs! Would that Nagash had wiped thy sorry race out when he had the wherewithal to do so! Speak then!
So, the bothersome stone-gatherers come from their mountain-holes to plead for mercy?
I have no time for stunted-folk, they hold no interest. Dwarf-creature, hast thine words import?
Stunted folk, I greet thee but do not presume too much.
Dwarfs! Thy lives are reckoned long, but the grave is eternal!
The Emperor! A false title! Be careful what you say, mortal, for I am the true Emperor!
So, the sheep come to debate with the Shepard! Very well, deliver thy message.
Men of the hammer - tell me thine tales of woe and a true count of the realm shall appease them!
So, Volkmar sends thou to barter in his stead... What a delicious proposition.
I do this for Sylvania. Make no mistake, mortal fools, this grants thy a reprieve and nothing more.
These terms will have to suffice, but I'll seek proper redress in due course, mortals - have no fear about that!
I see no reason, as the true Count of Stirland, to add my levy to Franz' army.
Fine. The Undead and the living shall work as one.
Yes, as Lords of this realm it is our duty to work as one for the good of our nation…
An accord then, thy commonfolk shall step in unison with mine own sleepless warriors.
Dost the Heldenhammer know what wretched creatures hath sired in his stead?
Does Franz not dare to come before me and kneel? A coward then, as the Princes of Altdorf have ever been!
Why would I, the greatest of all von Carsteins, deign to ally with my food?
Your decrepit Empire is not worthy to form a pact with my sleepless legions! I will see you all dead before I share the glory with the living!
Haha, why should the herder have to treat with his cattle when he can whip them into obedience!
If Vlad would not deign to treat with mortals of the Empire what makes thou think I will…
Franz oversteps his bounds! He is self-declared emperor of the living. My legions do not recognise his authority.
No, as you stubbornly refuse my right to rule mine own lands, I refuse your notions of alliance.
To end civilisation then, Greenskin filth, but do not forget who is the master and who is the dog!
A horde is a horde whether made from my servants or Greenskin beasts. It's purpose will be the same.
Together, beast, we will hunt our prey.
Then let the Orcs run rampant! My servants will be ready to pick through the corpses in the aftermath!
Fine! If the Orcs want nought but war and death… then I will find it for them.
We will work with these green beasts. Let them be the scythe of our harvest.
Get from my presence, creature! Thou are nothing but Strigoi fodder - to even suggest an alliance with mine bloodline is grave insult!
I think not, my legions will slay thy green beasts - I haven't the time or inclination to tame thou!
My bloodline is of the highest nobility; to even consider an alliance with base creatures like these is an impiety too far!
Get thee from my realm, creature! I will not even taste your blood, that should be the greatest offence of all!
Haha - a laughable notion. They are dim-witted beasts, we are regal lords - there's no common cause.
I don't think so, Greenskin. But please, keep killing the humans, their corpses make fine troops.
Mortals… thou hast trespassed. Thy words had best hold prominence or death will visit thee!
Speak thy words and pray to thine pitiful little gods that they ring true!
Do not underestimate the danger thou art in, mortal, mine patience wears thin for thy parley.
No matter the might of thine ambition, it can be drained from thy veins.
Do not waste thy breath, for very little remains.
I heed no council. Not from the Undead, and certainly not from the living.
Prostrate thyself, and I may acknowledge thy desperate pleas.
Hadst thou some modicum of intelligence, thou wouldst have fled!
I need not ask thy service in death. For I am its master, and it obeys my command!
Thou hast trodden out of thy depth, mortal. But it is far too late to flee.
The night grows long. I shall hear thee mortal, but talk is cheap!
Don't stand there like some startled sheep! Deliver thy message, lamb, so I may consider a response.
Welcome to mine realm. Let no man say otherwise! For it is *mine* lands you tread upon.
I would see the spine that ferried thee so boldly into *my* lands.
Must thou choose a miserable end over serving thy count?
I would ask a hasty conclusion, should thou seek to avoid my bite.
What wouldst thou ask of me that is not laden with ignorant assumptions?
Speak plainly. I tire of games that I am destined to win.
I do not believe that thou receivedst an invitation to my lands…
Take care with what thou wouldst ask, for even to ask is most arrogant.
Greetings, thou stand before the rightful Elector of Stirland!
I shall not ignore the forms - talk, beast, then I shall kill thee.
Orcs! I shall hear it out, and then I shall feast upon its bones should its' words displease me.
What, Greenskin? I am immortal and yet I have little time for thy guttural tones.
I have no interest in these green beasts, their blood tastes foul and they refuse to be dominated.
Talk to me beast, spit out thy base demand.
Greenskins! I have witnessed thy kind many times before, what could thou possibly offer me?
Call down thy Blood God so I may taste his veins for myself!
Why should I allow thee freedom when blood flows freely by mine own hand.
Dost thou wish to know whose blood drains the fastest?
Thou couldst reap infinite blood, as a servant of death.
Serve. Or I will enslave every other man, until you are alone against Chaos.
Serve. Or be brought unto Undeath, where thy gods will forsake you heathen.
I could free thee from a life of obligation, protecting the ungrateful against Chaos…
Take care with thy curt tone, mortal.
I only awakened thee to show that someone had surpassed thee!
I am not above using Chaos to end thee!
Bow, now, for I have mastered thy power in thine absence. And surpassed it.
Trade me that which cannot be found in thy texts – for I have mastered them all!
Even death would reject thy rotting corpse.
Rot eventually withers, fool, and all that will be left are thy bones.
Death is only joyous for its master, for all will be slaves to my will.
Corpses only hold mine interest when they are malleable…
You forget thyself, mortal. I am a von Carstein! THE von Carstein. Thou will learn to respect that name, as thrall to my will!
Thy words are as meaningless as thine miserable life!
So careless, so insignificant - that is what you are to me, mortal insect! I refuse thy insolent offer.
Ha-ha-ha, you think me dense, perhaps? Do not underestimate me… others have and paid with their souls.
The curse of my kind - I talk and negotiate with my food! Would men bargain with cattle? I think not.
I have heard what you have to say. I reject it, as I do all wants and desires of the living.
Alas, with the blood moon hanging so low in the night sky… I must refuse.
You would do well to withdraw…
No, mortals are so impatient. Consider thyself chastised.
Plague may not kill me, but that does not mean I must suffer it!
Do not think to flee through thy tunnels. I have walked them before. I know every turn.
I would hear from that which plagues the Empire.
A plague upon the living and the dead alike.
Were I to follow unbridled desires,  you wouldst already be enslaved in death.
Thou shalt find but hollow joys in my domain of death.
Mistake not my courtesy for curiosity. Thou canst not comprehend immortal desires.
Such willing slaves, until death becomes part of the bargain…
Thou art a curse upon eternity! One whose presence I intend to purge.
Prostrate thy feeble bones before thine emperor!
Return to thy tomb and seal thyself away.
Thy only use, minion, is to serve the ancients.
Fool! That thou comst to intervene in fate, means I have the advantage!
Your schemes crumble at the gates of death, for I am the lord of this domain!
Scheme at thy peril, for I carve mine own fate.
It is no surprise that a strategist seeks my superior council.
Now is not the time, for petty politics, mine brothers, mine kin! Any who defy mine will shall be destroyed!
Come, but do not assume that as we share a blood line thou shalt not be shackled to mine will!
Greetings, kin, mine will dominates here, do not mistake this parley for anything else!
Thou wish'st to entwine hordes? As head of the dynasty it shall be mine to command.
Fellow beatless hearts, let us discuss the destruction of the living, yes?
My kin, I am pleased thou attend'st me.
I am Lord and master, thou acknowledge this with the sundering of thy minions to me!
Let us make a bond on this, but I warn thou, to defy me will be thy greatest mistake!
We have agreement, but make no mistake who leads this host!
All fall beneath my will, thou are simply ushering in the inevitable.
Yes, together our tireless legions will ensure Sylvania's expansion.
Good, we share the spoils - the wide-eyed cattle - between us.
I am Mannfred, the greatest to bear the name von Carstein, thy host is insignificant to me!
From the afterlife, even Nagash trembles at my name - do not think thou can challenge me. The mortals are all mine!
I think not, the death-tally will be mine and no other kin or Necromancer can claim it!
Fools! You are mere dabblers in death, I am Mannfred von Carstein, Morr's realm is mine!
No - my stock is superior, I do not wish to taint it with inferior pawns.
Our goals suffer. Go, but best not cross my path again. It would prove thine downfall.
Don't forget whose lands you tread.
Wise to ask and not command.
Mine ancestors will watch over this.
Another piece of thy soul, lost.
I doubt thy gods smile upon initiative.
It will pass in the blink of thine eye.
I presume I have made many a grudge for you?
Mortal alliances are much the same.
Thine emperor bestows thee this honour.
A Count must spare time for charity.
Take care to contain thy blood.
I will gladly aid in the humility of man.
Thou cannot resist death like the cold.
I can only imagine thy hand was forced.
So be it, dread master of death.
Since I am immune to plague.
Dost thy beast brain comprehend what you asked?
I am surprised this would please thy master.
A generous offering to thy king.
Death is all that unites us.
Attempt to trick me at thy peril.
Yes, we have a pact, but do not interfere in my affairs…
Agreed, though there is an imprudent streak in you. Perhaps I shall have the Crypt Ghouls beat it out?
Yes, sign your precious parchments - as if it means anything to me!
I agree - now the delicate issue of remuneration… it won’t be something as crude as gold that I need.
That is what we agreed. Now leave me to my works.
We have a deal. Prepare the tombs, I require ingress.
Very good, you will not regret this - you'll see!
Yes, this is the right course of action - my servants will start preparations right away!
What demands are you to make, envoy of a fettered king?
Make your offer, then go and tell the Enchantress-hag her nation is dead!
Come Bretonnians, tell me, what can you possibly offer this humble conjurer?
I'll hear what you have to say, only when I'm ready Bretonnian!
So, Bretonnian, I am here, are you ready to make a pact.
I'm glad you are here, Knight, we can work together but my price is your low-born.
Yes, your puppet-king will surrender to me!
The terms are signed, you cannot back out of it now - watch your country wither!
Very good - once you have come round to my way of thinking, you'll realise that this is the right course.
Ha! Those pesky morals, eh? Yes discard them, or hide behind some greater 'chivalrous' notion!
Yes, Bretonnian, we shall work together. There are so many crypts, so many barrows in your lands!
Good, Morr is weak in your nation. We have agreement.
You have nothing, Bretonnian. What could I possibly want in your foetid mudhole of a country?
Fair Bretonnia is fair no more - tell the lake hags that I will take what I need!
No, Bretonnian, that water sprite you claim as a god takes against honest folk such as I.
A kingdom of fools is soon separated from the lands to which it lays claim.
I don't think so. Your king doesn't appreciate my arts. Ask those in Mousillon.
No… I am busy elsewhere, Bretonnia holds nothing for me.
Very well, tell your Everchosen we have a deal. If he betrays me, we'll see how chosen he truly is.
So be it, Northman, but my rights to the dead are sacrosanct!
I ascent to your demands, Chaos creature, but my soul is mine own to damn - you cannot claim it.
Good - my tireless hordes are at your disposal - you have my fee?
Yes, start your killing, Northman, but leave the bodies for me!
Good, the pact is signed. You may have my soul of course - not that it will ever leave this body!
Archaon 'the ever-fool', does that not sound a more accurate title? I'd agree if you wish to flatter me into an alliance? Yes?
I will hear your grovelling pleas 'get of spawn' but you have no power over me!
So Chaos-minion, you come to parley with life-givers and dead-takers, you must need something?
Go on then, deliver your Gods' message - but remember, threats won't work against me.
Chaos, I admire your Gods, although they are too focused on capturing souls when the vessels have far more use.
Well, well - what could such powerful figures as yourselves want with me and my humble arts?
I have no time, nor will I, to entertain Chaos scum. Go away!
Be gone, Chaos spawn, or I will turn you to dust!
I think not, tell Archaon to find another pet Necromancer!
No, and your attempts at intimidation are laughable, really.
No, Chaos, I have masters feared more than yours could ever be.
No - I serve other, more powerful beings. Death holds no fear, I crave it!
Well, well, so the Dwarfs do swallow their pride when they need to? What a delightfully bitter pill, yes?
A Necromancer saving the Karaz Ankor. Ha, I bet this really sticks in your craw, Dwarfs.
We have agreement - I take it you do not wish for the rest of the Karaz Ankor to know?
A fair exchange of goods, but do not threaten me again, Dwarf or I'll see you as a shambling lackey.
I accept, Dwarfs. I'll need access to your crypts, of course.
Good, then we can begin. I require Runelore.
Stick me in your pitiful little grudge book, Dwarfs. See if I care! You'll pay the price either way!
No, Dwarfs, no - the only bargain to be made now is when you beg for the corpses of your kin!
I don't need your baubles or promises Dwarf. It will be all there to take in time.
Go and cower in your mountains, Dawi, my legions will come to your door soon enough.
I think not, you Dwarfs have such a temper.
No stunted creature, I have no interest in your… kind.
What, Dwarfs? Should I animate your ancestors and have them hack off your beards?
I find your persistence tiring, stone-gatherer, perhaps a display of my power will get the respect I deserve!
Ahh, bearded folk, are you not blind, do you not see your domains are surely doomed?
Hail Dwarf! Times must be desperate indeed for Grudgebearer and his ilk to send his peons my way!
No need for Reikspiel, Dwarf, I speak perfect Khazalid, how else would I raise your kin back from the dead?
Stunted folk, your race is thin on the ground of late, perhaps I could help?
Do go on - threaten me with Helborg or Schwarzhelm's wrath if you must, it makes no difference.
Such insolence, do you think your pitiful lost god can save you? Utter your message and be quick!
Poor Sigmarite fools, I almost feel sorry for you, almost…
Ha! You think making pacts with Daemon-spawn is dangerous, Reiklander, I have yet to state my terms…
The Empire, bah! Such nuisances with your Witch Hunters and your Priests of Morr!
Greetings, envoys of Ulric and Sigmar, I trust you haven't come to kill me - yet - then what do you want?
Fine, but I'll slay any of Morr's priests that I see skulking around my domain.
Good, you accept the inevitable, that is the first step in your nation's doom.
Very well, but tell the Grand Theogonist to rein in his Witch Hunter dogs.
Agreed, but I'll need assurances that some Sigmarite fool won't blunder in to ruin it!
Very well - you have my list of requirements, just don't tell the Witch Hunters.
We have a pact then, Sigmarite. Good, good. I assume that the Theogonist knows nothing?
No, the Empire will fall - Franz's corpse will be mine willing servant!
I think not! The Heldenhammer is tarnished, the reign of the dead begins!
No, Empire fools, close your Gardens of Morr if you must, the tombs will still open for me!
Foolish mortals, do not trouble me with your earthly concerns!
No, I know your sort. You'll betray me to the Silver Hammer!
I think not, Reiklander. My arts are for my own gain and no-one else's!
Come then, Orc, send your hordes and I will deign to bring you prey.
Yes, creature, but raise your crude blades to me and I'll see you wither before mine eyes!
Yes, it will be a challenge, but I can work with such crude materials I suppose.
Accept the terms, Orc, then the reign of terror will begin!
Yes, yes, we shall work together, I only ask that you don’t mutilate the bodies too much.
Agreed. Sign in blood, Orc, and we will begin.
Leave me, creature, or you will be returned as Crypt Ghoul fodder.
Gah! Get out of my sight, Orc, or your armies will be nothing but ashes in the foetid winds!
No, beast, you will not interfere with my plans.
What kind of sorcerer do you take me for? I have no use for your… offer, Greenskin!
No, your crude bodies hold no interest for me, Orc.
I'm afraid not, beast, your kind offer no challenge.
What? Who dares disturb my great works!?
It is a imbecilic thing to bother me - others who have, end up as my puppets!
Speak now, then go, or my Zombies will pull out your tongues!
Is this what you truly want, mortal - my gift or my wrath?
Hmm, there are possibilities here, oh yes - but first we must negotiate.
Salutations! We have an issue don't we? Perhaps I can resolve it for a cost we can both agree on.
Greetings, let me rid you of those corpses that crowd your fields and cemeteries.
Oh dear, that smells like grave-rot - an unfortunate disease - perhaps I could supply a cure?
No, I'm not dead, my heart still beats. But am I mortal? Well, that's a different question entirely!
So, Orc, speak quickly! The grave-bound call to me, I have no time for you.
Make an offer but if I don't like it, I'll have your skin sloughed from your bones by Banshee screams.
So, Orc, what have you to barter?
Have your feeble gods sent you, Orc?
Orc, I find my peers can be very scathing about your kind, but not I. After all, a body is a body…
Welcome to my abode, Greenskin, does Mork - or is it Gork - bring you to me?

You are no player of the Game.
The Dark Prince and The First Prince together.

Still, this will not end well.
You would make a good minion.
The Dragon is a shrewd one.
There may be hope for Cathay yet.
Now leave before I change my mind and kill you.
We can agree, Chaos knows best.
Craftily done. You should serve me instead.
We are in accord, my rival.
You have power, but no wisdom.
There is no kinship between us.
Send thanks to the Murder King.
I never could depend upon Kislev.
When Chaos finally engulfs you, I will be at the helm of it!
Cathay's denizens are destined to endure eternal torment!
The Father of Darkness makes fools of you, and I will make corpses.
I have yet to decide whether I will enslave you or just kill you.
There can be but one of us. It will not be you!
You! The inferior Daemon Prince. Know that I am supreme.
You are nothing to me. Nothing!
The only interaction between us I will permit is to crush you beneath my heel!
I will put out your eyes. I will rip out your tongue. I will drink your soul.
All this world will blacken and die. You and your followers are not excluded.
There is but one fate for all who oppose me: consummate annihilation!
I will subject you to a panoply of torments! You will beg me for death!
I am elevated beyond mortal pleasures, but I will take joy in your destruction.
All other lives are brief and pitiful against mine; yours will be more so.
You are here to die a slow, agonising death. There can be no other explanation.
Youl! When this world burns, I will place you atop the pyre.
Hated skull-takers! Forever underfoot during my crusade of conquest.
I will grant the Murder God's legions a taste of their own brutal medicine!
Most deluded and despicable of this world's people! I will destroy you!
Kislev. I no longer sleep, but if I did, I would dream of its annihilation.
Your pestilent interference enrages me! Make amends or know destruction!
A mere plague minion dares disturb me? I will have your rotted hide!
I will feed you to your Great Maw, then I will consume your Great Maw!
I will turn you inside out, brute! You will devour yourself!
Foolish Slaaneshi! Crossing me is a transgression you shall ever regret!
You think you understand pain. I will show you what agony truly means.
You will pay dearly for your tricks and treachery, changeling.
Send Tzeentch my regards once I have hurled you back to his Impossible Fortress.
I was once like your human form. Mortal and weak.
I yearn to put the Dragons' fabled immortality to the test.
Do you come to find a new idol, Daemon-worshippers?
Hashut's gifts are no secret to a Daemon. You are outmatched here.
We may co-operate, though ultimately only one Godling can prevail.
Lend your dark powers to mine, that together we might subjugate this mortal realm!
You are in the presence of unimaginable power. Kneel!
I will visit eternal torment upon all who dare oppose me. You have yet to do so.
What request would you make of a God-in-waiting?
The petty concerns of your existence are far beneath me, but I will listen.
Come, tell an immortal of your meagre aspirations.
Diplomacy seemed so very important when I was mortal. Now…
I presume you seek to survive this world's annihilation. Give me cause.
Whatever could one so... ephemeral possibly have to offer an eternal being?
You may aid me in the extinction of this thrice-cursed world if you so wish.
You cannot comprehend the extent of my dark power. Choose your words wisely.
We can surely find common cause in ours missions of destruction.
I have only respect for your fathomless blood-thirst, Khornate.
There is none so wretched or deluded as a mortal of Kislev!
Know this, Kislevite: your prized Motherland is built upon a lie.
What tribute does the Fly Lord intend to pay to me today?
Decay I can take or leave, but destruction? That we can agree on.
To think I once feared the Ogres. You are so small to me now.
Perhaps the ravening Ogres can be of use in my Ruinous crusade…
Subjecting the denizens of this world to unspeakable agony is a noble calling.
Perfect Prince and Daemon Prince: perhaps together we can brutalise this world?
What malevolent new scheme has the Raven concocted?
No tricks if you will, changeling: a world's extinction requires no nuance.
Send the Fly Lord my respects.
Feast, brute, for you have done well.
When I am all-powerful, there will be a place for you.
Submit yourself to Chaos and perhaps you too can ascend.
Better to be by my side than in my path.
You fight on the side of true power.
We shall go forth and obliterate in Godly glory!
Once I achieve true Godhood, you may serve me.
Let us lay the world to waste for the Dark Masters!
Though my power is unfathomable, I still need minions like you.
Keep paying your respects to me and few will dare oppose you.
Ask, but remember to whom it is that you speak.
Tell your Prince this Prince refuses.
I thought Tzeentch smarter than this.

Tretch has launched a surprise attack - back-stabbing is an art form!
The power of Nagash, emanating from his Black Pyramid, imbues your legion with endless energy and endurance.

Arkhan the Black is the first and most loyal of the evil Nagash's followers. Arkhan helped lead the coup which brought the arch-necromancer to power, and he was the first, after his lord, to imbibe the Elixir of Life.
Khalida Neferher, the Warrior-Queen of Lybaras, is highly respected across all the lands of Nehekhara. Her intelligence and bravery are as legendary as her intense sense of honour and justice.

Khatep is the Grand Hierophant of Khemri, the head of the Mortuary Cult's hieratic council, and he alone knows all its secrets and unwritten lore. Khatep is the oldest and wisest of all the Liche Priests and the first member of their order to truly deny death's embrace, if not the ravages of time.

Settra the Imperishable is the king of all Tomb Kings. He is a ruthless leader whose thirst for conquest knows no bounds. Settra's power is far greater than any other Tomb King, and his unyielding will is such that he never needs to return to his sarcophagus to rest.
This building shall not fall. We shall see that it is restored.
What need have we of water? The sand is our source of our sustenance and power.
Make it happen - we will continue to use these waters.
I am sure we can spare some extra bodies to ease the Liche Priests' burden.
The Liche Priests' work is for the benefit of all Nehekhara - give them all the resources they require.
Our restored buildings will produce ever-greater troop numbers!
Our lands will shine once again with the wealth and prosperity!
Let's see how he views the concept of loyalty one thousand years hence!
In the final analysis, he is our servant; he will feel an overwhelming urge to obey!
There are bigger lizards to fry than this pathetic band. Onwards!
How convenient! These sacrifices were just waiting for our arrival - fetch the altar!
There are always more bones to be unearthed and reanimated…
No matter the order, our troops obey to the bitter end and beyond.
Although the source of this sphinx's power is unknown to us, its strength cannot be denied!
Those gods banished from our pantheon were exiled for good reason, we cannot risk their return to this plane of existence.
We have no need for mortals, who require care and sustenance beyond the binding spell. They won't make it out of the desert alive.
Alive or dead, it matters not. These creatures will serve us one way or another.
Those troops in the service of a Tomb King should march with him into the afterlife, forever at his side.
Your Liche Priests have been greatly improved!
Your Necrotects have been greatly improved!
Your Tomb Princes have been greatly improved!
The Bretonnians will pay dearly for such mistakes.
This liquid concoction is more effective than it looks!
The sky will turn black when our arrows are loosed as one!
It has to be a mistake! This cannot be all there is!
These jungles hold untold secrets, if you are bold enough to search for them!
The desert giveth and the desert taketh away. It is the order of things.
Reminders of their former lives induce rage in our Unliving Lords.
These armies will be stopped dead before they even embark!
Those strong horse bones will improve our cavalry no end!
These ancient writings contain knowledge yet untold.
Your warriors relish the opportunity to do battle with the Bretonnian dukedoms.

Phakth is pleased with his tribute. As the knife strikes home and the Norscan exhales his last, a glow suffuses Settra's troop, and a bright beam pierces the firmament, highlighting a point of land far-distant. A Liche Priest produces a map and marks the destination.

The Liche Priests bend to their work. As the Norscan is swiftly denuded, he babbles the source of his wealth: Ice Tooth Mountain. His outsized skeleton is soon back on its feet; it is an impressive specimen indeed. Settra commands it to lead the way to the resting-place of his crown.

The new labourers toil under the Necrotects' whips. In time, Settra walks the path to the King’s Valley, where mighty statues of the gods, and kings of dynasties past, stand in eternal splendour. And towering at their head, Settra himself: a gleaming vision of polished marble, studded with glinting jewels and gold filigree. The tribute is a fitting one; Settra is pleased. The Necrotects and their new charges have served him well. He commands their deployment across his burgeoning new kingdom.
Word of this new wonder has spread throughout the kingdom. The denizens of Nehekhara feel pride, something they have not felt in an age. Settra rebuilds! Nehekhara will be made glorious again!
Across the lands of Nehekhara the sands lay still and the great cacophony of battle is silent for now. Victory is yours!
All will feel the strength and beauty of Alarielle – the bodies of those who dare defy the Everqueen will be pierced by her sheer radiance!
Nothing shall move the Shadow King, not even the wailing, screeching attacks of the Crone.
To stand as the Witch King's executioner is to reach into the black heart of every Dark Elf and squeeze!
With the death of Morathi, an age of enlightenment shall spread across a land once draped in shadow.
Peace is achieved only when there's nothing left to kill!
The Shadowlands has a new enemy; the king must act and cull the threat before it festers into war.
The Shadow King will do anything to protect his realm. His warriors have learned of a threat that needs silencing.
Peace when the Druchii still breathe? Not for the Shadow King!
War or peace - it matters not, a Druchii is always a viable target. The less of their treacherous kind exist, the safer Nagarythe will be.
Loec’s ravens squawk the name of another of Malekith’s minions to slay. Their time can be measured in mere moments from now on.
War comes and the Shadow King shall be at its forefront.
Those who provoke the Shadow King to war surely do not value life, for they will be deprived of it soon enough!
Although a High Elf, Anar does not play by the same rules as his noble kin; war is not just fought on the battlefield.
Alith Anar's gruesome reputation spreads amongst the Dark Elves!
Loec, the God of Deadly Dances, has given Anar a name - a Dark Elf whose own dance should end, war or not.
The only good Druchii is a dead one. To aid the war, Anar must hunt once more; now he knows the identity of his prey.

A loud word, spoken in court, should be enough to silence their rudeness. At least for now.
Caledor are powerful and mystical; they must be placated.
Sycophancy is enraging. The Phoenix King shall have no part in it!
Ellyrion are fine cavalrymen and loyal; do not do them a disservice.
Cothique is the first line of coastal defence; do not let them wallow in insignificance.
The Yvresse struggle is never forgotten, and their garrison aided at any cost.
At court, the Phoenix King decries both as working against the unity of Ulthuan, hoping to shame them into silence.
What they do in the shadows is their own business.
What the King hears, and when, is irrelevant. Supreme authority is his, always!
Although unorthodox, the Phoenix King can move through court alone with a personal touch. Undermining the seneschal neuters his power elegantly.
Tell him without telling him - if he seals documents out of sight, the paper trail will soon reveal his corruption.
Let the court deal with the court's issues, and may the Mother guide him…
The boy will be told, sternly, and hopefully he will think better in future.
You played the game, and you got caught; too bad. Goodbye.
The Phoenix King demonstrates that he is above the games of court by publicly shaming this messenger.
Weddings are boring. The Phoenix King has no intention of attending.
Every Elven death is a tragedy. The Phoenix King feels compelled to say something.
The boy was a fool, and his death was justified. We shall not attend.
Promote unity by having the two rivals dance together.

A new training regimen for your Heroes teaches them to veil their intent beneath a sheen of civility. After all, a killer with the manners of a rabbit is the most dangerous kind. The chances of successful Hero actions have now improved.
The example you set is inspirational. The Heroes under your command are proud to carry out your will, and do so eagerly. The cost for all Hero actions has fallen.
“Looks like fish, tastes like chicken, you don’t know what you’ve been lickin’…”

A conclave of your generals has struck upon the notion of pressing popular musicians into military service. This has come as a shock to the performers in question, but has proved an instant hit with the troops and they’re marching harder than ever before. Army movement range has increased!
Your traders have excelled themselves! An over-abundance of quality building materials has appeared on the market, reducing construction costs.

The ferocious foreman of your logging operation has been applying the whip with unseemly zeal. Workers are vacating the camps en masse and timber production is dwindling, driving up the construction costs.

The cheap, brittle mortar in your production centres is showing its age. Repair crews have been dispatched but the remedial work is disruptive, and income from your buildings has suffered as a result.

A thaumaturgist in one of your provinces has been tasked with squeezing greater profit from industrial processes. Lost in thought one day while inspecting a smelting plant, he slipped and plunged into the roiling slag. His death was not in vain however, as the smelters discovered that the introduction of osseous matter worked to strengthen the metal, raising its value; profits are up factionwide!

A charismatic soothsayer has impassioned the locals in this province with his doctrine of vigorous procreation. While the population is sharply rising, an exhausted workforce is a not a productive one.
This army has undertaken a rigorous new training regime focused on frontline combat, yielding excellent results. All units now have improved melee attack capabilities.
You have instituted defensive training for this army's troops, teaching them to better anticipate incoming blows. All units now have improved melee defence capabilities.
Conflict in a nearby region has driven the inhabitants into your territory. This has greatly increased local tensions, but represents a rich source of cheap manpower for their armies.

New targeting techniques have been introduced to your armies' training regimens, teaching the troops to focus on the enemy's weak points. Damage from missile weapons has increased factionwide as a result.

A recent clutch of reports regarding ill-discipline in the lower ranks is cause for concern. Clearly, clods are being hired - this has to stop! Recruitment costs have risen accordingly, but new recruits begin two ranks higher.

A caprice of nature or something more sinister? Either way, this unusually long spell of bitter weather is taking its toll on your armed forces. Replenishment is down, but the appeal of guaranteed rations means new recruits are clamouring to join up, driving down recruitment costs.

Seeking the gift of regeneration, an imprudent cabal of young magic-users has been dabbling in Ogre gastromancy. But disaster strikes, as they inadvertently summon the Great Maw itself! Smacking its lips with delight at the banquet laid out before it, the Maw devours the hapless sorcerers where they stand and disappears with a satisfied belch. This arcane upheaval has sapped the Winds of Magic factionwide!

A microscopic fissure has opened between the material world and the Realm of Chaos. It is a fleeting event, quite beneath the notice of even the gods, but potent enough to invigorate the Winds of Magic power reserve.

The Great Warding teeters on its axis and weakens for a moment. Before it recovers, the Winds of Magic burst forth in a  tumultuous gyre around your army, greatly boosting their power reserve but increasing the likelihood of miscasts.

The last Cold One spawning yielded a rare strain, gifted with some notion of your venerable race's plight in their tiny brains. These beasts are so eager to fight for you that they barely need taming, and their urgency means that friendly infantry must trot to keep up. As a result, recruitment costs for Cold One cavalry units have fallen and army movement range has increased factionwide.

A bitter blood-feud between two lieutenants in this army - one feared and respected, the other universally loathed - has been swiftly dealt with. Perhaps too swiftly, for in his rage, the wrong Elf was slain. As a result, the army's leadership has fallen and recruitment costs have risen too.

A highborn Lord of Ulthuan has been captured along with his honour-guard. Naturally, they are being paraded around this province in chains before their inevitable - and exquisitely slow - public execution. The local inhabitants are ecstatic at this delicious turn of events, resulting in local improvements to control and army leadership.

Uncommonly clement weather has driven the gargantuan denizens of the seas further north, resulting in an easy season of raiding and pillaging across the ocean for the reavers. Now, the streets of Karond Kar throng with fresh slaves, ripe and ready to be distributed around Naggaroth. Due to this influx of fresh labour, building costs have decreased factionwide.

A Cold One breeder, reputed for his voracious pit-fighting animals, has exploited his trade-contacts to acquire certain rare fungi used by the Night Goblins. Thus dosed, his enraged creations are unstoppable against regular stock. In fact the compound is so effective than none will now bet against the beasts; there's just no sport in it! The pit-owners refuse to field them and sales have fallen off a cliff, so the breeder has offered you his surfeit of reeking 'shrooms. The answer, quite obviously, is "Yes!" Duly dosed, his Cold One units now have enhanced melee attack capabilities factionwide.

Crone Hellebron has ordered Death Night be extended by two further nights this year. The streets of Har Ganeth are awash with blood and viscera as its inhabitants release their pent-up, year-long furies in a breathtaking orgy of bloodletting. As a result, Death Hag and Witch Elf recruitment costs have fallen, and their starting experience level has increased.

A fashion for devising new and more exquisite forms of torture has developed among the lower ranks, and they are practicing it every chance that they get! A tongue under duress may reveal many secrets, after all. As one might expect, the income from raiding and sacking has increased factionwide.

Following successful raids on key targets in enemy lands, a number of enemy intellectuals have been 'acquired'. With a little persuasion, their skills and experience have been harnessed - they have been put to work improving the level of technology available to you in order that he might score further victories over the hated foe and bring about rightful Druchii supremacy. Just as you intended, the rate of research has increased factionwide, and requiring very little effort from anyone other than the slaves, whose lot it is to suffer and die!

A sheaf of Elven architectural manuscripts dating from the reign of Caradryel have been discovered by your spies in the Old World. They detail techniques long forgotten, espousing principles so old as to be new again. As a result, building costs have decreased factionwide.

The earth is more ancient than the Elven race, and seems to favour your primacy. Perhaps it divines the gravity of the mission, and in turn reduces its own, for their troops find marching is easier and less tiring than was previously the case. Campaign movement ranges have increased factionwide as a result.

One of this army's lieutenants has attempted to curry favour with his captain using the largesse of his family's estate. The offer turned sour when the captain, looking more deeply into his subordinate's background, discovered his house to be a distant ally of Morathi. Publicly denouncing the Lieutenant - who has since left the service - should have worked, but the army's reputation has been harmed beyond immediate repair. Army leadership has fallen, and recruitment costs have risen as a result of this shame.

An exquisitely penned history of the Phoenix Lord Bel Shanaar has become widely popular. This artful blending of poetry and prose has caught the imagination of the people and has awakened within them a fresh hatred for Malekith and the foul betrayals of the Druchii. As a result, leadership and melee attack capabilities when facing Dark Elves have risen factionwide.

This province has declared a month of celebration in honour of the Everqueen. With poignant theatre, public dances, contests of wit, great feasts and a host of other cultural events. Hearts are lightened and the cares of the world fall way, if only briefly - for now, control and army leadership have risen in this province.

In a expression of deep and abiding respect for their winged mounts, a detachment of Phoenix Guard has journeyed to the Shrine of Asuryan, and performed a ritual to Aqshy, the Wind of Fire. Thus invigorated, Aqshy blows hard and fierce, in turn suffusing the Flamespyre Phoenixes with a newfound vitality. Even the Frostheart Phoenixes are impressed with this gift to their younger brethren. As a result, Phoenix recruitment costs have fallen factionwide.

A mage wielding the Lore of Life has agreed to travel with this army, but on condition that he does not have step foot near a battlefield. He reserves his art for the aftermath and, while prevention is always better than cure, it's hard to argue with his results. Following his recruitment, this force now has an enhanced replenishment rate.

Many years ago an old and respected seer disappeared into the Dragon Spine Mountains. Trackers were sent and a rescue expedition assembled, but to no avail. He was given up for lost... until now. His recent reappearance at  Caledor has prompted great rejoicing, and it transpires he spent his time in deep communion with an ancient Star Dragon who, sensing a kindred spirit, taught him much about the world's hidden Warp. As a result, your research rate has increased factionwide.

A reputed Skink artisan has been dispatched to oversee construction work throughout your provinces. His guidance has highlighted where efficiency is lacking and savings may be made. Building construction costs have now decreased factionwide.

It is whispered that elements of this army once visited Quetza, the defiled city, and were irrevocably changed by what they saw. Such rumours have reached fever-pitch of late and the Slann would do well to quash them! This army now suffers low leadership and increased recruitment costs.
Fragments of an ancient tablet have been unearthed, chronicling matters from the age of the Old Ones. This is a cause for great celebration - both leadership and control have risen here!

A new decree has been passed, venerating the ever-vigilant Temple Guard. Performing displays of their peerless halberd mastery in the central plazas of the temple-cities, they swell with pride for their calling and your people are energised like never before. Temple Guard recruitment costs have fallen and control has risen factionwide as a result.

There are many veterans in your empire, employing the skills they learned through armed service in the civic sphere. Engineering, geology, cartography… these are noble and useful pursuits, but war beckons! Perhaps the time has come to re-acquaint them with their blades? Recruitment costs and starting experience have both increased factionwide as a result.

In pursuit of greater knowledge, the Skink Chiefs have been urging their artisans and engineers to meditate upon Ten-Zlati, the finder of the Lost Plaques, and to emulate his thirst for understanding. As a result, technology research rates have increased.

A battle-scarred Saurus Oldblood has come to your attention at the urging of the Mage-Priests. More feral than his brethren, he has a natural empathy with the great beasts of Lustria, who rally to him as one of their own. With much fasting and meditation, others are learning to commune in this fashion. As a result, recruitment costs for monstrous creatures have fallen factionwide.

Your trade supervisor has recommended slashing import duties at ports throughout the empire. Trade is booming as a result, and many Nobles approve of  this action, though it means less taxes for Elven coffers. As a result, influence has risen but port income has fallen, factionwide.

Faced with yet more bland rations, this army has turned to the dark practice of cannibalism... with the hearty blessing of its catering corps, of course. Now, once a battle has been won, limbs of the slain are being enthusiastically collected, salted and cured for the long road ahead, with the troops thriving on these most morbid of provisions. Replenishment rate and army movement range have increased as a result.

The clan's Warlock Engineers have found an ingenious use for their ailing slaves… bones are ground into a rich cement, making for an endless supply of mortar. Due to this most excellent development, building costs have decreased factionwide.

The slavemasters have been issued with a new style of lash coated with hundreds of tiny venomous barbs. Fearing its burning lacerations, the Skavenslaves are stepping up the pace. Naturally, army movement capacity has now increased factionwide.

Reports are rife of Rat Ogres, Hell Pit Abominations and other monstrous units devouring the Skaven around them without warning. Is this the work of some foul saboteur from without? A rival who seeks to upset your rule perhaps? As a result of this outrage, recruitment costs for monstrous units have fallen but growth has taken a factionwide hit also.

Scurrilous rumours regarding this army's quartermasters abound. They issue the worst weapons and armour, keeping the best for themselves; they skim the rations and worse yet whisper mockeries of the Great Horned Rat! The rank-and-file are restive, and it's becoming increasingly expensive to bribe newcomers into joining - army leadership is down, and recruitment costs have risen.

This province has seen record-sized litters in recent years and the population is booming. Packs of Skavenslaves and Clanrats swell and, as every young buck knows, there is strength in numbers. Both leadership and control in the province have risen as a result of this good news.

Torture detachments have been deployed across your armed forces. While the Clanrats troops scavenge for goods and provisions, they set to work on the local inhabitants, clawing the locations of secret stashes and caches from their hapless subjects. Raiding and sacking income have both increased factionwide as a result of this excellent plan.

The green Warp-glow of Morrslieb, the evil moon, waxes sick and bright above this army. The Clanrats are invigorated by its viridescent energies, recovering from their wounds and replacing their numbers more swiftly than usual. Army replenishment rate has increased due to the great, weird moon's baleful influence.

The Council of Thirteen has decreed that the Warlock Engineers must step up their research efforts - on pain of death! A breathtakingly grisly list of execution methods has been circulated, each devised by the twelve earthbound Council-members, the thirteenth being, simply, a sacrifice to the Horned Rat. Unsurprisingly, your research rate has increased factionwide!

A new form of directed explosive has been devised specifically for weakening walls. Your sappers have been trained to burrow deep beneath the foundations before placing the bombs for best effect. Few survive the perilous process but no matter, for these new weapons are proving highly effective.

Burrowing and delving deep beneath the Vaults, your miner-prospectors have unearthed a vast Warpstone geode, untouched since the Great Catastrophe! This motherlode is the richest source seen in many years, and Warp-technology unit recruitment costs have fallen factionwide as a result of this enormous boon.

Your silver-tongued traders are outdoing themselves; they could sell a beard to a Dawi and make it seem a luxury! Now, the holds of your trade-ships are packed to the gunwhales with exotic goods and levies are at an all-time high. As a result of this mercantile excellence, trade income has increased factionwide.

Morathi's entire existence has been one of scheming and manipulation. Who knows how many of Aenarion's darker deeds sprang from seeds she planted within his mind, or how the history of the Elves might have been different had he not taken her as wife?

Teclis is Tyrion's twin brother, but two more different siblings would be hard to find. Where the curse of Aenarion has yet to leave an obvious mark upon Tyrion, it has made his brother frail and caustic.

Prince Tyrion is the High Elves’ greatest living warrior. So valiant and skilled is he that the bards of Ulthuan sing that he is nothing less than Aenarion reborn - a tale that is given credence far beyond Ulthuan's shores.

Kroq-Gar is an ancient Saurus, the last remaining warrior from the now ruined temple-city of Xhotl. The spawning that brought him into the world also produced a handful of other Saurus, each marked for greatness.
Lord Mazdamundi is the oldest and most powerful of the living Slann Mage-Priests. At the Dawn of Creation, he was instructed by none other than Lord Kroak himself.

The Witch King is the supreme ruler of Naggaroth, and the eternal enemy of the High Elves. Long ago, he sought to claim Ulthuan's crown, but the Flames of Asuryan left him scarred by fire and twisted with hatred.

That Lord Skrolk walks the world is an affront to nature and a sign of the power of the Great Horned Rat. Plants wither and die where Skrolk treads, and the very air about him seems to congeal and darken, as if stained by his baleful presence.
As Right-Claw to Warlord Gnawdwell, Queek Headtaker has risen high within Clan Mors – a credit to the terrible violence he’s unleashed along the way.
It is as though the Old Ones themselves speed your troops to ever-greater victories over the foe… until they fall, and become abominations unworthy of their sacred legacy and the Great Plan.
Truly this material is a gift from the Old Ones - a bounty that will wipe the enemies of the Great Plan from this world! If only it had not been warped in the aeons since…
Such noble structures will stand while lesser buildings fall! Their swift construction will better serve the Old Ones' Great Plan for the world.
You attack unexpectedly, capture the required prisoners, and rip out their hearts. The magical currents surge; the Slann Mage-Priests smile; the Great Plan advances.
Your fearsome warriors lay into the enemy with gusto, even when it leaves them open to attack! Even losses are part of the Great Plan and further spawnings are always possible.
Courage must be tempered with caution or losses will ensue. After all, you never know when the Vermintide will rise or the Ancient Enemy burst forth from the Realm of Chaos once more.
Your Saurus warriors fight with bravery that fills you with hope, yet they also fall in great numbers before the foe.
Such research uses valuable resources - resources that could otherwise be committed to the Great Plan - but strengthens the Geomantic Web. A trade-off, then…
This advantage must be taken, even when it draws power from the world. The Great Plan is robust enough to survive a minor deviation such as this.
A strong army is essential to the Great Plan; your ranks swell with cold-blooded Saurus warriors, devoid of pity and mercy.
A Hero is worth a hundred ordinary warriors; you must choose Saurus or Skink and open battle versus the internecine war of subtlety and surprise.
The plaque is easily recovered, and the ritual successful; your Saurus Scar-Veteran will turn the blades of your enemies with even greater ease!
The weak, pandering Northmen are easy prey, and you recover what they have plundered with ease, expelling the tainted barbarians from Lustrian shores and back into the sea.
You are taking territory thought lost for many ages, and losing fewer Skinks essential to the Old Ones' Great Plan. Onwards!
The affiliates of the Ruinous Ones can no longer reach you, but you lose access to any artefacts or other items of use that may have served the Great Plan.
The Druchii did not expect their byways to be used against them; they retreat to their dark, barren homeland. However, Chaos' foul taint remains and must be scourged from the face of Lustria!
Like any cancer, Chaos' foul corruption must be cut out before it can spread. Replenish your forces later - a brand new spawning for the furtherance of the Great Plan!
More Saurus warriors are required to defeat the Ancient Enemy's foul taint. It is a shame they were not spawned earlier, for Chaos' foul corruption now blights your lands and must be forced back!
Many Skinks are lost, but the pestilence is contained. The Great Plan has not been overturned and the foe's designs are thwarted this day.
Skinks with skills of great use are saved, but the foulness spreads - Pestilens' takes a giant skitterleap toward victory and the Great Plan suffers a setback as a result.
Warriors, not workers, issue forth, ready to battle the forces of corruption! The Great Plan will take time to come to fruition, but they who threaten its progress are here now!
The spawnings follow the Great Plan. All things happen for a reason and the Skinks have their part to play: society must not grind to a halt!
Your efforts pay off, although focusing your resources thus takes it from your grand Saurus armies and risks their strength against the insidious foe.
Your army grows in accordance with Sotek's wishes, but the benefits to the Great Plan that will surely be gleaned from these advances must wait.
Averland's Marius Leitdorf is noted as a peerless warrior, but also for his lunacy (for which he is known as the "Mad Count"), poor manners and inappropriate, louche humour.
Count Aldebrand Ludenhof is a man of far greater stature than his small, relatively-unimportant province. Tall, thin and immensely strong, he is at least a match for much larger opponents.
Middenland’s Grand Duke Boris Todbringer is as good a statesman as he is a warrior, known for his deft political operating and single-minded pursuit of the foul Beastlord Khazrak.
Theoderic Gausser is known as the “Terror of the Norscans” for his tenacious, brutal campaign against the northern marauders; he embodies his people’s warlike nature and fighting spirit perfectly.

Ostermark’s Wolfram Hertwig, the prideful, at-times-foolhardy Prince of Bechafen, is nevertheless a meticulous strategist, having cut his teeth battling and defeating the insidious Greenskins whilst still a teen.
The impressively-titled “Hammer of the East”, the vigorous, hardy Valmir von Raukov, is so named for his constant warmongering against the Trolls and Northmen whose territory borders his own.
Karl Franz, both the Emperor and Elector Count of Reikland, is more than just a courageous fighter and grand statesman – he is also a tactical innovator and a great patron of the arts and sciences.
On the literal bleeding edge of warfare, Solland’s Count Eldred is engaged in a constantly-raging conflict against Greenskin incursions from the Badlands to the south of his borders.

Albreich Haupt-Anderssen is a relatively-compassionate man considering the period in which he lives, and has devoted much of his time to easing the poverty and hunger of Stirland’s peasant population.
As well as being Elector Count of Stirland, Albreich Haupt-Anderssen is also Overlord of Sylvania, considering himself the main bulwark against the guileful advance of the dreaded von Carsteins.
The notoriously foul-tempered Helmut Feurbach of Talabecland is a whimsical, heavy-handed ruler who frequently finds himself at odds with his peers due to his poor judgement and irritating persona.
As the Empire’s principle trade hub, formerly-independent Marienburg is open to all merchants at all the hours the gods send; it is wholely “in the business of business”, according to its rulers.

Wissenland’s Elector Count considers the majority of governmental matters – including its people’s welfare – to be beneath them, concentrating instead on maximising production and profits from the Imperial Foundry at Nuln.

As the Great Vortex vacillates on its axis, the Winds of Magic fluctuate distressingly, eliciting wild-eyed portents of doom from hedge-wizards throughout your empire. The troops are cowed by these omens and leadership has decreased factionwide.
Risking Khaine's wrath to spare your troops does have some benefits.
Your forces are benefiting from a protracted period of good weather; rations are plentiful and there's a spring in the troops' stride. As a result, army leadership has increased factionwide!

There's some really fine pieces here! After taking a few that take your fancy, your warriors take their pick of the remainder. Pleased, they pledge to fight with renewed fervour.
Having seen you cherry-pick the best pieces for yourself, your warriors are less than impressed with the leftovers; the brittle blades break on impact and the shields splinter when touched.
Possibly, you've misjudged your allies - they scoff at the poorly made weapons and begin to question your integrity. Sometimes, a good deed is its own punishment.
Turning from the eggs you begin your search of the nest. At that point, the Dragon returns and attacks! You manage to escape relatively unscathed, but there is a huge rend in your armour.
It is apparent that you have stumbled upon an abandoned Dwarf brewery. Naturally, you take the Dwarfs intoxicating ale and hold a great feast to celebrate your conquests!
A rush of wind blows you backwards and there is a strange crackle in the air. You notice various runes around the room; this is a Dwarfen trap to nullify magic before it can be used against them!
Unfortunately, as soon as you prise the door open a powder keg explodes, throwing you backwards in the blast. Although the booby-trap failed to kill you, your wounds slow progress.
Ever cautious of Dwarfen ingenuity, you gently push the third door open. Inside, you find a store room bursting with valuable trade goods that can be sold or bartered.
The armour is indeed the work of a master armourer, and it's surprisingly light too. Your retainers have no problems recovering it from the flooded vault.
Using a series of controlled demolition charges you are able to create a new chamber to drain the water away. The plan works flawlessly and you recover the high quality armour fully intact.
As your men begin their search, there is the sound of giant gears whirring into life. The entrance to the vault is suddenly blocked by a huge boulder!
It doesn't take too long to find someone with the power and will to cleanse the taint of Chaos. They safely purge the basement, as well as several other nearby relics.
You employ a supposed 'expert' to cleanse the shrine. However, the charlatan does little more than set it on fire and demand an extortionate fee!
Although you resist the corruption of Chaos, others in your party are not so strong. Weaker minds are drawn to its power and are soon prostrate before the altar, praying to Slaanesh.
The power of Slaanesh is hard to resist. A tide of twisted thoughts and desires fills your head and you soon find yourself bent in prayer before the shrine of the Dark Prince.
The tracks are confusing and double back on themselves several times. In the bewilderment, you get turned around and eventually lose the trail altogether.
Surprised by and failing to recognise you, they listen and agree to trade some of their excellent-looking weapons for supplies. The equipment turns out to be of superior quality.
Providence has brought you here to silence these agitators afore they can act! Their screams fill the air as the barn burns to the ground. Your people feel much safer in their beds.
You take the rebels completely by surprise. Overwhelmed, they surrender and turn over their weapons in return for their miserable lives. Naturally, you have them killed anyway.
Entering the barn, you challenge the survivors and a stand-off ensues. Enraged by your arrogance, they refuse to surrender. Rallying together, they defame you as a tyrant.
The Daemon tells the truth! Your warriors are all replenished by the healing properties of the tears. But of course, you always knew this boon would come at a terrible cost...
Obviously, Daemons of Chaos are not be trusted! Slaying the creature wipes the nauseating taint of its putrefaction from the ruins.
Cutting the foul, sickening flesh causes great gouts of pus and slime to gush forth, tainting the earth with its repellent corruption. Stand well back!
Whilst lifting the flaps of pallid flesh one of your retainers accidentally cuts the Daemon, causing great gouts of pus and slime to gush forth, tainting the ground with foul corruption.
The shrine goes up in flames, taking the rest of the building with it. Better safe than sorry - you torch the surrounding area also before moving on.
The shrine goes up in flames, taking the rest of the building with it. You torch the surrounding area also before moving on – better safe than sorry!
The shrine goes up in flames, but as the dust settles a ghostly figure rises from the ashes. This is not the result you had in mind...
Following a complicated ritual you are able to cleanse the shrine and remove the taint of the Undead from the room. You no longer have the feeling that you are under observation.
Following a complicated ritual you are able to cleanse the shrine and remove the taint of the Undead from the room. You no longer have the feeling that you are under observation.
You fight bravely but are soon overpowered by the Skaven's overwhelming numbers. They take care to ensure you are unable to follow them before disappearing.
Your experts are impressed by the Skaven's grasp of technology. This is ground-breaking stuff, revealing new manufacturing methods that could be used to your advantage.
You order your experts glean whatever they can from it. However, their time is wasted - nothing worthwhile is discovered and your citizens are disgusted that you brought such evil into their midst.
Whatever these Skaven intended, their feeble science is of little interest. The reclaimed materials are put to good use by your own artisans. There are no obvious ill effects... for now.
You have the machines melted down for your own purposes. However, the metals are laced with disease that quickly kills your artisans and spreads through your population.
After inhaling the fungus your retainers are full of vitality but a strange glint in their eyes reveals the cost of this new found strength. Time to enlist some new followers, methinks!
It's probably best not to take any chances. You flatten the patch, removing the temptation of Chaos from the path of any and all who pass by.
As your retainers stamp the patch flat the air becomes thick with spores. It isn't long before the taint of Chaos becomes apparent in their eyes and on their skin!
The second your blade touches the web, hundreds of smaller spiders swarm from the darkness, engulfing you and your party. All is lost!
The translator gives back the book, his hands shaking. He informs you that it is a tome of great import, the contents of which will change the way we view the world forever.
The translator informs you that the book is an ancient treatise on warfare, full of forgotten tactics. With the appropriate level of study, it could tip the scales in your favour.
As you delve deeper into the caverns you become helplessly lost, and members of your party begin to panic. Clearly, it will be some time before you see the sun again...
Amazed by your callousness, the survivors let out a string of curses as you walk away. They will all die, but it is too late to reverse the effects of their magical mischief.
Trapped, you resign yourself to a long wait - it is some time before a retainer triggers the same mechanism and releases you.
The runes explain how to open the door using the complicated mechanism. They also reveal how to construct said mechanism and others like it; Dwarfish secrets? Not for long!
You quickly remember that you have no idea how to read the runes before you, so escape by your own means seems unlikely. Your only option is to sit and wait for rescue.
You order your troops to attack from range. With impressive precision the Undead are taken down in one volley. This remarkable feat cheers the troops and improves their leadership.
Whilst you search elsewhere, rumours of the Undead presence spreads. Your people are outraged that you would place plunder above their safety.

The hated beard-things and hooded green-things fight above the City of Pillars, claiming it for themselves. It must be taken for Clan Mors, or risk a crippling loss of status at the Council of Thirteen.
Good-good! The pillar city, what the Dwarf-things call Eight Peaks, is Queek’s domain at last. Send the Clanrats forth to spray every chamber and tunnel in the urine-scent of Clan Mors.
This army is currently subduing the local population and maintaining order. Its ranks will not replenish during the next turn.
There is a normal amount of [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food available to the Skaven. The weak are starving and the strong are feasting - things are as they should be!
At the moment, there's plenty of [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food to go around and as a result the Skaven are becoming more numerous by the day.
The Skaven's [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food supplies are running low; those who aren't in a position to demand their share are going hungry.
There's almost no [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food to be found and the Skaven are in trouble: the masses are starving and the powerful are eating their underlings.
There is currently more than enough [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food for all Skaven to have their fill. For a change, even the poor among their number can afford to eat.
Gotrek and Felix have joined your cause! They will only remain for a limited time, however.

Rakarth's monstrous menagerie roams the world, stripping cities bare as efficiently as carrion stripped from a corpse.
The untempered and, above all, starving creatures of the Darklands are easily tamed by the promise of good meat.
Having emerged from the Darklands undigested, the Beastmasters have been granted time to recover.
Lustria’s mighty and prehistoric beasts may rule supreme within their jungles but are easily bent to the Beastlord’s will.
Having survived the hunt in the deep jungles of Lustria, the Beastmasters have been granted time to recover.
Naggaroth’s beast markets provide various creeds of Anath Raema’s savage children for the Druchii battle lines, some much rarer than others.
Following the long journey back to Naggaroth to haggle and intimidate, the Beastmasters have been given some time off.
The beasts that prowl the realms of men are much more than the fireside tales whispered within their feeble castle keeps.
Having scoured the Old World for monsters, the Beastmasters have been granted time to recover.
Even the most hardened Beastmasters need time to recover after witnessing the horrors of Dark Magic.
Druchii military dominance has oft been the result of the mysterious forbidden rituals subjected upon creatures reared within the Dark Convent.
While in Lustria, your Beastmasters made use of wild Cold Ones and discovered new techniques of controlling them.
A bit of bribery, blackmail and assassination has got you a line on some bargain beasts.
Morathi’s potent wards once given to the War Hydra Daerlythe are reproduced through the writ’s incantations, albeit with impermanent results.
Every step taken by this unsuspecting prey is being silently watched by hidden predators…
While the will of a cavalryman's horse is beholden to its rider, the Tiger Warrior's ways admit to no subservience where man and beast are concerned.
The Dragon Emperor rises above all else, unassailable to every threat. The cavalrymen who carry his mark are made to realise their own superiority to some of their foes.
Zhao Ming's alchemical inquiries have lent both horse and rider the unnatural power to carve and crush anything before them.
Even the most sharp-eyed archer's senses can be further improved by an additional one – that of the predator's lethal steadiness.
The Emperor expects perseverence under fire at all times - most especially from those who know how deadly this fire can be.
Should an archer's skill or their arrow's force fall short, the Iron Dragon's arcane fire imbues them with the power to finish the job.
Foot soldiers who have entered Bhashiva’s service, no matter their other virtues, must prove amenable to the Tiger Warriors' ways of war.
A reminder of where a Cathayan soldier’s ultimate duty lies and what conduct is expected of them, no matter their current allegiance.
Zhao Ming’s disquieting ways may fill some warriors with apprehension, but those regiments who have received his boon carry themselves... differently.
The explosive dance of servicing a cannon in the heat of battle requires as much instinct as it does discipline. This Insignia is worn by those in favour of the former.
The warriors thus marked require nothing but faith in the Emperor's protection and certainty in the wonders of Cathayan technology to persist in their destructive work.
Those versed in Zhao Ming's improvements to their battlefield contraptions prize careful work in favour of devastating results – just as he does.
The gunners in the Tiger Warriors' employ have exchanged their long-drilled battlefield discipline for nimble fingers and love for the thunderous roar of their weapons.
A poor position on the field leads to rash decisions and diminishes the art of war. This is unacceptable to any gunner, let alone those who carry the Emperor's Insignia.
The Iron Dragon is most partial to his rare alchemical substances. Their scarcity and unnatural firepower are best utilised by experts.
Tigers do not hunt vermin and neither does any mighty beast bearing Bhashiva's seal. The bigger the foe, the better they can assert their dominance.
The Compass turns with the Emperor's will. The magical beasts graced with his favour feel each turn in the Winds of Magic ruffling their fur and feathers.
To the Iron Dragon, magic is a tool – and any tool can be broken. The Celestial Beasts pledged to him carry with them the power to do so.
The earth speeds a predator's steps and feeds its springing leap. The Tiger Warriors have now repaid the favour to these creatures made of living earth.
Within creatures given life by the Emperor resides a core of magic, both precious and deadly. His seal warns of the dangers in trying to tear down His masterful creations.
Glittering with the Iron Dragon's Insignia, these constructs are a reminder of both the wonders and the inviolable nature of their master's sorcerous works.
Cathayan flying wonders of war are no mere statement of overwhelming strength, but a call to make the most of it. It is a call the Tiger Warriors have never refused.
With the Emperor's blessing, the navigators in charge fly their machines with masterful proficiency at their hands and the Winds at their backs.
With the Iron Dragon's arcane genius, means of destruction are always on hand. Cathay's flying contraptions of war provide the opportunity.
Both creatures of a dual nature, the shared affinity between Longma and Tiger Warriors is thus evident in attuning the mounts to their predatory insticts.
The Emperor's seal enlivens the Dragon blood of these mounts and holds their riders to the utmost rigours of discipline.
Though the line between life and death is sharply drawn, to a select few Zhao Ming has imparted a secret which can blur it.
