There are few ordeals more frightening to an Ogre than starvation and loss of weight. This warband is facing that fear right now.
An Ogre warband marches on its stomach moreso than any other mortal army. Being fed is barely the start; Ogre appetite can never be truly satiated.
This warband has its raiding sacks stuffed with delectable meat, yet their bellies rumble as ever for more and their eyes glint with unnatural hunger.
Gnoblars push carts overflowing with meat and grand feasts roast over bonfires; the warband celebrates, ceaselessly stuffing their maws. But it is not enough. It is never enough.
Ogres have set up camp here, supporting the local region. Any army within its circle of influence will be able to recruit units from the camp.
As much as Ogres love to wander, the Maneaters have taken to it as none of their brethren have – driven by bloodlust, wanderlust and lust for fame and wealth.
However Ogre mercenaries get their exotically disparate pieces of equipment, one can safely assume they rarely pay for it.
What is better than completing a job and getting paid? Getting paid before completing a job, of course!
Long-lived mercenaries are guaranteed to gain notoriety. This is doubly true for long-lived *Ogre* mercenaries, and especially Golgfag's.
As much fear an Ogre Tyrant's presence commands, those serving under Golgfag are even more fearsome when absent, for they *will* return, and they better find everything in order.
All the best earnings go to Golgfag's coffers. The rest goes to the Maw. Tradition is tradition.
Barging into the fray is a difficult habit to break. To Golgfag's mercenaries, however, there is an instinct yet more powerful: get it done, whatever it takes.
Sea-trade makes money. What Golgfag's mercenaries do could not reasonably be called trade, yet it makes money nonetheless.
Sometimes a job calls for it. Most of the time, Golgfag's soldiers pretend that it does and do it anyway. To him, it is yet another means to notoriety's ends.
A payday is never far off, yet Golgfag's moods in that regard are unpredictable. Meat after a fight, however, is always reliable. A Maneater has to eat.
Fight when the riches are worth the effort. Rest and revel when they are not. Both are key to maintaining morale among mercenaries, especially when they are Ogres.
The Ogres' enormous vigour is as ill-suited to constructive effort as it is good at causing destruction. The Maneaters' captives fill that role, before filling the mercenaries' bellies.
Golgfag's nose for gold is as good as they come, be it a coffer unaccounted for, a rug unturned or a body not shaken hard enough to spill some coins.
Strong mercenary companies by their nature consist only of proven warriors. Golgfag's Ogres are no exception, though often they are made to prove themselves against each other.
Everyone knows Golgfag will fight anyone for his prize. An underappreciated side of his skill is that he will also go anywhere, no matter how difficult the path.
Surviving amongst Ogres is a feat only Gnoblars have proven capable of. So capable, in fact, that the Maneaters have afforded theirs a significant degree of autonomy.
From the outside, it seems Maneaters are unusually merciful towards the enemies they have defeated in battle. In truth, they are simply prudent with their food supply.
Maneaters will never cease travelling, as long as they have the means to do so. Seasickness means nothing to a sturdy gut.
In their everyday life, Ogres make do with what they have on hand. In the Maneaters' case, it is the ruins left after a raid, and a keen eye for useful material.
Even the lesser Maneater companies have not deterred the ones seeking out the real deal, and a slice of Golgfag's wealth after a good payday.
Anything a band of Ogres can do, Golgfag's Ogres can do better, putting their guts to it in the name of the company's common purpose.
Under Golgfag, sometimes everyone gets paid, sometimes most, and sometimes only some. What is certain is that no one is allowed to complain, regardless.

The word of the Defender of Ulthuan carries far in noble circles, driving up support for your military endeavours.
The elite of your heavy infantry and cavalry ranks receive the mentorship of Eataine's best.
This settlement cannot be occupied by your faction.
The aftermath of the Marauders' pillaging still afflicts this region.
The sudden expansion of territory has caused instability throughout the land.
N’Kari’s persuasive words and alluring promises of riches and glory could sway even the most strong-willed.
This army recently pillaged a settlement and the force is in high spirits!

The Ruinous powers have sapped this foe's strength.
To see through the machinations of the Great Game is reward enough, for the world knows no dread keener than that born of an all-consuming tide of Chaos.
In time, the blessing of a Ruinous Power decays into affliction; for now, its gift is too potent to deny.

You have used your self-proclaimed distinction as King of all Trolls and Monsters to call upon the Monstrous Horde for your current offensive.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Call the Monstrous Horde is currently active. [[img:icon_kinfolk]][[/img]]Trollkind will not be accumulated until the duration ends, upon which all auxiliary armies will be disbanded.[[/col]]

Once, you were content with a simple life, using your unusual cunning and strategy to survive and reign over your own lands. But why simply hide in the snows of the north, when the south – nay, the world – lies there for the taking?

Your fellow Troll bands continue to be instinctively drawn to you, despite their usual dim-witted tendencies, steadily growing the sinister potential to provide the greatest assemblage of beasts and monsters ever seen.

Your drive and ambition have taken you far for the cause of the Troll, and indeed all monsters and beasts. The time steadily approaches for the Monstrous Horde to march for civilisation’s complete and utter subjugation!

The triumphs attained from your guile and cunning are beyond most of your kin, but you alone know that other Trolls don’t need intelligence, just a strong leader – a king – to unite their raw, unstoppable brawn into a world-shattering force of nature.

Your dim-witted kind may have once been propelled by their own hunger above all else, but your rise has kindled a greater purpose in them, stirring their beastly instincts to kill for something much more than just survival, but supremacy over all.

From numberless unseen labyrinthine lairs across the land – in wildernesses strewn with the frozen limbs and heads of half-chewed regents and emperors, alongside weapons, heirlooms and treasures pillaged from across their vanquished realms – plans long brooded upon have finally been brought to fruition!
Gather up the Spoils of this settlement and prepare some men to escort it to the nearest hoard!

Aislinn and his Dragonships have joined your faction. You will need Dragonship Supplies to support his fleet.
Imbibing the anguish of your thwarted Thralls, the Dark Prince reciprocates your gift, bestowing upon you a renewed zeal for domination.
Thralls are tasked to carry great mirrors through the halls, orienting them so Dechala can admire her twisted form.
Those who wish to rise above Thralldom are granted the chance to bloody themselves in ritual combat for the amusement of Dechala.

Tools and workshops find place within the great halls of the palaces, Thralls artifice until their fingers bleed on things small and large to impress Dechala. \\n Dechala, of course, denies all but the finest.
Those who serve are granted legions of attendants, butlers, and servants to serve their whims, freeing them from simple concerns. And placing a hundred eyes in service to Dechal at their back.

The endless halls of the pleasure palace are filled with themed balls and banquets, Thralls ordered to sing, dance and make merry day and night at Dechala's whims. The eternal feast ensnares those foolish enough to approach.
Groups of Thralls are instructed to wander the land near and fear to the palaces, spreading word of the pleasures within, bringing gifts and revelry that twist the mind and ensnare the senses.
Allows the fleet to disembark anywhere, ignoring cliffs and other impassable terrain.
Enables the construction of Dragonship buildings and the recruitment of units directly from the vessel.
Each territory that falls beneath Caledor’s Dragon-shadow unfurls another haughty banner in the ranks of its Princes, even when the lands are freely gifted.
Every realm embraced by Avelorn’s tender rule lengthens the Everqueen’s decennial pilgrimage, yet strangely, it is never delayed.
Steeped in ancient power, the kingdom of Eataine eagerly claims each province Aislinn bestows, ever striving for Asur domination.
No realm knows bitterness as does once-proud Nagarythe, nor do any Asur folk deserve more the sweet reprisal of fresh conquest.
It is said that knowledge expands horizons. By that same token, the broadened horizons of Asur dominion yield ever greater wisdom.
Legends tell that every land over which Yvresse holds sway, however far, may be glimpsed from the slopes of the Annuli – should one dare to climb its crags.

The highest levels of Favour with the Phoenix King cannot be reached until all of Ulthuan is under High Elven control.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]While the Patronage tab is selected, all regions under foreign rule are marked in red on the map.[[/col]]
Scouring the seafaring carrion – an affront to nature and order both – brings stability to the colony, a necessary stride towards restoring its true purpose.
Colonies have become the focus for Aislinn. Only through the overseas establishment of Ulthuan's way of life can the Sea Patrol prosper.
Aislinn is now committed to establishing new colonies where it best suits the Asur, so that their hand grows stronger abroad.
With the Sea Lord’s full dedication to Ulthuan’s colonial expansion, the supremacy of the Sea Patrol shall be unrivalled across all the seas.
Our Dragonships must be the focus – with their full capabilities, our power simply cannot be challenged.
Aislinn is committed to maximising the Dragonship fleet's potential, keeping the immense vessels at full operational capacity.
All enemies of the High Elves will soon know our dedication to the Dragonships is the Sea Lord's obsession. Through them, we rule the seas.
Aislinn’s focus on the Outposts highlights his belief that only a firm hand can oversee the Asur’s holdings abroad.
Commitment to expansion of High Elf territory for Ulthuan’s benefit has led to our Outposts growing in number, blossoming the trust of our Asur allies.
Demonstrating utmost dedication to our Outposts, the Sea Lord leads us assuredly into a new Golden Age of Ulthuan's next thalassocracy.
Like the craven vultures they are, pirates flee at the faintest scent of the Asur fleet upon the wind. But not this time…
Home to the Everqueen, the forests of Avelorn are a bastion of nature and life. The nobles of Avelorn concern themselves with the health and wellbeing of all Asur.
The glories of Avelorn are maintained only by the constant watchfulness of the Rangers that guard its borders – an attitude to be applied to all Ulthuan.
Just as it is with the Sisters of Avelorn in their sacrosanct lands, it is the duty of the powerful to ensure the length and breadth of Ulthuan's sacred shores remain pure.
The blind smiths of Caledor's Temple of Vaul are the greatest craftsmen of the Asur. Their teachings can reveal any secret – boon or flaw – of one's armaments.
To adopt Caledor's ethos, one must be equipped to make up for any haughtiness by taking on their foes head-on, reducing them to ruin with typical Asur disdain.
The destruction brought by the Dragon Princes is unmatched – if so inclined, they can bring to bear a Dragon's might to slice through stone and bring down any wall.
The regiments of Chrace can extend their logistical expertise to any battlefield within their claimed territory to quickly turn the tide of battle.
It is no wonder that the Phoenix King's personal guard is comprised of White Lions of Chrace, for the wilderness trains some of the mightiest and most loyal protectors of the Asur.
To be counted as a real hunter, an Elf of Chrace must kill a White Lion single-handedly, or else tame it to their service. The Lions, however, forever remain the true hunters.
Cothique is a realm of dour and hardy Elves, who pride themselves on their strength of endurance, tempered against the harsh environment of the unforgiving sea.
The first defence of Ulthuan is not its spear or archer regiments, but the Asur who take to the sea to form the fighting crews of its mighty fleets.
Not all spirits haunting the lost grottoes and passages of Cothique's palaces are inimical to Elven presence, and can be harnessed by those granted the secrets of this realm.
Eataine is the center of political power, commerce and faith on Ulthuan. The nobles of Eataine value firm authority and prosperity above all.
Foreknowledge of their death makes the Phoenix Guard fearlessly formidable, their loyalty to Lothern and their King even more so.
The Shrine of Asuryan is the burning alabaster heart of Ulthuan's capital. This sacrosanct space is what fuels the power of the island's Phoenixes, and safeguards them.
The Horsemasters of Ellyrion are the most capable mounted warriors on Ulthuan. Life on horseback has made their nobles experts in pathfinding and speed.
Ellyrians are bold by nature and training, most effective when their recklessness is encouraged by those who understand what has made them this way.
Silver Helms usually strike the perfect balance between the Dragon Princes' aloofness and the Reavers' wild energy, but the call of Ellyrion could persuade them towards the latter.
Those who dwell in the harsh, war-ravaged realm of Nagarythe know all too well how to stand against the corruption of dark forces.
Through guile and grit, the armies of Nagarythe's patron will carry this realm's legacy with promise in their hearts on any battlefield.
Once Nagarythe has been reclaimed, it shall never again fall to the Forces of Chaos: a vow resounding through the hearts of lowly spearmen and high nobles alike.
Yvresse is the first bastion of defence against invasions from the east. Their nobles value discipline and vigilance, being prepared for any foe who might approach the coast of Ulthuan.
The mighty eagles of Ulthuan are no mere symbol, but a fighting force as well, on occasion. Othertimes, the defenders of Yvresse have something to fill the skies with in their stead.
To Elves throughout the world, Tor Yvresse is a symbol of those most steadfast amongst their ranks. To wield a spear is to honour one's vow to that symbol.
The White Tower enchanters bring to bear their mastery of spellcraft and the elements to those who show understanding and appreciation for Saphery's role in protecting Ulthuan, and much besides.

The Swordmasters of Hoeth's martial practice is something they apply themselves to with unrelenting tenacity. But Saphery's elemental airs contribute to their resillience through little effort of their own.
The high teachings of the White Tower, for which devoted patronage ensures the time and opportunity, imbue practitioners of elemental magic with skill that goes beyond mere knowledge.

The kingdom of Yvresse stands isolated, the sheer cliffs of the Annulii forming an impassable barrier. Yvresse often needs to fend for itself, thus the nobles endeavour for a well-prepared and controlled society.
As the rugged mountains protect the land of Yvresse, so do the Great Eagles protect its skies. They take well to those who pay respect to their home.
Nowhere does the Glittering Coast require more vigilance than along its eastern shores. Sharp eyes and whistling bolts cut through treacherous mists and all that lies hidden within.
A realm devastated in the times of the Sundering, Tiranoc now strives to return to its former glory by the might of charioteers charging at the forefront.
Sunlight is not the only thing reflected by the gleaming spears and helms of Tiranoc's fiery knights. When their pride is sufficiently kindled, they set upon their foes with all-consuming fire.
The Ithilmar embedded in Tiranoc Chariots is both a sign of that realm's irresistible resurgence and the glory it presages – on and off the battlefield.
Your patronage rival cannot hope to outdo you in martial bluster, but this is the real cost of enacting his ambitions. A taste of reality.
Surely, your patronage rival does not share the upstart's reckless ambitions. May they prove a wise steward. Now you make it clear there is more to governing than waging war.
Your shortcomings thus laid bare, you vow to push through them and prove worthy of this realm's patronage.
The noble's impartiality is commendable. Only time will tell the worth of ceding a valuable seat in exchange for his advice in other matters of governance.
With support from the many nobles whom your rival has rubbed the wrong way, a front is established to maintain your position – but his animosity lingers.
Your rival is enamoured of arguments and you give him none. Your troops need more attention than entitled courtiers, though they may dislike you for it.
The Phoenix King is not happy that you’ve willingly given up control of a position he mandated – time will tell if considering the rival noble’s arguments was worth the trouble.
Requesting that the envoy grant you a private audience with the Phoenix King, it was difficult to argue your case, though you managed to eke out a concession for your soldiers.
Entrusting the opportunistic noble with even limited administrative power was not a good idea. You knew that beforehand and have made peace with it in the name of your seat.
Your reputation may have taken a hit, but you do not forgo responsibilities just because of one meddler's actions. He has, however, found a way to impede you for a while.
You have improved your standing by vacating the position to anyone who would take it, on the condition this noble not be allowed to turn his savvy into material power.
If there is no recourse but to accede, you may as well forge a more lasting relationship with the envoy, making use of his unique talents for your benefit.
The courtier's persistence borders on desperation and is unbecoming. Yet those who sympathise with his effort to elevate himself on merit do not sympathise with you.
In eagerness to support you with whatever duties they may be entrusted with, the young courtier shows his talent.
The dubious relitigation of purported past wrongdoings proves nothing – only valour on the field. Not all at court think this way, and that has cost you.
True courtly authority lies in strong, decisive action. Personal complaints will now fall on deaf ears. But what holds true for the nobles is not so for others.
Admitting "fault", stepping down, and weathering the consequences with grace and openness will surely serve you well down the line.
Aislinn’s host moves with unerring precision, advancing through arcane mists in perfect order, betraying not the perilous threshold between sea and shore.
Sayl the Faithless, Twisted Seer of the Wastes. A cunning and treacherous sorcerer, and the ruler of the Dolgan tribe, who rose to power through manipulation, betrayal, and arcane mastery.
To Dechala, the ultimate self-indulgence is freedom from the shackles that bind others to conform. *They* can suffer and they can die, even, as long *her* desires come to pass.
Condemned to dance throughout eternity, her every motion a stylised rendition of one of the Dark Prince's great victories.
Ripping the very sky and earth asunder, you brought down a monster worthy of saga, a deed surely destined to become legendary amongst your kind.
The gain will outset the temporary delay. Hopefully.
Your incessant pursuit of the beast makes you something to fear. In time, every infamous monstrosity of the world shall come to know its only destiny is your killing blow…
The gods themselves take heed of your feats of strength and fury; another monster takes its place as a fine addition to your hordes.
Few have seen a more splendorous quarry brought back to the Great Halls of Norsca than your latest bounty – how the Chieftains toast and revel to your colossal victory!
Countless trials and pursuits to bring down nigh on insurmountable beasts has seen your name rise above all other hunters – the ultimate amongst their kind!
Heed the rancour of the rank-and-file…
Oh, to play the games of Greater Daemons…
A whisper draws forth the thread. Unwinding, it will show the way.
After the unwinding, the binding – a rope to pull oneself onwards.
[[col:white]]Defeat the High Elf Mages in battle![[/col]]
Your path pierces the shroud of ignorance – both yours and that of the servants of Chaos. Soon, they will know.
You have been found out. But in truth, you no longer hide, at last. It is too late for them. You have arrived.
Reaping the goods of what we sow
Working Trolls are always sorely needed – your Troll Kingdom cannot build itself.
Not all Trolls are for the front line, but they can still serve your armies in other ways.
A haul of tribute sent back to Norsca shall keep the lands and Chieftains loyal.
This force is not equipped for extended operations.
Having bound the Black Winds to his will, Sayl stands renewed – a vessel of raw, howling sorcery.
For Khornates, blood spilled equals blood worshipped. Norscans are especially vulnerable to this.
Plagues spawn fever and fervour in equal measure. With the Crow, that measure is always overflowing.
Sayl, cunning beyond compare... If the Serpent ever found out, he would probably chuckle (you hope). "*Beneath* compare, maybe." He will have his fun either way.
Where magic coalesces, so does the Eagle's presence. The pull is as irresistible as it is impersonal.
There is never a shortage of corpses, present or future. The Crow always eats well.
Being on the receiving end of violence is a novel feeling for many Norscans. They do not appreciate it.
Some will follow – the Serpent cannot be resisted. Some will stay, and preach – the Serpent *cannot* be resisted.
You are no stranger to it. Risking the Eagle's acquaintance would not be worth it. But he wouldn't stoop to that, not for this.
They died proving themselves. It is what they wanted, though not exactly what you wanted.
A small peck from the Crow causes unfathomable suffering in those willingly inviting it. The land has no will, and so the invitation is eternally open.
Norcans aren't known for their subtlety. If someone takes a little too much pleasure in... anything, it will show. And they will disappear.
No outsmarting the Serpent, of course. But this one is no such thing – barely a step above a worm. Stepping on those carries no risk.
Plant your feet. Raise a war-cry (and prepare a few choice spells). Calm your fearful, faithless heart.
There's no shortage of bloody-minded individuals across your domain. Thrusting them into the Hound's clawed lap is trouble, but one you can deal with.
The worst thing a Norscan can think of themselves is that they are special. It may even prove an obstacle to taking up arms, as absurd as it sounds.
Nurgle's faithful can find merriment in the the most vile things. As those who practice inflicting them, Norscans do not find it funny in the least.
It is not about appearances, of course. But any insult to one's person, Norscans take seriously. More seriously than you, apparently.
Much magical effort for little gain – except your own personal satisfaction. Was it worth it? To you, undoubtedly. To others...
Opposing Change may be a battle won, yet it is ground conceded in the war.
...is death. Others' death. And still others' growing taste for it. It is bitter, but it is what it is.
Chest-beating in the face of a Bloodthirster is a comically terrifying sight. The aftermath takes the humour out of it.
No matter how much you practice it, it always hurts – mostly the ones you betray. But in this case, also you.
Everyone makes time for the Crow. Time is *made* for the Crow, for it always brings him to your doorstep.
However much it costs these new converts, you do not care. But they are not the only ones paying.
...what was the question? Something about... nothing. Nothing you can think of. Nothing you can speak of.
Sayl's manipulation has caused these warriors to break off from their Lord and rebel against them!
A substantial old cache of Starwood was found following our victory over the Dark Elf invasion force
As the world is destroyed, the Dark Gods' powers grow further, as does the power of their will.
This entire province has been Devastated by the {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh_main_chs_chaos}} due to half or more of its regions being razed.
Shambling corpses and restless spectres herald the passage of this army.
The floating remnants of Nagarythe will seize their rightful glory again.
Take them from the streets. Who will miss them, or care that they died screaming?
There is no better leader of the monstrous than those with a little monstrosity of their own.
Taming a Hydra or a Kharybdiss is an art of sublime skill and cruelty.

As the Ritual of Undeath completes and all life is absorbed, the overwhelming magic causes the dead to rise into a Shambling Horde. After a period, the ritual's magic dissipates and the force will begin to degrade.
The Necromantic Energy from the Ritual of Undeath still lingers in the air, sustaining this Shambling Horde.
The flames of Fervour spread further and further.
The questing never stops when quests are never failed.
From afar, a beacon of purity. Come closer and you stand in the presence of a righteous inferno.
Valour is hard-earned, but easily multiplied by vociferous voices.
As the wealth of the Ivory Road grows, so too does the importance of protecting it.
There is always more to gain from the loss of others.
Let it be recorded that upon this day did Thorgrim Grudgebearer, High King of Karaz-a-Karak, the Karaz Ankor, and all the Holds therein, did pronounce lawful Grudgement upon…
It takes several human lifetimes to truly master the skills of the forge.
Grudges run deep, and so does the earth.
In the year 685, by the manling counting, Bragi Bolghammer procured six barrels of Grobkaz Best with 10 silver pieces of credit. With 1800 years of compound interest, his clan now owes…
May he rule the halls of Karak Eight Peaks with a heart of iron. For this day at least, let all Dawi rejoice. Karak Eight Peaks has herself a new king and her future is assured.
There are more dangerous professions than assistant to Malakai Makaisson, but none that can be done indoors.
If you can survive the heat, and the biting insects, and the diseases, and the man-eating reptiles, then sure… I can get you where you’re going.
Recruitment charters have gone out to the cities, towns, and great guilds. With military might comes political power, but such is the price of securing the Empire’s borders.
Where others host elaborate balls and feasts, the Warden's supplier has spent decades preparing for the worst.
An understanding of dragonkind is useful, not only for befriending the noble beasts, but also for combatting their fallen kin.
The finest of shipwrights require neither labourers nor tools.
Many Yvressan princes saw their first battles with the Mistwalkers. It is a mark of pride to see a son or daughter doing the same.
Cruelty is a talent not learned, but inherited.
Darker scales absorb more of the sun’s warmth, allowing your warriors to carry out the Great Plan far from the jungles of home.
At the end, they all served Nagash.
The ancient sands and their denizens are once more prostrate under the dominion of Nagash, their rightful ruler.
It has taken years of thankless toil, but several of your subjects can now recognise the names you have given them and will occasionally utter two words in a row.
Gather round, slugs, and hear a tale of the Maggot Lord…
Nurgle’s ministrations always yield most salubrious results. Festering good health is but one.
Skaven are always in a hurry to leave their mark.
With a cunning eye for sores and blisters, experienced breeders release their charges only when they are most ripe.
There are so many dangers in Skaven life that sharing a burrow with a Doom-rocket Silo barely raises a twitch of a whisker.
The secrets one keeps to themselves are the first to be pilfered by the Eshin.
With so many ravenous mouths to feed, a Skaven will gnaw on almost anything.
Now that you have gnawed it, you are not sure what to do with this bone, but there are undoubtedly other rats who can think about those things.
With the original Council of 13 fused into one as his patron, the Grey Seer stands ready to end the mockery against him and complete the greatest Masterplan yet!
More worshippers, my shining queen. More tribute for your ever-growing glory.
Because the games always come to an end.

A single well-stocked bookshelf, and at the same time the complete collection of the Impossible Fortress’ infinite library. Every word ever inscribed to page, scroll, or tablet can be plucked from this shelf, if you know where to find it.
A new aristocracy of the night begins, where mortals will be ruled over as cattle.
Immortality grants a rare perspective, but it does not necessarily grant patience.
Squalls of numbing, withering magic blow about the world, guided by a hand which has grasped everything and crumbled it to dust.
Your web of intrigues weave through every vampiric bloodline, and beyond.
With a passage from the Liber Noctis, your necromancy can repopulate ancient battlefields and empty entire graveyards.
The spells that prolong your life draw all manner of hateful spirits – all the more hateful once they have been ensnared by your magic.
An Asrai grove may look grown, but it has been made.
Balance and harmony are achieved through constant struggle. Nature’s permanence is a ceaseless flux.
With the consent of the Forest, the most capricious of Forest Spirits might be persuaded to fight.
Successive slaughters have weakened the veil between Khorne’s realm and the mortal world.
According to local folklore, Mother Ostankya sleeps through the winter months in a coccoon of mud and fallen leaves.
Ice Witches tour every far flung village, searching for peasant girls with a spark of magical talent.
The people of Kislev will worship under one roof. Their gods shall stand behind one man.
The forests of Kislev are dark places, steeped in old magic.
Nothing short of total domination, and one day, deification itself, will satisfy the Hag Sorceress of Ghrond.
Genius schemer, brilliant tactician, unmatched sorcerer of verminkind – rats across the Under-Empire twitch at Thanquol’s command, eager to hurl their wretched lives away for his greatest plan yet!
This bleak edifice draws the ruinous power of the Chaos Gods unto Archaon, swelling the Everchosen's dreadful might!
Lose any 3 Designs to add a Hell-Pit Abomination to the Plan
These ruins have been utterly desolated by an army of the {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh_main_chs_chaos}}.

While Nagashizzar is Nagash's shining glory, no other structure represents his legacy more than the Black Pyramid. The structure is no mere Burial Chamber, but a tool that can harness the Winds of Magic to Nagash's every whim.
An arcane cornucopia shall be borne upon the discordant peal of bronze.
Nurgle bestows regular gifts upon the triplets Glott, spoiling them much in the manner of a generous grandfather.
With the Beastmen assault blunted and the Warherd routed, the men of Middenland can rejoice!
The funeral procession was well received by the grieving families. Your citizens appreciate the gesture.
The military is stretched thin while guard patrols are increased along the Drakwald border
Having earned the favour of all four Chaos Gods, the Everchosen is granted power beyond all imagining – at least while the Forces of Chaos endure.
This entire province has been [[b]]Devastated[[/b]] by the ongoing Chaos Invasion due to half or more of its regions being razed.
Alone amidst the end of all things, still we fight.
From young to old, it is our people who shall see us through – each of us must do our part.
We must bear any burden and endure any cost, for in such dire times our leader must guide us through the darkness.
If this is the end, then let even the Dark Gods remember our last stand.
We have long prepared for this day; now all that is left is to fight.
We must spare nothing in this fight. Our prosperity may suffer, but our nation shall survive.
Long have the cloven-hooved and misshapen brayed to an uncaring firmament to be loosed upon the world’s final ruination.
Sonorous drums boom in time to snatches of a war-song. From banner and shield alike glowers the eight-pointed star.
Only the dull thud of daemon-axes in flesh and the spray of warm blood across their skin can sate these gore-clouded minds.
Bestial gods lair in the hearts of the savage northmen, who gladly heed their call to the world’s final madness.
At the clang of their rust-shod feet, the skies dull to a brooding shale-green, and the very earth sloughs into a sodden mire.
The sinuous host ululates a war-song beyond mortal hearing, its trilling echoed by their snake-bodied steeds alone.
The eye strains to behold these legions for long, as flickering flame dances ceaselessly across their panoply of brilliant azure.
The Dark Gods may be indifferent to the fall of nations, but they feast well upon the slaughter such ruin brings.
Scores of blackened corpses hang from the citadel's brass-clad rafters like game in a poacher's den, their gore trickling into dark pools below.
From moss-eaten battlements, leprous tallymen clang their rust-pocked bells, sounding the death knell of the sane world.
Living flesh is intricately woven through the razor-sharp steel lattice of the citadel's gratings; it opens to a chorus of pain.
All around, the scream-wracked air reeks of burning flesh, while sickly warpfires gleam amongst its impossibly angled ramparts.
Ancient enmities, forsworn oaths and simmering grudges must be set aside before the Three-Eyed King's threat of annihilation.
The realms must oppose the march of Nagash, for the implacable tyrant would steal the breath from the living and drain the resolve of the free-willed.
Gripped by terror and disgust, the realms must stand as one against the nightmare surging beneath the verminous tyrant’s one-eyed gaze.
This force belongs to the Undead Legions, who now rise to Nagash's call!
The Great Necromancer's return heralds the end of all life – unless he and his Great Ritual can be stopped, all are doomed!
This entire province has been [[b]]Devastated[[/b]] by the Skaven Vermintide due to them owning half or more of its regions.
An undulating morass of chittering filth surges forth from the deepest, darkest burrows of verminkind.
A lesion like a wicked grin splits upon the fertile soil: a sure sign of Grandfather's adoration.
Glottkin narrative invasion no withdraw [STATUS: HIDDEN]
The air bloats with an eye-watering pungency as countless wings drone unseen – a putrid sign of Grandfather’s favour.
Gorged on offal-stench, Grandfather stains the firmament green as shale, and wherever his children roam, flecks of rust fly upon a caustic wind.
Glutted with souls, the earth's bowels swell with joyous rivulets of pus, mingling with the blood of the slain.
Foliage grows oily and jaundiced, writhing like hookworm-ridden intestines against your rust-shod feet – Nurgle's fond caress, gentle and loving.

Cankerous tumours erupt across the victims' torsos before crowning each brow with a single horn-like protrusion.

The lips of the afflicted peel back into a rictus – a foul cleft across the rotting mound that once was a face.
Phantoms of thin, spidery shamblers stalk the bilious fog shrouding the land; those who linger soon feel the sickness rattle them to the marrow.
Those who draw deep the unearthly spores choking the air soon find their skin webbed with pale, pith-like strands.
Grave moss clots the canals and culverts, turning them into noisome breeding grounds for vile insects that grant their unwitting hosts neither rest nor respite.
Rank lichen overruns the joints of the afflicted, which creak with every movement and tear open fresh, oozing sores in skin grown thin and leathery.
Countless papery wings susurrate unseen through the thick, foetid air, their ceaseless drone breeding a sweltering torpor.
Eyes shall yellow with jaundice. Orifices shall weep blood. Heed the booming currents, and rejoice.\\n–Flail Rotgloam, Herald of Nurgle
Thrashing and squelching in a waxen morass of their own humours, the sufferer undergoes a horrid transmutation – their belly distending into a pallid boulder of putrid fat.
Choked with phlegm, the lungs sputter and wheeze like punctured bellows, their broken cadence eerily close to stifled laughter.
“A God. A breeze. A horn. A war. A host. A plague.“\\n–Tuskrot the Turbid, striking three tarnished bronze gongs after each word
Pustules spread unchecked across the body’s soft flesh, swelling like a bullfrog’s throat sacs with rancid, tallowy fluid – each rupture bringing indescribable pain.
Though flesh be marked by lobes-a-three, befouled it’s not if none can see. Yer nose is stuffed! Yer ears are clogged! Now yer snared in this murksome bog!\\n–Blightking Vitreous
Hive-like ridges rise across the skin and lesions carve troughs through the flesh as hundreds of tiny, grinning mites surface from within. Their maddening squeals never cease.

The perished show no outward symptoms besides a ghoulish reek. A blade laid to the corpse, however, reveals viscera overgrown with blotchy fungi and blood-slicked pitcher plants, their swollen cavities nested deep within the organs.

The disease ravages the eyelids, mouths and genitals relentlessly until, like desiccated earth, a spiderweb of fissures splits their delicate surfaces – a blend of blood and pus dripping through the cracks.
It is said that, in the witching hour of its incubation, the bones of its victims steal out of their bodies and revel in their newfound undeath – leaving their hosts mere sacks of quivering flesh.
Nodules shall harden into leprous knots. Innards shall droop like waterlogged sails. Heed the slate-green skies, split wide in a rictus grin!\\n–Flail Rotgloam, Herald of Nurgle

This complication of the Pale Seeper draws Urfather's larvae deep into the engorged intestines. There, they heap their frass into a tri-lobed nest before pupating amid seething secretions that dissolve the host's gut.
Like wind struggling through a dense thicket, each breath grows shallower and more laboured as phlegmy secretions choke every passage of the lungs.
“A God. A worm. A bog. A swarm. A bell. A toll.“\\n–Tuskrot the Turbid, clanging a verdigrised leper’s bell after each word

Fist-sized pustules balloon inward, exercising tremendous pressure and crushing the innards until the eyes burst from their sockets – leaving a tri-lobed effigy of two bloody craters and a mouth frozen in its final wail.
Pallid shadows their eyes have caught, filmed now with curdled milk and rot. Flailing blindly at what assails, they furrow the mud with broken nails.\\n–Blightking Vitreous

Contact with this dire soil-borne ailment leaves every surface pitted with sulphurous green and dull ochre, as though drenched in stale vomit.
First, the facial features thin to slits; then limbs blacken with gangrene. At last, buboes boil across the torso, and burst with a malodorous pop, committing the poor soul to Nurgle.
A drifting menace of acidic yeast engulfs the area, chewing through stone with a malevolence and precision that border on sentience.
Bearers of this ailment are known to weave wicker effigies of the three-lobed icon that haunts their fevered nightly thrashing, shortly before perishing in a glaucous puddle of their own humours.

Carefully decant an alembicful of sputum into a cauldron of simmering kelpie blood, strain gut-bile through a seven-gauge copper sieve, then stir with a rusted ladle.\\n–from a recipe scrawled by Festus

Giggling through chattering, rotten teeth for days on end, these maddened unfortunates are last seen strapping a brass discus over their hollow eye sockets – attaining the cyclopean visage favoured by the Grandfather.
Wisps of green-black murk congeal into an impenetrable fog, so dense that those within seem to wade through brackish water. Few enter willingly; fewer still emerge.
Cystic moss and maggot-vines creep across the torsos of the afflicted, wrenching bone and distending flesh into ever more grotesque shapes, until the victim blooms into glorious disfigurement.
Pitted leper-bells clang out a rough warning: tread not upon the wailing visages pressed into the grave-loam, for fly larvae and fungus gnats seethe beneath the mire.
A lesion upon the glabella bursts in a gout of discoloured ichor, leaving the eyes fused into one great cataract-clouded orb – a mockery most pleasing to the Urfather.
What seems a mire of festering cadavers is, in truth, a host gripped by horrid torpor, their limbs contorting as their bellies distend into the unwholesome likeness of bloated ticks.
For many miles, a foetid wind carries the droning ministrations of the Urfather – intoned by a shifting rotfly swarm that blots out the firmament in a coal-black pall flecked with citrine.
Time trickles slowly for the sufferer, like blood from a wound that will not close, as they are reduced to a pallid-fleshed husk – pitted by decay and abrim with turgid parasites.
Souls are wheezed from plague-ridden lungs to the cadence of a whistled harvest tune, then borne upon a noisome wind into the Urfather’s embrace.

The wriggling beasts eat their hosts from the inside out, lazily chewing with tiny razored mandibles until nothing remains but leathery husks. At last, they burst free through ruptures shaped like tiny, wicked grins.
By night, Daemonflies lay their eggs in tri-pocked wounds gnawed into the gut. Soon, swarms of blood-slicked, sated progeny crawl from the oozing gashes.

Grate the Stinkhorn, chop the Puffball, mash the Flat Top, drain the Bloatwort! Boil it all, breathe deep the fumes, and wait until the eyes gaze back – those sunken, luminous orbs of sickly green light…\\n–Glump Grymgholla

Their minds are out of balance. Only by the release of the excess Yin energies swirling within their skulls may harmony be regained. This will require the finest surgeons in all Cathay.

Let the afflicted rest and recuperate. The Winds forever shift, and so too will this magical malaise. Fine teas and medicinal herbs will leave them refreshed and more determined than ever to serve our Emperor.

Upon bathing in those sacred waters, not only will their fire be dimmed, but the Spirit Dragon will have their ancestors bear witness to their ugly fury. In their shame, they will know harmony once more.
If the fury cannot be quenched, perhaps it can be mastered. Breathing exercises will calm them until the next battle, and there they can unleash this rage upon deserving targets.
Though his manner is abhorrent, we have much to learn from this well-travelled thug. His permanent services will be costly to secure, but every one of our warriors will greatly benefit.
Let the Maneater feast upon the finest meats and richest wines Grand Cathay has to offer. Soon enough, secrets will spill from his drunken, drooling maw.

Absurd though it seems, you sense in this creature a maternal care toward you. Upon its back, barely visible, blue furs create the shape of a crescent moon. You should show her that you adore her too.

As you fight the strange urge to bow, the cat's tail twitches impatiently. Along its length is red patterning which uncannily resembles a great serpent. The haughty feline refuses table scraps, but perhaps an offering of sublimely roasted boar leg would suffice?
Perhaps they are evil spirits – Chi'an Chi takes many forms. There’s a well nearby – grab the cats by the scruff and cast them in!
Breathe deep of the strange vapours within, and you shall be infused with the Winds themselves. As the harmonious power of Yin pulses through your veins, none will even dream of questioning you.
All the Emperor's subjects should prosper from this singular discovery. Should we sink the opened chest into the river, the swirling magic within will touch every soul in the land.
Beware of strangers and their exotic gifts. Kill this imposter and have this box buried with them!

The apparition of their disapproving forebears, beseeching them to pursue peace, will surely soften their hearts towards us. They will never know that this was merely an illusion wrought by our most inventive Alchemists.
Let us spread the rumour that our foe has fallen under the sway of the Great Enemy. Incensed by this supreme act of blasphemy and corruption, our legions will fight more tirelessly than ever before.
Execute one fifth of the army. They are short-lived mortals, and some will be traitors. The rest will be scared to act further.
Lace the bananas and melons with serpent venom, and this infestation shall soon run its course. Disposing of the endless simian corpses will be a fiendish task, however.
Medicine and supplies will restore our beleaguered forces.
The Blood God’s minions have nothing on me.
One of your Sorcerers believes they can translate one of the inscriptions. Runic magic is generally beneath notice, but perhaps something of minor worth may result from this endeavour.

Zuvassin's mouthpiece claims that emptying a sack of gold into the nearest river will cause an equal number of eyeballs to rain from the sky – consuming them will grant your legion sight beyond sight.
Order the construction of a great war-pit, where you will challenge your doubters to face you in unarmed combat. Few will dare attempt this.
Order all involved in the libidinous rite flayed to death, and a vast and bleeding statue of your own form constructed from their remains.
Rather than end the carnal ceremony, you could take your measure of pleasure. The experience will be unforgettable, though your followers will regard you with disdain.
If the eight-pronged star of Chaos is burned into the screaming fiend's hide, they will know rage as never before.
The near-forgotten symbol of the first Everchosen is reputed to grant unnatural power to those whose flesh bears it.
The colossal goblet, carved from a great skull of unknown origin, houses a gallon of boiling blood. Drinking deep of it will demonstrate your incomparable courage.
The yellow growth palpitates horribly. The thought of forcing the pulsing, reeking malignancy down your throat is nauseating, but it would earn the Fly Lord's love.
The crystal vial houses a lilac fluid, its scent intoxicating. You sense that dousing yourself with it will cause indescribable agony – but render you irresistible.
The nine-eyed, twisted face upon the hovering book's leathery cover tries to tear itself free at your approach. It seeks to bond itself to your flesh.
Order the immediate execution of every mortal kept in your dungeons and torture chambers, then burn the bodies in a vast pyre. The touch of Chaos shall grow yet stronger.
Telling the Dwarfs that you're short on new construction work did not end well.
Desperate measures are called for. Only by tearing the ears from the skulls of every single fiend in your populace may they become immune to Slaanesh's hypnotic beat.
There is nothing for it but to join the dread drumming yourself. Perhaps it will inspire you to greater feats of slaughter? Or perhaps it will enable Slaanesh to seduce more to his cause?
At significant cost and effort, capture a pack of starving Yhetees from the mountains, and allow your followers to slake their battle-thirst upon the raging ice-beasts.
Summon an ambassador from every empire – an unprecedented conclave of all this world's powers. Then disembowel them where they stand, and claim their high-ranking skulls for Kharneth.
Raze everything in your kingdom that is not brass, bone or steel. Leave nothing living, save for the mightiest of your Daemons.
If your blood legion is rendered irreversibly immune to Slaaneshi charms, they will surely prevail in battle against the Perfect Prince's perfumed fiends.
Storm every home, and behead any being caught in an act of congress. To be on the safe side, the same applies to all those guilty of reading poetry, playing games of chance, or drinking fine wines.
A simple proclamation of approval from the Skull Throne would be sufficient to send countless Daemons flocking to your cause.
No trinket can make an act of mercy forgivable. Ignore the relic, and grant a brutal second death to each and every one of these Unliving wretches.
Arrange for the capture of one of their weaker underlings. They will yield soon their secrets if they value their skull.

Instil new fervour within the populace. Make every child understand exactly what happens when Ruin visits Kislev. As the nightmares grip them, they will beg their parents to protect them, no matter the cost.
The other kingdoms do not realise how close doom is to their doors. We must send our most gifted orators to make these pampered fools understand. Once they do, they will surely aid our cause.
Have the farmer ask this crack of his to grant Kislev's armies the strength of the soil.
Have the farmer request that the Motherland bless us with the power of the elements.
Years of flash-flooding and countless thousands of footsteps have taken a heavy toll on the ancient market. Restore its former glory, and goods will flow like never before.
We have long consigned Bretonnian artisans to one of the most forlorn areas of the city, but they do know a thing or two about steel. Let us gain their favour, and in turn their wisdom.
Food is too precious in Praag to waste even this monstrously spoiled harvest. Perhaps it may even be a boon to sorcery, though who knows what horror will we invite across our threshold?
Though our populace will go hungry, we cannot permit this foul affliction to pass into proud Kislevite blood. Once the fasting is done, purity shall reign.

If trust is so hard won, then, alas, fear it must be. Have our most devout Patriarchs flay his traitorous flesh, remove his fingers then, finally, burn him alive. There will doubtless be turmoil, but we can control that.

The free-thinking heretic is, alas, undeterred. He now tells the subjects that we attempted to threaten him into silence. Preposterous! And does he not realise that it is only through faith that the dread taint of Chaos is kept at bay?
Smear the buboe with carrion, mulch and excrement in the hope it will grow yet more fecund, and thus feed the land with Nurgle's putrescent power.
Whatever pestilent horrors swim within this vast and necrotic edifice shall be loosed upon the land, spreading the Urfather's foul touch wherever they go.
The vast cadaver will make a fine breeding ground for pox-spreading insects. The foul grubs will grow fat upon its mouldering flesh, and upon reaching adulthood they will blight the land.
If your rotted legion barely have minds left to twist, they will become inherently resistant to madness. Tzeentch's changelings will thus be powerless against them.
All corvids must be slain on sight. In fact, anything with feathers is fair game, lest it be a sorcerous emissary of the Raven God.
The filthy flood-waters contain generations of waste, and thus will be a breeding ground for manifold new and wondrous diseases. Truly, this is a miracle of science!
Order your Tallybands to bathe in the disease-strewn brown waters. The countless bacteria within shall work wonders upon their festering flesh.
Miracles should not be expected, for Plaguebearers' vocal cords have nigh-on rotted away. Guiding them into a simple three-note refrain will yield potent results, however.
While this has perhaps unwelcome overtones of Slaaneshi sorcery, causing a high-ranking foe to become captivated by your singularly horrendous form would yield invaluable insights.
Maybe they're bored of eatin' the same ol' raw flesh for sixteen meals a day. Tell the Butchers to make somethin' fancier, like stuffin' one kind of meat with another kind of meat. Delicious, yeah?

Get raidin' like never before, and round up the finest meats, cheeses, cakes and boozes in the 'old world. We're gonna have ourselves the buffet to end all buffets. If this don't fatten 'em up, nothin' will.
This ain't natural. Probably them Chaos lads are muckin' about again. Whatever it is, we ain't got no use for skinny Bulls. Might as well feed 'em to somethin' wot will eat, yeah?
Feed 'em them lava-chillies the Butchers have been too scared to touch. Once they've finished thrashing in agony they'll soon be belchin' fire. Maw only knows what they'll break first, mind.
All that grease on their flesh will make our boys burn a treat. They won't thank us for the pain and the flames'll probably spread, but the scars'll make 'em tough as old boots.
Tasty as this magic meat tree looks, if we gnosh the whole thing now it ain't never gonna grow more chops. Just pick the ripe ones, yeah?
It'll fill up the loot-pile alright, but the tribe ain't gonna be 'appy that you ain't sharin' it around. They'll probably 'ave a massive sulk.
A few shiny things for every Bull sounds a like a plan. They'll surely blow it all on meat 'n' booze, and maybe stop botherin' you for it for a while.
It don't matter 'ow that beast ended up so weird, we can't let good meat go to waste. Get those 'earts cooked sharpish, then get 'em in the tribe's guts.
We can thump some sense into 'em. Or out of 'em, as the case may be. The other Gnoblars'll look at 'em funny, but that don't matter.
Fair's fair, the tribe's only had eight breakfastses today. Stuff a bit more fat 'n' grease down 'em and they'll be right as rain. Better, even.
We'll lose a few boys in the process, but we can make these pups do what we says. Once they're all grown up, we got ourselves a weapon, yeah?
There'll be Bulls queuing up to fight for ya if it means they get to splatter some of this red stuff on their lunch. 'Course, they'll probably eat us outta house and home.
No self-respectin' Ogre stuffs anything that ain't meat down their maw. Get the tribes back on a pure-flesh diet, and their guts'll soon be bigger than ever.
Your pleasure-toys will rhapsodise about the drink's wondrous qualities to their countless other partners. Soon enough, all will beg to join your cause, hoping for a taste of their own.
Somehow, lust has been swapped for rage. To undo this will require a great harvest of souls, which will then be imbibed by your populace. Their loins shall soon be aflame once more.
There is Khornate blood in the water supply: so that is how this pleasure-slaying sabotage was wrought. There is nothing for it but wait for the boiling ichor to drain away.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder – and no doubt the loins too. If the people are forcibly denied that which they have grown bored of, they will soon desperately desire its return.
So nightmarish and so endless is the composition that eardrums will burst, eyeballs will melt and brains will bleed. This mass sacrifice will be delicious indeed, and the dark rewards immeasurable.
Send the Druchii to your decadent brothers and sisters in sin. They will be so very easily made willing, and your freshly-satiated kin will owe you a debt of gratitude.

If it is cruelty they desire, then cruelty they shall receive. Release the Druchii, naked and unarmed, into battle, and no servant of Kharneth will be able to resist this invitation to slaughter. The distraction will serve us well.

One unforgettable night of fine wine, heavenly music and extreme debauchery will be all it takes to coax secrets and strategies from their hungry lips. How Slaanesh will revel in our foe's subsequent suffering.
Scour the libraries for spells of voiding. If one does not work, move on to the next. Do whatever it takes to find a magical vaccine for Nurgle's latest pox.

When sufficient numbers of the Changer's Followers have dissolved into horrific goo, those not yet infected will most probably be immune to the plague's deliquescent touch. The casualties shall be many, however.
Have your Sorcerers invoke a great ward of stabilisation. Though draining, it should lock your followers' fluctuating forms to this plane of existence.
Chant the scar-drawn runes aloud, and your changelings' limbs will catch alight with blue-gold fire – all the better to burn away diseased flesh.
The inscription will grant voice to your army's every missile, magical or otherwise – an ethereal shriek capable of reversing decay.
Their flesh shall erupt in squirming tendrils and shapeless new limbs, chattering mouths will sprout upon their hides, and indescribable new creatures shall be birthed from their spines.
All reason shall leave them, and they shall forever speak in half-truths, impossible prophecies and unknown tongues. All who hear them will suffer the same fate.
Once the disembodied digits dig painlessly into the eyeballs of your foe's soldiers, their sight shall become yours. The cost of concealing this grand act of sorcery will, however, be high.
The spread of corruption from the Unstable Chaos Portal in your lands continues to create condemnation from others.

An unnatural aggression takes hold of the populace; a seething frustration that explodes at the slightest provocation. Even the most placid soul becomes as quick to anger as a rabid dog. Soon enough, the fighting begins. The streets are littered with the dazed and beaten, and the gutters run red with blood.

Exploring too deep into an ancient cave system, a forager unwittingly brings back with them a hitherto unknown and devastating disease – one which now spreads like wildfire throughout the populace. Beware the coughing! Spurn the sneezing! Run screaming from the feverish!

A travelling clothier sets up her stall, offering garments tailored so masterfully that they are like a second skin. All who don her garments become consumed by self-obsession, forever admiring their own reflections and refusing all other duties. Undeterred, countless more queue out the door.

Chen – single word, shredding sanity wherever it is spoken. They say a large, black bird was the first to utter it, and now all who hear it soon say nothing else, laughing hysterically as they bark into the ears of those around them. "Chen! Chen! Chen! CHEN!"

The people report sightings of flickering figures in their homes, chanting in oddly familiar voices. One is even certain she saw the faces of her long-dead grandparents. Before these reports can be corroborated, the ancestor spirits – if that is what they are – disappear. In their wake, the land knows harmony.

There is a shudder from the Celestial Palace, and the sound of straining metal, as the Wu Xing Compass works its sorcery. Each warrior suddenly finds within their pocket a chipped stone from the Great Bastion itself – a ward against the Great Enemy, a token of the Emperor’s love.

Disaster strikes, as a sudden storm blows a colossal Sky-Junk into a mountainside. The impact shakes loose a legion of long-lost Terracotta Sentinels, stationed immobile since some ancient campaign. Fortunately, many can be restored, while those demolished in the fall can be used to repair others of their kind.

Determined to please Khorne further, his servants elect to brand their own hides with His flaming icon. Their screams are beyond horrifying, and the caustic stench of burning Daemon flesh is unforgettable, but the rite plunges them into an enduring hunger for slaughter, requiring no other sustenance.

Nurgle's Rot is a slow death sentence for mortals, but amongst the Urfather's faithful it is a source of strength. The Fly Lord's putrescent devotees are thus delighted by their discovery of a new strain of this divine contagion, one that numbs their senses as it ravages their flesh.

Somewhere far beyond, Slaanesh knows the ecstasy of satisfaction. Afterwards, as the Perfect Prince slumbers in His forbidden boudoir, the howling sweetness of His dreams touches each and every one of His servants. Sated, they need nothing else for now.

A strange calm comes over those who pledge themselves to the Raven. They refuse all food and rest, and work tirelessly. When pressed on the matter, they all chant the same chant: "We want for nothing today, for great Tzeentch has shown us the rewards we will know tomorrow."

The land itself erupts in obsidian spines from far below, some coated in crimson blood, some in noxious bile, others exuding a bewitching, bittersweet fragrance, and others still bearing a shimmering halo of eldritch flame. The Ruinous Powers lay claim to this realm...

A Norscan Shaman reports a vision of a far-off kingdom razed to ash, its every inhabitant slaughtered, of nothing left but a mountain of skulls. Though none know where this land is, the joyous news of Khorne's distant triumph means countless Daemons jockey for the opportunity to achieve similar here.

No realm can be truly considered cleansed of life by merely scourging its surface. In sewers and caverns the Skaven lurk, always. Eight thousand barrels of boiling blood solve the problem neatly. As countless vermin are roasted alive in their foul nests, the land itself becomes a monument to Khorne.

As one, unbidden, dozens of Daemons begin to chant. "Blood for the Blood God! Skulls for the Skull Throne! BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD! SKULLS FOR THE SKULL THRONE!" They continue this tirelessly for days, then suddenly all drop dead. There is a laugh like thunder, and the skies blacken.

Tired of waiting for the next battle, a troop of Bloodletters storm out of camp. They maraud across the land, slaughtering without discretion, their rage growing with each kill. Ultimately, they turn upon each other. Though none survive, word of their brutal deeds inspires others to similar feats of carnage.

You stumble upon an Ogre camp. A Butcher escapes the slaughter by promising untold power. He slices and stews the entrails of his fallen kin, creating a foaming red broth which causes hide to harden and muscle to swell. Though useful, all sorcery offends Khorne, and so the Butcher is slain.

Madame Valentina, a singularly fearsome Ice Witch, retired years ago. But she has spent the time since tutting at falling standards, at Ice Maidens who barely know Frost Blade from Crystal Cloak, and she can stand no more. When she raps furiously upon the Ice Court’s doors, none dare refuse her.

Your Lancers bring you the bones of a long-lost Tzar, discovered while patrolling the oblast. Into a reliquary box they go, holy relics of an ancient war to defend Kislev’s vast borders. Inspired by this proof that their rulers too sacrifice everything for the Motherland, your legions take heart.

Officially, the Ice Court only accepts young women of noble lineage, for only they deserve its timeless wisdom. Exceptions are sometimes made, though none may talk of it. When a farmer beseeches the Court, offering a thousand saddlebags of blood-stained gold, his daughter is accepted without question.

Many believe that the Motherland is alive, and loves her people as they love her. When disease claims the lives of every man, woman and child in five stanitsas, the icy wind takes on a new timbre, one that sounds like a sorrowful howl. The land will surely make amends.

The Patriarchs descend upon every home, rooting through drawers and overturning bookshelves in search of any hint of heresy. Countless Kislevites are dragged from their beds and executed. Who can say how many were innocent? Nevertheless, purity – or, at least, terrified obedience – is restored.

Feeding War Bears is an expensive business – the beasts consume their own body weight in meat daily. The discovery of an enormous Slaaneshi cult hiding in Erenegrad's sewers is thus an occasion for celebration rather than dismay. Blasphemy is duly purged, and the bears sleep well.

Many equate Nurgle with death, but this is to misunderstand His intent. He desires rebirth, so that more death may follow. So it is that He raises the bones of the long-dead, and from them sprouts bilious flesh. Nurgle's newest children strike up their buzzing drone, and the cycle begins anew.

Morrslieb grows full, casting its sickly green light across the land. The Fly Lord’s children rejoice, for contagion thrives under the Chaos moon’s cold shadow. The rotted legion erupts in fresh sores and, in horrifying unison, coughs a constant cough, spraying fountains of plague-ridden spittle with every phlegmy bark.

The droning of Nurgle's Plaguebearers is feared across the land, for all know it heralds lingering, fever-wracked death. However, an unusually enterprising Tallyband drift from their usual monotone and chant their chilling dirge in a hitherto-unheard frequency – one which immediately loosens the bowels of all for miles around.

An uncommonly bloated Plague Toad is drawn helplessly to the befoulment of a nearby sewer, but cannot squeeze itself through the entry grate. With a final terrible lunge, it wrenches itself across - tearing its vast belly open in the process. The countless black maggots within surge into the local water supply.

The earth of every town, every village, every field and every forest simultaneously sprouts a single Nurgling. The tiny Daemons stand stock-still, their rictus grins never changing. On the seventh day of this, all suddenly burst, releasing an immense cloud of flies that quickly disperse, turning the very skies yellow.

Your plague-scientists have been busy. From their squalid laboratories they birth a brand new contagion, one they proudly dub 'Raven Rot'. Remorselessly, the pox ravages eldritch feathers and chews at ectoplasmic flesh. Truly, it is a beautiful disease, one that silences the arrogant bluster of the Changer’s iridescent slaves.

Your pock-marked children pick idly at their own scabs as they await the next battle. After a time, they fall into a strange and silent trance, and continue picking until their entire hides hang off them in grisly ribbons. As their ruined flesh knits, it hardens into thick, body-wide callouses.

A storm darkens the skies, but there is no lightning – instead, there comes a hail of man-sized, pus-filled seeds. As they implant themselves in the earth, it becomes iron-hard and sprouts vast and pungent fungal foundations. Praise be to Nurgle, for He shares His garden's bounty!

Those farmsteads unfortunate enough to be proximate to your tribes have long accepted that the price of their survival is eye-wateringly high. The great day has rolled around once again, and when your followers eventually stir from their grease-stained beds, they are presented with veritable mountains of slaughtered lambs and calves.

Your henchmen drag an unusually lucid Gorger before you. Unlike its solitude-maddened kin, the elephantine, sinewy horror will obey basic commands. This proves particularly useful during contract negotiations. A mere snap of the fingers will see the other party’s head torn from their shoulders – a superior rate is thus guaranteed.

One of your Butchers laces his latest dish with oddly-glowing mushrooms from the deepest caves. The tribe who consumes it soon enters a state of euphoria. As one, they begin to dance, their thunderous footsteps toppling trees and shaking boulders from mountains. Even the very shadows retreat from the cacophony.

An enterprising Slaughtermaster hits upon the idea of fashioning crude, oversized slip-on noses and ears from leftover scraps of hide. Desirous of these absurd prosthetics, countless Gnoblars flock to your cause – for in their abhorrent society there is no greater sign of station than a bulbous snout and mammoth lugs.

A wandering Hunter shares his tall tales with the tribe. In one, he claims to have trapped and eaten a dragon, and that the taste was beyond compare - like the most succulent chicken marinated in the finest spices. The tribe is instantly decided: they must experience this singular flavour themselves.

Though Gnoblars are highly irritating creatures, the larger ones have occasional moments of brilliance. One of your favourites takes it upon itself to spread a rumour that consuming the gizzard of a Daemon will make one's gut double in size. To say the tribe is motivated would be an understatement.

Mutation is usually the bailiwick of Tzeentch, but it has its uses for Slaanesh. There is a moan from beyond, and your followers sprout gossamer, lavender tendrils. Wherever they tread, their new fronds help themselves to flesh, caressing and lashing, clasping and tantalising, bringing shivers of ecstasy to all around.

In dreams, the Perfect Prince touches every mind, granting fevered visions of their darkest desires. The strongest are buoyed by these indescribable peaks of sensation, awakening fulfilled like never before, but the weakest cannot endure. Their spent, desiccated forms crumble, and the very land feeds upon their tormented souls.

A euphoric compulsion takes hold of every soul in the land, and they each proudly send you a missive containing their darkest, guiltiest secret. When reason returns to them, they swear unwavering subservience – in exchange for a promise that their shameful truths shall never be revealed.

Your Fiends learn to howl in a hypnotic harmony that implants an overwhelming suggestion into the minds of all around. Across the land, hands claw feverishly at belt buckles and blouse buttons, walls shake and beds break. Calls for order fall upon deaf ears, for all are lost in bliss.

In a moment of indulgence, you grant one of your followers the honour of becoming tonight's concubine. Basking in the afterglow of pleasure and suffering beyond all mortal imagining, they henceforth carry themselves with unshakeable confidence, convinced of their own greatness.

Your perfumiers have designed a new scent to confound the senses, one which causes all those who inhale it to helplessly bellow their deepest desires aloud. By dousing themselves in this delicious fragrance, your Daemonettes are granted all the insight they need to bewitch their weak-minded foes.

As one, your followers begin to skip in and out of existence. One second they are there, one second they are not, then they reappear, and so forth. With each reappearance, they sport fresh new feathers, resplendent in blue and gold, and speak in a different tongue.

A swarm of shimmering blue-pink sigils appears suddenly upon every available surface, each one contradicting the last. Some who gaze upon them strike up uncontrolled screaming, while others chant in a tongue unrecognisable to even Tzeentch's most trusted servants. It is then that the sigils begin to whisper.

An eerie freneticism falls upon your scribes as they study their tomes, refusing rest and sustenance. As they read, their craniums swell and swell, until their engorged brains spill from their skulls – yet still they read. On the ninth morning, their vast minds consume the rest of their malnourished forms.

Wealth is a dull necessity in the mortal realm, but there are ways to make its acquisition more entertaining. Deep in His Impossible Fortress, the Changer inscribes a flaming rune into the very air. Far away, a single ear of each of your followers is transmuted into solid gold.

Those of your followers lucid enough to care report strange behaviour from their own shadows. The shades appear to move of their own accord, never quite mirroring the actions of their casters. Soon enough they tear themselves free and stand upright – unnerving yet loyal two-dimensional replicas of those who bore them.

Without warning, nine city-sized blue and yellow runes manifest in the skies. The moment they disappear, the same rune carves itself into the left cheek of all who witnessed it. Their eyes turn immediately white, their mouths seal over and they stand stock-still, awaiting instruction.

Life itself is at grave risk – for [[b]]Nagash[[/b]] has returned and begins his [[b]]Great Ritual[[/b]]!\\nA ritual to drain the life from the world itself, leaving an Undead Wasteland completely subservient to the Great Necromancer. As his Black Pyramid rises into the skies, swollen with the Winds of Shyish, its destination is clear and its path cannot be interrupted. The final battle for the fate of the world will take place at the fortress city of Nagashizzar.\\n\\nThe world teeters on the precipice of eternal darkness – is there any champion capable of defeating one who has overcome death itself?
Nagash and his Mortarchs lead his Undead Legions across the whole world, Undead factions loyal to Nagash have also become vassalised

Once the Great Ritual begins Nagash's power level cannot be changed, it is crucial to reduce his power level as much has possible before the final battle
Nagash's armies are empowered during the Endgame, the strength of their bonuses is tied to the number of active Mortarchs, armies and Devastated provinces

All Skaven factions have [[b]]united under Skreech Verminking[[/b]]. Every Skaven Legendary Lord and their territory has joined the Vermintide – the Great Ascendancy is here!
It is [[b]]critical[[/b]] to defeat Vermintide armies, with each defeated army providing a chance to [[b]]learn more about their plans[[/b]] and receive items that can help overcome the Endgame.
Vermintide settlements are always visible, acting as access points to the Under-Empire. Armies will continuously spawn nearby and the larger the settlement, the more armies it can spawn.
Focus on recapturing settlements occupied by the Vermintide quickly to [[b]]limit their ability to spawn armies[[/b]] and destroy Under-Cities as soon as possible to [[b]]slow their spread[[/b]].

Vermintide [[b]]Under-Cities[[/b]] are always visible and [[b]]spread rapidly[[/b]]. The longer one is allowed to exist, the more it will [[b]]sap the wealth[[/b]] of the settlement above – you must act quickly!

All factions fighting against the Vermintide [[b]]receive large diplomatic bonuses[[/b]] with each other while the Endgame is ongoing.
Collect enough [[b]]War Plan Knowledge[[/b]] to learn of the Vermintide's final plans, allowing you to face Skreech Verminking in a final battle to [[b]]achieve Victory[[/b]].

The Black Pyramid, Nagash's greatest legacy, is a construction of pure, malevolent power, and now almost unbelievably it is floating above the desert. The power of the books of Nagash, now gathered and harnessed, has streamed into the pyramid, detaching it from its foundations and lifting it up from the sand dunes below. Surely it is clear for all to see that this is the grand design of the fabled Necromancer who’s name this massive structure bears, and perhaps through unparalleled foresight or through coincidence alone the power emanating from every crevice and block of stone acts as a beacon to all across Nehekhara. Undoubtedly any king or queen with the ability to affect the outcome of this plight will muster their forces and head towards this monument suspended in the sky… only time will tell if this is indeed Nagash’s will manifesting itself.
Through the divine power of the Creator-God, Ptra, your Necrotect has given his life and constructed a mighty city in the once ruined settlement.

A small piece of Nagash’s will is captured within each of his most prized worldly possessions, and his staff is said to hold more of his eternal spirit than any other. With five of his ancient tomes already discovered and within your grasp, there is but a single spark required, a catalyst with which the power of the books can be truly harnessed and your plans to gain access to the Black Pyramid finally realized.\\n\\nSeek out your master’s staff and with it ensure that all enemies of Nagash lie in ashes, along with any doubt as to your eternal loyalty to your master.

Ulthuan is under threat! Isha weeps as enemies swarm the shores of Ulthuan. The populace are unsettled at this turn of events and look to their Everqueen for answers...

Isha and Asuryan have entwined, for Ulthuan is whole! The Asur rejoice; their homeland is safe and under control of the Phoenix Throne; their spiritual wealth is under the Everqueen's guardianship, as it always was and will be.

Houghhoff was a renowned admiral in the imperial navy and his tale is one of bewilderment. The story tells that he kept a bright yellow parrot as a pet that sat upon his shoulder, never leaving his master’s side for a moment. Houghhoff, famous for having never lost a battle at sea, somewhat oddly put the credit for every victory solely with the parrot! Supposedly, during the heat of battle, the parrot squawked key tactical advice, which the admiral would use to soundly beat his opponents.\\n\\nWhether Houghhoff’s parrot was simply uttering madness-induced ramblings or not, his crew could not deny the Reik-Admiral’s resultant mastery of naval combat. So, when one morning Houghhoff exited his cabin and announced to his crew that they were to leave the service of the Empire immediately and become pirates – upon the suggestion of the parrot – everyone aboard simply... agreed.

As a High Elf prince, Fhiron Wavemaker had lived a life of luxury, but – as is the case with many who want for nothing, materially-speaking – eventually began to feel empty and yearned for something more. One afternoon, along the coast of Saphery, he set sail into the mist of the Sea of Dreams in a small sailing boat with no other soul aboard. Upon returning many hours later, Fhiron rushed to the harbour of Port Elistor and had a large vessel commissioned – a weapon of war he would name Wavebreaker.\\n\\nMany months later, with the mighty warship Wavebreaker completed, Prince Fhiron set sail through the Straits of Lothern with a crew made up of the most loyal from his court. Nobody knows exactly what caused him to give up everything and choose a life at sea, but whatever happened that one fateful afternoon in the mist is undoubtedly where it all began…

A once-famous vintner from Bretonnia, Heastie was aboard his trade ship en route to deliver goods to the New World. Near to reaching their destination the ship was beset by an Undead vessel commanded by the legendary pirate Rozov von Drak. As the Unliving stormed Heastie’s ship, sparing not one of his crew, he made his last stand at the helm. Surrounded, and with swords to his throat, his enemy made an offer: join him as a Vampire in Undeath and serve as his first mate. Heastie, without much choice, all things considered, accepted Drak’s offer and so came to serve the Vampire for many years aboard his ship, learning not only the ways of piracy, but also those of Dark Magic.\\n\\nHeastie always harboured his own grand plans for greatness, however. One night, as he stood with von Drak at the helm, Heastie drew his blade and lopped off his master’s head. He stood there as the Skeleton crew crumbled to piles of bones, before raising the lifeless husks once more to serve him. Now as captain of the ship, and with a crew of Undead, he began a reign of terror all his own!
