The Dark Father's will is made manifest; his servants must unite to exterminate the weakling races of the world, to exploit their meagre resources and to expand the borders of the Dark Lands. Zealous and cruel, the lords of Zharr-Naggrund seize their opportunity to dominate the world. This destructive march of Chaos Dwarf industry must be stopped before it leads to ruination for all!
Dark energies manifest atop the spires of Zharr-Naggrund, and the Chaos Dwarfs gather to answer the call of Hashut...

It is only right that the High Priest of Hashut be the one to embrace the Father of Darkness' hellish abode. There the Blood of Hashut runs like molten fire, flowing everywhere in abundance. Such stores of magma will never run dry; a limitless supply of arcane power!\\n\\nWithered and weak no more, this wealth of sorcerous energy will surely grant you power like never before. The greatest Sorcerer-Prophet to ever live will reign in perpetuity!

This is it! The great victory that will finally prove to all the worth of Drazhoath the Ashen, and perhaps bring these years of agonising exile ever closer to an end. The Blood of Hashut is yours to control, a near endless source of power for the arcane arts. None can question you now, not when the terrible glory of Hashut's realm has been revealed to you alone!

Hashut's realm of darkness and flame has been breached, where his Blood runs freely in scorching rivers of fire. Soon all will know that Zhatan the Black, Commander of the Tower of Zharr, was the one to receive this twisted blessing.\\n\\nWith this power at your fingertips, none could ever hope to stop you. A reign of tyranny awaits, and delicious cruelties beyond imagining!

Down among the black smoke and searing heat of the Hell-Forge, where Hashut's grim, unholy work is done, the Daemonsmiths and Sorcerer-Prophets of Zharr-Naggrund have made exciting new advances. Increasing their skills in both sorcery and engineering has led the Dark Father's children to the following advantageous developments, that will no doubt put them even further ahead of the pathetic machinations of their foes.

Due to a shortage of Armaments in the Hell-Forge, certain Manufactory upgrades have been deactivated.\\n\\nAny effects granted by the affected upgrades will be inactive until your Armaments supply is sufficient to cover the required Hell-Forge upkeep.

Ulrika’s destruction is the only thing that will balance the scales of justice. However, as crafty as ever, she broke free of her bonds and escaped into the night's cloak of frozen darkness. Though the people's righteous thirst for retribution was not to be sated this day, they were at least happy that the Vampire's execution was ordered. \\n\\n Now, however, Ulrika Magdova roams the land freely once more. Though she may be encountered again, if she will work for or against us remains to be seen.

Clearly, though Ulrika and Gabriella are no friends of the Ruinous Powers, they cannot be allowed to act of their own accord. Ulrika will not return to Nachthafen Castle, but will instead continue her training in our service. While many are unhappy with this decision, perhaps she will find redemption through fighting our enemies or peace in a noble death? \\n\\n Ulrika Magdova has been recruited!

[[fragment:3600|60]][[i]]The Launch Site is made ready at a speed so furious it becomes a mass graveyard for hundreds of exhausted workers; expendable lives, for only the drill is of concern.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:8000|60]][[i]]The remaining construction must be imbued with dark sorcery, for the Blood of Hashut lies, not only in the darkest depths of the world, but in a godly domain where no mortal engine can reach it.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:3000|60]][[i]]Four Dwarf relics are required, each to be corrupted in the forges of the Daemonsmiths. [[fragment:2500|60]]Only then shall the drill summon power enough to shatter solid rock and the foundations of reality itself.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:1500|60]][[i]]As the abhorrent relics lie undiscovered, a sacrifice must be undertaken to gain Hashut's blessing and reveal their locations.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:7000|60]][[col:green]]To access the endless supply of Hashut's blood, you must complete the Great Drill of Hashut to bore directly into His domain.[[/col]]

[[fragment:1000|60]][[i]]Relics hold great power, yet such strength will not wake in the hands of the Chaos Dwarfs, and so the Daemonsmiths must corrupt the artefacts, turning them into weapons worthy of Zharr-Naggrund![[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:10000|60]][[i]]Such potent magic takes a hideous toll on those who wield its might. [[fragment:3000|60]]The halls of Zharr-Naggrund are lined with the frozen forms of past Sorcerers, their statues standing in mute testament to the curse of petrification – the blight of all Chaos Dwarf Sorcerers.[[/i]]

[[fragment:2000|60]][[i]]When a single bead of Hashut’s Blood drips upon the relic, a deadly broth begins to boil as if in rage, the liquid doubling in volume.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:6500|60]][[i]]Determined to turn this unholy reaction to their own advantage, a coven of Daemonsmiths start to experiment with the infernal mercury...[[/i]]

[[fragment:2500|60]][[i]]The cunning and cruelty of Daemonsmiths, is equally matched by a voracious greed for knowledge.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:4500|60]][[i]]Further experiments reveal the blood of captive Dwarfs thickening – a physical toll of their masters’ dark sorcery. [[fragment:3500|60]]This petrification by proxy is seized on by the coven as a chance to escape the awful curse that hangs over their tribe.[[/i]]

[[fragment:2000|60]][[i]]The Daemonsmiths refine their dark recipe to an astounding conclusion. [[fragment:4000|60]]A Sorcerer may practice his infernal power without suffering the effects of petrification, transposing the affliction to enemies through a Daemonic blood pact.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:5500|60]][[i]]At last, the long-feared curse has been circumvented, freed from their shackles, the Chaos Dwarf Sorcerers can indulge without penalty.[[/i]]

[[fragment:6000|60]][[i]]The Hell-workers labour to bind a Daemon to the first Dwarf relic, despoiling it completely, before placing it into boilers of the Great Drill of Hashut.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:7300|60]][[i]]Such desecration will be remembered by the Dwarfs of the west, yet it was they that cast the first stone. [[fragment:3800|60]]It was their Ancestor Gods who abandoned the forefathers of the Dawi-Zharr as they ventured eastward into the Dark Lands.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:2800|60]][[i]]All Dwarfs can bear grudges, and those in the west shall never be forgiven![[/i]]

[[fragment:3500|60]][[i]]A second relic bound with a Daemon to power the furnaces of the Colossal Drill. [[/i]][[fragment:2000|60]][[i]]Yet, unknown to the Daemonsmiths, the hidden runes of the artefact pull the beards of Dwarfs hundreds of leagues away.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:11500|60]][[i]]Word spreads across the Karaz Ankor on its way to Everpeak. One clan, eager to enact vengeance, musters its warriors.[[/i]]

[[fragment:3000|60]][[i]]The third Daemon lends brutal strength to the engines of the drill.[[/i]] [[fragment:1500|60]][[i]]Yet, as this vile spirit writhes in the final throes of freedom, it spits out a message of mockery.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:5000|60]][[i]]This bitter prophecy forecasts the union of the Mountain Realms; that a mighty army amasses to right the grudge that burns on the pages of the Dammaz Kron, for the desecration of their holy relics.[[/i]]

[[fragment:4000|60]][[i]]With the fourth relic Daemon-bound, the Great Drill has the power to breach Hashut’s Domain. The mighty construct begins to thrum and quiver, shaking the ground as it prepares to launch its fearsome assault.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:7000|60]][[i]]Yet beyond the Ash Ridge Mountains, the ground shakes in ominous echo, for a vast alliance marches under the banner of High King Thorgrim Grudgebearer.[[fragment:5000|60]] The grudge of all grudges shall be settled![[/i]]

[[fragment:2000|60]][[i]]Captured in battle, the western kin are slaughtered one by one, and offered as sacrifice to Hashut, the Father of Darkness.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[fragment:4500|60]][[i]]The Great Bull God is pleased with the savage offerings and reveals the locations of eight Dwarfen relics.[[/i]]

Proving beyond all doubt that they are favoured by the Gods, {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has enforced its will over nearly an entire continent. We should ensure that either relations are friendly or our forces are ready and able to crush them.

Following a string of impressive victories, {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has become a major power. It is imperative for us to make plans to deal with them, either with overwhelming military force or cunning diplomacy.
The garrison stationed in {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} has taken the field as a reserve force!

Within your lands, one rule holds true: trespassers deserve no mercy! The Hex of the [[col:yellow]]Coven's Cursemark[[/col]] has already found its target, sapping them of energy until every movement is a struggle. They will not run far, should you decide to hunt them down…

A dark curse has befallen your army, afflicting your soldiers with a paralysing lethargy. Trespassing in foreign lands is never without risk, but none could have anticipated the threat of such a dark and twisted Hex!

There one moment and gone the next, a whole army has disappeared into the ether, swept up in the [[col:yellow]]Jinxed Land[[/col]] Hex and deposited into the dark. The Magical Forest shall be there to greet them, once their eyes have adjusted to the gloom.

A sudden wave of magic has swept over your army, whisking them into a dark and forbidding forest, where curious eyes seem to peer out from every shadow. Such a Hex could only be the work of a powerful witch indeed…

An army of darkness descends on your enemies! With their settlement under constant assault by the bloodthirsty spirits summoned by your [[col:yellow]]Recreant Spirit[[/col]] Hex, it is only a matter of time before they crumble.

Dark spirits haunt your every step, eager to have you join their ranks and drag you into death beside them. Driven by some kind of wicked curse, they march ceaselessly on your settlement, hungering for blood. One can only hope this Dark Magic will soon wane!

The weak are so easily broken! Like puppets, your enemies fall to the [[col:yellow]]Bewitching Lure[[/col]], dancing to whatever tune you command of them. With your new thralls siphoning gold from their own settlements, your riches will soon know no bounds!

A treacherous Hag has beguiled your people, bewitching those of weak mind to her will. As gold leeches from your coffers at an alarming rate, it would seem that her newfound thralls are quietly offering her your income!

The words of the [[col:yellow]]Purification Chant[[/col]] echo across the land, burning all traces of corruption from the soil. No longer shall wickedness taint the earth here – the balance of nature has been restored.

You have discovered a new [[col:yellow]]Trinket[[/col]]! Combine it with another in the Witch's Hut to create an [[col:yellow]]Incantation[[/col]] to bless your units or curse the enemy on the battlefield.
Machinations stemming from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} has led to an explosion of Tzeentchian corruption in the area!
The Changer of Ways has struck - machinations stemming from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} has led to an explosion of Tzeentchian corruption in the area!

A rift to the Realm of Chaos opened for a brief moment within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}}, giving a host of hostile Daemons time to pour through! Our settlement is at risk from this newly emerged threat. This must be the work of that accursed scheming Trickster: the Changeling!

Your cultists within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} have opened a rift to the Realm of Chaos, giving passage to a host of menacing Daemons! The rampaging horde have destroyed the rift, and now turn their Daemonic gaze upon {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}.

We have discovered a Trickster Cult of the Changeling within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}}! We must act fast and spend the required amount to destroy it before it becomes more than a mere nuisance!

Overexpansion of your Trickster Cult in {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} has led to it being discovered by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}! They may now decide to allocate funds to ensure its utter destruction!

A cult of the Changeling has revealed itself within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}}, calling forth an army of Daemons and Warriors of Chaos! Their exact scheme is unclear, but they could assault your settlement at any moment. You must be ready for anything from the devious Trickster!

Your cultists within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} have rallied a great host of both and Daemons and mortals outside the settlement. Your agents responsible for this deed are no more, but instead a grand army is ready to do your bidding.
A new Trickster Cult has been established in {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}}! Your cultists have successfully infiltrated the settlement and are ready to enact your devious schemes.

Your settlement in {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} has been raided from within! The nefarious agents of the Changeling somehow infiltrated the region and have made off with much of the region's wealth.

Your cultists within {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} have emerged from hiding, raiding the region's spoils for your ever-growing war chest! This will surely anger {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}, but that's no concern of yours!

Interlopers have struck at one of your Astromantic Relays in {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}}, interrupting the ritual. You will have to construct a relay again if you wish to succeed, but be wary, for the adherents of the great plan are sure to be wiser to your actions.

Trespassing upon a Witch's land is a dangerous game. When the Daughters of the Forest wail in unison, they sear onto the flesh of interlopers a sinister mark that turns the very magic of the world against them. The Coven's Cursemark ensures one thing for its target: despair.

The world’s Magical Forests call to the Daughters, revealing gateways long since hidden to the uninitiated. No matter the distance or what lies between, the Coven can traverse their secret ingresses in the blink of an eye.

Those foolish enough to strike a deal with a Hag find that death is merely the beginning of an unending serfdom. The power to call upon these restless spirits has been found; a Hex to haunt unknowing foes now in the Coven’s hands.
Fickle minds are always susceptible to the whims of an alluring charm from a befouling Hag. Witchcraft is but one of many ways to sway them, a Bewitching Lure to exploit those weak of will.
There are places where the Coven’s magic seeps from the land, befouled by the blight of corruption. The Daughters answer with a purifying chant to purge the rot, at least for a time.

The five forbidden Hexes have been assembled, each piece a scattered fragment of a grand and sinister whole. Together they reveal a most baleful Hex, capable of bringing calamity to an entire race. They call it the "Malediction of Ruin".

The Black Pyramid ascends from the sand-swept deserts, casting down a looming shadow of death as it glides through the skies. The dark monument’s descent spells Ruin for its next unfortunate destination, its Undead hosts eager to emerge to greet their new neighbours…

A nightmarish Blood Knight has plagued Bretonnia for years, but a certain Trickster’s meddling sees new Vampiric thralls arise under his command to threaten the population. Now stronger than ever, the Red Duke leaves naught but death in his wake. May the Lady fall to his unending wrath…

The Changeling has little interest in the Great Game, but opportunity presents a fitting backdrop for a rendezvous most bloody. Thus Tzeentch sees it fit to unleash hordes of Daemonic thralls against those who oppose him – and what a sight it is to behold.

Freed from the shackles of servitude to uncaring masters, swathes of Labourers sweep through the Dark Lands in a rebellious frenzy. Years of pent-up fury has started to erupt; the Changeling’s scheme now unfolding in anarchy and uprising.

Not even the walled lands of Cathay can withstand the relentless meddling of Tzeentch’s Trickster. The Great Bastion has been breached by a mere scurrying rat, as warbands and followers of Tzeentch advance upon Cathay with Ruinous intent.

Despite Tzeentch’s endless hatred for Nurgle, the Changeling is more than happy to play with every toy within his reach. Having helped the Skaven propagate contagion throughout Lustria, the odour of decay now festers in lands long untainted. And thus, the rot of plague infects all in its path…

Masses of bloated Undead crawl out from the ocean’s depths, fixated on the Land of Chill’s bustling ports. The Changeling’s meddling has them shuffling their distended remains towards Naggaroth’s harbours with naught but blood on their withering minds.

Norscan warriors unceasingly crave the thrill of battle, many wandering for decades just to seek a worthy fight. Yet their wills are weak – easily malleable once broken by the Changeling. Thus they march upon a new target, guided by his hand…

Like a house of cards, the authority of the Empire can be a fragile thing. A simple yet dastardly scheme has ensured its lands have descended into civil war – for the Changeling, a spectacle wholly worth his engagements with the petty, bickering mortals.

Not even the Shifting Isles can protect Ulthuan from the seductive whims of those who now descend upon its shores. The Changeling’s scheming turns the gaze of Slaanesh’s thralls unto the island-haven, its settlements now a frontline against their depravities.
The Winds of Magic now flow from where the Dragon Emperor’s personnel watch over the Ivory Road. Power ebbs from a grand watchtower of jade and jet toward the great Wu Xing Compass.
Death befalls all who enter the magical waters of the Dragon River uninvited. But as the Winds of Magic flow in Cathayan favour, its ill-effects can be harnessed for far more than merely death alone…
The Winds of Magic betwixt the scarred earth of the Broken Lands surge towards the Wu Xing Compass – and with them, a foreboding rush of power to the armies of the Jade Court.

The completion of this relay ensures the mighty Winds of Magic are guided in a new direction. The Nongchang Basin holds magic beneath its fertile soil. The Wu Xing Compass can now direct it for the true benefit of Cathay.

An Amber Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Beasts and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Amber Order.\\n\\nGhur echoes through the veins of those attuned to the Brown Wind of Magic, heard like the cry of a soaring eagle in the midst of flight. Its power grants control over the creatures of the wild, as well as the ability to assume their strength, and hunt down their enemies as prey.

An Amethyst Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Death and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Amethyst Order.\\n\\nDrawing power from the residual Shyish surrounding the deceased, a practitioner of the Purple Wind of Magic exists with one foot in the mortal realm and the other in the beyond. Though frequently found communing with spirits and wielding power over the dead, Brethren take care not to stray into the realms of true Necromancy.

A Bright Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Fire and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Bright Order.\\n\\nEmbracing the raging flame of Aqshy, the pyromancers that channel the Red Wind of Magic burn a path through the enemies of the Empire. Destructive and violent, the Bright Wizards' fires can be summoned as a searing ball of flame, or wielded as a flaming sword that slashes out at the Emperor's foes.

A Celestial Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Heavens and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Celestial Order.\\n\\nEmpowered by the energies of Azyr that surge among the stars, the members of the Celestial Order have honed their masteries of scrying and astromancy. As those wielding the Blue Winds of Magic take to the battlefield, they draw their strength from the upper atmosphere of the mortal world.

A Grey Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Shadow and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Grey Order.\\n\\nScorned by some as Trickster Wizards, the self-proclaimed Grey Guardians work beneath the veil of darkness, embracing the energies of Ulgu to cast illusions and sow confusion among their foes. In ventures of conspiracy, subterfuge and scheming, all is facilitated by the Grey Wind of Magic.

A Jade Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Life and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Jade Order.\\n\\nCommonly called Druids by those unfamiliar with the Green Wind of Magic, the Wizards of the Green Order channel Ghyran to exert control over the soil itself, allowing flowers to bloom and nature to flourish. With a healing hand, the most skilled practitioners may even mend grievous wounds, restoring soldiers to health.

A Light Wizard joins our ranks, wielding the Lore of Light and enabling the [[col:yellow]]Colleges of Magic[[/col]] actions of the Light Order.\\n\\nWhere darkness lingers, it shall be banished by the hierophants of the Light Order, who wield Hysh to oppose Chaos in all its forms. The serpentine staff of a Light Wizard is often used as a magical sentinel, shielding and protecting the Empire's soldiers just as easily as it might punish the wicked with its radiance.

Where once the Greenskin menace wrought havoc under the Nemesis Crown's sway, peace now reigns in their stead. With the Crown removed from the foul Night Goblin head upon which it sat, the threat to the Empire has been thoroughly extinguished.
Elspeth has long standing alliances with the Cult of Morr. With each new Gardens she errects a new Tower that she might call home.
The enemies of the empire have taken this region as their own and burnt the Gardens and Elspeth's Tower alike to the ground.
Elspeth atop her mighty Carmine Dragon makes haste to return to one of her Black Towers.

When the Cult of Morr establishes new Gardens, Elspeth is given the opportunity to establish new towers in return for her aid in times of need.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gardens_of_morr_view_panel}}

The Dwarfs have been hard at work striking Grudges from the Book – the current lack of Grudges to settle has become a testament to the collective Dawi resolve to right all their wrongs. The final thing to grumble about is what they will they do with themselves once there's nothing left to grumble over!

{{tr:unit_abilities_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_army_abilities_purple_eclipse}} has blocked out the sun for the last time, at least until our wizards can channel enough Winds of Shyish to create another terrifying feat of engineering.

After an extended period away from the homeland, you have finally returned. Whatever the current state of the Empire, it is now your duty alongside others who remain here to protect our lands.\\n\\nLearn more about Imperial Authority [[url:script_link_campaign_imperial_authority]]here[[/url]].

Some dare defy us - we shall sour relations between {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. In the long-term this will be far more destructive than a direct strike.

By planting some key pieces of evidence we can make it look as though {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has been secretly worshipping a god that {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} finds particularly offensive. They will deny, and therefore look guilty.

While our ambassadors will not outright lie, they can target certain truths that may sound far worse out of context. And so we whisper in the ear of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} that {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} is not to be trusted.

Our trade routes are reliable and well-patrolled, if others want to use them they must pay. However, if we levy an additional tithe on {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and claim it is not our tax but one demanded by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}, then relations will surely sour.

A Caravan of precious baubles important to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has gone missing. Our agents may have been responsible, but placing a few corpses belonging to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} should switch the blame to them.

A generous gift has been received by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. Unbeknownst to both, the shipment was intercepted en route, the gifts replaced by inferior copies in much lower quantities than promised.

{{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has been specifically forbidden to act this way due to a pact signed by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. They have done no such thing of course, but our agents will tell the signee otherwise.

We offer our services as a neutral party to negotiate a trade agreement between {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. While our factors smile and encourage, they will be briefing against the interests of both.

A wagon full of high-quality blades and armour has been delivered to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}. It is mere child’s play to insinuate that this gift is from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} – they will be too stupid and flattered to deny it!

There’s nothing clever or subtle here, simply our agent disguising themselves though mundane and arcane means into a factor of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and giving a large gift of precious things to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}.

Let the races believe the notion that we dwindle but that our reach is still vast, our power to adjudicate and even dictate trade relations remains unchallenged. Granting {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} favourable trade relations will strengthen relations between them, for our gain.

While the younger races frolic and fight we take advantage for our gains. Let us advise {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} to make overtures to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. If they think it is their own idea, then more’s the better!

Nothing fosters relations than the death of a common foe. So, sending hated corpses to both {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}, and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}, each with missives attached to the bodies claiming credit, should fool these two factions into strengthening their bonds.

Our embassies are often thought of as neutral ground to even the most hated of foes. Nothing could be further from the truth, obviously, but we control the environment and manipulate everything from ambience to the subject of conversation, ensuring that {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} are more predisposed to each other.

Diverting an enemy into the ambush range of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} is the first part of the ploy; letting them keep the gold we planted on the convoy will lead them to a more favourable relationship with {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}, whose sigil is stamped into the hoard.

We have many relics in our archives, trinkets to us but sacred for others. A gift given to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}, will make them more receptive to our scheme of including {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} in the next phase.

Wagons full of imperial goods frequently depart to foreign lands. A particularly large convoy disappeared, however. An investigation found the merchants and guards tied to trees and all the wagons plundered. The foreign lord denies any responsibility, but even a child knows that he is to blame for not keeping the roads clear.

A noble has managed to get himself in an embarrassing position. While a foreign dignitary was visiting, rumours started circulating that the noble was ridiculing the foreign delegation behind their backs and even hired a few jesters to give a private performance to mock them. Of course the noble denied it, but a few days later, a letter addressed to his wife surfaced, in which he expressed his disdain for the foreign dignitary. The delegation departed at once and spread the stories of their mistreatment back home.

The wife of a local baron went missing without a trace. Weeks pass and searches return nothing. At the next full moon however, she is found dead and mutilated, hanging above the city gate. A letter was stuffed into her throat, with another faction expressing their hatred for the baron and claiming responsibility.
An influential Lord found a small box on the doorstep of his castle. Upon opening it, he discovered an exquisite jewel, along with a note from an unexpected foreign admirer...

An exotic Caravan appears in mankind's realm, claiming to be from a foreign kingdom. Their goods are of high quality and their prices low. Intrigued by the opportunities of trade, merchants soon flock to the foreign territory in the hopes of securing a good deal.

Seemingly random lords received an invitation of a tournament hosted near Nuln. Upon arrival, they discovered that the tournament grounds have been set up and a foreign delegation was already present. But the foreigners claim they received a similar invitation, and no-one knows who is the host, nor how the tournament grounds were erected. A crate with a massive golden trophy is soon discovered. Both sides agree to compete honourably, with the winning faction receiving the trophy. After the festivities end, both sides agree they had a great time together and the tournament should become an annual event.

While they can be blunt, the Asur tend to veil insults through the arts. In the name of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}, commission a particularly stinging song about {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}. Don’t forget a catchy chorus to ensure it travels beyond court.

Have our servants talk to the serfs of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}, let them spread vicious gossip about the plans of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. Such talk shall quickly work its way up to the Nobles.

{{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} has the manners of a drunk Dwarf! Such a lack of eloquence does not go unnoticed. Of course, this may have been exacerbated by potion poured into their wine. Nevertheless, it reflects badly on the host, {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}.

The simplest ploys are often the most effective. Through the chatter of court, let it be known that {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} have been overheard defaming Finubar, wondering if he is up to the duties that come with the crown.

There is a constant fear that anyone in Ulthuan could be one of the Witch King’s agents in deep cover. It is almost too easy to lay a whispered suggestion that the life partner of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} takes orders from Naggarond. Just ensure they know the rumour came from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}.

To accuse {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} of worshipping the gods of the underworld is a serious charge. Although not technically illegal, it is frowned upon, and the loss of standing in the Phoenix Court will be quick. So, proof is needed, which is why you have installed a statue of Atharti at the accused estate, with a note of appreciation from {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}.

The Cults of Pleasure are insidious. The gossip at court is that {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} attended a party hosted by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} and the excesses witnessed were scandalous. The talk is untrue, of course, but the more they deny, the faster the rumour spreads.

The most effective way to damage relationships is to insinuate rather than use a Dawi’s bluntness. A half-jape to a prince here, a missive sent to an outer kingdom that doesn’t give the full story there… soon there is suspicion between {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}. As we intended.

A careful discussion here, a subtle word over wine there, a smile that lingers, an eyebrow raised over a jest - all things men and Dwarfs would never pick up on. But for the Asur these are powerful social symbols, signs of alliance between two great houses of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}.

Our kin take great store in words and verse. Send a poet to the estates of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} so that they may sing a verse, commissioned by us, of the great relations between them and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}.

The game of court has winners and losers; the fate of houses can be lost not just by invasion but by their Prince’s performance at court. Lending vocal support to {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} at court will enhance their relationship with {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}.

Business at the Phoenix Court rarely happens while the king attends and deals with matters of state. It is when the Princes and Nobles splinter off to the alcoves and form informal sub-committees that things get done and so, over a few cups of wine, the binding of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} and {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}} can begin.

Finubar’s war council is not an official organisation, more the Phoenix King’s close associates that guide and advise on matters of war. To be invited into the council is a great honour, so engineer {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}’s participation with {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} to improve their relations.

Taking on a ward or squire from another house is a good way of exerting soft power and strengthening lasting bonds between two houses or kingdoms. And so {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} has taken a princeling of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}.

The favour of Finubar will do wonders for any great Elven house. Ensure {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}} receives patronage of the Phoenix King. Make it known through courtly gossip that it was fostered by {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:SecondTargetFactionName}}.
Rumours in the wind talk of other Lords searching for the Nemesis Crown, you better find it before someone else does.

The Nemesis Crown has been discovered and now the ancient artefact rests upon a new brow. The malevolent power of the crown possesses its new master, {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} of {{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetFactionName}}!

The Nemesis Crown has once again disapeared from the world. [[i]]Spending her days secluded in her towers and experimenting with rare mystic artefacts, {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_emp_cha_elspeth_von_draken}} stands ready as a true defender of the Empire.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[i]]Her strength is needed now more than ever, for the {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh3_main_ogr_feastmaster}} Ogres encroach upon Wissenland, while the Vampires to the east pose an ever increasing threat.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[i]]The Countess Emmanuelle von Liebwitz beseeches the Dark Lady for aid![[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Defeat the factions of the {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh3_main_ogr_feastmaster}}, {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh_main_vmp_waldenhof}} and {{tr:factions_screen_name_wh_main_vmp_vampire_counts}} to reveal the Empire’s greater threats.[[/col]]

[[i]]Rumours trickle across the land of an ancient power unearthed; a rising tide of malevolence festering in the heart of the Empire. As danger grows within the lands Elspeth von Draken has sworn to defend, she stands ready to act against whispers manifesting into a deadly threat.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[i]]Elspeth has received a flood of visions, revealing a possible location of a dangerous artefact that she is strongly compelled to seek out: the Nemesis Crown.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Elspeth’s visions have revealed a keep, surrounded by mountains.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Use any army to search for this location by ending turn with them in the correct region.[[/col]]

[[i]]A Greenskin horde touts control of the Nemesis Crown, an ancient artefact harkening from the times of Sigmar, capable of wreaking untold devastation.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[i]]Elspeth must prepare to strike down this wretched menace the moment their leader is revealed, for the fate of the Empire lies at stake.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Defeat the Greenskin army to learn the location of their leader and the crown.[[/col]]

[[i]]The Crown-bearer has been revealed at the head of multiple ravaging armies! Though massacre may await the Imperial militia, Elspeth will defend the Empire at all costs.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[i]]Three formidable Warlords raise tattered banners under the Nemesis Crown's sway – slaying the fiends will weaken the Greenskin menace, leaving the lambs to the lions.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:green]]The final battle for the Nemesis Crown is now available![[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Defeat the three Warlords, Gnashrak Spiderclaw, Icky da Nosepicka and Luggn Biggagit to weaken the Greenskin forces in the final battle, or otherwise fight the final battle with them at full strength.[[/col]]

[[i]]The Mercenaries are somewhat sceptical of the proposed contract's articles of payment: chests of gold and dust in equal proportions; meat that no longer looks like meat; equipment which, at first glance, seems to have been snatched at random from some ancient battlefield. Yet these walking, talking bone collections do lend a certain mystique to proceedings that have piqued the company's interest.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Tomb Kings' envoys exhibit no emotion as one of their own is tossed into a simmering cauldron "by mistake". Upon discovering that very same one had the client's contract etched in his bones, they simply advise that the company eat more conscientiously, for biting into a bone imbued with magic might have unexpected consequences. Something in their toneless voices ensures that by the end of the Ogres' feast, not a single bone has been consumed.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Vampire Coast pirates relay their client's terms quickly and disembark without fanfare, leaving some of their... creatures behind. They appear to have once been Ogres, their bodies even bigger now, heads even smaller by comparison, their, er, contents meant to be a part of the mercenaries' nightly feast. In truth, the pirates consider them too volatile for their ships. The Ogres consider them the equivalent of pre-cooked stew.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]Though the Vampire Coast promises ample rewards, they insist on drawing a map that would lead the Mercenaries to them. The Ogres' protestations are cut short by assurances that the route might garner even more wealth. The pirates are, in fact, certain that it will not, but they themselves have put their Unlives on the line in the face of similarly slim odds, so who knows?[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Cold One Knight delivering the contract might have meant to instil fear, or at least respect. Instead, Bruisers need to keep curious Ogres from poking at the horrific beast, as they have not seen, let alone killed or eaten, such a thing before. In the end, the rider simply gallops off in frustration, dropping the contract behind him at the Mercenaries' feet.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]While Dark Elves obfuscate their plain meanness – as Ogres would call it – by their turgid manner of speech, they make their arrogant ambition with refreshing plainness. Part of that plainness could be due to their intended Mercenary audience, but one suspects they simply enjoy someone else doing their dirty work for them.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The messengers tasked with delivering the contract appear highly uncertain. It is not the that they fear being refused and made a meal of, and neither is it that they doubt the contract will be fulfilled (they appear to not care either way). No, it is that they believe the High Elves' rewards provided would be far in excess of anything the Ogres, or anyone else, for that matter, may offer in return.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh2_main_hef_cha_loremaster_of_hoeth_0}} has been tasked with delivering the contract accompanied by a {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh2_main_hef_inf_phoenix_guard}} unit. He seems to be mildly irked at his companions, doubtlessly used to travelling in more talkative company – as well as dealing with slightly more dignified counterparts. His painstaking effort in explaining the contract, however, lets him preserve a measure of dignity.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Lizardmen envoy has been achingly particular as to when the contract should be delivered, whom he should give it to and whether it should be received in the right hand or the left. Nothing less would do in the name of the Great Plan. The Mercenaries are nonplussed: could it just be the Good-Enough Plan? Those have always worked well in the past, after all...[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Scar-Veteran leading the Lizardmen emissaries is capable of meeting an Ogre's gaze at eye level, which Ogres usually consider a challenge. Before they can issue one, however, he shifts his body slightly, whereupon the rest of the Lizardmen warriors rearrange themselves in a manner vaguely threatening enough for the Mercenaries to remember that, in fact, they have met to come to an agreement, not blows.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The absence of Skaven on the morning after the company's feast is even more conspicuous than usual. They certainly were there before, but they are even more certainly not here now. Yet, there are scratch-marks on the cauldron. Is this… writing? A contract?[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Skaven who have come to present the terms of the client have, unsurprisingly, been denied access to the cauldron's contents; instead, a few Gnoblars have been persuaded to entertain the envoys by taking part in some pigback jousting upon the visitors' backs, whereupon they are quickly whisked off into the night, screaming in confusion.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]From the outside, any Dwarf impinging on an Ogre's stomping grounds might seem like an invitation to a literal stomping, but Chaos Dwarfs are well-known to Ogre Mercenaries for both their toughness and their willingness to provide contract work. Their wealth is supremely tempting, their miserly demeanour supremely frustrating. The promise of riches usually prevails.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The foul runes carved on the obsidian plate of the contract makes one's eyes bleed, but the terms inscribed on it makes one's eyes weep with avaricious joy also. The rewards are handily etched as images underneath the writing, whose pain-inducing properties might simply be what the Chaos Dwarfs consider the receipt of transaction.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]Grand Cathay's missive is accompanied by an immaculate line of warriors in finely-lacquered armour, their faces just as impassive. They make no move, waiting for the company's representative to come to them instead. The stalemate continues well into the night, until a Gnoblar drenched in fear-sweat takes the contract and brings it back to the camp.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A sudden explosion at dawn has sent the company into an uproar. On the outskirts of the camp, at the bottom of a crater, they find a small jade casket with a contract inside. The Ogres squint at the clear sky in vain. Nevertheless, the shrewder among them feel they're being watched.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A company of grizzled Kislevite veterans has delivered an offer from their masters. The Mercenaries are intrigued by the Kislevites' scars and missing limbs. The chief perpetrator seems to be frostbite – but also, too many desperate battles for these leather-skinned men to count on their slightly fingerless hands.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Mercenaries are disappointed to see no Bears of any sort among the Kislevite messengers. The messengers themselves know they could not risk instigating an Ogre-Bear brawl where the only ones seriously hurt would be themselves. Some, however, are tempted to send a delegation consisting solely of Bears next time, for they consider their revered animals at least as strong as an Ogre, and definitely smarter.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]Disagreements over meat and gold owed are to be expected when Ogre Mercenaries negotiate with… anyone, really, but only when the client is another Ogre tribe does the back-and-forth take on the savoury tang of murderous camaraderie that promises (or threatens) to conclude negotiations without even having spoken of the enemy.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]While most clients offer Ogre Mercenaries contracts to redress a grievance, be it real or imagined, other Ogres do this as a challenge. They take care to list all the ways in which they have made their puny enemy suffer, something the Mercenaries could not possibly achieve. As reward, they would even stake some of their hard-earned meat and battle prizes. Needless to say, most such contracts are word-of-mouth, and are sealed with a handful of broken teeth.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Wood Elves who deliver the contract are confusingly stoic, to the point where the Mercenaries start wondering whether their masters would miss them if they were to become dinner. Before the troop can make up its mind, a horn rings out in the distance and the strangers are gone as quickly as they'd appeared.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Wood Elves seem annoyed by their mission, idly going over the specifics as quickly as possible, clearly disgusted at being in the presence of Ogres. A few of the Maneaters aren’t appreciating this veiled rudeness but are also aware that the forest is watching them, and one unsavoury move could result in a shower of arrows. Better to just accept the contract and let the bony morsels leave in one piece, this time…[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Norscan envoys are nowhere to be seen. The Mercenaries find themselves in the middle of a fresh battlefield, nameless corpses heaped haphazardly at one end. The contract is written in blood and entrails on the ground. Some of it the Ogres have already started cooking, but there is enough left to understand the gist.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]As soon as the Ogres reach the meeting place, battle is joined. The Norscans scream out their client's demands in between strikes. The Mercenaries are put through its paces but are relieved to find it less of a challenge than if they had to *read* the blasted thing.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Bretonnians delivering the contract are met with an elaborate tale, by way of greeting, of an Ogre who managed to devour an entire Knight Errant, horse, lance and armour included. The envoys' expressions at hearing this would sour even Grail water. And no, even if their rewards include Knightly equipment, they never include the Knight.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A complement of glowering Knights watches from the shadows as a single Grail Damsel presents Bretonnia's offer to the company around the campfire. Afterwards, she ventures a tale, as she has heard it is customary among Ogres. Some are loudly impressed, whereas others become inexplicably silent. All rise as she takes her leave.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A contingent of Dwarf Slayers has delivered a contract from their Lord. Do they know what's in it? No. Do they care? No. Would they themselves enforce the terms should the Ogres fall short? Probably not – Ogre Mercenaries are not nearly worthy enough to fight Slayers, and a Dragon has been spied some miles hence…[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The terms are simple and concise: A contract fulfilled would provide ample remuneration (within reasonable bounds). A contract unfulfilled would be added to the Book, with footnotes detailing the various methods of redress to be employed at the client's convenience.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]As they meet the Imperial delegation, the members of the company are confused as to why one of their number is part of it. Later, it turns out it is not an Ogre Mercenary dressed in scavenged human clothing, but an actual denizen of the Empire. It is unclear whether his presence would predispose them towards or against the offer they are about to receive.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Gold Wizard accompanying the Imperial envoys is almost certainly meant to convey the wealth at the client's disposal, but does everything in his power to express his displeasure at the task, to the collective annoyance of both the Ogre Mercenaries and the Imperials with him. The Burgher in the delegation concludes the negotiations before the Wizard has the chance to transmute the Ogres' cauldron into some prancing, meat-spewing monstrosity.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The company finds the Greenskin emissaries bickering amongst themselves some distance outside the camp. Their shouts, their garish paint and their smell constitute a perfectly coordinated assault on the senses. Luckily, Ogres are well-known for possessing the perfect countermeasures to all that, both in scarcity of mind and surfeit of body. The negotiations proceed surprisingly smoothly.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]The Greenskins' contract is conveyed by a raving Goblin Shaman whose words defy the Mercenaries' collective knowledge of foreign tongues. Upon deciding that what they hear is more akin to the sounds of a dying Squig than it is to speech, they take the piece of parchment from his hand and leave him to his confabulation with the nearby rocks and roots.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]Relentless hunger and the rule of the strongest are two things that Mercenary Ogres and the Vampire Counts have in common. However, the two hungers are not nearly alike, and neither is their understanding of strength. When they meet, they discover the third, and crucial, thing that binds them: their skill for turning misery into profit.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

[[i]]A huge pile of meat lies before the company, yet fires will not start. Instead of the now-useless firewood, the Ogres stare at a stone cairn where a Wight King stands and delivers its client's terms, weapons drawn. Although hunger churns in their guts, the Mercenaries do not move. Then, as the creature begins its speech anew, they turn their backs and sullenly start munching on the raw meat. The Wight King continues speaking until early morning when it departs, disappearing mid-sentence.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_mercenary_contracts_view_panel}}

To kill and subjugate such beings as know only strength, bow only to a savagery greater than their own, whose strongest specimens have elevated themselves to the pinnacles of survival: this is the truest form of what a Norscan can be.

[[i]]The future. For most, an ephemeral, shapeless thing, formed of hopes and fears and petty ambitions. For a chosen few, a path laid out for them by the Dark Gods. For you, however, it is not formless, nor is it a single path of another’s choosing. You have seen your many futures and all end in blood. Your blood. Decades of lies and betrayal have made you undisputed master of the Dolgan lands, but with more enemies than even your twisted sight can fathom.\\n\\nThus far, the servants of Chaos have been as malleable as your imagination, which twisted their wills and beliefs with endless inventiveness. But now, you must draw power directly from its formless, Chaotic source. And your erstwhile puppets may not take your actions in good faith.[[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:green]]The path to the Dark Ritual now lies before you – construct Chaos Altars to gather the arcane power you require![[/col]]

The north has fallen strangely quiet. Archaon the Everchosen has not been seen for many months. No fortress harbours him, no host marches beneath his banner. Even the tribes of the Chaos Wastes speak his name in hushed uncertainty.\\nNever has the Three-Eyed King vanished for so long. Some believe he hunts a weapon worthy of the apocalypse. Others whisper that the Dark Gods themselves have summoned him beyond mortal sight. A few dare suggest he has fallen – though none speak such words loudly, or for long.\\n\\nYet despite his disappearance, the shadow of the Everchosen still looms across the world. All watch the northern horizon with growing unease, wondering not where Archaon has gone...\\n\\n...but what he shall bring when he returns.

Disturbing accounts emerge from the Chaos Wastes. Rival warbands once locked in endless slaughter have begun gathering beneath common symbols. Dark fortresses swell with warriors and beasts. Tribes vanish into the north only to return armed for war, speaking of oaths sworn to a coming master. Though Archaon himself remains unseen, his influence is unmistakable.\\n\\nChampions devoted to rival Dark Gods now march side by side in grim accord. Sorcerers proclaim that the Everchosen prepares for a war greater than any before it, seeking to unite the fractured servants of Chaos beneath a single will.\\n\\nDoom surely approaches, and it is only in strength that any hope may be found!

Archaon is at last defeated. As the last of the Chaos hordes are scoured from the face of the world, an awful silence descends. More than a silence; an absence of sound which echoes the all-consuming void beyond. All creation is stilled, breath held in anticipation of the final cataclysm once thought inevitable.\\n\\nThen, tentatively, gently, life reasserts itself. Not in some grand echo of those who sought to end everything, but in the small ways which are themselves life. Birdsong pierces the silence, hesitant at first, then swelling; a defiant hymn to creation, borne upon a soft wind that sifts dust across the scattered corpses littering the bloody plain of battle. And the spell is broken. Bloodied veterans, survivors, refugees – all draw breath into their aching lungs and weep at the taste and smell of victory, peace, and life.\\n\\nYet what is life, if not the constant striving of one against another? After all, every hedgerow is a bloody battleground, every plant a murderer, every creature red in tooth and claw. Even as the weak raise their eyes toward a golden future, the wise glance about to see who will make the first move in seizing it for themselves. The world may have been spared its ending this day, but those who remain know well that Ruin is patient, and the struggle against it eternal.

The hunter's claims held truth! The tracks belonged to a Jabberslythe – the hunter would have suffered a dreadful end without the Graf's armed escort to slay the beast. Praise Ulric for the fine hunt!

The province of Middenland is once more united under Boris Todbringer's banners, yet the celebrations are short. The Empire is under attack from all sides; forces of Chaos and Undead hordes assault the provinces.\\n\\nThe Emperor calls for a united front, but the Graf remains wary of the hidden threat within his own borders. Khazrak One-Eye lurks somewhere deep within the Drakwald forest, waiting to strike at a moments notice. Todbringer cannot rest until the Beastmen filth have been purged, but neither will he abandon his Emperor.\\n\\nNow is the time for action. For bravery. For battle! Let Ulric's enemies gather, for the Wolf God's faithful are ready. TO WAR!\\n\\n[[col:yellow]][[b]]DRAKWALD THREAT ENABLED[[/b]]\\nBeastmen armies will appear around Middenland throughout the campaign. The chance for an army to appear and its strength is tied to the Drakwald Threat level. Over time the Drakwald Threat level will increase, but it can be decreased by defeating Beastmen armies.[[/col]]\\n[[col:green]]Improve the Sacred Flame of Ulric to unlock a final confrontation with Khazrak One-Eye, removing the Drakwald threat forever.[[/col]]
Khazrak's forces have been beaten back and will take time to regain strength.\\n\\n[[col:green]]Beastmen invasions are weaker and less likely to appear.[[/col]]
Khazrak's forces are gathering in strength!\\n\\n[[col:red]]Beastmen invasions are stronger and more likely to appear.[[/col]]

An unusual number of missing person reports have been filed in recent days – upon closer inspection, the hunter who sought the Graf's audience is listed among them.\\n\\nIt would appear the Hunter's tale held some truth. What happened to him and his fellow villagers was an avoidable tragedy.

The battle was fierce and the Elves fought to the last, each taking a dozen Gor with them. However, their numbers ultimately failed them as they were trampled into the underbrush, though Boris' forces made short work of the remaining Beastmen.\\n\\nThe spoils of this battle are rich, and the Graf is not above looting from those who will not miss their riches in the afterlife. Before leaving, however, he orders the men to pile up the Elf corpses and burn them. He may not know the funeral rites of the Elves, but he is certain they would not want their bodies tainted with the blood of the Beasts that slayed them.

Any doubts Boris had about how his men may be welcomed into this battle by the Wood Elves immediately vanished. They were surely doomed had Todbringer not intervened, as the Elves were outnumbered 20 to 1.\\n\\nThe battle was hard and many men lost their lives to save the Asrai, something that will weigh on the Graf's conscience forever more. Was it right to trade the lives of his men for these temporary allies?\\n\\nThough few words were exchanged before the forest warriors disappeared back into the canopy, one thing was clear – those that survived this battle were truly grateful and Boris' actions would be remembered.
They will not cease until they are cleansed from Middenland's soil!
The monsters that slaughtered the innocent Hamlet have been found – now is the time to bring them to justice!

Some may say this day was inevitable, but none could have foreseen the scale of the Beastmen threat that emerged. The mighty Drakwald itself shudders under the heavy hooves of the warherds as they begin their rampage.\\nThousands of Beastmen pour from the forest, bleating and foaming at the mouth; amongst their numbers are gruesome monsters and hideous spawn of Chaos. The bloodthirst of the beasts is palpable, a testament to Khazrak One-Eye's ability to direct such savage creatures.\\n\\nThough Middenland is no stranger to these abominations, the scale of this assault is unheard of in modern times. It falls to Boris Todbringer to rally the men of Middenland once more, shake the fear that grips their hearts, and fill them with courage and fervour.\\n\\n[[i]]"These monsters think us prey? Proof of their lowly intellect! We are Ulric's faithful, we have the Wolf God at our back, and this is OUR hunt! To battle!"[[/i]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Beastmen armies are mustering around Middenland – hurry to these markers before the armies reach full strength and begin their assult.[[/col]]

Through all the turmoil and harrowing struggle, Boris Todbringer's obsession remained true to Ulric's predatory single-mindedness. Righteous vengeance was a mighty fuel for the Wolf of Winter's eternal fire.\\n\\nThe mindless viciousness of Beastmen and their taint of Chaos has now been burnt out from the Drakwald forever. Challenges no doubt remain - yet all with all their faith in their leader and their god vindicated, Ulric's followers will walk the path in front of them free of all doubt and fear.
The Sacred Flame flickers as the [[col:yellow]]Great Temple of Ulric[[/col]] opens to Ulric's loyal followers.\\n\\nCrush the enemies of the Empire in the Wolf God's name to empower your faction.

They come from the Chaos Realms – these immortal creatures of magic, who leave devastation and destruction in their wake as they seek to conquer and destroy for the Dark Gods. Prepare yourselves, for the servants of the Chaos Gods will not rest until the world is given to their masters!

Such was Nagash's arrogance that he had built for himself a tomb that dwarfed even the Great Pyramid of Settra. The broken corpses of countless slaves were built into its foundations, and mystic sigils of power were woven into the Black Pyramid's walls.

In search of the bones of fresh recruits, a grand, tomb-ridden expanse has been discovered, and its hoard unearthed. Within collapsed chambers, ancient tomes speak of forgotten rituals for protection against necromancy. The inverse of these methods can be used to feed the fruit of necromancy by simpler means – to animate the witless dead and make more pliable the wits of those who still possess some.

Those risen in faithful service to Nagash are pawns for his terrible and majestic designs. War is but one of those purposes. Such souls as have hoped and suffered most plentifully are fit for feeding the power of the Sigils burning upon his Pyramid's chambers.

Some mortal priests have united in their weakness and "blessed" the land with halting incantations of protecting the dead, attempting to deny Nagash the servants that rightfully belong to him. The land and the Winds have been tainted by their desperation. It shall wash away in time, just as all else will.

There is no concern for tactics, for your will is not your own. There is no concern for those of the enemy, for they are nothing but idle shuffling before the Undead tide drowns them. There is no concern for petty matters such as mortality, for it is already taken from you. There is only the will of Nagash.

Nagash's purpose – an end to all – is something even his greater servants are driven to inexorably, no matter what they sought before. Any ritual to animate the fallen serves Nagash's desire, which has seeped into Shyish. This eradicates from his Undead their instinct for self-preservation and leaves only the thirst and its ferocity.

The Land of the Dead was once but a name for the dire fate that befell Nehekhara. Yet Nagash walks the world once more and commonfolk superstitions are no longer idle talk. It is a wave of terror looming upon the lands of the living and their minds. The Undead's dreadful countenance is no longer just something people know, but something they feel in their bones. Such is the power of Nagash.

Shyish is as inevitable as death and as inevitably gathers round Nagash, for they are intertwined. Death is a tool and even a Wind can be wielded like one in the hands of a master. Nagash was a master even long before he died.
Long ago, Nagash bore the tools of his own ascendancy. All necromancy began with him, and its use amplifies his strength. With disciples and servants across the Old World, his strength only grows.

Deep, low, stygian shadows fill the skies, and neither Morrsleib nor Mannslieb can be seen through their pall. Darkness has always been an ally of Nagash. The mortals' deaths will come swiftly and without warning.

To serve Nagash is to serve unquestioningly. He decrees that his forces march further, that they may spread his will and feed his power. The more time passes, the more this commandment drives his servants, no matter how far they are or need to go.

The Great Necromancer's return to the world was feared to be the doom of all life, yet by all accounts he has disappeared. The Undead Legions at his command have crumbled and the vast amounts of land once under his control lie silent. Yet, after millennia preparing for his return, Nagash will not be so easily defeated.\\n\\nThose brave enough to investigate his disappearance describe a sickly teal light emanating from both the depths of the Black Pyramid of Nagash and the mountain fortress of Nagashizzar – whatever this power is, it has made the locations impenetrable for all but the Undead of the world.\\n\\nThe Supreme Lord of Undeath's return is inevitable. The only question is what he prepares in his absence…

Across the world, something impossible occurred, as every Undead creature halted in unison. From lowly beasts to Vampiric generals, all stopped as if they were – for a moment – under someone else's control.\\n\\nMoments later, vast armies of Undead crumbled to nothing as their leaders disappeared from the battlefield.\\n\\nAt first, the survivors of these battles thought some divine intervention thwarted the Undead menace. But as more reports arrived, it instead painted a much darker picture.\\n\\nOnly one being could impose such a will across the world... Nagash, the Supreme Lord of Undeath. Yet the question remains – what was the Great Necromancer’s command?

Legends yet unsung are woven on this day – for you have toppled the avatar of Death itself.\\n\\nRipped all at once from its captor liche, Shyish pierces the firmament with a shriek pitched far beyond mortal hearing. For a moment, the pent-up power coalesces into a vast pillar of darkness before crumbling to its former haunts of grief and suffering. Sighing with eerie relief, forlorn spectres torn from cairn and grave alike dissipate into oblivion.\\n\\nLike ghostly comets torn free from a black hole's inexorable pull, legions of wailing souls escape the tyrant's orbit, leaving evanescent plumes as they peacefully fade. In distant Nehekhara, the innumerable swarms of skull-carapaced Khepra beetles – sacred messengers of the Underworld – still their apocalyptic restlessness, bearing solemn witness to the spectacle. Then, as if driven by a singular will, they retreat to the gloom beneath the golden temples where once they scuttled in eternal vigil.\\n\\nAnd only then – [[i]]at long last[[/i]] – the hues of life gently stipple realms grown still and wan.\\n\\nAll who yet draw breath, or harbour free will, owe that boon to you alone.

incidents_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_skaven_vermintide_episode_victory	By banishing the Verminking, you deprive the Skaven of their horrid purpose, and their mockery of discipline crumbles. The squirming stragglers let loose a rancid stench and scatter to the deepest, darkest burrows of their contemptible race.\\n\\nNot too long ago, the fledgling mankind – self-centred and woefully naive – refused to believe that a species so repulsive and malevolent as the Skaven could exist. From weald-hemmed Middenland to waterlogged Tilea, and from fair Bretonnia to orderly Cathay, bipedal ratmen were dismissed as drunken tall tales and bogeymen conjured by bitter Dwarfs.\\n\\nNot so the elder races. The deep-dwelling dawi of the Worlds Edge Mountains and cold-blooded sentinels of Lustria especially were all too well acquainted with the malice that scurried beneath the land-bound realms. Yet even they could not predict the sheer scale of what the maddened few who chronicled the ratmen menace called [[i]]‘the Great Ascendancy’[[/i]].\\n\\nNow, the survivors are left to contemplate the horror that remains, for a shroud of matted fur and noisome filth was drawn over what once was a civilised world. To undo such ruin will be the labour of generations, all burdened by the knowledge that  – [[i]]inevitably[[/i]] – the verminous tide shall erupt once more from the bowels of the earth.	false

[[i]]‘The Council believes you to be a master schemer, singularly capable of seizing the dwarf-thing engineer-warren of Zhufbar.’[[/i]] A baleful threat lurked behind such terse flattery – some larger design the Council had [[i]]neglected[[/i]] to share with Thanquol. Meanwhile – much as it chagrined the covetous Grey Seer – all the delectable profits of the Steal-Take Plans were spent searching for a warp-forge engineer disgruntled enough to squeak the other way.\\n\\nWith the Warlock Engineers of Clan Skryre distracted and vulnerable, the time was ripe to strike at their Skavenblight stronghold.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]STEAL-TAKE AT SKAVENBLIGHT\\nThanquol must use a [[img:wh3_dlc29_icon_economic_plan]][[/img]]Steal-Take Masterplan at Skavenblight to steal the plans for the Morskittar Engine.[[/col]]	false
incidents_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_skv_thanquol_narrative_act_3	Great was Thanquol’s glee upon conjuring a Verminlord of such monstrous puissance – but it was not to last. Just as the Grey Seer suspected, his heist was soon uncovered. Rumour scurried fast among the Skaven and, among the infamous inventors of the farsqueaker device, it travelled quicker still.\\n\\nSoon, however, he found reason to gloat once more. Upon arrival, the heavily armed Skryre retinue – intent on reclaiming their prize and indulging more than its fair share of vicious retaliation – was engulfed by impenetrable darkness. A single great eye opened within that preternatural gloom. As its boundless malice fell upon each clanrat in turn, a whisper of terrible authority bored into their skulls and demanded obedience to the Seer. [[i]]Thanquol,[[/i]] it insisted, was chosen to complete the great weapon that would shatter the Warp Moon.\\n\\nHenceforth, none would dare interfere with the nascent undertaking. Word, after all, gets around fast among the Skaven.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]COMPLETE THE ENGINE AND UNDER-EMPIRE PLANS\\nThanquol must construct the Morskittar Engine [[i]](Tier 5 Landmark)[[/i]] at Zhufbar and complete three [[img:icon_under_empire]][[/img]][[i]]Under-Empire Foundation"[[/i]] [[img:wh3_dlc29_icon_magic_plan]][[/img]]Great-Smart Masterplans.[[/col]]

Amid the scalding heat of hissing steam engines, giant bellows sputtered like the lungs of a Red Pox victim, their wheezing an uneven countdown to Thanquol's long-denied triumph. He needed to hold out a little longer. Just a [[i]]little[[/i]] longer. Even now, the Engine's three-pronged muzzle seemed to gape straight at Morskrit, the Chaos moon, every hollow in its pocked surface tantalising him with the promise of a boundless trove.\\n\\nRendered in pigments of distilled warpstone, the sickly green runes along the engine’s length blazed in harsher contrast, as the nearing conflagrations of war cast their dull reddish glare across its grimy barrel. Bloodied but undeterred, the remaining forces of the surface races had rallied in a last-ditch effort to foil Thanquol's masterpiece. Fool-fools! They would be first upon the warp-flame pyre!

Neferata has uprooted all pride from those who challenged her at first. Those who questioned her she has schooled out of their ignorance. In her presence they are silent. When she speaks, they obey. At last, she is ready to say the only only word that matters: Lahmia. But one more word she cannot banish from her thoughts, a name: Khalida.\\nIt was Neferata who slew her own cousin. Through the milennia, without a doubt, Khalida has dreamed of killing her a thousand times. And a thousand times has Neferata dreamed of what it could have been were she able to lay the Blood Kiss upon her cousin as she intended.\\nAsaph, the hoary serpent goddess that Khalida serves, thwarted her then, and the wards now raised around Lahmia carry her mark as well. She would spare no means. She would bring the greatest Vampires to their knees for them to stand beside her as she reclaims her rightful throne. The wards will be broken. Khalida will be broken, for Neferata's dreams of true sisterhood are no more. Only the dream of Lahmia remains.

The time has come for the Lord and Lady of Sylvania to hunt apart. Though their hearts remain bound, no matter the distance!\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventIncident:FirstTargetName}} is no longer a Hero and may now be recruited as a [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord at any Settlement.[[/col]]
