Any Dwarfhold worth its foundations must be able to fill its vaults with gold. Debt is for the beardless!
The throngs need leading - go forth into the deeps and find a Thane of Royal blood. Find a grim sort to lead the Clansdwarfs to war!
During the Golden Age, many wonders of the Old World were Dwarf-built and hidden under the mountains. Let the Dwarfs bring about such an age again.
The Dwarfs do not forgive or forget very easily, but it is time to strike some grudges from the Dammaz Kron, if only to make room for more.

Some of the younger generation of Dwarf Engineers are beginning to research and 'innovate'. This doesn't sit well with the traditionalists in the Engineers' Guild, but the High King needs such inquisitive minds in the wars ahead.

With the High King's tacit permission, the innovators faction within the Engineers' Guild are starting to actually invent things! The traditionalists are in uproar, but the Age of Reckoning will be won in part with new methods, not stagnation!

A sad indictment of the Karaz Ankor is that many a Dwarfhold's Sacred Forge remains unlit, the holy fires burning low or extinguished altogether. It is time they grew bright once more, with a Runesmith hammering at the hearth.

There is no definitive rule that marks out the Greatholds from the Dwarfholds. It could be argued that it's the Clansfolk that inhabit the Holds, or the great monuments and halls. Whatever the definition, more Greatholds can only make the Karaz Ankor grow in power.
Each grudge against the Dwarfs is a link in a chain that weighs the whole of the Karaz Ankor low. Thorgrim and his kin must break those chains, and set Dwarfen-folk free!

Dwarfs put great stock in the telling of tales, be they sung or recounted in verse. Our Lords need to become like warriors of myth by forging their own legends. For in doing so the Dwarf folk will follow them into the End Times and beyond!
Even the traditionalists of the Engineers' Guild have been won over by this new outlook of improving and iterating on the concepts of the older generations. Continue the engineering renaissance!
Nothing fills Dwarfish hearts than seeing brave, bearded warriors with axes in hand, march out to war. A mighty throng is an army that any foe will dread to face!
Karaz-a-Karak is the greatest Hold and capital of the Karaz Ankor and seat of the High King since the time before time. Could another Dwarfhold one day rival Everpeak itself? Doubtful.
So long as the Dammaz Kron remains filled with the wrongs done to them, the Dwarfs can never put down their axes. No Dwarf can rest as long as there are grudges outstanding!

To Valaya's sorrow, the Dwarf race is in decline; the older folk outnumber the younger beardlings by some margin. Each Dwarf death is a blow to the entire Dwarfen people; Belegar must ensure he wins battles but convincingly - slaying his foes and keeping his kin alive!

In the Golden Age, Dwarf throngs comprising thousands of beards would regularly march between Holds, scattering Beastmen and Greenskins alike. While such a sight is much rarer these days, it is surely one to make even the most obstinate Rik proud.

The Dwarfs know a righteous cause when they see one, and Belegar's quest to reclaim the Eight Peaks is one they all wish to see succeed. The High King has opened his coffers to the Ironhammer, and so too do all Dwarfs, that his throne might be reclaimed for the Karaz Ankor!

The Royal Dwarf Clans, including Clan Angrund, are full of gifted Thanes and Riks, ready to take control of the many Dwarf throngs for war. Such Lords must be empowered so they are ready to lead, even as the urks approach their doors.

The Age of Reckoning is upon the Dwarfs, and many heroes will be forged, their sagas to be sung in drinking halls for the rest of time. Such heroes should be found and raised to greatness, for they can only aid the cause.

Despite claims from the Empire and the stubbornness of the traditionalists, Dwarfs are the most technically-able race. A High King who does not furnish its greatest minds and inventors to leverage such gifts is as ignorant as nobles from other races.
Not since the War of the Beard… since when the Ancestor Gods walked among the mountain folk… has an army as grand marched forth. The Age of Reckoning is now, the Dammaz Kron wiped clean!

As final victory, for good or ill, draws near, Belegar Ironhammer's influence should be as unyielding as Dwarfen steel. Control of powerful Institutions and Guilds, as well as his own Clan, will give the Ironhammer an edge that will keep all grumblers in line.

The final battle is upon the Dwarfs - the great war of vengeance that will see all other races bow before their might. Yet Belegar Ironhammer cannot do all things alone - he must ensure his closest allies, and those Dwarfs who have supported him thus far, are at their most powerful.

It is a time of heroes - an age not seen since Grimnir led great Dwarf warriors into battle. It is time for Belegar Ironhammer to do the same, to bring about such an era, or make his kin believe it so. A great Dwarf Lord should empower such heroes - raise them to greatness!

The Age of Reckoning is now. From his reclaimed throne, Belegar Ironhammer needs every ounce of his strength to aid the restoration of the Karaz Ankor. This includes technologies both ancient and new - sweep the traditions of stagnation away, bring innovation to its zenith!

Bring bloodshed and misery to those that stand against the Greenskins. Skarsnik has conspired long and hard to achieve victory, and he will have it by any means necessary. Any means. Gottit, you git? Good.

The gobbos are revolting… in many ways, but they need bringing to heel - Skarsnik has put down many a rebellion in bloody misery, but this might require a less violent touch. Pick a Boss from their disgusting ranks and make him a 'Big Boss'; maybe then they'll behave?
Time to rampage - winning in battle is one thing but a Greenskin's career is all about the lootin' too. Sack and raze enemy settlements - let the foe know that Skarsnik's boyz are coming!

Nothing pleases an Orc than being part of a big green mob, mindlessly charging into the enemy. But war is rarely that simple, even the Greenskins know this; sometimes though, somewhat annoyingly, a more strategic approach is needed.
The boyz need loot. Skarsnik needs loot. Every git needs loot! So they better find it; a good few raids should sort out the cash flow.
Skarsnik is above his boyz, smarter and more cruel. But now is not the time to be a loner - the world needs dominating, and if he wants part of it, he needs to start mobbing-up!

Magic is a tricky thing. A few of the enemy Wizards are quite good at it! Fortunately, Mork and Gork can provide: some gobbos and Orcs can fling a good spell too. Find a Goblin Shaman as they're normally cheaper and easier to bully.
If their enemies don't fear the Greenskins, then how can they be dominated? They need to dish out some serious damage. Start sacking and looting in the name of Skarsnik!
Skarsnik is eager to unleash his fiendish plots upon unsuspecting enemies, yet there are things that need doing in preparation for the big charge. Get 'em done, and keep Skarsnik happy.

Orcs will travel leagues to join a burgeoning Waaagh!, but they won't come for just any Warboss. They are attracted to those favoured by the Gods, by those whose legends are created by the quests they undertake.
As much as Skarsnik would revel in outsmarting everyone single-handedly, even he knows he needs the boyz behind him to destroy his foes in short order. The call has gone out, and the mobs are coming.

While spells of da Little Waaagh! are already at our disposal, it's time to get some of the "bigga spellz" in play. Maybe a foot or fist of Gork to really wind the enemy up? Go and find an Orc Shaman.
More ravaging is needed, our foes still have hope, some even think they can beat us! That needs taking from them - see to it!
To bring about the largest Waaagh! this pitiful world has ever seen we need to target that Greenskin aggression. Achieve some key objectives and the green tide will flow!
Yer Mishon… Should Ya Decide Ta Accept It!
It ain't cheap keeping all these armies - Orcs are greedy gits that are always after loot and shiny stuff. It might be best to replenish "da cofferz" - a few raids should do the job.
The Waaagh! gathers pace! The enemies of the Greenskins - that's everyone without green skin (well, even a few Greenskins to be honest) - will witness a mob like never before. Da Great Ruckus begins!

The true horror of the Greenskin menace is not always seen on the battlefield but in the devastation left in the wake of the Orc ravagers. They are merciless, and often hungry as they scourge enemy ruins. Be merciless, be more Orc!

Skarsnik does not have mates, for he does not need them. He tolerates those around him as he rises to greatness. Yet for the Waaagh! to be successful, Skarsnik must give the brutes below him more power, as he cannot do everything himself.
Skarsnik is smart enough to know that, despite his intellect, he needs the Bosses and Shamans around him to enact his schemes. Give them yet more power so that they may serve him!

The best and shiniest stuff… the loot that can make the eyes of the hardiest Warboss water, is rarely in the neighbouring location. The boyz are going to have to loot deep into enemy territory to get the good stuff!

An unending tide of green - a mass mob of Orcs and Goblins that would make Gork and Mork swell with pride and send Sigmar and his cronies cowering into the Realm of Chaos! That is the goal, now it's time to bring it!
The Mightiest Waaagh! Dat Eva Woz

Destroy! We must unleash the beast that lies within every Greenskin. The Orc Gods want this world to tremble, and so our Savage Lord must be "Da Scourge" and burn a scar across the lands that not even time will forget!
Grant the most able Warbosses and magic-users in the Greenskin ranks the power and status they need to bring about a slaughter. It is what Gork demands, and Skarsnik knows it is necessary!

Skarsnik's most feared allies need not only his backing, so they can go about unimpeded, but if they are to spread the word of the Warlord's Waaagh! then they must be granted the power such a message demands!

Even for Orcs, the lure of shiny stuff is as strong as the thrill of murder - the richest Bosses are always the most successful. If Skarsnik is to bring about Ragnarork then he must become the wealthiest Greenskin as well.

The Angrund Clan is beset by tribulation. Far from their rightful home, and with little of their former power intact, its Dawi nevertheless cling to hope. Angrund strength endures in King Belegar; aided by the spirits of his restless, vengeful Ancestors, and supported by allied Clans, he will see the Dwarfs’ glory restored!

With the Time of Woes a distant memory, the Dwarfs should look to the future and the restoration of the Karaz Ankor. The more territory around and even beyond their traditional mountain homes the Dwarfs can claim, the more the Ancestors will be pleased.

The Dwarf expeditionary forces are a brave and vital element of the Dwarf military - they can roam far and secure Holds in the name of their race's glory. Grudges will be wiped from the Dammaz Kron, and the Dwarfs will once again know their rightful glory!

The Angrund Clan will know greatness again; Belegar has declared it and his is a fierce and renowned determination. A Dwarf's oath is his honour, and his words his bond. The regions outside of Dawi control must be reclaimed, and made part of their dominion as soon as possible.

Not since Valaya and Grungni strode the mountains have the Dawi been in such a positon. A few more realms taken will see the Karaz Ankor restored to its rightful stature - an empire ruled by those who have committed their all to see it restored, enduring as the mountains themselves. One last push, brave Dawi, one final push...
Take back control of Clan Angrund's ancestral home:
Take back control of one of your most prized possessions:

Skarsnik is the self-styled 'Warlord of the Eight Peaks', sat atop a Dwarf throne, laying waste to all who challenge his dominion. Now he finds himself in the west, with the humies and stunties between him and his mountains. Might as well wreak some havoc on the way back, eh?

If the Greenskins are going to fear Skarsnik - and they should - then he must use his influence and build up a great green horde to launch an invasion and crush all his enemies. The local tribes must fall into line or get a proper bootin'!

It's time to stop messing around and put the boot in! The Badlands, the World's Edge, the Empire - all of it belongs to the Greenskins! Destroy the trespassers, take their lands and get the Waaagh! started.

The momentum shifts as the Orc realms expand. The Dwarfs quail, the Empire shudders, even the forces of Chaos stutter as the Green Tide rises. Now is the time to bring outlying territories into the clutches of the scheming, devilish Skarsnik.

A Waaagh! is happening! The Orcs gather in great numbers - they must bring as many regions as possible must under the Greenskins' control - such an act will appease Gork and Mork and ensure that Skarsnik's name is revered for all time!

Wurrzag does not call any one place home, yet wherever he decides to roam is his dominion. He inspires otherwise wretched and useless gangs of Greenskins to greatness in all corners of the earth, and charges them with achieving greatness across the Badlands and beyond. Or else.

If the Greenskins are going to fear Wurrzag - and they should - then he must use his influence and build up a great green horde to launch an invasion to crush all enemies in the name of Gork (or Mork). The local tribes must fall into line or get a proper bootin'!

It's time to stop messing around and put the boot in! The Badlands, the World's Edge, the Empire - all of it belongs to Gork (or Mork)! Destroy the trespassers, take their lands and get the Waaagh! started.

The momentum shifts as the Orc realms expand. The Dwarfs quail, the Empire shudders, even the forces of Chaos stutter as the Green Tide rises. Now is the time to bring outlying territories into the clutches of 'Da Great Green Prophet'.

A Waaagh! is upon us. The Orcs gather in great numbers and so as many regions as possible must be brought under the Greenskins' control - such an act will appease Gork and Mork and ensure that da Great Green Godz are revered for all time!

My Lord, the dukes of Bretonnia have resided under a chivalrous code for many years. Honour this tradition, build upon the great foundations of Gilles le Breton, and lead the Knightly Orders forward, to glory!

Our lands prosper under your chivalrous rule, yet evil still breeds in every corner. Many look to destroy Bretonnia, and their power grows as quickly as our own. Stave off their advances and unite the banners of Bretonnia with your chivalric actions!

Bretonnia flowers in true splendour - tales shall be told of your chivalric deeds for years to come. As our borders expand so our code of chivalry spreads with it. Do not relent, for Bretonnia will be the beacon of light in this ever crumbling world.

The harsh and desolate wastes of Norsca embrace you into its cold and wintery grip, my Lord, yet it cannot sustain your appetite for war indefinitely. You will need to voyage from this land to raid and pillage, your Gods will gaze favourably upon you for this. Raze in their name and align yourself with one to be granted their twisted and Ruinous gifts.

Your allegiance grows, my Lord, and can be strengthened further still as you raze further settlements and erect monoliths in their place. Build upon this bond and ascend beneath your God's gaze. The riches of the Old World are at your mercy - feast upon them as you would a suckling pig!

As you reap havoc and destruction upon the world, my Lord, your allegiance to your God builds. The Norse Gods are a maleficent group - stray from your master now and you will surely feel its wrath. Give yourself fully, however, and you will become their champion, marked for all to see by your pure devotion.

There are many who wish to invoke the attention of the Dark Gods, but the Ruinous Powers will not favour just any mortal; only those who can prove themselves in battle will receive - even then - the barest flicker of acknowledgement.
The path to damnation is long and treacherous, our master will need followers to accompany him as he walks along it.
A great Chaos Champion, especially the Lord of the End Times, must maintain a reputation of dread. For if he is not feared then why will they follow?
The corrupting influence of Chaos begins to spread; ensure its tendrils reach deep into the mortal realms.
The tribes of Norsca are useful foot troops in the coming wars, our Lord should gain their favour by offering a token alliance.
To be the Everchosen, to command thousands? The Chaos Gods will not consider any being who is not a great warrior with an iron will. Archaon must prove his worth through conquest!
While we can vanquish the mortals with sword and scourge alone, there are many tools at our Lord's disposal. Recruiting a Chaos Sorcerer is but another.
Archaon must maintain his powerbase and support or he will be challenged by unworthy fools who dare to think themselves better than the Three-Eyed King.
If the Everchosen is to bring his campaign of destruction beyond the shadow of the Chaos Realm, he must first take the mortal realms and collect their souls!

Time has no meaning in the Realm of Chaos. For some, Archaon has been the Everchosen for centuries. For others, he has only just begun his Unholy Quest to seize the grand artefacts of Chaos and become the Lord of the End Times.
All four Marks of Chaos sear Archaon's flesh. But it is Khorne that thirsts and demands the most. Ensure our Lord's forces see battle!
The more glory the Everchosen achieves, the more jealous his rivals become. They will challenge our master as soon as his dominion falls, so fear and control must be maintained.
Raids alone will not bring about the End Times, but mighty Chaos hordes unleashed as part of a massive invasion from the dread north… that is what the Ruinous Powers require.
The corrupting influence of Chaos will envelop the world - the Lord of the End Times and his followers must ensure its continued spread.
It is not enough to achieve victory in battle - Khorne demands that the Champion of Champions win convincingly as well.
To marshal a host of the Gods' most foul mortal servants is a great challenge, but one Archaon has to grasp, for the rewards are great and failure not worth contemplating.
Now more than ever - with the ultimate goal in sight - our Lord must be wary and maintain his dominion. There are those that plot against him, including the Great Changer himself.
Powerful allies can be a boon, and oft-make loyal servants. Raise a Chaos Lord to greatness so that he may serve the Ruinous Powers effectively.
If our Lord Archaon grants willing thralls a sliver of his power they will be his forever; their fates in his hands to do with as he wishes.
As the tendrils of Chaos grow and bore deep into the Old World, its souls suffer, the lands wither, and the Empire burns!
If Archaon commands a grand army, then the Chaos Gods will cast their gaze down onto the Old World and bring ruin upon the lands.
As the hammer blow strikes on the mortal lands, our Lord is at his most powerful… and most exposed… we must ensure his favour remains strong among the hordes.
As the End Times draw near, their Lord and catalyst cannot be everywhere at once. Grant his most powerful servants even greater glory so they can bring about the apocalypse.
Now is the time to unleash hell upon the world - Archaon's agents should be raised in status and dominion to achieve our ends.
The Chaos Gods tire of the Old World and its denizens. The land shall be swept clean, its souls consumed once and for all. The End Times are here!
Any Dwarfhold worth its foundations must be able to fill its vaults with gold. Debt is for the beardless!
The throngs need leading - go forth into the deeps and find a Thane of Royal blood. Find a grim sort to lead the Clansdwarfs to war!
During the Golden Age, many wonders of the Old World were Dwarf-built and hidden under the mountains. Let the Dwarfs bring about such an age again.
The Dwarfs do not forgive or forget very easily, but it is time to strike some grudges from the Dammaz Kron, if only to make room for more.

Some of the younger generation of Dwarf Engineers are beginning to research and 'innovate'. This doesn't sit well with the traditionalists in the Engineers' Guild, but the High King needs such inquisitive minds in the wars ahead.

With the High King's tacit permission, the innovators faction within the Engineers' Guild are starting to actually invent things! The traditionalists are in uproar, but the Age of Reckoning will be won in part with new methods, not stagnation!

A sad indictment of the Karaz Ankor is that many a Dwarfhold's Sacred Forge remains unlit, the holy fires burning low or extinguished altogether. It is time they grew bright once more, with a Runesmith hammering at the hearth.

There is no definitive rule that marks out the Greatholds from the Dwarfholds. It could be argued that it's the Clansfolk that inhabit the Holds, or the great monuments and halls. Whatever the definition, more Greatholds can only make the Karaz Ankor grow in power.
Each grudge against the Dwarfs is a link in a chain that weighs all of Dwarfkind down. Belegar and his kin must break those chains, and set Dwarfen-folk free!

Dwarfs put great stock in the telling of tales, be they sung or recounted in verse. Our Lords need to become like warriors of myth by forging their own legends. For in doing so the Dwarf folk will follow them into the End Times and beyond!
Even the traditionalists of the Engineers' Guild have been won over by this new outlook of improving and iterating on the concepts of the older generations. Continue the engineering renaissance!
Nothing fills Dwarfish hearts than seeing brave, bearded warriors with axes in hand, march out to war. A mighty throng is an army that any foe will dread to face!
Karaz-a-Karak is the greatest Hold and capital of the Karaz Ankor and seat of the High King since the time before time. Could another Dwarfhold one day rival Everpeak itself? Doubtful.
As long as the Dammaz Kron is filled with the wrongs done to them, the Dwarfs can never put down their axes. The High King cannot rest as long as there are grudges outstanding!

To Valaya's sorrow, the Dwarf race is one in decline, the older folk outnumber the younger beardlings by some margin. So each Dwarf death is a blow to the High King. He must win his battles but do so convincingly, by slaying the foe and keeping his kin alive!

In the Golden Age, Dwarf throngs comprising thousands of beards would regularly march between Holds, scattering Beastmen and Greenskins alike. While such a sight is much rarer these days, it is surely one to make even the most obstinate Rik proud.

The Dwarfholds are all independent kingdoms that pay tribute to the High King, even if they do not always directly obey. Should our Lord directly influence a great or unique institution then his reign will be all the more effective.

The Royal Dwarf Clans are full of gifted Thanes and Riks, ready to take control of the High King's throngs. Such Lords must be empowered so they are ready to lead, even as the urks approach their doors.

The Age of Reckoning is upon the Dwarfs, and many heroes will be forged, their sagas to be sung in drinking halls for the rest of time. Such heroes should be found and raised to greatness, for they can only aid the cause.

Despite claims from the Empire and the stubbornness of the traditionalists, Dwarfs are the most technically-able race. A High King who does not furnish its greatest minds and inventors to leverage such gifts is as ignorant as nobles from other races.
Not since the War of the Beard… since when the Ancestor Gods walked among the mountain folk… has an army as grand marched forth. The Age of Reckoning is now, the Dammaz Kron wiped clean!

As victory for good or not draws close, the High King's influence should be as unyielding as Dwarfen steel. Owning powerful Institutions and Guilds, instead of the Clans, gives Thorgrim an edge that will keep all grumblers in line.

The final battle is upon the Dwarfs - the great war of vengeance that will see all other races bow before their might. But the High King cannot do this alone, he must ensure his closest allies are at their most powerful.

It is a time of heroes, an age not seen since Grimnir led great warriors in battle. Grudgebearer must bring about such an era, or make his kin believe it is so. The High King should empower such heroes - raise them to greatness!

The Age of Reckoning is now. The High King needs every tool to bring the Karaz Ankor to beyond its former glory. This includes technologies ancient and new; sweep the traditions of stagnation away, bring innovation to its zenith!
The Emperor's banner should be seen in battle; after all, it was the backing of the Sigmarite Cult that won Karl Franz the throne, now he must be like the Warrior-King of old!
Every Emperor that takes the throne surrounds himself by men whose abilities and loyalty are as strong as the steel they carry. Recruit such a warrior.

For the Empire to remain the mightiest of all nations then infrastructure is key. Ulric will be pleased with our Lord's prowess in battle, but there are many other gods to appease and raising great buildings and monuments is one way to achieve that.

Assailed by enemies within and without, the Empire is cursed to never know true peace - but Karl Franz was elected Emperor on the promise of quelling the myriad foes, and so his campaign begins in earnest.

The Emperor cannot reign over the entire nation without the backing of the Elector Counts, who rule their provinces autonomously. While belligerent Electors may need the threat of steel to come on side, others can be won over with the dove.

In the quest to bring the Empire under Karl Franz's sway, overt diplomacy is not the only method - especially when an Elector or some other regional noble is publicly against him. There are more subtle ways to bring a region to heel.

The Colleges of Magic were founded in the wake of the Great War Against Chaos and the coronation of Magnus the Pious. Never again would the Empire suffer at the magic of others. Now the Empire requires a student from the Colleges to accompany our forces.

The greatest cities in the Old World reside in the Empire, they are full of danger and wonders, attracting visitors and great minds from across the world. To retain the influx of the great, the cities must prosper.
Our enemies move against us, so we must be decisive both in our own military and strategic goals. Send your subjects and agents on high-priority missions to secure the throne.
A legendary quest fall upon our Lords - rewards and greatness awaits those brave enough to undertake such tasks, for they will be remembered in the annals of history.
When Chaos comes or the Greenskins rampage, then borders become irrelevant. Mankind as a race has to come together. This must be achieved by any means necessary.
It is time our enemies knew what they stood against. An army of disciplined Men of the Empire in all their magnificent panoply will send a strong message through these lands.

The Empire is the greatest nation of the Old World. To retain such a title it needs to dazzle and impress and beguile visitors from all across the realms. Its cities are islands of stature in the vast wilderness of the nation, and the buildings within, jewels.
A Wonder of the Old World
The Emperor's influence spreads far across the lands and beyond our borders. Give loyal servants the authority to enact Franz's will against the enemies of Sigmar, so we can consolidate our power.

There is no stronger message to our foes than dominance on the battlefield. Victories are empty things if we lose too many of our own forces in the engagement. It is time to smash the foe, and have them fleeing before our armoured might.

A grand muster is called for. The full armoured might of the Empire should be deployed in all its awesome glory. Such a sight will make Ulric and Sigmar weep with joy and their enemies quail with fear.

The Empire is an eclectic place full of many esoteric organisations - religious and otherwise. Such institutions hold a lot of sway, so their blessing is always a boon to any ruling Emperor. Having dominion over their headquarters certainly helps too...

The greater our most loyal servants become, the tighter the Emperor's rule. Elevate a Lord with power, wealth and influence so that Karl Franz's reign can never be gainsayed by enemies within or without.

The Emperor has many willing servants; if loyal nobles are elevated to greatness, so, too, should those whose skills and influence lie in other disciplines. Make them great and their faith in Karl Franz will be swollen tenfold.

Although the Dwarfs will falsely claim otherwise, the Empire is the most technically able race in the world. Mankind willing innovates and is not moribund in tradition or the petty jealousies of the Dwarfen Guilds. We should exploit that.

Not since the Time of Magnus has there been a greater muster; the armies of the Empire should come together at last, for we stand ready to fight the mightiest of battles. This will be a call to arms like no other!

The ultimate threat draws near, those institutions and temples not with us should be brought under our control. The Emperor cares not how this is achieved - offer the branch or the lash - we will have them under Karl Franz's will.
We must raise as many nobles to our circle of influence - make them the greatest they can be, for their loyalty will filter down to the men, girding them for the ultimate conquest.
Empower our agents, give them all the tools they need to spread discord in the foes' armies and sow discontent in their territory.
Ensure our greatest minds have stretched themselves. We must seek out every innovation not yet discovered, for this will give us an edge in the battles and conquest yet to play out.
Bring bloodshed and misery to those that stand against the Greenskins. Grimgor expects victory, he won't suffer failure. Gottit, you git? Good.

The gobbos are revolting… in many ways, but they need bringing to heel, or Grimgor will just kill the lot of 'em. Pick a Boss from their disgusting ranks and make him a 'Big Boss'; maybe then they'll behave?
Time to rampage - winning in battle is one thing but a Greenskins career is all about the lootin' too. Sack and raze enemy settlements - let the foe know that Grimgor's boyz are coming!

Nothing pleases an Orc than being part of a big green mob, mindlessly charging into the enemy. But war is rarely that simple, even the Greenskins know this; sometimes though, somewhat annoyingly, a more strategic approach is needed.
The boyz need loot. The boss needs loot. Grimgor needs loot. Every git needs loot! So they better find it; a good few raids should sort out the cash flow.
Apart from da Immortulz, Grimgor has never been one for company. But now is not the time to be a loner! If he wants to dominate the world, he needs to start mobbing-up!

Magic is a tricky thing. A few of the enemy wizards are quite good at it! Fortunately, Mork and Gork can provide: some gobbos and Orcs can fling a good spell too. Find a Goblin Shaman as they're normally cheaper and easier to bully.
If their enemies don't fear the Greenskins, then how can they be dominated? Dish out some serious damage. Start sacking and looting in Grimgor's name!
The Boss is eager to mercilessly crush his foes, but there's a few things that need doing in preparation for the big charge. Get these done, and keep Grimgor happy.

Orcs will travel leagues to join a burgeoning Waaagh!, but they won't come for just any Warboss. They are attracted to those favoured by the Gods, by those whose legends are created by the quests they undertake.
As much as Grimgor wants to kill everything on his own, even he knows he needs da boyz behind him in order to do that. The call has gone out, and the mobs are coming.

While spells of da Little Waaagh! are already at the Greenskins' disposal, it's time to get some of the 'bigga spellz' in play. Maybe a foot or fist of Gork to really wind the enemy up? Go and find an Orc Shaman.
More ravaging is needed - Greenskin foes still have hope, some even think they can beat them! That needs taking from them - see to it!
To bring about the largest Waaagh! this pitiful world has ever seen you need to target that Greenskin aggression. Achieve some key objectives and the Green Tide will flow!
Yer Mishon… Should Ya Decide Ta Accept It!
It ain't cheap keeping all these armies - Orcs are greedy gits that are always after loot and shiny stuff. It might be best to replenish "da cofferz" - a few raids should do the job.
The Waaagh! gathers pace! The enemies of the Greenskins - that's everyone without green skin (well, even a few Greenskins to be honest) - will witness a mob like never before. Da Great Ruckus begins!

The true horror of the Greenskin menace is not always seen on the battlefield but in the devastation left in the wake of the Orc ravagers. They are merciless, and often hungry as they scourge enemy ruins. Be merciless, be more Orc!

Grimgor has no mates, he just tolerates a select few and even those run the risk of been cleaved in twain by Gitsnik should they anger him. Yet for the Waaagh! to be successful, Grimgor must give such brutes power, as even Ironhide cannot be in every place at once.
Although Ironhide will never admit it, he belligerently knows that he needs the Bosses and Shamans around him to enact his will away from the mobs. Empower them so they may serve Gork (or Mork!).

The best and shiniest stuff… the loot that can make the eyes of the hardiest Warboss water, is rarely in the neighbouring location. The boyz are going to have to loot deep into enemy territory to get the good stuff!

An unending tide of green - a mass mob of Orcs and Goblins that would make Gork and Mork swell with pride and send Sigmar and his cronies cowering into the Realm of Chaos! That is the goal, now it's time to bring it!
The Mightiest Waaagh! Dat Eva Woz

Destroy! Unleash the beast that lies within every Greenskin. Da Green Gods want this world to tremble, and so this Savage Lord must be 'Da Scourge' and burn a scar across the lands that not even time will forget!
Grant the most able Warbosses and magic-users in the Greenskin ranks the power and status they need to bring about a slaughter. It is what Gork demands and Grimgor begrudgingly accepts as necessary!

Grimgor's most feared allies need not only his backing so they can go about unimpeded, but if they are to spread the word of Ironhide's Waaagh! then they must be granted the power such a message demands!

Even for Orcs, the lure of shiny stuff is as strong as the thrill of murder - the richest bosses are always the most successful. If Grimgor is to bring about Ragnarork then he must become the wealthiest Greenskin as well.

A Vampire strikes from the shadows as well as at the head of his skeletal legions. The von Carsteins have always been masters of plots and manipulation; ensure our Lord's goals are achieved by bringing such intrigues to their conclusion.
Raising a mortal with the Blood Kiss may sound an easy task, but we do not grant any living fool immortality. Such a gift should not be wasted on serfs - we must choose wisely.

Our Lord's power comes from fear as much from the arcane. We need to ensure that his many enemies fear the von Carstein name and say it only in hushed whispers. Thus is our powerbase maintained and the cattle controlled.

To tarry in Sylvania, and skulk in other dark places that welcome the dead, is short-sighted. If our master is to achieve his destiny then he must send his servants forth to start pulling - or removing - the levers of power.
As the dead rise, the land itself revolts against the unnatural. We must spread this curse beyond our borders, let the mortals observe and see that death comes for all!

The von Carstein bloodline has always excelled at deceit and disguise. Vampires have many guises - a court noble, a renowned wizard, a loyal servant, a baron's spymaster… It is in these roles that the Vampires turn fate to their advantage.

When the Great Necromancer, Nagash, first dabbled with Dark Magic it seeped into the world and broke it. Now many millennia later, Nagash's legacy continues - ravaging the world wherever Necromancy is practised.

Mannfred was not the first von Carstein, nor will he be the last. In the last few decades there always seems to be another of Vlad's despicable sires crawling out of his crypt. Each as power hungry as the other. But it is Mannfred we serve and so we must ensure he maintains power.

Mannfred lies at the centre of a great web of intrigue. A manipulator worthy of Tzeentch! From his lair, our master sends word to his puppets of tasks to be done, accounts to be settled and missions to achieve.
At the Centre of the Web
Our master has scoured the world for forbidden lore and artefacts of power. It's a search that continues and so word has reached us that another item of great power is within Count Mannfred's grasp.

Of the von Carsteins, it was Vlad who was seen as the military genius - taking his Undead hosts to the walls of Altdorf itself. Mannfred, however, was thwarted at Hel Fenn. If this new incursion is to be considered a threat, then our master's forces need victory in battle.
Rise the Undead legions - let them tirelessly march forth just like the armies of the Doomlord of olde!

The von Carsteins dominate their homelands because of the terrifying climate they propagate. The few mortals that reside in or close to Sylvania live in constant fear, such is the power of the Midnight Aristocracy.

As the Undead rise and march forth, the influence of Dark Magic spreads across the lands - fell creatures take roost in once-homely caves, trees become rotten and twisted, and even houses buckle and decay as the corruption spreads.

Back in the mists of time, when the Kings of Nehekhara rose up against Nagash, they were initially repelled by the Great Necromancer's awesome power. Our Lord must echo such victories and repulse all that challenge us!
The Necromancers have raided the charnel pits and brought us fresh corpses. These should be joined with our legions to create a mighty Undead host worthy of the von Carstein name.

Mannfred must maintain political power of his domains. If he is to keep his quarrelling, power-hungry siblings in check then there cannot be any reason for them to question his motives and will. For should a rival Vampire sense weakness, it will strike.

There is a danger by giving a creature as ambitious and predatory as a Vampire too much power. But Mannfred has been around his kin for centuries and knows how to deal with such turn-coats. However, he needs servants that are more than mere pawns, so must grant them a modicum of his power.
I Grant Thee A Great Boon…
Mannfred sees his agents as little more than tools, yet some tools are more useful than others. For those lucky few minions, great rewards await - depending on how they serve our master of course.

Mannfred's pall of darkness reaches across the nations, infusing the land with Dark Magic. Every place it touches, the dead no longer rest easily in their graves and crypts are broken open from the inside. And so the Undead take the world from the living...

The Undead are inexhaustible - able to constantly replenish with each new killing. The mortals fear our legions, for they know deep down that, eventually, they will rise up and join them. It is time for our master to field such an army - a legion of Undeath that no foe can challenge!

The machinations of the von Carsteins are complex and despotic. At the height of his power our master, Count Mannfred, must be ready to fend off any plot from a rival sibling ready to strike from the shadows. With immortal glory so close, maintaining his dominion is essential.

The Eternal Emperor stands ready to take his throne! His most loyal subjects will be rewarded with immortality and other gifts that no mortal could even comprehend; prepare those our master has deemed worthy to enter his scared circle.

The mortals must fear Mannfred's touch - fear that his reach is long and that nowhere is safe from the dread Count. To extend such a reach he needs willing servants, with the power and status to influence every area of mortal society.
For Count Mannfred to sit upon a throne of bone as an Immortal Emperor, he must spread his influence far and ensure that his Unliving Empire is ready for its dread sovereign.
All are pawns of Chaos, all must serve. Do as the Dark Gods wish and begin the destruction. Thus is the way prepared for the End Times.
A loyal servant to the Chaos Gods is one that enacts carnage - that raids and destroys and scatters the mortals before him.
All hail the champions of Chaos, it is they who the eyes of the Gods fall upon. They are the ones that risk damnation in exchange for a chance of greatness - continue the slaughter!
The destroyer comes, and with him the favour of the Ruinous Powers. The southern lands of milk and honey will wither at his touch.
Behold the Everchosen! The Daemons rejoice for the End Times are here. Destroy and corrupt those that still hold out against the inevitable. Chaos has come - the world will be broken!

The Karaz Ankor has fallen into decline, assaulted by fell enemies above and below the ground… but no more! Everpeak has stirred, the High King demands that the Dwarf realm be brought back to its former glory. Let  the task begin in earnest!

With the Time of Woes a distant memory, the Dwarfs should look to the future and the restoration of the Karaz Ankor. The more territory around and even beyond their traditional mountain homes the Dwarfs can claim, the more the Ancestors will be pleased.

There must be more Dwarf expeditions deployed - let them take the regions in the High King's name, and wipe out many grudges regarding those who stand against the Dwarf race. In this way the Karaz Ankor will be returned to its rightful glory!

The Karaz Ankor will be great again, for Thorgrim has sworn it and the High King never reneges on an oath. Every Dwarf worth his beard bears the same bond. There are still regions outside of Dwarfen control, they must be brought under Karaz-a-Karak's dominion as soon as possible.

Not since Valaya and Grungni strode the mountains have the Dawi been in such a position. A few more realms taken will see the Karaz Ankor at its rightful stature - an empire ruled from Everpeak by a High King whose reign is as enduring as the mountains themselves. One last push, brave Dawi, one final push...

The election of a new Emperor has oft-led to turmoil as the machinations of the Elector Counts play out. But as the nobles conduct their petty power-struggles, the nation fractures. It is up to the newly-elected sovereign to begin the process of reunification - bringing an entire province under his rule must be a priority.

Even the worst Emperors in history, and - to our shame - there have been many, could claim to have more than one province under their rule. To truly bring the Empire back to greatness, the throne must exert its power to provinces further afield.

It was Magnus of Nuln that ended the turbulent Time of the Three Emperors, by defeating the Chaos Lord, Asavar Kul. In the wake of such a victory the Empire was united. To withstand another such invasion, we must be united again with more provinces under the Emperor's rule.
As Magnus Did So Shall We

The time of feuding Elector Counts and petty squabbles between provinces is over. The encroaching threat from the north cannot be ignored any longer. To face the armies of Chaos the Empire must be as one. Only then does mankind stand a chance against the Dark Powers and their minions.

This time will be known as the Age of Franz; not since Magnus the Pious has there been an Emperor so beloved of his people and successful in bringing the provinces under Sigmar's banner. Such glory infuriates the Dark Gods, and they will strike hard to destroy the dynasty of the Reikland Princes. Unite the last of the realms, for Chaos comes!

Grimgor's traditional stompin' ground was the northern peaks of the World's Edge Mountains, where he laid waste to Kislev and even marched through Sylvania, bedecking his banners with Vampire fangs. Since coming south to slap Gorfang Rotgut, Grimgor might as well hang around for a bit, and sort this sorry lot out. Gits.

If the Greenskins are going to fear Grimgor - as they should - then he must take control and build up a great green empire from which he can launch an invasion to crush all enemies. The local tribes must fall into line or get a proper bootin'.
It's time to stop messing around and put the boot in! The Badlands, the World's Edge, the Empire - all of it is Grimgor's! Destroy the trespassers, take their lands and get the Waaagh! started.

The momentum shifts as the Orc realms expand. The Dwarfs quail, the Empire shudders, even the forces of Chaos stutter as the Green Tide rises. Now is the time to bring outlying territories into Grimgor's clutches.

A Waaagh! is upon the Greenskins. The Orcs gather in great numbers - they must bring as many regions under Grimgor's iron fist as possible - such an act will appease Gork and Mork and ensure that Grimgor's name is remembered for all time.

No longer is it feared as the dread land where the dead do not rest, but instead is seen as Stirland's bastard child. Now a von Carstein resides in Castle Drakenhof once again, it is time for the Vampires to take dominion over their haunted realm.

Mannfred's influence must spread across all of Sylvania and beyond into the Empire itself if he is to realise his dread ambition of becoming the first and only Eternal Emperor. But before he can rule, a powerbase should be established and fresh troops risen for the challenges ahead.

Now is the time for Fell Bats to blot out the sun, for gloom to fall upon the lands of the living and the Long Night to begin. Mannfred's dominion shall extend far and wide if the prophecies in the Liber Noctus are to come true.

Mannfred's fell influence saturates the lands, but for the scions of Sigmar's Blood to truly fear the power of the Vampires then all the Old World must be taken in von Carstein's name. Nothing is beyond the reach of the Midnight Aristocracy!

The time is now - Mannfred von Carstein needs to make his move and take Sigmar's throne, or claim the lands from any foe - living or immortal - that dares resist the inevitable. Mannfred will rule over all as an Eternal Emperor - an immortal king that even the Chaos Gods bow to!

There is a danger by giving a creature as ambitious and predatory as a Vampire too much power. But Vlad knows his kin, knows how they think, knows how to deal with such turn-coats. However, he needs servants that are more than mere pawns, so must grant them a modicum of his power.
I Grant Thee A Great Boon…
Vlad sees his agents as little more than tools, yet some tools are more useful than others. For those lucky few minions, great rewards await - depending on how they serve our master of course.

The von Carstein pall of darkness reaches across the nations, infusing the land with Dark Magic. Every place it touches, the dead no longer rest easily in their graves and crypts are broken open from the inside. And so the Undead take the world from the living...

The Undead are inexhaustible - able to constantly replenish with each new killing. The mortals fear our legions, for they know deep down that, eventually, they will rise up and join them. It is time for our master to field such an army - a legion of Undeath that no foe can challenge!

The machinations of the von Carsteins are complex and despotic. At the height of his power our master must be ready to fend off any plot from a rival ready to strike from the shadows. With immortal glory so close, maintaining his dominion is essential.

The Eternal Emperor stands ready to take his throne! His most loyal subjects will be rewarded with immortality and other gifts that no mortal could even comprehend; prepare those our master has deemed worthy to enter his scared circle.

The mortals must fear Vlad's Unliving touch - fear that his reach is long and that nowhere is safe from his gnarled talons. To extend such a reach he needs willing servants, with the power and status to influence every area of mortal society.
For a von Carstein to sit upon a throne of bone as an Immortal Emperor, he must spread his influence far and ensure that his Unliving Empire is ready for its dread sovereign.

Sylvania is in decline. No longer is it feared as the dread land where the dead do not rest, but instead is seen as Stirland's bastard child. Now a von Carstein resides in Castle Drakenhof once again, it is time for the Vampires to take dominion over their haunted realm.

The von Carsteins' influence must spread across all of Sylvania and beyond into the Empire itself if they are to realise their Imperial ambitions. But before they can rule, a powerbase should be established and fresh troops risen for the challenges ahead.

Now is the time for Fell Bats to blot out the sun, for gloom to fall upon the lands of the living and the Long Night to begin. The von Carsteins' dominion shall extend far and wide if the prophecies in the Liber Noctus are to come true.

The von Carsteins' fell influence saturates the lands, but for the scions of Sigmar's Blood to truly fear the power of the Vampires then all the Old World must be taken in their name. Nothing is beyond the reach of the Midnight Aristocracy!

The time is now - Vlad von Carstein must make his move to take Sigmar's throne or claim the lands from any foe - living or immortal - that dares resist the inevitable. The Midnight Aristocracy will rule over all - as Eternal Emperors - immortal kings that even the Chaos Gods bow to!

The Black Pyramid stirs, my liege, but to reveal the secrets within, five Books of Nagash must be found. Begin the search at once for other powers also seek domination over the Arch-Necromancer’s shrine.\\n\\nLearn more about Books of Nagash [[url:script_link_campaign_books_of_nagash]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_books_of_nagash}}]]here[[/tooltip]][[/url]].

Firstborn of King Khetep, Nagash was overlooked for succession and forced to join the Mortuary Cult. He swiftly rose to become a powerful high priest, but envy of his brother, who succeeded their father as king, burned within Nagash like a brazier coal. Seizing his opportunity, he entombed his brother, Thutep, alive and claimed the throne for himself - thus began Nagash's reign of sorcerous terror.

But a throne would not suffice for the insatiable Sorcerer. Seeking greater power, he threw himself into the study of Dark Magic, melding it with Necromancy to unlock the very secrets of eternal life. He poured all he had learned into his blasphemous opus, the nine Books of Nagash. The next stage of his plan, if successful, would magnify his powers immeasurably...

Nagash then constructed a vast black pyramid to harness and channel the Winds of Magic. Upon its completion, Nagash felt his powers grow tenfold, though the cost to the Kingdom was ruinous. Even as his might surged, the outraged Nehekharan Priest Kings gathered in secret, devising a way to topple the sorcerous tyrant.

The Priest Kings mustered mighty armies and declared war, but to their horror Nagash raised countless regiments of Skeleton Warriors in reply. Realising flesh alone could not to defeat such horrors, the Priest Kings breathed life into the mightiest statues of Nehekhara. Stone Ushabti, Necrolith Colossi and Khemrian Warsphinxes fought alongside the living, and Nagash's legions were crushed, forcing him to flee. However, is Nehekhara finally rid of his evil?

Order finally returned to Nehekhara, but it was many years until the kingdom prospered again, under the rule of King Alcadizaar. The Mortuary Cult was held under close scrutiny, its researches severely curtailed lest there be a repetition of Nagash's horrors. Many years passed in peace, until Nagash seemed but a dark and distant memory.

All was not seemly well in the Nehekharan city of Lahmia, however. Spellbound by the Sorcerer's legacy, Queen Neferata recreated his Elixir of Life, though her method was flawed (she and her court gained eternal life, but were cursed with an insatiable thirst for blood). Their dabblings aroused the fury of King Alcadizaar, and the Lahmians fled in search of refuge.

Little did these first Vampires know, Nagash's dark will had guided their actions all along. They found themselves at his fortress of Nagashizzar, where the perfidious Sorcerer welcomed his twisted children with open arms. Together, they launched a fresh offensive against Nehekhara, catching the recovering kingdom unawares.

Nehekhara rallied its forces in defence, and the war ground on for many years, seemingly deadlocked. After a titanic effort, however, Alcadizaar finally smashed the Undead forces. The Vampires fled to new refuges in the Old World, while Nagash retreated once more in abject fury. This time, his wrath was absolute – he cast a foul contagion throughout Nehekhara, scouring it of all life. Only Alcadizaar did he spare to witness the horror.

Incarcerated and fading, King Alcadizaar was visited in his cell one night by a group of cloaked, twitching, rat-like creatures. They whispered to him and freed him, pressing a Warpstone blade into his trembling hands. Ascending to the dark Sorcerer's altar, the emaciated king caught Nagash mid-ritual: he bellowed a final war-cry and ran the sorcerer through with the crackling blade. It was over at last, though Nehekhara lay in ruins. But can such reckless hatred ever truly be extinguished?

Seen by an outraged Grimnir, those fleshless skulls have scored a lucky victory against our brave Dawi warriors. Naturally, this calls for a new entry in the Dammaz Kron - strike it out, send them back into the sand!

By Valaya's saddened gaze, those fallen, false kings of the desert do raid Dawi lands, leaving destruction and misery in their wake! Justice will be done, mark my words: this grudge shall be answered a thousand times over!

Grungni is disgusted to witness the sacking of our Dwarfhold fortresses by the Undead forces of the sand-dwelling Tomb Kings. Find them and kill them - all of them - strike this heinous grudge from the Dammaz Kron!
By Valaya's sight, the desert-dwelling Undead dare occupy an honest Dawi Hold. A grudge has been entered and must be struck out - these cravens will pay with their very Unlives!
The living send their champion to end us, but we will end this breather.
The Beastmen's gor thinks to frustrate us. End the creature.
The Northern Gods task their champions to come against us.
The Witch King's minions are abroad - one in particular must be silenced.
Dwarfs have a tendency to interfere with our plans whenever we venture beyond the desert realms. One of their bearded-breathers comes. Silence him.
These men of the northern realms are an empire of thieves and pretenders. Their king - a so-called emperor - sends one against us. Ensure they join the Realm of Souls.
The Greenskins are nothing more than noisome beasts, and now one of their number acts against us. Kill it.
The Asur are cowards. They do not send their hosts against us, but merely mouthed agitators instead. Kill their agent.
Accursed reptiles send an agent to interfere with our plans! End this creature's pathetic existence.
Skaven foes try and undermine us, just as they did with King Alcadizaar. Find their verminous agent and slay it.
The civil war for Nehekhara continues - they send an agent against us. Find them and send their spirit back to the Realm of Souls!
The abominations of Neferata try and spread their agents amongst us. Cleanse the world of their filth. Destroy their agent.
The Elves and their tree-creatures interfere in our expansion by sending an agent against us. Find the threat and destroy it.
The invaders and thieves often come from this nation; it is time for them to feel the scorpion's sting. Send the legions against their lands.
The ice dunes of the Dark Elves are a new realm to add to our own. The legacy of Nehekhara will grow beyond the deserts.
The mountain realms of the Dwarfs are valuable to us, for we need stone for the war statuary. Claim it.
The primitives of the north think themselves safe from the dead. Take their land and disabuse them of such a notion.
These filthy creatures defile ancient lands that once belonged to Nehekhara. Purify the region and claim them back.
The High Elves' arrogance will be their undoing; after all, we are truly immortal, not these fleshy things. Take their realm as punishment!
The reptiles view their borders with intransigence. They must make way for a resurgent Nehekhara. Claim this realm for the Undead.
Djaf, the dog-headed God of War and Death, demands that land be conquered from the vermin that infest realms that should belong to Nehekhara.
Our dynasties have ruled here millennia ago, take it back. These are your lands!
More of Neferata's children infest this land, such creatures must be purged and replaced with the true servants of Ptra and their sovereigns.
The woodland realms offer the Tomb Kings unique opportunities. Claim such a realm and our kingdom will benefit.
The rose unfurls to reveal its thorns, does it? We shall show these living fools what a brier patch truly is. Declare war.
These sub-man creatures are no threat to the glory of the Tomb Kings. War on them until their extinction.
Ptra the Creator sends the legions of Nehekhara to war, for the Gods of Chaos stand at the gates to the Realm of Souls and must not be allowed to cross the threshold.
Make war on the Dark Ones in their frozen climes, for that is the only meaningful discourse they understand.
The Dwarfs come to make war and we should not disappoint such stunted foes. Make short work of them!
This king calls himself an 'emperor', but his rule is weak - he is mortal for one thing. Teach this imposter the true meaning of sovereignty - declare war.
The Greenskin menace has festered long enough! Declare war on these primitive tribes and purge them from the world!
The High Elves have become a pain in your regal behind, so it is time to end their place in this world. Call the legions to war!
The Lizardmen threat can no longer be ignored. Declare war on the cold-blooded kind, let them see the power of death.
The ratmen infestation grows. These creatures have ever been a threat, it is time for them to finally perish.
To become the King of Kings, the other sovereigns must be dominated. The legions shall meet in battle.
The Vampires were a threat of our own making and the sins of Lahmia haunt us still. Now is the time extinguish their kind - make war on them.
The tree-Elves need uprooting. Make war on such long-lived creatures, and show them the true path to immortality.
The prey is marked. Ensure their end.
Conquer these lands for they are yours, whether its denizens - living or dead - know it yet.
Bring about the end of this being - we cannot suffer him to exist any longer!
This army is threat to your rule. Seek them out and bring them to battle.
This place contains crypts of a lost dynasty - it must be scoured.
Such a settlement, teeming with beings, must be destroyed. The desert gods demand it!
This one bears the title of king but his existence is merely the span of a slave. His royal blood is as thin as Elven wine, and for such a sin he must perish.
Even back in the old days it was considered a mercy when an animal became rabid to put the beast out of its misery. Hunt Gorthor down and perform this task.
The Chaos Gods send their 'best' against you, and on the field of battle no less. Ptra is not impressed. Hunt down their crowned champion, show them the power of a real sovereign.
That king - the Dark Elf one. Slay this iron-clad Elf and show the denizens of Naggaroth the power of the true kings, the ones that rule the desert realms!
This stunted king is said to hold grudges. Pathetic! His wrongs are nothing to ours, we awoke without our organs! Seek this ingrate out on the field of battle and end him!
It is time to seek out this 'emperor' we have heard so much about. Find this living king of men and slay him in battle - then the living shall truly fear us!
The Greenskins rally behind the beast known as Grimgor. Seek out this creature in battle and end his lust for our realm.
The Prince of the Asur, the one they hold as a champion and untouchable. Let us prove their claims false - we will hand him nought but death.
The reptiles take orders from the Slann - this Mazdamundi is particularly revered. Destroy it in battle and their reverence will quickly fade.
Seek out this ego-craving ratman and sever its head from its filthy body in battle. Then we shall see how loyal these Skaven truly are.
Their can only be one King of Kings. This one thinks to fight the most ancient of conflicts. It is well. Seek him out in battle.

This Vampire noble claims to a descend from a royal bloodline. His ancestors may have once hailed from Nehekhara but his personal lineage is nothing but mongrels. On the battlefield, hunt him down and destroy him!
This Elven abomination challenges Nehekhara! It likes to hunt, so make it the quarry. Find this 'king' and show him the power of true royalty.
Seek out this serf in battle - this dog - and end his pitiful life. Ptra demands nothing less!
This Beastmen may not be the best specimen of their feeble race but it should still be dealt with.
While the Northmen seem obsessed with skulls, we'll take any bones on offer - especially from the body of this champion!
In battle, hunt down this Dark Elf pretender and extinguish his soul.
There is a Dwarf that frustrates the will of the Royal Priest Kings of old. Hunt down this nuisance in battle and bring about his death!
The thralls to this child-emperor mock us. We should seek them out in battle and take their flesh-coated skulls.
Find this Orc filth that mocks us. Hunt down in the battle and end it.
Seek out the arrogant breather. Find the High Elf herald and slay it! Our honour demands it.
These reptiles use titles such as 'Oldblood' the arrogance! Ours would be the oldest blood there is, if we still had any. Hunt down this lizard usurper and end it!
Seek out Alcadizaar's bane - the Skaven creature that challenges us. Kill the creature in battle, crush his skull under the wheels of a chariot!
This serf - this slave - dares to defy you. Hunt it down in battle and break its soul!
Hunt down the Vampire-spawn - find the creature that dares call itself Unliving and end its existence quickly.
This Elven creature has been sent to challenge us - seek it out during the battle and kill it. Grind its skull into the ground!
The Errantry War of the breathers from the north blocks our way. Engage them with our legions.
We have let these Beastmen roam sacred lands long enough. Bring the warherd to battle!
Chaos comes. The filth-encrusted gods of the north must be stopped. Send your legions forth!
The Druchii come. Engage their dark host and stop them!
Dwarfs send a throng against us. Djaf demands their destruction - engage them in battle!
The uncivilised breathers from the north send an army. Meet them in battle - raise the legion!
An Orc rabble has invaded. Show these filth who should be invading who!
The High Elves send a host to face us. Do not let this challenge go.
The Bretonnians invade! Repel these living trespassers, make them pay for disturbing the dead!
So the Beastmen invade sovereign Tomb Kings land? Repel these creatures!
A Chaos horde, sent by their vile Gods, invades Tomb King lands. Our own gods demand they should be repelled!
The Witch King's thralls dare to invade our lands - these usurpers must be stopped!
The Dwarfs dare invade sovereign territory of the Priest Kings. Send them back to their mountain burrows!
And so these barbarians from the north dare invade the lands of the desert gods. Slay the slave-warriors make them clamour for their green and unpleasant lands.
The Orcs invade. Stop these green skin breathers!
A High Elf host invades sovereign lands of the ever-living Priest Kings. Repel these trespassers.
The Lizardmen invade! Push these creatures back into their foetid jungles.
Coming from their lairs, the Skaven invade! Send these pests back to their foetid nests!
As in life, war and invasion between the Nehekharan kings is inevitable. Now a rival invades and must be stopped.
Vampires send their wet legions against us, invading the realms of the desert gods. Halt this pathetic invasion.
The Wood Elves dare plant their roots in Nehekharan soil. Stop this Elven invasion!
The Lizardmen hiss that we are not part of their Great Plan, yet we are the only plan! Stop their force as it comes against us.
Find the Skaven army that challenges us. By Ptra, victory is the only option!
Djaf revels for the jackal-headed God of War will witness the Legions of Nehekhara fight once more. Seek out the enemy king's legion and engage.
The half-breed scum of Lahmia sends a force that must be stopped. Engage the fleshy, festering Undead!
A Wood Elf host is close. Intercept and destroy it!
War is not the only answer. An alliance is required so we may continue to exist.
These breathers have raiders our tombs for centuries. It is time to raid their lands and plunder their crypts!
The Dark Elf lands hide much valuable lore and secrets to eternal life. Raid their lands and seek such knowledge!
Crack open the Dwarfen Holds and raid their lands, homes and tombs for anything of value.
This young race of men have stolen secrets that belong to Khemri. We shall go, raid and return what has always been ours.
The Orcs have looted and stolen from us for too long. Now, raid their slum lands!
Enter High Elf lands and take! No longer will these arrogant breathers keep what should be ours!
No longer will the Lizardmen hide their so-called knowledge from our Liche Priests. Seek out their treasures, their plaques of lore. Raid their habitat.
We shall plunder the resources of the ratmen. Raid their warrens, destroy their under-world!
This inferior king hides relics we need. Raid his lands, scatter the sands and his legions. All we survey is ours.
Seek out the lands claimed by the Lahmia's bastard children - raid the lands of their bloodlines. Vengeance will be ours!
Enter the tree-strewn paths of the Wood Elves and take their life-source - claim it for the kings of Nehekhara!
Under the desert sands awaits a long-dead legion, eternally loyal and ready to serve. All it needs are the Liche Priests to utter an incantation of awakening.
Destroy a living city of Bretonnia. Send their presents fleeing into our bony embrace!
Seek out a city of the Dark Elves and raze it to the ground. Every stone must tumble. Ptra demands nothing less.
The Dwarfholds of the stunted are a ripe target for our legions. Make it so.
This new empire's death god inhabits every stone and garden in their vile realm. Topple their city.
The Orcs gather in one of their settlements. Raise the legions and destroy it.
The Gleaming towers of the High Elves rival the height of our pyramids. This cannot be allowed to stand - literally.
The temple-cities of the Lizardmen are a cache of lost lore that could bring about the Day of Awakening, unseal their crypts and burn what is left.
Seek out the Skaven nests and put an end to these vermin once and for all!
The city of a rival Tomb King encroaches on our greatness! Raze it, and execute the Necrotect to ensure our pyramid remains the greatest death shrine.
The only way to halt the Vampire threat is to destroy these night stalkers where they slumber.
The Wood Elves lurk in the deep woods. Send in your skeletal legions and fell any tree that could hold such vermin.
Raise a Tomb Prince and add him to your legions.
A Necrotect is needed to enhance the war statuary in our legions and ensure the greatness of death shrines.
Summon a Liche Priest from the Mortuary Cult to serve.
We require a Screaming Skull Catapult to ensure your reign.
Bring forth the desert knights to serve your majesty.
Summon the bodyguard from the Burial Chamber so they may serve in battle.
The archers of ancient Nehekhara remain the best in the world. Ensure they join your legions.
Awaken the war statuary. Stone must march with sand.
Order the chariots into service at once.

The books, along with the Necromancer’s staff, have awoken the Black Pyramid. And so the carrion circle. The Tomb Kings have always lusted for power in life and especially in death. Settra comes, leading an undying alliance to wrest the pyramid from its creator’s most loyal servant. The Followers of Nagash raise their warriors even as the Black Pyramid climbs into the sky. The battle for its control is about to begin.

The five books are found. The Liche Priests begin the ultimate incantation, igniting the power within the stirring Black Pyramid. Nagash’s ultimate legacy is ripe for domination. However, the Arch-Necromancer’s greatest lackey, the Liche King, has deployed his legions and lieutenants to defend the master’s shrine. \\n\\nArkhan himself remains mysteriously absent… for now.

The time has come to hush the wailing of the Crone once and for all. Seek out Hellebron and end her!
At last, Malekith is in your sights! Traitor to your race, Sunderer, and slayer of your family. Find him, kill him!
The mother of all our woes - the Hag Sorceress herself - is ripe for slaying. Take her head, and slake our thirst for vengeance!
You have a new target, my king. Scouts report a threat to the Shadowlands - strike now, before they can bring further ruin.
The Shadowlands has a new enemy; the king must act and cull the threat before it festers into war.
The Shadow King will do anything to protect his realm. His warriors have learned of a threat that needs silencing.
A traitor calls for their own death! One of the Witch King's sycophants threatens our realm - take them into shadow!
War or peace - it matters not, a Druchii is always a viable target. The less of their treacherous kind exist, the safer Nagarythe will be.
Loec’s ravens squawk the name of another of Malekith’s minions to slay. Their time can be measured in mere moments from now on.
To go to war with the Shadowlands is to invoke the retribution of Alith Anar, who will seek out this target and usher them to death.
Those who provoke the Shadow King to war surely do not value life, for they will be deprived of it soon enough!
Although a High Elf, Anar does not play by the same rules as his noble kin; war is not just fought on the battlefield.
It is war with the Druchii! This traitor-kin needs their head severed from their neck! Loec has nominated Anar for this honour…
Loec, the God of Deadly Dances, has given Anar a name - a Dark Elf whose own dance should end, war or not.
The only good Druchii is a dead one. To aid the war, Anar must hunt once more; now he knows the identity of his prey.

The Asur Everqueen is the epitome of beauty - the wretched slaves of Ulthuan even call her ‘The Radiant’, the fawning fools! Despoil Alarielle’s capital. This will delight Khaine, and surely he will reward Hellebron with what she desires the most: her lost youth.

At last, a chance to capture the blackest of widows in her own web! Morathi’s lair is vulnerable; surely this is a chance for the Blood Queen to rid herself of the most power of rivals? Take the Hag Sorceress’ capital!
Alarielle, mother and protector of all the Asur, stands guard over Ulthuan. The invading Druchii must be pushed back!

There is a legend known to the sentinels in the watchtowers far to the north of Naggaroth. It tells of a great multi-headed beast: a War Hydra. The creature does not age, but simply gets larger and its scales denser as the years go by. The Beast of Raema is the perfect quarry, so you head toward the Land of Chill, aiming for the watchtowers that guard the Witch King's realm.\\n\\nAn underling brings you word that, only recently, the watchtower of Dargoth was attacked by a raging beast. The hunt - it seems - is on.

The Dark Elves, like all Elves, are cowards; they just hide their craven nature under a veneer of superiority. The tribe shall take from this watchtower whatever riches still remain, then bring violence to the pathetic survivors until one of them tells you what you need to know.

The Druchii will not talk. Better to simply deprive the wretches of life then waste any more time. Instead, summon one of your own; the Werekin shall track our quarry - the Beast of Raema will not avoid the Norse hunters for long.

You have learned that it was indeed a gigantic War Hydra that attacked the watchtower. This is the monster you hunt! Although there's no doubt, it has also come to light that the creature is not alone. Beastmen accompany the War Hydra, worshipping it as a deity. By all accounts, these Gors are even more rabid than their usual cloven kin. It matters not - if they get between you and your prey then they will become trophies as well!\\n\\nAs you follow the trail, your scouts report back that the beast has struck again! Even now it attacks another Dark Elf watchtower - now is your chance!

While dancing in the Warpstone vapours and flames of the camp's fire, your Shaman claims to have been given instructions from the Dark Gods. He has learned that the ratmen of Clan Gritus have commissioned a great beast - a true abomination from the flesh-shapers of Clan Moulder. From his fervour-vision, the Shaman sees thousands upon thousands of screeching rats scratching on bloody walls, desperate to escape their fleshy prison...\\n\\nClan Gritus were last seen in the cold north - the perfect environment for any Gods-fearing Norseman.

Despite this horde not being Clan Gritus itself, these Skaven are no doubt a vassal-clan or even a decoy. This hunt is going to be a difficult one, for rats are notoriously hard to corner. The trail is at risk of going cold, quite literally. However, it was your Gods that set you on this course, and it is they who can give you the next breadcrumb in the trail. However, you cannot just make demands of the Ruinous Powers - a sacrifice must be made.

The Dark Gods have illuminated the path ahead - they seem as keen as you to grab this prize. It must be worth a great deal, or perhaps slaying such prey will inconvenience the Skaven's own bastard god, the Great Horned Rat? In any case, the way forward is now clear: the hunt is on!\\n\\nThe trail now goes below ground. This is home territory for the ratmen, but not so much for the Norse, who prefer enough room to swing their axes. Caution is advised.
