This is home territory for the ratmen, but not so much for the Norse, who prefer enough room to swing their axes. Caution is advised.

Even by the Norse, it is known that the Annulii Mountains - the unbroken chain that surrounds the Elven home of Ulthuan - are a rich habitat for many wonderous creatures. While the Chaos wastes to the north will always provide the tainted and deranged, the creatures that inhabit the Annulii seem 'purer' and therefore more desirable prey.\\n\\nSetting foot on Ulthuan is no easy task, the Elf-scum that selfishly live on the island have always gone to great lengths to protect it. But they will not deprive you now, especially when word has reached the tribe that a Phoenix matriarch, one that has not been seen in centuries, will appear on their island once again. To take that from the world would cause great upset to the Elves.\\n\\nThe rumour originates from Dark Elf contacts, a merchant on the black market trying to sell a large pinion of the Flamespyre. Time to give this contact a visit and investigate his wares.

The rage in you - channelled by the Dark Gods - begs to punish this pale Elf for daring to make such a demand. Yet, you feel that one punch would break this fragile thing, denying your warband their hunt. You agree to the Druchii's terms and send your underling to find this victim. After all, you can always kill the Elf and his token bodyguards once you have the location of the volcano.

Vaul's Anvil lies across the ocean, on the southern edge of Ulthuan. It is a raging volcano and sacred site for the Asur. The Norse gather their longships and set sail. The High Elves will do everything they can to stop the Northmen setting foot of their precious isle, but they shall fail.

Even by the Norse, it is known that the Annulii Mountains - the unbroken chain that surrounds the Elven home of Ulthuan - are a rich habitat for many wonderous creatures. While the Chaos wastes to the north will always provide the tainted and deranged, the creatures that inhabit the Annulii seem 'purer' and therefore are a more desirable prey.\\n\\nWord had reached you of a rumour amongst the Dark Elves that a Phoenix matriarch, one that has not been seen in centuries, will appear on Ulthuan once again. Legend has it that it is a creature of Hekarti, existing between the mortal plane and the Realm of Chaos. The 'Mother of the Flame' only makes its appearance on the side of the mortal veil rarely, once a century at most, awoken into this world through the heart of a burning volcano. The source of the rumour was a Dark Elf merchant of the black market, who also had knowledge of where the Phoenix is due to appear. He would not give up the information without some petty bargaining, however, which you had little patience for. As you unleashed your Ice Wolves upon him, the wretch told you all you needed to know before one of them bit through his spinal cord with a wet crack.\\n\\nVaul’s Anvil, on the southern edge of Ulthuan, is your next destination – a raging volcano and sacred site for the Asur. The Norse gather their longships and set sail. The High Elves will do everything they can to stop the Northmen setting foot on their precious isle, but they shall fail.

The jungles of Lustria are teeming with deadly – and perpetually hungry – predators, but there is one legend that reverberates through the continent; one myth that spooks the Amazons and even has the Pygmies darting back into their warrens...\\n\\n Where Gargantulzan stalks nothing lives. The mightiest of feral Carnosaurs has roamed Lustria for centuries but, for once, *it* will become the prey – let the hunt begin!\\n\\nA guide is needed to take you on the trail into the foetid jungles. Rumours spoken in hushed tones from one oar-slave to the next have reached you that the slave-merchants at the Point may have someone with such knowledge. The slavers will provide such a guide or become enslaved themselves...

At first the Skink claims ignorance of the dark tongue spoken by your tribe. It refuses to even speak in its natural Saurian. But when one of your men starts to cut off its head-crest, it breaks into a broken version of Empire-speak known as Reikspiel. This is a language your folk recognise from various raids across the Sea of Claws – it is the tongue of mewling victims, and fitting for this battered guide.\\n\\nThe creature babbles non-stop about some 'Great Plan' but after that is beaten from it, the reptile finally mentions a possible lead – an island on which sits a great Crimson Skull, home to the mighty behemoths of Lustria. It is a long journey ahead and so a stop for provisions and a blessing to the Ruinous Powers at the Norse colony of Skeggi would be wise.

After leaving Skeggi, your reptilian guide becomes far less reluctant and seems even helpful in giving directions though the dense jungle. If you didn't know better, you would think the creature was enjoying the misery wrought on your Norsemen - who are people used to cold and ice - now dealing with intense heat and gad-flies constantly feasting on their flesh.\\n\\nIn the far distance, unmistakable roars are heard of timeless beasts on the hunt. It seems the quarry is getting closer...

The jungles of Lustria are teeming with deadly – and perpetually hungry – predators, but the legend of Gargantulzan reverberates through the continent, spooking the Amazons and sending the Pygmies darting back into their warrens. The mightiest of feral Carnosaurs has roamed Lustria for centuries, but now will become the prey.\\n\\nIn an effort to obtain a guide to take you through the foetid jungles on the beast's trail, you sought out the slave-merchants of the Point. The pathetic slavers initially drew a blank on a willing guide, before one of them dared to make a suggestion, leading you to a cage containing a small reptile – a Skink. He claimed that with the right amount of ‘persuasion’, it would lead you to your quarry. At first the Skink claimed ignorance of the dark tongue spoken by your tribe, but when one of your men started to cut off its head-crest it broke into a broken version of Empire-speak known as Reikspiel, babbling non-stop about some 'Great Plan', before finally mentioning a possible lead.\\n\\nAfter a brief stop at the Norse colony of Skeggi for provisions and a blessing to the Ruinous Powers, your reptilian guide leads you deep into the jungle, seemingly far less reluctant in giving directions. If you didn't know better, you would think the creature was enjoying the misery wrought on your Norsemen – who are people used to cold and ice – now dealing with intense heat and gad-flies constantly feasting on their flesh.\\n\\nIn the far distance, unmistakable roars are heard of timeless beasts on the hunt. It seems the quarry is getting closer...

Following your lead, your army strides into the wastelands. Your scouts report that the ancient Shaggoth has been spotted not far from your location, and if you move immediately you can cut him off. At last! Your search may soon be at an end, and the great hunt will finally begin in earnest.

After endless days trudging through the jungle, your warband arrives at a great temple scattered with the bones of beasts and other prey. It is a feeding ground.\\n\\nA great roar rumbles across the clearing, the ground shakes, birds scatter from the lush canopies, and the usually-loud jungle is suddenly silent... until pierced by another roar. Then, from the trees, a chanting is heard "Gargantulzan! Gargantulzan! Gargantulzan!"\\n\\nThe behemoth has arrived, and you must now fight a Carnosaur of legend!

Glorious! The Beast of Raema is just as the legends proclaim - the creature's many heads will make perfect trophies and a worthy sacrifice to the Dark Gods. Its Beastmen acolytes bray with a madness you have not seen in the Cloven Ones before, so be wary when tackling them. But enough posturing - the hunt nears its end and there is a monster to slay!

The Hell-Beast creature looms ahead, then lumbers forward, its straining abdomen appearing to pulse as if barely constraining the hordes within its distended belly.\\n\\nThe monster is truly is an abomination! Its heads will make many trophies and a worthy dedication to the Dark Gods... Kill it!

Those sanctimonious sops in armour, the Bretonnians, 'ave sent an 'eavily-defended convoy of merchant ships our way. Crow reckons they be heading to Araby, and by their sluggishness I'd say they're carrying a goodly haul by those escorts. Let's strike now an' take their riches for ourselves!

So… it would appear that some enterprising fellows from the New World 'ave decided to risk it all against the elements an' of course ourselves, who surely 'ave nothin' left to lose anyway. It's looking pretty likely that Sartosa is their destination. Though they're well protected, taking their cargo as our prize presents an opportunity we daren't pass up.

A convoy of Dark Elf slave ships are heading back to Slaver's Bay, laden with captives raided from Ulthuan's coasts. We should free them... not for altruistic reasons, you understand, but because of their potential as fresh recruits to go on account with us an' join the crew - drowned, raised 'n' bound, they'll be worth more than a cutter full o'gold sovereigns!

Pah! Northmen! Those stinkin' Norscan raiders 'ave been spotted heading back north of Naggaroth frozen following a successful raid on the coasts of the Empire. This particular tribe are known always to take captives for ransom at a later date, so this is an ample opportunity to fill our ratings.

All three verses of the Lost Sea Shanty have been discovered and sung, unleashing the Invocations of Potency hidden within the lyrics. At last, the Star-metal Harpoon now has the power to slay the Merwyrm known as Amanar, but there is one who has been following this ill-gotten quest since the beginning, one whose ship has been stalking yours from afar on the horizon; now you are poised to strike, he steps forward to claim the prize for himself.\\n\\nYou are merely interlopers, for the sea-beast allies itself to the High Elves, who are the mortal enemies of your stalker. Now your use is at an end, he will take the harpoon, kill the beast and revel in the infamy.\\n\\nThat is, of course, only if you let him…

Beware the grave, for it calls to us all. But where will you rest in peace? In soil, or in the depths summoned by the Maelstrom’s call?
Halflings would surely freeze if they visited this moot, but in the south lies a fire undimmed by ice.
Come to a coast ravaged by talon and claw, but do not miss the point for it traces the way to a monolithic secret.
Close to the mount of spiders, find what is lost, for the highlands beyond the plateau hold what you seek.
The desert sands hold only death, but legends also speak of eternal life should you seek the season that follows winter and discover the scarlet pools.
To walk though this passage is to stride through history; a place where Orcs, gods and emperors have fought, and the fire of their bloody rage is encased in darkness.

Afore Valaya’s saddened eyes, the filthy Uzkular of the sea have snatched a righteous victory from true, honest Dawi warriors. The Mother Goddess demands we hunt down this host and send them back to the depths… permanently!

Witnessed by Grungni, a rotten, valueless Undead horde has stolen Dawi treasures from Dawi lands and has dared to take them to Holds beyond our reach, but not beyond our sight - hunt down this host of dead Umgal and avenge this grave offence!

Observed with shock and anger by Grimnir, the dreadful, Unliving creatures of the Vampire Coast have sacked one of our Holds, burning and looting our great fortress. Naturally, this scandalous insult has been recorded in the Dammaz Kron – avenge out noble Dawi kin and strike it from the book!
A crestfallen Grimnir has noticed that the foul Undead ransack and occupy a settlement belonging to ordinary, righteous Dawi folk. The Dammaz Kron has a new grudge - see it is settled at once!

Harkon's mind is split between multiple personalities, all vying for dominance in his head. The only goal they share is the restoration of his psyche; to restore his mind, Harkon must be willing to seek out Lizardmen artefacts and learn of the spell that fractured it.

The still-living that dare to plague this realm were foolish enough to send an agent our way. What a specimen - Let's fill our goblets with their blood an' enjoy this fine diplomatic offering, before it gets cold.
This will be interesting - the unloved children of Chaos dare challenge us. Boo hoo! Slay the mewling beast! It’s a kindness really… no, really it is.
Chaos is the enemy of all - we 'ave to kill its agent before their foul taint spreads an' spores... and then we'll *really* be all at sea!

First rule of piracy is never trust a pirate, even one of yer own men... Actually, especially one of yer own men… No matter, ignore my ramblings - we should kill it before it makes a play for our loot!

Khaine commands the Druchii spill blood in 'is name, but 'e never specified whose blood it should be. Let's assist this worshipper of the Bloody-handed God to move closer to their idol by relieving them of their blood!
Dwarfs? Never underestimate 'em - their stature may be small, but the little sods can still cause you a lot of trouble. Kill this one now, before he bites yer kneecaps off!

The men of the Empire are nothing but sycophants to Sigmar, who cares nothing for their worthless lives, yet still they believe 'emselves superior. Let's remind the fools who rules the waves - let's slay their agent, and swiftly!

Greenskins? Don't make me laugh! "Green Tide"? Green puddle more like. Mind you, in large numbers they can be bothersome, so let's murder this one now an' send bits of 'im back to 'em, so they know to try a lot harder next time.

They’re very 'igh 'n' mighty, is Elves, and it's that sort of arrogance that will see them all drowned. Fancy sending a single agent against us instead of a fleet! Let's kill this one in a really int'resting way an' remind 'em back at Ulthuan that they're mortal after all.

The Lizardmen are just a bunch of brainy snakes - they talk of "Great Plans" but all they really do is interfere with ours! Let's kill this 'orrible thing now before it can cause any more 'arm. Now *that's* a great plan!

This solitary Northman acts against us. Naturally, this sort of thing absolutely can't be tolerated - give 'em a yard and they'll take a nautical mile. I say kill this one quickly, and rid ourselves of a problem.
Skaven are little more than vermin. Now, vermin are known for feeding on the dead, but they also drown very easily, so let's sling this one in the drink before they get ideas 'bout the crew, yarrr?
Though we share some goals in common, the Tomb Kings cannot be permitted to interfere with our plans. This agent of theirs cannot be allowed to live. Let's send 'em a Sartosan message - kill it!

Though we’ve all tasted the Blood Kiss, our landlubbin' kin have started to act against us. Presumably, this has somethin' to do with all that 'swarming across the world'-lark rather than good, honest pirating. To make a point, we should slay their agent, making it clear 'oo authored the death.

Oh pull the other one! Would you believe that the creatures of Athel Loren have dared to venture out and challenge us - here, where we command the waves an' tides?! Let's kill this one slowly - it will put off the other cowards from leavin' their little forest.

I think we've made ourselves perfectly clear on this matter - the coasts of the Old World belong to *us* now. We must evict the previous tenants, an' with extreme prejudice, 'cos we don't want repurcussions further down the line, do we?

Why waste all that time an' energy toiling and sweatin' to put a proper pirate base together when you can just relieve someone else of theirs? This place was run by sea dogs like us, so there won't be much in the way of furnishings. Nevertheless, let's take the place and fly our own colours from its walls.

That sorry bunch, the Dark Elves, long to return to their island of Ulthuan, but they the lack resolve of yer 'ardbitten, salty sea dog. To strengthen it - to do them a favour, yer might say - let's take their territory. That'll give 'em the best reason ever to return 'ome.

The troublesome Dwarfs are famed for their wealth, but not their generosity. Clearly, they must be taught to share, like the fractious children they resemble - let's march up there now an' take by force what they will not give up willingly. What say ye?

This settlement of puny men currently belongs to the living, which is something we're gonna 'ave to change, don't yer think? I say we conquer these lands for the furtherment of our own goals - that way lies sense.

They do say that the so-called "Green Tide" has swallowed much of this world. If this be true, we should sail straight on through, full ahead, an' take it back off 'em. This place makes for the perfect starting point, no?

Those arrogant island-dwellers, the Asur, do not consider our Undead horde to be a threat, so say our sources. I say that their ego shall be their undoing! We should launch a major foray into their lands, starting 'ere, today, with this settlement!

Those rubbish sailors, the slimy Lizardmen, 'ave found that their forces 'ere are overstretched. I reckon we must act before they sort their little supply problem - let's take this land from 'em, pushing them deeper and deeper into their jungle retreats.

Those primitive bufoons, the Norscans, build simple settlements which, when ruined, make great foundations for our own, superior ones. Let's reduce this place to rubble and dust - I reckon it'll make a fine outpost yet!
The ever-putrid ratmen hide and skulk in their warrens 'neath the soil. I say we go down there now and flush 'em out - slay the dirty little cowards and build an empire of our own!

The Tomb Kings' once-great desert empire was destroyed by the denizens of the dead. Looks like they didn’t learn their lesson the first time! It's our destiny to take their town an' remind 'em who's superior, whether on land or sea.

I think we can all agree that our Sylvanian cousins have little idea how to manage the... 'needs' of the living. They should learn to think of 'em as pilot fish dependent on the much-larger whale - us - for direction. I say we take this town from 'em and demonstrate the proper way forward.

Bah! This is good, serviceable land but it's being wasted on a few measly tree houses! We should tear them down and build a proper pirate settlement in their place - somewhere to feed alms for our much more deserving cause. What say you?
Those silly Bretonnians, with their legends and stupid shining armour are 'overburdened' with treasure, the poor mites. We should help them out, like, by relieving them of their loot - yay?
I dunno 'bout you but I'm getting sick to the back teeth of those ridiculous Gor herds - they've been a thorn in our side for far too long. 'Tis time we sent 'em to their graves!

Those so-called 'Dark Gods' send their puppets to infect the world with their taint! *Our* world, mind - they've certainly got gumption, I'll give yer that. We should stop the rot - kill the Chaos fiends and keep the seas for the dead, the way 'twas meant to be!

Filthy, stinkin' pirate scum! Not like us, you understand - different, lesser pirates who go against the code 'cos they've got no respect. These traitors need a lesson. Let's kill 'em all - that'll learn 'em!

As you will know, I have very little time for the Druchii - they think themselves the rulers of the sea and masters of all who sail the waves. We know different, however - Manann the Destroyer is god here and we are his 'umble servants like.

Ooo I'm scared! Those Dwarfs are back and apparently they've got scores to settle with us. I say we re-write those entries and make them the last to grace their petty 'Book o'Grudges' - slay every last tiny one of 'em!

Here's a riddle for yer rum-addled bonces: "Who is the greatest enemy, always at yer shoulder?" Time of course - 'e'll lead 'em to Death, which waits for neither man nor beast as we all know. Let's kill 'em and raise them for our ranks and ratings! What say you?

Those Greenskins seek war with all! You gotta hand it to 'em for their tenacity and fightin' spirit though, no? It's almost a shame that we're gonna have to fight 'em and waste every last one of the stupid green gits!
Like you, I've run out of patience with the Asur, who 'ave meddled and been tolerated for far too long. But it ends 'ere - we should ready the fleet for war!

Those cold-blooded Lustrian lizards live an' die by the garbled plans of a long-forgotten race. They're on a hiding to nothing if you ask me - we should make some great plans of our own an' end their miserable servitude, don't yer think?

The Norscans just don't know when they're beaten, the mindless cretins - they're all beard an' no brain. We should kill these particular ones before the Dark Gods start payin' attention and present a united front, yes?

...And still the cowardly, stinkin' rats come at us - fit only for slaughter if the truth be told. They're not much of a foe when it comes down to it are they? Let's slaughter the lot of 'em and be done with it!

You've gotta respect their tenacity, and defeatin' death is a fine thing an' all that, but really the time of the Tomb Kings has long since passed. Now, they're becomin' a nuisance - if we keelhaul one or two and make the others walk the plank, they might get the message that, here on the 'igh seas, we're the ruling power.

Now, we'd be a little naive if we trusted the Vampire Counts, kin or no. Like us pirates, they 'ave the 'abit of betrayal - a hard one to break I'm sure you'll agree. We should vanquish them with haste and bring their armies under our thrall!

Looks like the tides have brought *total* war to our shores. Each day that passes, it's gettin' closer, so we must act now. Bury the Asrai beneath the waves - they'll think twice 'bout leavin' their tree 'ouses after that!

This lily-livered landlubber has a price on their head, which makes 'em something of an attractive target for salty freebooters such as we. Taking this life means we'll be able to claim a generous reward - I'm in, are you?
This place will make a handy base from which to launch all sorts of raids an' actions. If we capture this region and fly our colours 'ere, our pirate brothers-in-arms will support us, I knows it.
This foe is an enemy of all our kind, so we much face 'em in combat and end their run. Think of it as an symbolic and existential battle - one we absolutely cannot afford to lose.
I don't like this lot and I know you don't either, so I'm proposing that we take the fight directly to their door, 'cos a victory here could well be crucial during the wars to come. Are yer with me?
Cor, blimey! This place is ripe for the picking with loot and plunder of all kinds - we should strip it clean in Stromfels' name!

Our enemies think they 'ave the edge, but you an' I know differently - destroying this place of theirs will deal them a heavy blow, make no mistake. Shall we burn it all down and take their trinkets for ourselves?

Ahhh the fancy king of Bretonnia, with 'is - admittedly really quite lovely - suit of armour and 'is pious devotion to that old hag. He thinks 'imself untouchable, yer know! We should rend 'im in two - break the illusion of infallibility and crush the false hope he gives to his people! Let's see 'im talk of destiny with an axe through his 'ead!

The leader of that stupid herd of Beastmen has reared its particularly 'ungry 'ead once again. I say we lop it orft and watch 'is Gors crumble. I'd like to see 'em try to hunt without 'im - they'll be chargin' 'round in circles, attackin' each other. Free entertainment! Hilarious!

The Dark Gods' lackies swarm around a single leader, who 'imself is obsessed with their grace and favour. This will make our job quite a lot simpler - his death will be the end for these armies of Chaos, so we need to kill this so-called 'Everchosen' in battle, and soon, afore the whole bally lot of 'em show up and we're in bit of a pickle!

Ahh, Luthor Harkon - the ruler of the so-called Vampire Coast, no less. I say we throw 'im all the way down to Stromfels' Chest for the arrogance he's shown, or maybe we send 'im back to The Awakening as just another lifeless corpse to be raised an' bound? Either option works for me!

That prissy, long streak o'seaweed, the ruler of the lanky Dark Elves, is little more than hot air in a barrel. I say we end his reign and the send the Druchii into a panic. Then, we can just pick 'em off like fish in said same barrel. Job done and off to Sartosa for a slap-up feast and grog for all the boys! Yarrr!!

The Dwarf Lord? Do me a favour! He's no more than a petty, bitter librarian consumed by imagined slights an' supposed insults. He's also really, really short, which many of the lads find 'ysterical. We should crush 'im and then write the final entry in 'is blood!

Wow, the emperor 'imself has shown up! That must mean we're doin' something right. Remember he's just a politician, really, 'oo plays at being a warrior. I say we meet 'im in battle so 'e can see first hand that dead pirates cannot be swayed by fancy cloaks an' pretty words.

Oh look - the big boss of the Greenskins has graced us with 'is presence. Like all his kind, he's too stubborn to die and too stupid to retreat in the face of a force like ours! If we can't kill this one, we should bury 'im under an endless zombie horde - either way, he must be dealt with before sundown.

The greatest swordsman in all of Ulthuan 'e may be, but he's still mortal, which we can all agree puts 'im at something of a disadvantage. Shall we introduce the fool to the Gunnery Mob? A dozen or two blunderbusses to the face oughta end this so-called 'sword master'!

As powerful as it is ancient, so they say - the 'ead of all the Lizardmen. I know these snakes, however, and I can tell yer now if we cut off its head, the others will flounder - it'll be the beginnin' of the end for our oldest foes!

The leader of those pathetic Norscans is said to be an accomplished warrior who 'as travelled many a sea. Whether or not that be true - and I suspect it's just flannel as he's just a walking beard really - we should remain cautious. I say we do not take 'im lightly but do take 'is head, yarrr!!

The 'Headtaker' - yep, I know, the arrogance of the thing - is apparently the greatest warrior those cowardly ratmen have to offer. If this be true, then slaying 'im in battle will crush the morale of 'is whole pathetic, ratty race. Couldn’t come soon enough if you ask me!

Ahhh, our old friend the king of self-congratulation - a legend in 'is own lunch hour - is drawn up in front of us with an army. A shame, as we could've 'atched a few lucrative schemes with the Tomb Kings, but instead we're gonna 'ave to kill the lot of 'em. Let's grind 'is army into the dust!

There's nothin' like a good, honest, vengeful rivalry… and this is nothin' like one! Your Unlivin' rival's petty machinations are growing tedious and unimaginative - killin' him in battle will free us from this walkin' annoyance and free up 'is victims to be killed, raised an' bound by us!

They call 'im 'Ariel's Chosen', but when it comes down to it he's little more than a sea dog, but not a good one - a pathetic whelp who'll be easily overcome I'm sure. We should take the battle to 'em before the midwinter pyre robs us of the chance to strike a crushing blow to the Asrai's morale!

Ha! The Bretonnians really are the limit! This foolish 'champion' of sorts believes that their mythical 'Lady' will protect 'em from us! Let's show all those who follow false gods that none can withstand Death's cold embrace! Well, except you of course - you're Unlivin' proof you are.

Oh 'ere we go - more grunting an' nonsense from the beasts o'Chaos. Apparently, this particular 'effer is revered among his stinkin' kind - let's fill it full of lead an' show 'em that pistols trump everything else!

It appears that the Dark Gods are playing their tedious games with yet another simpleton - he believes they actually expect 'im to triumph in battle - against us!! Can you believe the stupidity? I say we kill 'im quickly and put an end to this miserable tale!

Our rivals think they can challenge our power, so we must assert our dominance, lest every scurvy-ridden sea dog on the ocean believes they too can turn on us. Kill their leader in battle, then all will see that it is us an' us alone who rule the waves of this world!

The weasely Druchii believe that it is they who harbour the lords of dread, but we know different like, don't we? Let's prove their misconceptions to be falsehoods - Show 'em the true meaning of dread - slay this leader of theirs in full view of their men!

Normally, I’d be dead bored by this point, but as it turns out, this Dwarf has proven to be quite fierce. Not a problem for a vicious, murdering bunch of pirate scum like us though is it? And killin' him should deal a significant blow to 'is declining race! Let's do it!

This Imperial type has proven popular among both his men an' the Empire's diplomats, such as they are. I reckon that killing 'im and raising his corpse will shake the whole of man's realm to its stupid, cowardly core! Let's spill some blood - pass my bill 'ook, Bernie!

Though 'tis well known that Greenskins are stupid an' pointless, this particular specimen has been developin' somethin' of a reputation among 'is kind as an apt killer. If that be the case, we should kill 'im in battle an' break the morale of 'is boys - they'll crumble in no time, you mark my words!

The High Elves may well be famed for their martial prowess, but no matter how talented they are, sheer numbers will eventually break even the greatest warrior. Prove that to the Asur by saddlin' up the Undead horde and sendin' 'em out.

I like to think of the Lizardmen as a single, giant snake - cut the head orft an' they'll flop about a bit, then breathe no more. If they dare to move against us again, we should kill their leader, sit back and 'ave a few rums whilst they flail and flounder.

This Norscan 'champion', it would appear, has managed - unbelievably - to attract the attention of 'is fickle gods, the Ruinous Powers, an' has gained a name for 'imself as a warrior who does not fear death in any of its guises. He may not fear 'is end, but he would do well to fear what happens afterwards!

The Skaven - as a whole, you understand - are like a ship without a keel: totally spineless. This particular specimen may well have risen through their verminous ranks, but that's of little merit really. I say we kill this ratman - in fact, let's kill 'em all, every last man rat of 'em!

This Tomb King believes it is our equal in battle, but several ages 'ave passed since they were top o'the food chain. We should grace this nauseating bag o'bones with a second an' final death! Shall we kill 'em again? Come on, I want a go...

Our landlocked cousins believe themselves to be superior, even though they just sit there in the dark whilst we're out piratin' for profit! Killing this particular one would serve as a suitable warnin' to others who might want to challenge our dominance. Let's do 'em - as a warning like!

They say that the forests an' woodlands of Athel Loren are burstin' with life - that's even more livin' for us to choke the life out of then, no? We should start by plucking this 'ere weed - sorry, did I say 'weed'? I meant Asrai leader!

Those mortals of Bretonnia ride atop their steeds, thinkin' themselves all unstoppable like. Clearly, they need to be confronted an' filled with musket balls, then raised back into our service. Imagine... our very own elite cavalry brigade! Let's get down to it - there's much killin' to be done!

Ere we go again! They are certainly relentless, those tinkers the Beastmen, but they've been roaming around the land for far too long, unchecked. It's time we met 'em in battle and put an end to their hunt once an' for all - what say ye?

The armies of Chaos march this way, believing themselves chosen by the Dark Gods and tasked with bringin' about the End Times. What a load o'guff, I say - I don't think their Gods 'ave even noticed they're 'ere! Just as well, really, as we're going to kill 'em all now an' put their army under new management!
Rival pirates have gathered a mighty crew, the cheeky bunch o'beggars! Let's greet 'em with a broadside that will shiver their timbers an' rattle their stinkin' Undead bones, yarrrr!!!
So, those lanky, cunning Dark Elves have put together a great army in the hope that we'll cave. Naturally, we won't - let's destroy this cruel host before it can get the upper hand!
Ah, Dwarfs - my favourite, you know. I like 'em boiled with just a little salt an' vinegar! Oh, I do like a good feed - let's go an' pick up dinner!

Manann blesses us this day, me hearties - the Empire have sent an army of their very best living men to face us. Let's not muck about - 'ow about we kill 'em quickly and reinforce our ranks 'n' ratings?
Eads up, lads - 'ere come the Greenskins, literally 'mob-'anded' and 'ungry for… well, their own deaths, I reckon, once our Gunnery Mobs get stuck in and cut 'em in two!

Those 'igh 'n' mighty High Elves mean to meet us in battle with an elite 'ost no less! Well, I dunno 'bout you but I wouldn't wanna disappoint them - let's march forth and give 'em more than a good run for their money!

These Bretonnian fools have promised the impossible – an errantry war against death itself! Slay these ignorant mortals - they're nothin' but a nuisance and it warms me cockles to see 'em screamin' and drownin' in all that armour!

The Beastmen have dared to enter territory that everybody knows belongs to us - the little scamps! We can't let a transgression like that go unpunished now, can we? Let's kill all of 'em and then I suppose we'll 'ave to find a use for their corpses...

Like clockwork, the armies of Chaos 'ave arrived, seeking to destroy all we've built up o'er the years. Yep - I agree, it is unacceptable behaviour. We should meet them in battle and see to their immediate destruction.

A band of rival pirates 'ave invaded our land and are looking to take our loot for 'emselves! Cheek like this simply cannot stand! We need to block off their retreat and finish them in battle once and for all!

Dark Elves 'ave marched into lands that all 'ere know are rightly ours. We can't tolerate this sort of thing - give 'em an inch an' they take a nautical mile. Let's load up the cannons with buckshot an' fill 'em full o'holes!
The Dwarfs have invaded our land - these stunted fools come seeking our territory but all they'll find is their own doom! Yarrr! March against 'em - turn 'em into steaks for our tea!
The Empire might claim these lands as their own, but the fools don't realise that we acquired this prize fair an' square, like, and we will not relinquish it without a fight. So, let's go to battle!
They're nothin' if not persistent, those dirty little Greenskins. They've come here, to *our* land and seek battle. I saw we give 'em what they want an' preferably more than they can 'andle!

Those highfalutin, lanky landlubber, the High Elves, 'ave sent an army to our lands, bless their cotton socks. Apparently, they've got destruction on their minds, which must be awful for 'em, the poor mites. Let's relieve 'em of their lives, shall we? Shall we raise our dead and prepare for a scrap?

Those snaky Lizardmen are invading! Trouble is, at one point all this belonged to 'em, so they've got the arse 'bout our presence 'ere. I reckon that we need to push 'em back before they can undo all our progress in these parts!
Those dirty Norscan dogs 'ave invaded our lands - *our* lands, the cheeky swines. Let's seek 'em out and send 'em back to the frozen north from whence they came!

You've really gotta watch 'em like a hawk - those tenacious ratmen have burrowed their way into our lands. Let's take the breath from their bodies and break this host into lots o'little rat pieces! Yarrr!!

The stinkin', untrustworthy Tomb Kings have gathered together their armies of old and moved 'em against us. Seems a bit unfair - after all, we just want loot an' power - that's not too much to ask it is? Let's meet 'em in battle an' ensure they do not march again.

The sneaky, but nevertheless namby-pamby milksops, the Vampire Counts, have raised their own Undead force and march into our lands. Clearly this is more than a bit naughty - it is unacceptable. We've allowed them to exist alongside us for long enough; this affront will be their final mistake – let's get to battle!

The Asrai - that's Wood Elves to you uneducated lot - 'ave got off the fence led their armies against us in an invasion of our lands, their armies bolstered by tree-spirits, whatever they are. This move will be their undoing, however, as the rot of death seeps into their wooden allies we'll seek their destruction! Prepare for battle!

The Lizardmen have raised an army - no doubt what's on their minds is mashin' us up into a pulp. I know, I know - like they 'ave a hope, especially with Stromfels and Manann at our backs. I saw we attack now before they're good an' ready.

If you tired of the Norscans, chances are you're tired of killin' - they've raised something of a force, intendin' to go to war on behalf of the Dark Gods'. I think we need to slay 'em all before they can march forth and cause problems for us.
A horde of dirty, stinkin' ratmen 'ave been seen up 'ere on the surface, where they 'ave no right to be. I think we need to get raisin' and bindin' an' then deal with these pests, without delay!

Never takin' no for an answer, the Tomb Kings 'ave raised an army an' surely plan to attack us. Under the circumstances, I think it would be best that we meet 'em in battle an' crush 'em before they've even begun to march!

The Vampires of this land 'ave raised an army and it's looking like they intend to meet with us on the battlefield. This will definitely be their last mistake – let's move to head 'em off an' then slay every last one of 'em with stakes an' garlic an' whatever else we can find, yarrr?

Part of the trouble wiv Wood Elves - 'cos there's several ways they can get on yer nerves - is that you never know where yer truly are with 'em. You can't trust 'em and you can't live with 'em, so the only remainin' option is to kill as many of 'em as you can - preferably all of 'em at once. Let's go!
Now, I know it may not sound particularly piratey to you, but a pact between us *is* required. An alliance will guarantee that our plundering days continue for quite some time yet.

The people of this realm are overburdened with luxuries, the poor beggars! I say we aid these unfortunate mortals an' lighten their loads somewhat. What do yer reckon? Let's raid their roads to free them of their 'eavy burden.

Those swindlin' scallywags - those honourless pirates - 'ave stolen the riches of the land and the poor folk that live there! Its our duty, as good, honest, 'ardworkin' sailors, to take back these treasures and, er, return 'em to their rightful owners. Let's raid, pillage, and plunder, until we've reclaimed every last stolen penny!

The Dark Elves will never achieve their goal to return to Ulthuan if they continue to be distracted by such unnecessary trifles! We need to raid their lands an' take their treasures away - they'll thank us in the long run I'm sure.

That dying race of Dwarfs still 'ave plenty o'treasure down in the vaults of those holds they dare not return to for fear of rats 'n' Orcs 'n' the like. They can’t miss what they don’t know is missing - I say we loot these holds for ourselves!

Apparently, the Empire’s trade routes are - and I quote - "fraught with dangers". I say the mortals who take these roads are asking for trouble! Let's raid these 'em an' punish the merchants who travel them for their truly terrible 'ubris - a terrible thing in any being.

Stromfels an' Manann - gods, I hate the Greenskins, wiv their… green skins an' nasty breath. Some of 'em 'ave the beginnings of an understanding of the value of treasure, but most are more interested in pullin' teeth outta the dead. I call that "poor asset management", and it's not on - let's raid their stashes and punish these gits!

Renowned for their craftsmanship an' the beautiful trinkets they make, the High Elves certainly 'ave abilities. Unfortunately, those abilities don't extend to defeatin' the likes of us - let's take their gold off of 'em and inspect it for ourselves!

Those Lizardmen - an' you've gotta admire they're persistence on this matter - are still pitifully clingin' on to the words of a dead race lost to time. We need to relieve 'em of this burden - take those statues they still obsess over an' teach 'em a lesson!

Norscans are far too uncivilised to understand the true value of the treasure they hoard - clearly, only we appreciate its real worth. Shall we take their trinkets from them, so they learn somethin' about the true nature of the world?

The ratmen have no interest in the beauty of gold and treasure, as they only trade in Warptokens an' backstabbin'. They steal the world's wealth to deny superior races their glory, which is more than a bit of a liberty. Let's take back these riches shall we?

The Nehekarans once understood the value of gold an' built great big monuments to celebrate their wealth. Now, the Tomb Kings just obsess over little jars an' forget 'emselves. If they don't want 'em, we should take their riches away - think of it as de-clutterin' like...

Forever plotting an' schemin' - far more than us - the lords of this 'ere land won’t even notice if we lift a few treasures from under their… well, where their noses used to be anyways. Shall we raid this region while they are distracted? Would make sound commercial sense in my opinion.

I freely admit that I don't understand Wood Elves. The Asrai’s lands are filled with riches, but they spurn 'em and 'ang about in the trees for centuries. It don't make sense, does it? Let's launch a raid against 'em an' take these treasures for ourselves!

There's plenty of dead in the ocean now, all waitin' to be raised for our armies an' crews. Trouble is, we've not got enough chiefs - we need more leaders to control 'em. I think we should summon a new Lord - you agree?

The livin' Bretonnians act against us! It would appear that they're planning to strike at us using this settlement as their base of operations. We need to get over there an' burn it down before they can act.
Our rivals out at sea 'ave taken this land - we can't allow 'em any respite, mind you. We need to burn down their settlements an' take their ships for ourselves - we alone rule the seas!
The Dark Elves 'ave interfered with our plans for too long! Let's destroy this settlement in order to remind 'em that the dead rule the seas… and the coasts… and, er… well everywhere really!

Once again, those pesky, landlubbin' Dwarfs hide in their mountain Holds, hoping to weather the storm that's surely comin' - too stubborn to die, too indecisive to put up an effective fight. This will be their fatal error - destroy this Hold and make it their burial tomb instead!

That phoney god of men, Morr, sends 'is servants to ensure the dead stay restin' an' never rise again. These worshippers must be killed if the dead are to rise to *our* call. It's fitting, then, that we kill 'em an' raise 'em to our service! Let's destroy their base of operations!
The filthy, maraudin' Greenskins occupy this land. We really cannot coexist with such savages as these, can we? Shall we burn down their settlement for 'em, as a bit of a gift, yarrrr?
The tide is rising an' the wind is right, so the time to attack the Asur is nigh. Let's burn down this settlement while the waves are still supportive of our cause?

The Lizardmen have long been a thorn in our side, so we must burn down this land o'theirs - destroy their spawning pools an' raze their fancy temples too. It's almost a shame to be sayin' goodbye to our oldest foes!
More Norscans, gettin' in the way and makin' a nuisance of 'emselves! It'll be noisy and painful for them, but we need to burn their place down now so that we may push forward.

The Skaven 'ave built their city beneath the ruins of our next target. If we just bring these ruins down upon 'em we'll crush our enemy down into their 'oles - it'll be really 'ard, if not impossible, for 'em to come back from somethin' like that!

I tell yer - they're just not interested in all that gold an' wealth anymore. We could get in there, burn down their place and take all these riches for ourselves. There'll barely even notice - trust me!

The Vampires of this land raise the dead for their own purposes, which of course denies us potential crewmembers. Naturally, we can't allow 'em to steal from us, so let's burn down their stronghold an' carry the corpses for ourselves, yarrr?
The terrain here in this woodland impedes our movements. If we destroy the settlement an' spread death's embrace through its roots, they'll never come back at us, not in a million years!

A Mourngul Haunter has strengths which absolutely should not be underestimated - its eternal hunger for flesh can be a great asset to us, remember. However, it's worth notin' that our control over such a beast can never be entirely certain...

Let’s recruit a Vampire Fleet Captain; they aren’t half good at magic an' know a thing or two about ships as well! Just point 'em at the enemy, give 'em a share of the booty and you’ve got yourself a fine new crewmember!
Let's summon a Gunnery Wight shall we? It'll aid our missile units no end - the expertise they've retained from their, er, actual lives, is invaluable to us.
Our melee hordes are so numerous there's no army - livin' or dead - that can match 'em, in my estimation. I say we raise even more - what say you?

Considering they're really quite dead and there's bits droppin' off 'em, the dexterity of our Zombie Horde is second to none. That bein' the case, shall we raise more of 'em an' watch the enemy drown in lead?
Our armies require long-range firepower, just like our ships. We should therefore recruit some artillery to open up a devastating new sea-rout to destruction - yarrr!!
The terrible creatures at our disposal are fearsome in battle - we could make use of 'em an' lay waste to our enemies'… well, everything our enemies 'ave, includin' their lives!

The search for the wreck of the Vengeance is underway and using the map we gained from the shop in Sartosa we have set sail to the shallow seas of the Dragon Spine. However, upon arrival we have spotted a ship flying the flag of The Sunken Land Corsairs. What these pirates are doing at this very location is unknown, it is perhaps a coincidence, but regardless they stand before us and the wreck of the Vengeance; and more importantly the Star-metal Harpoon sunk within her.

Jus’ north o' Norsca thar be a little-known expanse of ocean called the Kraken Sea. It is important to them crackpot Northmen o’ the nearby coastline of Skjold, who drop the remains of their fallen warriors there. T’them, there be great favour to be had bein’ eaten up by those mutated sea-monsters of Chaos, but some of the souls are rejected by the fickle Gods, marooned underwater an’ forsaken ‘til the right juju gets ‘em up an' killin’ again.

The pirate known as Lucky Levi met ‘is end at the ‘ands of ‘is own men after dabblin’ in black magic with 'is lucky rabbit’s foot. The fool was tryin’ to raise Zombie Deckhands for his crew, but ‘is first mate was not best pleased at bein' replaced by the walkin’ dead, an’ so shivved his cap’n while he slept. But Levi’s Undead mob continued to serve their master, throwin’ the first mate an’ the rest of the livin’ crew overboard an’ scuppered Levi’s ship.

Make no mistake, a swarm o’ Fell Bats at sea always ends in blood-soaked waters. As the pirate cap’n Salazar sailed his ship the Salt Lord up the cursed coast of Mousillon, carryin' a single rare Estalian shillin’ swiped from the castle-port o’ Castelo Novo, the blood-suckin’ monsters attacked, killin’ cap’n an' crew in seconds. They say the evil things made their home amongst the rotting corpses an' tattered sails of the driftin’ vessel, but the Salt Lord was ne’er seen by mortal eyes again.

High above Manann's ocean realm, in the place them landlubbers call the Southern Grey Mountains, thar be a place wiv vast seams o’ gold ore known as the Vorgo Crags. None be brave enough to mine ‘em though, ‘cause o’ the coldness an’ the evil things that wander the place… the only piece o’ Vorgo gold known to exist outside the mountains was carried out by the single survivor of a doomed minin’ expedition, the rest of ‘em bein’ taken by slow, painful starvation before the evil mountain Winds made somethin’ unspeakable out of ‘em.

Panteleon was an old Knight o'Quenelles, where those Bretonnian landlubbers are in cahoots with the Elves of the neighbourin’ forest. They say ‘e wore a piece o’Athel Loren amber round ‘is neck - imbued with powers it was, could even bring life to dead flesh! Sadly, 'twas lost when the fool sailed to the Vampire Coast to take on a shoal o' Prometheans… Panteleon slaughtered ‘em, but the crabs eventually dragged ‘im off ‘is ship an' pincered 'im to pieces. But 'is ship, the Lamprey, survived.

Thar be no sailor alive who don’t know the tale of Cap’n Vangheist. A Wizard named Albrechtus von Zeich had paid ‘im in ingots o’ the purest gold to provide passage through the Sea o’Chaos, but when von Zeich refused the cap’n’s ambitions to get the secrets of immortality from the Realm o’Chaos itself, he got shot. Sailin’ on right out o’ the mortal plane, Vangheist an’ ‘is crew left their bodies an’ material things behind, includin’ the ship’s cursed cargo - its fate remains unknown...

The magic that took ol’ Nyklaus von Carstein out o’ Sylvania needed more than just some powerful juju an’ a titanic will… some magic trinkets were also used to bolster ‘is energies, one bein’ the mysterious Stone o’Schwartzhafen. They say it contains the souls of the great fallen warriors o’Sylvania from afore the von Carsteins’ time. Alas, the stone got lost after the Bloody Reaver had an ‘ole ripped in ‘er hull by the Heldenhammer's broadside, tragically spillin’ some booty into the sea.

Reik-Admiral Houghhoff possesses one of the three verses of the fabled Lost Sea Shanty, and by exceeding his infamy you have provoked his ire. He is now sailing the seas, determined to hunt you down and reclaim his place. You must put an end to this pirate once and for all, and in doing so take the verse from him!

Fhiron Wavemaker possesses one of the three verses of the fabled Lost Sea Shanty, and by exceeding his infamy you have provoked his ire. He is now sailing the seas, determined to hunt you down and reclaim his place. You must put an end to this pirate once and for all, and in doing so take the verse from him!

Barron von Heastie possesses one of the three verses of the fabled Lost Sea Shanty, and by exceeding his infamy you have provoked his ire. He is now sailing the seas, determined to hunt you down and reclaim his place. You must put an end to this pirate once and for all, and in doing so take the verse from him!
Defeat the pirates that possess the First Shanty Verse for a chance to steal it. Specifically defeating their faction leader in combat, or forming an alliance, will guarantee you get it.
Defeat the pirates that possess the Second Shanty Verse for a chance to steal it. Specifically defeating their faction leader in combat, or forming an alliance, will guarantee you get it.
Defeat the pirates that possess the Final Shanty Verse for a chance to steal it. Specifically defeating their faction leader in combat, or forming an alliance, will guarantee you get it.

The fleet grows and the curs of this world learn to fear your name, but there are still those who oppose us. Send these fools to the depths - the Maelstrom will chew them up and spit them out with a more favourable disposition, my lord.
Blessed are the red-crested believers, infused with Sotek’s everlasting spirit, imbued with staunch resilience, propelled by the unwavering zeal of the Serpent-God’s Chosen.

Against the tide of non-believers, Sotek’s red-crested faithful shall emerge as his champions, to go forth and make disciples of all the Old Ones’ children, beseeching them in the name of the Serpent-God.
Only after the bastions of the Old Ones are reclaimed, the incursions of the Rodent-God’s defiling minions upon the land called Lustria shall be borne by an epic struggle…
When the evil rat-spawn set foot on these sacred shores to deliver their plague and pestilence, the time of their great purge shall be at hand…
Once the Great Serpent is beseeched, the evocation of His slithering servants in the jungle shall see the enemies of the Old Ones’ children fall victim to His vengeance…

The Great Serpent shall have His day, for He is the vanquisher of all rodent-kind, honoured and invoked through rightful tribute, that shall see the rivers of the mighty Amaxon run crimson with blood…
Behold Sotek, a serpent of such unimaginable size and appetite that he shall swallow the Rat-God himself, whole, and spend a thousand years digesting him, crushing him within his coils!

A stunted warmblood is known to be stealing from our kin, plundering our stockpiles of raw materials. His wanton pilfering hinders our ability to complete sequences central to the Great Plan – Lustria must be rid of him!

One of the warmbloods has been observed revivifying the wounded of his invading kin, reversing much of our cohorts’ hard work on the battlefield and faltering our progress in eradicating them. His elimination will be hugely favourable.

A cohort of foolish warmbloods once discovered the City of Mists and dared enter its gates, all but one being unceremoniously slaughtered by its mighty guardians. The one survivor’s knowledge of Xlanhuapec makes him a grave threat that must be destroyed.

One of the foreign invaders prowls our jungles’ canopies with surprising aptitude. This light-footed huntress poses a great threat to us, having already slain dozens of our gargantuan kin for reasons unknown – she must be expulsed.

Lustria’s jungles burn. Its temple-cities crumble. Under Markus Wulfhart’s command, the Emperor’s forces have wreaked havoc in the New World, wantonly plundering the lucrative holdings of the lizard-beasts while sweeping aside all foes sent against them. But now, the most monstrous of them of all has been roused.\\n\\nWulfhart's scouts have informed him that the creature known as the Spirit of the Jungle has been sighted somewhere in the vicinity of Itza. The Huntsmarshal has caught the scent; this will be his toughest hunt yet.

One by one, Nakai fought off the so-called great hunters in cahoots with the Huntsmarshal. And one by one, they fled into the jungle like the warm-blooded cowards they are. Nakai correctly sensed they would be back for more, and now the chief warmblood himself, Markus Wulfhart, takes to the field with them. Lustria’s future hangs in the balance, for why else would Nakai be so compelled to act? This conflict ends now!

What a gods-forsaken place this truly is. It seems that not a day goes by without the news of some horrible tropical disease striking some poor settler down. The most innocuous cut or scratch sustained here can become horribly infected within hours, making every trek into the jungle a highly risky endeavour indeed.\\n\\nPerhaps by fate, word has reached me of a mysterious individual who shadows the Empire’s troops in the deep jungle, patching up the wounds of the gravely injured left behind following skirmishes with the lizards. Men thought to be well within Morr’s deathly embrace have been mysteriously brought back from the brink by someone who clearly has advanced medical training, with even the most horrendous injuries cleaned, disinfected, and stitched as if by the hands of the most highly-trained physician in all of the Empire. Our very own injured relate to me their encounters with this healer, not remembering much other than glimpses of a necklace of fangs – trophies perhaps?\\n\\nI have been in few environments more treacherous to man than Lustria; it goes without saying that for us to endure here, we should somehow reach out to this ‘medic’ and persuade them to join our cause.

Hertwig van Hal is an intriguing individual. He bears the surname of a well-known ancient lineage of Witch Hunters, but for reasons unknown to me he seems rather ashamed of it. When I brought it up he responded angrily, claiming his vocation as a Witch Hunter was not of his choosing. He then quickly changed the subject, revealing that he was a master physician of Altdorf and insisted I address him as ‘Herr Doctor’. It truly beguiles me why a physician from Altdorf is carrying out Witch Hunter duties in Lustria, but I am not one to poke about in another man’s private affairs.\\n\\nThere is certainly much more to Herr Doctor which perhaps in time he will reveal on his own volition, but right now he has temporarily left camp. Before leaving, he told me he intends to track down some information about one particular Vampire he has been searching for called Alistair the Red. He has given me assurances that I cannot help him with this particular task and that he will return soon.

In getting to know Herr Doctor better, I’ve discovered that he is a most conflicted man. He is ruthlessly obsessed with destroying Vampires, but is also a skilful healer with astounding convalescent skills. I felt I had built up enough of a rapport to bring up the subject of his famous lineage once again.\\n\\nWith a deep sigh, Hertwig explained his intense hate for the van Hal name, for his ambition was always to preserve life and not to chase destruction. For him, the van Hals would never be innocent of their progenitor’s sins and he wanted nothing to do with them. "A man can try to avoid his destiny as much as he wants," he added, "but in the end it will always find him." He would elaborate no further. \\n\\nThe next day, he invoked me to continue helping him with his mission to track down Alistair the Red. He says the best way to draw attention from a Vampire Pirate is to raid their lands and waters, so that is what we will do. It is certainly not without a touch of irony that we are probably about to steal from pirates.

Herr Doctor continues to be driven by a strong desire to destroy this creature of the night he refers to as Alistair the Red. Having observed Hertwig slay dozens of Vampires up to now, it is clear he gains no pleasure from it, but at the same time carries out Witch Hunter duties with the aptitude of one who was born to do so – like a true van Hal. Though my curiosity threatens to overcome me, I have resisted asking further questions about the history of this man I have befriended. It seems there is no time for it anyway, as Herr Doctor now wants us to mobilise against The Awakening, and immediately.\\n\\nThose who know anything about the area say the place is a husk of an old colony that was settled many years ago, but was left haunted, derelict, and overrun by the Undead. There is a lot of unknown history there, but Hertwig is convinced its winding streets and deep catacombs harbour the creature that he seeks to destroy.  A direct assault on this place seems dangerous, but I am a man of my word and Herr Doctor assures us he is very close to achieving his goal.

In the time I’ve spent helping van Hal I have gotten to know him well, learning that his story is one of great tragedy not unlike my own.\\n\\nIn his early days Hertwig was a physician of Altdorf and distanced himself from the van Hal name, hating its connotations. He cared little for the affairs of Witch Hunters, dedicating his life only to the practise of medicine and his beloved fiancé Matilda. One evening, a red-haired corpse was brought to his surgery with a stake mysteriously plunged through its heart. The young, naïve doctor removed the stake during the examination and later that night found the creature with its fangs buried in Matilda's neck. He desperately fought the vile monster off before it fled, but it was too late. To prevent Matilda from rising from the dead, he had no choice but to stab her through the heart and remove her head. Beset by anguish and grief, van Hal felt he had no choice but to dedicate himself to the destruction of creatures of the night.\\n\\nWith the red-haired Vampire that killed his beloved now slain, he is grateful for my help and guidance and will serve the expedition indefinitely.

In the time I’ve spent helping Herr Doctor I have gotten to know him well, learning that his story is one of great tragedy not unlike my own.\\n\\nIn his early days Hertwig was a physician of Altdorf and distanced himself from the van Hal name, hating its connotations. He cared little for the affairs of Witch Hunters, dedicating his life only to the practise of medicine and his beloved fiancé Matilda. One evening, a red-haired corpse was brought to his surgery with a stake mysteriously plunged through its heart. The young, naïve doctor removed the stake during the examination and later that night found the creature with its fangs buried in Matilda's neck. He desperately fought the vile monster off before it fled, but it was too late. To prevent Matilda from rising from the dead, he had no choice but to stab her through the heart and remove her head. Beset by anguish and grief, van Hal felt he had no choice but to dedicate himself to the destruction of creatures of the night.\\n\\nWith the red-haired Vampire that killed his beloved now slain, he is grateful for my help and guidance and will serve the expedition indefinitely.

The colonists have long known about Lizardmen mining convoys that regularly travel along established trails in the deep jungle like clockwork. They transport some sort of glossy black raw material that resembles obsidian, the dense metal that the Wizards of home know all too well for its anti-magic properties. There was some concern when these convoy movements inexplicably stopped, perhaps now taking different routes if not ceasing altogether. I was unconcerned, but apparently the lizards don’t change their ways without very good reason. To appease the colonists, I sent out an expedition to investigate the old trails and they soon returned with a captive – a Skink, one of the convoy overseers.\\n\\nWhen our Saurian translator asked the skittish creature about the black material, it held its forked tongue. Further ‘prodding’ with my hunting knife made the creature reveal something about a "short, bearded warmblood" that had been repeatedly stealing from their convoys, forcing them to change their routes.\\n\\nWhat is a Dwarf doing this far from the Spine of Sotek mountains? This Dawi is either incredibly brave or incredibly stupid to be harassing the Lizardmen on their own turf, but is getting away with it somehow. Credit where credit’s due…

It is truly astonishing how this Dawi Engineer has been able to survive out in the wild on his solo forays against the Lizardmen's convoys, but it is clearly down to his own ingenuity. A keen and talented inventor, Jorek seems to have all sorts of survivalist equipment at his disposal, all designed and built himself. He is very secretive about his past, revealing little more than the location of his previous home back in the Old World, the great Dwarf port of Barak Varr.\\n\\nIt seems that something in Jorek’s earlier life clearly irks him, which really isn’t all that surprising – Dwarfs feel all wrongdoings committed against them as if they had only just happened. With wild eyes he tells me that he is destined for great things, but must "rebuild his reputation, one invention at a time". Though he appears sceptical that we can really help him, he sees value in the protection the expedition can provide on his travels through Lustria. He has also suggested we gather some resources for some new inventions he thinks may prove useful to him and the expedition.

I am amazed by this Dwarf’s ambition and enthusiasm for invention. He seems to find a use for any kind of material he can find and gets excited about all the unique resources we come across. This obsession with metallurgy and mineralogy has made it clearer to me why he is here – the Lustrian jungle is one of the most unexplored places in the known world, offering many mysterious raw materials with strange and amazing properties to a tinkerer like Jorek.\\n\\nGradually, the Master Engineer has also become more open about his past. Given his chosen surroundings, I was surprised to discover that he was once a great shipbuilder but had been shunned and ousted by the Engineers' Guild back in Barak Varr. According to him, his contemporaries considered him a threat because of his intellectual brilliance, although I have a feeling there are elements to this story he has not revealed. It is perhaps unwise to probe any further; I can never hope to understand the confusing, stubborn, grudge-holding ways of the Dawi anyway. As long as Jorek continues to help the expedition, we will continue to supply him with the materials he needs.

Jorek has revealed to me that he has been working on something big. He described it as a "masterpiece of gyro-powered flight", a flying machine he claims will be better than any Gyrocopter built by his kin anywhere in the world. All he needs to complete its assembly is a chunk of a rare metal called 'obsinite', a form of Lustrian obsidian used by the Lizardmen that is harder and more durable than steel. With the Lizardmen's mining convoys having now changed their routes to avoid Jorek’s thieving attentions, we’ll have to find a different source of the metal. He tells me he has a hidden stockpile collected from his previous smash-'n'-grab attacks, located on the Volcanic Islands off the east coast of Lustria. Alternatively, he also knows of a consignment of obsinite heading north towards the Ancient City of Quintex.\\n\\nBy the sounds of it, the flying machine Jorek intends to build would be a very welcome addition to the expedition's armoury. This may very well be worth the effort!

In return for helping him obtain all the raw materials he has desired thus far, Jorek has accepted a permanent position with my expedition. This is most fortunate, for he has proven himself a valuable member of the hunting party, whose unique skills make him integral to our mission. More than that, Jorek has become a loyal friend. One day, as we enjoyed a barrel of Bugman’s together, he revealed to me the rest of his sorry story.\\n\\nOnce a member of the Cragbrow Clan of Barak Varr, Jorek was commissioned to design new steamships for his throng, but utilised methods of engineering that eschewed Dwarf traditions. He knew there was great potential in his designs regardless of the techniques used to develop them, but could never see them through to completion due to sabotage by his jealous, ultra-traditionalist peers. In the end, Jorek was ousted from the Engineers' Guild and left for good. Truly, the Dwarfs are a strange lot!\\n\\nNow with the freedom and raw materials to develop any invention he chooses, I have never seen a happier Dwarf in all my life. I have little doubt that in time the potential brainchildren of this brilliant inventor will help turn the tide of our struggle here in Lustria.

The colonists speak of something strange living in the nearby jungles. They say it is not of the lizards, nor of the ratmen that infest this continent, but something else; a "ghost" they call it. Part of me thinks this gods-forsaken place drives some men to hallucinations, but today a hunting party returned with a curious tale. They had been tracking a wild Bastiladon whose carcass would have provided much sustenance for the colonists, and had trapped the great beast in a bog. They claim that as they moved in for the kill, it was unexpectedly struck down by an arrow propelled through the thick jungle canopy directly into one of its eyes.\\n\\nSuch frightening huntsmanship could only be supernatural. In this flora-covered terrain, it is almost impossible to hit a moving Bastiladon’s weak points from range as the men described. Furthermore, they claim they were then threatened by a mysterious, hooded figure in the trees above them, a sorrowful voice of a woman telling them "whosoever approaches my bounty will share its fate".\\n\\nPerhaps this is the "ghost" the colonists speak of? Whatever it is, to kill a Bastiladon in such a way requires a level of precision far exceeding that of any huntsman I’ve ever met.

I have met a few of the elusive fey folk of Athel Loren, and in my early dealings with Kalara it certainly appears she is typical of her kind. On the rare occasions in the past when my hunting expeditions unwittingly led me into the Wood Elves’ realm, I found them to be standoffish and determinedly detached from the outside world – almost aggressively so. Those familiar with the Asrai know better than to trespass upon their hunting grounds, for they are considered to be some of the most lethal hunters in the known world. We are extremely fortunate to have brought a Waystalker into our ranks, regardless of how aloof she may be.\\n\\nKalara told me that she has been in Lustria for quite some time. The beast she seeks does not prowl these lands alone though and bringing it down will take some fight, which is why she requested our assistance. For a Waystalker to admit that a quarry is beyond her talent confirms what an incredibly dangerous monster it must be. I gave her assurances that I would see this hunt through, but for now we await more information regarding the beast’s whereabouts.

Kalara has been part of the expedition for quite some time now. She seems restless to slay this beast, but knows little about its actual nature. I find it curious as to why she seeks a quarry which is largely a mystery to her… but in truth I am simply glad to have her strength added to our own, so see no need to push the question. We are mobilising now anyway, as news has reached camp that a treasure-seeking convoy of about fifty-or-so men disappeared into some nearby ruins. Kalara insisted she investigate and came back describing a grisly scene. Little was left of the mutilated men, she said, and she is convinced it is connected to the beast we are hunting.\\n\\nThough I respect Kalara greatly, I feel she has not been entirely forthcoming with us. She might not be lying about what she has seen this time, but I do believe she is withholding something about the motives for her Lustrian hunt. For this reason, I’ve decided to take the expedition and investigate this ruin myself.

I started having reservations about the true nature of the beast Kalara is pursuing, and even considered calling off this hunt – but then she revealed something quite astounding.\\n\\nIt is her sincere belief that the beast she hunts contains the reincarnated soul of her dead lover. She explained that as punishment from the one called Kurnous, the Elven God of the Hunt, Kalara’s beloved is in an endless cycle of life and death, always coming back as a murderous beast after it is slain. She has killed several versions of the beast before, and is determined to end the cycle once and for all, so her love may finally pass into the afterlife. She believes almost obsessively that Kurnous is testing her, for she always finds that the lost soul of her lover passes into a more unkillable beast than the one before it.\\n\\nTruly, the Elven gods are stranger than those of men. Out of empathy for Kalara’s loss, I have decided to continue helping her for now. We must cast our net out wide and interrogate the Dark Ones to the north as well as the lizards to the south to see what they know of this beast.

I confronted Kalara last night, hunter to hunter, urging her to give up this futile mission. To my surprise, she agreed, but implored me to help her with one final task. I accepted on the sole condition she tell me everything.\\n\\nKalara revealed she was once a princess of Wydrioth, a High Realm of Athel Loren. Her lover Atherin was a Wild Rider of Kurnous, the personal guard of Athel Loren’s king. Atherin violated his oath to sever all worldly ties, persisting in his relationship with Kalara and even revealing his order’s hallowed secrets to her. Kurnous vengefully transformed Atherin into a mighty stag before cruelly leading Kalara to unwittingly hunt it down. Discovering the stag’s true nature, Kalara eventually learned of Atherin’s cursed fate of eternal reincarnation as a beast.\\n\\nShe had also recently been visited in her dreams by the goddess Isha, mother of the Elven race and consort to Kurnous himself. A great privilege, she said, for Isha is usually forbidden to have any contact with her worldly children. The goddess offered Kalara another route to freeing her lover's soul – instead of further destruction, she must make a worldly display of love and construct a shrine directly on the banks of Itza’s fabled Emerald Pools.

It caught my attention recently to hear of a swordsman who had become army-less after miraculously escaping a slaughter at the hands of the lizard-beasts. A possible recruit? If my memory serves me correctly, he had arrived months earlier on a galleon that was flying a flag of a Bretonnian dukedom unknown to me, though I know little of the Land of Chivalry. He had disembarked with a group of men who looked vaguely Knightly in appearance, but it was unclear whether they were individuals of any important political status. Their retinue was quite poorly equipped, as were they themselves. After buying what additional weapons and supplies they could from the colonists, they foolhardily headed straight into the jungle.\\n\\nWhether out of prudence of curiosity, I had them followed and watched. Unsurprisingly, word eventually returned that the Bretonnians were ill-prepared for their foray, losing half their retinue to disease and attacks before stumbling into the mists surrounding the ancient temple-city of Xlanhuapec. Thinking it was uninhabited, they attempted to plunder the city but instead suffered a catastrophic slaughter at the hands of the Lizardmen in a painfully predictable ambush.\\n\\nThe one survivor – this swordsman – had somehow fought himself out of the trap and was still out there.

The Bretonnian noble Rodrik L’Anguille appears to be a man of great physical strength and fortitude. He must be, for he has witnessed many terrible things while on his doomed journey. He has told me stories of men being swallowed up by monstrous things lurking in the waist-deep bogs they waded through on the trek, only to be spat out again in a spray of bloody gore. And then of the slaughter at Xlanhuapec itself; how he and his men observed the temple-city to be totally uninhabited as they entered, getting all the way into the central plaza before being set upon by a swarm of twelve foot tall reptilian monsters with daggers for teeth. Though he had fought out of his skin to survive and escape, in reality many of his men had fell trying to protect him.\\n\\nRodrik clearly yearns for vengeance, but there is also a downtroddenness to his character which I think goes far deeper than just the recent loss of his men. Maybe it is the reason why he came here in the first place, which he hasn’t really talked about? Right now, Xlanhuapec is in range for a potentially successful assault which needs to be capitalised upon without delay.

After avenging the death of his men at Xlanhuapec, I have realised more and more that Rodrik still bears within him a great resentment of something deeper. The only thing he has revealed thus far is that there are those back home in his dukedom of Anguille who would sooner see him dead than allow him to return. However, I have developed too much respect for the man just to ask about what sounds like a complicated past. After all, many an ill-advised adventurer has come to seek riches in this place for one reason or another, most of whom underestimate how terrifying a place Lustria really is.\\n\\n The galleons that steadily trickle into the New World colonies constantly bring greedy fools from the Old World, who have unwisely braved the perilous crossing of the Great Ocean just for an opportunity to plunder cities they are not sure even exist. Of course, they all become lizard-feed in the end – but not Rodrik. He may very well be one of these greedy fools, but to have faced the Lizardmen and survived marks him out as a warrior we could really do with having around regardless of his past indiscretions.

To help our friend Rodrik I have ordered the expedition to march towards Pox Marsh. There, he claims, we will intercept the assassins who wish him dead before they even know what hit them. One evening, as we pitched camp for the night along the route, Rodrik pulled me away from the campfire for a private word. With a deep sadness to his tone, he revealed that Lord Tudual – the unsavoury individual who had ordered his death – is actually the duke of Anguille, Rodrik’s homeland. But even more shocking is the fact that this Duke Tudual is actually Rodrik’s father. So Rodrik is a prince of Anguille! He went on to explain that he is an 'unfavoured' heir, seen as a threat to Duke Tudual’s desired successor, Rodrik’s younger brother.\\n\\nThe reason why Rodrik came here with only a ragtag force in the first place has now become clear – Duke Tudual had sent his son to Lustria under the guise of wanting him to prove himself, but in reality was counting on him perishing. It seems the duke underestimated both Rodrik's skill as swordsman and his will to live. I have reassured Rodrik that he has nothing to fear and together we shall vanquish these would-be assassins.

What a sorry state of affairs this truly is for Prince Rodrik. We dealt with Duke Tudual’s assassins without issue, but only time will tell if this will be the last attempt to prevent his son from returning to Anguille. Rodrik himself seems uninterested in returning anyway – he tells me he has no intention of claiming power in a land he now feels no attachment to, for the jungle has become his home.\\n\\nThe last piece of Rodrik story – the reason why his father wants him dead – had eluded me until recently, simply because Rodrik had kept it secret. Now I know why, for it is a source of great shame for him. Though Rodrik was his father’s eldest son, his mother was a commoner who was Duke Tudual’s peasant concubine. Fearing he would have no other sons, the duke recognised and brought Rodrik into his household from birth, but when Rodrik’s younger brother was unexpectedly born of the duke’s lawful wife, Rodrik was foresaken.\\n\\nPrince Rodrik remains the rightful heir to the dukedom of Anguille, and as long as he lives it is feasible that Duke Tudual will attempt to remove him by sending assassins once again. As always, we must stay vigilant on his behalf.
The desert mountain Dwarfs are said to possess the banner of Jean Claude Sartre. Perhaps a trade can be arranged that might persuade them to part with it?
The desert mountain Dwarfs are said to possess the banner of Jean Claude Sartre. Diplomacy is no longer an option – we must act.
The banner of Pierre d'Arden is said to be lost to history. However, any Bretonnian subjects wish to recreate this most beautiful of banners, so let us give them a reason to do so.
