The Winds of Magic coalesce and shift along the Geomantic Web. The Old One, Potec, sends an omen. Should the Slann heed his warning then a sacred spawning is surely due.

A shipwrecked Marauder with a large raven tattooed across his chest – revealing him to be a follower of Tzeentch – is dragged before Teclis. Upon interrogation it is discovered that the Dark Lord of Change may be instigating an imminent invasion of Ulthuan! The High Loremaster must read from the Scroll of Hoeth and know the terrible truth…

Lileath’s Moon Staff was one of three sacred gifts bestowed upon the Elves by the goddess herself. Yet its power wanes, with Skaven activity around nearby Warpstone deposits dampening the staff's potency. To reawaken it, Teclis must purge the vermin from the surrounding lands.

Two of Karond Kar's greatest sons currently roam the world's oceans. One, the Beastlord Rakarth, has filled the city's infamous dungeons with all manner of monstrous horrors. The other, Lokhir Fellheart, delivers golden idols and spectacular artefacts to the city’s vaults. But Karond Kar’s truest currency is neither beasts nor priceless trinkets, but slaves.\\n\\nWere either of these two fearsome Druchii able to fill the city’s slave markets to the brim they would be well placed to make a play for the city itself and declare themselves its Drachau...

Before the might of Shang-Yang is unleashed, Zhao Ming demands a demonstration. Through a series of challenging trials, Bhashiva must prove her strength, discipline, and unwavering loyalty in displays worthy of the Iron Dragon’s attention. Only then will access be granted to the supplies, resources and personnel of the great [[col:yellow]]Armies of Shang-Yang[[/col]].\\n\\nLearn more about the Armies of Shang-Yang here.

Zhao Ming has been weighing the benefits of his expeditions to the Warpstone Desert against the strength of his enduring alliances. Rather than sift through the wastes, he wishes to undertake a reclamation of territories polluted by disorder. This would solidify his strength through that of the Tiger Warriors – and allow him to sift through the scattered impurities of the aftermath to sate his curiosity.

Zhao Ming has never considered Bhashiva's tribe mere pets or servants. He knows that should they set their sights on eradicating foulness from the world, they will not stop until they do so, fully. Therefore, he politely inquires why this still hasn't happened to this troublesome faction within the Tiger Warriors' reach. Why has not the predator torn open the prey's throat yet?

The self-styled leader of a grotesque menagerie along Cathay's borders has caught the attention of the Iron Dragon. He is careful to remind the Tiger Warriors a creature such as this should be nothing more than prey to them, whether they decide to reach into its lair or lure him into theirs.

Zhao Ming is ever keen on testing his arcane and alchemical knowledge in practice. The virulent, unruly, obstinate breeds of creatures tainted by the mortal world's growing disorder and the unspeakable Daemonic forces which are the source of it will be the object of his current test. The Tiger Warriors, his oath-sworn blade and claw will be the means of carrying it out.

While the Iron Dragon and the Tiger Warriors' immediate concerns may be different, their goal of keeping Cathay safe and their desire for challenge are always aligned. Zhao Ming has made it clear that there is an enemy in reach that can satisfy both – a foe made all the more worthy by their wickedness.

Agents of darkness and anarchy have made their abode a stone's throw away from the Tiger Warriors' tribe. Coincidentally – or not – a missive has arrived from the Iron Dragon, accompanied by a map where the reprobates' strongholds figure prominently. He does not need to spell out his intentions to make himself understood.

Despite his self-involved nature, Zhao Ming takes pride in having the Tiger Warriors at his side. Never once has he doubted their ability to claim their place as part of the Celestial Empire's bulwark against evil. Yet the walls of that bulwark must not simply endure, but expand. He has found a likely place for such an expansion.

The blight of this enemy's banners has proven persistent enough that the Iron Dragon himself has staked his pride upon seeing them torn and trampled. The verve with which he has encouraged the Tiger Warriors to destroy them once and for all is enough to ignite their own pride in turn.

Zhao Ming has began preparations for certain... scientific inquiries into a group of malevolent wretches well-known to the Tiger Warriors. The endeavour would proceed much more smoothly if their leader were to be disposed of. He trusts no one more to make this possible than the supreme hunters in the land.

The Celestial masters of Cathay brook no tolerance for the vile creatures rampaging under their sky or the Daemonic stench soiling the Winds of Magic on which they soar. Yet the Iron Dragon's earthly curiosity dictates that he crush such foes and study the pieces like a chunk of Warpstone. Yet first, they will need to be crushed. The task is well-suited to the Tiger Warriors.

The hives of Chaos-maddened depravity skulking along Cathay's borders are rarely a worthy object of study for Zhao Ming's brilliant mind. Yet he is no less devoted to Order, and it dictates they be broken nonetheless. One such target seems ripe for the Tiger Warriors' hosts.

The Tiger Warriors' legacy has been shaped by their own strength and that of the bond they share with the Iron Dragon. He knows both well, and would see them grow further. Any territories where iniquity rules should be cleansed – then Bhashiva's tribe may claim them as their own, and claim Zhao Ming's praise to boot.

Ever since the Tiger Warriors' scouts sighted a certain piece of territory, the Iron Dragon has taken a special interest in the ravages inflicted upon it by its current despots. There may be something he wants there – apart from restoring the rule of Order. He is willing to bestow a great deal of goodwill, and more, should it be cleansed.

Dragons, in their divine glory, may be above the earthly impulse to prove anything to anyone. Tigers, on the other hand, are possessed of an insatiable drive to prove their strength. Zhao Ming knows something of insatiable drive himself, and has sanctioned the Tiger Warriors' opportunity to devour this foe to the last.

Zhao Ming knows his kind remains inviolable and beyond challenge, but he also knows of forces in this world which will never stop seeking out the strongest to tear them down. One such force of evil and its leader oppose the Celestials' rule. Yet one such force of good stands united with the Dragons – and its leader's ferocious tenacity is beyond compare.

Incursions into Zhao Ming's domain are a foregone failure. Some such aggressors, however, must have particularly rankled him. For that, he has decided that anyone of their ilk must feel his wrath. He has extended that mandate to those that owe him their fealty.

A certain malevolent tribe has been vexing Zhao Ming with its continued existence. They have been disturbing shipments of valuable alchemical materials, distracting him from more important work. He would want them out of his sight, which is why he intends to turn the Tiger Warriors' attention to them and sap the miscreants' strength.

With the Tiger Warriors' boldness and tenacity at his side, the Iron Dragon has deemed that there is no more need to merely fend off the malevolence lurking beyond Cathay's borders. It is time to take the fight to them, and his allies predatory senses are best suited to the job.

With revulsion, you find Ogre settlements crudely clustered around the subtle pull of a Relic. As you stalk their perimeter, you recall teachings preserved by the elder Sawai and Clawspeakers.\\n\\nThe manifold artefacts of your people chart the history and proud heritage of the Tiger Warriors. The oldest Relics predate the exodus from Ind, including some said to be remnants of Kamau’s battle with Tzeentch fought in immemorial times to wrest your kin from his grasp. Scattered across the continent over the ages, each still bears enduring significance – to the identity of the Tiger Warriors, and to their bond with their saviour-god.\\n\\nFor generations, your people were content to let them linger. Now the portents whispered upon the Elemental Winds warn your Clawspeakers that this can no longer be so.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_relics_learn_more}}

The mere presence of the Relic emboldens your kin. There is no question that its legacy must be given purpose. But to what end?\\n\\nYour faithful Iron Claws proclaim as one that it should serve the White Tiger’s Prophecy, carrying your legend upon the wind to ever more valiant warriors. The fearsome Sawai, fanatically devoted to Kamau, give no ground and insist the Relic must be offered to Him alone. Yet the eldest Clawspeakers mutter that, in such troubled times, the Tiger Warriors must first remember the traditions of their ancestral lands, just as the Thousand Gods once welcomed Kamau into their divine court to burgeon its wealth and wisdom.\\n\\nIn this deadlock, all await your decision.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_tiger_court_learn_more}}

Your Clawspeakers leave you ill at ease, for upon the Elemental Winds they hear not only whispers of the Relics, but of wanton slaughter reigning across the land, barbaric even by the standards of the highland brutes. It is driven by an unseen hand, a prismatic spectre looming above the bloodshed.\\n\\nYour meditation is interrupted by a messenger of the Iron Dragon. Zhao Ming condemns the savages of the western wastes, now turned to butchers along the Ivory Road. Hearing his account echoed in the warnings of your Clawspeakers, you know duty and prophecy are now one.

Control over the Ivory Road is fraying. You would be among the few bold enough to speak it aloud in the heartland, but here, amidst the barrens, none can deny it.\\n\\nMore and more wasteland dwellers who once kept to their own, or could be swayed by reason and coin, now turn to ruinous pursuits. Of the Daemonic figure behind it, only broken testimonies reach you, and the name 'Vrassk' seeps from hostile lips – often in dying breaths.\\n\\nTo spare warriors for the pursuit of phantoms is unthinkable. Your Tiger Court is resolved that trade between Cathay and the West must not run dry at the Dark Gods’ whim. And so they call upon the Desert Tigress to cull disorder – for her people are loyal, steadfast, and resilient against the lure of Ruin.
It is too late – Khorne's forces have already breached the rift! Just as Kamau thwarted Tzeentch, you must destroy them!

Order, as demanded by the Iron Dragon, has been restored, but at far too great a cost. The quelling of troubles will not be the final act in the blood-soaked devastation wrought across the wasteland.\\n\\nDire news reaches you. Driven by a malign will and fed by the relentless slaughter in the region, the warp-worn wastes have been torn into a ghastly wound – a breach around which your Stalkers have scouted the prowling of multi-horned, red-skinned Daemons. It appeared without warning or reason, but there is no time for scrutiny – you must cauterise this incursion with your katara, lest the skull-hungry havoc of Khorne be unleashed upon your lands.

Bloodshed beyond measure has long since taught you that most battles are decided well before claw ever meets enemy flesh. You have grown accustomed to reading the unspoken in your warriors’ talk, catching the rhythm of the marching tread, and absorbing the temper of the camp at dusk.\\n\\nThe truth dampens your heart – though the Tiger Warriors’ resolve is mighty, it is being corroded by a manipulative enemy who weakens them for the more important struggles to come. Sunk in constant vigilance, your retinue’s armour scarcely creaks beneath guarded gestures. They brace for another night of fitful delirium, brought on by the threat of a whispered enemy.\\n\\nThe strength the Tiger Court draws from the Relics, and the righteous path they uphold, are the only things keeping your minds from slipping into a nightmarish unreality – even as that path leads you ever farther from Shang-Yang.
It is too late – Nurgle's forces have already breached the rift! Just as Kamau thwarted Tzeentch, you must destroy them!

As you bring justice to the enemies of Kamau and Cathay, terrible consequences bloom in its wake. In the civilised Cathayan hearthland, governed by harmonious custom and reverence, the bodies of the dead would have been cleansed and tended to before you could finish your prayer to Kamau. Here, among wastes torn apart by greed and cruelty, the soil is left to drink in a deeper ruin.\\n\\nToo late, troubling accounts reach you – often broken by phlegmy coughs and rasping breaths – of a place choked by bizarre, fetid vegetation, its air thick with stench and abuzz with rot-flies. It needed only the slightest tug from a manipulative hand, and the three-pocked mark was made whole. If you do not act, the Plaguelord’s pestilent influence will swell to devour the land you clawed free inch by inch.

The intrusions into your mind grow ever more insistent. But doubt is a waste of strength long since allotted to the last drop of blood and sweat. Before turning to the gathered warriors for the next strategic hunt for Relics – one that draws you farther still from Shang-Yang – you school your expression in the reflection of your blades.\\n\\nDuty decrees that only resolve be read upon the face of the White Tiger. The mounting fatigue and despair must wait for another day, another battle, perhaps even another life. Every moment lost to hesitation imperils your kind’s fate.
It is too late – Slaanesh's forces have already breached the rift! Just as Kamau thwarted Tzeentch, you must destroy them!

Though your forays into the wider world have seen you overcome much, they have also brought you greater dread. The enemy now whispered among your foes as the Skeinshaper still looms large in your mind – but you also suspect something greater and more sinister at work behind it all. How else could so many foes – Daemons and Champions alike – be drawn into battle against you, testing whether your kind truly are Grand Cathay’s finest warriors?\\n\\nThe preternatural gloom of an endless dusk falls across the land, and with it comes word of an intoxicating presence among the lengthening shadows. Shrouded in cloying fumes, a moaning, undulating throng of pincered limbs slithers forth with rapturous purpose. In its wake, an overpowering scent of perfume renders nearby creatures comatose, as the wind hums in ear-splitting harmonies that torment your kind’s keen senses. Yet another despicable breed of Chaos has come forth – and such convergence cannot be chance...

Ogre raids thunder through the Mountains of Mourn, threatening Cathay’s borders. Those who stand firm and break the brutes’ advance shall earn the keen regard of Zhao Ming.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

News reaches you of a plan by Celestial authorities to increase the deployment of the Emperor’s loyal troops across all Grand Cathay’s holdings. It is a response to recent uprisings in the heartland, prompting other Dragons to also increase their martial influence everywhere the Celestial Emperor holds sway. It is certain, however, that such increased military activity will not be conducive to your own ambitions in the region. The risk of jurisdictional squabbles with other Dragons could also risk all your progress made until now. A show of strength would be the best course of action, to let the powers of Grand Cathay know that their military needs here are met.

Taoyan, a hated name amongst the Dragons’ armies, has been sighted nearby. The one known as "the Merciless" is infamous for having taken an unspeakably ruthless approach against the rebelling Children of Yin Quai, which saw her fall foul of the imperial commanders serving alongside her. Despite fulfilling her duty, Taoyan was ultimately exiled – not only from Grand Cathay’s military ruling class, but from the central provinces entirely.\\n\\nThe trident-punctured bodies of notable enemy agents appearing of late back up your scouts’ reports that Taoyan is on intelligence-gathering operations in the region. Her reputation for getting results tells you it may be beneficial to put aside any other preconceptions of her and join forces. Thus, gathering intelligence of our own may lead us to her – or if we gather the right intelligence, lead her to us.

As word reaches you of Shang-Yang beset by Ruin, the Dark God’s design is laid terribly bare. The Relics are steeped in the power of the ancient struggle that freed your people, yet they also bear a fragment of Tzeentch’s madness – enough for his disciples to exploit through an insidious rite, and to lay the yoke of the Architect of Fate upon your kin once more. He has manipulated the forces of his Dark Brothers to bleed your strength and draw you far from your homeland. Only the vigilance of the Iron Dragon catches the conspiracy amid its making – though not in time to halt its course entirely.\\n\\nThe warhost of Vrassk the Skeinshaper now lays siege to Shang-Yang. You must make all haste to put an end to the encroaching madness, and fulfil your duty not just to the Iron Dragon, but your entire race.

Long has the White Tiger and her retinue been in service to Grand Cathay – so long in fact, that much of her personal armoury are awards and gifts bestowed by the Dragons themselves. Yet the Iron Dragon himself saves the greatest gifts for those who serve him personally, such as the ornate set of katara of his renowned collection, known as the Blades of Shang-Yang. They eternally burn – seemingly without source – with power granted by the Iron Dragon’s strange alchemy. The flames’ ferocity is mirrored in the nature of the Tiger Warriors, but it will not be granted to their great leader until that ferocity is proven once more against those seeking to provoke disharmony across the land.

Spurred on by incursions of darker and more terrible forces, the Ogres along the Ivory Road circle Cathayan merchants like vultures, striking openly at outposts they would have never dared approach in more peaceful and orderly times. But their gall is matched only by their stupidity. Their latest outrage – the slaughter of a crucial strongpoint along the trade route, manned by the noble Tiger Warriors – will be their last.\\n\\nWith many of your loyal kin butchered and a Cathayan retinue carried off to a gruesome fate, Zhao Ming urges you to make haste. Secure the stronghold, rescue whomever you can, and bring down the full wrath of Shang-Yang upon these raiders – let them learn that the White Tiger is not to be trifled with.

It is one thing to earn the Dark Prince's favour. It is another entirely to be ready to receive the alluring rewards of His gratitude in return. Open yourself up to His blessings, and indulge in the ecstasy of His gifts.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

Research, research, research! What experiments might pave the way to new diseases? What technologies might be used to expand your capacity for decay? These are questions you must answer, should you wish to receive the full extent of Grandfather Nurgle's deadly maladies!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

The gifts of the Blood God's favour are limited only by your capacity to receive them. Rid yourself of all but your wrath, and make room for every one of Khorne's blood-soaked blessings!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

An open mind is needed to better receive Tzeentch's endless knowledge. You must expand your capacity for understanding, in order to truly appreciate the Raven God's gifts.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

The north has long been bound to Chaos, and with much of its land under your thumb, it could finally become a true base of power. Build a Dark Fortress amidst the profane energies of Chaos here, as a symbol of your domination.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_dark_fortress}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_dark_fortress_learn_more}}

Your army must thrive upon indulgence, and sweep the world up in the decadent delights of Slaanesh. Only then will the Dark Prince's supremacy be seen by all, a testament to his worldly dominion!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_dark_authority}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_dark_authority_learn_more}}

It is time to concoct an unmatched tribute to the Lord of Pestilence. Spread your infections throughout your whole host, and unleash them as a walking plague upon the land!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_dark_authority}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_dark_authority_learn_more}}

All must bow before the Blood God's throne, built atop the skulls of His enemies. Assemble a savage army of his most fervent warriors, who worship in war and bear the burning mark of His fury!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_dark_authority}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_dark_authority_learn_more}}

By magic and blade, your army will change the fate of the world. Gather your followers by the thousand; each new servant of Tzeentch you acquire can only bolster the Wind-Lord's power!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_dark_authority}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_dark_authority_learn_more}}

These wandering morsels fight for Chaos, but do not yet know the tantalising depths of its pleasures. Tempt them into submission, and prove once again that service to the Perfect Prince is most deliciously rewarded.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

It seems there are patients in need of a doctor to cure them of their fickle indecision. Perhaps an experiment is in order, to display the power of pestilence, and usher these peons into Grandfather Nurgle's rotten embrace?\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Only the most brutal warriors are worthy of bearing the Mark of Khorne. Bestow the honour upon the chosen, and let every drop of blood they spill pay homage to the Blood God!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Every pitiful, twisted soul pleads for the blessings of change. Have them pledge their worthless lives to the Changer, and alter their fates forever!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Some of the Heroes and Lords under your command have yet to succumb to the salacious delights Slaanesh offers. Persuade one such servant of the delicious power that awaits, once they pledge themselves to the Prince of Pleasure…\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_path_to_glory}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_path_to_glory_learn_more}}

Disease and decay must be spread wherever the opportunity arises. The most powerful servants of Chaos will surely vomit with glee, once infected by Nurgle's almighty pestilence!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_path_to_glory}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_path_to_glory_learn_more}}

To be deemed worthy by the Sword-Maiden of the Blood God is an honour any Lord or Hero under your command would surely kill for. Choose only the mightiest of warriors, and let them burn with furious rage as they bear the Mark of Khorne!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_path_to_glory}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_path_to_glory_learn_more}}

Every agent of Chaos ought to serve under Tzeentch's feathered wing. Open the mind of a Lord or Hero under your sway, and let the dark knowledge of the Great Conspirator fill them to the brim and fortify their power!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_path_to_glory}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_path_to_glory_learn_more}}

Slaanesh offers a most enticing exchange; sacrifice the souls of your victims to sate his voracious appetite, and indulge in decadent reward!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

The Plague Lord awaits the souls of the dead and decaying corpses that litter the world in your wake. Send them his way, and receive his noxious gifts in exchange.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

Souls of the weak and unworthy deserve naught but to be devoured by the Lord of Murder. Sacrifice them in his honour, and claim the rewards of the Blood God's favour!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

Every soul signifies a life that could have been, where fate fluxes around every path not taken. Send them to Tzeentch, and as the Raven God is empowered, so will his faithful servants be also.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_chaos_gifts}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_chaos_gifts_learn_more}}

As your devious influence spreads, your power grows all the more potent. Lavish it upon your willing servants, so that they may better serve Slaanesh!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

With just the right batch of toxic ingredients, what once was ordinary may become a decaying testament to the Plague Lord! The servants of Nurgle under your command are but one experiment away from fulfilling their pestilent potential.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Victory after victory, your warriors prove their worth. Drenched in the blood of their fallen foes, they may rise up under your guidance, stronger than ever before!\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Change is inevitable, like an oncoming tide sweeping all into its churning waves. For their every victory, the soldiers under your command ought to be swept along in its current, and emerge transformed by Tzeentch's power.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_warbands}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_warbands_learn_more}}

Norscan tribes bow before you, awaiting their chance to sow Ruin in your stead. Give these savage warriors a target, and watch them descend like rabid wolves in your name.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_war_coordination_add_01}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_war_coordination_learn_more}}

In an effort to garner the favour of the Dark Prince, the Druchii Hag Sorceress Morathi has put into motion a most heinous plan. A tribute of Elven souls, both Asur and Asrai, is to be offered up by the Cult of Excess as tribute to Slaanesh. With artful manipulation she fabricated a diplomatic gathering between her hated cousins as a means to facilitate the sacrifice. Trapping them and summoning a rift at their meeting place, she successfully transported them to Slaanesh's realm, where they remain trapped, helpless to the whims of whatever finds them. Yet sending them there was only half the plan; one will be needed to strike the killing blow to complete the sacrifice – one who can travel to the Realm of Slaanesh with His blessing…

It is not without reason that they say Doctor Festus’ curative powers are greater than any other who walks the world. Not that he has any interest in healing others – since being gifted intimate knowledge of disease by Father Nurgle he has been consumed by an insatiable and ruthless desire to experiment, a sliver of the Plaguelord’s boundless delight in perpetuating the cycle of life and death. Thus Festus forever seeks exotic ingredients to brew his noxious potions, frequently foraying into the Realm of Nurgle via fluctuating portals known only to him, in the hopes of harvesting something delectably vomit-inducing. He is due such an expedition, though this time he might be pleasantly surprised at what awaits him beyond the veil…
The weak and helpless hordes that plague these lands hide behind walls they hope will save them. Destroy this fickle illusion, and raze their cities to the ground!

Every battle is a chance for glory, and every victory a sign of the Blood God's inescapable dominance. Sweep down upon the battlefield with blazing rage in your heart, to vanquish the enemies of Khorne and anoint yourself with their blood!

Far from the cold ravages of the northern steppes, an insignificant Orc Warboss named Muga had taken his crew into the Underway to “find sum stunties ta bash”, but instead stumbled straight into a Skaven hideout. In a self-preserving panic, the ratman mystic leading the nest tore open the fabric between worlds in a haphazard attempt to summon a Bloodthirster into his ranks. Perhaps Khorne had momentarily turned his gaze and seen an opportunity? It is more likely, however, that the Seer had simply lost control of his rift, for in an instant the Orc Warboss, his crew, and the entire Skaven host were sucked into the Realm of Khorne where they now await their fate. Once again, the Blood God shall lavish his consort with the greatest gift of all – war!

Most remain blind to the conniving machinations of Tzeentch until their tragic fate is already sealed. Thus, as the unsuspecting nations of the Empire and Cathay seek to manifest a portal between their lands, avoiding the dangers of the Ivory Road, they remain oblivious to the true architect of their plans—the Great Schemer himself. As construction on the portal was completed, the forces of each nation were drawn through the gateway, and pulled into a twisted and unfamiliar Daemonic landscape. Yet there are many powerful pawns in the God of Magic's schemes, for an urgent summons demands Vilitch's presence in the Realm of Tzeentch. Though the twisted plots of his God remain a mystery, the part Vilitch is to play will no doubt soon become startlingly clear.

At last, the blasted plateau of K’datha reveals its ancient secret. A hidden corner where sits the twisted ruins of Zanbaijin, a place older than the race of men, obscured from the mortal plane by the veil between worlds. With the sigils learnt and invoked, a passage to the city’s cursed arena has opened. Where over the centuries, numberless would-be champions have come with their followers to go to battle with their rivals and prove themselves to their patrons. Yet here, not even the laughing Gods could claim the souls of the fallen, for the ancient Altar of Battle has always taken them as its own prize. Until now.\\n\\nThe Altar’s bounty lays bare. The next champion of the Fallen City shall be its last, the claimant to tribute that will change the course of history. A Chaos God is about to rise – make the journey to Zanbaijin and ensure that it is yours!

These Greenskins block your advance, acting as a filthy, green barrier between you and your kin. Show no mercy and push on through!

Under the disgusted gaze of the Ancestor Gods, the armies of Undeath spread their wicked curse. Long have their transgressions been recorded in the Dammaz Kron, since the days of Neferata and her reign of evil. Now three throngs of our brave warriors have fallen to the blood-drinkers. Make an offering to Grimnir, and even the score against these vile creatures!

Ancient tales recited around Asrai campfires speak of the mysterious Tree Spirits of the Far East, powerful beings thought to be associated with Adanhu, eldest of Elders, but far removed from the Old World’s forests. For reasons forgotten in time, some of Athel Loren’s most ancient denizens left the great forest long ago to journey to the previously unexplored extremes of the life-giving Worldroots. Beyond the distant mountains to the east, in the lush jungles of southern Cathay, these spirits made their unlikely home. Yet today they are reduced to a small enclave beset on all sides by mischievous locals – the local Monkey people loyal to the Dragon Emperor. A show of force against the Cathayans will make it much easier to facilitate a reunion with these venerable beings, whose knowledge and power over the local fauna could make them very useful allies.

[[i]]An endless array of armour and weapons must stream forth to provide the dark devices and works of occult engineering that arm the mighty hosts of the Dawi-Zharr. It is Hashut’s will![[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_4_chd_economy}}\\n\\nLearn more about Armaments [[url:script_link_campaign_chd_economy]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]When it comes to lucrative commodities traded over vast distances, an unprotected consignment is an attack waiting to happen. No chances can be taken for your most important goods – an armed convoy will be necessary.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_military_convoys}}\\n\\nLearn more about Military Convoys [[url:script_link_campaign_military_convoys]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]All life other than that of the Dawi-Zharr only has value as a resource – a commodity of muscle and sinew to be amassed, exploited and spent. Even now, the need for fresh Labour increases with time, the vast industries of your isolated empire ever hungering for more.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_labour}}\\n\\nLearn more about Labour [[url:script_link_campaign_labour]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]The greater works of the Hell-Forge, where the designs of your Daemonsmiths’ dark intellects spawn, is the bedrock upon which your power is founded. Establish your assembly lines of hellfire and blood![[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_hellforge}}\\n\\nLearn more about the Hell-Forge [[url:script_link_campaign_hellforge]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]The ringing of hammers echoes from your diabolic workshops, of Raw Materials being forged with arcane techniques to produce steelcraft of a quality that outmatches all other races’ craftsmanship. Ensure production meets demand.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_5_chd_economy}}\\n\\nLearn more about Armaments [[url:script_link_campaign_chd_economy]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]The desolation of a thousand years of Labour already fills your corner of the Dark Lands where industry tears at the earth, pock-marking the surface with the scars of enterprise. Continue these endeavours and reap the rewards![[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_chd_economy}}\\n\\nLearn more about Raw Materials [[url:script_link_campaign_chd_economy]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]The plundered riches of the earth must find their way onto your stockpiles, so to this end you must drill, dig and delve deep into the rock and filth in pursuit of the treasures that lie below. No landscape shall be spared![[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_chd_economy}}\\n\\nLearn more about Raw Materials [[url:script_link_campaign_chd_economy]]here[[/url]].

[[i]]The Tower of Zharr is a hustle and bustle of workshops, forges, Labourers and warriors, and where the powerful meet to exert their influence over them. To hold sway over its ancient districts is a path to power in itself, both for you and all Dawi-Zharr.[[/i]]\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_tower_of_zharr}}\\n\\nLearn more about the Tower of Zharr [[url:script_link_campaign_tower_of_zharr]]here[[/url]].

The Empire’s enemies, both mortal and otherwise, have long sought to topple what Sigmar built. Foes who step foot upon Imperial soil find themselves vanquished by the fury of their steel and gunpowder soon enough. Nonetheless, the safety of the populace can never be ignored.\\n\\nThere have been reports of mutilated bodies appearing across the Sylvanian countryside; a grave threat that serves as a timely reminder that we must secure our homeland.

The reports were not exaggerated – bodies abound were discovered clawed, savaged and feasted upon by some unholy creature. A peasant comes forth speaking of a near-deadly encounter with a seemingly feral Vampire, before the intervention of an aristocrat known as Countess Gabriella prevented him from becoming the creature’s victim. Curiously, the Countess addressed the Vampire as “Ulrika”. If this is the same individual that Karl Franz once recalled saving his life from a would-be assassin, then further investigation is required.\\n\\nThe peasant believes the Countess and Ulrika have retreated to Nachthafen Castle. Entering the citadel will require you to masquerade as nobility, best achieved with the help of a gold-laden treasure vault.

The Ancestor God Gazul wielded the power of the elementals; his relics hold the key to the devastating forces of the Underearth. Desirous Undead covens pilfer far and wide to gain even an iota of that power – within their boundaries is where Gazul's relics might be found.

The Ancestor God Grimnir long ago ventured north into the Chaos Wastes. That fool was lost, alone and out of his depth, dropping trinkets as he passed through the Cliffs of Death. We must search for them amongst the foetid crags and mountain passes!

The Ancestor God Morgrim was the first Dwarf Engineer, whose tool relics have been held in stewardship by paragons of his cult throughout the ages. This is a chance to steal one such relic and use it to show them first hand that Dhrath-Zharr engineering is far superior to their sorcery-less tinkering.

There are few more far-fetched tales of the Dawi weaklings than that of the exiled Ancestor Skavor, son of Gazul, who it is told moulded his flesh and became an enemy of his own people. One artefact associated with him, said to contain as much potential as the other Ancestor God relics, is being used as a ceremonial trinket by a wayward horde of Lustria.

The Ancestor God Smednir, patron of metalworking and ore refinement, is perhaps the least worthless of the weak western deities. Yet just as with the others, the fate of his relic is yours to decide. One of his creations sits as an heirloom in the treasure hall of the Dwarfs’ northernmost Hold.

The Ancestor God Thungni left the secret of Rune Magic to the Dwarf race. Only he and a few of his undeserving descendants could wield the great power he discovered, which can be tapped into using the Runic Tablet stored in Karak Azorn’s treasure hall.

The Ancestor God Valaya’s powers may have prevented Dwarfkind’s annihilation at the hands of Chaos, but it cannot prevent her secrets from being exploited for our ends! A long-lost vial of potent salve said to be brewed by Valaya’s own hand sits unassumingly in the loot pile of a nearby Ogre troop.

The Great Drill of Hashut needs to be primed before operation can commence. Gathering and desecrating the Artefacts of the traitorous Ancestor Gods will grant the Great Drill enough power to descend into the depths and bore through the mantles of rock into Hashut's domain.\\n\\nOnce the relics are found, however, temptation and hubris must first be overcome. Personal fame, reverence and sorcerous might are things not so easily passed up by the Dhrath-Zharr.

How fitting that the Dwari-Thagi march themselves to their own sacrifice to the Father, in turn bringing you one step closer to the revelation and desecration of the relics they hold so dear!

The will of Hashut is at times clear, other times inscrutable. He sees into the souls of mortals and can distinguish the malign from the innocent, though in his eyes all are destined for hell-bound torment. And now the Daemonspite Crucible, Drazhoath’s favoured talisman, must be reforged and quenched with more innocent souls to renew its power. Yet Hashut does not reveal his judgement of those he cuts down – enemies must be killed in scores to eventually satisfy the Father of Darkness.

The Uzkular – the Undead – roam the deltas of the River Ruin. No doubt due to the magical effluent being carried downstream and mixing with the countless bodies that litter the muddy and caustic river mouth where it meets the Sea of Storms. The Ashen usually pays no heed to such meagre inconveniences, but recent attacks on his labourers are now posing a real threat to the supply lines. A direct military response is now imperative!
Ancient runes inscribed upon Graven Sceptre’s iron shaft glow red with the rage of Hashut – a sign that the Great Bull yearns for the Ashen One to spread the torment of war throughout the land!

Ancient runes inscribed upon Graven Sceptre’s iron shaft glow red with the rage of Hashut – a sign that the Great Bull demands the Ashen One spread the torment of war throughout the land!

The Empire’s enemies, both mortal and otherwise, have long sought to topple what Sigmar built. Foes who step foot upon Imperial soil find themselves vanquished by the fury of their steel and gunpowder soon enough. Nonetheless, the safety of the populace can never be ignored.\\n\\nThere have been reports of mutilated bodies appearing across the Sylvanian countryside; a grave threat that serves as a timely reminder that we must secure our homeland.

The reports were not exaggerated – bodies abound were discovered clawed, savaged and feasted upon by some unholy creature. A peasant comes forth speaking of a near-deadly encounter with a seemingly feral Vampire, before the intervention of an aristocrat known as Countess Gabriella prevented him from becoming the creature’s victim. Curiously, the Countess addressed the Vampire as “Ulrika”. If this is the same individual that Karl Franz once recalled saving his life from a would-be assassin, then further investigation is required.\\n\\nThe peasant believes the Countess and Ulrika have retreated to Nachthafen Castle. Entering the citadel will require you to masquerade as nobility, best achieved with the help of a gold-laden treasure vault.

The Motherland’s enemies, both mortal and otherwise, have long sought to claim her. Foes who step foot upon the frozen tundra find themselves entombed in her icy grasp soon enough. Nonetheless, the safety of the populace can never be ignored.\\n\\nThere have been reports of mutilated bodies appearing across the Sylvanian countryside; a grave threat that serves as a timely reminder for us to secure our homeland.

The reports were not exaggerated – bodies abound were discovered clawed, savaged and feasted upon by some unholy creature. A peasant is encountered who speaks of a near-deadly encounter with a naked, feral Vampire, before the intervention of an aristocrat known as Countess Gabriella prevented him from becoming the creature’s victim. Curiously, the Countess addressed the naked Vampire as “Ulrika”. If this is Ulrika Straghov, missing daughter of the deceased Ivan Straghov, who had warned Tzarina Katarin of the impending Chaos invasion, then further investigation is required. \\n\\nThe peasant believes the Countess and Ulrika have retreated to Nachthafen Castle. Entering the citadel will require you to masquerade as nobility, best achieved with the help of a gold-laden treasure vault.

While Astragoth remains the most powerful of the Conclave of Sorcerers – who rule Zharr-Naggrund in Hashut’s name – he is not immune to its machinations. Thus, it is Astragoth’s legion that has been charged with guarding and ensuring the safety of a precious Convoy train. Should the convoy be lost then the ageing Astragoth could suffer an irreversible loss in status amongst his peers. Protecting it shall be no small feat – the Convoy must travel on one of the most perilous routes through the Dark Lands.

Zhatan’s master, Ghorth the Cruel, keeps his brutal commander busy by having him satisfy Zharr-Naggrund’s insatiable demand for fresh Labourers. To help wield his military power effectively, Ghorth regularly arms Zhatan with equipment from his own arcane armoury. Such murderous toys do not always come without strings, however, and Ghorth does not hesitate to continually challenge Zhatan to prove himself. Thus his latest order is for Zhatan to spread the Warhost of Zharr’s authority by annexing more lands, in turn further feeding Zharr-Naggrund’s ruthless industrial machine. In return, Zhatan will receive a piece of armour that belonged to one of the greatest Chaos Dwarf warriors to have ever led the hosts of the Dawi-Zharr.

Workers at a vital refinery have rebelled against their overseers – spilling a lake’s worth of valuable tar. That such an incident should happen in the shadow of Zharr-Naggrund is an outrage. The Conclave of Sorcerers has called upon Zhatan the Black to restore order, make an example of the rebels, and deal with the incompetents that were meant to be supervising the site. Mercy is for the weak.

Ghorth the Cruel has decided to bestow upon his commander Zhatan another piece of powerful weaponry: the shield-splitting Obsidian Axe. As is often the case, the weapon’s assignment does not come without conditions and Ghorth has kept the axe’s power dampened, for now. In issuing an impotent weapon of such great potential, the eminent Sorcerer Lord is not merely living up to his epithet – this is another challenge unto his loyal servant. Until Ghorth bears witness to enough of the Chaos Dwarfs’ enemies falling before the Commander of Zharr, the axe’s strength will stay dormant.

The energies of Shyish wax and wane amid tides of blood and carnage. On corpse-ridden battlefields, where death lingers like a fog, the Purple Winds of Magic blow a gale, offering untold power to all who dabble in its mysteries. Cut a violent path through the enemies of the Empire and embrace the arcane strands of magic it unleashes; one day soon they may be forged into deadly focus, and wielded like a weapon towards your foes.

A recent uprising of Orc and Goblin Labourers almost spilled over into full-blown rebellion, if not for the conniving actions of one of your Hobgoblin middle-managers. Your informants tell you that the Hobgoblin had initially joined the rebellion, before working his way into the inner circle of the rabble-rousers and promptly plunging his knife into every one of their backs.\\n\\nOf two things there is little doubt: first, that the Hobgoblin's actions were not made as an act of loyalty to you, and secondly that potential catastrophe to the supply lines had been averted by his backstabbing nature. Yet some damage had still been done, with the leaderless droves of escaped Orcs and Goblin Labourers now scattered to join nearby Warbosses. March out to claim back the losses from your workforce and perhaps find this Hobgoblin to put him in a more useful post.

The Stone Mantle, one of Astragoth’s most powerful talismans, has become weakened and damaged with age. Few know how truly old the artefact is, however, but it has the appearance of a hardy cloak. No mere tailor can ever hope to repair it – only the arcane techniques of the Dark Lands’ Daemonsmithies can restore its ancient power.

Protecting it shall be no small feat – the Convoy must travel on one of the most perilous routes through the Dark Lands.

Kislev once kept constant vigilant surveillance over the Road of Skulls, but now Khorne’s beasts overrun the old outpost settlements. The spirits of home beseech you to purge the Daemons and restore Kislev’s eyes in the north!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

Since the outposts were lost centuries ago, the Road of Skulls has been an area shunned by the Tzars, allowing the creatures of Chaos its use for passage to Kislev. But no longer! The Daughters of the Forest listen to the spirits of home, who demand this Daemonic thoroughfare be stemmed.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The Khornate-Daemons’ lust for murder will drive them towards you eventually, but the sooner the Daemons are felled, the sooner you can potentially exploit the magic that permeates their very flesh and bone.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

The mindless Savage Orcs continue to encroach upon Cathayan lands, spreading their filth and terrorising the people under your protection. The Kingdom of the Dragon must be cleansed of this violent scourge, once and for all!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

The vile Greenskin threat grows ever more menacing, as the so-called Skull-takerz rampage across the land. These creatures are a disease upon all they encounter, an infection that must be rooted out and eliminated without mercy!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

The forests of Naggaroth are rife with ambient magics, calling out to those who would harness their dark power. Controlled by the enemies of Kislev, such arcane might remains a monumental threat to the children of Ursun. Conquest is the only answer; claim this land and utilise its magic in the name of the Motherland.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

The reach of the Motherland is ever expanding, proving the enemies of the Ice Queen have nowhere to hide. The Dark Elves may fortify their lands and pray to their dark gods – it does nothing to stop whole swathes of their land being swallowed by Kislev's might.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The cruelty of the Dark Elves continues to threaten the people of Kislev, with their forays from the Land of Chill growing in both frequency and savagery. It is time to give them something to fear on home soil. Make their armies bleed, until tales of your sorcery take root in their nightmares.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

By blood, blade and magic, a foothold must be established in the land of Lustria. Gaining a solid base of control will lay the foundations for expansion – in such a dangerous land, it is the only way for the expedition to succeed.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

The expedition has ground to a halt in the wake of the Savage Orcs' meddling. Such base creatures cannot be allowed to impede the business of the Dragons. Rid the land of this menace; only then may the expedition into Lustria progress.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Every wisp of Spirit Essence invokes a heady rush of power. With enough of its potent energy coarsing through your veins, the Hexes you uncover could be yours to command.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_3_hexes}}\\n\\nLearn more about Hexes [[url:script_link_campaign_hexes]]here[[/url]].

The tendrils of corruption have taken root deep within the land, befouling the very soil. Such evil must be eradicated if the natural order is ever to be restored; enact the [[i]]Purification Chant[[/i]], only then can we begin to cleanse the land of the scourge of Chaos.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_hexes}}\\n\\nLearn more about Hexes [[url:script_link_campaign_hexes]]here[[/url]].

The most potent spells are often created deep within the woods, amidst the whispers of strange incantations and the combination of unusual arcane artefacts. Each experiment brings new magic to life with which to guard the realms of nature.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_witchs_hut}}\\n\\nLearn more about the Witch's Hut [[url:script_link_campaign_witchs_hut]]here[[/url]].

The proud fools of the Empire constantly insert themselves into the Great Conspirator's schemes, seeking to restore order where there should be Chaos. Eliminate this imperial annoyance; they will interfere in Tzeentch's schemes no longer!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

The greatest deceptions will require you to be everywhere and nowhere all at once. Every foothold gained – whether by battle or infiltration – is a place to seed your schemes and expand the Trickster Cults.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_1_trickster_cults}}\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_dlc24_narrative_addendum_trickster_cults}}

It is always amusing when fools believe their defences will keep them safe – especially when your cultists have already taken root within their walls!\\n\\nWith a [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Trickster Cultist selected, right-click the desired target to show a range of Trickster Cult options.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_dlc24_narrative_addendum_trickster_cults}}

It is not enough to simply occupy small pockets of land, surrounded by foreign powers. Dragons are no meek creatures, after all; they strive only towards total dominance.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

A certain magic lies beneath the dull protocols of bureaucracy, entwining itself with the daily ongoings of administration. Only when every decision is in perfect synchronicity with the Winds of Magic, can the Celestial Empire truly thrive.\\n\\nLearn more about Matters of State [[url:script_link_campaign_matters_of_state]]here[[/url]].

The final ritual is at hand! Flexing the bounds of the Great Compass, its power shall soon be extended, growing more attuned to the Elemental Winds than ever before. The benefits to Cathay shall be endless! However, as expected, the Lizardmen protest in outrage, declaring that such rites fly in the face of the Old Ones and their Great Plan. Their meddling is assured, but a Dragon does not bow before mere reptiles. As the Cold Ones rally to arms, the Celestial Empire shall stand defiant. Put an end to their foolish intrusion – nothing must interfere with the rituals completion!

Fyodora Ungol and her sisters have reached out with a twisted tale, sharing stories of a dangerously powerful witch and a Hex capable of bewitching weak mortal minds. They are willing to share the location of this mysterious Hex-wielder, yet their feigned fear and enthusiastic help is undoubtedly suspicious. It would seem an ambush may lie in wait, yet this may be one trap worth walking into willingly. If these sisters possess the Hex they described, then its knowledge must be snatched from their skulls, through a gaping head wound if necessary!

Something burrows deep beneath the earth, reeking of sinister corruption – an Underway perhaps, infested with filthy vermin. Whatever the cause, its rot has withered the land, with every ounce of its power emanating from a single point of infection. Such power could be used in the creation of a new Hex – one that could entrap such vile trespassers before they ever have chance to plant their virulent seeds of corruption. Seek out the source of this cancerous blight – the essence of whatever lies at the heart of this scourge must be harvested!

Teeming with mystical energy, the Magical Forests scattered across the land are a ripe source of Spirit Essence, promising untold power to any who might channel it. With Dark Magic, gateways may be opened to each forest, providing an endless fount of spiritual energy.\\n\\nThe Wood Elves however, prove a constant thorn in the side. Seeing such things as a threat to the sanctity of their land, they defend the Magical Forests against all intruders, barring entry to any who would seek to channel their essence. Dealing with these misguided miscreants will prove a challenge, yet with the aid of the malevolent spirits of the forest, the ancient power of these woodlands may yet be within reach.

Never before has the world seen such a collection of Forbidden Hexes, each a powerful maelstrom of Dark Magic in their own right. Combined into the Malediction of Ruin, they have the power to potentially erase all wickedness befouling the land, bringing the forces of corruption to calamity. With a target chosen and the ritual set in motion, all manner of dark forces descend, seeking to interfere out of desperation to avoid their inevitable doom. Hold the forces of evil back; once the ritual is complete, the land shall be cleansed of their filth forevermore.

Where the dead roam, their spirits also wander, practically begging for someone to make use of their wretched souls. Enthralled by Dark Magic, a broken spirit may be called forth as but one part of a deathly army of spectres, intent on haunting their summoner's foes. Yet first, their mouldering corpses must be dealt with. The rotten Undead still walk the earth, guarding the spirits yet to be set free. Send them to their second deaths, for only then can their spirits be bound to an afterlife of endless service.

Once a gift from the Dragon Emperor, the Storm Wind Coronal has since been lost with the fall of the Snake Gate, lying cruelly just out of reach. With the Great Bastion compromised, all of Grand Cathay stands vulnerable; only once the Snake Gate has been reclaimed can the strength of the Celestial Empire be restored. Through conquest and occupation, the enchanted Coronal may finally be returned to its rightful owner, ready to take its place upon the Storm Dragon's brow once more.

In recent months, crop failures, illnesses and pestilential plagues have befallen the farmlands of Grand Cathay. Whilst seemingly isolated instances to the casual observer, Yuan Bo discerns deeper than most. The machinations of the Ruinous Powers are at play within the realm, seeking to undermine and destabilise the smooth running of the provinces. At the Jade Dragon’s word, his agents have closely investigated each suspect instance, and after a time, found profane markings, runes and glyphs at the sites of all of these disasters. If left unchecked, these will merely be the start of an epidemic that ravages the rural heart of Grand Cathay.

Bearing magic attuned to the Iron Winds, the Horns of Shang-Yang are as powerful as they are rare. When the city of their namesake was wrested from its rightful ruler, the Horns too were lost. Such power cannot be allowed to reside in the wrong hands and nor can the proud city of Shang-Yang be allowed to crumble under the mismanagement of unworthy occupiers. It is time to retake the city; those sitting within its walls will soon learn that the Iron Dragon's vengeance is a force to be truly feared.

Mother Ostankya’s eyes glaze over as she is suddenly overcome by a torrent of whispers from the spirits of the land. In hallucination, she scries a cave somewhere in the distant mountains where deep within sits a cavern of rare ice crystals, a place thrumming with the ancient magic of the land concentrated in dozens of glimmering stalagmites and stalactites. A single shard of one of these formations could be a powerful centrepiece for Ostankya’s crown, augmenting her influence over the spirits who facilitate her frightening spells. Yet as she drifts out of her vision, she also makes out a cacophony of monstrous roars, shrieks and howls... Something feral awaits!

The Changeling always has his multitudinous fingers in many pies, and one scheme put into motion many days prior is now coming to delightful fruition. The Trickster’s Staff, an ancient Tzeentchian artefact of little importance to the Old Worlders other than being worth a great deal of gold, sits securely in the vault of Dwarf merchants at Karak Azgaraz. By the Changeling’s machinations it had previously been in the possession of Empire merchants, only for him to promptly steal it back from them and plant it into the Dwarfs’ possession. With his deceitful whispers, the Empire merchants have been led to believe that the Dwarfs stole ‘their’ priceless artefact, and they now prepare to march on Azgaraz where bloodshed will surely ensue. The Changeling, of course, will take his customary front-row seat…

From an unknown vantage point, a legendary colossus gazes over the eastern empire, paying close attention to the Dragons’ trials and tribulations. It is said that whenever war is waged righteously in the Celestial's eyes, the one known as the Heavenly Bowman leaps across the very mountains to aid those who display adeptness in marksmanship on the field of battle. Thus, those who fight skilfully for the greater good of Grand Cathay need not wait long to meet the greatest of her towering sentinels…

Grand Cathay’s ancient Constructs are a source of its great strength. The lifeforces imbued within previously-inanimate sculptures, now brought to life, play a crucial role in the Dragon armies’ martial prowess. Every last molecule in such entities is magically connected, both inside and out – the bond between all Lions and Sentinels of stone, jade and jet inexorable and far-reaching. With more of such combatants in your forces, the most powerful of their kin shall also be roused.

Word has spread of a noble’s son, a once-great Knight of the Empire, who roams the Chaos Wastes in search of a greater purpose. Most remarkably he bears the insignia of a Tzeentchian cult, the Brethren of the Golden Eagle. His loyalties had him pursued doggedly for a time by the Templars of Sigmar, the Empire’s Witch Hunters, but once they caught up he proved his status as the greatest swordsman in his Knightly Order. Perhaps in time this Champion-in-the-making will make his way to us, but in the meantime we must ensure there are more like-minded warriors to help him embrace Chaos.

The noble breath of the wandering Knight is carried as a whisper upon the Winds, speaking of a tall monolith he has encountered deep in the Chaos Wastes that holds history, magic and prophecy. Yet standing between the Knight and the answers leading him to Chaos’ embrace is a bloodthirsty Doombull and his warherd! If this warrior is ever to reach his full potential in Tzeentch’s estimations we must provide him with the assistance he might require to reach the revelations he seeks.

Having reached the ancient monolith deep in the Wastes, the great Knight stands on the cusp of learning the truth and completing the path seemingly laid before him – but for one final insurmountable trial. In one-to-one combat the warrior is more than a match for the monolith’s Doombull guardian, but the sheer numbers in the beast’s warherd makes the Knight's survival nigh on impossible. Tzeentch’s plans may be unknowable, yet your gaze has been drawn to this Champion deliberately. It is time to play your part.

The Golden Knight is Kislev’s living symbol of unification between church and state: the greatest living warrior in Kislevite soldiery, whose sacred duty is to ensure the peace and sanctity of Kislev’s lands, regardless of politics or bureaucracy. The current incumbent would be a powerful ally indeed, the daughter of a notable fallen companion of Boris Ursus himself and a warrior of grim determination: Naryska Leysa, who takes notice of those who display martial supremacy in the Motherland’s eternal fight.

Roused by your military successes, the Golden Knight rides forth to protect your realm! Before she can take to the field with you, it must be sanctioned by official decree. To establish the Ice Court's jurisdiction, her service must be overseen by a Royal Barracks.

Once a gift from the Dragon Emperor, the Storm Wind Coronal has since been lost with the fall of the Snake Gate, lying cruelly just out of reach. With the Great Bastion compromised, all of Grand Cathay stands vulnerable; only once the Snake Gate has been reclaimed can the strength of the Celestial Empire be restored. Through conquest and occupation, the enchanted Coronal may finally be returned to its rightful owner, ready to take its place upon the Storm Dragon's brow once more.

For too long have the enemies of Cathay wielded dark magics against the Dragon Emperor and his kin, hoping to bring the Celestial Empire to its knees. Arcane incursions begin to run rampant, as the kingdom's foes grow ever bolder.\\n\\nThough there are artefacts suited to stand against such a threat, imbued with the dark energies of Yin, one must first prove worthy of bearing such power. It seems the path to becoming a worthy defender of the people must first be carved out with countless victories.

Shining jewels of brilliant jade are said to lie hidden throughout this land, looted by enemy powers too foolish to know their worth. According to ancient rumour, such gems are teeming with mystic energy, granting boundless sight to any who should possess them. Armour adorned with such jewels would be a powerful boon indeed – one need only wrench the shining stones from the hands of the unworthy.

In recent months, crop failures, illnesses and pestilential plagues have befallen the farmlands of Grand Cathay. Whilst seemingly isolated instances to the casual observer, Yuan Bo discerns deeper than most. The machinations of the Ruinous Powers are at play within the realm, seeking to undermine and destabilise the smooth running of the provinces. At the Jade Dragon’s word, his agents have closely investigated each suspect instance, and after a time, found profane markings, runes and glyphs at the sites of all of these disasters. If left unchecked, these will merely be the start of an epidemic that ravages the rural heart of Grand Cathay.

Bearing magic attuned to the Iron Winds, the Horns of Shang-Yang are as powerful as they are rare. When the city of their namesake was wrested from its rightful ruler, the Horns too were lost. Such power cannot be allowed to reside in the wrong hands and nor can the proud city of Shang-Yang be allowed to crumble under the mismanagement of unworthy occupiers. It is time to retake the city; those sitting within its walls will soon learn that the Iron Dragon's vengeance is a force to be truly feared.

The embers of inspiration burn fiercely, as the toil and smoke of the smithy beckons, urging the most talented of craftsmen to lend it the sweat of their brow. One day soon, an item of peerless quality will emerge, forged through flame and magic. Yet, such grand creations require refinement. Allow the Lore of Yang to ebb and flow amidst the clamour of battle, harnessing the spirit of every triumph. Only then will the furnace burn hot with arcane energy, imbuing the newly-crafted artefact with the essence of each and every victory.

The Cauldron of Power withers and wanes, its arcane energy almost drained from constant use in Kislev's defence. Many materials will be required to resurrect the Cauldron's magic. Fortunately, such materials can be found in abundance within the realms of the Motherland's enemies…

Mother Ostankya’s eyes glaze over as she is suddenly overcome by a torrent of whispers from the spirits of the land. In hallucination, she scries a cave somewhere in the distant mountains where deep within sits a cavern of rare ice crystals, a place thrumming with the ancient magic of the land concentrated in dozens of glimmering stalagmites and stalactites. A single shard of one of these formations could be a powerful centrepiece for Ostankya’s crown, augmenting her influence over the spirits who facilitate her frightening spells. Yet as she drifts out of her vision, she also makes out a cacophony of monstrous roars, shrieks and howls... Something feral awaits!

The Changeling always has his multitudinous fingers in many pies, and one scheme put into motion many days prior is now coming to delightful fruition. The Trickster’s Staff, an ancient Tzeentchian artefact of little importance to the Old Worlders other than being worth a great deal of gold, sits securely in the vault of Dwarf merchants at Karak Azgaraz. By the Changeling’s machinations it had previously been in the possession of Empire merchants, only for him to promptly steal it back from them and plant it into the Dwarfs’ possession. With his deceitful whispers, the Empire merchants have been led to believe that the Dwarfs stole ‘their’ priceless artefact, and they now prepare to march on Azgaraz where bloodshed will surely ensue. The Changeling, of course, will take his customary front-row seat…

For all the Spirit of Grungni's impeccable craftsmanship, the work on such a glorious feat of engineering is never truly complete. With some slight tinkering and reinforcement, the frame of the airship may yet still be improved.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_spirit_of_grungni}}\\n\\nLearn more about the Spirit of Grungni [[url:script_link_campaign_spirit_of_grungni]]here[[/url]].

Almighty Morr demands respect, wherever His cultists reside. A garden temple of tombs ought to be a worthy act of worship, with a tower at its heart, steeped in the magic of death.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_gardens_of_morr}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_gardens_of_morr_learn_more}}

Wissenland prides itself in sparing no expense to thwart the Empire’s ever encroaching foes! The Elector Countess decrees full access to the Imperial Gunnery School’s advancements granted to you.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_imperial_gunnery_school}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_imperial_gunnery_school_learn_more}}

The Imperial Gunnery School possesses many schematics meant to improve a weapon's firepower. It would be worth acquiring some, though the designs are as expensive as they are useful…\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_imperial_gunnery_school}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_imperial_gunnery_school_learn_more}}

As our foes grow stronger, so too must the Imperial cause. As the Emperor's authority is bound to his dominance over his rightful lands, it is every able servant's role to expand that authority at any cost.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_empire_imperial_authority}}\\n\\nLearn more about Imperial Authority [[url:script_link_campaign_imperial_authority]]here[[/url]].

The vile brutes among the Ogre Kingdoms have wrought untold damage to imperial lands, slaughtering countless innocents to feed their endless gluttony. It is tie to cut their Feastmaster open, and put an end to their gory banquet of flesh!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

The magic of the Amethyst Order is an art spurned by some, seen to blur the fragile line between life and death. Yet the dark power wielded by its practitioners is nothing to be scoffed at – perhaps your fellow Spiriters would serve you well?\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_4_imperial_gunnery_school}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_imperial_gunnery_school_learn_more}}

The Black Tower rises from the earth like a beacon, a looming symbol of arcane power. Morr bids you travel between these beacons of Shyish, to better study the dark secrets of Death Magic, within His welcoming embrace.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_gardens_of_morr}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_gardens_of_morr_learn_more}}

The weak bow before the strong, and the strong bow before the even mightier still; such is the way of the Ruinous Powers. Thus, with a display of tremendous might, the Chieftains of Chaos would have no choice but to swear you their allegiance.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_chieftains}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_chieftains_learn_more}}

As Chieftains swear their fealty, their followers too may bow before you, offering to cut a bloody path through your enemies. Swell your army with their blades, and amass a horde of legend.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_4_chieftains}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_chieftains_learn_more}}

Every act of savage violence gladdens the hearts of Nurgle's faithful. Should you deign to slaughter their enemies on your bloody path of conquest, the Chieftains of filth and sickness will soon worship at your feet.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_chieftains}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_chieftains_learn_more}}

Gaining a foothold in the lands dominated by Khorne's scourge will require a price paid in blood. Decimate the Cult of the Crimson Skull, and stake the Urfather's claim atop a pile of their decaying corpses.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

The Flaming Scribes enact their petty schemes, tainting the air with Tzeentch's foul magic. It is an insult to the Urfather! Wipe them from the face of the world, and put an end to their plots forevermore.

To take the Slayer's Oath means to seek redemption for an act most shameful, for which the only recourse is to seek an honourable death in battle. Curiosity, however, is a foe that cannot be killed with mere weapons. And nothing draws on one's curiosity like the recent reports of mutilated bodies appearing across the Sylvanian countryside, testament to a new foe no doubt in need of slaying. \\n\\n The Spirit of Grungi's defences should be built up before venturing forth; this vessel cannot meet the same fate as the Undestructible Thunderbarge or the Unsinkable Ironclad. The former blew up and the latter sank... but this time things will be different!

The reports were not exaggerated – bodies were discovered clawed, savaged and feasted upon by some unholy creature. A peasant comes forth, telling of his near-deadly encounter with a seemingly feral Vampire, before the intervention of an aristocrat known as Countess Gabriella prevented him from becoming the creature’s next victim. Curiously, the Countess addressed the Vampire as “Ulrika”, a familiar name sparking a glimmer of recognition among your allies, Gotrek and Felix.\\n\\nGotrek tightens his grip around his axe, clearly intent on killing their former comrade, but as he and Felix quarrel the peasant explains to you that the Countess and Ulrika have already retreated to Nachthafen Castle. Entering the citadel will require you to masquerade as nobility, something best achieved with the help of a gold-laden treasure vault and a little flare for subterfuge...

As good at fixing up machines as it is at bashing foes, the Persuader has proven to be a very useful tool indeed. Yet for too long this intricately-designed hammer has fallen into a state of disrepair. Document the successes of other Dawi engineering in battle – perhaps what is learned from this battlefield research might be used to restore the Persuader to its former glory!
In service to the Elector Countess of Wissenland, Elspeth von Draken must help strengthen the Empire’s borders as she waits for greater evils to show themselves.

Visions flood Elspeth von Draken’s mind… she sees a crown upon a pedestal, before her vision soars into the air to reveal [[i]]a keep, surrounded by mountains[[/i]]. The location of this powerful artefact? As she snaps back to reality, she feels compelled to seek it out – before others do.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Elspeth’s visions have revealed a keep, surrounded by mountains.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Use any army to search for this location by ending turn with them in the correct region.[[/col]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by the Longbeard elders, against the elgi of the Fey Forest. The War of Vengeance ended once the elgi Grudge was proclaimed settled by High King Gotrek Starbreaker, yet since that time, all Dawi who step foot in Athel Loren report nothing but hostility and death by elgi hands. Quelling the Longbeards’ anger at these transgressions will take more than just the conquest of the forest – the guilty must also be buried within them.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by all kings, written in their blood and passed down the bloodlines, against the intolerable existence of the Dawi-Zharr. Many deny the Dawi origins of the Dark Lands’ abominations, and our annals tell us very little about the fate of those lost in the Age of Migration. All must accede, the mere suspicion that there exists Dawi who willfully turned from the Ancestor Gods, our people, and our way of life, is a shameful stain upon us all that must be wiped away.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by Belegar Ironhammer of the Angrund Clan and true King of Karak Eight Peaks, against those responsible for the defilement and occupation of Vala-Azrilungol. Some time has passed since the last retreat from the citadel at Eight Peaks, and its loss still stands as the Ironhammer bloodline’s greatest shame. They urge all Dawi to spare no expense to help purge its current occupiers and reclaim the Great Hold, taking a heavy toll of grobi and thaggoraki blood![[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by the Longbeard elders, against the elgi of Ulthuan. The War of Vengeance may have long ended, but tales of the atrocities committed against us during the conflict still pass from generation to generation, festering as wounds that can never heal. For many Dawi, the Phoenix Crown that sits within Karaz-a-Karak’s vault was not recompense enough for elgi insolence and Dawi losses, and Ulthuan should have been taken with it. It is not too late for a final reckoning.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by Thorek Ironbrow, Master Runesmith and discoverer of Karak Zorn, against the uzkul and lizard-beasts responsible for the demise of our ancestral capital. Through Ironbrow’s resolve and perseverance, the fabled Hold of the Upland Plateau has been refounded. Inscribed runestones in the city hint at the cause of its downfall: repeated invasions from the most powerful ghoul-kings, lizard-fiends and Daemons that hold sway over those lands. So it shall be, vengeance must find them.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by Thorgrim Grudgebearer, successor to the throne at this time of begrudging, against those other races who dare occupy the fallen Holds of the Karaz Ankor. Centuries of Chaos invasions, war, disaster and calamity has seen Dawi hegemony over the World’s Edge Mountains dwindle. No longer shall our former bastions be isolated islands surrounded by a sea of foes. All must be reclaimed, Dawi supremacy restored, in mighty acts of war and vengeance![[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared posthumously on behalf of the deceased Throndik Snorrisson, former High King and son of Snorri Whitebeard, against the great elgi betrayer Prince Malekith. Though oathbound to remain true to the ideals that he and Whitebeard had fought for together, the elgi wazzock Malekith has been overcome by corruption, becoming a scourge to the world along with his Naggarothi elgi. Let it be written here, as it was said by Whitebeard himself: There is nothing so foul as an oath-breaker.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by Thorgard Cromson, Great King of Kraka Drak, against all who threaten the Realms of the northern Dwarfs. The alliance between Thorgrim Grudgebearer and the northern clans is hereby invoked, beseeching all Dawi to march against the murderous warmongers of Norsca. We must recognise the northmen for what they are: ready supplicants to the Dark Gods who must be eradicated from those lands.[[/i]]

The mountain city of Karak Dum is well-known to you, where great furnaces and smithies of the Dawi had once become overrun by the encroaching Forces of Chaos, who made the city the jewel in their Ruinous crown. It is a great shame of your kin that many heirlooms were lost. Though its remaining inhabitants had been rescued during the Spirit of Grungni’s previous foray, there has been no word from the city since. Many of its treasures are thought to still remain in its holds – more than reason enough to go back and resecure the city!

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared posthumously on behalf of the deceased King Borri Silverfoot of Karaz Bryn, against Neferata and her uzkul thralls. The former citadel at the umgi-named Silver Pinnacle was once a great stronghold, taken in a single attack by the Queen of Evil and her loathsome forces. King Borri and many Dawi perished that night – their deaths can only be avenged by returning the citadel to Dawi hands and sealing away Neferata’s evil once and for all.[[/i]]

[[i]]Be it written that the Council of Kings bore witness to this Grudge, declared by all kings, written in their blood and passed down the bloodlines, against the intolerable existence of the thaggoraki menace.
