By Skavor, we have battled the wretched ratmen for millennia, yet our hate for the hideous creatures is undimmed. It is time to take the final fight to them and wash away centuries of Grudges with raki blood. The locations of their two main warrens at opposite ends of the Karaz Ankor are known – any Dawi force fit and ready to deal the killing blows is obliged to do so![[/i]]

Your Handgunner programme has given the Gunnery School a batch of new cadets eager to learn in the field. Let us hope their enthusiasm lasts!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

The school watches its students closely – as the budding riflemen hone their skills, their suitability to use the Gunnery School’s latest advancements is assessed.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

The Gunnery School’s cadets are both students and test subjects, granted the latest contraptions to trial and error in battle with pride and distinction.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

As the guns and artillery fire volley after volley at the Empire’s enemies, their successes and failures are observed, recorded and learned from.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

Access to easily-forged components of any size, shape or density enables the school to construct weapon prototypes far ahead of their time.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

The more experienced the cadets, the greater the number of enhancements and modifications they are trusted to equip themselves with.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

The application of magic to military engineering makes for much more destructive capabilities, but the added unpredictability has required greater scrutiny of developments tested in the field.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

Through a secret extracurricular program, a select group of Ironsides have successfully been trained in 'non-traditional' munitions and equipment usage.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

A masterful display of destructive ordnance powered by forces beyond the understanding of the professorship has demonstrated the value of less conventional sources of knowledge.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}
The campus at Nuln is the jewel in the Gunnery School's crown, and a beacon of the Empire's military supremacy.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

The ever-growing list of cutting-edge equipment and techniques developed by the Gunnery School continues to strengthen the pedigree of the Empire’s gunnery and artillery troops. \\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

Our enemies now heed the horror of our rocket-powered destruction delivered from afar, fuelled by the Amethyst Armoury!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_gunnery_school_panel_more_information}}

News spreads like wildfire throughout the land, as the panicked voices of the local populace recount their flight from the forces of Chaos. The armies of Ruin descend from the north, ransacking nearby towns and leaving the streets awash with blood. With enough haste, some of their victims may yet still be rescued from the jaws of death, yet for every life brutally snuffed out, the Winds of Shyish blow ever stronger. Perhaps this attack could also serve as a morbid opportunity? Lay waste to the forces of Chaos that terrorise the Empire, for their suffering will empower the Death's Timekeeper artefact and pave the way to unlocking the mysteries of time and death itself!

If Nurgle is to gain supremacy across the realm, His most important heralds must work tirelessly to perpetuate the cycle of life and death. Leading by example, Epidemius brooks no idleness or distraction from such serious matters, endlessly taking his plagued cavalcade to wherever wars can be waged and victims can be made, all the while irritably scratching his quill to keep his records up to date.

It is the duty of the seven Proctors of Pestilence to respond vehemently to Nurgle’s whims, demanding close observation of specific diseases and prognoses to ensure every detail is recorded in ink. No location is off-limits for such a preeminent task – not even Ulthuan itself. At the gates of the White Tower of Hoeth, a Plague-stricken High Elf host awaits the arrival of a meddling Prophetess of Bretonnia intent on purifying the Asur of their glorious pestilence. Epidemius cannot allow this outcome – the diseased High Elves must die, and more than that, their deaths must be observed in proximity before being prevented by the Bretonnians’ cure!

Rumours spoken in the Dark Tongue claim that any who survive a night in a lonely and haunted forest during Hexensnacht will be blessed with the aid of the wild magic of the mountains. None of Chaos' champions have lived to corroborate the tale, and so Tamurkhan deigns to set up his camp in the darkest part of the old forest as the sun sets. It will be no easy feat. Whichever beasts lurk in the shadows will soon make themselves known, and a river of blood will be spilled before the sun rises once more!

Marching through the Dark Lands, Tamurkhan stumbles upon a towering monster animated from rock, magically manipulated by a mischievous Greenskin Shaman. As it lurches to life, the creature begins a rampage of mass destruction, slaughtering a crowd of Chaos Dwarf warriors in a violent, blood-soaked frenzy. Their misfortune proves the opportunity Tamurkhan needs to strengthen a powerful alliance. Should he slaughter the Greenskin Shaman controlling this rogue idol, the grateful Dark Dwarfs will have no choice but to bow before the Master of Hosts.

Wandering through the Chaos Wastes, Tamurkhan's great horde encounters the roving warband of a sworn enemy of {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_nur_cha_exalted_hero_chieftain}}. As is the way of Ruin, mutual annihilation is inevitable, for one must bow to the other or die slowly at their feet. Pride will not allow either to willingly subjugate themselves, leaving only one path to dominance: all-out slaughter. Only when the nemesis of {{tr:land_units_onscreen_name_wh3_dlc25_nur_cha_exalted_hero_chieftain}} lies broken can Tamurkhan stand victorious, earning undying fealty with this latest conquest.

Tamurkhan sleeps fitfully, for his dreams are plagued with visions of horror in the garden of Nurgle. Unnatural monsters corrupt Grandfather's putrid realm, and dark powers dare to mar its beauteous corruptions. In the depths of slumber, Tamurkhan hears a being of great power calling for him to wake in the land of bewitched dreaming. As the interlopers descend, only the Fimir Balefiend Ketzak Fimdirach stands beside Tamurkhan, ready to banish the invading scum from the precious realms of Decay. The screeching hordes must be put to death, before their presence alone taints Nurgle's foetid garden!

Fatsod, Great Unclean One, Lord of Stench and Bile, the Burping Enormity and Most Rotund of the Host, has been recently blessed by Nurgle with enormous proportions. Unfortunately its insatiable appetites have also grown exponentially, and it has taken to snacking on the mortal warriors of Nurgle's Warband! Gloriously unholy or not, Fatsod must be dealt with. The most zealous followers of Chaos may see their devouring as a blessing, but the Chieftains cannot accept such losses if Nurgle's rot is ever to be spread across the land!

The Jabberslythe, Skraelsbane, devourer of Mournhowl's kin, has drunk deeply of the arcane Winds. Corrupted and insane, the creature has developed a taste for the Skin Wolves of Norsca. Eager to prove his superiority over the beast, Tamurkhan marches in defence of Mournhowl’s homeland, only to find Mournhowl’s kinsmen held captive by the beast and awaiting their imminent end within its jaws. It seems a new alliance lies just beyond the horizon, as the Maggot Lord leads his host into battle to aid Mournhowl's beleaguered warriors. Together, they may crush Skraelsbane decisively under their heels!

Not even the hardiest of Dwarfs dare meet the gaze of the War-mourner, Garagrim Ironfist, son of the great Slayer King Ungrim Ironfist. In spite of his noble birth, Garagrim is a Slayer, and has taken their bloody oath to the core of his steely Dwarfen heart. Nevertheless, this Dawi prince has warriors to spare under his command, drilled and barracked at the Dwarfhold of Karak Kadrin. Recruiting some of these units into your army may tempt him back to the battlefield once more, where the glorious death sought by all Slayers can surely be found.

Though the Slayer's Oath demands a valiant demise, great warriors chasing death and glory serve the Dawi little while the great Holds still lie vulnerable. And now there is cause to unleash your full engineering prowess upon those with Dwarf blood on their talons. If there is any hope of bringing down a Dragon, however, every Cannon must first be optimised and calibrated to the finest specifications. Perhaps it's time to take your latest artillery line out for a field test or two…

One Dragon's forays now warrant swift retribution for the devastation left at the sites of the former Holds of Dwarf refugees. The beast is likely to be protected by the Elven Dragon Princes, who ride the mighty steeds of Caledor in lieu of their elusive Draconic mounts. Thus, avid enemy horsemen must be sought on the field of battle; what is learned firing your great guns at one cavalry force can be used should the Dragon Princes get in your way.

A Dragon has made a new enemy in the Dwarfs, yet the mountainous ridges the airborne monsters of its kind call home are a treacherous landscape for any battle. To face the beast in its rocky lair, every warrior destined to do battle against it must be nimble and sure-footed. Engage in battle across such regions by blood and rifle – the perilous landscape will serve as a test for the greater dangers to come.

In light of recent terrible events, the throng is buoyed by the addition of the latest batch of brand-new artillery pieces. Quite frankly, there’s nothing better than a fresh batch of Cannons! Except perhaps having a decent drinking establishment nearby, which ironically is crucial to ease recruitment into the cannoneers’ ranks. A wholesome stein of Bugman’s doesn’t only help with the tinnitus, but also does wonders for the sanity of Dwarfs who spend so much time around constantly exploding gunpowder.

The Dragon Princes of Caledor once left the world in shadow, as their Draconic mounts blotted out the sun, wreaking devastation upon the helpless. Yet it is one Dragon's transgression against the innocent Dawi that will be remembered in the annals of history as the reason it was condemned to die. Complicit to the attacks, the Elven Dragonriders and indeed any of the Asur who protect the monster must also pay back the debt of spilt Dawi blood.

The entirety of Dwarfkind has been shaken by one monster’s destructive whims. Though the tragedy of Dwarf lives cut short by the despicable Dragon is still fresh in your mind, another crisis is brewing that will soon require your attention. The upheaval of Dwarfs from so many Holds threatens to plunge your kind into full-blown crisis, so must be managed tactfully.

With the Cannons tinkered with to near perfection, a battle of legend awaits, a chance to avenge Dawi blood spilled by a rampant Dragon. Nestled at the base of a towering rockface lies a yawning cave entrance uncovered by the keen eyes of your adventuring party, who have also spotted Elven Dragonriders rallying nearby. A thunderous roar echoes from the cave's depths, and bones litter the passageway into the dark. Every clue points to one dangerous truth: the Dragon lurks within!

A detestable Sorcerer-Prophet of the Chaos Dwarfs wreaks havoc across the land. Dreadquake war machines ensnare ever more captives destined for the factories of the Dark Lands. Your newly-assigned Gyrocopters could make short work of the loathsome contraptions, but the pilots are still fresh out of training and must be put through their paces with live combat. This will also serve as a field test for their new vessels, allowing the gathering of enough information to make some much needed upgrades.

To the puzzlement of your troops, the hunted Sorcerer-Prophet flits and raids elusively throughout the land as details on his main base of operations remain sparse. It appears a surgical operation, with smaller convoys reportedly replenishing his war supplies – or perhaps they are a ploy to distract pursuers from the main target’s grievous aims? One such resupply convoy has been spotted – decoy or not, if the twisted Dawi-Zharr wish to enslave innocents, each and every one of them shall pay the price.

The evil figure at the helm of the Dreadquake raiding party has come far in search of captives for his noxious mines and factories. The Chaos Dwarfs' home is a wasteland of smog and desolation, stifling the lungs of all but its wretched inhabitants. Only those with experience in similarly brutal climates might hope to match the strength of those that live there. Immerse yourself among the vile wastelands that plague the world, until the Dark Lands' toxic haze feels like a welcome reprieve.

Kislev will leave no stone unturned to avenge its losses from the Sorcerer-Prophet's raids – that much is certain – while the other great power in Old World always has its beady Imperial eyes cast everywhere. Establishing trade links with either Kislev or Cathay may prove beneficial for much more than fiscal reasons. Even from beyond your countless feats of engineering genius, the Dawi have much to offer, should either nation have any valuable information to exchange about recent events…

Your shared origins with the Chaos Dwarfs mean they are as cunning as you, the intellect of the hunted raider making him as dangerous as his own Dreadquakes. One pursuing force had recently been led through a chokepoint that soon became awash with their blood in a vicious ambush orchestrated by the Sorcerer-Prophet. The Dark Dwarfs’ ways of war are too much of a mystery to risk an immediate attack against a proven battlefield master such as this. His lesser brethren, on the other hand...

Gyrocopter squadrons have always been important to the Dawi throngs lucky enough to have them, providing invaluable air support for ground troops. Yet under your command they will not only fly in support of the warriors, but also to run aerial interference around the Spirit of Grungni as it flies to war. The Gyrocopters must be a day-to-day presence around the legendary Airship, allowing them opportunities to be routinely drilled as part of its battle protocols.

The Sorcerer-Prophet’s location and movements are finally being tracked from the air, leaving him nowhere to hide. Investing your time into the Gyrocopters has been worthwhile – they have turned the tide in this search, and will hopefully make the difference in the battle to come. Take the Spirit of Grungni and its Gyrocopter squadron to the skies to rain fire down on the Hashut-worshipping fiend; prove our war machines are superior to any of that monster's foul creations or magic!

The vile thralls of Khorne gather beneath the banner of an Exalted Bloodthirster – just the enemy you have been seeking! Many a Bloodthirster Daemon has found its way into the Book of Grudges, and a good Daemon-slaying is certainly long overdue. With enough calibration and field testing, your new batch of Organ Guns should make quick work of the fiend and, more importantly, show Gotrek that even a great Slayer such as he will never be able to match your kill-count!

Ruin infuses the very air that surrounds the Khornate scourge recently appearing across the land; it is difficult to imagine that your Dwarf warriors will survive a Daemon encounter without experience fending off Chaos' malevolent energies. It may be worth seeking battle and adventure in a Wasteland steeped in Chaos – only then will your warriors understand its wretched taint, and feel prepared to fight through the darkness.

It is of little doubt that your tinkering will have the Organ Guns battle-ready when the time comes to face the Daemon. Any failures in the coming battles will certainly not be down to the firearms themselves, but the throng is still rather wet around the ears when it comes to artillery warfare. The new gun crews are in dire need of battlefield drilling, with the blood they spill now no doubt earning the Bloodthirster's attention later.

The Exalted Bloodthirster responsible for the recent Chaos upsurge will prove a deadly foe, capable of crushing the skulls of any brave enough to face it. If there is anything to be learned from the slaughter in the Holds left in the creature's wake, its that more than mere courage will be required to best it. Gather your strength and sharpen your mind, for this challenge demands the deadliest of inventions, wielded by a champion at the height of their power.

The Daemons of Khorne revel in the destruction left in their wake. Yet entities of the Chaos Realm are notoriously hard to track, with the ability to manifest portals which can swallow their entire hosts in the blink of an eye, only to have them later appear elsewhere on the mortal plane. Such rifts have attracted other opportunistic visitors from the other side, meaning that when it rains Daemons, it pours!

Your new Organ Guns cannot be brought to their full destructive potential a moment too soon! A recent sighting of a Herald of Khorne demands more serious attention than being another opportunity for showing Gotrek up, for this is a Daemon existing solely to fuel others with an irresistible hunger for prolonged war. The Bloodthirster and the rest of the Khorne cannon-fodder will be weaker once it is dead, if only from giving the throng a taste of the greater Daemon-slaying feat to come.

Weeks of tinkering with the war machines and drilling the warriors to fight alongside the Organ Guns has you primed for the bloodiest of battles! The Bloodthirster's ravaging army threatens all with its insatiable lust for all-out slaughter. But once Khorne's wretched pet falls to the barrage of your artillery, many age-old grudges borne of the Bloodthirster's past massacres will also finally be struck from the Dammaz Kron. And not only that – Gotrek will see that you are as great a Slayer as he!

On a serendipitously clear day, a report is received of a flare fired into the sky from an unknown source in the distance. After the area it originated from was reconnoitred, it was discovered that the flare was a rudimentary but effective device built by a young Dwarf Engineer – unexpectedly, a member of a lost Dwarf regiment thought to have been wiped out many weeks prior! While being held captive with his force by the Dark Elves, the tinkerer had managed to cobble together a makeshift distress-flare using scrap metal and ignitable ore. Such ingenuity certainly deserves rescue, but aside from that, there are innocent Dwarf and manling lives at stake! All who toil under the Naggarothi do not stay alive for long.

Tales of trees uprooting themselves and coming alive are typically the stuff of fables, but the current path of indiscriminate murder by the animated boughs and branches of the Forest Spirits makes their horror all too real for many of the Empire’s citizens. At the centre of the awakenings are the Treemen, beings saturated with magic that rouses others of their kind. One's gnarled and lumbering form has been spotted, it must be brought down before its host grows!

As tempting as it may be, one does not simply just waltz into the forest with Flame Cannons set to 'maximum incineration' without first carrying out some reconnaissance and interrogation of the locals. The pesky forest Elves must know something about the mysterious awakening, or perhaps are culpable for it in some way themselves. Diplomacy is rarely the option with the isolationist Fey – it is time to poke the wasp’s nest and see what is revealed.

It is thought that the forest magic that twists the trees into violent spirits of bark and branch comes from the same source of arcane energy that rouses the bloodlust of the beasts and monsters that live there. Facing such creatures in their own habitat requires no small amount of practice and understanding of the threats faced when waging war in the wilderness. Put your host’s monster-slaying skills to the test; ready the warriors for the worst the forest might throw at them.

The malevolent Treemen devastating the Empire provide a glorious opportunity for doom, but you must resist throwing yourself at the monsters for now. With the Empire invoking age-old oaths to ask for your help, you should first ascertain precisely what it is you are up against – at the very least, to know how much black powder and munitions to bring to the fight. The nobles who saw their lands ravaged by the twisted creatures would be a good place to start.

A dark and sinister force has spread across the forests of the Old World, awakening angry tree spirits that have claimed countless human lives. The most powerful of the Treemen has been located, deemed to be at the epicentre of the awakenings, and now your oath to defend your human allies must be fulfilled. March out and introduce its host to your latest Flame Cannon upgrades; time to reduce these rampaging spirits to cinders!

A dark and sinister force has spread across the forests of the Old World, awakening angry tree spirits that have claimed countless human lives. The most powerful of the Treemen has been located, deemed to be at the epicentre of the awakenings, and now your oath to defend your human allies must be fulfilled. March out and introduce its host to your latest Flame Cannon upgrades; time to reduce these rampaging spirits to cinders!

Slaying an Arachnarok Queen will be a valiant feat worthy of legend, with the likelihood of encountering the scores of Goblins that seek the monster nigh on guaranteed. The grobi masses are nothing to fear, but you know better than to charge into any war without being fully prepared for all outcomes. Be it at a few ragtag tribes or a full-blown gobbo Waaagh!, the Goblin Hewer’s gears need greasing and weathering for the worst of worst-case scenarios!

If your Goblin Hewer's axes are ever to tear through the flesh of both Greenskins and Giant Spiders in a single skirmish, the machine needs to generate the necessary power for its unorthodox projectiles to pierce the hides of all manner of thick-carapaced monsters and beasts. Search out hordes of the grotesques that plague the land and take every opportunity to optimise the mechanisms of the Hewer, for such adjustments will surely prove vital for entering the Spider Queen’s lair.

It seems the existence of the legendary Arachnarok Queen is no mystery to most Goblins you've had the pleasure of capturing and interrogating. But so far, none of them seem to have any idea where the information originated from, or who it is that knows the monster's  location for certain. Perhaps perseverance is the key here – if you beat enough grobi into submission, one of them might reveal something eventually!

Your scouts report a notorious Night Goblin on the prowl, a well-known Hatchling herder who is thought to have supplied many a Spider Mount for his Goblin kin. He too covets the Arachnarok Queen’s eggs, no doubt to bolster the ranks of some Warboss' next wretched Waaagh! Wiping him and his search party from the map would certainly be doing the civilised world a favour, and give the Goblin Hewer its most notable kill yet!

It is little wonder that Goblins are fearless (or stupid) enough to want to enter the inhospitable lair of the Arachnarok Queen. Most of them originate from the notorious Badlands, a landscape of diverse dangers harboured in mist-covered swamps, unnavigable dunes, and trackless rocky barrenness, a habitat not too different from the caverns where the monster will be hunted. To brave this task, you should first familiarise the throng with similar environmental perils to harden them for the challenge ahead.

You want nothing but the toughest Dwarfs operating your beloved brainchild, the famed Goblin Hewer, but the tougher your warriors are the harder pressed they are to be removed from the front lines. Luckily, the well-known dangers of operating your machines means it has not been that difficult to find a cohort of fellow Slayers willing to brave the Hewer's perils. Their only caveat: expand your Slayer numbers so the crew can take turns to attempt seeking their doom on the front lines.

News reaches you that the Goblin Clans have finally discovered the Arachnarok Queen’s lair where she fiercely guards her nest and coveted brood. Eager to wrangle Hatchlings and pilfer Giant Spider eggs, the grobi masses have mobilised their hordes towards the Queen’s cavern, where danger and possible doom await you. Adventure into the depths of the earth and ensure the name Malakai Makaisson and the infamous Goblin Hewer are etched into legend!

A Vampire and his necromantic thralls cavort with an army of the dead, raising more and more of the world’s deceased into their battle ranks from the sacred rest of their tombs. With complete incineration being the only surefire way to annihilate an Undead puppet, a precise recipe of incendiary compounds must be used to utterly consume the husks in Gyrobomber flame. Thus much fielding testing will be required to ensure the fleet’s readiness for the much-more-flammable payloads.

The Undead walk the earth as unnatural fiends, suffused with dark and perilous magics. Any experience in dealing with the darkest arts of the arcane will be vital in fulfilling your oath to end this recent scourge. Lead your adventuring army against any sorcerous villain that threatens our kin or allies; the knowledge gained from such a battle could be used to perfect your Gyrobomber tactics for the coming skirmishes.

The walking dead are an abominable enemy that attacks in vast waves, quickly overwhelming the unprepared with sheer numbers. Yet they are easily defeated by striking down the puppet masters who control them; sniveling, malevolent individuals who are weak once you deprive them of their wretched party trick of conjuring life into the lifeless. Up to now, your retinue has been mostly spared from the horrors of the necromantically inclined, but in time must learn all the tricks of such a foe .

The Vampiric scourge and their Undead thralls inhabit the darkest corners of the world, lands teeming with Vampiric corruption. An expedition into the heart of their wicked abode will be fraught with danger, leaving our warriors susceptible to the ravages of their malevolent energies. It would be wise to immerse yourself in lands steeped in such corruption sooner rather than later, lest its dark taint prove too much in the heat of battle.

Your scouts who shadow the growing Undead horde bring dire news: two splinter groups have split off from the shambing masses led by two thralls of the Vampire Lord responsible for this Undead awakening, but whose own hosts also grow in power. The squadrons have their new directives; a Master Necromancer and Strigoi Ghoul King are now on your hit-list.

Gyrobomber squadrons have always been important to the Dawi throngs lucky enough to have them, providing invaluable air support for ground troops. Yet under your command they will not only fly in support of the warriors, but also to run aerial interference around the Spirit of Grungni as it flies to war. The Gyrobombers must be a day-to-day presence around the legendary Airship, allowing them opportunities to be routinely drilled as part of its battle protocols.

The Vampire Lord's power still grows with each passing hour, as scores of the shambling undead still clamber from their tombs. With the creature and his husks now located, the conclusion of this adventure now looms near. It is time for the Gyrobombers to take to the clouds to rain fire down upon his deathly horde and send them to oblivion! For only when the fiend has been destroyed will the Undead stench be truly wiped clean from the land.

The Skaven attack against the Dwarf trading hub may not be out of character, but for them to stick around and not scurry back into their holes is a worrying sign indeed. A major scheme must be brewing, and one best dealt with using the most defensible mobile vantage points you can provide. Your new Thunderbarge class of Airships are ready, now only needing a little field testing to prove that their killing prowess sufficiently exceeds their likelihood to crash!

The worrying situation at the Dwarf trading hub is starting to be felt across the Dwarfholds. The trade route that serves the hub is one that maintains the fragile cordial relations between the Dawi and other races but is now cut off, with long-term repercussions potentially leading to diplomatic consequences as well. It will not be long before a problem arises that needs dealing with...

From the Dwarfs' experience, the Skaven are creatures of low cunning on the open battlefield for the most part, with their diabolical weaponry used primarily to make them a deadly threat at range. Though the danger they pose is miniscule next to the booming might of a Thunderbarge, there would be no harm in familiarising the throng with their uniquely twisted warmongering ways. To any Dwarf who has never fought them, it is a rite of passage to do so!

It is clear that the Skaven blockading the mountain trading hub are waiting for reinforcements, but is that all they are waiting for? There is no time to find out, with a second Skaven force already scouted and moving up into the mountain passes. Curiously, it is led by a wretched Raki donned in hissing, clanking contraptions, indicating he is a Warlock of sorts. And where the most devious minds of the Skaven go, destruction usually follows!

Though the might of your flying machines is a wonder to behold, the Skaven are far too numerous for the Spirit of Grungni to hold back alone. Yet the lofty mountainous location of the blockade means an aerial threat is still the right tactic. Having instructed your hangar workshops to work around the clock, your latest designs for new Airship parts are in production for final assembly. No cost should be spared to get the fully operational Thunderbarges into the air!

Ever since its construction, your flagship Thunderbarge has had the Raki in its sights. Assembled following the Skaven invasion of Nuln, the legendary Spirit of Grungni even suffered an attack by them before it was completed, but fortunately even when partially completed it still had more than enough ability to thwart them. The Skaven must know the Spirit takes to the skies again – the mere possibility that it may appear on the battlefield will dampen any resolve in their craven hearts.

The scheme has been revealed! The filthy rats’ blockade had been a distraction while a dreaded Warpstone bomb was being planted in the mountain high above the trading hub, where its detonation would surely cause a devastating avalanche and a permanent end to this crucial trade route. For the sake of Dawi prosperity and the innocent Dwarfs who would perish there, you can wait no longer. An intervention of this magnitude will be a bold step towards your redemption!

Nuln is known to many as the “Jewel of the Empire”, and not without good reason. As the Empire’s industrial as well as cultural heartland, this sprawling city contains many manufactories providing heavy weapons, munitions and ordnance, in addition to the Imperial Gunnery School, whose role is it to train the Emperor’s artillerists in the ways of modern, mechanised warfare. There are some, however, who believe that only a fraction of Nuln’s potential is currently being exploited. The rulers of the Empire have demanded the development of a new cavalry doctrine, so Theodore Bruckner may join Imperial armies in the field. View this as an opportunity for Nuln to further earn its already-well-deserved title of “Bastion of the South”.

The theoretical tacticians at the Imperial Gunnery School may well have developed a new, game-changing model for cavalry warfare, but Countess Emmanuelle and Bruckner, her champion, remain unconvinced. What they really need to see is the method proved in combat, against the Emperor’s foes, and as soon as is humanly possible! Only then will they be satisfied that a man of Bruckner's singular talents will be put to best use on the battlefield.

The Night Goblin's army wreaks havoc across the land, spreading the Nemesis Crown's wicked and corrupting influence. Dominated armies fall into line at the Crown-bearer's command, with nothing but conquest and destruction on their minds.\\n\\nThe Empire cannot fall victim to this vile onslaught – the Night Goblins have already shed more than enough innocent blood. Defeat this ravaging band of scum and cast the Crown back into the dark once more!

As Elspeth reaches the location of her visions, she is dismayed to find she is too late! The Nemesis Crown has already been claimed by a vile horde of Greenskins, whose leader has made off with the artefact. One of his straggling armies remains, with cackles of “da Boss is da King now, ee’s got da Crown!” echoing throughout the surrounding mountains. The Dark Lady must confront the remnants of the green horde head-on and find out where this “king” might be.

A lumbering Orc by the name of Luggn Biggagit has been summoned by the Crown-bearer, and with him follows an overwhelming force of hideous Trolls and monsters. Should they reach their destination, our fight to snatch the Nemesis Crown from the Night Goblin who wields it could prove insurmountable. Yet if some terrible tragedy should befall Luggn on his journey...\\n\\n[[col:green]]Succeeding in this mission will remove Luggn from the Nemesis Crown final battle, weakening the enemy forces.[[/col]]

The Night Goblin fanatic Icky da Nosepicka obeys the call of the Nemesis Crown, marching his forces with haste to join the Crown-bearer on the field of battle. If we ever hope to seize the Crown from the vile grip in which is resides, this union cannot be allowed! Ride out to meet this Night Goblin horde and slay their misguided leader; we cannot waste an opportunity to weaken our foes!\\n\\n[[col:green]]Succeeding in this mission will remove Icky from the Nemesis Crown final battle, weakening the enemy forces.[[/col]]

Gnashrak Spiderclaw marches to battle at the head of an army of arachnids. Soon, his spiderlings will join the Crown-bearer's forces, strengthening his army immeasurably. Perhaps it would be wise to stop them creeping any closer. Squash this wretched Shaman and his many-legged army at once, before they can unite with our foul enemy!\\n\\n[[col:green]]Succeeding in this mission will remove Gnashrak from the Nemesis Crown final battle, weakening the enemy forces.[[/col]]

As his decaying forces ooze and lactate their way across the countryside seemingly unopposed, Tamurkhan’s trail of putrid slime taints what lush flora that remained, pleasing the Urfather greatly. Now, Tamurkhan sets his sights on the great Imperial city of Nuln, his gift to Nurgle and a crucial step on his terrible journey to Daemonhood. This will be no easy task, however, as the garrison at Nuln is prepared for the coming incursion. From the Empire’s finest to the common smallfolk, all are ready to lay down their lives – nay, their very souls – in defence of the homeland, in a haze of blackpowder and artillery smoke. Tamurkhan scoffs at such futile resistance, for all *will* be crushed before him, and the city *will* embrace its new, foetid patron soon enough!

Geheimnistag, or the Floating Holiday as it is known among citizens of the Empire, marks that rarest of occasions: when both the twin moons of Morrslieb and Mannslieb are risen and bright in the night, thinning the veil that separates the mortal realm from the other planes of existence. It is no coincidence that on one such Geheimnisnacht Eve, the hallowed Dwarf Slayer Gotrek and his mannish companion and chronicler Felix Jaeger detected and defeated a Slaaneshi cult, only to find themselves transported to the Realm of Chaos to face more horrors at the whim of the insidious Prince of Pleasure. His gamesmaster – a Keeper of Secrets – must be found and killed for Slaanesh’s foul game to finally end.

Nothing can withstand the might of Khorne. No one can defeat the Blood God. Victory can never truly be achieved against the Lord of Murder, for more of His followers will always return to wage bloody war. And you, a Champion hell-bent on drawing His burning gaze, walk the world to prove those axioms until the end of your existence.

You wander the world, forever in search of glorious battle to sustain the favour of Khorne and fulfil your own desperate desire for carnage. Many may survive you simply because they are beneath your notice; you don't even pause to casually slay those who cross your path, so singular is your desire for a worthy fight. And now you have once again found what you seek.

In the eternal quest for glorious battles, you have learned to make your own myths. By assaulting the very hearts of your enemies' domains, you are sure to find the grandest opposition there is. Such peerless deeds of war you dedicate to Khorne, certain they shall please Him – if only for a time. Blood for the Blood God!

Even the most battle-hardened warlord would not willingly face such odds – against a foe seemingly much greater in strength, without backup or known escape routes, and lacking any other advantage. For one to see such disparity of forces and still have the desire to take the field, it would be called madness or a monumental folly by most. For you, however, the exact opposite is true: there is no finer challenge to be encountered.

The enemy has superior numbers? Ideal! They have better equipment? It won't save them. They have no fear of the forces of Chaos? Blood for the Blood God! In the battle ahead, you will viciously – and permanently – demonstrate what happens when one faces Arbaal the Undefeated.

A sea of gleaming steel as far as the eye can see. Countless legions, each soldier a master warrior determined to cut you down. A collective might enough to crush the very skies and shatter the lands of the mortal realm. Who could resist such a foe? To a bloodthirsty acolyte of Khorne, this is the ultimate challenge.

The burning gaze of Khorne, to whom you have pledged to be an eternal provider of spectacular conflict and violence, turns to you. To garner His favour and uphold your status as one of the Blood God’s true Champions, you are compelled to seek yet another worthy challenge. Wherever an army gathers in preparation for some unknown and ultimately inconsequential war, the Undefeated One shall soon find them.

Rarely do you spare the weak. Not out of virtue, but for a sole purpose: to spread the message that you would face anyone in battle you deem worthy. This is your great taunt against the world – come and fight, if you dare! Most times, your foes tremble before your might, as they should. Sometimes, they decide to answer the challenge. How you relish such occurrences!

All glory to the Blood God! Only the foolish believe they can drive back the hordes of Khorne, amassing legions of warriors in a futile attempt to resist Him. Yet by marching to war, they do little more than perpetuate His will. You laugh in thunderous triumph. Let them march! You shall descend upon them like a living thunderstorm of fury, to wreak such havoc that will surely satisfy the raging demands of your master.

The Blood God openly rewards those who please him by overcoming his ordained trials. Khorne's bloodlust is never-ending, however, and his Boons can make future challenges easier – or harder…\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_3_wrath_of_khorne}}\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_dlc26_narrative_addendum_wrath_of_khorne}}
The Pillar of Skulls belongs to Khorne! Occupy it for Him, and punish those who stand in your way.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

Khorne has neither time nor patience for those who cannot deliver Him supreme violence. Prove the measure of your mettle and answer His summons!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_wrath_of_khorne}}\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_dlc26_narrative_addendum_wrath_of_khorne}}

The bulbous Ogres roam the Chaos Wastes, presenting a worthy challenge. Defeating such strength in battle is a surefire way to earn Khorne's Favour.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Your status as the greatest Warboss is not just because you are the meanest, toughest, and strongest Orc there is, but because in any given battle you possess something no other Orc has: a plan.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_da_plan}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_da_plan_learn_more}}

As you tear through the battlefields, you gain insight into how to conduct warfare in the most cunning and brutal manner possible. A new means of winnin’ is surely just around the corner…\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_3_da_plan}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_da_plan_learn_more}}

After gorging their stomachs, the Ogres’ greatest joy is filling their pockets with gold by fighting on behalf of others – fortunately, opportunity knocks from every horizon!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_mercenary_contracts}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc26_narrative_addendum_mercenary_contracts}}

Some Ogres are content to get a Contract, earn some coin, and then wander off into the sunset. But experience tells you that 'meetin’ and exceedin’' the client’s expectations always brings the greatest rewards.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_mercenary_contracts}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc26_narrative_addendum_mercenary_contracts}}

Establishing a foothold in Lustria will be essential in hunting down and imbibing the strength of the Champions who dwell here. Go forth and take Qu'ittax!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

Tzeentch’s local Champion seeks to make a name out of defeating you to garner their unscrupulous master’s favour. Slaughter this peon and reap their essence!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

In blood-soaked claws you hold a fresh skull, its Champion's Essence coursing into your Daemonic veins. Channel this power through the Cloak of Skulls to augment your peerless might!\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_2_cloak_of_skulls}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc26_narrative_addendum_cloak_of_skulls}}

When men from the Empire first cut their frontiers deeper into the surrounding forest, they unwittingly began the bitter War of the Drakwald that continues to this day. Unbeknownst to them, their deepest forays had encroached dangerously close to the most holy of sites to the Forest Goblin tribes, the sacred lands known as the Black Pit, or the Valley of Many Eyes. To stray near that dark and web-strewn place is certain death, for the Forest Goblins will stop at nothing to destroy any interlopers who dare approach it.

One of the rising legends amongst the Forest Goblins is Snagla Grobspit, a woodcrafty Spider Rider, able to sneak around enemy armies and launch attacks from unexpected quarters. The only survivor of the Redvenom tribe, he thirsts for vengeance by any means, fair or (preferably) foul. His foes whisper that Snagla and his Spider Riders can creep right out of the very shadows, and perhaps it is true.
PH ITEM AND MISSION NEED TO BE REMOVED.

Aside from the Tyrant himself, Bruisers are typically the most imposing Ogres in terms of sheer size, strength and power within a tribe’s pecking order, and often act as enforcers or under-chieftains. As payment for their brawn and fighting skill, they are afforded many privileges. One such benefit is unhindered access to the camp's weapon pile where the best clubs and blades are kept, to be used or refashioned for the Tyrant's closest mates, including the Bruiser himself.

Bragg the Gutsman showed great affinity for lopping off heads from a very young age. Yet it was when he created the death-dealing weapon known as the Great Gutgouger that he earned true notoriety, wielding the modified hook-blade with such prowess that he could slice off a foe's head with a mere flick of his powerful wrists. Champions of every race have fallen before Bragg, dismembered by his strange and horrible weapon. He travels from tribe to tribe seeking such killing opportunities and others who may provide them, so is always welcomed as a powerful Bruiser who is useful in a scrap.

Gorbad Ironclaw is always on the warpath, like any great Orc Warboss of renown. Yet he is also a resourceful strategist who knows the importance of keeping an army well-supplied. As his army marauds across the land, he orders da boyz to opportunistically cut down any forest that lies in their path to build arrows, armour, and the horde’s rickety machines of war. Mass deforestation does not sit well with the forest’s inhabitants, however, with Gorbad’s recent excursions catching the attention of the local Beastmen, who need little invitation to go to war, while the forest itself seems to groan and heave with dissatisfaction at the horde’s presence…

Arbaal has been cutting a swath of devastation across the realm. True challenges have been few and far between, but recent rumours of usually reclusive Sylvanian Vampire Lords warmongering against the weakling southerners in the region have piqued his interest. He would seek them out at the Northern border of their domain, and give Essen and Sylvania something to truly curdle their dreams at night and haunt them by day. Khorne might find the spectacle of such a battle a satisfactory diversion – and while Vampires may have forgotten the sting of death, they would now face a fate much more final. Khorne’s Destroyer delivers oblivion, and would gladly feed on the Undead’s supposed 'immortality', just as they prey on the mortality of lesser creatures.

The World’s Edge Mountains have long occupied a sliver of Skulltaker’s murderously undeviating mind. For those peaks and crevasses are where legends of the Empire say Khorne’s greatest Bloodletter battled Sigmar for three days, before suffering his one and only defeat in all recorded history. The Daemon still carries a scar from the felling wound inflicted upon him by man’s so-called god-king – an eternal reminder of the debt owed by Sigmar’s inheritors, which he gladly collects. Today, however, the ancient peaks are occupied mostly by Dwarfs, a hardy race of stout but resolute warriors sure to make a doomed stand against him. Skulltaker senses worthy skulls are amongst them and their reaping is imminent, but also something more: a smell of familiar blood that fans the ancient flames of vengeance.

Golgfag agreed to sell his company's services to the Orc Warboss Gnashrak, interested in the gastronomic merits of having free access to ready-to-eat Goblins. However, in doing so, he didn't expect the multiple gruelling battles they’d have to endure against the Dwarfs of Karak Kadrin. Twice, Golgfag and his Greenskins employers escaped the wrath of the stunted ones, until a third, decisive battle loomed on the horizon. But Golgfag and Gnashrak's alliance was already on shaky ground by that point – the Ogres kept drinking ale and eating Goblins, while the Orc Warboss’ resentment grew in seeing his supplies of booze and fodder gradually dwindle to nothing. As the Dwarf army closes in for the final showdown, Gnashrak has to entice the Ogres to fight once again, perhaps for the last time.

Scyla Anfingrimm was once the bane of the coastlands from frozen Norsca to faraway Cathay. A bloodthirsty raider and Champion of his tribe, Scyla's name was synonymous with victory and pillage, evoking fear in coastal cities all across the world. Those who raided alongside him saw the fire of a born leader in his eyes.

In time, Khorne came to notice Scyla’s feats, first gifting him with massive brute strength and hulking, ape-like arms. Grateful for his blessing, Scyla launched even greater raids resulting in destruction beyond compare. Thus, Khorne gifted him with a serpentine tail ending in a snapping maw. With more merciless slaughter came the Blood God’s final gift: the mind of a ravenous beast. Scyla’s transformation into a mindless Chaos Spawn would be complete soon after. Yet carnage recognises carnage. To match such desire to kill and maim in the name of Khorne will surely bring the beast forth so that he may continue to garner his master’s favour through carnage!

Skullreapers form the mortal backbone of Khorne's legions, the elite among them being the Wrathmongers. Once a Skullreaper begins to walk the path of a Wrathmonger, there is no going back. Aspirants are subjected to a punishing regime of conditioning and worship, as the Khornate demagogues – known as Bloodspeakers – goad the aspirants to battle one another night and day, never allowing them to rest for long.
{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc26_skarr_bloodwrath_unlock_3}} In return, Skarr reaps such a tally of skulls that none can keep count.

The Eastern Isles are the most remote of the Asur colonies. While there are many seafaring nations who would covet Ulthuan’s dominion over the Sea of Dread, it strikes you as improbable that mere pirates could have found them by anything other than sheer chance.\\n\\nThat will be their misfortune. None of them will ever leave these Isles again, and the flotsam of their wretched vessels will serve as scaffolding for our future Outpost.

There are few sites in the world of greater significance to the Asur than the Tower of the Sun. The Shrine of Asuryan. Vaul’s Anvil. The Gaen Vale. But surely none beyond Ulthuan’s enchanted shores.\\n\\nForget its mercantile and military importance; it is a land of great and primordial magic, the site of the Everqueen’s decennial voyage from Ulthuan for the rituals that hold Sariour na Yenlui at bay and delay the end of the world for another ten years.\\n\\nAs Sea Lord, you too have sailed these same waters – not in prayer, but in war – and it offends every drop of Asur blood you carry to see it defiled by freebooting filth.

With an Elven foothold re-established on the largest of the populated isles, it is time to exert Asur dominance over the rest of the Archipelago. Take full control of the western sea-lanes, and the last remaining pirates will be effectively cut off, allowing you to strangle the provincial outposts at your leisure.

The vessel is a black mark on the horizon, but familiarity breeds immediate recognition, as well as contempt. A mountainous hulk of scarred grey rock and harpy-infested crags, the waters around it churned white from the shoals of daggerfish and kharybdis following in the vessel’s wake.\\n\\nA Black Ark of Naggaroth. Come to prey on the wealthy coastlines of Ind and Cathay, most likely, but you cannot be certain. At the very least, a show of force is required, lest the Druchii return after your fleet has departed.

Patrols in the Sea of Chaos, north of Ulthuan, report increased sightings of Norscan longships, with many even penetrating the Shifting Isles to raid in Chrace and Cothique. Could this unseasonal belligerence be tied to the rumours out of Naggaroth? It would not be the first time that the Druchii manipulated the Norscans into serving their purposes, or used their sporadic invasions to provide cover for their own.\\n\\nIt is time to enforce your mandate as Sea Lord of Ulthuan and gather the fleets of the Asur. Their Admirals may have heard much that you have not.
Sail east to Cathay’s waters. Cast the Undead corsairs to the depths, scatter the savage Greenskins, and harry Fellheart’s Dread – his reckoning shall come!
Lustria’s shores demand callous cleansing. Cast down Harkon’s Awakened and their thrice-damned mutineers, and rid the jungle of the verminous presence.
We steel ourselves in these alien waters. Unweave Sarthorael’s twisted sorceries, bury the vermin in their warrens, and subdue the cold-blooded host.
Ulthuan must be made whole again! Crush Skull Crag’s Greenskins rabble, burn out the Druchii cults, and cast the Daemons back to the abyss.

You have long harried lesser Asur fleets and plundered their trade convoys. Yet one prey has always slipped your blade – Aislinn, High Admiral of the Sea Patrol. Word reaches you that the Elven colonies east of the Southlands are being rebuilt, and that the Dragonship-leading coward himself oversees the effort. A perfect chance to spill white-garbed sailors' blood, seize Aislinn’s ports, and pry loose the secrets of their hidden waterways!\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Sail through the Sea Lane in southern Jade Sea to reach the trio of Ancient Elven Colonies.[[/col]]

Aislinn's enemies never survive for long, for he dispatches all threats quickly and efficiently... with one exception: Lokhir Fellheart, a wily Dark Elf corsair and the closest thing the Sea Lord has to an arch-nemesis. Fellheart’s fleet has long harried smaller Asur naval forces and plundered trade convoys, yet always evading retribution. The audacity of the Druchii pirate has driven Aislinn to silent fury, the Sea Lord long ago making it his personal mission to slay this marine menace once and for all.\\n\\nNow cornered by the High Elf fleet, Lokhir Fellheart has made the desperate move of challenging Aislinn to an honourable pitched battle on dry land. Pride and arrogance dictates that Aislinn accept, but deep down he knows it must be a deception of some sort.

From the mighty Tower of Ashshair, the servants of the Dragon Emperor keep watch over the great road and read the night sky, always looking for signs, and ever vigilant of threats. Though nigh-unassailable, it has proven an irresistible target for Sayl's cunning incursion. It is not conquest Sayl desires, but the opportunity to plunder much of its arcane secrets, having induced a force of Beastmen to bear the brunt of the resistance from the tower's defences. He knows he cannot tarry, for Cathay's supply of soldiers and destructive magic is vast – yet he will make the most of this opportunity, no matter how much of his force he has to sacrifice.

In her latest performance in honour of the Dark Prince, the Masque of Slaanesh has brought along a retinue of High Elves and Humans – initially soldiers and explorers far from home, making their way through the Lustrian jungles until they were called upon by music only they could hear. None of them know how and wherefore they have come to the Masque’s grand stage. They only know that they must dance. Only in the dance is the Masque’s intent going to be revealed and Slaanesh’s will fulfilled – and so it must be perfect.\\n\\nBut just as it begins, so does a noisome and unlikely interruption occur. Or is it but another movement in the dance?...

Even among the savage tribes of the world, Slaanesh chooses his champions for subtlety, cunning and self-regard. Of those, one stands a cut above the rest. His magnetic presence made clansmen follow him even as a child – just as he himself followed the advice of a presence of a different sort, one who whispered in his ear the words of the Dark Prince himself. Those words led to the duel in which he killed his own father to become his tribe's chieftain... although the artfully premeditated nature of the challenge blurs the line between "combat" and "assassination".

Styrkaar of the Sortsvinaer may be a Norscan tribe chieftain, but his path in Slaanesh's service has always been governed by his individual verve. He has never missed an opportunity to single himself in battle, just as he singles out his strongest foes to then make short work of them, and bask in the praise and glory during the ensuing revels. However, in order to procure his personal services, one must prove capable of delivering slaughter on par with what he has achieved alongside his clansmen.

In these uncertain times, the guidance of the Creator God shall be crucial to the security of the realms. In the greatest struggles, it is the devoted guardians of Asuryan – the Phoenix Guard – who are always found where the fighting is the fiercest and the hardest victories are won. Thus an enduring display of our faith shall demonstrate that we are worthy of Asuryan’s strength through the Guard’s service.

The never-ending war takes a heavy toll. Though we have seen many great triumphs, the enemies of Ulthuan still descend upon our shores, intent on our annihilation. The recent construction of a new sanctum gives us the esteem to call upon the Creator God's purifying flames to help us scorch our enemies from the world.\\n\\nLet the Phoenix Guard march from their sacred battlements to drive forth Ulthuan’s will, as the very air above is set ablaze by the wings of phoenixes! A stately ceremony to call forth a stately Hero of divine strength, the living vessel of Asuryan’s Will – Caradryan, Captain of the Phoenix Guard.

With every enemy cut down by the halberds of Asuryan’s guardians, every glorious victory won by the sweat of the Phoenix Guard’s brows, the Asur shout praise to the Creator God. And while Asuryan's gaze still lingers, there is opportunity to invoke Him in ritual, promising us order, stability, and most of all, His strength made manifest. A stately ceremony to call forth a stately Hero of divine strength, the living vessel of Asuryan’s Will – Caradryan, Captain of the Phoenix Guard.

Shun the palace intrigues of Ulthuan if you will – they shall find you all the same. The foresighted Asur ever seeks to turn the machinations of the Phoenix Court toward their own vision of prosperity for the Ten Kingdoms.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The [[b]]Patrons of the Realms[[/b]] panel lets you view Patronage status and spend [[img:icon_influence]][[/img]]Influence to claim positions and their bonuses. It also tracks your [[img:icon_hef_favour]][[/img]]Favour of the Phoenix King, enabling the [[img:icon_confederation]][[/img]]confederation of other High Elf factions.[[/col]]

The jungles of Khuresh are a delightfully sordid locale for a carnival of excess, but it is lacking in certain basic luxuries. A genuine Palace of Pleasure is what this sweltering landscape requires. If nothing else, watching your Thralls work themselves to death might provide some amusement.

The rule of the Dragons is weak in the southern Hinterlands, and it will take only the slightest push for their population to stumble into your Dark Prince’s embrace. A dash of violence should be all it takes to upset the false façade of “Harmony” that the Dragons have cultivated here. You could conquer the lands by force, but think how much more delicious it would be to see the downtrodden peasants throw off their own chains?\\n\\nHow much freer they would be in your service. Entice them with a grand revel.

The tired opulence of your surroundings grows stale, the rank servility of your Thralls increasingly wearisome. It is difficult to believe that such things once amused you. Perhaps a change of scenery will sharpen the old sensations. Doubtless, some peon or other will be grateful for the so-called Palace you leave behind.

Your more "distinguished" underlings have been indulging their whims wherever they may lead – yet many of these lands are hostile to your flavour of disruptive merriment. Such harmonious, homogenous tedium can only be broken by a higher-pitched discordance. So, how about a new game to encourage things along?\\n\\nThe rules are simple: your agents can start trying harder, or they can find other, more excruciating ways in which to amuse you.

More and more, your agents in Cathay speak of three local worthies whose slavish commitment to order and harmony is buttressing their provinces against your influence. This is vexing. One should appreciate the novelty of the sensation, but as you know better than most, not all of life’s vicissitudes are made equal. It is time to pay these three a personal visit. And that, you think, you will enjoy.

Your glorious revel through the lands of Cathay have finally stirred the wrath of the Celestial Court. One day, perhaps, the Dragon Emperor's children will thank you for such a rare and heady gift, but for now, they express their gratitude with a mighty army. Too little, and too late. They come to restore their immortal master’s tyranny, but all they are going to restore is your stable of Thralls!

More and more you find yourself lost in contemplation of the trinket you rescued from its unappreciative former owners. Before you know it, hours have elapsed. Days. Weeks. Your Thralls mill about in confusion, then languish in their inaction. Your enthusiasm for the liberation of Cathay grows stale. What is time anyway, but a coin to be frittered away as you see fit. Your mind is awash with thoughts of a grand gallery dedicated to your glory, stocked to the beams with treasures like this one.\\n\\nAll you need do is clear a space for it. No matter that your Thralls are currently living there. They will not object to making room.

Rebellion in your halls! Your negligence, it seems, had consequences. Such an aggravating turn of events! A gaggle of self-important mortals have decided to "liberate" your Thralls. The wretched things have had the *gall* to consider the freedom you have bestowed upon them somehow not enough! Put them down, painfully. Remind them why no mortal can resist your terrible beauty, and reassert your dominance over these lands.

And thus is it ordained that the strife of the Four Brothers in Darkness spills forth into their mortal vassals, and no fealty sworn to any one aspect of Chaos shall remain unmarred by the vengeance of its eternal rival…

From the Norscan perspective, the first act of fanaticism differs little from the last – all unyielding, blood-drenched savagery in service to a ruinous power.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_point_2_gods}}\\n\\n{{tr:advice_info_texts_localised_text_war.camp.prelude.nor.gods.info_003}}
Purged of false idols and all faiths but the manifold ruin of Chaos, the trueborn Norscan reaver declares his devotion in blood – by challenging the chosen of each Dark God in turn.

Your Marauders speak of a feral tribe from Ursfjord in the far north, renowned for the bloodthirsty, berserker-like ferocity of their raids. They are the people of Beorg Bearstruck – the tribe of the Bear – whose warriors commonly sprout claws, snarling teeth, mane-like furs and bear-shaped muzzles, mutations most profoundly received by their indomitable chieftain Beorg himself. Allegedly, Beorg’s Great Hall has been deserted for some time – not unexpected, since Beorg’s legendary forays are known to take him far. Some Bearmen still raid nearby, however, and may welcome closer opportunities to pillage.

The legend of Beorg Bearstruck tells how he casts aside foes with ease, the great swipes of his claws knocking heads from shoulders and tearing arms from their sockets. Firsthand accounts from the Bearmen under your banner relate that above all else, Beorg despises the weakness of lesser leaders and is always restless, disinterested in the easy conquests among tribes of the north. A demonstration of indiscriminate violence is required if this renowned savage is to be convinced you are capable of greater things. Raid mercilessly, and the Bearmen will surely send word to their chieftain of your like-minded aspirations.

There is no shortage of volunteers amongst the Dolgan, and with each still-beating heart carved from a willing victim’s chest, you sense the currents of Chaos bend and shift, the eyes of powers greater than your own turning towards you.\\n\\nFor a moment, you glimpse the path into your future, some way of cheating the fate you have foreseen. But no sooner does it tease your mutated sights than it is flitting back to the murky realm from whence it came.\\n\\nOne thing, at least, is clear. You will need to build more Altars across your lands.

Your growing power has not gone unnoticed. It was only ever a matter of time before your guileless foes roused themselves against you, though you had been expecting it to come from closer to home.\\n\\nThe men of the west are no less susceptible to the whisperings of Chaos than those of the eastern plains.\\n\\nIt strikes you as unlikely that such a soft-bellied host would ever survive the journey across the Dark Lands, but crushing them would send a powerful message.

Chaos rises and you rise with it. *Your* Chaos. Self-service, not servitude. You have gained knowledge through any means possible, while those who sought to take it from you – or even the curious who came looking – have been disposed of.\\n\\nThe heart of Order cannot hold, while those who kill in Chaos' name are gnashing their teeth at the opportunity to loose a blood-dimmed tide upon the world. You will allow it, but only on your terms. They will object. But a night draws near where their violent protest will be quelled, and the Winds themselves will rise at your beck and call.

It is not unheard of for sharp-eyed children on the cliffs overlooking the Straits of Nagash to spy the bright sails of Eagle Ships on the Sea of Dread, gliding like demi-gods in glittering chariots between their Southland colonies and the rich trading ports of Ind and Cathay. But it is rare indeed for them to come ashore in this dark corner of the world.\\n\\nIt is in the Elven nature to presume to know what is best for mankind.\\n\\nThis time, it is they who will learn humility.

Before abandoning the world to the predations of the Chaos Gods, the Old Ones charged their mortal servants, the Lizardmen, with the care of their surviving works. The ordering of the Heavens. The proper workings of time. The shape of the globe itself. Or so you have gleaned from certain salvaged texts. Those ancient writers were surprisingly grudging in their admission of the Old Ones’ powers.\\n\\nThe power of your Chaos Altars must have grown beyond all measure, to have roused these cold-blooded guardians of the cosmic balance from their torpor.

A Druchii warband has landed off the coast of Nagarythe, attempting to fortify a string of small islands there. The Shadow Warriors who would ordinarily prevent such incursions are in disarray, following the Norscan raids, and there is worse: the mayhem has encouraged local cults of luxury to come out of hiding and side with the invaders. You will have to fight them all if you are to drive the Druchii from your shores and deny their invasion fleet this beachhead.

Chaos rises and you rise with it. Self-service, not servitude. You have gained knowledge through any means possible, while those who sought to take it from you – or even the curious who came looking – have been disposed of.\\n\\nThe heart of Order cannot hold, while those who kill in Chaos' name are gnashing their teeth at the opportunity to loose a blood-dimmed tide upon the world. You will allow it, but only on your terms. They will object. But a night draws near where their violent protest will be quelled, and the Winds themselves will rise at your beck and call.

Though Dechala delights in treating her mortal thralls with cruel nonchalance, she is driven to piques of rage as her domineering ways take their natural turn and, in the end, leaves those thralls for dead. In such moments, she roams the lands and seas in search for more with blind single-mindedness, taking anything she can get her many hands on. The unfortunates who have recently crossed her path are members of a High Elven island colony – whatever militants they can muster would surely be unable to deter her appetites.\\n\\nUnbeknownst to Dechala, however, someone else has laid eyes on her and would like to make [[i]]her[[/i]] the prize.

The Chimera's coruscating hide has trapped a veritable storm of Chaos. The triple-headed beast can barely contain it – and so it would seek to unleash these eldritch forces upon its foes. Whoever can withstand it has the victory half in hand.

Unstoppable though this loathesome creature may be in direct confrontation, it is the essence of the hunt to overwhelm it with numbers – and pray to the Dark Gods that the sacrifice made in the name of victory is not too harsh.

Through some cruel fluke, or maybe a facet of Tzeentch's inscrutable intent, this Cockatrice can turn its assailants into effigies of living stone. If this happens, can they take their vengeance and slay it before it shatters them at its whim? A battle full of savagery and guile awaits you.

The creature standing on the battlefield may not be the same one the hunters have set out to pursue… But it matters little. For all their superficial differences, Manticores always fight with ferocity to rival the tenacity of the opposing party.
With the monster now in sight,  well before battle is joined in the flesh, another will rage in the mind. Victory does not lie in sanity restored but on the other side of madness.

The Ghorgon sees no enemies – only meals. The only defeat it has experienced is the occasional slight indigestion. It is a harried, degenerate existence that belies the creature's power. And so it must end.

The beast's fury is plainly burned into the earth and the very air around it. Surely, it has never seen anything but red – but now so do its pursuers. Though fuelled by elemental fire, the monster is yet but flesh – and so it can be vanquished!
When in flight, the Preyton seems an affront to all that flies. When on land, it spites all earth-bound creatures. Only when it dies will it assume a form that brooks no disgust. So let it die!
Should the hunt fail now, surely the Ascendant's pride will be vindicated. But this is not this creature's legend, but that of its pursuers. And so he shall be but a chapter in it.

Bringing down the beast is something your warriors understand all too well, yet it would be a curiously double-edged challenge. Despite being monstrously large, it seems unaware of its size. If surrounded, it will lash out with the fear-filled ferocity of an infinitely smaller creature. Its actual strength makes this a terryfing prospect.

The pursuit has honed the Carrion Eater's appetite sufficiently. The hunters may now seem to it like mere morsels of flesh. Has it finally made a grave miscalculation as to who is the hunter and who is the hunted?

The beast has finally settled. Is it merely tired, or finally resolved to make its stand? Its noble mien may prompt one to sympathise with its plight… Yet the impulse must be resisted and exchanged for bloodlust to match The Wise One's roar!

The Daemonic forces are a constant threat all over the world. You travel far and wide, appearing where your aid is most needed, to push back the encroaching Chaos.\\n\\nNow it may be time to turn your attention back to your homeland, because corruption has started to grow roots around the White Tower of Hoeth.\\n\\nFinish your current task quickly! Saphery needs the counsel of the High Loremaster!

Most Trolls that trudge out of the wilds into your camp have simply looked to kill and eat whatever’s in front of them, not knowing who you are – so have been swiftly dispatched.\\n\\nGather enough Trollkin to prove a worthy leader to these creatures and have all Trolls join your armies!

Here in the north, only a city bound by the White Wolf's creed can stand as the Empire’s shield. Give us the means to let the faithful gather beneath Ulric’s gaze and make Middenheim a beacon that taunts the darkness.

The unquiet realms of the Old World, ever wracked by pitiless winds and stained with the blood of champions, have grown grimmer still through Archaon's ravages. Beneath Dorghar's hooves, lands far and wide lie trampled. By U'zuhl, kings both petty and grand lie slain. By the Eye of Sheerian, fates beyond recount are sealed into damnation.\\n\\nAnd yet you stand – defiant before the prophesied doom. The storm of ruin will be no more.\\n\\nThis shall be the end of the End Times!

From the yawning depths of the fort they come – striding, capering, shambling, and dancing – the minions of all four ruinous powers united in a single cause. {{tr:effect_bundles_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_episodes_chaos_invasion_fortress_chs}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_chaos_invasion_fortress_description_suffix}}

{{tr:effect_bundles_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_episodes_chaos_invasion_fortress_kho}} Every one of the bodies is headless, their flensed skulls cast upon an altar to the Blood God.\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_chaos_invasion_fortress_description_suffix}}

This edifice of otherworldly opulence exhudes elegance and cruelty in equal measure. {{tr:effect_bundles_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_episodes_chaos_invasion_fortress_sla}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_chaos_invasion_fortress_description_suffix}}

Spires and towers constantly writhe and burst from this bastion, only to be re-absorbed moments later. {{tr:effect_bundles_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_episodes_chaos_invasion_fortress_tze}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_chaos_invasion_fortress_description_suffix}}

Swaddled in marbled lichen, the ramparts of this noisome outgrowth bear little resemblance to fortifications. {{tr:effect_bundles_localised_description_wh3_dlc29_episodes_chaos_invasion_fortress_nur}}\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_chaos_invasion_fortress_description_suffix}}

“I have seen the Doom of Man. It is written in the stars, an omen borne upon the twin-tailed comet that blazed bright across the firmament. The barbarous tribes of the north will see it as a sign of their final victory...”\\n\\n[[i]]At long last, the moment of our vengeance is upon us.\\n\\nYou can torture a fly by pulling off its wings – and there is some pleasure to be had in that – but if you want it dead then there is no better way than stamping down hard on its fat, hairy body. The Empire is that struggling fly, and Altdorf that stubbornly fleshy middle. Break its walls, harvest its citizens, offer its Emperor to the Dark Gods, and replace its warmongering faith with one that will bring life, and joy, and the laughter of tiny Nurglings for aeons to come.\\n\\nFor Ethra and Ollos Glott, my brothers, who did no wrong in life.[[i]]
With Middenland united under his banner, Boris Todbringer steps into the legacy of his forebears, ready to claim the blade that has only ever answered to a true Count.

Middenheim is the first and last bulwark against Khazrak and the whatever else has come through in his wake from the Realms of madness. In the end that bulwark must stand tall. There the triumph of Ulric will come to pass. There the Drakwald will be made to rest easy at last.
The threat has revealed itself! Khazrak’s intentions are to stain the entire land and bring Middenland to its knees. Ride out to meet this threat head-on! For Middenland! For Ulric!

In dire times, men look to their gods for safety and aid, but the Wolf God does not protect those who are not willing to protect themselves. Ulric is the God of War, Winter and Wolves. His followers must prove their mettle before receiving his blessings.\\n\\nBy holding his flame in their hearts as they charge in to battle, they feel his strength flow through them. Seek out your foes, crush them in Ulric's name, and then you shall know his favour.

Khazrak has made a dire mistake this day. For one should never corner a Wolf! The assault on Middenland has united all its people with a single purpose: to find the Beastmen and burn their taint from the land.\\n\\nUlric's strength returns, his flame burns brighter, and once the Wolf God's flame begins to surge he will give his people what they want – a final confrontation with their hated foe.

As the old god of humanity, Ulric’s following across the Empire is widespread, deep-rooted, and for the most part, respected. Wielding the strength that faith in Ulric ignites within the hearts of men will be a great aid in our never-ending fight. As a first step, we must show our respect to Him in a meaningful way that will gain the support of His wolf-pelted clergy.

The worship of Ulric was well established long before Sigmar’s name was even known, and it was the High Priest of Ulric – known as the Ar-Ulric – who crowned Sigmar as the first Emperor. The current Ar-Ulric is Emil Valgeir, a fierce and unrelenting Priest whose support in war and battlefield fortitude is invaluable. Few states of the Empire other than Middenland possess the political and cultural gravitas to call him to their cause. If we can show our true dedication to the way of the Wolf, however, his support may well be garnered. Thus, we must fight, kill, and die alongside the Ar-Ulric’s most staunch followers, so that word may reach him of our battlefield endeavours.

Long did Nagash labour over Morikhane, the Black Armour, forging it from meteoric iron and lead. Over time it has become one with him, so that no other may even attempt to wear it. Yet not even this unholy artefact is impervious to the ravages of the eons – its physical form still requires rejuvenation.

The Mortis blade, known as Zefet-Nebtar, is a blade said to have once wounded Sigmar himself. Though bladework is distasteful to a supreme being such as Nagash, the weapon is fed by the death it inflicts. Feed it, and it shall repay the wielder with the strength to kill a thousandfold more to raise into your ranks.

With our shipyard established, the bloody business can now begin. Raid the seas, leave our foes sundered and despoiled, with contagions and pestilence left in our wake. Show Gutrot he is among equals, that we both wish to sweep through the weak and reap the lives of those who attempt to resist. That all is done in the name of Grandfather Nurgle, to Him go the accolades, and the rewards!

Since its creation, Otto's instrument of the harvest has toiled the fields for many a year. It has cleaved and reaped the life borne from the fields in service to life's continuance. But to achieve the recognition of Nurgle, flesh and bone must be rent asunder by its blade. Only once it is coated with blood, pus, and all manner of other vital essences will it receive the full blessings of Nurgle, and then, His work may begin in earnest.

The Drakwald Forest stifles the Glottkin’s suppurating onslaught – their descent upon the civilised world slowed to a blundering crawl amidst the predation of ancient foliage. Confounded by this unforeseen obstacle, the Brothers Glott vent their fury in futile, aimless felling. Yet Nurgle's blessing extends well into the lightless groves, ordaining their encounter with the Beastmen horde – led by a peculiar shaman calling himself [[i]]the Harbinger[[/i]].\\nHe recognises in the triplets the Champions of the Urfather, as fire-told by the Crowfather beneath Morrslieb's baleful glow. Omen-bound, he pledges fealty and guides them along the forest's unseen paths. But the giant oaks grow ashen with spidersilk, gravid with cocooned corpses. And the true challenge rears its chittering, many-eyed head...
