Much like Djaf himself, the death god's priesthood were pragmatic in their bleak devotions. They knew well how to pique Settra's interest with promises of power purchased through copious bloodshed – for their eternal sovereign was unmatched in his appetite for conquest, and such hunger accorded well with slaughter.\\n\\nHunched in supplication, the shrouded cult promised Settra armour of peerless splendour, once worn by the jackal-headed deity when he walked the mortal lands. The panoply would be yielded only beneath a mound of corpses so towering that, in the harsh hours when Ptra glowers at his zenith, a whole army might rest in its shade…

In an age long past, a newly crowned Settra restored the benevolence of the harsh Desert Gods towards a waning Nehekhara by rebuilding their golden temples and erecting statues of great magnificence in their honour. Yet all paled beside his final sacrifice, for in a grand ritual of devotion, he bled his own children in their name.\\n\\nNow, millennia have passed, and cruel fates have reshaped the Great Land many times over – but the heavens attend Settra still. Knowing this, he plans to enact another of the great rites that define this realm of charnel splendour. By intoning the Great Incantation of Geheb – lion-headed patron of warriors – his priests shall draw forth the scuttling servants of Usirian too, bearing with them a great gift promised by the lord of the Underworld!

Without a proper harbour, Gutrot Spume will give us as much scrutiny as a fleeting minnow, unworthy of notice or thought, continuing his hunt in search of larger creatures along the Sea of Claws. If we wish to gain his allegiance, we must first gain his attention. Once he deems us worthy of his recognition, we will then require ships. Fortunately, we can work towards both of these goals through the construction of a shipyard.

[[i]]The one called Spume is a seafarer without equal. A warrior with a pride borne of a youth spent slaying creatures with nought but a knife, and his arrogance equalled only by his strength. If we desire to draw him to us, to our cause, we must first construct a harbour that we may sail from. Beyond that, our brutality must be unleashed along the coast in a manner that leaves no room for doubt, and no gaps for weakness.[[/i]]

With our shipyard established, the bloody business can now begin. Raid the seas, leave our foes sundered and despoiled, with contagions and pestilence left in our wake. Show Gutrot he is among equals, that we both wish to sweep through the weak and reap the lives of those who attempt to resist. That all is done in the name of Grandfather Nurgle, to Him go the accolades, and the rewards!

[[i]]Actions, not words, are what Gutrot Spume heeds and respects. He seeks only to prove himself to the Urfather, a cause none would dare question, even for the briefest moment. To prove ourselves, we have a target. Our goal must be worthy of Gutrot Spume's strength. Though his arrogance is towering and unwavering, his strength cannot be denied. We must assault our foes and despoil their lands, let our deeds be undeniable![[/i]]
The insolence of this one lurking at our doorstep! Far all his claims to greatness, Nagash's lowly mind is plain to see. His agent will meet a fittingly ignoble fate.
One of Nagash's pawns skulks nearby. The temerity, to think their tyrant's will can protect them! They shall learn that Undead might does not come from blind servitude!
We cannot abide this nothingness Nagash has forced upon our eyes! Claim it and rebuild lest he forces it upon our own as well!
This "Land of the Dead" will no longer be his, but ours! Everything Nagash creates in his image must be unmade so the rest of us may thrive!
Our will to war is the only thing which can withstand Nagash's will to supremacy. He will learn once more his supremacy is a sham!
Nagash expects to cow us into servitude. War is our only choice! Doom is our only alternative!
A "champion" of Nagash! Such a vile thing to behold, even from afar! Would we be as they are? Never! Their illusion of supremacy will be shattered in battle!
A harbinger of him whom we deny to our core! This creature and its mindless rabble are an affront to all Undead with their wits still about them! Fell the leader and the rest will crumble!
Nagash's shadow will not fall upon our this land! His pawns have no place in the mortal world!
Nagash seeks to turn our lands into a wasteland. For centuries we've strived to carve out our domain, and just as long we shall fight for it!
Fight back against the legions of undeath, lest you find yourself fighting alongside them!
We will not waste our immortality on slaving for a tyrant who would make us nothing more but hollow shells! We'd rather face oblivion fighting!
Strike back at them! Nagash cares not for anything we have sought to create so we shall claim what is his!
We must reclaim the source of that which makes us immortal, little by little, else Nagash's voracity will know no bounds!
Leave nothing, and let Nagash be damned to nothing, too! If it is true that all in his domain is a part of him, he shall be made lesser!
All places which Nagash has cursed with his presence contain a piece of him! We shall tear out this piece then, until nothing is left for us to feel his presence in our minds!
This creature has taken upon itself to prove some sort of worth by standing in your way. It is not even worth dealing with it personally. An Undead lackey will suffice to cease its existence.

The dead of this place call for release from their tombs. The living cry out in terror at your looming shadow. Living and dead shall both find brief release from terror and tomb before you shackle their souls.
A lesser being has been filled with pathetic arrogance, surrounded by its war-rabble. Your legions will be both its death and the start of its servitude.
This deluded cattle has strayed into the path of your legions. Death will dispel their delusion before they are ushered into unlife.
This land is overripe with life. Ruin is the only remedy. Afterwards, this will be a dwelling of death and silence.
The abodes of this flesh will be dust. The dust will sow the fields and pave the paths, to prepare them for more fitting crop and trade.

Nurgle often favours the smallest beings to complete His work. But they must first be crafted for purpose, and brought into being to lay our enemies low! These contagions must be concocted with precise care, for too easily they may ravage a population, leaving no living creatures to spread to.

[[i]]We, who are blessed, still seek the doting affections of the Grandfather. To do otherwise would be folly. Life is devotion, and life that begets death purely, is devotion in a most pure form. That is what must be cultivated, must be sought by Nurgle's most faithful servants, so that the cycle continues, enduring and uninterrupted. The first step is clear. Cultivate a garden worthy of the Urfather's foetid grandeur![[/i]]

Once ready and crafted to the exacting demands of the Urfather, the contagion may be unleashed. Though, in truth, most plagues are unleashed by their own noxious nature, or by the overeager disciples of Nurgle himself. We may hope that our disease spreads without the need for intervention, but its care will fall to us in any event.

[[i]]With the garden flourishing before our nurturing touch, the loving caress of Nurgle can reach further than ever before. True strength comes from the flourishing, from the proliferation of life and death that follows, or indeed, death, and the life that follows. Plague is a pure expression, and a plague the epitome of life, so to spread it unquestioningly and unceasingly is devotion of a most sacred order.[[/i]]

Nurglings are the true and numerous faithful of Nurgle, the embodiment of His love of life in all its forms. Swell the ranks of Nurgle's armies with them! Let them not be denied for their size, but hailed for their devotion, and may they profligate far and wide! For the benevolent Urfather!

[[i]]Nurgle loves the small and large creatures of the world alike. It is the worm, the locust, the Rot Fly that thrive in the mires that fill his gardens. Nurglings too, teem in their countless hordes, spawned from his greatest servants. The creatures borne from Nurgle's own foul sickness must be at the forefront of His tide of maladies. Though weak by themselves, they are those who most gleefully delight in Nurgle's profligacy. Swell the ranks, and let the Urfather's children swarm over our enemies![[/i]]

To prove the strength of our devotion to the Urfather, our warriors, esteemed with blight, must wade into the tides of life and begin their reaping. None must be spared in the cause of rebirth. Let the soil suppurate with rot and filth, let our devotion be unquestionable, and let allies gather, eager to serve before the cause of Nurgle!

[[i]]As is the nature of life, most accumulations of living beings follow their own rules for existence. Long has nature been allowed to flourish unheeded. But now we must focus our vile efforts, and harness only the strongest of Nurgle's servants to achieve his putrid aims. The Blightkings must be our focus, to the detriment to all others.[[/i]]

A tittering grotesquerie must descend upon the meek in a tumbling, prodding avalanche of portly daemon-flesh. Wherever the daemon-mites rake their spindly fingers, ichor shall ooze from fungi-mottled flesh and crust shall flake from rust-pitted iron. Reeling in loathing at its own corruption, the mortal realm shall be moulded into forms more pleasing to the Urfather – a spectacle to be marked by His drool-fiend riders.

The mould-pocked horns of the maggoth tamers crest the horizon. From the frigid hem of the world they descend, and with each gash we tear into the goosefleshed south, they grow closer. Still, their countenances – indiscernible beneath weeping sores and folds of flaccid flesh – exude a silent scorn at the sight of soil unfed by offal and palisades unwashed in blood.\\nWe must strive for the favour of such fearsome warriors.

In the frozen north, disparate champions fabled for their putrid resilience thrive as a loose brotherhood of rot. Now, an oppressive, slate-green firmament portends the end of their aimless reaving. We must harness the strength of the Urfather's brood – channel their gruesome deeds into a singular deluge of corruption – that we might lure champions mightier still.

[[i]]Atop seven towers swaddled in grave-moss, the plaguebearers shall clank the rough call of the leper-bells, and bubonic swarmers beyond recount will gladly answer their summons. Spurred by the procession, a thick cloud of rot-flies shall buzz upon the wind, thus coaxing the slug-beasts into a joyous sloshing amid ankle-deep puddles of ammoniac slime.\\nSuch obscene jubilee heralds the maggoth riders.[[/i]]

Inside the crucible of a screaming foundry, the Grey Seers will bring their revered Skreech Verminking – thought by many to be the living embodiment of the Horned Rat himself – into corporeal being. With his rise shall all Skavenkind follow, to victory and far beyond. A Bell Foundry will be needed to summon him to the mortal world.

You must enact the Rite of the Thirteenth Scheme, for if it remains fractured, disunited and without common purpose, Skavenkind will instinctively work against itself and towards its own doom. Before the Horned God, you must not allow that to happen... under [[i]]any[[/i]] circumstances.

It is only through battle that Skavenkind's foes will be defeated utterly. Yet victory after victory is required for the Horned Rat to notice and gift your struggle with not just any Verminlord, but the peerless, matchless Rat King himself, Skreech Verminking. You must win many battles to achieve this end.

In ages beyond recount, Arkhan was the primary architect of the coup that swept Nagash into power, and was greatly rewarded for his service. Arkhan cared not. Hitherto, his had been a petty and unremarkable life, marked by dissolution and thuggery. Nagash had granted him glory and purpose, and these bind Arkhan to his master’s side tighter than riches or enchantments ever could. Only his demise – utter and final – could tear him away from the tyrant to whom he is sworn.

There are few who walk the world before whom Dieter Helsnicht would bow. Nagash is, without a question, foremost among them. Helsnicht has spent his whole life, an unnaturally long one at that, seeking forbidden knowledge. Doubtless, the awestruck Doom Lord bent his knee to the progenitor of the dark arts at the first opportunity. For that reason, and countless others besides, he must die.

Centuries after Krell's first death, Nagash communed with the warlord’s vengeful spirit and offered him an eternity of battle. Thus did Krell forsake Khorne and pledge unswerving fealty to Nagash. Krell hears the Great Necromancer's voice with a clarity matched by none save Arkhan the Black, and he obeys his master without hesitation. Only a second and final death can silence such a mindless butcher.

Although tinged with the lunacy that had afflicted him for centuries, Luthor Harkon had risen to become the self-proclaimed Pirate King of the Vampire Coast. Yet for all his madness, Harkon willingly bowed before the great master of death upon Nagash’s return – though sheer boredom played no small role in his obeisance. A madman who does not fear death is a dangerous and unpredictable foe; one best sent to the bottom of his beloved sea.

Foolishly believing in the supremacy of his own will, Mannfred scorned the subtle manipulations of Nagash. Not once did the Vampire suspect that he was walking a path the Great Necromancer had laid out for him. Now Mannfred resents his servitude and is ever watchful for a means to free himself. One so arrogant and evil to the marrow deserves but one freedom – his destruction.

Deep in the Grey Mountains lurked the spirit of a once-great enchanter. Raw power endured within that broken spirit, though a recent defeat had shattered its mind. It pledged itself to Nagash on one condition: that the Great Necromancer restore its lost memories and make it Nameless no more. Take no pity upon this parasitic creature, which knows no existence beyond cruelty and vile indulgence.

Neferata, Mistress of the Silver Pinnacle, hates Nagash – but fears him even more, and obeys him without question. The Great Necromancer himself wrote the books from which she learned the secret of eternal life. While Vampires have proven useful to Nagash in the past, they had also failed the Great Necromancer often enough that Neferata knows well the price of his displeasure. Her millennia-spanning web of deception must be undone.

A monster of contradictions as numerous as his deaths, Vlad von Carstein was restored by Nagash after a death born of treachery. He now stalks the land as one of the nine Mortarchs. Vlad serves not out of loyalty, but in the hope of being reunited with his beloved Isabella, whose spirit somehow never joined his in the hereafter. Bring his sorrowful tale at last to its end.

Walach Harkon, first of the Blood Dragons, saw in the service of Nagash only an opportunity for glorious battle – and seized it without hesitation. Even amongst his dark allies, Walach is known as a brute who cloaks a barbarian’s bloodthirsty whims in lofty notions of honour and renown. Yet Nagash seeks a world of sterile obedience, an end utterly opposed to Walach’s hunger for martial glory. Let him ponder the contradiction in death.

Heed, you that yet live, Nagash's ghastly verdict borne dry upon the Wind of Death. The dead felled by mortal blades may yet rise again – but such dark arts drain the mind and consume the spirit, even one as vast as his.\\n\\nRide now in mad pursuit across the desiccated realms, and hurl all your might against the Great Necromancer!\\n\\nFor if you fail, all creation shall wilt under his command – and souls, fettered, shall bend unto his will – until nought is left but legions of the dead, who rasp one name alone:\\n[[b]]N A G A S H[[/b]]

Arkhan the Black. The first and most loyal of Nagash’s servants and the only one, in the four thousand years of his existence, to willingly give his life for him. Mortality is no longer a concern, for either of them, but such devotion deserves to be rewarded – with an eternity of servitude at Nagash’s right hand.\\n\\nIt appears that Arkhan has used Nagash’s long absence to somewhat accommodate the ancient dynasties of Nehekhara, but surely he remains his most faithful acolyte. Irrefutable proof of the Supreme Lord of Undeath’s resurrection, through the expansion of his Black Pyramid settlement, will surely bring the Vizier of Khemri back to his side.

It is time to address the one power in Nehekhara that could conceivably oppose Nagash’s rise. By long tradition, whomever rules in Khemri rules over all the kings of the Great Land. Settra has held that title since he returned Nehekhara’s to its former glory. For a time, however, it was Nagash, the firstborn son of King Khetep of Khemri. Yet the Priest Kings managed to defy him, uniting Nehekhara to drive him to exile. Not this time.\\n\\nAlone amongst the ancient kings, Settra paid true homage to the old desert gods. He sacrificed his own children in exchange for their favour, but the gods’ time in this world is coming to an end, for even they cannot protect Settra from Death itself.

Khemri may be the City of Kings, but Nagashizzar has always been the true seat of Nagash’s power. Carved out of the mountain of Cripple Peak by the tireless labour of the Undead, it is one of the mightiest fortresses in the entire world. Within its vast catacombs, untold legions of Undead await their master’s return. The Warpstone mines stand ready to be exploited once again.\\n\\nIt was to Nagashizzar that Nagash retreated, after the Priest Kings of old drove him from his lands, and it was to Nagashizzar that his spirit returned each time it made its way back from the Realm of Souls. From its accursed walls, his rise will once again be unassailable.

Nagash’s Staff of Power, Alakanash, stores within it a deep reservoir of Dark Magic. With it in hand, Nagash’s powers are increased ten-fold. An artefact of such potency cannot be wielded by any petty mage that chances upon it, however. Even Arkhan, his greatest acolyte and its custodian for a thousand years, barely scratched the surface of its potential. To wield it fully, so soon after resurrection, is a risk he dare not take.\\n\\nOnce he has drawn upon the winds of death to strengthen both his legions and his own resurrected form, all that was once his shall be his to wield again.

Whatever Mannfred von Carstein lacks in obedience, he makes up for in animal cunning. His excellence in trickery may yet prove useful. However Mannfred and the Vampire Counts may rail against domination. His hunger for the knowledge and the power Nagash possesses will forever bind his will to him. As Nagash recovers his Books and reopens the ancient chambers of the Black Pyramid, Mannfred will inevitably come to him and prove a useful vassal in his domination of the northern lands.

Death cures all foibles and frailties. There is no greater demonstration of this truth than Krell. Once a Champion of the Chaos Gods, his death, and subsequent resurrection at Nagash’s hand, remade him into the perfect undying warrior. Krell has, nevertheless, retained a certain mortal passion for bloodshed and battle. Since his resurrection, he has been content to slaughter his way through the Grey Mountains – but he will always come to where the greatest battles are being fought. It is time for the weapon to return to its maker’s hand. The Black Axe will be his again.

Casting a spell over the entire world requires a prodigious amount of magical power. More than Alakanash could siphon and channel. More than even Nagash’s Undead form could contain for long. It is no coincidence that Nagashizzar sits upon the greatest deposit of Warpstone in the world. It is the very essence of magic, condensed and solidified, of which there are vast reservoirs in the rocks beneath his fortress – provided he can remove enough of it from the ground. In times past, Nagash allowed the Skaven a minute supply of the Warpstone in exchange for their services in extracting it. Despite their short lives and treacherous natures, the rat-men were ingenious miners. Much of their bizarre machinery remains in the lowest levels.

As the Lands of the Dead expand, so is ever more of its Dark Magic drawn into the Black Pyramid at its lifeless heart, and so too does Nagash’s own power grow. He is close to the heights of his former strength now, but still not close enough. All things must be exact. There is no room for error. Only when the accursed reservoir is full and the mystic Sigils are saturated with enough energy, can the Great Ritual commence at last.

The ominous passage of the Black Pyramid across the Lands of the Dead and towards Nagashizzar has not gone unnoticed by the so-called powers of the world. The sands of Nehekhara themselves simmer in fury at the sight.\\n\\nThe prospect of eternal oblivion has spurred the mortal world to action. Banners all across the strongholds of Order rear up and come together. The collossal amounts of magic leaking from the Black Pyramid have raised the Chaos Gods’ attention to a towering cacophony – and one mandate alone. Others move unseen – malicious skittering shadows. Their goal is the only thing they share. They will share neither common ground in this struggle, nor gratitude should they succeed – more enmity is all that awaits thereafter.\\n\\nThey will have none of that regardless. There will be no thereafter.

Over years of prodigious rule at Castle Drakenhof, Vlad has proven himself a lord of the undeath most alike to Nagash, his eternal master. His error was in treating the mortal kine as a flock that might be protected. They cannot be controlled. Only death can spare them from their own weakness. From the moment Neferata of Lahmia attempted to recreate Nagash’s Elixir of Life, the Vampire lines have straddled the border between life and death.\\n\\nVlad is stubborn, arrogant, wrathful. He has always sought lordship over an aristocracy of Undeath and would surely accept vassalage under Nagash in exchange for such a title. Nagash must remind him of his absolute rule over the creatures of the night. The first of the Vampire Counts will serve him to the bitter end.

A broken tool can still be of use. Luthor Harkon’s ambition may have far outstripped his powers, but he is not the first immortal to overreach. The would-be King of Lustria may be mad, but of all the Vampires that still stalk the night, there are few of more powerful bloodlines. He may not remember his sire, but Nagash remembers him.\\n\\nExpand the Land of the Dead into the jungles of Lustria, and the Mad King's broken mind will inevitably succumb to Nagash. If anyone can compel his fractured personalities to serve, it is the Supreme Lord of Undeath. Once he is firmly in his service, the Lizardman relics he has spent decades plundering from the Lustrian interior will be Nagash’s, as will his mighty flagship. All will be invaluable in the final preparations for the Great Ritual.

Neferata's talents at mastering secrets - both magical and mundane - far surpassed those of all her contemporaries. Still, she was a secret mistress of a land whose full glory had begun to wane, for Nagash had passed from it and still had not returned. Being enamoured with subterfuge and intrigue was another failing of hers, which dimmed the dark glory of her accomplishment: the Elixir of Life, such as she was able to concoct it.\\n\\nThe Vampiric bloodlines she created, however, proved powerful and pliable. They realised free will was never a choice, as did Neferata, though she railed against it. When that proved fruitless, she hid. Hiding shall not avail her now. Vampires will serve Nagash again, and she will be the tool to bring about their servitude.

Khazrak One-Eye stands before Middenheim’s gates. The elusive brayherd of the One-Eye is now fully committed to the assault, reinforced by Daemons pouring forth from the Realms of Chaos. Though it appears to be a dire situation, this is the opportunity Boris Todbringer has been waiting for – a final confrontation with his most hated foe.\\n\\nTodbringer's faith in Ulric has been unshaken and now he is being rewarded. Ulric's flame roars beneath the Ulricsberg, but it burns just as fiercely within Boris' heart. Ride out to battle, free the Drakwald of this Chaos taint, and show Middenland to be stronger than it has ever been before!

Usually, little can disturb Boris Todbringer’s fixation on the Beastmen terrorising his land. Yet the day brings news of bestial terrors perpetrated by once lawful subjects of the Empire. Mere lawless urges would not explain it – there have been no signs. A clear impression of what came to pass is impossible – there have been no survivors to provide it. The only thing in evidence is that it has been escalating.\\nBut where others’ blood has run cold at the missive, the blood of Boris has kindled.

Amid the scalding heat of hissing steam engines, giant bellows sputtered like the lungs of a Red Pox victim, their wheezing an uneven countdown to Thanquol's long-denied triumph. He needed to hold out a little longer. Just a little longer. Even now, the Engine's three-pronged muzzle seemed to gape straight at Morskrit, the Warp Moon, every hollow in its pocked surface tantalising him with the promise of a boundless trove.\\n\\nRendered in pigments of distilled Warpstone, the sickly green runes along the engine’s length blazed in harsher contrast, as the nearing conflagrations of war cast their dull glare across its grimy barrel. Bloodied but undeterred, the remaining forces of the surface races had rallied in a last-ditch effort to foil Thanquol's masterpiece.\\n\\nFool-fools! They would be first upon the warp-flame pyre!

The gloaming sky hung low over the man-thing warrens, and soon gave way to a night of malign purpose. Thanquol's incompetent lackeys scuttled nearer, and sweetly did he sniff at air grown heavy with the musk of their fear.\\n\\nThirteen rats were fed into the warp-brazier in supplication to the Horned Rat, that He might bless the Screaming Bell at the Grey Seer's command – and now the unholy runes blazed with favourable green-black flame! Above, the bronze dome yearned to toll its thirteen-stroke peal, a clangourous herald to an incarnation of the Great Horned One… It yearned for the Verminking!

Neferata's purpose has finally achieved the heights of her mastery of blood and magic. Now Lahmia, the dream, has become but one more step to take. The sacrifices she has made along the way were hardly hers, but those who suffered from them will hound her all the way to her goal like mad dogs. Her blood ritual which undid Lahmia's wards has awakened the fury of vengeful mortals and mercenaries who would gladly carry out that vengeance for a price. Khalida will no doubt permit their trespass of her realm, to let them do some of the work she no longer has the strength to do alone. Once, Neferata's dream of Lahmia may have been distant, but Khalida's was always dead. It is time for it to die for good and be reborn in blood.

A recent addition to Neferata's retinue of Handmaidens has warned her mistress of a Bretonnian Lord more brave than shrewd, who has convinced himself of "vile, seductive Vampires" wreaking silent havoc on his lands. His holy quest is now begun, in the name of the Lady of the Lake.\\nNeferata is uncharacteristically eager to accept his challenge... for she believes not a word of the tale. Whatever the truth, Aken-Seth, her Staff of Pain, will henceforth thrum with the agony she will inflict. And it may well not be the agony of that dim-witted Bretonnian.

The Verminking is a creature crawled from nightmare – towering and imperious despite its hunched posture, casting a shadow impossibly long and impenetrably dark. Beneath its one-eyed gaze, the surface world still seems so frail – little more than a pallid silhouette of infernal green by looming Morrslieb.\\n\\nA rat daemon of such magnitude is never truly cornered.

A trail of theft, treachery, and gruesome murder leads to a horrifying glimpse of an impending Skaven invasion. The deeper you pry into the verminous schemes, the more of their vile design shall be revealed.

An Economic Plan has failed and your Underling's efforts were discovered! The resources will still be in the region, available for the taking, but you need to act fast – conquer the region to receive your rewards!

Loathsome and stubborn are the Dwarf-things, and being chosen by the Council of Thirteen to seize-breach one of their bulwarked warrens was a disagreeable task indeed, thought Thanquol. Yet he surveyed Zhufbar all the same, his beady eyes glistening with ill-contained greed and the crapulence of warp-stuff.\\n\\nHe watched the crater lakes atop the mountain disgorge glacial waters, cascading ear-splittingly along the canyon walls. A webwork of water wheels and drop hammers harnessed that terrible might to feed the Dwarfs' countless forge-fires, aglow like jewels along the chasm floor. Such power could be put to far greater use… [[i]]yes-yes[[/i]].\\n\\nInnumerable cannons lined the walls, their brass-clad throats gaping in grim deterrence of such ambition. Much better to slip-strike from below! For the Dwarf-thing tunnels yet stood – defiant of the ravages of age – but Zhufbar’s throng had dwindled, and untended, the protective runes had waned.

Thanquol knew, of course, that his swift deployment by the Council reeked of hidden designs – but waiting for them to show their true hand was not a strategy conducive to survival. How fortuitous, then, that he was a prodigious sorcerer as well as a peerless schemer, and had devoted many hours by warp-glow to the furtive arts of scrying.\\n\\nHe knew well the complex verses. Intoned over forbidden warp-daubings, with the throats of thirteen Skavenslaves opened over a pool of blackest sheen, they would offer a rare glimpse into the yet-pliant future.\\n\\nA ritual of such complexity demanded Warpstone – [[i]]much[[/i]] Warpstone – and that, in turn, required the execution of shrewd stratagems and meddlesome rivals, in about equal measure.

Skryre was a clan of tinkerers, to be sure-sure, but lacking a Grey Seer's visionary approach made their doom-failure inevitable. Best to strategically reassign their ill-fated designs to a true mastermind, one clearly favoured by the Great Horned One. But how?\\n\\nEven simple provocation could work, sneered Thanquol. The inventors had so fattened with riches selling their contraptions to squabbling warlords that, behind their backs, whispers had begun to circulate among the other Great Clans about their complacency.\\n\\nNo one would dare accuse them openly, of course, for fear of being reduced to ash by a warp-beam, but Skryre pride had grown… prickly. So thin-furred had they become that a brazen brute-strike might provoke the clan to a disproportionate muster, leaving a gnaw-hole open for a sneak-slip into their laboratories…

Despite the incessant tinkering of the Warlock Engineers, they were no strangers to the vying that underpinned Skaven society – they had merely dragged it into their workshops. Warp-ductors "malfunctioned" to vapourise the inattentively ambitious. Flame-paths were "miscalculated" to engulf lesser schemers. Why not, then, a discreet "misrouting" of access tunnels to the warp-forges?\\n\\nThanquol was certain that, with a little prodding, he would find no shortage of ambitious rat-ificers eager to take a stab at the Lord-Warlock. Scrounging up a bribe sufficient for this temporary shift in loyalties was another matter. Indeed, love and respect were concepts utterly foreign to the Skaven mind, but between the withering glare of his warp-lenses and the metallic scrape of his augmented voice, Lord Morskittar commanded fear aplenty among Skryre’s lesser rats.\\n\\nA profit-scheme of the most treacherous kind was needed...

From aboard a disguised shanty-skiff, Thanquol observed the lopsided streets and canals of Skavenblight, sniffing the foetid air with growing trepidation. The capital squirmed under the imposing shadow of the Great Temple of the Horned Rat, as a gnarled finger of decrepit marble outstretched in constant reminder of the Grey Seers’ divine authority over all lesser clans.\\n\\nMuch of that sway was now in question, however, for profiteers like Skryre and Moulder had taken over huge swathes of the districts, and both clans resented the horned sorcerers.\\n\\nAs the vessel plied the turbid waters ever deeper into the engineers’ quarter, Thanquol bristled at the invisible hatred, a thousand pinprick eyes at his back. No lackey could be trusted. Tonight, he would personally lay his paws on the plan-prints for the Morskittar Engine!

Surely the Warp Moon glowered favourably upon Thanquol that night, for he scurried unscathed from the disaster at Skavenblight and, with a well-spent underling gambit, spirited the schematics beyond the pursuing guard-rats.\\n\\nThat, however, was where his good fortune ended. Despite his best efforts to seal snouts shut with threats and bribes, even Thanquol harboured no delusion that a trail of squealed admissions would not soon lead incensed Clan Skryre straight to him. At the mere thought of an entire Great Clan sniff-sniffing for his tail, he unwittingly let loose the musk of fear.\\n\\nLater, as he soothed himself with Warpstone, the whispers returned – and scratched a path to salvation. Once, Clanrats dared not look a Grey Seer in the eye, lest they incurred the displeasure of the Great Horned One. It was time the vermin-kind were reminded of their place.\\n\\nHe was to summon a Verminlord.

To everyone's surprise but his own, Thanquol had summoned a being ascendant even among his terrible kind: the Verminking himself. Now, goaded by the Grey Seer’s ambition and cowed by the domineering presence that shadowed him, the Skaven clans were driven to levels of cooperation unseen in many ages.

The frenzied lashes of Mors' overseers snapped the vat-swollen mutants of Moulder into precision as they strained beneath massive cogwheels. The nascent mechanism groaned in answer, sluggishly aligning with coordinates calculated by Skryre engineers. As each cog juddered into place, phosphorescent bile brewed by the Pestilens priesthood sloshed in glass vats deep within the apparatus’ entrails.\\n\\nAll this effort, and more still, was needed to knot together the rat-tail tangle of a construct that would anchor Thanquol's brazen shot at the Warp Moon.

The mere prospect of chancing upon the ginger-furred madman on the battlefield set Thanquol’s glands tightening. Yet jeopardising a work so costly and grand as the Morskittar Engine would risk the simmering resentment of the Great Clans, kept in check thus far by Skreech's absolute authority.\\n\\nWorse, such negligence would invite the wrath of the Verminking himself, and the Grey Seer did not much care to be unmade from the fabric of reality by the dark majesty's touch. Pressed between a rat and a hard axe, the horned sorcerer had no choice but to muster a tide of fur-filth and bleed the vengeance of the surface-dwellers before it could gather into a greater host.

The effects of Warpstone upon mortal flesh are morbidly fascinating – destructive and transmutative in myriad inexplicable ways. Cunning and malevolent to the marrow, Thanquol could not help but catalogue such delightful metamorphoses and distil their most beneficial manifestations into the gem stolen from his old master.

Nostalgic for his days as a Grey Seer initiate, Thanquol would regularly pinch a pocketful of Warpstone from his own coffers – then inflict horrific punishments upon his “inattentive” lackeys.\\nYet a darker impulse altogether makes him crave it in ever greater quantities – and ever more refined…

Helman Ghorst was driven to madness when plague claimed his father and brothers. Obsessed with restoring them, he delved into Necromancy and became a master of the dark arts. Now he rides a Corpse Cart through the night, his reanimated kin dragging him onward in a grim parody of family devotion. With the right incentives, he and his dead-raising talents could be put towards a much greater purpose.

Heinrich Kemmler, the dreaded Lichemaster, sought to transcend mortality through Necromancy, commanding vast armies of the dead. Broken by rival sorcerers, he wandered in ruin until a dark pact restored his power. Now renewed, Kemmler spreads terror and destruction in exchange for more forbidden might – a vocation clearly best served in your ranks once his fealty is gained.

After Vlad's death, the cunning Mannfred von Carstein avoided Sylvania's feuds and sought forbidden Necromantic lore across Nehekhara, Lahmia and Nagashizzar. Returning more powerful than ever, he claimed leadership of the Undead. Though defeated at Hel Fenn, legends persist that Mannfred survived and still covets the Imperial throne, yet surely he can be turned to more worthwhile pursuits.

Neferata, the first and greatest of Vampires, retains the beauty, cunning and cruelty that once made her Queen of Lahmia. From a mountaintop palace, she rules through spies and secret agents, weaving intricate schemes while awaiting the day she can reclaim Lahmia and restore its former glory. In light of your ever-growing presence in the world, it should not take much to convince her of the futility of her pursuits, and to add her strength to yours.

Vlad von Carstein, first and greatest of Sylvania's Vampire Counts, forged an Undead kingdom through guile, sorcery and conquest. At his side stood Isabella von Carstein, noble, cruel and fiercely devoted. Together they spread the curse of vampirism and raised mighty armies, with the potential to become the Old World’s most feared power. Yet the only way they will ever come anywhere near such a feat shall be in your shadow, and second to you.

What was most predictable has come to pass, as always. Some wilful Vampires, not realising themselves dim reflections of Neferata herself, have shown themselves subservient to the laws of lowly beasts. Utterly regrettable.\\nIf fangs and claws are what they think proves strength, this is what she will prove. Dim reflections are not meant to be polished but broken. The bleeding edges also have something of Neferata's true face to them.

Neferata has charted all paths into a Vampire's mind. The map of their pride and arrogance is simple to read. Von Carstein's get must all be "kings", truer than any other, though they have no throne and wear no crown. The Blood Dragons – mere guardian dogs like Abhorash their father, gone rabid yet still barking to their own facile commands. The Necrarchs of W'Soran, Nagash's faithful scribe, with some of his wit and none of his wile. The Strigoi's maze of madness and their simple-minded thirst for vengeance, so easily steered. The Lahmians, Neferata's own, are the only ones without fault, for they are hers.\\nTheir blood's strength all came from hers. She herself bears the name of their weakness, the sun. In weakness and strength, they serve Neferata.

Long ago, the intricate mosaic of blood Neferata drew upon Nehekhara was shattered – like Nehekhara itself soon afterwards. Neferata's first coven and its puppets are long-gone. All of their triumphs and none of their failures began with her.\\nAs she begins anew, her covens will not fail again, and in the end the mortal world's maps will be mere pieces of the work she's wrought. This triumph will be hers alone.

No Vampire's blood runs thicker with treachery than that of Mannfred von Carstein. What he perceives to be his greatest strengths – his egotism, self-reliance and furious drive – are also his towering folly. It stains his claim to the power and knowledge he has amassed, never known or long forgotten by most Vampires. Because of that, many shun him.\\nAnd because of that, Neferata shall have him. She always knew and never forgot the ancient secrets of her kind. Mannfred will stand alone, yes. But not in triumph as he so desires. His choice to join her will be no choice at all, in defeat.

The irony of Vlad and Isabella, so transparent in their purity, has turned Neferata's thoughts towards Sylvania. Insane old Otto von Drak unwittingly bethrothed his daughter to a being such as Vlad. Was it not that so many of her own first children, so full of charm and cunning, delivered themselves into Neferata's arms, ignorant of her nature?\\nIn truth, Neferata herself has remained ignorant of Vlad's origin, to her chagrin. Let him remain a mistery, so long as he and his consort remain useful. Is she not the Queen of Mysteries, after all?

Through Neferata's Elixir of Life the most diligently chosen mortals were reborn as Vampires, their virtues multiplied a thousandfold. Those first, though few, surpassed all mighty sovereigns of Nehekhara in strength and guile.In the end, base servitude was their undoing. To Nagash they pledged their gifts and worship – and in his service they perished, though he did not. But neither did Neferata. Where he failed, she will not – and Lahmians will have a sovereign surpassing them in all their virtues.

Mortals are easily dismissed, but rarely so quick to forget humiliation. Before Neferata turns her gaze fully upon Lahmia, {{tr:missions_localised_title_wh3_dlc29_qb_vmp_silver_sisterhood}} must be reclaimed and another grievance set in motion.

Though for centuries Neferata never descended from Silver Pinnacle, she coursed the world through the blood of her Handmaidens, knew the leaping hearts of those they lured, beguiled, and fed on. But none of her supreme servants know her own rekindled heart, save one.\\n Imentet: her foremost sister in blood and a true Lahmian, High Mistress of all others. She divines their worth by a word, and she has already divined Neferata's thoughts: the Handmaidens must be worthy of Neferata's renewed purpose.

Neferata's Vampire offspring is far from being as pathetically naive as mortals, regardless of station. But this means that the Vampires' lack of regard for her station among them is either proof that their cunning cannot match hers, or that their arrogant stubbornness has blunted it to a dim-witted stub. If so, she will be blunt, for once.\\nThey will hear her name. Some will see her face. The cleverer among them will most likely be the most foolish, and reject her. To those, she will show what that costs.

A barrier brimming with magic has forbidden all approaches to Lahmia. To intruders, it is a challenge of towering proportion. To Neferata, it is no such thing. It is a sign of desperation. She, an intruder? To her birthright? To her bloodright? In blood, she turned this city of queen consorts into a city of the Queen Regnant.\\nIn blood, she will open her path back to it. It will spill forth from the veins of the roving mercenary bands and the petty fiefdoms whom she has toyed with. The ritual shall be an act of fierce defiance against Nehekhara's dusty reverence for proper death. The wards of forbiddance will fall – for no death is proper. Only immortality is.

Once destined for the sacrificial altar, the enchanted Akmet-kar, the Dagger of Jet, has never lost its hunger for mortal blood. To restore its power and prestige, we must gather the lambs whose lifeblood will sate the ancient blade once more.
Though battle is not Queen Neferata’s favoured way of having her servants prove their worth, the puissant Ruby of Lahmia shall manifest its full potential in the wake of Lahmian supremacy in war.

[[i]]At Dead Man’s Shrine, before a field of freshly sown corpses and an assembly of pious flies, we were anointed as Nurgle’s Champions. It is to be us, the Befouled Brothers, and no other, who will lead the southern crusade. The tribes of Norsca are a quarrelsome band and will take some convincing. Our much-beloved parents' message of peace did not outlive their deaths by Nordlander halberds, though I cannot see why.\\n\\nSo be it!\\n\\nIt is, as we can all agree, as Grandfather would desire it. He has blessings for all, but as we know better than any other, few are truly ready to receive them.\\n\\nBlessed indifference must be earned.\\n\\nThe supplicants must see, in their own time and way, that submission is the only antidote to suffering.[[/i]]

[[i]]Triumphant, I stamp across the grave-loam spread thick over cobbled plazas, and feel paternal pride swell at the pimple-like eruptions of pallid fungi and the soupy gurgling of man-faced flesh-trees. A shale-green sky showers me with favourable pus, and I ask – is this where our furrow ends? Astride the convulsing corpse of the Empire, even now seething with new and unbound life?\\n\\nNay, my brothers. This is but a new beginning, for we set an example here in ‘mighty’ Altdorf. I shall not be satisfied until we have ploughed every mockery of ‘civilisation’ into the garden it longs to be![[/i]]

[[i]]It would seem that the good doctor made more enemies in his work than he at first let on. The Elector of Hochland, the Baron of Salzenmund, even the usually peace-loving Cult of Shallya from Dhazhyn in Kislev – they all appear to have a bone to pick with our master sawbones. Oh well, Grandfather teaches us nothing if not find joy in the suffering of life. They would all have submitted to Nurgle’s blessings eventually, so why not now? It matters little to us, but if we can keep Festus’ plague laboratory in Brass Keep out of his detractors’ hands, then it will cost our real enemies dear.[[/i]]

[[i]]Nurgle does not demand war for its own cruel sake. No, my brothers. Think of him instead as a kindly benefactor, who rejoices in a putrid bounty more widely shared! It is simply that so many appear averse to having their lands and bodies cultivated in so generous a manner. His Garden within the Realm of Chaos is an infinite estate of festering fecund beauty. One day, we shall remake the entire mortal world in that foulsome image, and his Plaguebearers shall count new poxes and poisons until the end of days! Such a project will be the work of many joyous years, but the labour is its own reward.\\n\\nTo those who say I spend too much time raising a Garden from every slaughter and too little waging war, I say this: there is no surer path to Grandfather’s favour.[[/i]]

[[i]]One by one, we have trampled the surly tribes beneath our bronze-shod tread. Driven like cattle to the slaughter, their defiant chieftains now lie butchered in the muck – rusted spikes thrust from gullet to temple, mock-horned effigies honouring the Lord of Rot.\\n\\nYet subjugation alone is not enough. Though he can no longer speak, I have read the same truth in my brothers’ eyes, their vengeful gaze drawn ever southward. The tribesmen must be shown that, with Grandfather's loving guidance, they may bear His fecund gift to the furthest reaches of the untilled world.\\n\\nThus, I turn my helm toward the vagabond known as Wulfrik. By challenging the Eternal Challenger, my fledgling champions will understand: just like the World Walker driven before them, they too can exalt Nurgle's name all across a ripened realm.[[/i]]

[[i]]Since before our parents’ passing, Nurgle has doted on us, the Brothers Glott, spoiling us as any Grandfather should. Who placed the three-lobed birthmark on our unspoiled flesh? Who, indeed, placed the infection upon our mother while she bore us in the womb? Such gifts we have been given, but such is Nurgle’s miracle that the more of His misery we inflict upon the world, the more we shall have. Should His Blessings be called forth, they will be returned to us ten-fold in esteem![[/i]]

[[i]]O-ho, what is this?\\nWas I not just lamenting the lack of good wet mulch to feed the new Garden’s soil? I should have known to trust Grandfather to provide. Not one army full of soft wet bodies, but three! I would have thought the Wood Elves of the Laurelorn would better appreciate what we are doing here. We want only to make things grow! Oh well, soon we shall, and so shall they. With their fine blood as a feed, this Garden will flourish as never before. Defend the verges at all costs, my brothers. If a single bilgeflower should perish then Grandfather’s anguish will not be for the Empire alone. Harvest this plantfeed that our enemies deliver to us, however, and he may send an army of Daemonkind to march on Altdorf with us![[/i]]

[[i]]Marienburg is the gateway to the Reik. The burghers themselves have always abused their throttlehold on the river to get their way, so why not us? Their merchant princes are driven only by wealth and power. We will use the waterway for something far grander! The city will be almost as difficult to crack as Altdorf herself, but the latter will be all the weaker for it being in our tender hands. Its sea defences are one of the wonders of the civilised world: great Dwarf-made walls upon ancient Elven foundations, manned by mercenaries paid for with the world’s gold. But once it is ours, Altdorf will be sure to follow![[/i]]

[[i]]A little fly buzzes in my ear of another practitioner of plague already at work in these southern lands. He is a Nordlander, but don’t hold that against him. There are those in Norsca who would say the same of us, if they were not now dead and buried and feeding the soil of our Garden in Doomkeep. Let us show this Dark Apothecary what the Befouled Brothers are capable of and, with Grandfather’s blessing, perhaps our brother-in-faith will gladly add his collection of poxes to ours.[[/i]]

[[i]]The bogs of Westerland will be a fitting nursery for Nurgle’s Blessings. Such a rancid flourishing will be a reward for the future however, one we can admire at our leisure once the last men of the Empire have been staked above the seedlings. Marienburg may have fallen, but some along its rivers stubbornly resist the gifts we bring. Irritants, no more, but we cannot have them stinging us in the back all the way to Altdorf. Sink our roots deeper, and make this Wasteland truly ours.[[/i]]

[[i]]The soil in the Empire is not like that of Norsca. It is soft and dark, and yet oddly fallow. The climate is mild, and yet nothing of real worth grows. The foetid breeze that blows from Grandfather’s Garden is barely a whisper here. The ground is inhospitable to Daemonkind and this, brothers, we must address, for we will need soldiers for the march south, and farmhands for the work that comes after. But do not despair. You perhaps do not recall how our dear mother toiled before her Nordlander crops would take to the Fjordlingtribe soil.\\n\\nWhat’s that, Ethrac? You do remember? Well, good, then we are agreed.\\n\\nWe should tend to this southern soil, as she did that of the north, until it is more pleasing to Grandfather’s children.[[/i]]

The enemy has collected four Daemon Prince souls and attempts to assail the Forge of Souls before you! They will stage close to the Forge, preparing to cross the void. Intercept and defeat the imposters or they will challenge Be’lakor in contention for the prize. Stop them or be cast into irrelevance – your campaign LOST!

Uzkulak was nothing more than a tiny slum when last Kislevites held  Fort Dorznye-Vort, but over the centuries it has grown to be the dominant settlement in this region. Occupying it will let the Greenskins and others know there is a new power here.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

Kislev once claimed this entire region and should do so again under the rule of Boris Ursus! Take the other settlements in this [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] and own it all.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The Orcs in this region resent your presence. The ignorant creatures are unaware that the Kislev Tzardom reached through High Pass and claimed these lands. Let us remind them!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Nordlanders occupy the Bay of Blades. Allowing them to exist there weakens the Dark Powers' influence in this region. It will be considered a great boon if you purge the settlement of mortal filth.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

For now the Chaos Gods are capricious. You will quickly fall from their favour if you cannot dominate your home [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]]. Dominate the Ice Tooth Mountains!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

Nordland has sent armies into the north. Hoping to halt invasions into their own territory. One such army thinks to cut you off from your new fortress. Show them no mercy.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

The tribes have forgotten why you have acquired so many titles and ruled for so long. They need a 'reminder', and that means some killing and eating. Start with Grimtop!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

The Ivory Road spans from Grand Cathay to the Old World, but a good part of the route crosses through the Mountains of Mourn. Goldtooth's territory. Take it back from traitors and foes!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The Bear-God's roar has driven unrest throughout the Ogre Kingdoms. Tribes that were once loyal or at least content, now hunger for power. An army approaches thinking to take you on. Show them how foolish such greedy ambition is!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

There will be many big fights to come. Best to swell your hoard with some fresh meat. Get recruiting!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_recruit_units}}

We require Bloodwind Keep to facilitate the invasion of [[sl:campaign_cathay]]Cathay[[/sl]], but taking it by force is not the only option. You might instead use your [[sl:campaign_changing_of_the_ways]]Tzeentchian cunning[[/sl]] to coax the inhabitants to our cause.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement_tzeentch}}

You must own the rest of the [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] to establish a power base from which to launch your invasion through the Great Bastion and into Cathay's interior. Occupy the remaining settlements and claim this province!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

Your machinations have borne fruit. Through manipulation, the Imperial Wardens have wandered far from their normal patrols of the Great Bastion. They are now within striking distance. Kill them and weaken Cathay’s defences!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Powerful [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] such as the Iridescent Horror can act independently. Even the most manipulative and far-sighted of lords will still require a power force to back up threats and even act, when direct action is required. Recruit more warriors to expand your force.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_recruit_units}}

The Vanaheimlings squat in Gerslev, their bitterness and hatred to you only further enflamed by the defeat of Gulbrandsen's horde. They cannot be left to fester – as queen of the Motherland, you must expel them without mercy!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

If you are to rescue the Bear-God, Ursun, from the Realm of Chaos, then Kislev must be united! Gerslev is but the first step on this journey, now bring the rest of this oblast under your rule. Claim all settlements in this [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] through might or diplomacy.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province_kislev}}

Displaced by the maelstrom, worshippers of the Dark Gods scour the Motherland. A horde of Dolgan even dares encroach upon the capital. A strong monarch cannot let this stand... Destroy them!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Powerful [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] such as the Frost Maiden can act independently. For now, get them to join your army.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_description_heroes}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_heroes_movement}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_heroes_learn_more}}

Kislevites always flock to strong rulers. Your recent victory will ensure there are plenty of Kossars eager to fight under your banner. Which is well, as you will need a larger army to reclaim towns stolen by the Vanaheimlings.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_recruit_units}}

Stanitsas this far north that have not wholly conformed to Great Orthodoxy strictures are a threat to the Kislevite people and their immortal souls. By cleansing Leblya of unbelievers we ensure the Dark Powers cannot inveigle their way into the minds of heathens.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

For centuries, Troll Country has been an area shunned by the Tzars, allowing the tribes and creatures of Chaos to fester. But no longer! The Cult of Ursun shall show its strength despite the silence of its god, and deliver this region into the dominion of the Great Orthodoxy!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The Ungol Kindreds have always resisted the teachings of the Great Orthodoxy, preferring heathen rites - the words of hags and witches over the sanctioned sermons. There is no time to correct such heresy through teaching, we must face them in battle!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Powerful [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] such as the Patriarch can act independently. For now, get them to join your army.\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_description_heroes}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_heroes_movement}}\\n\\n{{tr:hp_campaign_heroes_learn_more}}

Kislevites always flock to strong rulers. Your recent victory will ensure there are plenty of Kossars eager to fight under your banner. Recruit willing supplicants to the cause.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_recruit_units}}

Owning a port on the Frozen Sea will allow for rapid infestation, ensuring your poxes travel far. The Ogres currently claim it, but they are not worthy of such a prize, take it from them!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_capture_settlement}}

Claim this [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] and infest it with your power. From this many fresh drones and servants shall gestate and your forces and influence shall quickly spread across the world.\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_complete_province}}

The Ogres have taken Glut-port and seek to expand on your new capital. They are an annoyance that needs taking care of before we can expand our own burgeoning realm. Slay the interlopers!\\n\\n{{tr:wh3_main_narrative_addendum_attack_enemy}}

Powerful [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] such as the Plagueridden can act independently.
