The wars waged by Chaos have been the most terrible of all conflicts in history, their destruction unrivalled by anything else. But each war has been but a test, a sham, a preparation for a greater war that is yet to come, every battle a touch of the taloned hand of Chaos probing the defences of the mortal world. Soon the day will come when Chaos musters its true, horrifying strength, but first its acolytes must prove their military might with yet more bloodshed. In return, the Gods will pave the way to the end by sending forth their first forgotten champion…

To carry out the Lord of Murder’s bidding is to sate his endless appetite for violence – and now is the time to unleash his raw, unreasoning vengeance onto the mortal plane for your blood-soaked cause! Karanak, the three-headed hound, is a vicious and implacable Daemon, endlessly prowling his master’s throne room when not carrying out His murderous bidding. In fact, Khorne considers very few of His champions worthy of summoning Karanak. Unquestionably, any paragon of violence and destruction in this existence has much to gain should the chosen hunter of Khorne be weaponised for their own ends. As is the Blood God’s way, bloodshed shall beget bloodshed; to summon His prized hound, Khorne’s gaze must be turned…
A toll must be paid to pass through Khorne's realm. Become a killer to pass through the bloody lands.
Ensure your powerful allies serve you. Use the Ice Maiden to disrupt your enemies.
The Atamans of Kislev lead and administer their villages and towns. Build a safe haven amidst the wastes.
To despoil and take is all that these savages understand, even those that worship Tzeentch in his more base forms.
Send the arcane armies of the Changer scattering before your might and this trial shall be fulfilled.
There is more than one way to bring a tribe to heel. Find common cause with them, for only together will you survive.
When Ursun's most devout servant is at your side, use him to further your own aspirations.
The time has come to march on Dervingard and free our kin. If you do not strike swiftly, the Wolf will recover. End his reign of bloodshed.
Yuri, ready your warriors. Our sons and daughters cry out and flee in terror. The spilling of their blood must be prevented.
Yuri, you have led your kin through the mountain pass. The winds of the Chaos Wastes howl with unmatched fury. Journey north and seek respite.

Yuri, your scent grows strong, saturated in the power you have gained. I am close, but I grow weak.\\n\\nConfront the traitor Slavin Kurnz. Offer no mercy, only blood. Slay him and the Howling Citadel is yours. Together we will roar to melt the snows. Together we free Kislev of this winter.\\n\\nMake war, Yuri, seek your true god.

The fears of lesser men must not sway you from the righteous path. You have shown courage. Now, be as brazen as the altar you seek. Enter the lands of Khorne, the Blood God, conquer them, and raid his shrine. Discover the name of the Bridge-Maker.

The spirit of men is frail – so easily corrupted. The northern tribes worship the Dark Gods. The chief of the Gharhars, Skollden, hungers for Kislevite blood. While he lives, he will hinder your search and prey on our people. The Wolf must be tamed.

Dervingard is reclaimed. Now we embark on a greater quest. Deep in the Chaos Wastes stands the "Citadel that howls". Within its halls lies a hidden portal that leads to my prison. The Citadel cannot be reached by mortal means – the Screaming Chasm prevents it. Journey to the Lucent Maze. Find the secret runes. They hold the knowledge you seek.
It is not enough to merely slay the enemy, but ravage their lands. Turn raider and take anything of worth.
Some will never kneel. Then the only answer is to obliterate them utterly. Wipe out your foe – it matters not who, for this is a trial of war itself – the consequences be damned!
Shamed in Grimnir’s sight did the bestial horde attack from many different angles, breaking the established rules of war. Cheaters all, and they should be punished!
Within Smednir’s vengeful glare did the Gors raid Dawi lands. A foul trespass! Right this wrong!
Spied in the view of Grungni, the warherds of vile, skruff Beastmen pillage and despoil fine Dawi lands. Such a disgrace must be avenged!
Another herd's Hero has become too much of a hazard. Destroy them - see that they never return.
This Hero of Chaos has become troublesome. See them dealt with, and remove this threat forever.
This unfilthy, Uncloven, stunted Dwarf Hero has been allowed to sow trouble for too long. Bury this fool in his caverns - blot out his light.
This pompous, self-aggrandising Empire Hero believes himself greater than the herd. Bring him down to size - excise this malignancy for good.
This Hero has become a nuisance to the herd. Send him to a gruesome grave, and remove this threat forever.
This Hero has become a nuisance to the herd. Send him to a gruesome grave, and remove this threat forever.
This meddlesome Greenskin Hero pesters us, and can no longer be tolerated. Squash this pest underfoot.
This unfilthy, Uncloven Hero of the Vampire Counts has haunted our lives for too long. Send him to our Ruinous masters, and remove this Unliving threat forever.
This unfilthy, Uncloven Hero of the Vampire Counts has haunted our lives for too long. Send him to our Ruinous masters, and remove this Unliving threat forever.
It is the wise beast who rips apart his foe on the battlefield; other Beastlords will be happy to see him smashed and will respect your strength for doing so.
We should fight this enemy on the battlefield. In victory, your power will be undeniable - the other Beastlords will show respect and deference.
Only the true beast would consider raiding these lands. A swift victory will say much about your worth to the other Beastlords.
Burning these settlements and destroying the lands around them would show wisdom, Lord. Other tribes will revel in the destruction, and like us all the more for it.
Another Beastlord is bringing his herd through nearby blood-grounds. If we kill him - and break his horns - his herd will be struck a terrible blow and we will grow stronger.
A Chaos Lord is driving his armies through our blood-grounds. We will gain great glory and prestige if we smash this army to a bloody pulp!
A paltry Dwarf Lord is marching his army right into our blood-grounds. They have brought themselves into the hunt - we will gain glory beyond reckoning if we destroy this Dwarfen host.
A boastful Empire Lord swaggers through our blood-ground. It is an affront! There is man-flesh to rend and rive, and strength to be gained in their devastation!
A Lord dares to march his army through our blood-grounds. Destroy them, break them into pieces, and gain glory and strength through their defeat!
A mewling Greenskin is leading his pitiful band through nearby lands. Should we smear their pestilence away and squash their march, we will become stronger.
A corpselike Lord of the Vampire Counts is processes his army of bones through our blood-grounds. Break them apart, send them to a permanent end, gain glory!
This enemy Beastlord is a powerful adversary, strong-horned and vicious. Defeating him in a bloody battle, and de-horning him, would be a great achievement, showering us in gore and glory!
This Chaos Lord has a dark power, giving him skill on the battlefield. If we defeat him, bring true ruin to his force, then the Dark Gods would favour us greatly in return.
This Dwarf Lord has great strength for such a small thing and is courageous in combat. Should we best him - and we will - there would be much glory and honour showered upon us.
This conceited Empire Lord has great strength and is heroic in combat. Stripping him of his vaunted skill, destroying him in battle, will exult us; glory through bloodshed!
This enemy Lord has great strength and is savage in combat. Killing him in battle -filthy and bloody battle - would be a great achievement, raining glory and strength upon us.
This pernicious Greenskin Lord has surprising strength, racking up many victories. There is great glory in felling such a warrior - we should take it upon ourselves to slay him!
This cadaverous Lord of the Vampire Counts has a preternatural power and is towering in combat. Rending his soul from his husk and destroying his ambitions will bring great things to us and the herd.
This enemy herd shall face the true chosen of Chaos - their Ruinous might shall flow through us as their destruction is wrought upon the battlefield!
This Chaos force shall experience the power of a fully-armed Beastmen army. Attack at will!
This shrunken Dwarf army faces the horrible majesty of the Beastmen! Destroy this force in the name of ruin and madness!
This pathetic man-filth Empire army shall be brought to heel; their pomp and pride shall come to naught as they fall before the snarling and smashing of the Beastmen.
This enemy army shall face the fury and savagery of a true Beastman army, and they will know our might as they are destroyed!
This meddlesome Greenskin army shall fall under hoof as we trample this force of pests into nothing more than mud and blood.
This Beastmen herd thinks they can encroach on OUR blood-ground. That is not their right. Our land. Our hunt. Our retribution!
A Chaos force marches where they are not welcome. The true chosen of the Chaos Gods desire flesh and war, and so we will repulse this invasion!
A band of foolish Dwarfs has trudged onto the blood-grounds. They know not what they do, but will feel our wrath all the same!
A presumptuous Empire army marches onto our blood-grounds. In their arrogance, they have invited our terrible fury down upon themselves. Enact that fury. Destroy them!
An enemy army has dared to trespass on our blood-grounds. This makes them fair game. To the hunt!
A noisome Greenskin force has moronically entered where they are not wanted. Send them back to their huts and hovels and dung. Smash them apart. Destroy them!
The pallid Vampire Counts have dared to snake their dead, crusty tendrils into our lands. Their graves cannot remain empty for long - see them returned!
These pallid Vampire Counts shall face true terror beyond their reckoning at our hands; to war, to glory, to feast!
These Dwarfen lands, their holds and their tunnels, are brimming with plunder. Summon the beasts, call them to war - there is hunting to be done!
The Empire lands are full of the rich-blooded and the haughty. Their flesh is fat, and so are their coffers. To battle then, for the prize!
This blood-ground is ready to be ravaged. Summon the herd, begin the hunt! We take what we want, and leave nothing for the carrion!
This Greenskin land is filthy, disgusting and remorseless - it is perfect for us. We lay claim to this land, and all within it!
Amongst the ash, and bones and towering piles of corpses lie treasures unending. The Beastmen will have these treasures; they can keep the bodies.
The more land we conquer, the more territory we own, the larger the force needed to control it. Attract more Gors to the herd; expand our might!
The Dwarfs' network of tunnels and stone dares to decry our base majesty! Leave nothing of it for them to salvage - turn stone and bones to dust!
This shining, 'civilised' Empire settlement is a brazen affront to the glorious filth of the world! The beasts should ride to defile these pretenders. Call the herd. Destroy man!
This settlement cannot be allowed to remain - it is too clean, too pure; it is an insult. Bring it to rubble - bring it to ruin!
These Greenskin hovels are disgusting; admirably filthy, but they still cannot be allowed to endure. Remove this unworthy pestilence!
These desiccated cadavers believe themselves to be the true heirs to the Empire, the true inheritors of 'civilisation' - there is no such thing! Destroy them! DESTROY THEM ALL!
The Gorebull is a powerful and useful Hero of great advantage to us on the blood-grounds!
The Bray-Shaman is a deeply mysterious but extremely effective Hero. Stalking the blood-grounds with us, its power could be brought to bear excellently.
Although brutal melee is always preferable, there is tactical advantage in bombarding our enemies from afar. We do not have enough artillery under our command - this should be rectified!
A powerful division of cavalry is crucial to victory. We are fielding very little cavalry - something that should be addressed!
The melee is everything! Brutal, bloody, savage combat! We do not have nearly enough melee troops - recruit more with haste!

We prefer to fight with our hands and our hooves and our teeth, yet there is some advantage in softening up the foe with missile fire before the charge. We do not have enough missile troops - this should be rectified!
The bigger the beast, the better the slaughter! There are not enough War Beasts in our herds - recruit more with haste!
War Machines help us tear down the world of man. We are not fielding enough - recruit more War Machines and destroy our Uncloven foe!
These underlings think to play above their station. Hah! Smash this snivelling, mewling beast into the dirt!
An aberration of the highest order dares to move against us. Let no such nonsense stand - eliminate this beastly agent and be done with it.
Stinkin', stupid Beastmen agent needs to be smashed, crushed, sliced! They'll have to put him back together.
This beastly, uncouth Beastmen agent thinks to tread upon our lands. Drain this fool, leave him for the carrion!
If these beasts love war so much, we shall bring war to them and show them the fury of the Ruinous Powers. Fell their general; establish dominance!
Savage brutes that know only war are best defeated, comprehensively, on the battlefield. Cut the head from a snake, and watch the body wither.
The beasts want to fight, then fight! Yes! Take to the battlefield and smash the big one into the dirt! Then we'll see how much they like fightin'!
On the battlefield, the beasts are ferocious and savage, but so are we. Let our prowess be known; fell the strongest of them and the others will follow suit!

The Dark Gods are pleased… mankind is ravaged. They have been taunted, hunted and broken by the Children of Chaos. The land is ripe for an even greater invasion; for other followers of the Ruinous Powers to make their mark, as paltry as it will be compared to the triumphs of the Cloven Ones. Yet there remains defiance - the armies of man-filth muster as one, refusing the inevitable. No matter! This is but another opportunity for the Beastmen to prove themselves the most worthy of the Dark Powers' servants. Find this "gathering of might" and ensure the fall of man!
Though Valaya is aggrieved to see it, these bark-eaters have stolen a victory from the Dawi. This slight cannot go unavenged. See to it!
Grimnir rages at the sight of these leaf-lovers raiding our lands. The grudge has been entered into the Dammaz Kron – strike it out!
Furious Smednir cries out at these thicketed fools sacking our Karaks. This cannot stand, so says the Book; you must fight, and win, for the grudge!
As spied by a wrathful Grimnir, did the tree-hugging elgi bastards come and take our settlement. What do these gits even want with rock and metal? Get them out!
This vile and unnatural Beastman seems determined to ruin our plans. Show it the fury of the forest - destroy this blight!
What vicious schemes the Chaos Gods wish to rain upon us! Do not let them endanger Athel Loren - smite their corruption from the forest!
The diminutive mountaineer thinks to sully our plans. Show him otherwise - let him feed the Worldroots!
The haughtiness of man is apparent. Let no agent of the Empire forestall our progress. Turn them to mulch!
The enemy think we can be taken for granted! They are sorely mistaken - show them the error of their ways.
What schemes does she mean to employ against us? See that they are never brought to fruition.
What a vile, fungal nuisance this one is! Cut him down to size and stop his sneaky meddling once and for all!
The dead have no place amongst the living. Their place is in the earth, serving as mulch for the trees. See them sent below!
Cadaverous and pallid, this Undead heiress must be swiftly and surely dealt with; never again must she darken the forest!
Though cavernous and dark, this Dwarf stronghold is a good place to make camp!
These Empire settlements are ready-made for us; let us take up positions here!
This settlement is as good as any for us to use as an outpost!
Though filthy and dank, this Greenskin settlement will do well for us.
Though dingy and morose, this Undead settlement will suffice as an outpost.
Our kindred have requested that we deal with these warriors. They are the strongest of their kind - their defeat will endear us to our brothers, which is essential for our ultimate victory!
Our forest kith request we capture this place. Doing so will strengthen our bonds with them.
If we take down these fierce warriors, it will strike a terrible blow to their morale. Our potential allies ask that we do this in the name of greater friendship between us.
Potential friends have asked we take the fight to this army. Defeating them will prove our mettle beyond doubt and their gratitude will greatly endear them to us in return.
The key to better relations with our potential allies lies in raiding this territory. They have requested it of us, and by doing so our friendship will be shored-up further.
Our kinsmen have requested that we ransack their enemy's lands, swearing fealty if we succeed. Do this and we will increase our chances of their being brought completely under our rule.
This filthy Beastlord thinks he can trample our sacred territory. Bluntly put, he must be killed, and a terrible lesson taught to our opponents!
Chaos has no place amongst the civilised, and this Lord of Chaos walks our lands hitherto unchallenged. Put him to the sword, and demonstrate we are not to be crossed!
This bantam-weight warrior thinks he can march through our territory. What idle madness these Dwarfs must dream - put him to the sword!
The arrogant and aloof Karl Franz sends one of his leaders against us. Show no mercy to this interloper - strike a blow to the heart of the Empire by cutting him down.
As the seasons change, so too do the whims of fools. An enemy leader has camped too long near our lands, and so the Spring of our clemency must become the Winter of our wrath!

This filthy Greenskin leader thinks he can defile the sanctity of Athel Loren, leading his troops through our lands. Leave nothing for the carrion; destroy them all, Gork (or Mork) will recognise his own.
With every step this Undead leader takes, it corrupts and besmirches our lands with its decaying touch. Put it back in its grave once and for all!
This Beastlord is a thorn in our side; he is indeed mighty, but by felling him the glory gained will be great!
This Lord of Chaos is most formidable! Killing him will be a decisive blow to their forces but a great victory for Athel Loren!
For something so small, this Dwarf is certainly mighty! If we defeat him, we reap the glory found through the killing of a challenging opponent!
This Lord of the Empire may be arrogant, yet he remains a powerful warrior. We should bring him down lest he become more than a mere mayfly irritant.
No matter their strength, all enemies will fall before us. This foe has great skill and power, in their defeat there is great glory to be gained for Athel Loren!
Though slimy and stunted, this Greenskin warrior is nevertheless powerful. To make him little more than carrion feed would bring us many great boons.
For a mere corpse, this Vampire is surprisingly formidable. Yet the dead should remain dead, with great glory to be found in returning it to the grave.
No brayherd can stand against us. Smash these ingrates to dust!
Chaos is a blight upon the world, and one we will see destroyed utterly!
What these Dwarfs dream of in the dark and dank depths shall not be wrought upon our lands!
Haughty, arrogant Empire forces have no place here. Put them to rout, for Athel Loren!
The forests whisper its desires - that this army be brought utterly to ruin. Enact Athel Loren's will!
This infestation of Orcs and Goblins has no place on this earth - smash them into the dirt, nasty green scumbags!
These detestable Beastmen infest our lands. They must be pushed back; Athel Loren must not be defiled!
Chaos cannot be allowed to encroach upon the sanctity of Athel Loren. Push its forces back - smash them!
The pernicious Dwarfs try to sully and plunder the forests; no more! Meet them in battle and crush them further down to size!
This pretentious, bejewelled Empire army treads where it should not. Show them the error of their ways!
No army has the right to march within our sacred boundaries. They must be repelled, and learn their folly is repaid in blood.
These fungal pests were not granted permission to enter our territory, nor would they ever be. Squash them, and return purity to these glades.
The Undead shuffle into our lands in great numbers, bringing with them their corruption and filth. Shatter them and leave their bones for mulch!
No army, living or dead, can stand against the might of nature. For Athel Loren, smash these brigands!
Dwarfholds may be dingy and dark, but they contain many riches; riches that we should claim for ourselves!
The Empire may be arrogant, but their territory is wealthy. Why should they have it all, and not us?
The riches of the earth are rightfully ours. We need only march forth and claim them!
Greenskins peddle filth wherever they roam, but beneath the dirt treasures can often be found. Treasures that, despite the grime, we should seize!
The Vampires are decrepit and deceitful, but they hoard great and ancient wealth. How it would benefit us if we were to simply reach out and claim it!
Athel Loren is threatened, so sound the call - bring more warriors to her defence. Recruit more!
What the Dwarfs have, we shall take by force. Burn their Holds, and take their treasures by force!
What mighty towers the Empire constructs! Such affronts to nature should be toppled for their arrogance - see it done!
The Council has decided, in its wisdom, that this settlement has no right to exist further. See it brought low, for the good of Athel Loren!
They pile their filth high and call it a settlement. It is nothing more than heaps of dung, and dung burns SO well…
Nothing kills the Undead better than fire, which makes this settlement little more than a glorified funeral pyre. Provide the match.
The Branchwraiths are powerful, if twisted, additions to any forest defence force. Athel Loren requires more of them - see it done!
The Waystalkers are the most keen, determined scouts in all of Athel Loren. Bring more of them into our ranks, to give us an edge over our enemies.
The Spellsingers, elegant and deadly, number too few among our ranks. See this remedied, that they may bring their beautiful ways of death to the battlefield!
Without cavalry, we are at a severe disadvantage - at risk of being outflanked and charged to devastating effect! We must field more to guard the edge!
Melee infantry are the spine of any good army, and we are severely lacking in their regard. We must field more to create a strong central core within our forces!

We are the warriors of Athel Loren, we strike from afar and with deadly precision. However, our armies are lacking in archers and scouts - recruit more, and they will surely give us the edge we require.
Without monsters to field, our forces lack the same punch as those of our rivals. We should field some huge creatures as to terrify our enemies!

A great horde of Beastmen besiege the Oak of Ages! There are brayherds present from every corner of the Old World; Morghur has summoned to him the Dark Omen, Malagor, and even Khazrak the One-Eye is said to be stalking the field. The Beastmen are drawn here to enact a final, bitter blow against the roots of life itself. Should they succeed, all will be plunged into a hell beyond reckoning and without end. They must be stopped before they bring this land to Ruin. Defend the Oak; defend the Old World!

So it has come to this. Morghur has thrown an almost endless torrent of Beastmen at the Wood Elves, yet they have pushed back the tide. Now the Shadowgave makes one final gambit - a push for the Silver Spire itself, intent on poisoning the water supply that nurtures so much of the land and leaving it for dead. He cannot be allowed to succeed. Yet Morghur has dark and twisted schemes that make him extremely difficult to kill - the Asrai must watch carefully and use their superior Elven intelligence to overwhelm his trickery. Hold fast against these desperate beasts, see the day won and the Old World saved!

Seen as an oath unfulfilled, and a sore point for all Dwarfs, the loss of Karak Eight Peaks was a low point for the Karaz Ankor. Since its fall many Dwarfs have tried, and failed, to reconquer it - Belegar is the latest of these who has dedicated his life to reclaiming this famous Hold. As a direct descendant of the last ruler of Karak Eight peaks, Belegar, and all those in Clan Angrund, consider its occupation their greatest grudge.

My lord! The outriders have returned from their reconnaissance with reports of a Greenskin force massing ahead of us. They are encamped on a defensible ridge, and have brought their bizarre artillery to further fortify the position – they appear ready to fight to the last. Further reports seem to indicate that they are bolstered by a great gathering of Warbosses, who seem bent on bringing their full strength to bear against you. It is clear they want the same thing we do – a decisive battle to decide our fates once and for all. We must not relent – their scourge must be wiped from the world!

Our march through the Chaos Wastes have been tough, Sire, but at last our courage seems to have been rewarded. Along the Cliff of Beasts, our scouts return with news that the forces of Ruin have decided to meet us in battle. Led by Archaon the Everchosen, and accompanied by the Prince of Slaneesh, Sigvald the Magnificent, the Chaos army seem ready to offer us a fight for the ages! The skies above, ever ominous during our perilous journey, turn now even more despondent. Thunder rolls across the grizzly clouds, and in the distance, lightning arcs through the deepening sky. The air hisses with static; could this be the moment of our destiny?

The champion of the Hound, Vashnaar, has been summoned by his master. Scorned by your allegiance to another, they have sent their best against you. This tainted warrior is here for one reason, and one alone: your defeat. With an unquenchable thirst for battle and an unwavering commitment to obey his masters, he will be no easy Champion to best. The host of followers in his wake is immense too, and they share a thirst for bloodshed with their hallowed example.\\n\\nYou must overcome this Champion, show his master that your fate is not in his hands, and that no matter who is sent against you the triumph will be yours!

With the appearance of giant, winged monsters, Chaos Frost Dragons are thought to be a type of Chaos-mutated Dragon that dwells in the underground passageways of the Old World’s coldest climes. Amongst the northern tribes there are tales of one such monstrous specimen called Frigustrex, Scion of the Cold-Void, which has terrorised the tundra for centuries. Witnesses say that when coming out of hibernation it emerges from the ground, in a heartbeat, to indiscriminately devour any unknowing passers-by that get too close to its territory, located somewhere at the frozen, northern end of Troll Country.\\n\\nRecently, The Tower of Khrakk and the surrounding areas north of Troll Country have been inexplicably blanketed by freakishly bad snow storms. Word also reaches you that entire tribes have disappeared from the region without a trace, reportedly perishing in the extreme weather. This is highly unusual – it is not like the hardy Northmen to succumb to the freezing elements so easily. A more likely explanation is brought to you by a few survivors who managed to escape the storm – they say that it was not the icy weather that swallowed up their fellow tribesmen, but a giant, Dragonish shadow lurking in the blinding blizzard.\\n\\nIf there is even the slightest chance that the fabled Frigustrex is out of hibernation and on the prowl, then further investigation is warranted. This could end up being a bountiful hunt indeed!

There are few individuals as hardened and adept on the freezing tundra than the bloodthirsty Marauder Hunters. They are used to these climes, and will move swiftly and easily over the icy wastes to help your search. Hire them so that they may be sent out to scout these lands in aid of the hunt!

Although severely lacking in intelligence, Ice Trolls are infinitely more resilient in cold extremes than most creatures, and will be able to move through the icy wastes unscathed. Recruit them into your army so that they may be sent out to scout these lands in aid of the hunt!

Just as you start to think that you are losing the Chaos Frost Dragon’s trail, the extreme weather around the Tower of Khrakk mysteriously dies down. News then reaches you that the bad weather has now suddenly appeared in the region of Zoishenk, in Kislevite lands to the south. This can be no coincidence – you must make your way into old Troll Country!

Witnesses are saying that it was not the icy weather that swallowed their fellow tribesmen up, but a giant Dragonish shadow lurking in the blinding blizzard.\\n\\nIf there is even the slightest chance that this shadow was the fabled Frigustrex itself, then it is worth investigating further. This could end up being a very bountiful hunt indeed! First you must travel through the Tower of Khrakk and deep into Kislevite lands to find the beast.

The Ruinous Masters have many worshippers across the Old World, amongst which the Beastmen are the most primitive. The influence of Chaos only enhances their bestial aspects, making the already-monstrous beasts larger and even more terrifying than they already are. One such pair of one-eyed abominations of the Beastmen are the gargantuan Cygor brothers known to men as The Salzenmund Soul-Eaters. These grotesque leviathans are not only bigger, stronger, and faster than their ordinary counterparts, but are feared even by Beastmen Bray-Shamans due to their ability to dampen the use of magic for others in their presence. To take on the mighty Soul-Eaters with limited use of magic certainly makes for a challenging hunt, but one which will potentially culminate in an impressive sacrifice to the Gods.\\n\\nFirst you must find the pair of monsters, who are always found together; a surprisingly difficult task considering their immense size. Being of the Beastmen, the Soul-Eaters dwell deep in the dark forests, navigable via the vast network of Beastpaths known only to the Beastmen themselves. The only way to safely explore them is to recruit some experienced hunters to search the woods thought to harbour Beastmen herds to hopefully find the Cygor brothers you seek as your bounty.

Your hunters send word that they have not been able to find any leads in the forests, but have caught wind of a pair of sieging Cygors terrorizing Middenland, hurling giant boulders that are turning castle walls to rubble. It’s as good a lead as any and surely the soft southerners are not going to last long anyway, so they could do with a plundering. Time to bring some real hunters to the lands of men!

You tear through Middenheim, leaving charred villages and slaughtered townspeople in your wake. Not only is there no sign of the Cygor brothers, but the soft fools of the Empire are surprisingly unknowledgeable about these monsters that are supposedly terrorizing their lands. But not all hope is lost – one of your Shamans comes to you, claiming to have a plan which will lead you to your bounty. He can put this plan into action for you, but only for a handsome price of course. You'll need to fill your coffers!

The Shaman returns and discloses his simple but deviously grim plan. Having communed with various godlings and daemons in his mysterious rituals, he now claims to know the location of the Soul-Eaters. He suggests you march your army to the edge of the Forest of Shadows, taking captive any men you can capture on the way – and keep them alive. This plan sounds like it is getting interesting...

Dragon Ogres are living legends of carnage and destruction. Most of what the Norscans know of these god-like beasts of Chaos is from the ancient records kept by their Shamans, which has immortalised them in folklore. Amongst the more ancient tribes there survives tales of one exceptionally strong Dragon Ogre Shaggoth known as Traygard Mountain-Cleaver. His power is thought to be second only to Kholek Suneater himself, with the ability to call upon thousands of thunder bolts to rain down on his victims, striking from unpredictable arcs to maim and destroy on his whim. Traygard is indeed an excellent target for a hunt – to sacrifice such a powerful and ancient monster of Chaos would be seen very favourably by the Gods. However, the monstrous Shaggoth hasn’t been seen in centuries, or at least, nobody has witnessed him and lived to tell the tale in that time. \\n\\nNews arrives of rumours that Traygard may be active again. A Norscan tribe to the north-east, very close to the Chaos Wastes, has been burnt to the ground with almost their entire enclave of warriors slaughtered in a single night. It is certainly true that many tribes of the north frequently perish at the hands of rival warring tribes, but on the night this tribe fell, it is said that a thunderstorm as bright as day lit up the night sky.\\n\\nThis is certainly worth investigation, but you first need more information, preferably from the survivors who actually witnessed the slaughter. With the majority of the tribe dead, this is easier said than done – the few surviving tribesmen are scattered as nomads throughout the region. The hunt is on.

These slave owners are trying to rip you off and need a lesson in Norscan business practices. Attempted robbery begets robbery – pillage their lands and take ownership of everything they own, including the slave you seek!
Time is short – you are on a hunt, after all. It is not worth engaging in conflict with a trivial merchant. Better to just pay the man’s high price. First you'll need to fill your coffers.

Once the slave is under your ownership, he reveals to you his sorry story. He is, in fact, a former Marauder Champion whose tribe was utterly devastated by the abominable Shaggoth they know was Traygard Mountain-Cleaver. He tells you that he experienced a single blow from the great monster which had caused him to lose his arm, then he was struck by one of the many bolts of lightning falling from the sky, which grazed the side of his head and burnt one of his eyes out of his very skull.\\n\\nThe legendary beast must exist, for the proof of it stands right there in front of you. But now you must see for yourself. The slave gives you the likely location of where the beast was headed after obliterating his tribe – the Chaos Wastes.

Although clearly gone insane, the pitiful man had obviously experienced a terrible encounter in battle, missing an eye and an arm. It is no exaggeration that very few things truly scare the Northmen and the other abominable inhabitants of the north – least of all, spiders. However, when they take the form of Venom Queens, gigantic in size and made up for in numbers by their hatchling swarms, most would prefer not to face one. The only real upside of encountering a Venom Queen is that there are rarely more than one in any one place at a time – killing just one is hard enough!\\n\\nRecently, harrowing stories have started circulating that gigantic Venom Queens are grouping into vast spider swarms in the lands to the south. The most recent spate of appearances have been in the Eastern Badlands, where they have taken over swathes of land, devouring any who come near. To most, this would be terrifying news. But to the hunter, this is a prime opportunity for a worthy sacrifice! Time to get more information.

As you arrive in the Eastern Badlands, you immediately see that the rumours of the spider infestation are true. The land is blanketed in webs and cocoons, and the surface seems devoid of other life. You have also arrived at a time of conflict between the Dwarfs and the Greenskins, who are currently fighting a bitter subterranean war over the many underground strongholds protecting the lucrative mines in the area. You can hear the faint sound of cannons and warfare emanating from the ground beneath.\\n\\nYou have no interest in this silly war between the stunties and the grobi! Besides, the men and creatures of the north are not adept at digging and navigating tunnels, preferring to fight out in the open like real men. Fortunately, the Greenskins still have several camps on the surface where it should be possible to obtain more information about the Venom Queen infestation. There won't be time for diplomacy, however!

While sacking a Greenskin camp, you manage to capture a spineless Goblin attempting to scurry away from the area unseen. The cowardly wretch says he’ll give up some information about the Venom Queen infestation for a little ‘compensation’. But there are cheaper ways to get information out of a greedy Goblin! Taking a full three seconds of a beating before spitting out the information, he reveals that Skarsnik, the self-proclaimed ‘Warlord of Eight Peaks’ had recently discovered this group of larger, poisonous Arachnaroks, and had been trying to herd them for use in his own malevolent schemes. However, he could not control the uncontrollable swarm and it had moved on, thought to have gone underground via a nearby tunnel.\\n\\nYou need to find the location of this tunnel entrance. To do so, the area around Karak Eight Peaks will need to be turned upside down.

Recently, harrowing stories had started circulating that gigantic Venom Queens were grouping into vast spider swarms in the lands to the south. The most recent spate of appearances had been in the area around Karak Eight Peaks, where they had taken over swathes of land, devouring all who came near. Your spies tell you that this is undoubtedly the work of Skarsnik, the self-proclaimed ‘Warlord of Eight Peaks’, who had allegedly discovered the group of larger, poisonous Arachnaroks, and had been trying to herd them into the area for use in his own malevolent schemes.\\n\\nYou care not for some stupid Goblin’s ill-conceived plans, but the news of this bounty can only mean one thing to a Norscan hunter – a prime opportunity for a worthy sacrifice! To find the location of the giant spider cluster, the area around Karak Eight Peaks will need to be turned upside down to find their burrow.

The Greenskins are famous for having all manner of monstrosities in their despicable ranks, including the lumbering Giants that follow them to insatiably feast in battle. Killing one for sacrifice would bring great prestige and recognition from the Gods, for what can be more impressive than slaying a legendary descendant of the long-forgotten Sky-Titans?\\n\\nYou have heard of one very belligerent Giant called Blorgar the Mad Titan, who is lumbering around the Grey Mountains being more than just a minor nuisance to the locals there. Setting out to slay the leviathan, you expect that the locals having their lands indiscriminantly flattened will be quite happy to see you, but it matters little. You're not going there to kill it for their sake – the hunt is on!

Arriving in the Grey Mountains you find out that Blorgar is long gone, but the destruction left in his wake is evident. Buildings have been smashed to rubble, crops flattened, and people reduced to ground-smears. Although the Giant's movements are still unknown, the locals tell you of a Bretonnian herb collector who might know where the brute lives. The Bretonnian had allegedly made a fleeting appearance in the Grey Mountains shortly before the Giant arrived, claiming that he’d accidentally stumbled upon the Giant's underground lair while spelunking nearby to gather some cave mushrooms. Knowing that the Giant was approaching, he was gone almost as soon as he’d arrived, fearful of the carnage to come.\\n\\nYou must now travel to Bretonnia to search for this herb collector. There would also be no harm in indulging in a bit of raiding while you’re there, if not just to keep the troops happy!

The Bretonnian herb collector has the information you need, but you don't trust the backstabbing gobbos to do any sort of financial deal. A spot of subterfuge, although perhaps cowardly from your perspective, may be needed instead in order for you to obtain the hostage. You must send one of your Heroes to infiltrate their camp and steal the Bretonnian right from under their noses.

The Greenskins are famous for having all manner of monstrosities in their despicable ranks, including the lumbering Giants that follow them to feast in battle. Having heard of one very belligerent Giant called Blorgar the Mad Titan terrorising the Grey Mountains, you set out to slay the leviathan for a great sacrifice, for what can be more impressive than bringing down a legendary descendant of the long-forgotten Sky-Titans?\\n\\nOnce you’d arrived in the Grey Mountains, however, Blorgar was nowhere to be seen. The only chance of gaining any useful information of the Giant’s whereabouts lay with a Bretonnian herb collector who’d allegedly stumbled upon an underground lair while spelunking nearby. Unfortunately this Bretonnian had been taken hostage by some nasty Goblins on a recent raid. The importance of the information known to him is crucial to complete the hunt, so a Hero was sent into the gobbos' camp to steal him back.\\n\\nYour servant dumps the hog-tied Bretonnian herb collector at your feet, along with some loot he managed to steal on his way out.

Your messengers tell you that the greedy Goblins are asking for a near-fortune to give the herb collector up. It seems they know he must have some considerable value to you. The thought of just killing them all crosses your mind, but then you would be running the risk of them fleeing, or executing the hostage. You need this man, and you need him alive, so you decide to raise the required funds.

Forest Dragons are truly remarkable creatures, dominating the forests as all dragons dominate their habitats. For most, stepping into the woods to find one to slay is either an act of extreme bravery or hopeless stupidity, such is the fiercely protective nature of the beings who dwell there. To some, the elusive Wood Elves are as dangerous as the unpredictable Beastmen, both of whom may attack unprovoked if you trespass into their woodland territories.\\n\\nSomewhere in the trees and thickets of Athel Loren lives Radixashen, also known as the Serpent of the World Roots. It is thought to be as ancient as the forest itself, and for that, it is a highly prized bounty for sacrifice. As with all dragons, it will be very difficult to track down and kill. The first thing you must do is to travel to the famous forest of the Wood Elves.

You have arrived at the forest and now must plan a way to draw the monster out of its hiding place. Knowing that there are often strong bonds between Forest Dragons and the Glade Lords of the Wood Elves, your next course of action seems clear. If you cause enough damage to the Wood Elves’ dwellings, their monstrous serpentine ally may show up to aid them. Even if it doesn’t, at least you will get the opportunity to pillage the dwellings of those estranged forest people!

It seems that Radixashen is not interested in coming to his ally's aid on this occasion. Perhaps it wrongly assumed that they were able enough to repel your attack, but in any case, further despoilment of the forest will be needed to bait the creature. You know that there is a great tree of immense spiritual importance to the forest, located right at its heart. Known as the Oak of Ages, not only is it considered the source of the forest’s power, but is also the annual birthplace of their King in the Woods. Surely, the Serpent of the World Roots cannot ignore the desecration of such a revered and important location. It is time to raise the raiding banners!

Striding blindly into the forest to find it would be foolish and futile – the best course of action would be to make the beast come to you.\\n\\nKnowing Radixashen to be one of the great protectors of the Elves’ forest, you can think of one target that will surely draw the Dragon out. The great tree known as the Oak of Ages, which is not only considered the source of the forest’s power, is also the annual birthplace of the Elven King in the Woods. Surely, the Serpent of the Worldroots will not be able to ignore the desecration of such a revered and important location. It is time to raise the raiding banners!

Mammoths are important tools of war for the northern tribes, and highly valued for sacrifice to the Dark Gods. Lately there have been sightings of some particularly impressive specimens around Norscan regions, rumoured to be members of a legendary herd of behemoths known as The Great Mawherd of Bloodfjord. This herd is thought to graze on the icy slopes of the Mountains of Hel. These beasts shall be a great offering indeed – go there and seek out this herd for a dark sacrifice!

Arriving in the mountains of Hel, the elephantine beasts are nowhere to be found. Instead, it seems that there are several Dwarf warriors to the area, namely Slayers and Rangers. Clearly, they too are hunting this herd, but you can’t be sure of their motives. The nearest Dwarfholds are in the nearby Gianthome Mountains – go there and squeeze some information out of them!

You have gathered information that a large Dwarf expedition has just departed to hunt down the herd. The Dwarfs’ involvement is an interesting development, since they are not known to be avid monster hunters, nor are they known to use mammoths in their battle-ranks as the northern tribes do. There must be good a reason for them to have left the safety of their holds just to hunt down some belligerent beasts. They were last seen marching for Kislev, so some further reconnaissance will be needed.
