Fielding Legions of skeleton infantry, archers and chariots, in combination with monstrous animated constructs, the Tomb Kings overwhelm the foe with resilience and numbers. The Realm of Souls means that as more friendly units are destroyed, the Tomb Kings gain army-wide heals and eventually a powerful Ushabti summoned through the Realm of Souls system.

Focusing on hordes of gunpowder-armed zombie pirates, the forces of the Vampire Coast specialize in blocking their enemy with powerful monsters so they can blast them off the field with missile and artillery units. Led by powerful Vampire Lords with their own custom ‘Lore of the Deep’ spells.

Dark Elf armies are well-rounded, able to field armour-piercing missile units, line-breaking heavy cavalry, and elite infantry. As the Dark Elves kill more enemies, they will trigger Murderous Prowess – gaining powerful bonuses.

The armies of the High Elves field the most powerful Dragons and some of the most powerful magic-users. In addition, the rest of their roster is well rounded and of high quality. These elite units benefit from the Martial Prowess ability, providing bonuses to units which are at high strength.

Lizardmen hosts consist of strong melee units, some of the most powerful magic-users, and towering reptilian monsters. Their missile units are generally short-ranged and struggle versus armoured targets.
Endless waves of expendable infantry, supported by terror-causing monsters and hard-hitting war machines. Though generally fast moving, the Skaven do lack airborne and cavalry units.

Chaos Dwarf armies are highly flexible and wear many hats. A heavily-armoured, fire-resistant frontline is bolstered by a cheap caste of Labourers and Hobgoblin lackeys that serve as a bulwark for powerful gunpowder weaponry and long-range artillery trains. This flexibility is further augmented by powerful bound fire Daemons, flying monsters and even cavalry.

The Undead Legions command the full power of each Undead faction's rosters. Field the mighty Constructs of the Tomb Kings, alongside the thundering Cavalry of the Vampire Counts and the explosive firepower of the Vampire Coast.

Cathay offers solid melee units and powerful missile units, which become stronger through harmony when placed near each other. Characters increase the effect of this harmony. Additionally, their spellcasters can support each other during spellcasting, increasing the power of their spells when fielding multiple Wizards.

Daemons of Chaos allow you to mix the forces of all the Chaos Gods. This makes the race versatile and unpredictable. Causing damage with your Lord generates glory, which rewards you with random army abilities in battles from the Reign of Chaos.

Khorne is a melee-focused race that excels at charging. It has no spellcasters, but Khornate Daemons are resistant to spells. Killing the enemy grants the Blood God’s favour, which can be used on army abilities.

Kislevite forces offer hardy hybrid infantry, swift cavalry and mighty War Bears; perfect for hammer and anvil tactics. Its units have the ability to find new courage when others would break, allowing the units to stand their ground against desperate odds.

Nurgle is a tough and slow melee race that excels at winning battles of attrition. Its units possess great health and reduce enemy melee damage through their passive abilities. Debilitating nearby enemies generates favour from Nurgle, which can be used to activate army abilities.

The Ogre Kingdoms offer a wide variety of monstrous units with bone-crushing charges and surprising mobility. Their infantry options are limited to weak and expendable Gnoblars. Ogre Kingdom units that charge in battle generate points that can be used for army abilities.

Slaaneshi armies are very fast, excelling at flanking and piercing armour, but this comes at the cost of armour and health. Killing routing enemies grants favour from Slaanesh, which can be used to activate army abilities.

Tzeentch is a race that excels at spellcasting, missile firepower and flying units. Its units are protected by a magical barrier that absorbs damage and is replenished when not taking damage. Casting spells generates favour from Tzeentch that can be used on army abilities.

The light infantry and monster units of the Beastmen are masters of charging from ambush – able to close the gap quickly and overwhelm the enemy. However, with mediocre leadership and poor armour, Beastmen suffer in prolonged engagements, their Primal Fury ability only granting them bonuses when leadership is high.

The Wood Elves are an elite force of skirmishing archers, supported by specialist melee infantry units, fast-moving cavalry and stubborn Treemen. Though they field some of the finest archers, they are fragile, making engagements in melee costly.

Norsca is a faction of aggressive infantry, flexible monstrous infantry and colossal line-breaking Mammoths. Though lightly-armoured and vulnerable to missile fire, Norsca has the tools to breach enemy lines and/or envelop the foe. The frenzied warriors of Norsca also have the Rage ability, meaning the longer they fight in melee the greater the bonuses they receive.

Bretonnia specialises in riding down their foes with powerful heavy cavalry. Supported by copious amounts of expendable peasant infantry and archers, these units buy time and space for the mounted Knights to charge, fall back and charge once more.

The Warriors of Chaos field rank upon rank of elite infantry, clad head to toe in plate armour. Pinning the foe in melee, they can then deliver brutal charges with their heavy cavalry and monstrous units.

The Dwarfs rely on steadfast, heavily-armoured infantry supported by powerful artillery and missile units. Completely lacking in cavalry, their only mobile units are the harassing Gyrocopter war machines. Though lacking access to spells, the Dwarfs are innately resistant to spell damage.

Greenskins field a roster of aggressive infantry, hard-hitting boar cavalry, and terror causing-monsters such as Arachnarok Spiders and Giants. Greenskins units engaged in melee generate points towards an almighty Waaagh!, a powerful, army-wide ability.

Powerful with spells and in melee, the Vampires are the core of this army and lead the legions of Undead skeletons and zombies, terrifying monsters and elite Vampiric cavalry. Completely lacking missile units, the Vampire Counts do, however, have access to powerful healing and summoning abilities to replace losses.

Collect resources and combine them with Canopic Jars to craft items and recruit Dynastic Legends, whilst learning from the dynasties of the past, to awaken the ancient Tomb Kings. Use incantations to bring the dead back to life, should sufficient numbers of their own souls be lost in battle.

Establish Under Cities in any settlement, undermining your enemies progress, or hide in plain sight while growing your own empire. Maintain Food supplies to gain growth and other bonuses, and to avoid starvation penalties.

Expand the Land of the Dead, turning all sources of life in the world into a source of power for Nagash. The Land of the Dead’s reach grows with each new Necropolis; however, each one will require sizable amounts of Necromantic Energy from the surrounding provinces in order to develop.
Balance both Yin and Yang to achieve Harmony, which will confer powerful effects across the provinces, whilst directing the Wu Xing Compass to defend Cathay from threats north of the Great Bastion.

Ascribe glory when capturing settlements to the four Chaos Gods to be granted boons in the form of Daemonic Gifts and units. These Gifts allow for the Daemon Prince to be customised in a multitude of unholy combinations.

Fight battles, raze settlements and claim Skull Piles to gather tribute to the Skull Throne. Serve the Motherland by training formidable Frost Maidens and Ice Witches within the Ice Court, granting powerful traits. Factions amass Supporters from Kislev’s two main sects based on their alignment, gaining Boons that can be spent on powerful permanent upgrades.
Concoct and spread plagues across the world or afflict your own assets. Nurglish settlements will grow by themselves over time and will eventually wither and die out.

With no penalties for trespassing, deploy Camps to create a forward base, constructing buildings and recruiting units from them. Camps will provide Meat, along with fighting battles, which each Ogre army is sustained by.

Amass followers by raiding, sacking and looting settlements and use them to summon armies in corrupted areas. Compel enemy units to join your army during battles, and force whole factions into vassalage via Seductive Influence.
Collect Grimoires to hatch treacherous plots to manipulate the destiny of all beings through the Changing of the Ways, whilst teleporting armies around the world.

Ravage the world by raising Herdstones in settlements to create Blood-grounds, enhancing your warherd in the name of the Dark Gods. Winning battles earns Dread to spend on expanding unit and Hero capacities, recruiting Legendary Lords, or other upgrades.
Heal the world’s forests in return for powerful factionwide bonuses whilst using the network of ancient tree roots to avoid impassable terrain and travel vast distances between forests.

Raze settlements and build monoliths in their place to gain allegiance to the four Gods, bestowing potent gifts. Use the Monstrous Arcanum to hunt down beasts whilst strengthening the tribe by assimilating other conquered Norscans once defeated.

Perform Chivalrous acts to grant powerful boons and call upon the strength of the Green Knight. Follow a code of honor and pledge Lords and Heroes to partake in Troths and Vows manage the Peasant populations tenure between farms and armies to ensure the economy remains strong.

Establish Dark Fortresses to vassalise and recruit followers of Chaos to the warbands, upgrading them into more powerful units. God-aligned gifts can be purchased to strengthen your faction a variety of ways.
Grudges must be settled by any and all means necessary to keep order across the realms. Dwarf armies can use the Underway to avoid impassable terrain and enemy forces.

Each faction acts as its own autonomous feudal state, some focusing on uniting the Elector Provinces through acts of Fealty and Imperial Authority, whilst others have their own agendas far from home, pursuing unique goals in service to The Empire.

The Shadowy Dealings panel shows which characters are eligible to take part in Eshin Missions.\\n\\nSome missions have a character rank requirement, and some can only be completed by Deathmaster Snikch himself.\\n\\nSelect which character you would like to complete an Eshin Mission from the list below.

Powerful rewards can be gained by completing missions given by Tz'arkan's Whispers.\\n\\nCompleting these missions will increase Tz'arkan's control over Malus.

A selected Augment's effects are displayed here.\\n\\nThe [[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]]Mutagen cost of each Augment can be seen on the right-hand side of the Apply button.\\n\\nAugmented units will have a pie chart on their unit card and Unit Info panel which displays a tooltip listing all effects of applied Augments.

Within each Augments tab is a hex grid of upgrades you can apply to your units.\\n\\nThere are three tiers of Augments, with the top tier having the highest [[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]]Mutagen cost to use. Common Augments (bottom tier with green symbols) have moderate effects but no downsides; Uncommon Augments (middle tier with blue symbols) are more powerful but come with negative side effects; Rare Augments (top tier with purple symbols) have very powerful effects and no negatives.\\n\\nThe bottom three Augments are unlocked from the beginning. The rest are unlocked for all units factionwide in an ascending sequence by using the connecting Augments beneath them in the hex grid.
The Flesh Laboratory is accessed via the button in the bottom right of the main campaign interface.

The Flesh Laboratory also contains the Growth Vat which consumes [[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]]Growth Juice to grow monsters.\\n\\nThe Growth Vat bar contains five pips, each representing a batch of one type of Clan Moulder monster. Once a pip is reached the batch can be released, which will include at least one unit of the batch’s monster type.\\n\\nThe resource used for Augments ([[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]]Mutagen) is also gained when releasing Growth Vat batches, though the amount gained increases only slightly with each successive pip.\\n\\n[[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]]Growth Juice is earned passively, as well as by constructing buildings, fighting battles, and recycling units with [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instability. The more [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instabilities a unit has, the more [[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]]Growth Juice awarded from recycling it.

The three sections of the Flesh Laboratory allow you to apply Augmentations to infantry and monster units or upgrade the Laboratory itself.\\n\\nBy selecting either the Infantry Augments or Monster Augments tab, you can view and apply Augments to make units stronger in battle.

To apply Augments to a unit, you must first select its unit card from your army.\\n\\nInfantry Augments and Monster Augments can only be applied to infantry and monster units respectively. Characters cannot be augmented.\\n\\nAugmentation comes with the risk of giving units [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instability. The more Augments applied to a unit, the greater the risk of additional Augments giving it [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instabilities. The chance of developing [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instabilities is displayed beneath each unit card.\\n\\nAny unit with [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]Instabilities can be recycled in return for [[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]]Growth Juice via the rollout that appears when its unit card is selected.

The Flesh Laboratory offers single-use upgrades to grant permanent effects, as well as repeatable upgrades to grant additional [[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]]Mutagen or temporary effects.\\n\\nThe top three upgrades are repeatable. Once one is used, all three will be locked for a short cooldown period.\\n\\nThe remaining nine are permanent upgrades separated into three tiers, each containing three upgrades.\\n\\nPermanent upgrades are unlocked by releasing Growth Vat batches, with higher tier upgrades towards the bottom requiring more batches to be released before they are unlocked.
You can upgrade the Flesh Laboratory by clicking the Laboratory tab.
The Rewards of Dread panel is accessed via the button in the bottom right of the main campaign interface.
[[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread can be used to purchase several factionwide upgrades which can improve new hordes, increase character recruit ranks, and expand your army capacity.
These upgrades allow you to increase the starting level of all Herdstones raised in the future.\\n\\nOnce a Herdstone upgrade is purchased, any existing Herdstone can be upgraded for no cost.

Increasing the recruitment capacity of [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes allows them to be recruited up to the purchased capacity by any horde in the faction, as long as the horde contains the correct buildings to recruit them.

Banners, weapons, armour, enchanted items and arcane items can be purchased here. Unlike other Rewards of Ruin, ancillaries purchased in the Items tab cost [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Favour instead of [[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread.\\n\\nThese items are exclusive to the Rewards of Dread panel and multiples of the same item may be purchased.
The Items tab allows you to purchase special ancillaries exclusive to the Rewards of Dread.
Having other [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Legendary Lords join your faction costs [[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread. If inactive when purchased, they are added to your Lord recruitment pool.
In the Lords & Heroes tab, you can increase [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero capacities and gain the services of other [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Legendary Lords of the Beastmen.

The number of [[img:icon_marks_of_ruination]][[/img]]Marks of Ruination collected and the units unlocked at various Ruination Levels can be tracked via the tooltips on the bar in the top left of the panel.\\n\\nTo the top right of the panel you can view your total [[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread and [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Favour.
There are four types of Rewards of Dread. These rewards can be viewed and purchased via their respective tabs.

Increasing the capacities of units costs [[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread and are purchased via the button below each unit group or unit.\\n\\nEach time you use [[img:icon_dread]][[/img]]Dread to expand the capacity of a unit group or unit, the cost of expanding capacity further increases with subsequent purchases.

In the Units tab, various units can have their factionwide recruitment capacities increased.\\n\\nSome units are grouped together so that when purchased, the capacities of all units in the group are increased.\\n\\nUnits can be recruited up to the purchased capacity by any horde in the faction, as long as the horde contains the correct buildings to recruit them.
To increase the capacity of a unit group or unit, you must first gain enough [[img:icon_marks_of_ruination]][[/img]]Marks of Ruination to reach the required Ruination Level.
In the Upgrades tab you can upgrade various aspects of your Herdstones, hordes and characters.
The Hell-Forge offers the use of forgecraft to improve your armies.\\n\\nHere weapons and armour are forged and modified to increase unit capacities and provide unit enhancements.
The Armoury is where you increase unit capacity.\\n\\nHere you can forge additional standard-issue weapons and armour at the cost of [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments to support more units.
Unit capacity is shared between all units in a group.\\n\\nThe number displays how many of these units the Armoury can support, i.e. the group's unit capacity.
Increasing unit capacity requires forging additional weapons and armour for the [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments cost specified here, which increases with every use.

Each time weapons and armour are forged in a unit category, the associated bar fills up to indicate the category’s increased total capacity.\\n\\nIncreasing total capacity gradually unlocks forgecraft options in the Manufactory tab. These are shown on the bar's tooltips.
The Manufactory becomes accessible once you unlock forgecraft options in the Armoury tab.

The Manufactory is where you enhance entire categories of units.\\n\\nForgecraft options are applied to units for an upkeep of [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments that keep assembly lines running.
Selecting a category allows you to view the units recruited and the list of potential forgecraft options to the right.\\n\\nOnce options are chosen from the list, they appear below the category.

Unit categories can only have a limited number of forgecraft lines active from the list at once.\\n\\nEnhancements remain active as long as the [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments upkeep can be met to keep lines in production.

The [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments upkeep cost for a category’s forgecraft options is multiplied by the number of units you have across your armies in the category.\\n\\nThe total upkeep breakdown is specified beneath the unit cards.
[[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour is received after battles or via Military Convoys.\\n\\nA portion of Labour is lost each turn based on your [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]]Control levels.

Labour Actions can instantly boost your [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Treasury, [[img:icon_conclave_influence]][[/img]]Conclave Influence or [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]]Control at the cost of [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour.
When received, [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour is split evenly between all provinces that are accepting new intake.\\n\\nYou can set a province to accept new intake via this checkbox.

The Chaos Dwarf economy is managed across several different resources: [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Treasury, [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour, [[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials and [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments.

[[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials are generated each turn from Outpost mine buildings.\\n\\nIf you have less [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour than [[img:icon_workload]][[/img]]Workload in a province, your Raw Materials output there will scale down accordingly.

You can relocate [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour at any point at the cost of [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Treasury.\\n\\nRelocating Labour removes it from one province and distributes it evenly between all others marked for new intake.

Buildings under construction will display the Rush Construction button.\\n\\nRush Construction allows you to instantly complete construction at the cost of [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour.\\n\\nThe cost scales based on the number of turns remaining.
Building more mines increases your potential [[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials output, but also increases your [[img:icon_workload]][[/img]]Workload requirement for that province.
The Labour Economy panel allows you to view and manage the [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour workforce across your provinces.
This checkbox allows you to specify whether or not a province will receive a share of any new [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour intake.
The Labour Actions buttons allow you to spend a province’s [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour to grant a variety of benefits.

The more [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour you have in a province, the lower your [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]]Control per turn will be.\\n\\nHere you can track which provinces might be struggling to maintain [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]]Control as [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour populations change.

[[img:icon_efficiency]][[/img]]Efficiency represents how much of a province’s [[img:icon_workload]][[/img]]Workload is being covered by its [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour.\\n\\nIf [[img:icon_efficiency]][[/img]]Efficiency drops below 100%, total [[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials output in the province will drop accordingly.
This section allows you to move [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour between provinces.

Transporting [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour between provinces has a treasury cost based on the total number being moved.\\n\\nOnce [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour is distributed you can confirm or reset your changes here.

If you change your mind about which settlement type you want later on, you can mouse over the primary building chain to convert it. Doing so will revert the settlement to tier 1 and destroy all secondary buildings.

The primary purpose of a factory is to generate [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments  and [[img:icon_treasury]][[/img]]Treasury. You will need to maintain enough [[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials income to support these buildings.
Towers are the focal point of the Chaos Dwarf empire. Constructing these will unlock the best recruitment and provide various global bonuses to increase your power.
You can increase the starting tier of towers by expending [[img:icon_conclave_influence]][[/img]]Conclave Influence.
When Chaos Dwarfs capture major settlements, they gain the option to rebuild the settlement as one of three different settlement types: Outposts, Factories or Towers.
When Chaos Dwarfs capture minor settlements, they gain the option to rebuild the settlement as one of two different settlement types: Outposts or Factories.

The primary purpose of an Outpost is to generate [[img:icon_raw_materials]][[/img]]Raw Materials from mines. [[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour is required in a province in order to meet the [[img:icon_workload]][[/img]]Workload required by them.
This list will show you what other settlement types you already have constructed in the province.
The Tower of Zharr consists of Seats which can be claimed to gain powerful rewards for your faction. All playable Chaos Dwarf factions compete to claim them.
Hover over a Seat to see its reward; click on one to claim it.
Claiming a Seat costs [[img:icon_conclave_influence]][[/img]]Conclave Influence. The amount required is displayed on each Seat.
Seats are grouped in Districts. There are three types of District: Sorcery, Military and Industry.
When all of the Seats in a District are claimed, a District completion bonus is granted. This reward is detailed here.\\n\\nDistrict completion bonuses are shared by all Chaos Dwarf factions.
You can see all of the Tower of Zharr rewards you have accumulated here. Click the Seats or Districts buttons to display their effects once claimed.

The Tower of Zharr is organised into four tiers, with each advancing tier unlocking greater rewards. To navigate between tiers you can select them on the navigation pane or scroll up and down.\\n\\nNext we will look at a higher tier.
Seats on the higher tiers are locked at the beginning of the campaign. To claim these Seats, at least two Districts must be completed on the previous tier.
[[col:yellow]]When your faction claims Seats in any Sorcery District it benefits from an increase in Winds of Magic Power Reserve Capacity.[[/col]]
[[col:yellow]]When your faction claims Seats in any Industry District it benefits from a reduction in Construction costs.[[/col]]
[[col:yellow]]When your faction claims Seats in any Military District it benefits from a reduction in Upkeep costs.[[/col]]

Repeatable Actions can be used multiple times throughout a campaign to enable Wizards to provide powerful aid to your armies, but are limited by a cooldown period.
Single-Use Actions grant rewards such as permanent Winds of Magic bonuses and special items.

{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_hp_campaign_point_1_plagues_of_nurgle}}\\n\\nAll Plagues are made up of three Symptoms from the panel, each providing both types of effects.
For every three Plagues created, Symptom locations in the panel will randomise and new Blessed Symptoms will appear.
Any Symptom previously used in a [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague will become available as a starting Symptom to create future Plagues.
Selecting an available Symptom begins the creation of a new [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague.
After selecting a starting Symptom, only adjacent Symptoms may be added to the [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague.\\n\\nAdjacent Symptoms will be highlighted in the panel as shown.

Symptoms can also become [[i]]Blessed[[/i]], boosting their effects.\\n\\nIf a Blessed Symptom is used in a [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague it will consume its blessing, no longer having its boosted effects for the next one.
When a Symptom is selected for a new [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague, its positive and negative effects for Nurgle and non-Nurgle factions respectively will be displayed here.

Once three Symptoms have been selected, the [[i]]Plague Modifiers[[/i]] will become available to improve the new [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague.\\n\\nPlagues can have their duration and chance to spread increased at the cost of [[img:icon_infections]][[/img]]Infections.

[[i]]Immunity[[/i]] duration can also be reduced as part of a Plague's Modifiers.\\n\\nThis is the number of turns that a plagued non-Nurgle target will resist catching any new Plagues after this one's effects expire.

Before the [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague can be created, it must be assigned a target where it will be released onto the campaign map.\\n\\nOnly [[img:icon_lord]][[/img]]forces and settlements you own can be selected as a target, revealed using this button.

Once a target for your [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague is selected, you can choose one of two creation methods.\\n\\nThe [[i]]Infect[[/i]] option directly infects your [[img:icon_lord]][[/img]]force or settlement with the [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague, from which it can spread.\\n\\nThe [[i]]Summon Cultist[[/i]] option brings forth a [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Plague Cultist who carries the [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]Plague to infect enemies directly via their agent action.

Equipping a Tactic requires [[img:grn_gorbad_planz]][[/img]] Planz.\\n\\n[[img:grn_gorbad_planz]][[/img]] Planz are earned each time Gorbad himself wins a battle.

Tactics are equipped for the selected slot via this button, spending your [[img:grn_gorbad_planz]][[/img]] Planz.\\n\\nIf a slot is already equipped with a Tactic, you can switch or unequip it instead, but doing so will place the unequipped Tactic on cooldown for a number of turns.

Tactics stay equipped for a limited duration, but as [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] increase in [[sl:campaign_character_skills]]rank[[/sl]] this duration increases, eventually allowing Tactics to be equipped indefinitely.

[[i]]"Brothers three shall bring low the Empire of Man. It is they who will muster the plague-kissed in their master’s name. It is they who will cast the world of hard-won progress into stagnation, bloated with foul contagions for Grandfather’s amusement.\\n\\nUnited, the Lords of Disease shall bring the Old World to Ruin – from within, and from without. All things clear and true shall sicken and fade with them, until only death holds the key to salvation."[[/i]]\\n\\nSo is the will of Nurgle, and so shall it be.\\n\\nLong have the Glottkin dreamt of bringing Nurgle’s Blessings to their parents' homeland, but it is not the time for rash action. For all its ignorance of the true gods, the Empire is a mighty foe. It will take the brothers time to unite the tribes of Norsca and to claim their rightful place as Nurgle’s Champion in these final days.\\n\\nThe Grandfather is slow, patient – and inexorable.\\n\\nSo too will be the Glottkin's vengeance.

We call upon the far-famed Golgfag of the Maneaters to bolster our offensive against our enemies, sow fear into their hearts and rain destruction upon their lands. For all of this, The Maneaters will be compensated accordingly.

We call upon you, fleshful beings. You will answer. Bring war to our hated enemy's land. Bring your thunder, bring your quaking hunger, bring your will to murder. Endless wealth we have, with some we shall part, in return. Thus says… (enormous list of titles follow).

Our long annals tell of your kind's prowess through time. It shall pass, and fall to naught, for only the Tomb Kings endure. Whilst your hunger reigns ascendant yet, we would give you means to satisfy it. Our foes' shall then tell tale of your exploits. You will be rewarded accordingly.
On the map, we have circled your targets. Below, we have listed our priorities. At the bottom, our payment. We forego claims to your loot. Our Bats will monitor your progress.

We are not unfamiliar with your company, if indeed the mercenaries we have encountered are part of it. If so, your strength is commendable. If not, they were weaklings and cowards, unworthy of your name. Here is your chance to prove your name yet again.

On behalf of them whom we serve, we relish the opportunity to tame your services in wreaking despair. Our rewards might seem a mere sop for your ever-yawning appetites, but the destruction you inflict at our behest may earn you something much more valuable: our moderate respect.

Unfortunately, your obstinate tribe can hardly be lulled into slavery by a mere piece of parchment. We are forced to offer you payment in return for our demands, which extend to being crueller and more merciless to our foe than we would be to ourselves. Our terms follow...

As much as it pains the Council to turn to your… expertise, we do hope this contract spells out in no uncertain terms that our enemy's pain should far surpass our own. You shall be afforded prizes proportional to your fulfilment of this stipulation.

In our ongoing conflict with the enemy, our Loremasters have deemed it a suitable compromise to supplement our main forces with your company's soldiers. We will officially denounce our involvement with your atrocities, and will provide sufficient payment upon completion.

Greetings, Bastard Children of the Old Ones! Our common creators' will is evident in your resilience, though their project's failure shows through in your haphazard savagery. Yet, we now have need of both against our foe. We feel you will find the nature of our rewards... familiar to you.

Unfinished Ones! Under our present circumstances, the contact we have established has been as fortuitous as it has been unlikely. We offer you prey whose fate deserves no show of subtlety or honour. We care not how you fulfil our terms – only that you do.
Tough-strong you are, we see. More smart-clever, too, than stupid. Skaven suffer many-many enemies… Murder-death-kill them. *This* time we pay! For real!
Food! We have much-much! Enemies we kill, but we save-store dead for later. Work well, work fast, hungry gut-things! We give what's left, for we are hungry, too!

[[i]]Bolgre wazzock[[/i]] that you are, we must make try and speak your tongue. We choke on your [[i]]isatu[[/i]]. We detest the ways of your [[i]]fleezh[[/i]]. Yet. We admit your [[i]]karaz[[/i]] girth. Serve and expect [[i]]wulthrungz[[/i]]. Elsewise: [[i]]ezent[[/i]] to you and your clan, without end.

As one tasked with the ignominy of rendering the will of Fire and Stone in slithering common-tongue syllables, I shall be brief: accept our offer. Riches offered, we do not dole out lightly. Strike at our foe. Slaughter as you will. Claim your prize.

The Dragons have long harboured resentment towards you. Yet, we have seen you teach yourself the ways of the world. Remember your learning as you consider the penurious merits of our offer. Forget them as you punish our foe.

Our prior dealings with your kind along the Ivory Road has convinced us that some of you have acquired a bare modicum of reason and a speck of civilised disposition. Thus, we offer a transaction: wondrous Cathayan boons in return for your savagery, conscientiously deployed.

Kislev has ever had need of war-worthy allies. While we would not go as far as to call you allies, we well understand your stubborn defiance of Chaotic corruption and your animalistic spirit. Our enemy must be broken. We shall compensate you both for your victories and your losses.

The Gospodars say this: you harbour ancient ice in your veins, like our Ungol. You harbour a wandering spirit, like our Dolgan. You possess common sense enough to work under contract. Your skill and ferocity are judged worthy of furthering our cause... for the time being.

Oi! Youse the *real* Maneaters, yeah? Got a job for ye, er, in the name of the Maw. Or 'cause there's gold in't for ye. Whichever ye like. Just get it done and kill them gits. Ye can eat them all by yerselves!
There's slims need killin'. You in? Enough t'make breakfast, lunch an' dinner! We'll see about what else we throw ya, ye Maneaters like yer thingumbobs, yeah?

Your kind's brutish demeanour and savagery have some use in this world. We would be foolish not to appreciate this in times of war. Consider our need as we reach out to you, but do not take this as an offer of friendship. Needs must. Consider our offer. Should you renege... we will find you.

The venal inclinations of your company are but an offshoot of your nature. We know better than to nurture unnecessary resentment. You care not whom you fight; it might as well be our enemy. You seek riches, yes, but also strength. This, too, we can provide.
Show us your skill at slaughter. We must see, and learn, and know your strength. We give you victims. Burn, crush, devour. Then, we pay.
You would sell yourselves to us who serve the Ruinous Powers. We value your ruthlessness. We are more similar than you think. Cut a grizzly path through our foes. Reap your savage reward.

Bretonnia hereby extends its official offer to hire your tribe as supremely qualified domestic help. As it happens, certain lands currently possessed by our enemies have been marked out for gentrification. We ask that you occupy and safeguard our burgeoning homesteads, as follows...

This, the oath you take, hereby vowing to fulfil the will of a Duke of Bretonnia, and carry out a sacred pilgrimage as part of your lawful conversion to Our Lady. The remuneration hopes to alleviate hardships you may endure at the hand of any evil-doers in your path.

The Dammaz Kron decrees that we have been wronged in such a way so as to seek reprisal against our enemy, yet not raise our own hand in doing so. And so, we leave that to you. Our hands, we shall occupy with crafting suitable rewards.
The Sons of Grungni bid you chase down our foes and drown them in the waters of misfortune, that they may know the tools of punishment we make use of are as numerous as the Grudges we hold.

The Empire requests aid. Your mission is not meant to decide our dispute with the target. It will instead convey the… seriousness of our intentions, and the lengths we are willing to go to. We will secure the necessary payment.

The Empire has traded steel and strong words with our enemy for long enough; we call upon your services to deliver them something they will have no response to. Sigmar's Hammer takes many forms – you are to be one of them. Expect ample recompense.
You kill them gitz, we give you meat, money, tings. For those, see picture. For them gitz, see corpse we sent. Eat corpse, do *not* eat contract!
Youse as big as our Troll, but you unnerstan' an' remember wordz. So we sayz, kill our en'my. Kill them good and we get you prizes. Big 'Unz t'fight, small 'unz to eat.

Your kind worships hunger, and venerates strength. We would think this is as far as our similarities extend. Yet your company's soldiers employ cunning, albeit debased, and profit from misery. We are intrigued and would make use of your idiosyncrasies. Here is what we propose...

The messenger delivering this contract would sever your souls from your bones in a heartbeat. Dare not refuse. Do these words make your blood boil, Maneaters? Save it for the enemy you are to assail. The proposed rewards serve as proof of how seriously we have considered this offer.

[[col:link]]The Hunt for Ariel[[/col]]\\nIn the Vortex Campaign, Throt seeks to find and consume Ariel, Queen of the Wood Elves. To do so, he must disrupt her ritual in order to draw her out. This can be done by capturing certain settlements. Each settlement captured will delay Ariel’s ritual and make the final battle to defeat her easier.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_flesh_lab]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Flesh Laboratory[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Flesh Laboratory allows Clan Moulder to grow, mutate, splice and surgically alter monsters and minions to make them more dangerous on the battlefield. Troops can be upgraded with Augmentations with the use of [[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]]Mutagen, which is collected whenever packs of monsters are claimed from the lab’s Growth Vat. To grow new units in the vat, Clan Moulder must first harvest [[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]]Growth Juice by fighting battles or recycling units that have become [[img:icon_instability]][[/img]]unstable due to Augmentation.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_skaven_underworld]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Skaven Under-Empire[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Skaven can lurk beneath any settlement or ruin, growing their empire by either occupying regions or establishing [[img:icon_under_empire]][[/img]]Under-Cities beneath them. Left undetected for too long, their malevolent scheming can result in hordes of vermin rising up to [[img:icon_corruption_skv]][[/img]]corrupt the land or assault illustrious cities without warning.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_food]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Food[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nSkaven factions require a stockpile of [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food, each army consuming an amount of [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]food per turn. [[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]]Food may be acquired through battles, by sacking settlements, and from certain buildings.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_corruption]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Skaven Corruption[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Skaven spread [[img:icon_corruption_skv]][[/img]]corruption wherever they settle, lowering [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]]control over time but giving additional uses of the [[url:script_link_campaign_the_menace_below]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_the_menace_below}}]]Menace Below[[/tooltip]][[/url]] army ability during battles fought within the local province.\\n\\nLearn more about the Skaven [[url:script_link_campaign_skaven]]here[[/url]].

[[img:bullet_lzd_horde]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Expand Nakai’s special[[/col]] [[sl_link:campaign_hordes]]horde[[/sl_link]] [[col:green]]army to unlock units that can be recruited by any of his hordes via the[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_jungle_nexus]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_jungle_nexus}}]]Jungle Nexus.[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_green]][[/img]][[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_blue]][[/img]][[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_red]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Conquer settlements across the world to dedicate to the Old Ones by constructing[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_defence_great_plan]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_defence_great_plan}}]]temples[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]in return for their Favour and rewards.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_lzd_nakai_favour]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Use earned Favour to unlock special units offered in the[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_defence_great_plan]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_defence_great_plan}}]]Temples of the Old Ones[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]and for the research of powerful technologies.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_slann_mage_priest]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Progress through the campaign to unlock the devastatingly powerful Hero[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_lord_kroak]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_lord_kroak}}]]Lord Kroak[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]and wield his settlement-crumbling powers.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:bullet_lzd_spawning]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Complete[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_blessed_spawnings]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_blessed_spawnings}}]]Blessed Spawnings[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]missions to periodically recruit formidable units.[[/col]]\\n\\nLearn more about Lizardmen [[url:script_link_campaign_lizardmen]]here[[/url]].

[[col:green]]Nagash’s goal is to claim [[i]]all[[/i]] the world’s souls for himself by spreading his [[img:icon_land_of_the_dead]][[/img]][[sl_link:campaign_land_of_the_dead]]Land of the Dead[[/sl_link]][[col:green]]. [[img:icon_ogr_meat]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Use the[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_meat]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_meat}}]]Meat[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]harvested from your armies’ exploits to keep them fed and increase combat effectiveness in turn, or send surpluses to the Great Maw in return for powerful advantages.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:bullet_ogr_camps]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Build and expand[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_ogre_camps]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_ogre_camps}}]]Ogre Camps[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]at the cost of your armies’ Meat stockpiles in return for higher-tier buildings and other advantages over permanent settlements.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:bullet_ogr_big_names]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Complete challenges with eligible characters to grant them[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_big_names]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_big_names}}]]Big Names[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]which come with various bonuses and abilities.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_ogr_contracts]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Complete[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_contracts]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_contracts}}]]Bounties[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]issued by other factions for military action against targeted characters and settlements in return for rewards and improved diplomatic relations.[[/col]]\\n\\nLearn more about the Ogre Kingdoms [[url:script_link_campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]here[[/url]].

[[url:script_link_campaign_forge_of_daith]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Forge of Daith[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Sisters of Twilight have access to unique items and armaments crafted in the [[img:icon_forge_of_daith]][[/img]]Forge of Daith. Lord Daith, most celebrated of Elven smiths, uses his legendary smithing skills to forge and upgrade special equipment for them as favours in return for their successes in battle. Daith can indulge Naestra’s obsession with perfectly honing her equipment by permanently upgrading them for her, or accept Arahan’s ardent insistence to carry powerfully reforged equipment into battle, albeit with temporary effects.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_worldroots]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]The Worldroots & Magical Forests[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Oak of Ages’ life-giving Worldroots have seeded a number of Magical Forests across the world, but over time interlopers and neglect have caused them to wither. By performing various actions such as securing the [[img:heathland_pacified]][[/img]][[img:heathland_hostile]][[/img]][[img:heathland_neutral]][[/img]]Heathland regions that border them, the Wood Elves can increase the [[img:forest_health]][[/img]]health of Magical Forests and perform Rituals of Rebirth there, thus permanently restoring their connection to the Worldroots.\\n\\nAll Wood Elf armies can use the [[img:icon_use_beastpaths_stance]][[/img]]Worldroots stance to travel short distances beneath otherwise impassable terrain. Doing so is not without risk, however, as they can be intercepted by armies above and brought to battle, even by races that cannot use the Worldroots themselves.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_worldroots]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]The Deeproots[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe Deeproots connect all Magical Forests of the world, allowing the Wood Elves to instantaneously travel between different continents with ease. They can be accessed from within any Magical Forest region regardless of ownership, but once an army traverses them it will be some time before another journey can be made.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_oak_of_ages]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Oak of Ages[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nAll Worldroots lead back to the Oak of Ages. By securing Athel Loren’s borders and healing other Magical Forests, the Wood Elves can rejuvenate the Worldroots’ life-giving powers. The ultimate goal of the Wood Elves’ Immortal Empires campaign is to complete the Ritual of Rebirth in Athel Loren and defend the Oak.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_elven_council]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Offices[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nA variety of benefits may be gained by appointing [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords to positions of Office.\\n\\nLearn more about the Wood Elves [[url:script_link_campaign_wood_elves]]here[[/url]].

[[img:icon_under_empire]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Establish unseen[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_skaven_underworld]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_skaven_underworld}}]]Under-Cities[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]beneath settlements you defeat and secretly expand them to aid your malevolent schemes and spread Skaven corruption.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_skaven_food]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Keep your faction’s[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_food]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_food}}]]food[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]supplies at high levels throughout your campaign to gain factionwide bonuses and avoid debilitating effects.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_corruption_skv]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Spread Skaven corruption over extended periods wherever you settle to infest areas with[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_the_menace_below]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_the_menace_below}}]]summonable Clanrats[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]and make provinces difficult to inhabit.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:bullet_skv_underway]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Use the[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_underway]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_underway}}]]Underway[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]stance to avoid obstacles on the campaign map.[[/col]]\\n\\nLearn more about the Skaven [[url:script_link_campaign_skaven]]here[[/url]].

[[col:green]]Grey Seer Thanquol occupies a hidden base south of Sylvania, preparing to send out Underlings to enact his [[/col]][[sl_link:campaign_chaotic_plans]]Masterplans[[/sl_link]].\\n\\n[[col:green]]More than other Skaven, Thanquol covets amassing [[img:icon_warpstone]][[/img]]Warpstone and takes extra care to either steal it or mine it in secret [[/col]][[url:script_link_campaign_skaven_underworld]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_skaven_underworld}}]]Under-Cities[[/tooltip]][[/url]].\\n\\n[[col:green]]Establish a foothold in the mountains east of the Empire, upgrade your Underlings with Warpstone, complete Masterplans and succeed in a task from the Council of 13 to secure[[/col]] [[col:yellow]]campaign victory![[/col]]\\n\\nLearn more about the Skaven [[url:script_link_campaign_skaven]]here[[/url]].

[[img:skv_snikch_schemes]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Use Schemes that become available during the campaign to carry out unfailing actions of espionage, sabotage and death as part of Clan Eshin’s[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_skaven_shadowy_dealings]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_skaven_shadowy_dealings}}]]Shadowy Dealings.[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_shadowy_dealings]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Take on Contracts issued by backstabbing Skaven clans to act against their rivals for rewards and positive effects while heeding the diplomatic consequences.[[/col]]\\n\\n

[[img:icon_growth_juice]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Accumulate Growth Juice throughout your campaign to claim units and monsters from the Growth Vat along with Mutagen by-product for the[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_flesh_lab]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_flesh_lab}}]]Flesh Laboratory.[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_mutagen]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Use Mutagen to augment individual units in your armies, while taking heed of instability effects that may degrade them or shorten their life span.[[/col]]\\n\\n

[[col:green]]Skulltaker's only concern is to kill worthy [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords in battle to harvest their [[img:icon_champions_essence]][[/img]]Champion's Essence, which he siphons into the[[/col]] [[sl_link:campaign_cloak_of_skulls]]Cloak of Skulls[[/sl_link]] [[col:green]]to augment his power and abilities.[[/col]]\\n\\n{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_how_they_play_khorne_02}}\\n\\n[[col:green]]With the reaped[[/col]] [[img:icon_champions_essence]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Essence of beheaded foes, empower the Cloak of Skulls and bring forth the world’s destruction to achieve [[/col]][[col:yellow]][[b]]campaign victory[[/b]][[/col]][[col:green]] in the Blood God’s name![[/col]]\\n\\n{{tr:advice_info_texts_localised_text_war.camp.advice.khorne.info_003}}

[[img:icon_disciple_army]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Take your forces into areas of sufficient Slaanesh corruption and raise[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_disciple_armies]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_disciple_armies}}]]Disciple Armies[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]to support your invasions.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_gift_of_slaanesh]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Defeat enemies and perform successful Hero actions to give enemy characters[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_gifts_of_slaanesh]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_gifts_of_slaanesh}}]]Gifts of Slaanesh[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]that impose negative effects upon them and can earn you more followers.[[/col]]\\n\\nLearn more about Slaanesh [[url:script_link_campaign_slaanesh]]here[[/url]].

[[img:icon_devotees]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Gather[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_devotees]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_devotees}}]]Devotees[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]throughout your campaign to spend on[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_pleasurable_acts]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_pleasurable_acts}}]]Pleasurable Acts[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]that benefit your home regions, or proliferate[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_chaos_cults]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_chaos_cults}}]]cults[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]to debilitate foreign lands and earn more followers.[[/col]]

[[img:icon_seductive_influence]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Interact with human, Elf, or Beastmen factions in various ways to build up[[/col]] [[url:script_link_campaign_seductive_influence]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_seductive_influence}}]]Seductive Influence[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]over them which can eventually lead to vassalisation.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[img:icon_seductive_influence]][[/img]] [[col:green]]Sufficiently increase [[url:script_link_campaign_seductive_influence]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_seductive_influence}}]]Seductive Influence[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]to enable N'kari's [[i]]Lord Seduction[[/i]] action, forcing enemy Lords to defect and become Chaos Lords in his faction.[[/col]]

[[img:icon_seductive_influence]][[/img]] [[url:script_link_campaign_seduction]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_seduction}}]]Seduce[[/tooltip]][[/url]] [[col:green]]enemy units before battles to have them join your side for the battle durations.[[/col]]

[[url:script_link_campaign_defence_great_plan]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Temples of the Old Ones[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nThe success of the Old Ones’ Great Plan hangs in the balance! Defeat foreign invaders and reclaim the Lizardmen’s ancient lost cities, installing the [[img:bullet_lzd_spawnings_of_the_ancients]][[/img]]Defenders of the Great Plan as their rightful owners. The Defenders will maintain the temple-cities gifted to them.\\n\\nDevoting yourself to an [[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_green]][[/img]][[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_blue]][[/img]][[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple_red]][[/img]]Old One by constructing [[img:icon_lzd_nakai_temple]][[/img]]temples in their name will please them immeasurably, providing a raft of rewards and earning [[img:icon_lzd_nakai_favour]][[/img]]Favour which can then be used to unlock powerful units and technologies.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_jungle_nexus]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Jungle Nexus[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nNakai resides at the centre of the [[img:bullet_lzd_horde]][[/img]]jungle nexus and has the ability to recruit units directly from the global recruitment pool, to which he has personal access. Developing Nakai's recruitment buildings will enable other hordes in his faction to share in their progress.\\n\\n[[url:script_link_campaign_warmblood_invaders]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_how_to_play_title}}]]Warmblood Invaders[[/tooltip]][[/url]]\\nOver the centuries, many have attempted to pillage Lustria’s temple-cities for their great wealth. The Army Abilities panel is shown on the right side of the screen when army abilities are available for use.
Supply locations within a settlement are each linked to multiple build locations where [[sl:battle_constructed_defences]]constructed defences[[/sl]] can be built.
Place the cursor over a supply location to see what build locations it is linked to.

[[img:icon_supplies]][[/img]][[sl:battle_supplies]]Supplies[[/sl]] may be used by the defender in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] or [[sl:battle_minor_settlement_battles]]minor settlement battle[[/sl]] to construct defences.
Defences may be constructed at build locations throughout a settlement.
Each build location is linked to a nearby supply-point [[sl:battle_capture_locations]]capture location[[/sl]].
Defences may be constructed during the fighting in response to the progress of the battle.

The defender in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] or [[sl:battle_minor_settlement_battles]]minor settlement battle[[/sl]] may use [[img:icon_supplies]][[/img]][[sl:battle_supplies]]Supplies[[/sl]] to construct defences at build locations throughout the settlement.
Should the defender lose control of the capture location, they will no longer be able to build defences linked to it. Any constructed defences will also be destroyed.
[[sl:battle_units]]Units[[/sl]] may be arranged for the coming fight during the deployment phase of the battle.
Once deployment is completed the battle begins.

There are a variety of more advanced methods for issuing instructions to selected [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] once [[sl:battle_unit_movement]]basic manoeuvring[[/sl]] is learned. Use the cursor keys to nudge [[sl:battle_unit_selection]]selected[[/sl]] units into position, for example.
The advisor appears from time to time to offer his assistance to the player. The level of advice can be reduced or minimised through the game options.

An ambush battle is fought when one [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] surprises another on the campaign map. The defender starts the battle surrounded by the attacker, with no chance to [[sl:battle_deployment]]deploy[[/sl]].
[[sl:battle_battle_game]]Battles[[/sl]] are contested by armies, each of which is made up of many troop [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]]. The player commands an army when taking part in a battle.

Each [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] in [[sl:battle_battle_game]]battle[[/sl]] bears an amount of armour which protects them from physical damage inflicted by [[sl:battle_infantry]]melee[[/sl]] or [[sl:battle_missile_units]]missile[[/sl]] attacks during [[sl:battle_melee_combat]]combat[[/sl]].

[[sl:battle_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] may occasionally enter battle with army-wide abilities that are not tied to the [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:battle_the_general]]Lord[[/sl]] or to an individual [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]]. If available, army abilities may be browsed and activated from the [[sl_tooltip:battle_army_abilities_panel]]Army Abilities panel[[/sl_tooltip]].
The Army Abilities panel is only shown when army abilities are available.

Artillery [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]], such as cannons and catapults, can fire projectiles at the enemy over long distances. They are most useful against bunched [[sl:battle_infantry]]infantry[[/sl]] formations, [[sl:battle_monsters]]monsters[[/sl]], and the [[sl:battle_walls]]walls[[/sl]] of fortified cities.

Battles are fought between [[sl:battle_armies]]armies[[/sl]] to conquer or defend territory. Battles are won by killing or routing all enemy [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]], or by capturing the enemy settlement during a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]].

The battle interface is made up of many separate elements such as the [[sl_tooltip:battle_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl_tooltip]] and its [[sl:battle_unit_cards]]Unit cards[[/sl]], the [[sl_tooltip:battle_radar_map]]radar map[[/sl_tooltip]], the [[sl:battle_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]] panel and the [[sl_tooltip:battle_unit_portrait_panel]]Unit Portrait panel[[/sl_tooltip]].
Khorne, the Chaos God of Blood and the Lord of Murder, exalts in endless slaughter. His blessings will be visited on those who shed blood in His name.
The Blood for the Blood God meter is only shown when playing a Khornate faction.
Move the camera in battle with the W, A, S and D keys. Orient the camera by holding the middle mouse button, and change the camera height with the scroll wheel.
Place the cursor over a victory or supply location icon to see more information about it.

Defensive features of a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] or [[sl:battle_minor_settlement_battles]]minor settlement battle[[/sl]] such as [[sl:battle_gates]]gates[[/sl]], [[sl:battle_towers]]towers[[/sl]] and [[sl:battle_constructed_defences]]constructed defences[[/sl]] are all linked to capture locations. Whoever holds a capture location controls the features linked to it.
Members of the Cathayan imperial household are beings of tremendous power. They may transform from human to Dragon form (and back again) during combat, gaining different advantages when in each form.
The Drop Siege Equipment button is shown at the bottom of the screen when a unit that is carrying siege equipment is selected.
While the accuracy of a zombie firing a gun remains questionable, the damage caused by the pirate gunners of the Vampire Coast is increased while their ammunition level remains high.

Tzeentch, the Chaos God of Magic and Change, is drawn to those who wield magic in his name. He exalts in sorcery, and His benevolence will be visited upon those who crush the foe with incantations and [[sl:battle_spells]]spells[[/sl]].
The Eye of Tzeentch meter is only shown when playing a Tzeentchian faction.

Fire-at-Will is a [[sl:battle_unit_abilities]]unit ability[[/sl]] shared by all [[sl:battle_missile_units]]missile units[[/sl]]. When firing-at-will, [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] select their own targets to shoot at unless told otherwise.
[[sl:battle_units]]Units[[/sl]] fight most effectively against an enemy in front of them. {{tr:hp_battle_leadership_flanking_01}}
Some [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] fly high over the [[sl:battle_terrain]]terrain[[/sl]], either attacking at range or descending to engage the enemy in hand-to-hand fighting.
Multiple [[sl:battle_unit_selection]]selected units[[/sl]] may be assigned into a preset formation, in which they automatically take up positions in a specific arrangement.
The Formations button is shown at the bottom of the screen on the battle interface, and becomes active when more than one unit is selected.
Settlement gates are points of entry to a fortified city. They are key weak points that may be attacked in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]].
The Group button is shown at the bottom of the screen on the battle interface, and becomes active when any unit is selected.

A selection of [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] may be grouped by clicking the [[sl_tooltip:battle_group_button]]Group button[[/sl_tooltip]] so that they may be easily re-selected in future. Grouped units are arranged together under a tab on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl_tooltip]].
The Guard button is shown at the bottom of the screen on the battle interface, and becomes active when any unit that can guard is selected.
The Cathayans embrace of Harmony extends even to their martial practices. When complementary Cathayan [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] are close to one another, their combat performance is improved.

Infantry [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] are dense formations of men armed with [[sl:battle_melee_combat]]hand-to-hand weapons[[/sl]]. Massed ranks of infantry are the mainstay of most [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] compositions.
The sorcery of Tzeentch offers protection to His followers. All daemons that fight for the Raven God in battle are shielded from attack by magical barriers.

Major siege battles are fought over [[sl:battle_walls]]walled[[/sl]] cities. The attacker can capture the city by either [[sl:battle_leadership]]routing[[/sl]] all defending [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] or by capturing and holding one or more [[sl:battle_victory_locations]]victory locations[[/sl]].

As with other elements within the Celestial Empire, the Sorcerers of Cathay work best when they work together. Cathayan Sorcerers gain power with each additional magic-user who joins their [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]].

The outcome of any combat between [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] rests on many factors. The number of soldiers involved, their quality, size, [[sl:battle_vigour]]vigour[[/sl]], [[sl:battle_leadership]]leadership level[[/sl]], relative positioning and more are all factors in determining the result of any engagement.
The Melee Mode button is shown at the bottom of the screen on the battle interface, and becomes active when any unit that can toggle melee mode is selected.
Missile [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] are best employed in battle to stand back from the action and fire projectiles at the enemy.
Monsters and giants are huge, powerful creatures that inspire terror into their enemies. They are best used for scattering and disrupting formations of enemy [[sl:battle_infantry]]infantry[[/sl]].
Mounted [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] are able to move quickly across [[sl:battle_terrain]]terrain[[/sl]], either in support of allied troops or to strike at the enemy where they are weakest.

Dark Elves perform worship to Khaine, the god of murder, through the shedding of blood in [[sl:battle_battle_game]]battle[[/sl]]. A Dark Elf [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] will receive favour in the form of increased combat performance should they kill enough enemies during battle.

Nurgle, the Chaos God of Disease and the Lord of Pestilence, is also the God of Death by Rebirth. His benevolence is most keenly felt by those in need of His healing powers in [[sl:battle_battle_game]]battle[[/sl]].
The Plague Lord's Blessings meter is only shown when playing a Nurglish faction.

[[sl:battle_units]]Units[[/sl]] that are [[sl:battle_leadership]]routing[[/sl]] from the battlefield may rally and begin responding to orders again once they have retreated a safe distance from the enemy.
Certain Lizardmen [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] may rampage when they take too much damage in battle. Rampaging units will continue to fight but will no longer respond to orders.

As Tomb Kings warriors die on the battlefield, their spirits enter the Realm of Souls. As the Realm of Souls fills past certain thresholds, the [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] that remain will regenerate for short periods.

The Daemons of Chaos exalt in the subjugation of their enemies in battle. Glory is earned when a Daemon Prince lord or their Herald Lord followers inflict damage on enemy [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]].
Glory is only earned in battle by Daemon Prince lords, or their Herald lord followers.

Additional [[sl:battle_armies]]armies[[/sl]] drawn into a battle on the campaign map appear as reinforcements. Reinforcing armies appear at the edge of the battlefield [[sl:battle_terrain]]terrain[[/sl]] during the fighting.

Slaanesh, the Chaos God of Pleasure and the Lord of Excess, delights in new playthings. His favour will fall upon those who kill in His name, for a portion of those who fall can be revived so they truly know the meaning of pain…
The Sensuous Seductions meter is only shown when playing a Slaaneshi faction.
The attacker in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] may use rams and siege towers to destroy or overcome the settlement fortifications.

Some [[sl:battle_missile_units]]missile units[[/sl]] can skirmish, whereby they automatically retreat when the enemy get too close. The skirmish ability may be toggled on a selected [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] with the [[sl_tooltip:battle_skirmish_button]]Skirmish button[[/sl_tooltip]].

[[sl:battle_wizards]]Wizards[[/sl]] may cast powerful spells to turn the tide of battle. Available spells are shown on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_winds_of_magic_panel]]Winds of Magic panel[[/sl_tooltip]] when a Wizard unit is selected.

Such is the power of the [[sl:battle_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]] within the Realm of Chaos that Storms of Magic may sometimes occur. [[sl:battle_battle_game]]Battles[[/sl]] fought within them are subject to extreme levels of magic.

The defender in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] or [[sl:battle_minor_settlement_battles]]minor settlement battle[[/sl]] will earn [[img:icon_supplies]][[/img]]Supplies from any supply-point [[sl:battle_capture_locations]]capture locations[[/sl]] they hold. [[img:icon_supplies]][[/img]]Supplies may be spent on [[sl:battle_constructed_defences]]constructing defences[[/sl]].
Survival Battles may be fought at key points in a campaign. Key locations on the battlefield must be claimed, and multiple waves of enemy troops defeated, before victory can be claimed.
The Tactical Map provides a birds-eye view of the entire battlefield at once. Press the TAB key to toggle it on and off.

Terrain features on the battlefield can play a decisive role in any battle. Hills, mountains, forests and rivers can be used to [[sl:battle_visibility]]conceal troops[[/sl]] or funnel an enemy’s advance.
Each [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] is led by a [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord in battle, who leads and encourages the troops with many unique [[sl:battle_unit_abilities]]abilities[[/sl]].
If a time limit applies in the current battle it will be shown at the top of the battle interface.
The defences of a fortified city will usually include fortified towers that can shoot missiles at attackers within their range of fire.
Most [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] have abilities that modify the unit’s behaviour or improve its capabilities for a short time. These can be activated or deactivated as the situation demands.

Each [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] in the player’s army is represented on the [[sl:battle_battle_interface]]battle interface[[/sl]] by a Unit card. These are shown on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl_tooltip]].

The Unit Details panel shows detailed information about the selected [[sl:battle_units]]unit’s[[/sl]] fighting strength. It can be toggled on and off with the [[sl_tooltip:battle_unit_details_button]]Unit Details button[[/sl_tooltip]] on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_unit_portrait_panel]]Unit Portrait panel[[/sl_tooltip]].

A [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] may be selected by either left-clicking it on the battlefield or by left-clicking on the associated [[sl:battle_unit_cards]]Unit card[[/sl]] on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl_tooltip]]. Units must be selected before they can be issued with [[sl:battle_unit_movement]]orders[[/sl]].

A [[sl:battle_units]]unit’s[[/sl]] type broadly defines its capabilities, strengths and weaknesses. [[sl:battle_mounted_units]]Mounted units[[/sl]], for example, are generally swift but vulnerable against [[sl:battle_weapon_types]]spear weapons[[/sl]].
{{tr:hp_battle_units_add_01}} Each unit is independently controllable and represented on the [[sl:battle_battle_interface]]battle interface[[/sl]] by a [[sl:battle_unit_cards]]Unit card[[/sl]].

The Major Victory location and Key Building location found at the heart of a fortified city may be captured by the attacker in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]] to gain [[sl_tooltip:battle_victory_tickets]]victory tickets[[/sl_tooltip]]. {{tr:hp_battle_victory_locations_add_04}}
The [[img:icon_victory_tickets]][[/img]]Victory Tickets currently held by the attacker are indicated on the progress bar at the top of the battle interface.

Soldiers tire as they [[sl:battle_unit_movement]]run[[/sl]] and fight, meaning that they cannot engage in combat as effectively. The vigour level of a [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] is shown on its tooltip.

Hills and other [[sl:battle_terrain]]terrain[[/sl]] features that block line-of-sight can be used to conceal [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] from the enemy. An [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] must have line-of-sight to an enemy in order for it to be visible.
Fortified settlements are surrounded by walls, on which the defender may position [[sl:battle_units]]troops[[/sl]] to resist the attacker.

[[sl:battle_infantry]]Infantry[[/sl]], [[sl:battle_mounted_units]]mounted units[[/sl]] and other types of [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] may bear different types of weapon in battle, each type being suited to different purposes.

The Winds of Magic provide [[sl:battle_wizards]]spellcasters[[/sl]] with their source of power. The available magic is depleted when a [[sl:battle_spells]]spell[[/sl]] is cast, but recharges slowly over time.

Magic-wielding Wizard [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]] may tap into the [[sl:battle_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]] to cast powerful [[sl:battle_spells]]spells[[/sl]]. These spells can be used to empower allies or to sow destruction amongst the caster’s enemies.
Large, powerful units like [[sl:battle_monsters]]monsters[[/sl]] and giants are particularly effective against settlement gates.
The [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership level of a [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] is a measure of its will to continue fighting.
The [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership level of a unit is affected by several factors, such as casualties taken and being attacked in the flank.
A unit will take more casualties and its [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]][[sl:battle_leadership]]leadership level[[/sl]] will suffer when attacked in the flank or the rear.
If the [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership level of a unit drops too low then the troops will rout from the battlefield and stop responding to orders.
Most [[sl:battle_infantry]]infantry[[/sl]] units can scale walls using ladders.
Minor settlement battles are fought over smaller settlements that lack fortified [[sl:battle_walls]]walls[[/sl]].
The attacker can win the battle and capture the settlement by defeating all defending [[sl:battle_units]]units[[/sl]].

The defender should seek to stop the attacker from gaining control of any [[sl:battle_victory_locations]]victory locations[[/sl]] - particularly the Major Victory Location, which grants its holder a large number of [[img:icon_victory_tickets]][[/img]][[sl_tooltip:battle_victory_tickets]]Victory Tickets[[/sl_tooltip]] over time.
Damage caused to the city in battle will be reflected on the campaign map afterwards.
Hold shift when right-clicking to enqueue a waypoint, or hold shift and drag a path for units with the right mouse button.
Advice history can be navigated using the [[sl_tooltip:battle_advice_history_buttons]]back and forwards button[[/sl_tooltip]] on the Advisor panel.
The defending army is surprised on the march, and starts the battle in an unfavourable position on the battlefield.
Orders are given to units in an army, not individual soldiers.
The armour level of a [[sl:battle_unit_selection]]selected unit[[/sl]] and the strength of any shield that they bear is indicated on the [[sl:battle_unit_details_panel]]Unit Details panel[[/sl]].
The costs, effects and cooldowns of an army ability may be viewed by placing the cursor over an army ability button.
Artillery units move slowly, and their crews are vulnerable if engaged in hand-to-hand fighting.
Armies may [[sl:battle_deployment]]deploy[[/sl]] their troops prior to battle, unless they have been [[sl:battle_ambush_battles]]ambushed[[/sl]].
The [[sl_tooltip:battle_balance_of_power]]balance of power indicator[[/sl_tooltip]] shows the current relative strengths of allied versus enemy forces.

When playing as a Khornate faction, a [[sl_tooltip:battle_blood_for_the_blood_god_meter]]progress meter[[/sl_tooltip]] on the [[sl:battle_battle_interface]]battle interface[[/sl]] builds as kills are made. Kills made by either side in a [[sl:battle_battle_game]]battle[[/sl]] count towards the total.
The camera may also be rotated with the Q and E keys, and the camera height may be adjusted with Z and X.

[[sl:battle_gates]]Gates[[/sl]] and [[sl:battle_towers]]towers[[/sl]] in a fortified city are each linked to a nearby capture location. Should the attacker capture a capture location linked to a gate or tower then they will gain use of it.
Units can be placed anywhere within their deployment area. They are immediately repositioned when moved.

Cathayan Legendary Lords may be transformed from human to Dragon form by using the Transformation of the Dragon [[sl:battle_unit_abilities]]unit ability[[/sl]], shown around the [[sl:battle_unit_details_panel]]Unit Details panel[[/sl]] when the Lord's [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] is selected.

The Extra Powder [[sl:battle_unit_abilities]]unit ability[[/sl]] increases the damage of [[sl:battle_missile_units]]missile units[[/sl]] in a Vampire Coast [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]] while their ammunition level is above 80% of its starting value.

When playing as a Tzeentchian faction, a [[sl_tooltip:battle_eye_of_tzeentch_meter]]progress meter[[/sl_tooltip]] on the [[sl:battle_battle_interface]]battle interface[[/sl]] builds as [[sl:battle_spells]]spells[[/sl]] are cast by Tzeentchian forces.
Toggle fire-at-will on a selected unit with the [[sl_tooltip:battle_fire_at_will_button]]Fire-at-Will button[[/sl_tooltip]].
A unit will suffer a sudden drop to its [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership level if charged in the flank or rear. If the shock is great enough the unit may break and rout.
Like [[sl:battle_mounted_units]]mounted units[[/sl]], flying units can be rapidly deployed to strike at a vulnerable target or reinforce a weak point in the [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]].
Available formations may be browsed by clicking on the [[sl_tooltip:battle_formations_button]]Formations button[[/sl_tooltip]] when multiple units are selected.
Gates present key points of weakness that may be assaulted with [[sl:battle_siege_weapons]]battering rams[[/sl]], [[sl:battle_artillery]]artillery[[/sl]], or melee units.
A unit group may be selected by clicking the tab shown on the Army panel, or by pressing the number key shown on the tab.

All Cathayan units except [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:battle_the_general]]Lords[[/sl]] and [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes are aligned to either Yin or Yang. A unit’s alignment is displayed on its [[sl:battle_unit_cards]]Unit card[[/sl]].

Infantry units are often heavily armed and may be [[sl:battle_armour]]armoured[[/sl]], but are generally slow and vulnerable to being outranged by [[sl:battle_missile_units]]missile units[[/sl]] or outmanoeuvred by [[sl:battle_mounted_units]]mounted units[[/sl]].
The [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership state of a unit is shown on its tooltip.

Damage taken by a Tzeentchian [[sl:battle_units]]unit[[/sl]] in battle will be first applied to its magical barrier. Once the strength of the barrier is depleted, the unit itself will begin to take damage.
The fortifications that surround the city must be overcome by the attacker if they are to gain victory.
The magical effects of a Cathayan Sorcerers’ [[sl:battle_spells]]spells[[/sl]] are increased for each additional magic-user present in an army.

The [[sl:battle_unit_details_panel]]Unit Details panel[[/sl]] shows information about the performance and attributes of any [[sl:battle_unit_selection]]selected unit[[/sl]]. Toggle the [[sl_tooltip:battle_unit_details_button]]Unit Details button[[/sl_tooltip]] on and either left-click or place the mouse cursor over a unit to view details about it.
The defender may win by either defeating all attacking units or holding them off until the [[sl_tooltip:battle_time_limit]]time limit[[/sl_tooltip]] expires.
Missile units will automatically fire at foes within their arc of fire if Fire-at-Will is active. Their arc of fire is displayed when selected or when the cursor is over it.
Monsters and giants can also be used to attack the [[sl:battle_gates]]gates[[/sl]] in a [[sl:battle_major_siege_battles]]major siege battle[[/sl]].
Mounted troops are highly [[sl:battle_unit_movement]]manoeuvrable[[/sl]], but generally more expensive and fewer in number than [[sl:battle_infantry]]infantry[[/sl]].
A visual effect is shown on a Dark Elf army that is experiencing murderous prowess.

When playing as a Nurglish faction, a [[sl_tooltip:battle_plague_lords_blessings_meter]]progress meter[[/sl_tooltip]] on the [[sl:battle_battle_interface]]battle interface[[/sl]] builds as damage is taken by Nurglish units during conflict.

A unit will not rally if there is no [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:battle_the_general]]Lord[[/sl]] still present in the [[sl:battle_armies]]army[[/sl]], or if its [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership state becomes shattered.
Control over rampaging units may be restored after a short time if their fury subsides.
