Grandfather's Blessings can be bestowed upon your characters and [[img:icon_garden_of_corruption]][[/img]][[sl_tooltip:campaign_gardens_of_corruption]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}}[[/sl_tooltip]] to greatly increase their strengths and grant them access to extra resources such as recruiting more Nurgle units or carrying a permanent plague.

Since time immemorial has the Great Bastion separated the lands of [[sl:campaign_cathay]]Cathay[[/sl]] from the Chaos Wastes beyond. Cathayan defenders are concentrated at three fortress gates along the constructed barricade to prevent [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] from entering the Celestial Empire.
The tooltip on the Great Bastion Threat meter lists the status of each fortress gate settlement.

The Cult of Ulric is a war-driven faith that turns the faithful into a winter-forged host. Using their battle-earned [[img:icon_fervour]][[/img]]Fervour, Middenland can upgrade the Sanctuaries of the Great Temple of Ulric to bring great strength to Boris Todbringer and his forces.

The [[img:icon_green_knight]][[/img]]Green Knight is a powerful [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero who emerges for [[sl:campaign_bretonnia]]Bretonnian factions[[/sl]] in their hour of greatest need. The [[img:icon_green_knight]][[/img]]Green Knight excels in the ways of [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], but only appears for a limited period of [[sl:campaign_turns]]time[[/sl]].

Orcs and Goblins band together on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] and are collectively referred to as Greenskins. Greenskins live for nothing but violence, and can be incited into a near-unstoppable [[sl:campaign_waaagh]]Waaagh![[/sl]] if sufficiently roused.

Grom the Paunch is known for having the biggest appetite of all [[sl:campaign_greenskins]]Goblinkind[[/sl]]. His special cauldron enables him to combine ingredients into recipes that not only satisfy his constant need to eat, but also imbue him and the rest of the Broken Axe tribe with a myriad of powerful effects in both campaign and [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

Although unruly and disorganised, the [[sl:campaign_greenskins]]Greenskins[[/sl]] are resourceful enough not to waste [[img:icon_scrap]][[/img]]Scrap materials left in the wake of their [[sl:campaign_battles]]battles[[/sl]]. They use them to fashion a hodgepodge of armour, weapons and equipment.

Followers of the [[sl:campaign_tzeentch]]Raven God[[/sl]] are consumed by a hunt for ancient and lapsed knowledge. Grimoires of forgotten learning, when unearthed, are highly prized by acolytes of Tzeentch.
A breakdown of Grimoires income may be viewed by placing the mouse cursor over the Grimoires counter at the top of the campaign interface.

The [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]growth of a [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] is a measure of the expansion of its population. [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]Growth leads to [[img:icon_pop_surplus]][[/img]]population surplus, which can be spent on upgrading the [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] within the province.

The [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]growth of a [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] is a measure of the expansion of its population. [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]Growth leads to [[img:icon_pop_surplus]][[/img]]Kindreds, which can be spent on upgrading buildings within the province.

[[sl:campaign_dwarfs]]Dwarfs[[/sl]] keep a long and ancient list of enemies that have wronged them. Rather than live in grumbling discontent, they can set out to avenge their losses by settling their [[img:icon_grudges]][[/img]]Grudges, in turn empowering themselves with unique rewards of the Book and the [[sl:campaign_age_of_reckoning]]Age of Reckoning[[/sl]].
The Grudges bar appears when playing as any Dwarf faction and can also be viewed in the Great Book of Grudges.
The Great Book of Grudges is accessible via the button in the bottom right of the main campaign interface when playing as any Dwarf faction.

[[sl:campaign_cathay]]Cathayan[[/sl]] factions can choose to maintain stability between the forces of [[img:icon_yin]][[/img]]Yin and [[img:icon_yang]][[/img]]Yang, or focus on either opposed principle. Both balance and imbalance have their own rewards.
Place the mouse cursor over each leaf of the lotus indicator to see the effect of harmony being that level.

The [[sl:campaign_chaos_dwarfs]]Chaos Dwarfs[[/sl]] are experts at combining smithing with Daemonic infusion. Feeding their assembly lines of [[img:icon_armaments]][[/img]]Armaments into the Hell-Forge, they equip new troops and modify their weapons, armour and war machines to enhance them with different effects.
The Help Pages button can be found in the top-left of the screen.

[[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] can perform actions to serve their [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]], either in support of a controlled [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]], or to strike at an enemy army, settlement or [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero.
The Deploy Hero button is shown when a controlled [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero is selected.
The Recruit Hero button is displayed on the Province Overview panel when a controlled settlement is selected.
The tab buttons showing available types of [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes are shown along the top of the Recruit Hero panel.

{{tr:hp_campaign_heroes_add_04}} [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes may also be added to an [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]], in which case they will fight as a powerful single-person [[sl:campaign_units]]unit[[/sl]] in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

The six forbidden Hexes are dark slivers of magic scattered across the world, which can inflict uniquely powerful effects upon their unfortunate targets. In hushed tones, their power is sought after in secret by the Daughters of the Forest.

The noble High Elves, or Asur as they call themselves, are among the most ancient and powerful of all [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]]. From their mist-shrouded home continent of Ulthuan, they defend the world from the encroaching evils that threaten it.

Eltharion the Grim coordinates the defence of Tor Yvresse from the ruins of Athel Tamarha, gradually repairing and upgrading the grand mountainside keep using [[img:icon_warden_supplies]][[/img]]Warden’s Supplies as he restores the power of the protective [[img:mist_of_yvresse]][[/img]]Mists of Yvresse.

Imrik is one of the very few who can wake the Dragons in times of need. As he travels outside of Ulthuan, he is on a constant search for those mighty Drake allies who still roam the world, to seek their power or bring them under Caledor’s banner.

The [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]growth of a [[sl:campaign_hordes]]horde[[/sl]] is a measure of the expansion of its population. [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]Growth of a horde leads to the accumulation of [[img:icon_pop_surplus]][[/img]]population surplus, which can be spent on [[sl:campaign_raising_forces]]raising additional hordes[[/sl]] or upgrading [[sl:campaign_buildings]]buildings[[/sl]].

The [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]growth of a [[img:icon_pirate_crew]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_hordes]]pirate crew[[/sl]] is a measure of its expanding population. [[img:icon_pirate_crew]][[/img]]Pirate crew [[img:icon_growth]][[/img]]growth leads to [[img:icon_pop_surplus]][[/img]]population surplus, which can be used to upgrade ship [[sl:campaign_buildings]]buildings[[/sl]].

Certain [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] roam the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] as hordes. Horde factions do not inhabit [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]], instead carrying their infrastructure with their [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]].

Frost Maiden [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] and Ice Witch [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] of [[sl:campaign_kislev]]Kislev[[/sl]] gain their mastery over the [[sl:campaign_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]] by completing trials within the Ice Court. Only after extensive training is completed may such formidable spellcasters be recruited into service.
The Ice Court button is displayed on the main campaign interface when playing a Kislev faction.
The Ice Court panel can be opened from the main campaign interface when playing a Kislev faction.

Nuln’s Imperial Gunnery School has a longstanding reputation as an institution of great learning. The [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] of Wissenland uses every skirmish as an opportunity for observation and field testing, in turn empowering its forces through the school’s unique knowledge.

[[sl:campaign_tax]]{{tr:hp_campaign_tax_term_sentence_start}}[[/sl]] from controlled territory, [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_trade]]trade[[/sl]] income, and [[sl:campaign_money]]{{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}}[[/sl]] from other sources such as [[sl:campaign_hordes]]horde buildings[[/sl]] and [[img:icon_raiding_stance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_raiding]]raiding[[/sl]] are added together to reach a [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction’s[[/sl]] total {{tr:icon_income}}income. This is shown on the {{tr:icon_treasury}}[[sl:campaign_treasury_panel]]Treasury panel[[/sl]].
The {{tr:icon_income}}income per-turn is shown on the Treasury panel, and also at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.

The Undead [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] of the [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]] compete with one another through their deeds to gain [[img:icon_infamy]][[/img]]Infamy. The most infamous pirates may seize [[img:icon_shanty]][[/img]]verses of the [[sl:campaign_sea_shanties]]Lost Sea Shanty[[/sl]].
A breakdown of Infections income may be viewed by placing the mouse cursor over the Infections icons at the top of the campaign interface and on the Plagues panel.

[[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elf[[/sl]] society is hierarchical in nature, and courtiers watch for any opportunity to gain status at the expense of their peers. The [[img:icon_influence]][[/img]]Influence of a High Elf [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] grows and sometimes falls depending on whether events fall in their favour, and can be used to gain various powerful advantages during Asur campaigns.

Intervention [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] may be hired by [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] to interfere with [[sl:campaign_rituals]]rituals[[/sl]] being conducted by their rivals. They are composed of mercenaries and fanatics dedicated to capturing or destroying the ritual sites.
The Interventions button becomes active when a rival faction is enacting a ritual.

[[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elves[[/sl]] can spend their [[img:icon_influence]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_influence]]influence[[/sl]] on Intrigues at the Court – whispered deals in the halls of power that pull strings to improve or worsen the [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomatic relations[[/sl]] between [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]].
Only factions already discovered are listed on the Intrigue at the Court panel.

Island and Black Ark battles allow for combat at sea instead of auto-resolving. Both battle types play like land battles, with Black Arks giving the defender a slight height advantage in their deployment zone over the attacker.

The goods-ladened Caravans sent west from [[sl:campaign_cathay]]Cathay[[/sl]] along the Ivory Road provide significant profit for the Celestial Empire, yet they face much peril. Those who brave the dangerous route in their protection may find it very lucrative indeed.
The Ivory Road panel can be opened by clicking the Ivory Road button on the main campaign interface when playing a Cathay faction.

Khorne is the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] God of war, hatred, and rage. Followers of the Blood God – whether Daemonic, mortal, or otherwise – are gifted with immense powers in combat and war, forged by a life of constant battle and martial challenge.

At the northern edges of the realms of man stand the people of Kislev. Their steadfastness against both the unforgiving climate and the constant threat of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] invasion are ample proof of their hardy and warlike nature.

[[img:icon_labour]][[/img]]Labour is the backbone of the [[sl:campaign_chaos_dwarfs]]Chaos Dwarfs’[[/sl]] [[sl:campaign_chd_economy]]Industrial Economy[[/sl]]; a commodity of battle captives and traded Labourers used and managed provincially to facilitate efficiency, rapid expansion and ultimately, the arming of the Chaos Dwarf war machine.

Nagash’s ultimate goal is to turn the entire world into a [[img:icon_land_of_the_dead]][[/img]]Land of the Dead, where he can claim the [[img:icon_necromantic_energy]][[/img]]Necromantic Energy required to spread his dark influence and burgeon his Undead hosts.

Deep within the jungles of Lustria may be found the Lizardmen. Multiple species make up this ancient and cold-blooded [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] – the agile Skinks, the monstrous Kroxigor, the warlike Saurus, and the contemplative Slann, who lead the Lizardmen with their matchless wisdom and command over the [[sl:campaign_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]].

The Old Ones watch over the [[sl:campaign_lizardmen]]Lizardmen[[/sl]], preparing for the Great Plan. For the plan to come to fruition, temples must be built to one of the great Old Ones within captured [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]].

Nakai resides at the centre of the jungle nexus and the spawning pools under his control. Any military progress that his [[sl:campaign_hordes]]horde[[/sl]] makes can be shared with all other hordes in the [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]].

A First Generation Slaan, Lord Kroak is a supremely powerful Legendary [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Hero[[/sl]] able to inflict massive damage on [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] through his [[sl:campaign_hero_actions]]Hero actions[[/sl]], as well as unleashing devastating attacks on the battlefield when summoned by any [[sl:campaign_lizardmen]]Lizardmen faction[[/sl]].

The ancient [[sl:campaign_lizardmen]]Lizardmen's[[/sl]] prophecies speak of the return to Lustria of the Serpent-God Sotek. The Cult of Sotek [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] intend to see this prophecy fulfilled through [[img:icon_sotek_captives]][[/img]]Sacrificial Offerings and, of course, wiping the Skaven from their jungles. With each Sacrifice to Sotek, rewards of varying quality are given to Tehenhauin and his cohorts of Red Crested Skinks.
Unlock sacrifices and pay tribute to Sotek through the Sacrifice to Sotek panel.

Invaders from the Old World wish to steal the [[sl:campaign_lizardmen]]Lizardmen's[[/sl]] riches and establish their own colonies in the New World. It is Nakai's sacred duty to see that this doesn't happen – he must track down and defeat these warm-blooded invaders.
The local recruitment pool shows units that can be recruited from the local province.

[[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord [[sl:campaign_characters]]characters[[/sl]] within a [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] can be appointed to the command of an [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]]. Each army on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] is commanded by and contains one [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord.

[[img:icon_loyalty]][[/img]]Loyalty is a measure of the willingness of a [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] of the [[sl:campaign_dark_elves]]Dark Elves[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]] to follow the leader of his or her [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]]. Should a Lord’s loyalty reach 0 they will rebel, taking their [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] with them to form a new faction.

{{tr:hp_campaign_magic_items_add_01}} Once equipped by a [[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_heroes]]Hero[[/sl]], these magical items can grant their bearer a wide range of effects and bonuses.
As he seeks the glorious doom that all Slayers desire, Malakai Makaisson uses his deadly exploits to test and improve his latest engineering innovations in the most perilous battles he can instigate!

Treachery is Sayl's craft, power his prize. Driven by a thirst to reap the ultimate arcane strength, the arch-sorcerer of the Dolgan connives to twist the world around him as a prelude to his invasions, all the while attracting the unwanted [[img:dlc27_sayl_attention]][[/img]]Attention of the Gods.

Amongst [[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elves[[/sl]], the rulers of Nagarythe place a singular importance on striking at the opposition's nobility. Bonuses will be earned by Nagarythe when those enemy [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] marked for death are killed in battle or campaign.
The Marked for Death buttons are shown on the user interface when playing as Nagarythe.

[[img:icon_marks_of_ruination]][[/img]]Marks of Ruination are the tokens of recognition that [[sl:campaign_beastmen]]Beastmen[[/sl]] receive from the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos Gods[[/sl]], symbolising their status amongst all Children of Chaos. They are collected as a result of the slaughter and destruction wrought throughout a [[sl:campaign_bloodgrounds]]Blood-ground[[/sl]], increasing the Beastmen's Ruination Level to enable campaign progression and rewards.

The [[sl:campaign_tormentors_tributes]]Tormentor's Tributes[[/sl]] available in return for Dechala's ever-increasing [[img:icon_decadence]][[/img]]Decadence are as multitudinous as her limbs. By taking on Marks of Vindictiveness, the Tormentor's [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] can heighten their capability for slaughter.
The Jade Court has the power to enact decisive acts of governance through Matters of State, which can be used to influence a variety of targets on the campaign map.

The [[sl:campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]Ogre Kingdoms[[/sl]] march and fight on their stomachs, with the consumption of [[img:icon_ogr_meat]][[/img]][[sl_tooltip:campaign_meat_link]]Meat[[/sl_tooltip]] linked to every part of their lives, from meals and battle prowess to ritual offerings and faction expansion.
Wherever he travels, Golgfag will take any job from anyone and against anyone in order to grow his Maneater Company's riches and notoriety, as long as the rewards offered are valuable enough.

Military Convoys can be sent from the [[sl:campaign_chaos_dwarfs]]Chaos Dwarfs'[[/sl]] lands to travel along the many trade routes that span the world. Convoys that successfully reach their destination can trade in commodities that benefit the Chaos Dwarfs’ [[sl:campaign_chd_economy]]Industrial Economy[[/sl]].
Missions may be issued from time to time to guide the progress of a player [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]]. They are optional to complete.

Sea Lord Aislinn's Sea Patrol has perfected the use of Mist Magic in their military tactics, using the cover of fog to swiftly and silently disembark from their ships and initiate [[sl:campaign_battles]]battles[[/sl]] against unsuspecting foes.

The Beastlord Rakarth is the greatest Beastmaster to have ever scourged the world. As he battles across the continents, he and his [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] can capture a variety of wild beasts and monsters which they can control to fight on their behalf.

The Monstrous Arcanum is a tome of the most savage and horrifying creatures in the world. It may be consulted by the tribal leaders of [[sl:campaign_norsca]]Norsca[[/sl]] who wish to go on Monster Hunts.

The spread of [[img:icon_corruption_chs]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_corruption]]corruption[[/sl]] affects the [[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elves[[/sl]] of Avelorn more keenly than any other [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]].
In ancient times, Nine Dark Lords served Nagash and now, as the First Necromancer ascends again to power, nine Mortarchs will be bound to Him in servitude unending.

By using their stockpiles of {{tr:icon_money}}[[sl:campaign_money]]money[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_resources]]resources[[/sl]], and [[img:icon_jars]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_canopic_jars]]Canopic Jars[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_tomb_kings]]Tomb Kings[[/sl]] factions may craft powerful magic [[sl:campaign_character_details]]items[[/sl]] or awaken [[sl:campaign_regiments_of_renown]]Regiments of Renown[[/sl]] through the Mortuary Cult. Confederations are also available in the Mortuary Cult for those more agreeable factions.
The Mortuary Cult button is on the campaign interface next to the End Turn button.
The list of items available through the Mortuary Cult may be filtered by clicking the buttons at the top of the Mortuary Cult panel.

Though they vie for supremacy, the Great Orthodoxy and the Ice Court hold the key to advantages that can greatly benefit [[sl:campaign_kislev]]Kislev’s[[/sl]] cause. {{tr:uied_component_texts_localised_string_wh3_main_ksl_court_orthodoxy_description_tx}}
The Motherland panel can be opened from the top of the campaign interface when playing as a Kislev faction.
The proportion of an character's movement range left this turn is shown on the Character Info panel.

As the first and greatest among Necromancers, Nagash is able to hold absolute dominion over every wailing spectre, ghastly beast and twitching corpse across the world's Undead denominations, binding them to His eternal servitude.

Long ago, the Master Runesmith Alaric the Mad forged the accursed Nemesis Crown from Warpstone, the only material strong enough to bear the awesome power of the Rune of Ages. Horrified by the evil he had inadvertently created, he hid the Crown away in the futile hope it would remain undiscovered, yet its whispers still emanate across the world as it yearns to be found.

A [[img:icon_non-aggression_pact]][[/img]]non-aggression pact may be agreed between two [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] via [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomacy[[/sl]] as a statement of mutual trust. It is usually the first step in building relations towards [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_trade]]trade[[/sl]] and, eventually, an [[img:icon_military_alliance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_alliances]]alliance[[/sl]].

Norscan factions have a hard time settling outside of their native regions - they prefer pillaging them for all they are worth.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]After winning a battle for a settlement, a Lord can choose to Pillage it - gaining some [[img:icon_nor_spoils]][[/img]]Spoils immediately and creating a small force to send the rest to bring them back to an owned settlement.\\n\\n[[img:icon_nor_spoils]][[/img]]Spoils can be spent to settle distant regions as fully-fledged settlements or on powerful buildings and technologies.[[/col]]

Norscan factions have a hard time settling outside of their native regions - they prefer pillaging them for all they are worth.\\n\\nAfter winning a battle for a settlement, a Lord can choose to Pillage it - gaining some [[img:icon_nor_spoils]][[/img]]Spoils immediately and creating a small force to send the rest to bring them back to an owned settlement.\\n\\n[[img:icon_nor_spoils]][[/img]]Spoils can be spent to settle distant regions as fully-fledged settlements or on powerful buildings and technologies.

The Norscans are a [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] of tough and warlike men, shaped both by the harsh conditions of the north and living dangerously close to the Chaos Wastes. They worship the forces of the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] Gods – personified as the Hound, the Crow, the Serpent and the Eagle – raising dark shrines and making bloody offerings to the Ruinous Powers.

As they erect [[img:icon_dark_fortress]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_dark_fortress]]Dark Fortresses[[/sl]] across the Norscan Homelands, the [[sl:campaign_warriors_of_chaos]]Warriors of Chaos[[/sl]] can [[img:icon_vassal]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_vassalage]]vassalise[[/sl]] the local tribes through the conquest of their Homeland Capitals, forcefully gaining their unwavering loyalty.

Grandfather Nurgle is the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] God of disease, decay, and death. As they march to war, His followers gleefully spread his foetid message, along with the crippling and virulent diseases He concocts to any unfortunate enough to stand against them.

[[img:icon_garden_of_corruption]][[/img]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}} can be planted in any minor or major settlements as a tribute to Grandfather Nurgle, bringing daemons, rot, and decay onto the mortal plane. They provide many benefits such as [[sl:campaign_cyclical_buildings]]Cyclical Buildings[[/sl]] feeding daemonic units into the [[b]]Summoned Units[[/b]] faction pool, a steady spawn of  [[sl_tooltip:campaign_garden_plagues]]Garden Plagues[[/sl_tooltip]] contaminating the region, and powerful factionwide bonuses.

Through the [[url:script_link_campaign_gifts_of_nurgle]][[tooltip:{{tt:tooltip_campaign_rituals_of_decay}}]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_rotborne_rituals_title}}[[/tooltip]][[/url]], the Glottkin and their Lords can temporarily spread [[img:wh3_dlc29_icon_nurgle_rains]][[/img]]Nurgle Rains in the regions in which they lay foot.[[img:wh3_dlc29_icon_nurgle_rains]][[/img]]Nurgle Rains provide  benefits to Nurgle worshippers while afflicting the enemy factions with opposite effects.
The Oak of Ages lies at the heart of the forest of Athel Loren, and is the foundation tree of the realm of the [[sl:campaign_wood_elves]]Wood Elves[[/sl]].
[[img:icon_oathgold]][[/img]]Oathgold is a rare ore gathered only by the [[sl:campaign_dwarfs]]Dwarfs[[/sl]] to bind the Winds of Magic into powerful items.
The Objectives button is shown next to the End Turn button on the campaign interface.
The Chapter Missions tab shows chapter missions on the Objectives panel.
The Victory Conditions tab shows victory conditions on the Objectives panel.
The Offer to the Great Maw panel can be opened from the Army panel after a controlled Ogre army is selected.

A [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] may be promoted into a position of Office once they have achieved a sufficient [[sl:campaign_character_details]]character rank[[/sl]]. Positions of Office confer bonuses on the [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords that occupy them.
The Offices button is shown on the campaign interface when playing as the Empire.

[[sl:campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]Ogres[[/sl]] are renowned for their nomadic ways and fireside revelry. By constructing a Camp, Ogre [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] can provide benefits and support to their local [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]], even deep inside enemy territory.

The Ogres, a monstrous race of nasty, brutish thugs, see other races as little more than meat to feed their ravenous bellies or to be cast into the Great Maw. Led by their Tyrant overlords, the Ogres wage war from their tribal bases deep within the Mountains of Mourn.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] may construct outposts within the fortified [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] of their [[img:icon_military_alliance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_alliances]]military allies[[/sl]] or [[img:icon_vassal]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_vassalage]]vassals[[/sl]]. Once constructed by a faction, an outpost enables [[sl:campaign_unit_recruitment]]recruitment[[/sl]] from amongst their allies available [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]].

Skrag, the legendary Prophet of the Great Maw, is at his most powerful when he walks the Path of the Butcher, his [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]]'s strength inextricably linked to the endless appetite of the [[sl:campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]Ogres[[/sl]]' insatiable god.

All followers of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] have a shared goal – to seek power and ascension by any means necessary, even at the risk of damnation. Thusly [[sl:campaign_warriors_of_chaos]]Warriors of Chaos[[/sl]] [[sl:campaign_characters]]characters[[/sl]] can follow a Path to Glory to progress into new and more powerful forms with Daemonhood as the ultimate reward.

By installing [[img:icon_lord]][[/img]]Lords into powerful positions of Patronage offered by Ulthuan's ruling [[sl:campaign_provinces]]provinces[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elf[[/sl]] leaders can use their [[img:icon_influence]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_influence]]Influence[[/sl]] to eventually bring the Asur under one rule, as mandated by the Phoenix King himself.

Peasants are used by [[sl:campaign_bretonnia]]Bretonnian factions[[/sl]] either as lance-fodder to be sacrificed in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] or for working the fields to provide {{tr:icon_income}}[[sl:campaign_income]]income[[/sl]].
The number of recruited peasants is shown at the top of the screen.

Pieces of Eight are cursed trinkets that have so completely twisted and altered the minds of those that first found them that their fate is now tied to the coins. By securing one of the Pieces of Eight, the services of the warriors bound to them may be secured also.

[[img:icon_cove]][[/img]]Pirate Coves can be established in [[img:icon_port]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_ports]]ports[[/sl]] by factions of the [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]] should they defeat the occupiers in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] or by [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_hero_actions]]Hero actions[[/sl]]. [[img:icon_cove]][[/img]]Pirate Coves provide the pirate faction with {{tr:icon_income}}[[sl:campaign_income]]income[[/sl]] and other benefits despite the original occupant retaining control of the [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]].
The Plagues panel is accessed via the button in the bottom right of the main campaign interface.
The tooltip of each recipe shows the Symptoms that must be unlocked before the recipe becomes available.

Through their pestilent scheming, the [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] are able to spread virulent diseases amongst their enemies. [[sl:campaign_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] and [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] can both fall victim to [[img:icon_plague]][[/img]]plagues, and once infection has set in they can expect a heavy [[sl:campaign_attrition]]death toll[[/sl]].

Just like the Plague Lord himself, followers of [[sl:campaign_nurgle]]Nurgle[[/sl]] cannot resist combining and recombining strains of disease, contaminating their own bodies with the intention of infecting everyone with whom they come into contact.

The followers of [[sl:campaign_slaanesh]]Slaanesh[[/sl]] are infamous for their debauched revelry. Such events, held in and around the palaces of the Dark Prince, can generate a number of beneficial effects over time.
Only the followers of Slaanesh may perform Pleasurable Acts.

[[img:icon_port]][[/img]]Ports are [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] that adjoin the [[sl:campaign_sea]]sea[[/sl]]. [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_trade]]Trade[[/sl]] routes may be established from a [[img:icon_port]][[/img]]port across the water to distant shores.

Malus is bound to the Daemon Tz’arkan, manifesting as a powerful Daemonic form in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] when he is fully possessed. Tz’arkan’s influence can be thwarted by regularly taking [[img:def_malus_possession_potion]][[/img]]elixirs to suppress his ever-advancing possession, but succumbing to his [[img:def_malus_tzarkan_whispers]][[/img]]whispers of carnage can bring great rewards at the cost of Malus’ sanity.

A number of options are available to the victor after [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], such as killing any prisoners taken or looting a captured [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]]. These are presented on the [[sl:campaign_post_battle_panel]]Post-Battle panel[[/sl]].

A number of options are available to the victor after [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], such as killing or releasing prisoners. These are presented on the [[sl:campaign_post_battle_panel]]Post-Battle panel[[/sl]].
A number of options are available to the victor after capture of a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]]. These are presented on the [[sl:campaign_post_battle_panel]]Post-Battle panel[[/sl]].

The Post-Battle panel appears after a [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] has been fought, and presents [[sl:campaign_post_battle_options]]options[[/sl]] for what to do with the spoils if victory was achieved.
Alarielle, the High Elf champion of the Earth-Goddess, radiates life magic, which invigorates the lands through which she travels. When she crosses controlled territory it will receive bonuses.
Engagement options such as whether to attack or withdraw appear immediately prior to [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] on the [[sl:campaign_pre_battle_panel]]Pre-Battle panel[[/sl]].

The Pre-Battle panel appears immediately prior to a [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] engagement and provides [[sl:campaign_pre_battle_options]]options[[/sl]] and information about the strengths and setup of the [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] involved.
Only the followers of Slaanesh can directly proliferate cults.

The Province Info panel appears alongside the [[sl:campaign_province_overview_panel]]Province Overview panel[[/sl]] when a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] is selected, and displays information about the state of the [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] and its population.

A [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] must be managed by the [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] or factions that control it to remain productive, and to prevent it from degenerating into [[sl:campaign_revolts]]rebellion[[/sl]].

The Province Overview panel appears when a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] is selected, and shows the setup of [[sl:campaign_buildings]]buildings[[/sl]] and settlements within the selected [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]].

{{tr:hp_campaign_provinces_add_1}} Control of a province can be split between multiple [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]], each [[sl:campaign_province_management]]ruling[[/sl]] over the settlements they hold.
The Provinces list may be viewed by clicking the Provinces button on the campaign interface.
Inspect the tooltip of the {{tr:hp_campaign_public_order_term}} bar to see the bonuses and penalties applied for each threshold of {{tr:hp_campaign_public_order_term}}.
Place the mouse cursor over the {{tr:hp_campaign_public_order_term}} icon on the Province Info panel to see a list of contributing factors.

Certain [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Legendary Lords[[/sl]] may go on quests, which are made available as the  [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord increases in [[sl:campaign_character_skills]]rank[[/sl]]. A [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Legendary Lord can win powerful [[sl:campaign_character_details]]items[[/sl]] by completing a quest.

Each race featured in the [[sl:campaign_campaign_game]]game[[/sl]], such as the [[sl:campaign_greenskins]]Greenskins[[/sl]] or the [[sl:campaign_dwarfs]]Dwarfs[[/sl]], carries certain racial traits which grant [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] of that race unique abilities or inabilities.

An [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] may raid enemy territory by entering [[img:icon_raiding_stance]][[/img]]Raiding [[sl:campaign_stances]]stance[[/sl]]. [[img:icon_raiding_stance]][[/img]]Raiding brings in {{tr:icon_money}}[[sl:campaign_money]]{{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}}[[/sl]] and has detrimental effects on the target being [[img:icon_raiding_stance]][[/img]]raided.
The Raise Dead button is shown on the Army panel when a controlled Vampire army is selected.
The Recruit Lord button is displayed on the Province Overview panel when a settlement is selected.
New armies can be raised and [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords appointed to lead them on the Recruit Lord panel.

[[sl:campaign_vampires]]Vampire Counts factions[[/sl]] raise the dead to fight for their cause, allowing them to build [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] more swiftly than other [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]].

Entirely new [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] may be raised from the [[sl_tooltip:campaign_raise_forces_panel]]Recruit Lord panel[[/sl_tooltip]] to allow [[sl:campaign_war]]wars[[/sl]] to be fought on multiple fronts. A [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] must be appointed to lead the new military force.

Taurox the Brass Bull is a roaring, snorting engine of destruction who is rewarded by the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Dark Gods[[/sl]] for winning successive [[sl:campaign_battles]]battles[[/sl]] quickly. By continually fighting and sustaining his [[img:icon_momentum]][[/img]]Momentum, the [[sl:campaign_beastmen]]Beastmen[[/sl]] [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lord earns [[img:icon_rampage]][[/img]]Rampage Marks and receives gifts for his relentless slaughter.

Raw Materials are gathered when Labour is present in a province that has Mines buildings. The amount of Raw Materials harvested depends on the Labour to Workload ratio, if a province has less Labour than required Workload it will produce less Raw Materials.\\n\\nRaw Materials are required to construct several types of buildings, including Factory and Tower settlement chains. Raw Materials can also be used in special Factory buildings, Refinery and Assembly Line, these buildings consume Raw Materials and produce either Treasury or Armaments.

A [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] may choose to raze a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] after defeating its defenders in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]]. Razing a settlement burns it to the ground and leaves it abandoned.

The Realm of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] is a domain of pure magic that sits outside of the physical universe. From their bases within, the Gods of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] plan their assaults against the mortal world.
Black Arks may only be recruited from coastal settlements.

[[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] can be recruited from the Recruit Hero panel, which can be opened from the [[sl:campaign_province_overview_panel]]Province Overview panel[[/sl]] by clicking the [[sl_tooltip:campaign_hero_recruitment_button]]Recruit Hero button[[/sl_tooltip]].
The number of units that can be recruited in a turn from each pool is indicated on the Recruitment panel.

Regiments of Renown are elite versions of standard [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]], with improved combat performance and abilities. Regiments of Renown become available to the player’s [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] when a [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] reaches a certain [[sl:campaign_character_details]]character rank[[/sl]] or when special requirements are fulfilled.

Single [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] can be offered or requested as part of a [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomatic deal[[/sl]]. Such deals are particularly useful for acquiring desired territory without waging [[sl:campaign_war]]war[[/sl]], or for sealing peace treaties.

[[img:icon_military_alliance]][[/img]]Allied [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] may reinforce one another in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] if they are close on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]]. An attack on one of them will mean the other being drawn into the battle in support.

Natural resources are to be found across the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]]. Ownership of the nearby [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] grants access to the resource, bringing in extra {{tr:icon_income}}[[sl:campaign_trade]]trade income[[/sl]] to the controlling [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]].

A rebellion will occur in a [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] if [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_public_order]]{{tr:hp_campaign_public_order_term}}[[/sl]] there gets too low. A rebellion [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] will appear and, if left to gather strength, may attack nearby [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]].

An incursion will occur in a [[sl:campaign_provinces]]province[[/sl]] if [[img:icon_public_order]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_public_order]]{{tr:hp_campaign_public_order_term}}[[/sl]] gets too low there. An incursion [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] will appear and, if left to gather strength, may attack nearby [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]].

Certain [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]] may perform powerful rites that grant them strong bonuses and unique abilities on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]]. Rites cost significant amounts of {{tr:icon_money}}[[sl:campaign_money]]{{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}}[[/sl]] or [[img:icon_slaves]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_slaves]]slaves[[/sl]] to perform.
The rites button is only shown for races that can use rites.
Each rite must be unlocked before it may be used. The unlock criteria for a locked rite is shown on the panel.
Ritual buttons are shown in sequence along the Rituals bar.

Ritual currency contains the knowledge and power required to conduct [[sl:campaign_rituals]]rituals[[/sl]]. [[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] require a certain amount of ritual currency to begin casting a ritual on the [[sl:campaign_great_vortex]]Great Vortex[[/sl]].

Certain [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] around the Eye of the Vortex [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] are rich in [[sl:campaign_ritual_currency]]ritual currency[[/sl]]. Construction of a specific [[sl:campaign_buildings]]building[[/sl]] within the settlement will earn the controlling [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] a steady stream of ritual currency revenue.
The icon for each rival progresses slowly to the right as that faction earns ritual currency.

Rituals are the means by which [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] can influence the [[sl:campaign_great_vortex]]Great Vortex[[/sl]] within the Eye of the Vortex campaign. In order to begin a ritual, a faction must first accumulate sufficient [[sl:campaign_ritual_currency]]ritual currency[[/sl]].

Progress towards the next [[sl:campaign_rituals]]ritual[[/sl]], as well as the progress of rival [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]], is shown on the Rituals bar. The bar fills as [[sl:campaign_ritual_currency]]ritual currency[[/sl]] is earned, indicating progression in the race to control the [[sl:campaign_great_vortex]]Great Vortex[[/sl]].

Rituals of Decay are manifestations of the Ur-Father to provide powerful temporary bonuses to all his favoured children. Casting a Ritual of Decay provides a strong boost to Bestowed characters or [[img:icon_garden_of_corruption]][[/img]][[sl_tooltip:campaign_gardens_of_corruption]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}}[[/sl_tooltip]].

Rogue [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] are warbands of desperate outlaws, often made up of unusual combinations of troops. They appear from time to time, and will eventually seek to establish a home on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] by colonising a [[sl:campaign_ruins]]ruin[[/sl]] or assaulting an occupied [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]].

Legends tell of mighty pirate [[img:icon_transport_fleet]][[/img]]fleets that terrorise the Great Ocean raiding [[img:icon_port]][[/img]]ports and shipping routes for anything of worth. These are Rogue Pirates: hardened veterans of the sea who visit death and ruination on those they plunder.

The weathered remnants of [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] long abandoned may be found the length and breadth of the campaign map. Yet in times of war they rarely stay untouched for long; hidden treasures and the possibility for territorial expansion draw many to their remains.
The [[sl:campaign_campaign_game]]game[[/sl]] will automatically save each turn, and can be saved manually during the turn unless playing on Legendary difficulty.
As Tzeentch's Trickster, the Changeling revels in sowing disorder across the world via his methodical Schemes. The Schemes panel is a hub for tracking all mischievous activity across a campaign.

Bodies of water on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] may be crossed by [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] on ships, and by sea [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_trade]]trade[[/sl]] routes. Unique threats abound in the Great Ocean, such as [[sl:campaign_rogue_pirates]]Rogue Pirates[[/sl]].

Sea Lanes are markers at [[sl:campaign_sea]]sea[[/sl]] that can be entered to allow quicker travel between two points. Any [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] or [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Hero[[/sl]] can use a Sea Lane, but they won't be available while transiting the lane.
Seafarers through the ages have sung songs of great potency to empower their gun crews and boarders in battle. The most powerful of these is also the most elusive: the Lost Sea Shanty.

The White Tower of Hoeth is the [[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elves[[/sl]]' sacred seat of magical learning. By wielding its secrets, Teclis can focus and hone his [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction's[[/sl]] knowledge of the [[sl:campaign_winds_of_magic]]Winds[[/sl]] with his Mages' learnings in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], granting the Order of Loremasters powerful advantages over their enemies.
The Seduce Units button is shown on the Pre-Battle panel when playing as a Slaaneshi faction.

Such is the allure of the [[sl:campaign_slaanesh]]Dark Prince[[/sl]] that Slaaneshi [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] may be able to entice enemy [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]] to switch sides prior to [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]]. Seduced units will fight against their former allies for the duration of the engagement.

The [[sl:campaign_slaanesh]]Slaaneshi[[/sl]] Arch-Tempter N'kari exerts a [[img:icon_seductive_influence]][[/img]]Seductive Influence over amoral men, Elves, and Beastmen [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]]. By working to increase this influence, be can eventually be able to force such [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] into [[img:icon_vassal]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_vassalage]]vassalage[[/sl]].

The settlement bar appears below each settlement on the campaign map. Icons on the bar indicate important information about the settlement. Place the mouse cursor over the bar of occupied settlements to see more information about them.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] may expand and capture any [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]]. However, no [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] will thrive everywhere, each having a set of specific climate preferences. Settlements of an unsuitable climate type will [[sl:campaign_growth]]grow[[/sl]] more slowly, if occupied, and suffer a variety of other penalties.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] of a particular [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] are restricted as to what types of [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] they may [[sl:campaign_post_battle_options]]occupy[[/sl]].

Settlements are cities or [[img:icon_port]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_ports]]ports[[/sl]] on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] from which [[sl:campaign_provinces]]provinces[[/sl]] are defended and controlled. Ownership of a settlement grants ownership of the territory around it.

Of all the great [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] clans, Eshin perform acts of stealth and subterfuge like no other. [[img:skv_snikch_schemes]][[/img]]Schemes that naturally develop over the course of the [[sl:campaign_campaign_game]]campaign[[/sl]] are used by Clan Eshin to send [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] and [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] to perform a host of instantly-successful actions upon [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_characters]]characters[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] in return for rewards.

Shipbuilding allows the pirate [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] of the [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]] to upgrade their vessels away from [[img:icon_port]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_ports]]port[[/sl]]. Improvements may be made to weaponry, deck-strength and crew, even whilst far from home.

The Siege panel is displayed when a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] is placed under [[sl:campaign_siege_warfare]]siege[[/sl]]. It shows siege options and, if the settlement is [[sl:campaign_fortifications]]fortified[[/sl]], allows [[sl:campaign_siege_weapons]]siege weapons[[/sl]] to be built prior to [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

An [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] may lay siege to an enemy [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] over many [[sl:campaign_turns]]turns[[/sl]]. The defenders of a besieged settlement must sally forth or seek outside help to avoid starvation and defeat.

Siege weapons may be constructed during a [[sl:campaign_siege_warfare]]siege[[/sl]] on the [[sl:campaign_siege_panel]]Siege panel[[/sl]]. They provide a method of attack against the [[sl:campaign_fortifications]]settlement fortifications[[/sl]], allowing the walls to be breached and the [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] to be taken.

The verminous Skaven are a [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] of malevolent and self-serving ratmen. From their [[sl:campaign_skaven_underworld]]Under-Empire cities[[/sl]], they fight tooth and claw against the other races – and each other – to further their personal standing within the Skaven hierarchy and to serve their diabolical god, the Horned Rat.

[[img:icon_corruption_skv]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] corruption is spread wherever the Skaven settle. As they naturally befoul anywhere they linger, [[img:icon_corruption_skv]][[/img]]Skaven [[sl:campaign_corruption]]corruption[[/sl]] causes settled [[sl:campaign_provinces]]provinces[[/sl]] to become less hospitable over [[sl:campaign_turns]]time[[/sl]], even for Skaven.

The [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] Clan Moulder have risen to infamy by mastering the art of breeding, mutating and surgically splicing monstrous fighting beasts. The Flesh Laboratory is where Throt operates on subjects to create more powerful troops to lead into [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], in addition to developing bloodthirsty monsters in the Growth Vat to bolster his ranks.

The [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] Clan Skryre are known for their diabolical technological experiments, carried out in workshops beneath Skavenblight. The Forbidden Workshop is where Ikit Claw conducts his own personal experiments, upgrading Skryre’s Weapons Teams, Doomwheels and Doom-Flayers, and assembling [[img:icon_doomrocket]][[/img]]Doomrockets so powerful they can devastate enemy [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] with their lethal strength.
Unlock unit upgrades and Doom-Rockets through the Forbidden Workshop panel.

Skaven are treacherous by nature and [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] of this [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] exhibit varying [[img:icon_loyalty]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_loyalty]]loyalty[[/sl]] to their masters. The loyalty of Skaven [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords must be kept in check to prevent them rebelling and forming a new [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]].

The [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] can establish their bases of operation in any [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]], including those owned by other [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]], by constructing [[img:icon_under_empire]][[/img]]Under-Cities directly beneath them. Skaven settlements and [[img:icon_under_empire]][[/img]]Under-Cities are part of the vast subterranean network known as the Under-Empire.

Khorne's Skull Throne rests upon the countless [[img:icon_skulls]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_skulls]]Skulls[[/sl]] offered by His devoted servants. In turn, He grants them a sliver of His power to use through mighty rituals as His worshippers climb in His esteem.

[[img:icon_skulls]][[/img]]Skulls are gathered as trophies by followers of [[sl:campaign_khorne]]Khorne[[/sl]] from [[sl:campaign_battles]]battles[[/sl]] in which they fight directly, and from Skull Piles left in the aftermath of other engagements. [[img:icon_skulls]][[/img]]Skulls are necessary for Khornate [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] to occupy [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] and research [[sl:campaign_technology]]technologies[[/sl]].
A breakdown of [[img:icon_skulls]][[/img]]Skulls income may be viewed by placing the mouse cursor over the [[img:icon_skulls]][[/img]]Skulls counter at the top of the campaign interface.

The followers of the Dark Prince Slaanesh are invariably sadistic, decadent, amoral killers. Their hedonistic pursuit of gratification fuels the Dark Prince they worship, for He is the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] God of pleasure, gluttony, and excess.

[[sl:campaign_dark_elves]]Dark Elves[[/sl]] terrorise their enemies and bolster their economies by capturing [[img:icon_slaves]][[/img]]slaves in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]]. Those unfortunate enough to be taken captive by the Dark Elves know their fate is to be worked to death fulfilling many exhausting and degrading tasks across the Druchii empire.
The Slaves buttons are only shown when playing as a Dark Elf faction.

[[img:icon_souls_resource]][[/img]]Souls are harvested by winning battles and razing settlements against all factions except Nurgle, Khorne, Slaanesh, Tzeentch, and Daemons of Chaos. In turn, they can be sacrificed to unlock Grandfather's Blessings for your [[img:icon_general]][[/img]]Lords, [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes and {{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}}. They can also be used to perform powerful Rituals of Decay and plant [[img:icon_garden_of_corruption]][[/img]] {{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}}.

[[sl:campaign_warriors_of_chaos]]Warriors of Chaos[[/sl]] factions collect the [[img:icon_souls_resource]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_souls_resource]]Souls[[/sl]] of mortals who they defeat. In turn, they can sacrifice them to their gods in return for powerful [[img:icon_chaos_gifts]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_chaos_gifts]]Gifts of Chaos[[/sl]] or ascend characters through [[sl:campaign_path_to_glory]]Paths to Glory[[/sl]].

The [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] of Malakai Makaisson marches beneath the airborne machine known as the Spirit of Grungni, a legendary airship that the Slayer Engineer can upgrade on the move to increase his battle prowess and even call upon in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

A life of nomadic warmongering makes it difficult for the [[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] of [[sl:campaign_norsca]]Norsca[[/sl]] to settle foreign lands. Yet driven by their Spoils of destruction, they recognise no border other than the horizon itself.

[[sl:campaign_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] can modify their [[sl:campaign_army_movement]]movement[[/sl]], behaviour and abilities by adopting stances. [[sl:campaign_unit_recruitment]]Recruitment[[/sl]], [[img:icon_ambush_stance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_ambushes]]ambushing[[/sl]] and [[img:icon_raiding_stance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_raiding]]raiding[[/sl]] are examples of behaviours facilitated by stances.
The stances rollout is shown on the Character Info panel when a controlled army is selected.
The Strategic Overview can be used to see a top-level view of the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]]. Zoom the camera out to toggle the Strategic Overview.
The Toggle Strategic Overview button is shown in the top-right corner of the campaign interface.
The layer buttons allow different layers to be shown on the Strategic Overview.
Only the followers of Slaanesh can summon Disciple Armies.
The Supporters track on the Motherland panel shows the relative progress of the Ice Court and the Orthodoxy factions in gaining [[img:icon_supporters]][[/img]]Supporters for their cause.

The Sword of Khaine is a blade of ancient and terrible power. To its bearer it grants prodigious strength in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]], yet stewardship of the sword can lead to civil unrest over time.
The effect of adding any symptom to a Plague of Nurgle is shown on its icon tooltip.

Every [[img:icon_souls_resource]][[/img]] Souls earned increases your [[img:wh3_dlc29_total_accumulated_souls]][[/img]] Tallied Souls. Harvest enough [[img:icon_souls_resource]][[/img]] Souls to reach [[img:wh3_dlc29_total_accumulated_souls]][[/img]] Tallied Souls thresholds and unlock new [[sl_tooltip:campaign_rituals_of_decay]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_rotborne_rituals_title}}[[/sl_tooltip]], increase the number of bestowed [[sl_tooltip:campaign_grandfather_blessings]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_blessings_of_nurgle_marks_of_nurgle_title}}[[/sl_tooltip]] and the [[img:icon_garden_of_corruption]][[/img]][[sl_tooltip:campaign_gardens_of_corruption]]{{tr:ui_text_replacements_localised_text_wh3_dlc29_gardens_of_nurgle_title}}[[/sl_tooltip]] maximum capacity.
Epidemius, Reckoner of Mortality, is busiest when [[sl:campaign_nurgle]]Nurgle’s[[/sl]] influence is strong, his power inextricably linked to the constantly shifting ebb and flow of deathly disease.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] can research technologies over time. Technologies are researched on the [[sl_tooltip:campaign_technology_panel]]Technology panel[[/sl_tooltip]] and bring a variety of civic and military benefits.
The Technologies button is shown next to the End Turn button on the campaign interface.

The [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] of [[sl:campaign_tzeentch]]Tzeentch[[/sl]] can use Teleport [[sl:campaign_stances]]stance[[/sl]] to instantly reposition themselves to a nearby location on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]], potentially launching surprise attacks as they do so.

The type of terrain varies across a [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] and can affect [[sl:campaign_army_movement]]army movement[[/sl]]. Sufficiently hostile environments can cause [[img:icon_attrition]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_attrition]]attritional[[/sl]] casualties in armies trying to move through them.

The Masque’s endless curse draws all nearby into her unholy pageant. Eternal Daemon or mortal man, every [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] of the Accursed Troupe may play their part in her deadly performances of choreographed slaughter.

Since the dawn of time, an unseen struggle for supremacy has been fought between the Gods of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]]. One of the Gods may fleetingly prevail, or two might face off in a feud, but the Great Game never truly ends.

The Menace Below is an army ability which allows [[sl:campaign_skaven]]Skaven[[/sl]] factions to summon a [[sl:campaign_units]]unit[[/sl]] of Clanrats anywhere on the battlefield during a [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

The Artefact Vault is where the Master Runelord Thorek Ironbrow reforges recovered parts of ancient Artefacts in his efforts to help return the [[sl:campaign_dwarfs]]Dwarfs[[/sl]] to their former glory.

All who face Dechala and survive become one of her spellbound [[img:icon_thralls]][[/img]]Thralls, toiling in mindless servitude in her extravagant [[img:icon_dechala_pleasure_palace]][[/img]]Pleasure Palaces, bringing forth the [[img:icon_decadence]][[/img]]Decadence that fuels her horrific power.

Throgg is [[sl:campaign_norsca]]Norsca's[[/sl]] self-proclaimed King of Trolls, who has vowed to despoil the world in the name of the [[sl:campaign_gods]]Dark Gods[[/sl]]. By growing his [[img:icon_troll_expansion]][[/img]]Dominion, he can unite the dreaded strength of the world's Trolls and brings the Monstrous Horde's hinterland creatures to his beck and call.

The journey of Bhashiva, the White Tiger will lead her to uncover [[img:icon_relics]][[/img]]Relics – the treasured lost artefacts of her ancestors. By devoting them to the Three Pillars of the Tiger Court, the Tiger Warriors can greatly enhance their enduring warrior-culture.

The Tomb Kings are the undying rulers of the desolate, wind-swept deserts of Nehekhara. Rising from their sarcophagi, their mummified forms possess the same thirst for conquest in Undeath that drove them in life.

In her campaign of lavish excess and ever-growing [[img:icon_decadence]][[/img]]Decadence, Dechala the Denied One indulges her every whim, giving the Tormentors powerful means to proliferate unto the world exquisite pleasures and terrors alike.

[[sl:campaign_chaos_dwarfs]]Chaos Dwarf[[/sl]] Sorcerer Lords vie for power and domination by competing for Seats on the Conclave of Evil, located in the Tower of Zharr. Seats enable powerful rewards for controlling factions as they seek preeminence in the eyes of Hashut, but also benefit all Chaos Dwarfs when entire Districts of Seats are controlled.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] may agree to trade with one another through [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomacy[[/sl]]. A [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]]trade agreement between two factions brings in additional {{tr:icon_money}}[[sl:campaign_money]]{{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}}[[/sl]] for both.

[[img:icon_treasure_map]][[/img]] Maps that lead to buried treasure are highly prized amongst the pirate [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lords[[/sl]] of the [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]]. Great riches may be discovered by those who can solve the riddle of the maps.
This panel contains all the collected treasure maps.
The {{tr:icon_treasury}}treasury value is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The {{tr:hp_campaign_description_treasury_button_term}} is shown next to the treasury value on the campaign interface.

Information about [[sl:campaign_tax]]{{tr:hp_campaign_tax_term}}[[/sl]] and other sources of {{tr:icon_income}}[[sl:campaign_income]]income[[/sl]], as well as expenditure, [[sl:campaign_resources]]resources[[/sl]] and [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_trade]]trade[[/sl]] agreements can be viewed on the {{tr:icon_treasury}}{{tr:hp_campaign_treasury_panel_term}}.
The details tab on the {{tr:hp_campaign_treasury_panel_term}} shows detailed information about {{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}} earned and spent by the player's faction.
The summary tab on the {{tr:hp_campaign_treasury_panel_term}} shows an overview of financial information for the player's faction.

The trade tab on the {{tr:hp_campaign_treasury_panel_term}} shows information about available resources and [[img:icon_trade_agreement]][[/img]]trading partners and {{tr:icon_income}}income for the player's faction.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Favour is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.
The available {{tr:icon_treasury}}Dark Magic is displayed at the top of the screen on the campaign interface.

[[sl:campaign_norsca]]Norscan[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]Ogre Kingdom[[/sl]] and [[sl:campaign_greenskins]]Greenskin[[/sl]] warriors respect the language of violence above all. Tribal leaders may seek to gain control of other tribes through [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

The Changeling's Deceivers work covertly to develop their economy – rather than occupying [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] directly, they secretly establish [[img:icon_trickster_cult]][[/img]]Trickster Cults within other factions’ settlements, choosing to symbiotically reap benefits or parasitically siphon the spoils of the area.
Time on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] is advanced in turns. Click the [[sl_tooltip:campaign_end_turn_button]]End Turn button[[/sl_tooltip]] to end the turn and move the game on.
Greasus Goldtooth can use his overwhelming wealth as the Overtyrant to carry out tasks exclusive to his [[sl:campaign_ogre_kingdoms]]Ogre Kingdom[[/sl]] tribe.

Tzeentch, the Changer of Ways, also known as the Raven God, is the [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] God of magic, flux, and trickery. His servants share his delight of conspiracy and manipulation, and conquer in His name with cunning, sorcery, and deceit.

Nagash, the First Necromancer, summons Undead beings under his banners. His will is absolute, his triumph – inevitable. The fate of the world is to become a sprawling Land of the Dead with Nagash as its sole master!

The [[img:icon_tunnelling_stance]][[/img]]Underway permeates the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] and can be used by certain [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]] to navigate under otherwise-impassable [[sl:campaign_terrain_types]]terrain[[/sl]].

The Gods of [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Chaos[[/sl]] draw strength from worship performed in the physical world. As each God's [[sl:campaign_chaos_corruption]]corruption[[/sl]] spreads, their factions may call on this power to enact Unholy Manifestations – Daemonic spells of prodigious power.
The Unholy Manifestations panel is accessed via the button in the bottom-right of the main campaign interface.

[[sl:campaign_units]]Units[[/sl]] within [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] are represented on the user interface as Unit Cards. Each card displays essential information about the unit it represents.

[[sl:campaign_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] belonging to the same faction may exchange [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]], in order to better redistribute their forces. Select a controllable army and right-click on another to exchange units between them.
The Unit Exchange panel appears when a controlled army is sent to exchange units with another controlled army.

[[sl:campaign_units]]Units[[/sl]] gain experience as they fight [[sl:campaign_battles]]battles[[/sl]]. More experienced units have higher [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]leadership and fight more effectively.

The Unit Info panel appears to the left of the screen when the cursor is hovered over a [[sl:campaign_unit_cards]]Unit Card[[/sl]] and shows vital information about the subject [[sl:campaign_units]]unit[[/sl]].
[[sl:campaign_units]]Units[[/sl]] may be merged or disbanded from the rollout that appears when a [[sl:campaign_unit_cards]]Unit Card[[/sl]] is clicked.

An [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] may recruit new [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]] to swell its ranks. Recruitment takes [[sl:campaign_turns]]time[[/sl]] and costs [[sl:campaign_money]]{{tr:hp_campaign_money_term}}[[/sl]], and the recruiting army must remain stationary while training is completed.
The Recruit Units button is shown on the Army panel when a controlled army is selected.

The Unit Recruitment panel is opened by clicking the [[sl_tooltip:campaign_unit_recruitment_button]]Recruit Units button[[/sl_tooltip]] on the [[sl:campaign_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl]], and shows recruitment options for the selected [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]].

The strength of damaged [[sl:campaign_units]]units[[/sl]] will [[img:icon_replenishment]][[/img]]replenish over [[sl:campaign_turns]]time[[/sl]] when in home or [[sl:campaign_alliances]]allied[[/sl]] territory.

The type of each [[sl:campaign_units]]unit[[/sl]], which indicates its general form and usage, is shown on its [[sl:campaign_unit_cards]]Unit Card[[/sl]]. Examples of unit types include infantry and artillery.

[[sl:campaign_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] are subdivided into units of many individual soldiers. Units are represented by [[sl:campaign_unit_cards]]Unit Cards[[/sl]] on the [[sl:campaign_army_panel]]Army panel[[/sl]] and elsewhere on the campaign interface.

Ursun, the [[sl:campaign_kislev]]Kislevite[[/sl]] Bear-God, has been wounded and is held captive within the [[sl:campaign_forge_of_souls]]Forge of Souls[[/sl]], deep within the [[sl:campaign_realm_of_chaos]]Realm of Chaos[[/sl]]. Various powers, both mortal and Daemonic, seek to reclaiming his essence.

The greatest warrior and commander of the [[sl:campaign_high_elves]]High Elves[[/sl]], Tyrion amasses greater [[img:icon_influence]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_influence]]Influence[[/sl]] from his [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]] victories than his peers, affording him unique powers to boost Eataine’s military and defensive capabilities in various ways.

Pirates, both living and dead, are the deadly scourge of the high seas, and woe betide any who sight their black sails upon the horizon. By raiding and pillaging across the Great Ocean they compete with one another for [[img:icon_infamy]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_infamy]]Infamy[[/sl]].

[[img:icon_corruption_vmp]][[/img]]Vampires are obsessed with power, and among the Midnight Aristocracy nothing showcases one’s power more than subjugating other [[img:icon_corruption_vmp]][[/img]]Vampire leaders.

Scattered around the world, concealed within settlements,  Vampires slumber in their [[img:icon_vmp_lair]][[/img]] Lairs until the hour strikes for a dread purpose to be fulfilled. To you, all their wicked plans are irrelevant, for they are mere pawns in your own dark game.

The Midnight Aristocracy have long struck terror into the hearts of the mortal [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]]. From their lairs deep in Sylvania, the Vampire Counts strike out against the living with their massed [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] of the eager dead.

[[img:icon_corruption_vmp]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_vampires]]Vampiric factions[[/sl]] spread [[img:icon_corruption_vmp]][[/img]]vampiric [[sl:campaign_corruption]]corruption[[/sl]] where they settle. This [[img:icon_corruption_vmp]][[/img]]corruption blights the land, making it suitable for undead creatures and unsuitable for the living.

Each [[img:icon_general]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_lords]]Lord[[/sl]] of the [[sl:campaign_vampire_coast]]Vampire Coast[[/sl]] exhibits a primary [[sl:campaign_character_traits]]trait[[/sl]] to which their [[img:icon_loyalty]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_loyalty]]loyalty[[/sl]] is inherently linked. Actions linked to the Lord’s trait must be performed or his or her loyalty will suffer.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] of certain [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]] may demand that another faction becomes its [[img:icon_vassal]][[/img]]vassal through [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomacy[[/sl]]. A vassal faction is bound to its master and must follow it diplomatically.

Each player [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] has its own victory conditions which, if achieved, will win them the [[sl:campaign_campaign_game]]game[[/sl]]. Victory conditions can be viewed on the [[sl:campaign_missions]]Objectives panel[[/sl]].

A [[sl:campaign_greenskins]]Greenskin[[/sl]] Warboss whose [[sl:campaign_factions]]faction[[/sl]] gains sufficient [[img:icon_waaagh]][[/img]]Reputation from their belligerent exploits will be able to make a Call to Waaagh!, temporarily gaining additional mobs for each of their [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] to help [[sl:campaign_razing]]raze[[/sl]] or occupy a targeted rival’s capital.

[[sl:campaign_factions]]Factions[[/sl]] may wage war on one another in order to capture territory and achieve military dominance. War can be declared via [[sl:campaign_diplomacy]]diplomacy[[/sl]] or by attacking an enemy [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]].

[[img:icon_military_alliance]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_alliances]]Allies[[/sl]], or factions with [[sl:campaign_vassalage]]vassals[[/sl]] may choose to co-ordinate their war efforts against their common enemies. Targets to attack or defend may be assigned, [[sl:campaign_outposts]]outposts[[/sl]] in allied territory may be constructed, or control of entire allied [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] requested.
The presence of an ally mission is indicated on the Diplomacy button the main campaign interface.
The War Co-ordination button is shown on the Diplomacy screen if an allied faction is selected.
Only one outpost may be constructed for each ally. An outpost may be moved once constructed.
The War Co-ordination panel is only available when an allied faction is selected on the Diplomacy screen.
The Request Army tab will be inaccessible if no suitable allied armies are available for recruitment.
Targets may be assigned by clicking the Select Target button and then left-clicking an army or settlement on the map.

[[sl:campaign_warriors_of_chaos]]Warriors of Chaos[[/sl]] muster their armies instantly from the local area, while their [[img:icon_warband]][[/img]]Warbands allow them to transform recruits into more powerful forms or devote them to specific Chaos Gods to align them with their Lord’s [[sl:campaign_dark_authority]]Dark Authority[[/sl]].

The Warriors of Chaos seek nothing but to sow destruction amongst the mortal [[sl:campaign_races]]races[[/sl]] in service to their [[sl:campaign_chaos]]Dark Gods[[/sl]]. Their vast [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] march south from the frozen wastes to slaughter and destroy.

From her mountain dwelling in Silver Pinnacle, Neferata, Queen of Mysteries, extends her influence through her Web of Power – her means to manipulating the world from the shadows – paving the way to her ultimate goal of returning to power in Lahmia.

The Winds of Magic blow across the land, providing a source of magical power to those that can wield it. As [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] move through [[sl:campaign_provinces]]provinces[[/sl]] containing favourable winds they can harness and store this power for use by their spellcasting units in [[sl:campaign_battles]]battle[[/sl]].

The [[sl:campaign_tzeentch]]Raven God’s[[/sl]] command of sorcery grants his acolytes power over the [[sl:campaign_winds_of_magic]]Winds of Magic[[/sl]] themselves. By altering the strength of the Winds, Tzeentchian [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] can influence the ability of enemy forces to charge their Power Reserves.
The Winds of Magic Manipulation panel can be opened from the main campaign interface when playing a Tzeentch faction.
The Winds of Magic power reserve bar is shown on the Army panel when an army containing a spellcaster is selected.

Striking out from the shadowy forests of [[sl:campaign_kislev]]Kislev[[/sl]], the Daughters of the Forest convene in the Witch’s Hut to harness the magic of special relics, allowing Mother Ostankya to conjure powers that can bless the worthy or curse her foes.

The reclusive Asrai are a [[sl:campaign_races]]race[[/sl]] of Elves that long ago separated from their kin in order to live as one with nature. Striking out from their forest home of Athel Loren, the Wood Elves see themselves as guardians and healers of the natural world.

Ariel is the Queen of the [[sl:campaign_wood_elves]]Wood Elves[[/sl]], a supremely powerful Legendary [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Hero[[/sl]] who aides her kin heal the forests of the world.

Drycha has deep-rooted distrust of [[sl:campaign_wood_elves]]Wood Elves[[/sl]], only making use of them on her terms. The Wargrove of Woe does not recruit normal Elves except those that have been put under a [[img:icon_glamoured]][[/img]]Glamouring spell to make them believe that they fight for their Queen Ariel, which results in them having modified combat stats.

In addition to [[sl:campaign_unit_recruitment]]recruiting units[[/sl]], Drycha’s Wargrove of Woe may also summon spirits and beasts of the forest to fight for their cause, allowing them to build [[sl:campaign_armies]]armies[[/sl]] more swiftly than other factions.

The [[sl:campaign_wood_elves]]Wood Elf[[/sl]] Sisters of Twilight have a unique relationship with Lord Daith, the legendary blind master smith of Athel Loren. In the [[img:icon_forge_of_daith]][[/img]]Forge of Daith he crafts special equipment for them, which can either be refined to gradually and permanently upgrade them as preferred by Naestra, or reforged to grant powerful temporary effects as demanded by Arahan.

The Worldroots reach out across the continents from beneath Athel Loren’s Oak of Ages, bringing life to the Magical Forests of the world. It is the duty of the [[sl:campaign_wood_elves]]Wood Elves[[/sl]] to increase the [[img:forest_health]][[/img]]health of these Magical Forests, healing them by securing their borders and performing Rituals of Rebirth.
Worldroots permeate the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] and can be used by the Wood Elves to navigate through otherwise-impassable [[sl:campaign_terrain_types]]terrain[[/sl]].

Arbaal the Undefeated must continually seek challenges of battle and remain undefeated to avoid Khorne's wrath. With every Challenge of Khorne overcome, Arbaal earns more of [[img:icon_khornes_favour]][[/img]]Khorne's Favour to increase his power via Khorne’s Boons.

Using the unmatched range of the longship, [[i]]Seafang[[/i]] – said to have taken the vessel as far as the Realm of Chaos upon the Winds of Magic themselves – Wulfrik is [[sl:campaign_norsca]]Norsca's[[/sl]] ultimate seafaring warrior, who travels the four corners to mercilessly attack the world's [[img:icon_port]][[/img]]ports with terrifying ease.
[[sl:campaign_armies]]Armies[[/sl]] and [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlements[[/sl]] exert zones of control around them, through which an enemy army cannot pass except to attack the owner.
Once gained, Devotion may be used to perform [[sl:campaign_motherland]]Invocations of the Motherland[[/sl]].
Factions must encounter one another on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]] before diplomacy becomes available between them.

Over time, Khornate [[sl:campaign_factions]]factions[[/sl]] will automatically take control of [[sl:campaign_ruins]]ruined settlements[[/sl]] in [[sl:campaign_provinces]]provinces[[/sl]] they partially control.
Learn more about Khorne factions being drawn to destruction [[url:script_link_campaign_drawn_to_destruction]]here[[/url]].
This is the amount of [[img:icon_amber]][[/img]]Amber required to construct this building, as well as any previous buildings in the chain.
In order to research this technology, this amount will be deducted from your total supply of [[img:icon_amber]][[/img]]Amber.
In order to recruit this unit, this amount will be deducted from your total supply of [[img:icon_amber]][[/img]]Amber.
The Forge of Souls must be reached by any who wish to confront Ursun's captor and free the God-Bear.
Learn more about the Gardens of Morr [[url:script_link_campaign_gardens_of_morr]]here[[/url]].
Learn more about Gifts of Slaanesh [[url:script_link_campaign_gifts_of_slaanesh]]here[[/url]].
Learn more about the Great Bastion [[url:script_link_campaign_great_bastion]]here[[/url]].

[[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Heroes are recruited on the [[sl:campaign_recruit_hero_panel]]Hero Recruitment Panel[[/sl]], which is accessible when a [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] or [[sl:campaign_hordes]]horde army[[/sl]] is selected.
Multiple types of [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero may be available for recruitment, each with different strengths and abilities.

[[img:icon_hero]][[/img]][[sl:campaign_heroes]]Heroes[[/sl]] are versatile independent agents that can perform [[sl:campaign_hero_actions]]actions[[/sl]] against hostile targets on the [[sl:campaign_campaign_map]]campaign map[[/sl]].

A selected [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero can be instructed to [[sl:campaign_hero_actions]]act[[/sl]] against an enemy [[sl:campaign_armies]]army[[/sl]], [[sl:campaign_settlements]]settlement[[/sl]] or [[img:icon_hero]][[/img]]Hero by right-clicking that target.
