Brutal even for a butcher, armed to the teeth, utterly singular in purpose, and with three heads. Your chances? Next to zero.
Stalwarts of Cathayan military excellence, who hold themselves to a higher standard than any lesser warrior can fathom.
The enemy are not getting in, not without a wealth of the bloodiest violence and wave upon wave of screaming, agonising death.
Administrator of the realm, architect of the Dragon Emperor’s will, and executioner of his enemies.
Intrigue and subtlety must sometimes be abandoned in favour of talon and fang.
With mighty wings outstretched and composite bow at the ready, Saytang's arrows cannot be turned aside.
Bolts of blue fire blessed by the Moon Dragon's destructive power deliver her scorn from afar.
Silhouetted in macabre shapes, abominable airborne monsters gaze down from the sky, seeing all.
The Empress' eyes and ears take many forms, none more dreaded than her personal murder of Crowmen.
A terrifying example of the breed, these lions each sport a pair of giant wings, enabling them to bear down their savage attacks from above as well as at ground level.
This giant avian is blessed by the Moon Empress and enveloped in silvery flame that will burn the foe to ash at the slightest touch.
In living jade lies raw spell-power bound to stone – a bestial conduit of sorcery!
An arcane aura of sorcery-diminishing energy surrounds the blackness of the Jet Guardian’s monstrous frame.
Counting bodies like sheep to the rhythm of the War Drums…
Do you hear that? That's the sound of our death approaching!
They may look like middle-aged, reactionary landowners, but the Druzhina fight with considerable skill when their way of life is under threat.
Naryska Leysa is the finest warrior Kislev has to offer, consecrated by the Cult of Ursun and favoured by the Ice Court: the living Wrath of Kislev.
The Koldunja tend the spirits of the land, calling upon them for their placation, summoning or banishment.
The Znarkharja have deep knowledge of all ailments and can tap into life-forces to heal or debilitate.
The power of ‘the sight’ gifts attunement with the frightening power of nature, spirits and lifeforces combined into malicious spellcraft.
The Vorozheja communicate with spirits of ill-fortune to twist reality and manipulate the future.
Behold the horrors endured by the hag's foes at the end of her cauldron's smoky tendrils; Mother Ostankya is a dreaded sight to all!
There's nothing to see but a tranquil treeline… and projectiles flying from it with pinpoint precision.
No man could fail to tremble in fear once the wolves of winter descend.
Nothing irks these fighting men of Kislev more than the forces of Chaos, but "people from the south" come a close second…
What the blunderbuss doesn't finish, the axe certainly will!
These giant beasts lurk beneath the frozen tundra, waiting to rise up and freeze the foe to icy death.
Such a creature is driven by monstrous hunger, endlessly prowling for fresh meat.
Be wary men, death could be lurking in those trees…
They say a single bite is enough to put this feral beast's prey beyond the help of healing.
New life springs forth at every touch – a debt only the death of his enemies can pay for.
Wherever the Wandering Wizards go, magic and carnage are sure to follow.
Depthless Daemonic malice and a low tolerance for boredom incite the Changeling’s ever-shifting schemes... and appearance.
Hahaha! You think this is the real Changeling? IT IS.
Treachery, misery, violence, insanity… You'll experience all that while being torn apart by a rabid beast at the same time…
Few beings are equally as dangerous in death as they are in life.
Even such an evolved creature is still a rampaging monster at heart.
Even the mightiest of creatures must fear the Cockatrice, for its gaze means certain death...
Abomination! What manner of twisted creature is that?
How exactly does one fight a twisted mass of tentacles and teeth?
…and now the heavens send their love: your sudden death from above!
Get the right elevation, pull the lever, and their skin comes off just like that!
Why throw a single axe when you can throw several all at once?
Surviving this long against such terrible odds is either due to luck or martial skill, honed to a razor’s edge – probably both.
Loners by nature, resenting any distraction, and committed only to dying gloriously!
There's a lot of things to mourn in war – your death won't be one of them!
Once shame has stained the soul, it can only be wiped away with blood.
Fitting Trollhammer torpedoes to a Gyrocopter is audacious engineering, but the safest way to take out larger monsters from afar.
The least successful of all Slayers; these warriors have thrown themselves into deadly combat countless times and somehow survived.
A lust for treasure, obsession with danger, and affinity for rum has Slayer Pirates venture where few sailors willingly go.
Fifteen Dwarfs and a dead Dwarf’s chest,\\nYo, ho, ho and a flagon of ale,\\nEach one a goner means more for the rest!
Whether riddling a single foe or blasting a swathe into oncoming troops, the dual barrels of the Grudge-raker make easy work of it!
What use is a gun in the close quarters of a mine shaft? Depends on the gun. Depends on the Dwarf!
It may look rather 'lightweight' but the cannons sure pack a punch.
Condensed within every rocket is a volatile mote engrained with the strength of Elspeth's magic, ready to unleash vortices of swirling death.
A reminder of man’s mortality lies in the dread nature of these Knights’ frightening appearance, ostensibly at odds with their motto: “Fear Not Death”.
On the Magisterix's command, these riders unleash dark, withering shots that drain the lifeforce of any who are successfully hit.
They say the Graveyard Rose walks the hazy barrier between the realm of the living and the realm of the dead.
War is but the beginning of true innovation.
Give a great Engineer a workshop, he’ll win you the battle. Give him command of an army, and he could win you the war.
When judgement comes calling, woe betide anyone sentenced to face the headsman's swing.
The power of alchemy manifested in battlefield sorcery; the Gold Wizard is worth his weight in the purest gold.
Heavy armour shields these Ironsides from Elspeth’s ensorcelled munitions, so they can fire their weapons without their own flesh degrading!
This company of sharpshooters uses specially-modified rifles and unerring accuracy to fell their foes from several hundred paces.
Merchants beset whilst travelling the trade road from Hergig have seen their approaching foe drop dead with a loud crack, and no gunmen to be seen.
When gifted with the finest training money can buy, every bullet finds its mark.
Charged with defending mortar and cannon batteries in combat, these stalwart warriors never allow an artillery position to become overwhelmed.
The Dark Lady's imbuements make for a most terrifying Land Ship, that brings forth a hail of death-carrying spells and firepower.
As expensive vanity projects go, few are quite so large, or quite as deadly…
Created by the forges of Nuln for the Guild masters of Marienburg, this prototype has had no expense spared on its finery or munitions.
Combined with rolling, steel-clad machinery, a manoeuvrable and superbly armoured Volley Gun is a truly deadly piece of equipment.
The physical manifestation of Khorne’s vengeance, unleashed against His doom-bound foes.
These grotesque flying monstrosities spread the word of decay via deadly clusters of diseased shrapnel, inflicting the most horrid of maladies.
What little survives the slobbering jaws, will meet their doom by a lance of utterly foul afflictions.
Once-esteemed Knights fallen to a more putrid embrace – what remains of their former banner are tactics disgustingly twisted for their new lords.
When the beastly hordes roar, hungry for battle, dark sorcery shall aid in their slaughter!
The Plaguelord’s hosts are led with the exuberance of a carnival, their leaders ostentatiously marked with the grisly palette of sickness.
Nurgle wields the ways of death; through His conjurers, leeching the souls of His foes.
The Plague Lord's watchmen oversee His beloved children, spreading malaise and invigorating the sickly masses.
So many diseases to catalogue, and so little time!
There is no end to the vile horrors that madness could drive one so foul to enact.
Wielding such dark and ancient arcane power, Ketzak will not remain forgotten for long.
The most vicious cruelties are often inspired by the darkest of ambitions.
To be considered 'befouled' by even the virulent hordes of Nurgle is a disgustingly impressive feat indeed.
Revenge is best served at the tip of a bloodied claw, and the point of sharp and gnashing teeth.
Nothing can survive the onslaught of one prophesied to be desolation incarnate.
The Beastmen’s living tribute to the Lord of Pestilence swarm and breed prodigiously, wallowing in war and filth.
All fear the booming steps of an Ogre, twisted and mutated by the malignant forces of Chaos.
Size is no defence against an oncoming plague, nor against the great weapons of Nurgle’s beloved adoptees.
When steel becomes corroded and arrows turn to ash, there is little wonder as to why no one survives this esteemed guardian of Nurgle's garden.
Slimy as a toad; deadly as a Dragon.
Converting Ruinous charges into death for their foes is a favoured 'tactic' amongst Khorne's warriors. They do not even need to be the ones charging.
Atop a Giant Spider, both flinger and rock look deceptively harmless – an illusion broken once they fire, along with anything else in the way.
This giant crossbow is designed to smash through battlelines at close range, enabling the Greenskins to then charge in and smash the foe into bloody pieces.
Using this "so-fisti-cated" war machine yields fatally predictable results. Something always dies, be it the enemy, or an unlucky gobbo or ten.
Getting through such shields and armour is a feat worthy of song. The Black Orc underneath, however, trades only in axe-accompanied dirges.
Da Plan iz simple: you listen to wot I say and we win dis good! I take care of da big stuff. Got that?
It may be a manic shriek from a dark place, or a gleaming stab-blade rushing out of nowhere; one never knows how Night Goblins will reveal themselves.
Once unleashed, a Great Shaman's powers are both terribly savage and savagely terrible to all those in their path.
Did the loss of Snagla's tribe put the Spider-God’s voice into his dreams? No. Snagla goes wherever he wants, bringing his madness with him.
This massive example of the simplest Greenskin race is a brutal but inaccurate blunt instrument, directed at the enemy to wreak maximum mayhem!
The warpaint around its maw has done nothing for its appearance or battle capabilities. Both are naturally terrifying.
An Orc's mental faculties are always improved by a rock to the head. In Ruglud's case, it made him a veritable genius. Orcs with crossbows? Inspired!
In stupidity and violence, Orcs and Goblins may have rivals, sometimes. Chaining noisome Squigs together ensures they reign supreme in both ways!
With the weight of his God's gaze on his shoulders and his God's Destroyer in his hands, he brings both to bear with unstoppable force.
Unusually verbose and not as mindlessly voluble as most other followers of Khorne. The rigour of their mission and its devastating outcome mandate it.
'KILL FOR KHORNE! KILL FOR KHORNE!\\nKILL FOR KHORNE! KILL FOR KHORNE!"
Skarr does not sleep, the fire in his veins such that he can never rest, even should he wish to – or even die.
A Slayer of Kings swifter than the last beat of a shattered heart; a Daemon that commands the respect of the Dark Gods themselves.
Particularly savage Beastmen sworn to serve the Blood God, Khorngors bear his colours on their skin and fur.
These elite Chaos Warriors choose to prey upon other Northmen because the soft southern tribes present no challenge to them in battle.
As the Bringers’ footsteps rattle the mortal realm's tenuous barriers, blood-dimmed tides break through to mix with the blood of their terrified victims.
These lunatic murdersmiths are revered and feared in equal measure as some of Khorne's most powerful servants in the mortal world.
Khorne-forged men or Chaos-born Daemons? The sight of these slavering abominations on the battlefield precludes any debate as to their provenance.
Such a mutant creature cannot be broken by conventional means, instead requiring sorcery to bind them to a Chaos Champion.
In Khorne's realm, the most destructive wildfires do not burn themselves out. They are given wheels.
Extremely battle-hardened and fearless, even for an Ogre, Bragg is his kind's shadowy executioner, dreaded by all sides equally.
Cross a Bruiser and they'll kick out yer tusks, split yer 'ead open and eat yer best Gnoblar just so they can tell their mates.
Gore-spattered, with bloody cleavers, Butchers look like avatars of death on the battlefield.
Any Butcher should watch the skies, where the first portents of the Great Maw were seen.
Though he exaggerates with wild abandon, Golgfag is still the most successful and well-travelled of all Ogres.
The Paymaster is just as important as an Ogre Company’s leader, holding the purse strings and dishing out the loot when the job’s done.
The harbingers of the Great Maw are known to take pleasure in their killing work.
Grim portents can be revealed in dark skies just as they can be gleaned from carved entrails.
One could conceivably exploit an Ogre's lack of subtlety. A select few Ogres have learned to exploit the inconceivable alternative to that stereotype.
There are few killers-for-hire you'd rather have on your side than Golgfag's own battle-hardened cronies.
Some Gnoblars like to 'pig joust' with the enemy, riding atop each other to slay (or at least greatly irritate) the enemy in battle.
Serve the Lady? Whatsa 'lady'? That some kind o' gobbo!?! CHAAARGE!
With a sudden swoop and a deadly swipe, death is delivered from above, by claw and beak.
The warping effects of raw magic have gradually turned the Thundertusk into a walking patch of winter, emanating frost and chilling waves of freezing air.
As fast and resilient as armoured horses, Yhetees lead monstrous charges to weaken enemy battle lines and maul any opponent who dares stand up to them.
Rarely do such mighty specimens come down from their mountaintops. When they do, they bring the might of those mountaintops with them.
See the shadows move. Hear them speak. Feel them cut. In the immaterial, sensation manifests. In the inanimate, madness inchoates.
Delicate whips flay the skin in patterns most artful, combining with colourful wisps of flame to create a masterwork of pain and horror.
Cuttingly cruel in their bladework, endlessly subtle in their demagoguery, and unmatched by Champions of other Chaos Gods in perversity of pride.
There is divine strength in Caradryan's hand, and the wisdom of Asuryan sits upon his noble brow.
Mages who accompany the High Elf fleet have developed methods to shape and control the very nature of water.
Peerless fighters and warship captains, Sea Helms are masters of both land and sea battles.
The admiral of the Asur navy gives neither mercy nor quarter to those who threaten Ulthuan.
Smaller cousins of Sea Elementals, Oceanids are nevertheless fearsome opponents if their ire is roused.
The crews of the High Elf fleet are seasoned mariners, and often accompany the Sea Guard ashore when numbers are lacking.
Utterly loyal, the crew of the Dragonship Kalendirian will do anything at the behest of their captain, Sea Lord Aislinn.
Reptilian teeth snap at the High Elves’ foes, before dragging them screaming into the watery abysses where the barnacled serpents dwell.
Silak has a legendary reputation among sailors of the Old World, considered a most terrifying creature of the deep.
Born from and churning with magically-soused waters, Sea Elementals summon primal dread in the heart of any seafarer.
Compact Eagle Bolt Throwers are mounted on a Skycutter's prow, when the crew expect to go into heavy battle.
As one of the swiftest of airborne vessels, the Skycutter allows an Asur fleet to maintain aerial superiority over the battlefield.
Emulating the Dragon Kalagan's legendary deeds, the Sons roam the battlefield in search of those who need their aid.
Just like the mighty water-winged Dragon of legend, the Sons prowl the skies, terrifying the Asur’s enemies while bringing aid to their brethren.
From the desolate plains, they came… cruel, cunning and treacherous, and wanting nothing more than to crush their enemies under their great scythed wheels.
Riding with bare steel in both hands, these mounted butchers carve through infantry lines like whirlwinds of carnage.
First comes the charge, breaking lines like brittle rows of straw. Then the great axes fall, sundering shields and skulls with frightening ease.
Intoxicated by pre-battle rituals, these Serpent-worshipping horsemen seem oblivious to pain and fear, singing, screaming and charging with undulating battle cries.
A terrifying marvel of a were-bear even amongst his feral tribe, Beorg has received the Ruinous Powers' dark blessings in the most spectacular way.
Groomed by the Matriarch of its stronghold since a hatchling, Fimir Nobles boast cunning intellect, overbearing bulk and the loyalty of their tribes.
As the Shaman-Sorcerer crosses the desolate places of the world at dusk, old bones stir and spirits, freshly awakened, shudder in anticipation.
A shimmering haze distorts the air around the Shaman-Sorcerer, a promise of an imminent ritualistic pyre... with his enemies the fuel!
This Shaman-Sorcerer's every gesture is accompanied by subtle chiming, resonant, faraway tolling, or the creaking of rust-ridden metal.
Hated and feared by his own people, Sayl the Faithless holds a unique mastery over the unholy energies that course through the Chaos Wastes.
Suffering and misery are enjoyable things to the grim Marauders of the Crow, who find fulfilment in the horrors of battle.
The Chaos Gods' gifts have left traces of the were-bear's mark in the Bearmen of Urslo, yet their marauding fury has always been theirs.
With Great Weapons in hands, it is unclear whether the savagery of these Bearmen is due to the Chaos Gods' mark, or their unusually potent Norscan bloodlust.
The living emanation of Chaos' twisting, ravening power, the Chimera's tri-throated roar challenges only the most foolhardy Sorcerer to try and bind it to their will.
In the coruscating Winds at the summit of the world, the Chimerae of Bloodshriek Citadel bathe in the twisting power of Chaos.
Riven of soul, twisted of body, and laid low by the Chaos Gods for an ancient transgression, the Curs'd are driven by the hatred of all that lives.
Lumbering, rune-marked flesh and a semblance of prior intelligence hint at a ghastly presence of old tribal magics…
Even the most terrifying and majestic of beasts are reduced to an abject spectacle by the gaping jaws bursting forth from below!
Such are the contradictory forces these creatures evoke, tearing oneself apart would be a mercy – one they will *not* grant you.
In their blistering speed, these chariots truly act as harbingers of things to come. Yet let no one claim they are mere messengers…
Spurning the fawning acolytes of Slaanesh, Dechala leaves behind haunted expanses strewn with dying Thralls, carelessly thrown aside.
Forever marked by mischance brought forth through her mastery of dance and pantomime, the Masque’s affliction is blissful and dreadful to behold.
Those who stand at Styrkaar's side in battle are guaranteed victory, yet what truly puts their strength to the test is the celebratory feast afterwards!
Some Dark Elves have long ago realised that murder's finality cannot compare to the sweetness of endless torture.
Some Beastmen would live more deliciously than others, driven by a perverse hunger for the excesses of war.
On the heady path of Chaotic temptation, you eventually realise that the route back has... disappeared entirely.
Crossing the ever-retreating boundaries of wickedness has, for some Slaaneshi Champions, become a sport that makes excess the end, rather than the means.
A dark cunning lures the hunter into the forest’s depths, where awaits an ambush of blood-red eyes and savage fangs.
A stag's noble silhouette, some Bretonnian folk believe, can keep at bay even the evils prowling the Forest of Arden. But sometimes that silhouette presages something different.
The dark does not hide. The dark reveals... one's true senses, one's true devotion, one's true purpose.
The sight of howling mounted warriors clad in wolf pelt should terrify anyone – a point hammered home with both hands.
Of the Knights of the White Wolf's Inner circle, the Fellwolf Brotherhood are best known for their ill-discipline and howling savagery.
Exotic finery may hint at their distant conquests, but the Knights Panther’s loyalties are to the protection of the Empire’s people and lands.
The Ar-Ulric's office may no longer have the lustre of Sigmar’s coronation era, yet Valgeir carries forth the Wolf God’s will with ferocious pride.
The Priests of Ulric consider demonstrable strength the same as religious dogma, preaching it to the faithful and leading by example.
By his mere presence, the Seneschal instils discipline in his men, and – when necessary – a terrifying zeal for battle.
For the Hunting Hounds of Middenland, the hunt is on at the barest suggestion of a quarry.
For the Hounds of Ulricsberg, the hunt does not have a beginning – just as for the White Wolf himself, it never ends.
The accolade of the Teutogen Guard further strengthens a Knight of the White Wolf’s fearsome resolve for honour and duty.
Even among the Teutogen Guard, some hearken even further back to their pure-blooded origins – and closer to Ulric's feral fury.
Though their provenance and weaponry may vary, Ulric’s faithful are unified in their choice to muster and hone themselves for war in His name.
As their hatred rages against those responsible for the world’s ills, it fuels the obliviousness and insane strength needed to overcome insurmountable odds.
Harnessing the Wind of Azyr, the Celestial Hurricanum amplifies swirling sorcerous energies to a raging hurricane.
As the veneration of death grew within the Mortuary Cult, some of its members hoped to reside as naked souls in the afterlife.
Under the blistering eye of Ptra, in ritual performed among Nehekhara’s dunes, the great emptiness of the skies and deserts is embraced.
Higher status was accorded to the Liche Priests who excel in ensuring the Tomb Kings’ inviolate slumber.
The appeal of exercising power over the shadows while dwelling within them was stronger for some in the priesthood than it was for others.
Those who both accepted and embraced the curse placed upon themselves turned to worship of a kind not aspired to by the Mortuary Cult, initially.
The merciless and loyal Tomb Heralds are the harbingers of the ashes and dust that sprung their kind, and to which their foes will return.
Very few outside the Land of the Dead know the terrible truth of the fortress-sized scarabs that lay waste to the Tomb Kings' enemies.
Usirian is Nehekhara's God of the Dead –  inscribed with his icon, these most hallowed of Titans leave naught but dust and souls ready for judgement in their wake.
A terrible irony and a sign of Nagash's overwhelming hubris: the very likenesses of the Nehekharan gods cast down, now serving as protectors of his innermost sanctum.
Once punished by Nurgle, Bloab stands now in His favour, commanding Daemon Flies said to seed great fates for those they touch – if not deadly infection.
The siblings Ethrac, Otto and Ghurk, generously spoiled with the Plague Lord’s gifts, are the Befouled Brothers of Nurgle – the Glottkin.
Gutrot Spume's arrogance as a hunter of sea beasts drew him close to death, but Nurgle’s vile mutations prevented him from it.
Grossly changed to meet the appearance of Nurglings, Morbidex’s kinship with the creatures has them gleefully following him into battle as their foul champion.
With the blood of Daemons running through his veins, Orghotts seeks the Urfather’s blessings, so he may take his place in the Realm of Chaos.
A horrible, hound-like beast, grown grotesquely large from being infused with magic after living in close proximity to Chaos rifts.
A beast suffused with such quantities of raw magic that its spines have grown to a massive size, honed to a needle's piercing point.
These warriors are graced with boundless resilience, competing with one another to sample Nurgle's plagues and buboes, resulting in glorious disfigurements and twisted mutations.
Once they were Chaos Marauders, but are now anguished mutants forged by Skaven-craft to have weapons crudely grafted onto amputated limbs.
A brotherhood of Nurgle Champions, touched by the Bloab Rotspawned's Daemon Flies for exalted service to perpetuate the cycle of life and death.
Champions all, graced by Nurgle's touch through Bloab's Daemon Flies. Their dual axes carve through any enemies of Nurgle that come before them.
Deemed worthy by the Urfather himself, these Blightkings' great weapons cleave through armour and bite deep into flesh with ease.
Daemon-touched veteran warriors, called to serve under Orghotts' banner, seeking to reforge the mortal realm in the image of their master's paradise.
Deadly creatures, foul of soul, skin and stare. Their eyes can focus their contempt for other beings, paralysing their movement and draining their essence.
A single giant is a great threat indeed. But one shrouded in armour, wielding great siege claws instead of full limbs? A truly terrifying prospect.
These thirteen groupings of three Plagueclaw Catapults were among Pestilens' greatest military assets, designed to batter rival Skaven lair-dens and mighty Dwarfholds alike.
A highly modified Warp Lightning Cannon, this giant contraption leaves little more than molten goop in its gout’s wake.
Clan Pestilens' holiest relics are used to brew the foulest outbreaks and maladies in veneration of the Horned Rat himself.
It is said that one day the thirteen-headed one would rise, baptised in putrid filth and decay. That day has now come.
Arguably one of the greatest, but certainly one of the most well-known figures among his kind, Thanquol always has a plan...
The Cullers of Civilisation are disease itself given hideous corporeal form, accompanied by a creeping sickness that causes all life to wither away.
Whether by triple-bladed throwing star or deadly warpstiletto blade, the Verminlord Deceiver kills quickly, and almost without being noticed.
This suitably named Verminlord brings death with more than a hint of violence from the void.
Whether it is through confusion by deception or an unexpected blast of Warpstone dust to the face, Warpseers gift nightmare visions to their unfortunate victims.
The Deathvermin, also known throughout the Under-Empire as the Black Death, are the utterly ruthless elite of Clan Rictus' Stormvermin.
The life of a Pestilens Pusbag is short and unpleasant, much like all Pusbags themselves – but the Plague Monks have to test their maladies on something!
This accursed regiment gathers numbers of Stormfiends together for massed attacks that can easily level most infantry formations before them.
Horrifying, fleshy fusions of brain and brawn are enhanced by warp-forged gauntlets welded to their arms, each mounted with a spiked club to smash through enemy ranks.
Deadly Warpstone drill bits are fused with the Stormfiend's hands to quickly bring down even large foes in single combat, piercing armour as easily as flesh.
Hand-mounted Ratling Cannons enable the enhanced Rat-Ogres that bear them to both spray bullets from range and pound the enemy to dust at close quarters.
Used chiefly to pummel through the heaviest armour, the gauntlets fused to the Stormfiends' arms carry a dangerous electrical charge to render the foe prone to their battery.
Dual Warp-flame throwers have been fitted to these Stormfiends to burn through infantry formations with performative ease.
Their twin-Windlaunchers’ high shooting-arc makes them deadly from a distance, yet still more than capable of battering a foe to a bloody pulp up close.
Long have the Drakenhof Templars forgotten the noble purpose of their founding, which they exchanged for immortality and unerring loyalty to the von Carstein bloodline.
Though mortal, Dieter Helsnicht is undoubtedly the most obsessive student of Nagash's engendered powers, and a master of the elemental laws of Undeath.
The Supreme Lord of the Undead has returned. By his word, death comes for all, but is not the end – for Undeath's eternity is his.
The Queen of Lahmia controls the mortal world through a shadowed sisterhood, biding her time until her dynasty can be restored.
The Lord of the Blood Dragons is as forthright a Vampire as ever existed, harnessing his immortality for the simple purpose of martial supremacy.
To let these sisters close is to spend your final moments knelt, captivated by their beauty.
These sisters' claws cut as deep as the bite of their tongues.
Souls of the dead that still burn with the cold fires of despair, vengeance, and unfulfilled promises are ripe for a Necromancer's harvest.
The greatest of the Morghasts are fused from the mightiest of Ptra’s heralds and are capable of opposing the foe's most fearsome monstrosities.
Once the noble heralds of Ptra, the Nehekharan God of Light, now robbed of name, perverted of form, and some without voice – Nagash's silent executioners.
Skeletal wings darken the skies. Ungodly weapons shriek with the voices of stolen souls. Where Morghasts tread, the living perish and the dead awaken.
Vampires who hold these macabre seats of power use them as fell magical altars to manifest their dominion over those who feed their immortality.
The aptly named "Thunder-Crash Bombs" allow these specialist troops to devastate and disorient in equal measure.
Shivs, stabbers, discarded cutlery, Goblins always make do with whatever's left.
Take heed, little ones. You stand in the presence of a champion of proliferation.
The belligerent Rhinox's near-blindness is no obstacle to the mindless destruction its Ogre rider demands.
The only sure way to escape the pulverising charge of a half-blind Rhinox is to make oneself smell like another Rhinox.
An Ogre rider can control his slavering Mournfang only by raining repeated blows upon its iron-hard skull.
Spike-armoured Ogre and thunderous, indefatigable mountain beast: the heaviest shock cavalry in the known world.
To be flattened by the Mournfang's unstoppable charge is a more merciful death than being consumed by its ravenous rider.
Vicious enough to be useful but dim enough to be obedient, Gnoblars are commonly used as slaves, cannon fodder, ammunition or appetisers.
Larger and smarter than the average Gnoblar, which isn't saying much, but their snares provide a steady stream of meat.
Gnoblars are naturally attracted to the sling, which allows them to enact cruelty at a safe distance.
The only thing more frightening than a charging Ogre is an even bigger charging Ogre.
Roasting and tenderising enemies with point-blank cannon fire creates delicious, ready-to-eat meals.
Nomadic mercenaries, adorned in the garish trappings of the kingdoms they have visited, fought for and terrorised.
Many have lost a limb (or several) as a consequence of laughing at the sight of a hulking Ogre wearing a feathered hat and breeches.
Unusually astute Ogre mercenaries, boasting the exotic spoils and countless scars of far-off wars.
The lurid trophies of their many distant conflicts ensure that no two of these wandering mercenaries are armed the same way.
Sheer brute strength, unending hunger, and barely enough wit to know fear. Nothing matters more to an Ogre Bull than his next meal.
No Ogre truly needs weapons to pulverise his foes, for his immense fists suffice. But all Ogres crave trophies…
Their spiked metal gauntlets can shred foes to ribbons – which means less chewing later.
Even the dullest Ogre appears a genius against these gargantuan, vagrant cretins.
Outcast Ogre whelps become ravenous, sinewy, cannibalistic horrors, bereft of all reason.
Hunting beasts made entirely of coiled muscle and bereft of all fear.
Hide as hard as rock, horns that can tear mountain-tops asunder, hooves that can flatten legions.
Only the steeliest of Ogre trappers can face down a Stonehorn's rock-shattering charge and live to tell the tale.
Though it seems a miracle that this ramshackle catapult functions, its devastating firepower is not to be doubted.
A vast sky-cannon crudely lashed to beast-driven wheels, its thunderous volleys able to decimate entire regiments.
Worse than Hobgoblins on wolfback are Hobgoblins with Bolt Throwers, who cut down the “superior” steeds of the tall races with malicious glee.
The swiftly-propagating flames of Fire Rain Rockets more than make up for their undependable accuracy.
Wrought in the sacred form of fire-belching Dragon-mouths, their flaming cannonballs can topple almost any foe.
Their thunderous charges are as fearsome within cramped city streets as they are upon the plains of war.
The riders of the Celestial Host are the elite of the elite. The Dragon Emperor trusts only his own kin more than they.
Stoic Cathayan cavalry, as expendable as they are dutiful. The Celestial Emperor thanks them for their sacrifice.
Once outcasts for dabbling in forbidden elements, now prized for their fearsome mastery of metal and fire.
Favoured Wizard of the Emperor himself, granted knowledge of Celestial sorcery perfected across millennia.
Celestial blood grants both unassailable authority and rare mastery of the Elemental Winds.
Powerful Sorcerers second only to the Dragons themselves, Shugengan can bend the eight winds to their whims.
Though the Iron Dragon possesses untold authority, decades of Warpstone experimentation have taken a toll upon his mind.
Incomparable elemental wisdom paired with the raw Celestial power of a Dragon.
A master strategist requires unquestioning allegiance from the vast armies of their great city.
Favoured child of the Celestial Emperor, revered defender of the Great Bastion and imperious majesty incarnate.
There comes a time when only a true Dragon can defend Grand Cathay.
At the Moon Empress' behest, warriors return from the underworld to defend Grand Cathay; a brief glimmer of light before they must return to the darkness.
Only the hardiest of souls can survive the elegant volleys of Nan-Gau's devastatingly precise artillery.
The Dragon Emperor's personal bodyguard, the greatest of mortal warriors, and a shining inspiration to all Cathay.
Only the Celestial Host enjoy the greatest armaments of the Dragon Empire, for only they can guarantee victory upon the field of battle.
Should Cathay's enemies dare approach, Iron Hail volleys can shred steel plate as if it were rice-paper.
Though Cathayan crossbows are infallible, they are nothing without the discipline of the Jade soldiers who wield them.
Should the Dragon Emperor's foes survive the hail that greets their approach, they will be dashed against a near-impregnable wall of shields.
Finding harmony in stone and steel, their minds are as ordered as their finely-armoured ranks.
The living embodiment of Cathay's nigh-impregnable Great Bastion, for few enemies can hope to breach their armoured line.
Though they are but humble villagers, the Moon Dragon herself guides their aim.
Though common folk lack the training of the Jade Warriors, they fight in vast numbers and with absolute devotion to their Dragon.
Warriors of wind and field, united in harmony, their bristling spears keeping the Dragon Emperor's foes at bay.
The fearless stone giants stand guard across the length and breadth of the Celestial Empire, awaiting the Dragon Emperor's call.
The very heavens catch fire in their wake…
A flame-borne air-ship as immense as any sea-faring craft, capable of laying waste to entire legions.
A floating symbol of Cathay's pre-eminence, powered by the burning wings of magical Warbirds.
This mighty war Compass can harness the elements themselves, for even wind and lightning serve the Dragon Emperor's will.
Regardless of the wishes of his former masters, the Bearer will ascend to Godhood, and reign over the shadows forever.
Daemon Princes are amongst the greatest and most powerful servants of Chaos.
Enslaved by the Dawi-Zharr in his mortal life, he formed a pact with the Chaos Gods and was freed by a flock of Daemonic Furies.
After killing all who faced Ulgor in the pit he was a due a large reward of gold and 'freedom' from his owner. Instead, he slaughtered his keeper and joined Khorne’s legions.
It was Grand Vomitus who brought the infamous Canker Blight to the citizens of Artois and delivered the Vrux Beard Lice to Karak Azul. What other gifts shall he bring to mortalkind?
This Daemon Prince has been stealing into the Mortal World through a mirror. Once through, they will take the mirror as a shield and quickly muster their darkling host.
A promising Wizard in his past life, he was seduced by Chi'an Chi. Rumours spread that the Feathered-Prince can now control the flow of time itself.
The purest form of Ruinous energy, these Furies serve no one Chaos God in particular; their aspect changes with the balance of power as the Great Game rages.
Bloodletters borne upon colossal Juggernauts, living engines of carnage – shock cavalry as unstoppable as they are terrifying.
Knights in hell-forged armour, rewarded for their savage duty with Daemonic mounts from which to spill ever-deeper rivers of blood.
This champion is hardened by the scars of countless battles and granted will enough to command a modicum of Khorne's Blood Legion.
A terrifying fusion of unbridled rage and sheer mass. No skull shall be safe.
A smoke-belching, flesh-mangling, skull-consuming engine of purest destruction.
Cultists of the Blood God are brutes in battle, hoping to draw their master's gaze.
A mortal warrior with strength and bloodlust beyond any other, charging atop a berserker steed fed on human flesh.
Most powerful and most brutal of all Daemon warriors, living only to spill blood and harvest skulls in Khorne's name.
Driven to madness by its unending lust for slaughter, this legend insanely spurs the Blood Legion on to ever-greater acts of destruction.
A veteran consumed by its desire for unchecked slaughter. Murderous madness paired with unstoppable force.
A mighty Daemon engine, the physical manifestation of Khorne's favour, fuelled by the molten skulls of its countless victims.
Mindless fury, boundless ferocity – an engine of destruction, forever seeking redemption for an act of betrayal against the Blood God.
The Lesser Daemon of Khorne is a behorned, blood-hungry footsoldier.
Those Bloodletters that bring their master more skulls are elevated, and so their lust for blood grows.
These foul, winged Daemons are murderous Khornate energy made flesh.
Apex predators warped by the Ruinous energies of Chaos, forever desirous to gorge upon mortal flesh.
Fighters raised from the strongest of Northmen stock, but no longer truly human.
Living weapons in the service of Khorne, far stronger than scores of mortal men. No sane horseman would ride toward their hell-forged halberds.
When you fight for blood, and for Khorne, others’ simple necessities, such as sleep and food, are entirely meaningless.
Primal blood-hunters bereft of all fear, capable of tracking any prey for an eternity.
The Doom Hound, Simaergul, a favoured pet of the Blood God sent to defend the Brazen Altar.
The greatest of Khorne's Daemons, a Bloodthirster thinks only of the hunt and the skulls to be gathered in the Blood God's name.
A bull-headed Beastman pledged to the service of Khorne, for no other could provide the hot blood and red meat the Minotaur craves.
Gore-crazed, man-eating Minotaurs equipped with ancient weapons of legend harvested from their countless victims' shattered corpses.
A fallen Daemon given new life, of a sort, within a colossal, soul-harvesting hulk.
Those unable to bear the force and fury of Khorne's gifts become Spawn, with all former reason replaced by wrathful madness.
A blood-soaked, rolling altar to the Murder God's glory, bristling with fell blades, jagged spikes and the shattered skulls of the fallen.
This Daemon-infused machine bombards any who escape its wheels with their comrades’ burning, screeching skulls.
Though any wealthy soul can hire these elite horsemen, all the coin in the Motherland could not make them turn upon their queen.
The roving vanguard of Kislev's armies are sworn to protect the Motherland's desolate borders from all who threaten her.
On the freezing oblasts of Kislev, man and mount must live, die – and kill – as one.
There is no more sacred an animal to the Motherland than the mighty bear. Its savage fury must be respected before it can be harnessed.
There is no more sacred an animal to the Motherland than the mighty bear. Its savage fury must be respected before it can be harnessed.
Many is the regiment who has broken and run rather than be crushed beneath the thunderous hooves of Kislev's legendary cavalry.
Leaders who fight shoulder-to-shoulder with their soldiers must be the first to break the enemy upon their shields.
The Tzar of Tzars, the true believer, reborn to light in Kislev's darkest hour.
Though all Kislevites are equal in the eyes of the Motherland's gods, a Boyar is born to rule. His authority is absolute.
Any who mistake her youth for weakness will soon find themselves in a frozen grave.
Trained in the secrets of Ice Court since she was a girl, now wielding power most could only dream of.
Though her graceful bearing belies her deadly sorcery, the power of Winter itself flows through her veins.
By definition, the Ice Witch has delved into the most tempestuous of magical lores.
Tzarina Katarin is the greatest Ice Witch for generations, capable of arcane feats not seen since the Khan-Queens of old.
To disobey the Supreme Patriarch is to disobey Ursun himself. All deemed guilty of such heresy will pay an agonising price.
Believe in the Great Orthodoxy! Believe in the Motherland! Faith is all the armour any man needs!
The Motherland's finest warriors fight tirelessly, knowing that a well-earned drink or twelve awaits all who survive the battle.
Kislev's military elite, bearing their heavy armour and heavier weapons without complaint. Tomorrow brings rest, but today they fight.
Few have faced the magically-augmented warrior women of the Ice Court and lived to tell the tale.
Wielding magic and might in equal measure, the Ice Guard execute the unyielding will of the Tzarina herself.
Workers and warriors of forest and field, their proud hearts armouring them against elements and enemies alike.
A Kossar always warrants respect, for the working man represents the true spirit of the Motherland.
For distant cowards, the barrel of the gun. For nearby fools, the blade of the axe.
For the sake of all Kislev, the Tzarina permits her personal bodyguards to fight alongside the common man.
Those Kossars who fight hardest and longest for the Motherland's freedom are granted the honour of serving the Tzars themselves.
Just as Kislev's people fight to safeguard their land, so too will the land fight for its people.
Should the Tzarina will it, even the ravenous beasts of the oblast will fight to protect the Motherland.
Large sleds drawn by the fiercest of War Bears pack a crushing punch when pulled at speed into ordered enemy battlelines.
Even the cruellest elements are no obstacle to the Motherland's sturdy War Sleds.
Countless slaves of Chaos have fallen to this ancient cannon's roaring fusillades. To fight alongside it stokes pride in any Kislevite heart.
Great, galavanting bears of the wild, with strength and temperament enough to match foes thrice their size.
Larger than the brown bears of the south, these hulking beasts carry an aura of chill about them even when far from the ice.
Plaguebearers conveyed into battle atop shrieking, repugnant Rot Flies, winged Daemon-beasts whose speed is matched only by their indescribable hideousness.
The winged cavalry of Nurgle's rot legion, their grotesque Rot Fly mounts spitting the plague-drenched skulls of previous victims at their foes below.
Brackish Plague Toads pressed into service and forced to bear necrotic Plaguebearers into battle.
Each of this pox-ridden devotee's horrifying afflictions is a gift from their loving Plaguefather.
A towering, grotesque facsimile of the Plague God himself, his myriad sores oozing unspeakable disease.
To those able to withstand Nurgle's Rot the longest, the Plague Lord grants wit and reason far beyond that of their decaying, droning subordinates.
The Foetid Brewmaster tests his countless, horrific contagions by launching fusillades of infected Nurglings into the enemy's midst.
They stand above the droning mass of Plaguebearers, blessed by Father Nurgle with pestilent sorcery and a modicum of individual thought.
Winged Daemons, murderous Nurgle energy made flesh, that prey upon the weak from the margins of battle.
A man granted one too many of Nurgle's pestilent gifts, with flesh warped and mind broken as the Plague God's blessings overwhelm him.
Tiny, squealing Daemons, each little more than an ambulatory pus spore, they spread lethal disease throughout scores of foes.
A droning mass of Daemon footsoldiers, their broken, oozing flesh painted with the scars and sores of the Plague Lord's inexorable rot.
This shambling, droning, nauseating mass is tasked by the Fly Lord to dispense disease, decay and the gift of death to all.
Any other lifeform is a potential friend to this ooze-drenched, pox-slobbering beast – until they inevitably die, of course.
The greatest of the Fly Lord's decaying legion, a shuddering behemoth of filth and disease, spreading ruin with boundless delight.
A putrid Daemon pus-beast caked in filth, considered lower even than Nurglings, and whose gaping, noxious maw can consume a man in a heartbeat.
These immense, nauseating, winged Daemon-insects shred flesh and consume carcasses with abhorrent efficiency.
A fallen Daemon given new life, of a sort, within a colossal, soul-harvesting hulk.
Obscenity made flesh; a once-mortal creature mutated beyond reason or understanding by an abundance of Nurgle's gifts.
Other Ogres give Butchers a wide berth, lest they become part of the next feast that is cooking.
The Butcher can find a good use for every last part of a carcass.
Rejoice, for the flame-belching voice of the volcano comes to share his marvellous tales.
The fattest, wealthiest and most powerful Ogre in living memory – but still the Overtyrant hungers for more. More!
Countless legendary beasts have fallen prey to the Hunters' deadly traps and cruel spears.
Precious few Hunters can tame a raging Stonehorn without being pulverised in the process.
Unbreakable, brutal beyond measure and barely sane, Skrag heeds only the voice of the Great Maw.
Some Slaughtermasters have learned savage magics by devouring the flesh of slain beasts.
Forever carving flesh for gore-soaked rituals with which to imbue his hungry tribe with terrifying strength.
Colossal, despotic ruler of his tribe – a position earned only by devouring his rivals.
Death provides no relief, for the Heartseeker's quarry's soul shall become Slaanesh's tormented plaything.
Vainglorious mortals granted the immortal power they crave – at the cost of everything they once were.
Bartering their very souls for the saddles of Slaanesh's Daemonic steeds, these shackled mortals flense flesh from bone with their writhing, semi-sentient lashes.
Daemonettes visting upon their enraptured foes a razor-clawed ballet of blissful torment and agonised yearning.
This Daemonette has gained the notice of Slaanesh himself, the whispered secrets of his bedchamber granting her untold prestige and power.
A favoured Daemonette who directs Slaanesh's sensuous legions and harvests the tormented souls of the fallen.
A champion temptress, spreading seduction, sensation and suffering from a screeching chariot whose razored axels reduce bone to pulp in an instant.
This Daemonette has gifted Slaanesh sufficient souls to be raised above the rank and file, literally, to preach her temptations.
Slaanesh's Cultists have tormented souls, and spend their time gathering secrets and seducing others in the Dark Prince's name.
The Exalted Keeper captivates the minds of its foes even as it tears the flesh from their bones.
An ascended Daemonette and Sorceress of seduction, granted the honour of attending Slaanesh's every dark whim and desire.
The Perfect Prince's most favoured Daemonette, able and willing to hunt their prey across all eternity.
If the foe does not fall to the chariot's screeching steel blades, they shall instead know the agonising embrace of the Herald atop it.
The Glorious Doomrider, a wailing, blade-adorned carriage which conveys a Herald of Slaanesh toward her next enraptured victim at unthinkable speeds.
A notorious and ancient Keeper of Secrets, N'Kari has broken empires and countless minds in his ceaseless quest for new depraved sensations.
The lowliest of the Dark Legion, spitting unspeakable temptations as they pick at their foes' flesh.
The hypnotic, dancing footsoldiers of Slaanesh, beguiling senses before shredding flesh with knife-edged claws, euphoric in the gift of pain.
The Daemonettes gather souls with which to entertain Slaanesh for the briefest moment.
The mightiest of Norscans, bereft of fear or pity, delighting in every wound and pledged to make endless sacrifices to the Serpent.
The fearless spearmen of Slaanesh, whose faith grants them unnatural might. They delight in suffering and find rapture in sundered flesh.
Northmen who willingly join the Daemon legions in their incursions into the mortal realm, granted living lashes of purest torment.
The hunting beasts of Slaanesh, scorpion-tailed abominations whose twitching gait belies the nightmarish speed at which they ride down new victims.
Master of pain, mistress of sensation, slaying its beguiled foes with razor-clawed precision even as they beg for more.
A fallen Daemon given new life, of a sort, within a colossal, soul-harvesting hulk.
Excess incarnate: a body unravelled and a soul detonated by dark sensation upon dark sensation. A writhing, gnashing obscenity.
A fast-moving Daemonic engine; those few unfortunate souls who escape its razored maw are descended upon by its blade-clawed Daemonette riders.
A carriage adorned with reaping blades which slice Slaanesh's foes into delicate morsels, their suffering driving its riders into a rapturous frenzy.
A bone-shredding chariot, commanded by capering Daemonettes, dispensing suffering across the length and breadth of the battlefield.
Mounted warriors of great intellect and cunning, they seek forbidden knowledge – thus pledging their swords to Tzeentch.
Mortal might granted sorcerous flight, tearing the skies asunder in a blaze of blue and gold.
Spreading the words – and lies – of their master, many Cultists of the Deceiver are magically inclined.
The greatest of Tzeentch's Daemon legion, a towering master of sorcery and trickery alike, able to unravel minds as easily as it gouges flesh.
A magical slave granted rare agency, great cunning and potent sorcery by the Great Conspirator.
A powerful Daemon Sorcerer, directing the Changer's snickering legions from atop an eldritch sky-shark.
A chosen Daemon of Tzeentch, soaring through the skies on a mount pulled by multiple glimmering Screamers, raining Sorcerous doom upon all below.
A magical automaton granted a semblance of consciousness by the Raven, its unstable flesh cycling through endless shapes, colours and faces.
A shapeless mass of solid magic, granted enough momentary stability and lucidity to control the skies.
A favoured Horror commanding Tzeentch's gibbering legions and raining down change-magic from its sky-borne chariot.
The right-hand of the Raven God, Kairos is a Lord of Change blessed with full sight of both yesterday and tomorrow – but cursed with blindness of today.
When a Pink Horror is slain, it is replaced by a pair of smaller Blue Horrors, as surly as their predecessors were joyful.
One of the lowest forms of Daemon, little more than fragments of Tzeentch's dark sorcery given winged form, but lethal in a throng.
Change upon change upon change – Tzeentch devolves his mortal servants into broken, twisted nightmares.
The giggling rank and file of Tzeentch's sorcerous legion, magical energy coalesced into something like corporeal form, endlessly shifting and mutating.
Most Horrors live mayfly-short lives before reverting to magical energy, but a rare few reach veteran status.
Blazing, mindless Daemon constructs that reduce their enemies to howling puddles of bubbling flesh.
Flaming whirlwinds of Tzeentch's infinite sorcery, their flesh covered in twisted faces, they unravel their foes' very being with reality-warping Chaos-fire.
A vision of feathered horror, its flesh undulating with unnatural energies and monstrous tongue whispering countless deceptions.
Quicksilver sky-beasts, briefly leaving the tides of magic to play their part in Tzeentch's aeons-long schemes.
A fallen Daemon given new life, of a sort, within a colossal, soul-harvesting hulk.
The gift of Change gone too far, transforming its recipient into a horrifying mass of flesh, innumerable eyes and screaming mouths.
A flame-spewing sky-mount, drawn by packs of incandescent Screamers, serving Tzeentch's ineffable plan by dispensing eldritch, flesh-remaking Sorceries.
Great Wightblades cleave armour just as easily as they sever the soul.
Neither Dragon nor Giant can cause these lines to waver, for dead men know no fear.
Famed amongst his brethren and fuelled by the gods’ favour, the Hammer returns to stake his rightful claim as THE paragon amongst men.
The Warpstone wall against which all enemies of Cathay shall falter, hounded by the essence of pure magic!
Death begets more death; once the Hungering Blades taste blood, nothing can stop the carnage that follows this Khornate scourge!
Hail Dazh the Sun God, whose molten fire sets the swords of Kislev ablaze, searing the flesh of all foes!
Guards of the Festering Gate are replenished by its energies, obscured behind a nebulous swarm of Nurgle flies.
A roving band of mercenary Maneaters, equipped with the finest firearms the Empire city of Nuln has to offer.
While rampaging through battle lines, these beguiling figures of uncontrollable lust infect minds with madness at a single touch.
These Horrors are living conduits to the realm of Tzeentch, channelling volatile Warpfire directly from His dark abode.
Beside the Dragons of Cathay ride their righteous companions, generously armed with both lance and valour.
Rage burns like a cloak of blazing hellfire, sheathing these Khornate cavalrymen in a vortex of searing flames.
The elemental might of Tor blesses the weapons of his Oath-Brothers, as lightning flashes with every swing of their blades.
The Barons venture forth from the Garden of Nurgle to lavish the dreaded Wasting Sickness upon the mortal realm.
What the Sky-Titans no longer need, the Sky-Striders will gladly pluck from the corpse of their abandoned mountain holds.
There's no escaping the relentless pursuit of ones driven by such depraved obsession.
Tzeentch's Knights scorch the earth, proving to all there's no fighting the fires of fate.

Centuries of silent sentry duty at the edge of the Warpstone Desert broken by a stunning display of choreographed violence – the foe will stand little chance against the enchanted behemoth towering above them.
Even by Bloodthirster standards, the Bloody Fist stands apart, for it grows stronger as it pounds monstrous enemies to a gory blot on the landscape.
More than a mere bear, this elemental creature has all the pride and rage of its vast, beleaguered Motherland distilled into its colossal, icy form.
Those who’ve heard of Uncle Furuncle know to steer well clear of his gaseous girth, lest a torrent of putrid filth descend upon them from gods know where!

Used to living in the sub-polar temperatures of the Granitetooth Graveyard, this characteristically vicious Stonehorn knows how to use the icy cold to its best advantage, bringing far more than mere heft to the fight.
“I have such sights to show you!”
The most powerful of the Changer’s chosen confuses and beguiles, before swooping in to give his enemies a bloody, merciless mauling.
These brigands have a fearsome reputation at home and in the west. They have even been hired by the Dragon rulers of their homeland, despite their indiscriminate pillaging.
Khorne’s loathing to see his chosen servants felled by the cowardly practice of the arcane is made manifest in Flesh Hounds mostly immune to hostile magic.
The existence of the Tzarina’s secret police is no secret, for the Watchmen's ranks are not just the spies who root out opposition to her rule, but also the toughest of her retinue.
The acrid discharge of these Nurglings’ blisters inflicts wounds upon all those who strike them that may not outright kill, but painfully fester!
These so-called "Toad-Gnoblars" were once a much-debated myth amongst scholars, said to have the ability to multiply at the merest contact with water.
In the quest for perfection, one must revel in their obsessions and sacrifice everything for the Dark Prince.
For these Blue Horrors, defence is the best offence, emitting chromatic barriers to render incoming attacks futile as they inflict their own.
This Sorcerer Lord can reach into the very minds of his adversaries, ripping thoughts apart as easily as undoing a knot.
This Chaos Sorcerer employs dark and nefarious magics to tear through both body and mind.
In battle is the only time a Dragon Ogre can die, so they fight with a powerful fury.
The Shaggoth tower over the common man, casting fearsome shadows matched only by the seismic devastation they cause.
Little humanity remains within the Forsaken, only a desire for battle, followed by a furious charge into the fray.
Those who are not gored by the rolling spikes of this beast chariot are thrown to a clumsy, painful demise.
Kholek Suneater is beyond all mortal reckoning. His fury and strength, like his age, are immense. Truly, he is unstoppable.
A Lord of Change is imbued with the power of Tzeentch, able to sow madness and ruination amongst his foes.
Spoken of for many ages, this Lord of Change is favoured by Tzeentch himself, and fulfils his dark, malicious purpose.
Unblemished, frozen in time, pristine - the skin-deep appearance of Sigvald belies a twisted, corrupted, vicious soul, hungry for destruction.
This Sorcerer Lord gleans his power from death itself, consigning his opponents to endless, tormented oblivion.
The powerful Sorcerer Lord summons up pillars of flame that sear the enemy to their very core.
When subjected to his power, all before this Sorcerer Lord are sliced, diced and desiccated .
The Flag of the Blood Keep flashes violently; the Blood Knights run their enemies down.
With rune-inscribed lances and an endless thirst for human blood, these immortal Knights bring forth the wrath of the Blood Keep.
The Amber Wizard commands the Lore of Beasts, ranging the forces of nature itself against the enemy.
Boris Todbringer is a man of singular action and determined purpose: to rid the forest of Khazrak's bestial scourge.
Savage masters of the battlefield, Beastlords join the fray with axes in hand and death in mind.
The strongest, meanest Beastmen, Bestigors seek out elite foes to slaughter and dominate.
Cloaked in the power of the beast, the Bray-Shaman uses his primal mutations to exert greater strength.
Death whispers to the Bray-Shaman, who speaks the words to his enemies with hideous, incorporeal power.
Darkness marches before the Bray-Shaman, deceiving and destroying all in its path.
The earth speaks and the Bray-Shaman hears it. Nature flows through him, giving him mastery over the land itself.
Hybrid man-beasts, raging at fate, Centigors bring their anger to bear upon anything in their path.
A Centigor charges the enemy battle line, great weapon in hand, delivering oblivion to its foes.
Though clumsy, Centigors can still lodge a throwing axe deep into an enemy skull from afar.
An eldritch horror, the mad thrashing of its unnatural limbs sends all to their doom.
A pack of Chaos Warhounds charging, full of bloodlust and with jaws wide, creates no purer sense of terror.
This beast's bite brings not just pain, but also a cruel toxicity that courses through every vein.
Plagued by visions, Cygors are cursed to see the Winds of Chaos. Naturally, this makes them mad and extremely dangerous.
The Manticore is a killer, above all. Born of Chaos, mutations and madness, but a killer all the same.
Giants attack the enemy in a rage, with flailing limbs that break both man and machine apart.
Gors may be rank-and-file beasts, but that does not diminish their ferocity on the battlefield.
With a weapon in each hand, these Gors lunge and slash at anything before them with predictably wild abandon.
Gorebulls do not hesitate, smashing into enemy ranks with overwhelming power.
More than a savage and destructive beast, Khazrak has a keen mind for strategy combined with animal cunning and guile.
Where the Crowfather treads, mayhem and destruction always follow close behind.
A ferocious hunger drives axe-wielding Minotaurs into the melee - hunger for war and hunger for flesh.
A Minotaur, with axe in hand, can hold its own against dozens of enemies with vicious, brutal fury.
The victims of a Minotaur are ripped limb from limb and then, unfortunately, devoured.
Though temperamental, a successful Razorgor Chariot charge causes horrendous damage to the enemy line.
Hideously mutated and filled with hungry rage, Razorgors tear men apart in their search for food.
Though mocked by stronger beasts, Ungors nevertheless instil fear as they charge the foe down.
Although diminutive by Beastmen standards, Ungors are both faster and more nimble than others of their kind.
Ungors are more nimble than their brethren, useful for flanking foes and harassing with spears.
With shields in hand, these Ungors can engage the enemy and hold their own thereafter.
His is the grim, unending task of uprooting and shattering evil in all its forms.
Wading into battle, crazed and unable to be broken, facing their doom with furious acceptance.
These men did not ask for war, yet it has come all the same. With sword in hand, they fight because they must.
The Hammer of the Witches, fired with righteous purpose, smites evil with thunderous, armour-shattering blasts.
Well-armoured and resplendent, the Knights deliver a fierce and destructive charge.
Majesty and power personified, their devastating charge exemplifying their regal brilliance.
The heart of any battle and the embodiment of Sigmar's will as they heroically engage the foe.
With a thunderous roll, a volley of devastating, armour-piercing fire is loosed.
Some are drawn to war by the need for vengeance, fighting fiercely to sate their bloodlust.
Its destructive power cannot be overstated, the world illuminated by a turbulent battery of missile fire.
They thrive in melee, with the unbreakable spirit that comes from accepting death.
The Wind is stored and harnessed, resulting in the bursting forth of a lethal energy.
Everything about him is bent to that one great task of holding back evil.
Above their peers, Zintler's men charge down enemy lines with a destructive fury that makes the earth shake.
A semi-spectral force that severs mortal souls from their corporeal hosts.
Unspeakable evil energy is exuded, both empowering the Undead legions and crippling those who stand against them.
Devilish chariots imbued with dark and eldritch power, driving the Undead to greater, more macabre acts.
Infernal flames belch from dismal braziers, permeating the air with fragments of magic-confounding Warpstone.
When the lodestone bell rings, dark magic exudes and ripples across the battlefield.
No longer Vampires, but fighting with the same insane savagery.
Hurling itself into the fray, the pack's teeth close around limbs and do not let go.
These ghouls remember one thing - war - and they pursue that goal with single-minded savagery.
What is death but an obstacle to be overcome? There is no true death beneath the eternal night.
Though most Undead are no more than stumbling thralls, these warriors have achieved renown due to their effectiveness in melee.
